children.text: chāndogyopaniṣat
children.translated_text: <s>Chāndogyopaniṣat</s>

children.text:
atha prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ
āpyāyantu mamāṅgāni vākprāṇaścakṣuḥ śrotramatho balamindriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi, sarvaṃ brahmaupaniṣadaṃ māhaṃ brahma nirākuryāṃ mā mā brahma nirākarodanirākaraṇamastvanirākaraṇaṃ me 'stu, tadātmani nirate ya upaniṣatsu dharmāste mayi santu te mayi santu //
children.translated_text:
Now, the first chapter.
May my limbs, speech, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), eyes, ears, and also strength and all the <s>indriyas</s> (sense-faculties) be nourished. All is <s>Brahman</s> as declared in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. May I never deny <s>Brahman</s>; may <s>Brahman</s> never deny me. Let there be no denial; let there be no denial on my part. May those <s>dharmas</s> (virtues) that are in the <s>Upaniṣads</s> abide in me who am devoted to the <s>Ātman</s>; may they abide in me.

children.text:
oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādācāryaviracitaṃ bhāṣyam upodghātaḥ-
"omityetadakṣaram" ityādyaṣṭādhyāyī chāndogyopaniṣat /
tasyāḥ saṃkṣepator'thajijñāsubhya ṛjuvivaraṇamalpagranthaśrīmannarendrapurīyatīndraviracitaṃ chāndogyopaniṣadbhāṣyaṭippaṇamidamārabhyate /
tatra sambandhaḥ- samastaṃ karmādhigataṃ prāṇādidevatāvijñānasahitamarcirādimārgeṇa brahmalokapratipattikāraṇam /
kevalaṃ ca dhūmādimārgeṇa candralokapratipattikāraṇam /
svabhāvapravṛttānāṃ ca mārgadvayaparibhraṣṭānāṃ kaṣṭādhogatiruktā /
na cobhayormārgayoranyatarasminnapi mārge ātyantikī puruṣārthasiddhirityataḥ karmanirapekṣamadvaitātmavijñānaṃ saṃsāragatitrayahetūpamardena vaktavyamityupaniṣadārabhyate /
na cādvaitātmavijñānādanyatrā'tyantikī niḥśreyasaprāptiḥ /
vakṣyati hi-"atha ye 'myathāto viduranyarājānaste kṣayyalokā bhavanti" /
viparyaye ca"sa svarāḍbhavati"iti /
tathā dvaitaviṣayānṛtābhisandhasya bandhanaṃ taskarasyeva taptaparaśugrahaṇe bandhadāhabhāvaḥ, saṃsāraduḥkhaprāptiścetyuktvādvaitātmasatyābhisandhasyātaskarasyeva taptaparaśugrahaṇe bandhadāhābhāvaḥ saṃsāraduḥkhanivṛttirmokṣaśceti /
ata eva na karmasahabhāv.dvaitātmadarśanam /
kriyākārakaphalabhedopamardena"sadekamevādvitīyam" "ātmaivedaṃ sarvam" ityevamādivākyajanitasya bādhakapratyayānupapatteḥ /
karmavidhipratyaya iti cet /
na /
kartṛbhoktṛsvabhāvavijñānavatastajjanitakarmaphalarāgadveṣādidoṣavataśca karmavidhānāt /
adhigatasakalavedārthasya karmavidhānādadvaitajñānavato 'pi karmeti cet /
na /
karmādhikṛtaviṣayasya kartṛbhoktrādijñānasya svābhāvikasya"sadekamevādvitīyam""ātmaivedaṃ sarvam" ityanenopamarditatvāt /
tasmādavidyādidoṣavata eva karmāṇi vidhīyante /
nādvaitajñānavataḥ /
ata eva hi vakṣyati-"sarva ete puṇyalokā bhavanti /
brahmasastho 'mṛtatvameti"iti /
tatraitasminnadvaitavidyāprakaraṇe 'bhyudayasādhanānyupāsanānyucyante kaivalyasannikṛṣṭaphalāni /
cādvaitādīṣadvīkṛtabrahmaviṣayāṇi ityādīni karmasamṛddhiphalāni ca karmāṅgasambandhīni /
rahasyasāmānyānmanovṛttisāmānyācca yathādvaitajñānaṃ manovṛttimātraṃ tathānyānyapyupāsanāni manovṛttirūpāṇītyasti hi sāmānyam /
kastarhyadvaitajñānasyopāsanānāṃ ca viśeṣaḥ /
ucyate /
svābhāvikasyā'tmanyakriye 'dhyāropitasya kartrādikārakakriyāphalabhedavijñānasya nivartakamadvaitavijñānam /
rajjvādāviva sarpādyadhyāropalakṣaṇajñānasya rajjvādisvarūpaniścayaḥ prakāśanimittaḥ /
upāsanaṃ tu yathāśāstrasamarpitaṃ kiñcidālambanamupādāya tasminsamānacittavṛttisantānakaraṇaṃ tadvilakṣaṇapratyayānantaritamiti viśeṣaḥ /
tānyetānyupāsanāni sattvaśuddhikaratvena vastutattvāvabhāsakatvādadvaitajñānopakārakāṇyālambanaviṣayatvāt susādhyāni ceti pūrvamupanyasyante /
tatra karmābhyāsasya dṛḍhīkṛtatvātkarmaparityāgenopāsana eva duḥkhaṃ cetaḥ samarpaṇaṃ kartṛmiti karmāṅgaviṣayameva tāvadādāvupāsanamupanyasyate /
children.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ</s>, peace, peace, peace.
The <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda Ācārya</s>. Introduction:
The <s>Chāndogyopaniṣat</s>, consisting of eight chapters, begins with "<s>Om</s> — this syllable."
For those who wish to know its meaning in summary, this brief gloss on the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad-bhāṣya</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Narendrapurī Yatīndra</s>, is now commenced.
Therein, the connection is as follows: All <s>karma</s> (ritual action) that has been learned, combined with the knowledge of deities such as <s>Prāṇa</s> and others, is the cause of attaining the world of <s>Brahman</s> through the path of light (<s>arcirādi-mārga</s>).
And <s>karma</s> alone is the cause of attaining the world of the moon through the path of smoke (<s>dhūmādi-mārga</s>).
For those who act by natural impulse and have fallen from both paths, a miserable downward course has been stated.
Since on neither of the two paths is there ultimate fulfilment of the human goal, therefore the <s>Upaniṣad</s> is begun in order to teach <s>advaita-ātma-vijñāna</s> (non-dual Self-knowledge), independent of <s>karma</s>, by destroying the causes of the threefold course of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration).
Nor is there ultimate attainment of the highest good anywhere other than through non-dual Self-knowledge.
For it will be said: "Now, those who know otherwise than this, having other rulers — their worlds are perishable."
And conversely: "He becomes self-sovereign."
Likewise, for one whose conviction is directed toward the unreal in the domain of duality, there is bondage like that of a thief — just as in grasping a heated axe there is binding and burning, so there is the attainment of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. But for one whose conviction rests on the truth of the non-dual <s>Ātman</s>, like a non-thief grasping the heated axe, there is no binding or burning — there is cessation of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
Therefore, there is no vision of a dual self coexisting with <s>karma</s>,
because the cognition born of statements such as "Being is one only, without a second" and "The <s>Ātman</s> alone is all this" — which sublates the distinctions of action, agent, and result — cannot be contradicted.
If one objects that the injunction of <s>karma</s> is the valid cognition —
No, because <s>karma</s> is enjoined for one who possesses the natural knowledge of being an agent and experiencer, and who has the defects of attachment, aversion, and so on, born from that knowledge.
If one says that since all Vedic meanings have been learned, <s>karma</s> is enjoined even for one who possesses non-dual knowledge —
No, because the natural knowledge of agentship, enjoyership, and so on, which belongs to the domain of <s>karma</s>, has been sublated by "Being is one only, without a second" and "The <s>Ātman</s> alone is all this."
Therefore, <s>karmas</s> are enjoined only for one who possesses the defects of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the like,
not for one who possesses non-dual knowledge.
For this very reason it will be said: "All these attain meritorious worlds. One who is established in <s>Brahman</s> attains immortality."
In this context of the teaching of <s>advaita-vidyā</s> (non-dual knowledge), <s>upāsanas</s> (meditations) that are means to worldly prosperity are taught — those whose fruits are close to <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation),
and those that have <s>Brahman</s> as their object, slightly differentiated from non-duality, and others whose fruits are the success of <s>karma</s> and which are connected with the auxiliaries of <s>karma</s>.
Due to the commonality of being esoteric teachings and the commonality of being mental modifications, just as non-dual knowledge is merely a mental modification, so too are the other <s>upāsanas</s> — thus there is a commonality.
What then is the distinction between non-dual knowledge and the <s>upāsanas</s>?
It is stated:
Non-dual knowledge is that which removes the superimposed distinctions of agent, instruments, action, and result upon the <s>Ātman</s>, which is by nature actionless,
just as the ascertainment of the true nature of a rope and the like, caused by light, removes the knowledge characterized by the superimposition of a snake and the like upon the rope.
But <s>upāsana</s> (meditation) is the practice of maintaining a continuous flow of identical mental modifications directed toward some object as presented by scripture, uninterrupted by any contrary cognition — this is the distinction.
These <s>upāsanas</s>, by purifying the mind (<s>sattva</s>) and by illuminating the true nature of reality, are helpful to non-dual knowledge; and because they have a definite object of support, they are easy to accomplish — therefore they are presented first.
Therein, since the practice of <s>karma</s> has been firmly established, and since for one who renounces <s>karma</s> the directing of the mind to <s>upāsana</s> alone is difficult, the performer of <s>karma</s> — therefore the <s>upāsana</s> connected with the auxiliaries of <s>karma</s> is presented first at the outset.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.1

children.text:
om ity etad akṣaram udgītham upāsīta |
om iti hy udgāyati |
tasyopavyākhyānam || ChUp_1,1.1 ||
children.translated_text:
One should meditate on the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> as the <s>Udgītha</s> (loud chant),
for one chants the loud chant beginning with <s>Oṃ</s>.
Of that, the explanation follows.

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,1.1 ityupodghātabhāṣyam- omityetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta /
omityetadakṣaraṃ paramātmano 'bhidhānaṃ nediṣṭham /
tasminhi prayujyamāne sa prasīdati priyanāmagrahaṇa iva lokaḥ /
tadihetiparaṃ prayuktamabhidhāyakatvādvyāvartitaṃ śabdasvarūpamātraṃ pratīyate /
tathā cārcādivatparasyā'tmanaḥ pratīkaṃ sampadyate /
evaṃ nāmatvena pratīkatvena ca paramātmopāsanasādhanaṃ śreṣṭhamiti sarvavedānteṣvagatam /
japakarmasvādhyāyādyanteṣu ca bahuśaḥ prayogātprasiddhamasya śraiṣṭhyam /
atastadetakṣaraṃ varṇātmakamudgīthabhaktyavayavatvādudgīthaśabdavācyamupāsīta /
karmāṅgāvayavabhūta oṅkāre paramātmapratīke dṛḍhāmaikāgryalakṣaṇāṃ matiṃ santanuyāt /
svayameva śrutiroṅkārasyodgīthaśabdavācyatve hetumāha-omiti hyudgāyati /
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> (scripture) itself states the reason why <s>Oṃkāra</s> is denoted by the word <s>Udgītha</s>: "For one chants the loud chant beginning with <s>Oṃ</s>."

children.text: omityārabhya hi yasmādudgāyatyata udgītha oṅkāra ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since one chants the loud chant beginning with <s>Oṃ</s>, therefore <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the <s>Udgītha</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasyopavyākhyānaṃ tasyākṣarasyopavyākhyānamevamupāsanamevaṃvibhūtyevaṃphalamityādikathanamupavyākhyānam /
children.translated_text: "Of that, the explanation" — of that syllable, the explanation: describing the manner of this meditation, such powers, such fruits, and so forth — this is the explanation.

children.text: pravartata iti vākyaśeṣaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: "Follows" is the completion of the sentence.

Thus ends the introductory commentary. "One should meditate on the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> as the <s>Udgītha</s>." This syllable <s>Oṃ</s> is the nearest designation of <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self). For when it is employed, He is pleased, just as a person in the world is pleased when his dear name is uttered. Here, when used with the intention of referring beyond itself, its nature as a mere word-form, set apart by virtue of being a designator, is apprehended. And thus, like an image and so on, it becomes a <s>pratīka</s> (symbol) of the Supreme <s>Ātman</s>. In this way, it has been understood in all the <s>Vedānta</s> texts that <s>Oṃ</s> is the most excellent means of meditating on <s>Paramātman</s>, both as a name and as a symbol. Its excellence is well-known from its frequent use at the beginning and end of <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>karma</s> (ritual acts), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and so on. Therefore, one should meditate on this syllable, which is of the nature of a phoneme, and which is denoted by the word <s>Udgītha</s> because it is a devotional component of the <s>Udgītha</s>. One should maintain a firm, one-pointed mental focus — characterized by concentration — upon <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the symbol of <s>Paramātman</s>, which is a component of <s>karma</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.2

children.text:
eṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ pṛthivī rasaḥ |
pṛthivyā āpo rasaḥ |
apām oṣadhayo rasaḥ |
oṣadhīnāṃ puruṣo rasaḥ |
puruṣasya vāg rasaḥ |
vāca ṛg rasaḥ |
ṛcaḥ sāma rasaḥ |
sāmna udgītho rasaḥ || ChUp_1,1.2 ||
children.translated_text:
Of these beings, the earth is the <s>rasa</s> (essence).
Of the earth, water is the essence.
Of water, herbs are the essence.
Of herbs, the person is the essence.
Of the person, speech is the essence.
Of speech, the <s>Ṛk</s> (verse) is the essence.
Of the <s>Ṛk</s>, the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) is the essence.
Of the <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>Udgītha</s> is the essence.

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,1.2 eṣāṃ carācarāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ pṛthivī raso gatiḥ parāyaṇamavaṣṭambhaḥ /
pṛthivyā āpo raso 'psu hyotā ca protā ca pṛthivyatastā rasaḥ pṛthivyāḥ /
apāmoṣadhayo raso 'ppariṇāmatvādoṣadhīnām /
tāsāṃ puruṣo raso 'nnapariṇāmatvāt puruṣasya /
tasyāpi puruṣasya vāgrasaḥ /
puruṣāvayavānāṃ hi vāksāriṣṭhā /
ato vākpuruṣasya rasa ucyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore speech is said to be the essence of the person.

children.text: tasyā api vāca ṛgrasaḥ sāratarā /
children.translated_text: Of that speech too, the <s>Ṛk</s> is the essence — being the more essential.

children.text: ṛcaḥ sāma rasaḥ sārataram /
children.translated_text: Of the <s>Ṛk</s>, the <s>Sāman</s> is the essence — being yet more essential.

children.text: tasyāpi sāmna udgīthaḥ prakṛtatvādoṅkāraḥ sārataraḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: Of that <s>Sāman</s> too, the <s>Udgītha</s> — which, since it is the topic under discussion, means <s>Oṃkāra</s> — is the most essential.

Of these beings, moving and non-moving, the earth is the <s>rasa</s> — the goal, the ultimate support, the foundation. Of the earth, water is the essence, for the earth is woven warp and weft in water, therefore water is the essence of the earth. Of water, herbs are the essence, because herbs are transformations of water. Of those herbs, the person is the essence, because the person is a transformation of food. Of that person too, speech is the essence. For among the parts of a person, speech is the most excellent.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.3

children.text: sa eṣa rasānāṃ rasatamaḥ paramaḥ parārdhyo 'ṣṭamo yadudgīthaḥ || ChUp_1,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Udgītha</s> is the <s>rasatama</s> (quintessence) of essences, the supreme, the most exalted, the eighth.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,1.3 evaṃ sa eṣa udgīthākhya oṅkāro bhūtādīnāmuttarottararasānāmatiśayena raso rasatamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, this <s>Oṃkāra</s> called <s>Udgītha</s> is, by way of excellence, the essence of the successively higher essences beginning with the elements — the <s>rasatama</s> (quintessence of essences).

children.text: paramaḥ paramātmapratīkatvāt /
children.translated_text: It is supreme (<s>parama</s>) because it is a symbol of <s>Paramātman</s>.

children.text: parārdhyor'dhaṃ sthānaṃ, paraṃ ca tadardhaṃ ca parārdhaṃ tadarhatīti parārdhyaḥ paramātmasthānārhaḥ paramātmavadupāsyatvādityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Parārdhya</s> — <s>ardha</s> means "place"; <s>para</s> and that place is <s>parārdha</s> (the supreme place); one who deserves that is <s>parārdhya</s> — meaning "worthy of the place of <s>Paramātman</s>." The intended sense is that it is to be meditated upon like <s>Paramātman</s> itself.

children.text: aṣṭamaḥ pṛthivyādirasasaṃkhyāyāṃ yadudgītho ya udgīthaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: It is the eighth in the enumeration of essences beginning with earth. "Which is the <s>Udgītha</s>" means: that which is the <s>Udgītha</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.4
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.4

children.text: katamā katama rk katamat katamat sāma katamaḥ katama udgītha iti vimṛṣṭaṃ bhavati || ChUp_1,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: "Which, which is the <s>Ṛk</s>? Which, which is the <s>Sāman</s>? Which, which is the <s>Udgītha</s>?" — this has been deliberated upon.

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,1.4 vāca ṛgrasa ityuktam /
katamā sarkkatamattatsāma katamo vā sa udgīthaḥ /
katamā katameti vīpsā'darārthā /
nanu"vā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac" /
na hyatra ṛgjātibahutvaṃ kathaṃ ḍatamacprayogaḥ /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
jātau paripraśno jātiparipraśna ityetasminvigrahe jātāvṛgvyaktīnāṃ bahutvopapatteḥ /
na tu jāteḥ paripraśna iti vigṛhyate /
children.translated_text: It is not analyzed as "a question of the class" in the genitive sense.

children.text: nanu jāteḥ paripraśna ityasminvigrahe katamaḥ kaṭha ityādyudāharaṇamupapannaṃ jātau paripraśna ityatra tu na yujyate /
children.translated_text: Now, one might say that with the analysis "a question of the class" in the genitive sense, the illustrative example "which <s>Kaṭha</s>?" and so on would be appropriate, but it would not be fitting with the analysis "a question within the class."

children.text: tatrāpi kaṭhādijātāveva vyaktibahitvābhiprāyeṇa paripraśna ityadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in that case, the question is intended with reference to the multiplicity of individuals within the class of <s>Kaṭha</s> and so on — hence there is no fault.

children.text: yadi jāteḥ paripraśnaḥ syātkatamā katamargityādāvupasaṃkhyānaṃ kartavyaṃ syādvimṛṣṭaṃ bhavati vimarśaḥ kṛto bhavati //4 //
children.translated_text: If the question were about the class itself, then in "which, which <s>Ṛk</s>" and so on, an additional enumeration would have to be supplied. "It has been deliberated upon" means: the deliberation has been made.

It was said that the <s>Ṛk</s> is the essence of speech. Which is that <s>Ṛk</s>? Which is that <s>Sāman</s>? And which is that <s>Udgītha</s>? The repetition "which, which" is for the purpose of showing eagerness. Now, one might object: the suffix <s>ḍatamac</s> is used "in a question about a class among many"; but here there is no multiplicity of the class of <s>Ṛk</s>, so how can <s>ḍatamac</s> be used? This is not a fault, because in the analysis "a question about a class" means a question within the class, and within the class of <s>Ṛk</s> there is indeed a multiplicity of individual instances.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.5
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.5

children.text:
vāg evark |
prāṇaḥ sāma |
om ity etad akṣaram udgīthaḥ |
tad vā etan mithunaṃ yad vāk ca prāṇaś cark ca sāma ca || ChUp_1,1.5 ||
children.translated_text:
Speech alone is the <s>Ṛk</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is the <s>Sāman</s>.
The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> is the <s>Udgītha</s>.
That indeed is a pair — namely, speech and <s>Prāṇa</s>, and <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,1.5 vimarśe hi kṛte sati prativacanoktirupapannā vāgevarkprāṇaḥ sāmeti /
vāgṛcorekatve 'pi nāṣṭamatvavyāghātaḥ pūrvasmādvākyāntaratvādāptiguṇasiddhaya omityetadakṣaramudgītha iti /
vākprāṇāvṛksāmayonī iti vāgevarkprāṇaḥ sāmetyucyate /
yathākramamṛksāmayonyorvākprāṇayorgrahaṇe hi sarvāsāmṛcāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca sāmnāmavarodhaḥ kṛtaḥ syāt /
sarvarksāmāvarodhe carksāmasādhyānāṃ ca sarvakarmaṇāmavarodhaḥ kṛtaḥ syāt /
tadavarodhe ca sarve kāmā avaruddhāḥ syuḥ /
omityetadakṣaramudgītha iti bhaktyāśaṅkā vinartyate /
tadvā etaditi mithunaṃ nirdiśyate /
kiṃ tanmithunamityāha yadvākca prāṇaśca sarvaṛksāmakāraṇabhūtau mithunam /
ṛkva sāma ceti ṛksāmakāraṇāvṛksāmaśabdoktāvityarthaḥ /
na tu svatantramṛkca sāma ca mithunam /
children.translated_text: But <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> independently are not a pair.

children.text: anyathā hi vākca prāṇaścetyekaṃ mithunamṛksāma cāparaṃ mithunamiti dve mithune syātām /
children.translated_text: For otherwise, speech and <s>Prāṇa</s> would be one pair, and <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> another pair — there would be two pairs.

children.text: tathā ca tadetanmithunamityekavacananirdeṣo 'nupapannaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: And in that case, the singular reference "that is this pair" would be inappropriate.

children.text: tasmādṛksāmayonyorvākprāṇayoreva mithunatvam //5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the pairing belongs only to speech and <s>Prāṇa</s>, which are the sources of <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>.

When the deliberation has been made, the answer is appropriate: speech alone is the <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Sāman</s>. Even though speech and the <s>Ṛk</s> are identical, there is no contradiction with the eightfold sequence, because this is a different statement from the previous one, and is established as a quality of attainment: "The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> is the <s>Udgītha</s>." Speech and <s>Prāṇa</s> are called the sources of <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, and hence it is said: "Speech alone is the <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Sāman</s>." For by grasping speech and <s>Prāṇa</s>, which are respectively the sources of <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, all <s>Ṛk</s> verses and all <s>Sāman</s> chants would be included. And when all <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> are included, all <s>karmas</s> (rituals) that are accomplished through <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> would be included. And when those are included, all desires would be included. The doubt arising from the expression "the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> is the <s>Udgītha</s>" being merely devotional is dispelled. "That indeed" — thus a pair is indicated. What is that pair? He says: speech and <s>Prāṇa</s>, which are the causes of all <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, are a pair. "<s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>" — means that the causes of <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> are denoted by the words <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.6
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.6

children.text:
tad etan mithunam om ity etasminn akṣare saṃsṛjyate |
yadā vai mithunau samāgacchata āpayato vai tāv anyo 'nyasya kāmam || ChUp_1,1.6 ||
children.translated_text:
This pair is joined together in this syllable <s>Oṃ</s>.
When a pair comes together, they fulfil each other's desire.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,1.6 tadetadevaṃlakṣaṇaṃ mithunamomityetasminnakṣare saṃsṛjyate /
evaṃ sarvakāmāvāptiguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ mithunamoṅkāre saṃsṛṣṭaṃ vidyata ityoṅkārasya sarvakāmāvāptiguṇavattvaṃ prasiddham /
children.translated_text: Thus, the pair, endowed with the quality of fulfilling all desires, exists joined in <s>Oṃkāra</s> — hence the quality of <s>Oṃkāra</s> as the fulfiller of all desires is well-established.

children.text: vāṅmayatvamoṅkārasya prāṇaniṣpādyatvaṃ ca mithunena saṃsṛṣṭatvaṃ mithunasya kāmāpayitṛtvaṃ prasiddhamiti dṛṣṭānta ucyate /
children.translated_text: That <s>Oṃkāra</s> consists of speech and is produced by <s>Prāṇa</s> — this is its being joined with the pair. That the pair fulfils desires is well-known; hence an illustration is given.

children.text: yathā loke mithunau mithunāvayavau strīpuṃsau yadā samāgacchato grāmyadharmatayā saṃyujyeyānāṃ tadā'payataḥ prāpayato 'nyonyasyetaretarasya tau kāmam /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, the two members of a pair — a woman and a man — when they come together in conjugal union, they fulfil, they bring about, each other's desire,

children.text: tathā ca svātmānupraviṣṭena mithunena sarvakāmāptiguṇavattvamoṅkārasya siddhamityabhiprāyaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: so too, through the pair that has entered into its own nature, the quality of <s>Oṃkāra</s> as the fulfiller of all desires is established — this is the intended meaning.
This pair, having such characteristics, is joined together in the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.7
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.7

children.text: āpayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste || ChUp_1,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: One who, knowing thus, meditates on the syllable as the <s>Udgītha</s> becomes a fulfiller of desires.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,1.7 tadupāsako 'pyudgātā taddharmā bhavatītyāha-āpayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ yajamānasya bhavati ya etadakṣaramevamāptiguṇavadudgīthamupāste tasyaitadyathoktaṃ phalamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The worshipper of that also becomes endowed with its qualities — thus it is said: one who meditates on this syllable as the <s>Udgītha</s>, endowed with the quality of fulfilment as described, becomes a fulfiller of the desires of the sacrificer. Such is the fruit for him as stated — this is the meaning.

children.text: "taṃ yathā yathopāsate tadeva bhavati"iti śruteḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: 'As one meditates on him, so one becomes' — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture). //7//

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.8
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,1.8

children.text:
tad vā etad anujñākṣaram |
yad dhi kiṃcānujānāty om ity eva tad āha |
eṣo eva samṛddhir yad anujñā |
samardhayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste || ChUp_1,1.8 ||
children.translated_text: This [syllable <s>Om</s>] is indeed the syllable of assent. For whatever one assents to, one says just 'Om.' This alone is abundance — namely, assent. He who, knowing this syllable thus, meditates on the <s>udgītha</s> (chant) becomes indeed a fulfiller of desires. || ChUp 1,1.8 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,1.8 samṛddhiguṇavāṃścoṅkāraḥ /
katham-tadvā etatprakṛmanujñākṣaramanujñā ca sākṣaraṃ ca tat /
anujñānumatiroṅkāra ityarthaḥ /
kathamanujñetyāha śrutireva /
yaddhi kiñca yatkiñca loke jñānaṃ dhanaṃ vānujānāti vidvāndhanī vā tatrānumatiṃ kurvannomityeva tadāha /
tathā ca vede"trayastriṃśadityomiti hovāca"ityādinā /
tathā ca loke 'pi tavedaṃ dhanaṃ gṛhṇāmītyukta omityāha /
children.translated_text: And likewise in the world, when told 'I shall take this wealth of yours,' one says '<s>Om</s>.'

children.text: ata eṣā u evaiṣaiva samṛddhiryadanujñā yānujñā sā samṛddhistanmūlatvādanujñāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this alone — this very — abundance is assent; that assent which is abundance — because assent is the root of that [abundance].

children.text: samṛddho hyomityanujñāṃ dadāti tasmātsamṛddhiguṇavānoṅkāra ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who is prosperous gives assent saying '<s>Om</s>'; therefore, <s>Oṃkāra</s> possesses the quality of abundance — this is the meaning.

children.text: samṛddhiguṇopāsakatvāttaddharmā sansamardhayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ yajamānasya bhavati ya etadevaṃ vidvānakṣaramudgīthamupāsta ityādi pūrvavat //8 //
children.translated_text: Because [the meditator] meditates on [<s>Oṃkāra</s>] as possessing the quality of abundance, he acquires that quality and 'becomes indeed a fulfiller of desires of the sacrificer — he who, knowing this syllable thus, meditates on the <s>udgītha</s>' — and so on, as before. //8//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,1.8:] And <s>Oṃkāra</s> possesses the quality of abundance (<s>samṛddhi</s>). How? — 'This very well-known [syllable] is the syllable of assent' — assent (<s>anujñā</s>) is that which has the syllable [<s>Om</s>]; <s>anujñā</s> means approval, and <s>Oṃkāra</s> [is its expression] — this is the meaning. How [is it the syllable of] assent? The <s>śruti</s> itself [answers]: 'For whatever — whatever knowledge or wealth in the world one assents to — whether a learned person or a wealthy one, when giving approval therein — one says just <s>Om</s>.' And likewise in the <s>Veda</s>: 'Thirty-three — <s>Om</s>, he said' — and so on.

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.9

teneyaṃ trayī vidyā vartate |
om ity āśrāvayati |
om iti śaṃsati |
om ity udgāyati |
etasyaiva akṣarasyāpacityai mahimnā rasena || ChUp_1,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: By that [syllable], this threefold knowledge (<s>trayī vidyā</s>) proceeds. One calls out saying '<s>Om</s>'; one recites saying '<s>Om</s>'; one chants saying '<s>Om</s>' — for the worship of this very syllable, through [its] greatness and essence. || ChUp 1,1.9 ||
START ChUp 1,1.9

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,1.9 athedānīmakṣaraṃ stautyupāsyatvātprarocanārtham /
kathaṃ, tenākṣareṇa prakṛteneyamṛgvedādilakṣaṇā trayī vidyā trayīvidyāvihitaṃ karmetyarthaḥ /
na hi trayī vidyaivā'śrāvaṇādibhirvartate karma tu tathā pravartata iti prasiddham /
kathamomityāśrāvatyomiti śaṃsatyomityudgāyatīti liṅgācca somayāga iti gamyate /
tacca karmaitasyaivākṣarasyāpacityai pūjārtham /
paramātmapratīkaṃ hi tat /
tadapacitiḥ paramātmana eva sā /
"svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ"iti smṛteḥ /
mahimnā rasena /
kiñcaitasyaivākṣarasya mahimnā mahattvena ṛtvigyajamānādiprāṇairityarthaḥ /
tathaitasyaivākṣarasya rasena vrīhiyavādirasanirvṛttena haviṣetyarthaḥ /
yāgahomādyakṣareṇa kriyate /
taccā'dityamupatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: And that [sacrifice] serves the sun (<s>Āditya</s>).

children.text: tato vṛṣṭyādikrameṇa prāṇo 'nnaṃ ca jāyate /
children.translated_text: From that, through the sequence of rain and the like, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and food are born.

children.text: prāṇairannena ca yajñastāyate /
children.translated_text: Through vital breaths and food, the sacrifice is sustained.

children.text: ata ucyate 'kṣarasya mahimnā rasnti //9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore it is said: '[The sacrifice proceeds] through the greatness and essence of the syllable.' //9//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,1.9:] Now [the text] praises the syllable [<s>Om</s>] for the purpose of stimulating [interest in] meditation. How? — 'By that syllable under discussion, this threefold knowledge (<s>trayī vidyā</s>), characterized by <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the rest' — the ritual action enjoined by the threefold knowledge, this is the meaning. For it is not the threefold knowledge itself that proceeds through the calling out (<s>āśrāvaṇa</s>) and the like, but rather the ritual action proceeds thus — this is well-known. How? — From the indicators 'one calls out saying <s>Om</s>, one recites saying <s>Om</s>, one chants saying <s>Om</s>' — it is understood that [the context is] the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice. And that ritual action [is performed] for the worship of this very syllable — for the purpose of honoring [it]. For that [syllable] is a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>); its worship is indeed of the Supreme Self alone. [As stated in] the <s>smṛti</s>: 'By worshiping Him through one's own action, a person attains perfection.' [The ritual is performed] 'through [its] greatness and essence.' Furthermore, [it is performed] through the greatness, the grandeur, of this very syllable — that is, through the vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>) of the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) and the sacrificer — this is the meaning. And likewise, through the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of this very syllable — that is, through the oblation (<s>havis</s>) produced from the essence of rice, barley, and the like — this is the meaning. The sacrifice, offering, and the like are performed through the syllable [<s>Om</s>].

children.text: START ChUp 1,1.10
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,1.10

children.text:
tenobhau kurutaḥ |
yaś caitad evaṃ veda yaś ca na veda |
nānā tu vidyā cāvidyā ca |
yad eva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tad eva vīryavattaraṃ bhavatīti khalv etasyaivākṣarasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhavati || ChUp_1,1.10 ||
children.translated_text: By that [syllable], both perform [the sacrifice] — both he who knows this thus and he who does not know. But knowledge and ignorance are different. What one performs with knowledge, with faith, and with the <s>Upaniṣad</s> [meditation] — that alone becomes more powerful. This indeed is the detailed explanation of this very syllable. || ChUp 1,1.10 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,1.10 tatrākṣaravijñānavataḥ karma kartavyamiti sthitamābhipati-tenābhareṇobhau yaścaitadakṣaramevaṃ vyākhyātaṃ veda yaśca karmamātravidakṣarayāthātmyaṃ na veda tāvubhau kurutaḥ karma /
tayośca karmasāmarthyādeva phalaṃ syātkiṃ tatrākṣarayāthātmyavijñāneneti /
dṛṣṭaṃ hi loke harītakīṃ bhakṣayatostadrasābhijñetarayorvirecanam /
naivam /
yasmānnānā tu vidyā cāvidyā ca bhinne hi vidyāvidye /
tuśabdaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttyarthaḥ /
noṅkārasya karmāṅgatvamātravijñānameva rasatamāptisamṛddhiguṇavadvijñānaṃ kiṃ tarhi tato 'bhyadhikam /
tasmāttadaṅgādhikyātphalādhikyaṃ yuktamityabhiprāyaḥ /
dṛṣṭaṃ hi loke vaṇikśabarayoḥ padmarāgādimaṇivikraye vaṇijo vijñānādhikyātphalādhikyam /
tasmādyadeva vidyayā vijñānena yuktaḥ sankaroti karmaśraddhayā śraddadhānaśca sannupaniṣadā yogena yuktaścetyarthaḥ /
tadeva karma vīryavattaramavidvatkarmaṇo 'dhikaphalaṃ bhavatīti /
vidvatkarmaṇo vīryavattara[tvaṭavacanādaviduṣo 'pi karma vāryadeva bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ /
na cāviduṣaḥ karmaṇyanadhikāraḥ /
auṣastye kāṇḍe 'viduṣāmapyārvijyadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: In the section on <s>Auṣasti</s>, even non-knowers are seen [performing the role of] officiating priests.

children.text: rasatamāptisamṛddhiguṇavadakṣaramityekamupāsanam /
children.translated_text: [The meditation on] the syllable as possessing the qualities of essence (<s>rasa</s>), attainment, and abundance is one [form of] meditation.

children.text: madhye prayatnāntarādarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because no additional effort [for another meditation] is seen in between.

children.text: anekairhi viśeṣaṇairanekadhopāsyatvātkhalvetasyaiva prakṛtasyodgīthākhyasyākṣarasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhavati //10//
children.translated_text: For since [the syllable] is to be meditated upon in manifold ways through many qualifications — this is indeed the detailed explanation (<s>upavyākhyāna</s>) of this very syllable under discussion, called <s>udgītha</s>. //10//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,1.10:] Therein, it is established that the knower of the syllable [<s>Om</s>] should perform the ritual action — [the text says:] 'By that syllable, both — he who knows this syllable as thus explained and he who knows only the ritual action but does not know the true nature of the syllable — both perform the action.' And for these two, by the mere power of the action, there would be the fruit — so what [purpose is served] there by the knowledge of the true nature of the syllable? For it is observed in the world that whether one who knows the taste of <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan) [eats it] or one who does not — purgation [results] for both. [The answer is:] Not so. Because 'knowledge and ignorance are different' — for knowledge and ignorance are distinct. The word 'tu' (but) is for the purpose of excluding the [alternative] view. The knowledge of <s>Oṃkāra</s> is not merely [the knowledge of its being] an auxiliary of the ritual — [the knowledge of its qualities such as] essence (<s>rasa</s>), attainment, and abundance is something greater. Therefore, from the superiority of that auxiliary [knowledge], the superiority of the fruit is justified — this is the intended meaning. For it is observed in the world that in the sale of ruby gems and the like by a merchant and a tribesman (<s>śabara</s>), the merchant obtains a superior fruit because of [his] superior knowledge. Therefore, 'what one performs with knowledge' — being endowed with understanding — 'performs action with faith' — being full of faith — 'and with the <s>Upaniṣad</s>' — being endowed with the meditation (<s>yoga</s>) — this is the meaning. That action alone becomes 'more powerful' — [producing] a greater fruit than the action of one without knowledge. From the statement that [the action] of the knower is more powerful, the intended meaning is that the action of the non-knower too is indeed powerful. Nor is the non-knower unauthorized [to perform] the action.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya prathama khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the first chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>) of <s>Śāṅkara Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,2.1

children.text:
devāsurā ha vai yatra saṃyetire |
ubhaye prājāpatyās tad dha devā udgītham ājahrur anenainān abhibhaviṣyāma iti || ChUp_1,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Devas</s> (gods) and <s>Asuras</s> (demons), both offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s>, indeed contended with each other. The <s>Devas</s> took up the <s>udgītha</s> (chant), [thinking:] 'By this [chant] we shall overcome them.' || ChUp 1,2.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,2.1 devāsurā devāścāsurāśca /
devā dīvyaterdyetanārthasya śāstrodbhāsitā indriyavṛttayaḥ /
aśirāstadvirītāḥ sveṣvevāsuṣu viṣvagviṣayāsu prāṇanakriyāsu ramaṇātsvābhāvikyastama ātmikā indriyavṛttaya eva /
ha vā iti pūrvavṛttodbhāsakau nipātau /
yatra yasminnimitta itaretaraviṣayāpahāralakṣaṇe saṃyetire /
sampūrvasya yatateḥ saṃgrāmārthatvamiti saṃgrāmaṃ kṛtavanta utyarthaḥ /
śāsrīyaprakāśavṛttayabhibhavanāya pravṛttāḥ svābhāvikyastamorūpā indriyavṛttayo 'surāḥ /
tathā tadviparītāḥ śāsrārthaviṣayavivekajyotirātmāno devā svābhāvikatamorūpāsurābhibhavanāya pravṛttā ityanyonyābhibhavodbhavarūpaḥ saṃgrāma iva sarvaprāṇiṣu pratidehaṃ devāsurasaṅgrāmo 'nādikālapravṛtta ityabhiprāyaḥ /
sa ihaśrutyā'khyāyikārūpeṇa dharmādharmotpattivivekavijñānāya kathyate prāṇaviśuddhivijñānavidhiparatayā /
ata ubhaye 'pi devāsurāḥ prajāpaterapatyānīti prājāpatyāḥ /
prajāpatiḥ karmajñānādhikṛtaḥ puruṣaḥ /
"puruṣa evokthamayameva mahānprajāpatiḥ"iti śrutyantarāt /
tasya hi śāsrīyāḥ svābhāvikyaśca karaṇavṛttayo viruddhā apatyānīva tadudbhavatvāt /
children.translated_text: For the scriptural and the natural activities of the sense organs are his [Prajāpati's] opposing offspring, as it were — because they arise from him.

children.text: tattatrotkarṣāpakarṣalakṣaṇanimitte ha devā udgīthabhaktyupalakṣitamaudgātraṃ karmā'jahrurāhṛtavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, on the occasion characterized by superiority and inferiority, the <s>Devas</s> took up the <s>Audgātra</s> (chanting) ritual characterized by devotion to the <s>udgītha</s> — that is, they adopted it.

children.text: tasyāpi kevalasyā'haraṇāsambhavājjotiṣṭomādyāhṛtavanta ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since even the mere adoption of that [udgītha] alone is not possible [without the full ritual], the intended meaning is that they adopted [the ritual such as] the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like.

children.text: tatkimarthamājahrurityucyate anena karmaṇainānasurānabhibhaviṣyāma ityevamabhiprāyāḥ santaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: For what purpose did they take it up? — it is said: 'By this ritual, we shall overcome them, the <s>Asuras</s>' — with this intention. //1//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,2.1:] '<s>Devas</s> and <s>Asuras</s>' — the <s>Devas</s> and the <s>Asuras</s>. The <s>Devas</s>, [derived] from the root 'div' meaning 'to shine,' are the activities of the sense organs illuminated by scripture. The <s>Asuras</s> are those opposed to them — the natural, darkness-constituted activities of the sense organs that revel in their own vital breaths (<s>asus</s>), in the life-activities that are directed toward various objects, [which are] of the nature of <s>tamas</s> (darkness). The particles 'ha' and 'vai' bring out [the sense of] a past event. 'Yatra' — on what occasion — characterized by the mutual appropriation of each other's domains — 'they contended' — the prefix 'sam-' with the root 'yat' has the meaning of battle — that is, they engaged in battle, this is the meaning. The scriptural, light-constituted activities [of the senses], having set out to overcome [the Asuras] — and the natural, darkness-constituted activities of the sense organs, [which are] the <s>Asuras</s> — having set out to overcome those [Devas] of the opposite kind — thus what resembles a mutual battle of overcoming takes place in all beings, in each body — a battle of <s>Devas</s> and <s>Asuras</s> that has been going on since beginningless time — this is the intended meaning. This [battle] is narrated here by the <s>śruti</s> in the form of an illustrative story (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>), for the purpose of knowing the discrimination between <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (vice) — with the purport of enjoining the purification of the vital breaths through knowledge. Therefore, both <s>Devas</s> and <s>Asuras</s> are offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s>, hence <s>Prājāpatyas</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the person who is qualified for ritual action and knowledge. [As stated in] another <s>śruti</s>: 'The person alone is the <s>uktha</s> (hymn); he is the great <s>Prajāpati</s>.'

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,2.2

children.text:
te ha nāsikyaṃ prāṇam udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire |
taṃ ha asurāḥ pāpmanā vividhuḥ |
tasmāt tenobhayaṃ jighrati surabhi ca durgandhi ca |
pāpmanā hy eṣa viddhaḥ || ChUp_1,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: They meditated on the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) in the nose as the <s>udgītha</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> pierced it with evil. Therefore, by that [breath], one smells both — the fragrant and the foul-smelling. For it is pierced by evil. || ChUp 1,2.2 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,2.2 yadā ca tadudgīthaṃ karmā'jihīrṣavastadā-te ha devā nāsikyaṃ nāsikāyāṃ bhavaṃ cetanāvantaṃ ghrāṇaṃ prāṇamudgīthakartāramudgīthabhaktyopāsāṃcakrirejhrupāsanaṇṭakṛtavanta ityarthaḥ /
nāsikyaprāṇamadṛṣṭyodgīthākhyamakṣaramoṅkāramupāsāṃcakrira ityarthaḥ /
evaṃ hi prakṛtārthaparityāgo 'prakṛtārthopādānaṃ ca na kṛtaṃ syāt /
khalvetasyaivākṣarasyetyoṅkāramupāsāṃcakrira ityarthaḥ /
evaṃ hi prakṛtārthaparityāgo 'prakṛtārthopādānaṃ ca na kṛtaṃ syāt /
khalvetasyaivākṣarasyetyoṅkāro hyāpāsyatayā prakṛtaḥ /
nanūdgīthopalakṣitaṃ karmā'hṛtavanta ityavoca idānīmeva;kathaṃ nāsikyaprāṇadṛṣṭyoṅkāramupāsāṃcakrira ityāttha /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
udgīthakarmaṇyeva hi tatkartṛprāṇadevatādṛṣṭyodgīthabhaktyavayavaścoṅkāra upāsyatvena vivakṣito na svatantro 'tastādarthyena karmā'hṛtavanta iti yuktamevoktam /
tamevaṃ devairvṛtamudgātāraṃ hāsurāḥ svābhāvikatama ātmāno jyotīrūpaṃ nāsikyaṃ prāṇaṃ devaṃ svotthena pāpmanādharmāsaṅgarūpeṇa vividhurviddhavantaḥ saṃsarga kṛtavanta ityarthaḥ /
sa hi nāsikyaḥ prāṇaḥ kalyāṇagandhagrahaṇābhimānāsaṅgābhibhūtavivekavijñāno babhūva /
sa tena doṣeṇa pāpmasaṃsargī babhūva /
tadidamuktamasurāḥ pāpmanā vividhuriti /
yasmādāsureṇa pāpmanā viddhastasmāttena pāpmanā prerito ghrāṇaḥ prāṇo durgandhigrāhakaḥ prāṇinām /
atastenobhayaṃ jighrati lokaḥ surabhi ca durgandhi ca /
pāpmanā hyeṣa yasmādviddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is pierced by evil.

children.text: ubhayagrahaṇamavivakṣitam /
children.translated_text: The mention of 'both' [fragrant and foul] is not the intended [point].

children.text: yasyobhayaṃ havirārtimārchatīti yadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as [in the expression] 'for him, the oblation attains both pain [and pleasure].'

children.text: yadevedamapratirūpaṃ jighratīti samānaprakaraṇaśruteḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s> in the same context: 'that which [the organ of smell] smells that is unseemly.' //2//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,2.2:] When they desired to take up that <s>udgītha</s> ritual — the <s>Devas</s> meditated on the nasal [<s>prāṇa</s>], belonging to the nose — the conscious [faculty of] smell, the <s>prāṇa</s> [that functions as] the performer of the <s>udgītha</s> — they performed the meditation through devotion to the <s>udgītha</s>, that is, they practiced the meditation — this is the meaning. They meditated on the nasal <s>prāṇa</s>, perceiving [in it] the <s>udgītha</s>-syllable, that is, the syllable <s>Om</s> — [referred to as] <s>akṣara</s> — this is the meaning. For thus [interpreting], neither would there be an abandonment of the topic under discussion nor an introduction of an extraneous topic. 'This very syllable' — [means] they meditated on <s>Oṃkāra</s> — this is the meaning. For thus, neither would there be an abandonment of the topic nor an introduction of an extraneous topic. For <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the topic, being the object of meditation. [Objection:] 'But you have just said that they adopted the ritual characterized by the <s>udgītha</s>; how [can you] now say that they meditated on <s>Oṃkāra</s> by perceiving [it in] the nasal <s>prāṇa</s>?' There is no fault here. For in the <s>udgītha</s> ritual itself, [<s>Oṃkāra</s>] is intended as the object of meditation through the perception of the <s>prāṇa</s>-deity as the performer of the <s>udgītha</s>; [it is] a subsidiary part [of the ritual] through devotion to the <s>udgītha</s>, not independent — therefore, it is rightly said that they adopted the ritual, being purposive thereto. That [nasal prāṇa], thus chosen by the <s>Devas</s> as the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanter), the <s>Asuras</s> — [those] natural, darkness-constituted [tendencies] — pierced the luminous, divine nasal <s>prāṇa</s> with evil (<s>pāpman</s>) — that is, with the contact of <s>adharma</s> (vice) arising from themselves — they pierced it, made contact with it — this is the meaning. For that nasal <s>prāṇa</s>, its discriminative knowledge having been overpowered by the attachment to grasping pleasant odors, became afflicted. It became associated with that fault, with the contact of evil. This is what is stated [by the text]: 'The <s>Asuras</s> pierced it with evil.' Because it was pierced by the demonic evil, the organ of smell, impelled by that evil, becomes a grasper of foul odors for beings. Therefore, 'by that [organ], one smells both — the fragrant and the foul-smelling.'

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.3-6
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,2.3-6

children.text:
atha ha vācam udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire |
tāṃ hāsurāḥ pāpmanā vividhuḥ |
tasmāt tayobhayaṃ vadati satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca |
pāpmanā hy eṣā viddhā || ChUp_1,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: Then they meditated on speech as the <s>udgītha</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> pierced it with evil. Therefore, by that [speech], one says both — truth and untruth. For it is pierced by evil. || ChUp 1,2.3 ||

children.text:
atha ha cakṣur udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire |
tad dhāsurāḥ pāpmanā vividhuḥ |
tasmāt tenobhayaṃ paśyati darśanīyaṃ cādarśanīyaṃ ca |
pāpmanā hy etad viddham || ChUp_1,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: Then they meditated on the eye as the <s>udgītha</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> pierced it with evil. Therefore, by that [eye], one sees both — the beautiful and the ugly. For it is pierced by evil. || ChUp 1,2.4 ||

children.text:
atha ha śrotram udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire |
tad dhāsurāḥ pāpmanā vividhuḥ |
tasmāt tenobhayaṃ śṛṇoti śravaṇīyaṃ cāśravaṇīyaṃ ca |
pāpmanā hy etad viddham || ChUp_1,2.5 ||
children.translated_text: Then they meditated on the ear as the <s>udgītha</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> pierced it with evil. Therefore, by that [ear], one hears both — what is worth hearing and what is not worth hearing. For it is pierced by evil. || ChUp 1,2.5 ||

children.text:
atha ha mana udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire |
tad dhāsurāḥ pāpmanā vividhuḥ |
tasmāt tenobhayaṃ saṃkalpayate saṃkalpanīyaṃ ca |
pāpmanā hy etad viddham || ChUp_1,2.6 ||
children.translated_text: Then they meditated on the mind as the <s>udgītha</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> pierced it with evil. Therefore, by that [mind], one conceives both — what is worth conceiving and [what is not worth conceiving]. For it is pierced by evil. || ChUp 1,2.6 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,2.3-6 mukhyaprāṇasyopāsyatvāya tadviśuddhatvānubhavārtho 'yaṃ vicāraḥ śrutyā pravartitaḥ /
ataścakṣurādidevatāḥ krameṇa vicāryā'sureṇa pāpmanā viddhā ityapohyante /
children.translated_text: And therefore, the deities of the eye and the other [organs] are examined in sequence and dismissed as 'pierced by the demonic evil.'

children.text: samānamanyat, atha ha vācaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ mana ityādi /
children.translated_text: The rest is the same [as before] — 'then speech, the eye, the ear, the mind' — and so on.

children.text: anuktā apyanyāstvagrasamādidevatā draṣṭavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: And other deities, not mentioned [here], such as the hand (<s>agrasama</s>) and the like, should be understood [in the same way].

children.text: "evamu khalvetā devatāḥ pāpmabhiḥ" iti śrutyantarāt //3-6 //
children.translated_text: From another <s>śruti</s>: 'Thus indeed were those deities [afflicted] by evils.' //3-6//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,2.3-6:] This inquiry is initiated by the <s>śruti</s> for the purpose of the experience of the purity of the chief <s>prāṇa</s> (<s>mukhya prāṇa</s>), in order [to establish it as] the object of meditation.

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.7
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,2.7

children.text:
atha ha ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇas tam udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire |
taṃ hāsurā ṛtvā vidadhvaṃsur yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā vidhvaṃsetaivam || ChUp_1,2.7 ||
children.translated_text: Then they meditated on this very chief <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) of the mouth as the <s>udgītha</s>. The <s>Asuras</s>, having struck against it, were shattered — just as [a clod of earth], having struck against a rock, would be shattered. || ChUp 1,2.7 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,2.7 āsureṇa viddhatvādghrāṇādidevatā apohyāthānantaraṃ ya evāyaṃ prasiddho mukhe bhavo mukhyaḥ prāṇastamudgīthamupāsāñcakrire taṃ hāsurāḥ pūrvavadṛtvā prāpya vidadhvaṃsurvinaṣṭā abhiprāyamātreṇa /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,2.7:] Since the deities of the organ of smell and the others are dismissed because of being pierced by the demonic [evil] — then, the well-known <s>mukhya prāṇa</s> (chief vital breath), born in the mouth — they meditated on that as the <s>udgītha</s>. The <s>Asuras</s>, having struck against it as before — having reached it — were shattered, destroyed — merely by [the force of] the intention.

children.text: akṛtvā kiñcidapi prāṇasya /
children.translated_text: without doing anything whatsoever to <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath).

children.text: kathaṃ vinaṣṭā ityatra dṛṣṭāntamāha-yathā loke 'śmānamākhaṇaṃ na śakyate khanituṃ kuddālādibhirapi bhettuṃ na śakyo 'khaṇa evā'khaṇastamṛtvā sāmarthyālloṣṭaḥ pāṃsupiṇḍaḥ kṣutyantarāccāśmani kṣipto 'śmabhedanābhiprāyeṇa tasyāśmanaḥ kiñcidapyakṛtvā svayaṃ vidhvaṃseta vidīryetaivaṃ vidadhvaṃsurityarthaḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: [The commentary asks:] 'How are they destroyed?' — Here an illustration is given: just as in the world, a stone that is solid (<s>akhaṇa</s>) cannot be dug up even with picks and the like, nor can it be split — being indeed solid — [so too with Prāṇa]. Having struck against it (<s>ṛtvā</s>), a clod of earth (<s>loṣṭa</s>), a lump of dust, thrown against the stone from hunger [i.e., in desperation] with the intention of breaking the stone, without doing anything to the stone, itself is shattered — is scattered. Thus 'is shattered' — this is the meaning. (1.2.7)

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.8
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.2.8]

children.text:
evaṃ yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā vidhvaṃsata evaṃ haiva sa vidhvaṃsate ya evaṃvidi pāpaṃ kāmayate yaś cainam abhidāsati |
sa eṣo 'śmākhaṇaḥ || ChUp_1,2.8 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, just as a clod striking a solid stone is shattered, so indeed is he shattered who wishes evil upon one who knows this, and also he who harms him. That [<s>Prāṇa</s>] is this solid stone. (ChUp 1.2.8)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,2.8 evaṃ viśuddho 'surairadharṣitatvātprāṇa iti evaṃvidaḥ prāṇātmabhūtasyedaṃ phalamāha-yathāśmānamiti /
eṣa eva dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
evaṃ haiva sa vidhvaṃsate vinaśyati /
ko 'sāvityāha-ya evaṃvidi yathoktaprāṇavidi pāpaṃ tadanarhaṃ kartu kāmayata icchati yaścāpyenamabhidāsati hinasti prāṇavidaṃ pratyākrośatāḍanādi prayuṅkte so 'pyevameva vidhvaṃsata ityarthaḥ /
yasmātsa eṣa prāṇavitprāṇabhūtatvādaśmākhaṇa ivāśmākhaṇo 'dharṣaṇīya ityarthaḥ /
nanu nāsikyo 'pi prāṇo vāyvātmā yathā mukhyastatra nāsikyaḥ prāṇaḥ pāpmanā viddhaḥ prāṇa eva sanna mukhyaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But the nasal <s>Prāṇa</s> too, being of the nature of air (<s>vāyu</s>), is like the chief [<s>Prāṇa</s>]. There, the nasal <s>Prāṇa</s> was pierced by evil — [yet] being <s>Prāṇa</s> itself, why is it not the chief?

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect.

children.text: nāsikyastu sthānakaraṇavaiguṇyādviddho vāyvātmāpi sanmukhyaḥ sthānadevatābalīyastvānna viddha iti yuktam /
children.translated_text: The nasal [breath], due to the deficiency of its locus and organ, was pierced — even though being of the nature of air; the chief [<s>Prāṇa</s>], because of the superiority of the presiding deity of [its] locus, was not pierced. This is justified.

children.text: yathā vāsyādayaḥ śikṣāvatpuruṣāśrayāḥ kāryaviśeṣaṃ kurvanti nānyahastagatāstadvaddoṣavadghrāṇasacivatvādviddhā ghrāṇadevatā na mukhyaḥ //8 //
children.translated_text: Just as chisels and the like, when wielded by a skilled person, produce particular effects — but not [when] held by another's hand — so too, the deity of the organ of smell, being the assistant [of <s>Prāṇa</s>], was pierced on account of [its association with] faults; [but] the chief [<s>Prāṇa</s> was] not [pierced]. (1.2.8)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.2.8:] Thus, [<s>Prāṇa</s>] being pure, unassailable by the <s>asuras</s> — [this is said] regarding <s>Prāṇa</s>. This fruit of one who knows this, who has become identical with <s>Prāṇa</s>, is stated: 'just as a stone' and so on. This is the very same illustration. Thus indeed he is shattered, he is destroyed — who is he? It is said: he who wishes evil, who desires [to do] what is inappropriate, to one who knows <s>Prāṇa</s> as described — and also he who harms him, who injures the knower of <s>Prāṇa</s>, who employs reviling, striking, and the like against [him] — he too is likewise shattered. This is the meaning. Since this knower of <s>Prāṇa</s>, having become one with <s>Prāṇa</s>, is like a solid stone — unassailable. This is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.9
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.2.9]

children.text:
naivaitena surabhi na durgandhi vijānāti |
apahatapāpmā hy eṣaḥ |
tena yad aśnāti yat pibati tenetarān prāṇān avati |
etam u evāntato 'vittvotkrāmati |
vyādadāty evāntata iti || ChUp_1,2.9 ||
children.translated_text: By this [<s>Prāṇa</s>], one perceives neither fragrant nor foul-smelling [odors]. For this [<s>Prāṇa</s>] has evil destroyed from it. Therefore, whatever one eats, whatever one drinks — by that, it sustains the other <s>prāṇas</s> (vital functions). And at the end, not having obtained this [<s>Prāṇa</s>], one departs [dies]. [At death,] one opens [the mouth] at the end. (ChUp 1.2.9)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,2.9 yasmānna viddho 'surairmukhyastasmānnaivaitena surabhi durgandhi vā vijānāti ghrāṇenaiva tadubhayaṃ vijānāti lokaḥ /
ataśca pāpmakāryādarśanādapahatapāpmāpahato vināśito 'panītaḥ pāpmā yasmātso 'yamapahatapāpmā hyeṣa viśuddha ityarthaḥ /
yasmāccā'tmambharayaḥ kalyāṇādyāsaṅgavattvādghrāṇādayo na tathā'tmambharirmukhyaḥ kiṃ tarhi sarvārthaḥ /
kathamiti, ucyate-tena mukhyena yadaśnāti yatpibati lokastenāśitena pītena cotarānghrāṇādīnavati pālayati /
tena hi teṣāṃ sthitirbhavatītyarthaḥ /
ataḥ sarvambharaḥ prāṇo 'to viśuddhaḥ /
kathaṃ punarmukhyāśitapītābhyāṃ sthitireṣāṃ gamyata iti, ucyate-etaṃ (tamu eva) mukhyaṃ prāṇaṃ mukhyaprāṇasya vṛttimannapāne ityarthaḥ /
antato 'nte maraṇakāle 'vittvālabdhvot-krāmati /
ghrāṇādiprāṇasamudāya ityarthaḥ /
aprāṇo hi na śaknotyaśituṃ pātuṃ vā /
tena tadotkrāntiḥ prasiddhā ghrāṇādikalāpasya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the departure of the collection [of vital functions] beginning with smell and the like [at the time of death] is well-known through that [dependence on Prāṇa].

children.text: dṛśyate hyutkrāntau prāṇasyāśiśiṣā /
children.translated_text: For at the time of departure, the desire to eat [belonging to] <s>Prāṇa</s> is observed.

children.text: ato vyādadātyevā'syavidāraṇaṃ karotītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'one opens [the mouth]' — meaning one makes a gaping [of the mouth]. This is the meaning.

children.text: taddhyannālābha utkrāntasya liṅgam //9 //
children.translated_text: For that [opening of the mouth] is the sign of the departing [soul's Prāṇa] not having obtained food. (1.2.9)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.2.9:] Since the chief [<s>Prāṇa</s>] was not pierced by the <s>asuras</s>, therefore 'by this one perceives neither fragrant nor foul-smelling [odors]' — the world perceives both of those through the organ of smell alone. And therefore, from the non-observation of the effect of evil, [<s>Prāṇa</s>] has evil destroyed from it — destroyed, annihilated, removed is the evil from which — thus this one has evil destroyed, is pure. This is the meaning. And since the organ of smell and the like are not self-sustaining, because of their attachment to [particular] qualities like pleasantness and the like — they are not self-sustaining like the chief [<s>Prāṇa</s>]. Rather, [the chief Prāṇa] serves all purposes. How? It is said: 'by that chief [<s>Prāṇa</s>], whatever one eats, whatever one drinks' — by that eaten and drunk [food], the world sustains, nourishes the other [vital functions such as] smell and the like. For their stability exists through that [chief Prāṇa]. This is the meaning. Therefore, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the sustainer of all, hence pure. But how is the stability of these [functions] through the food eaten and drunk by the chief [<s>Prāṇa</s>] known? It is said: this chief <s>Prāṇa</s> — meaning that the sustenance of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> is food and drink — at the end, at the time of death, not having obtained [food and drink], one departs. The entire collection of <s>prāṇas</s> beginning with smell and the like — this is the meaning. For without <s>Prāṇa</s>, one cannot eat or drink.

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.10
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.2.10]

children.text:
taṃ hāṅgirā udgītham upāsāṃ cakre |
etam u evāṅgirasaṃ manyante 'ṅgānāṃ yad rasaḥ || ChUp_1,2.10 ||
children.translated_text: Him did <s>Aṅgiras</s> meditate upon as the <s>Udgītha</s>. They consider him to be <s>Aṅgirasa</s> indeed, because he is the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of the limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>). (ChUp 1.2.10)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,2.10 taṃ hāṅgirāstaṃ mukhyaṃ prāṇaṃ hāṅgirā ityevaṅguṇamudgīthamuyāsāñcakre baka ityeva sambandhaṃ kṛtavantaḥ kecit /
etamu evā'ṅgirasaṃ bṛhaspatimayāsyaṃ prāṇaṃ manyanta iti canāt /
bhavatyevaṃ yathāśrutāsambhave, sambhavati tu yathāśrutamṛṣicodanāyāmapi śrutyantaravat /
tasmācchatarcina ityācakṣata etameva santamṛṣimapi /
tathā mādhyamā gṛtsamado viśvāmitro vāmadevo 'trirityādi ṛṣīneva prāṇamāpādayati śrutiḥ /
tathaitānapyṛṣīnprāṇopāsakānaṅgirobṛhaspatyayāsyānprāṇaṃ karotyabhedavijñānāya /
children.translated_text: Similarly, [the <s>Śruti</s>] makes these worshippers of <s>Prāṇa</s> — <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Ayāsya</s> — into <s>Prāṇa</s> [itself], for the purpose of the knowledge of non-difference.

children.text: "prāṇo ha pitā prāṇo mātā"ityādivacca /
children.translated_text: As [stated in the text]: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the father, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the mother,' and so forth.

children.text: tasmādṛṣiraṅgirā nāma prāṇa eva sannātmānamaṅgirasaṃ prāṇamudgīthamupāsāñcakra ityetat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the sage named <s>Aṅgiras</s>, being none other than <s>Prāṇa</s>, meditated upon himself as <s>Aṅgirasa</s>, [that is,] <s>Prāṇa</s>, as the <s>Udgītha</s>. This is [the meaning].

children.text: yadyasmātso 'ṅgānāṃ prāṇaḥ sanrasastenāsāvāṅgirasaḥ //10 //
children.translated_text: Because <s>Prāṇa</s>, being the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of the limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>), is [called] <s>Aṅgirasa</s>. (1.2.10)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.2.10:] 'Him did <s>Aṅgiras</s>' — this chief <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s> — [that is, Prāṇa] having such qualities — meditated upon as the <s>Udgītha</s>. Some have made the connection [reading it as if] '<s>Baka</s>' [was the subject]. 'They consider him to be <s>Aṅgirasa</s>' — [that is,] <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Ayāsya</s> consider [him to be] <s>Prāṇa</s> — because of the word 'ca' [implying additional subjects]. This [reading] is acceptable when the literal reading is impossible; but when the literal reading is possible — as in [similar cases of] instruction by sages — [the reading should be taken] as in other <s>Śruti</s> passages. Therefore, the <s>Ṛṣis</s> — from <s>Śatarcin</s> onward — describe this very <s>Prāṇa</s> as a sage. Similarly, the <s>Śruti</s> identifies <s>Prāṇa</s> with the sages — <s>Mādhyama</s>, <s>Gṛtsamada</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and so on.

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.11-12
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.2.11-12]

children.text:
tena taṃ ha bṛhaspatir udgītham upāsāṃ cakre |
etam u eva bṛhaspatiṃ manyante |
vāg ghi bṛhatī tasyā eṣapatiḥ || ChUp_1,2.11 ||
children.translated_text: Him did <s>Bṛhaspati</s> meditate upon as the <s>Udgītha</s>. They consider him to be <s>Bṛhaspati</s> indeed, for speech (<s>vāc</s>) is <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and he is its lord (<s>pati</s>). (ChUp 1.2.11)

children.text:
tena taṃ hāyāsya udgītham upāsāṃ cakre |
etam u evāyāsyaṃ manyante |
āsyād yad ayate || ChUp_1,2.12 ||
children.translated_text: Him did <s>Ayāsya</s> meditate upon as the <s>Udgītha</s>. They consider him to be <s>Ayāsya</s> indeed, because he issues forth (<s>ayate</s>) from the mouth (<s>āsya</s>). (ChUp 1.2.12)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,2.11,12 tathā vāco bṛhatyāḥ patistenāsau bṛhaspatiḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.2.11-12:] Similarly, [he is called] <s>Bṛhaspati</s> because he is the lord (<s>pati</s>) of speech (<s>vāc</s>), which is <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: yathā yadyasmādāsyādayate nirgacchati tenā'yāsya ṛṣiḥ prāṇa eva sannityarthaḥ tathānyo 'pyupāsaka ātmānamevā'ṅgirasādiguṇaṃ prāṇamudgīthamupāsītetyarthaḥ //11-12 //
children.translated_text: Just as [he is called] <s>Ayāsya</s> because he issues forth (<s>ayate</s>), goes out, from the mouth (<s>āsya</s>) — the sage [<s>Ayāsya</s>] is none other than <s>Prāṇa</s>. This is the meaning. Similarly, any other worshipper should meditate upon himself as having the qualities of <s>Aṅgiras</s> and the like, [identifying himself with] <s>Prāṇa</s> as the <s>Udgītha</s>. This is the meaning. (1.2.11-12)

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.13
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.2.13]

children.text:
tena taṃ ha bako dālbhyo vidāṃ cakāra |
sa ha naimiśīyānām udgātā babhūva |
sa ha smaibhyaḥ kāmān āgāyati || ChUp_1,2.13 ||
children.translated_text: Him did <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> come to know. He became the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter) of the <s>Naimiśīyas</s> (inhabitants of Naimiṣa forest). He used to chant for them [the fulfillment of their] desires. (ChUp 1.2.13)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,2.13 na kevalamaṅgiraḥprabhṛtayaḥ upāsāñcakrire /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.2.13:] Not only did <s>Aṅgiras</s> and the others meditate [upon Prāṇa].

children.text: taṃ ha bako nāma dalbhyasyāpatyaṃ dālbhyo vidāñcakāra yathādarśitaṃ prāṇaṃ vijñātavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Baka</s> by name, the offspring of <s>Dalbhya</s>, [hence] <s>Dālbhya</s>, came to know him — he understood <s>Prāṇa</s> as described.

children.text: viditvā ca sa ha naimiśīyānāṃ sattriṇāmudgātā babhūva /
children.translated_text: Having known [this], he became the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter) of the <s>Naimiśīyas</s>, [those engaged in the] sacrificial session.

children.text: sa ca prāṇavijñānasāmarthyādebhyo naimiśīyebhyaḥ kāmānāgāyati sma hā'gītavānkiletyarthaḥ //13 //
children.translated_text: And by the power of [his] knowledge of <s>Prāṇa</s>, he chanted for these <s>Naimiśīyas</s> [the fulfillment of their] desires — meaning he indeed chanted [successfully]. This is the meaning. (1.2.13)

children.text: START ChUp 1,2.14
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.2.14]

children.text:
āgātā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste |
ity adhyātmam || ChUp_1,2.14 ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, he who, knowing this, meditates upon the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) syllable as the <s>Udgītha</s>, becomes the singer of desires. This [is the meditation] with reference to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>). (ChUp 1.2.14)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,2.14 tathānyo 'pyudgātā'gātā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati evaṃ vidvānyathoktaguṇaṃ prāṇamakṣaramudgīthamupāste tasyaitaddṛṣṭaṃ phalamuktam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.2.14:] Similarly, any other <s>Udgātṛ</s> — knowing this, one who meditates upon <s>Prāṇa</s> with the qualities described, [that is,] the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) as the <s>Udgītha</s> — the visible fruit of this [meditation] has been stated: [one becomes] the singer of desires.

children.text: prāṇātmabhāvastvadṛṣṭam"devo bhūtvā devānapyeti"iti śrutyantarātsiddhamevetyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But becoming identical with <s>Prāṇa</s> is the unseen [fruit] — [this is] established from another <s>Śruti</s> text: 'Having become a god, one attains the gods.' This is the intended meaning.

children.text: ityadhyātmametadātmaviṣayamudgīthopāsanamityuktopasaṃhāro 'dhidaivatodgīthopāsane vakṣyamāṇe buddhisamādhānārthaḥ //14//
children.translated_text: 'This [is] with reference to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>)' — this concluding statement [indicates that] this meditation on the <s>Udgītha</s> pertains to the self — [and serves] for the purpose of mental composure in the meditation on the <s>Udgītha</s> with reference to the deities (<s>adhidaivata</s>) that will be stated [next]. (1.2.14)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the first chapter in the <s>Śāṅkara</s> commentary on the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.1

athādhidaivatam |
ya evāsau tapati tam udgītham upāsīta |
udyan vā eṣa prajābhya udgāyati |
udyaṃs tamo bhayam apahanti |
apahantā ha vai bhayasya tamaso bhavati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_1,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, with reference to the deities (<s>adhidaivata</s>). One should meditate upon the sun that shines yonder as the <s>Udgītha</s>. Rising, he sings aloud for creatures. Rising, he dispels darkness and fear. Indeed, he who knows this becomes the dispeller of fear and darkness. (ChUp 1.3.1)
[Beginning of ChUp 1.3.1]

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,3.1 athānantaramadhidaivataṃ devatāviṣayamudgīthopāsanaṃ prastutamutyartho 'nekadhopāsyatvādudgīthasya /
ya evāsāvādityastapati samudgīthamupāsītā'dityadṛṣṭyodgīthamupāsītetyarthaḥ /
tamudgīthamityudgīthaśabdo 'kṣaravācī sankathamāditye vartata iti?ucyate /
children.translated_text: 'Him as the <s>Udgītha</s>' — the word '<s>Udgītha</s>' denotes the syllable [Om]. How does it refer to the sun? It is said:

children.text: udyannudgacchanvā eṣa prajābhyaḥ prajārthamudgāyati prajānāmannotpattyartham /
children.translated_text: Rising, or ascending, he sings aloud for creatures — for the sake of creatures, for the purpose of the production of food for creatures.

children.text: na hyanudyati tasminvrīhyādeḥ paktiḥ syādata udgāyatīvodgāyati, yathaivodgātānnārthamata udgīthaḥ savitetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For if he does not rise, there would be no ripening of rice and the like. Therefore, he sings aloud as if he were singing aloud — just as the <s>Udgātṛ</s> [sings] for the sake of food. Therefore, <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun) is the <s>Udgītha</s>. This is the meaning.

children.text: kiñcodyannaiśaṃ tamastajjaṃ ca bhayaṃ praṇināmapahanti tamevaṅguṇaṃ savitāraṃ yo veda so 'pahantā nāśayitā ha vai bhayasya janmamaraṇādilakṣaṇasyā'tmanastamasaśca tatkāraṇasyājñānalakṣaṇasya bhavati //1 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, rising, he dispels the darkness of night and the fear born of it for living beings. One who knows him, <s>Savitṛ</s>, endowed with such qualities — he becomes the dispeller, the destroyer, of fear characterized by birth, death, and the like, and of the darkness that is its cause, characterized by ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>). (1.3.1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.3.1:] 'Now, next' — the meditation on the <s>Udgītha</s> with reference to the deities (<s>adhidaivata</s>), pertaining to the deity, is introduced — because of the <s>Udgītha</s> being meditated upon in multiple ways. 'The sun that shines yonder' — one should meditate upon [it] together with the <s>Udgītha</s> — meaning one should meditate upon the <s>Udgītha</s> with the vision of [it as] the sun.

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.3.2]

children.text:
samāna u evāyaṃ cāsau ca |
uṣṇo 'yam uṣṇo 'sau |
svara itīmam ācakṣate svara iti pratyāsvara ity amum |
tasmād vā etam imam amuṃ ca udgītham upāsīta || ChUp_1,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: This one [<s>Prāṇa</s>] and that one [the Sun] are indeed the same. This one is warm, that one is warm. This one they call <s>svara</s> (sound), and that one they call <s>svara</s> (sound) and <s>pratyāsvara</s> (echo). Therefore, one should meditate upon this one and that one as the <s>Udgītha</s>. (ChUp 1.3.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,3.2 yadyapi sthānabhedātprāṇādityau bhinnāviva lakṣyete tathāpi na sa tattvabhedastayoḥ /
katham-samāna u eva tulya eva prāṇaḥ savitrā guṇataḥ savitā ca prāṇena /
yasmāduṣṇo 'yaṃ prāṇa uṣṇaścāsau savitā /
kiñca svara itīmaṃ prāṇamācakṣate kathayanti tathā svara iti;pratyāsvara iti cāmuṃ savitāram /
yasmātprāṇaḥ svaratyeva na punarmṛtaḥ pratyāgacchati /
children.translated_text: Because <s>Prāṇa</s> sounds forth (<s>svarati</s>) [continuously], but having died, does not return.

children.text: savitā tvastamitvā punarapyahanyahani pratyāgacchati /
children.translated_text: <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun), however, having set, returns again day after day.

children.text: ataḥ pratyāsvaro 'smādguṇato nāmataśca samānāvitaretaraṃ prāṇādityau /
children.translated_text: Therefore [the Sun is called] '<s>pratyāsvara</s>' (echo). Because of these shared qualities and names, <s>Prāṇa</s> and the Sun are the same as each other.

children.text: ataḥ satattvābhedādetaṃ prāṇamimamamuṃ cā'dityamudgīthamupāsīta //2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the non-difference of their reality, one should meditate upon this <s>Prāṇa</s> and that Sun as the <s>Udgītha</s>. (1.3.2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.3.2:] Although, because of the difference of location, <s>Prāṇa</s> and the Sun appear as if different, nevertheless there is no real difference between them. How? 'The same indeed' — <s>Prāṇa</s> is equal to <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun) in qualities, and <s>Savitṛ</s> [is equal] to <s>Prāṇa</s>. Because this <s>Prāṇa</s> is warm and that <s>Savitṛ</s> is warm. Moreover, they call this <s>Prāṇa</s> '<s>svara</s>' (sound), and likewise they call that <s>Savitṛ</s> '<s>svara</s>' (sound) and '<s>pratyāsvara</s>' (echo).

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.3.3]

children.text:
atha khalu vyānam evodgītham upāsīta |
yad vai prāṇiti sa prāṇaḥ |
yad apāniti so 'pānaḥ |
atha yaḥ prāṇāpānayoḥ saṃdhiḥ sa vyānaḥ |
yo vyānaḥ sā vāk |
tasmād aprāṇann anapānan vācam abhivyāharati || ChUp_1,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: Now, one should meditate upon <s>Vyāna</s> indeed as the <s>Udgītha</s>. What one breathes out, that is <s>Prāṇa</s>. What one breathes in, that is <s>Apāna</s>. Now, that which is the junction of <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>, that is <s>Vyāna</s>. That which is <s>Vyāna</s>, that is speech (<s>Vāc</s>). Therefore, without breathing out and without breathing in, one utters speech. (ChUp 1.3.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,3.3 atha khalviti prakārāntareṇopāsanamudgīthasyocyate-vyānameva vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaṃ prāṇasyaiva vṛttiviśeṣamudgīthamupāsīta /
adhunā tatsatattvaṃ nirūpyate-yadvai puruṣaḥ prāṇiti mukhanāsikābhyāṃ vāyuṃ bahirniḥsārayati sa prāṇākhyo vāyorvṛttiviśeṣo yadapānityapaśvasiti tābhyāmevāntarākarṣati vāyuṃ so 'pāno 'pānākhyā vṛttiḥ /
tataḥ kimiti, ucyate-atha ya uktalakṣaṇayoḥ prāṇāpānayoḥ sandhistayorantarā vṛttiviśeṣaḥ sa vyānaḥ, yaḥ sāṅkhyādiśāsraprasiddhiḥ śrutyā viśeṣanirūpaṇānnāsau vyāna ityabhiprāyaḥ /
kasmātpunaḥ prāṇāpānau hitvā mahatā'yāsena vyānasyaivopāsanamucyate /
children.translated_text: But why is the meditation on <s>Vyāna</s> alone stated with such great effort, setting aside <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>?

children.text: vīryavatkarmahetutvamityāha-yo vyānaḥ sā vāk /
children.translated_text: [Answer:] Because it is the cause of powerful ritual action — it is said: 'That which is <s>Vyāna</s>, that is speech (<s>Vāc</s>).'

children.text: vyānakāryatvādvācaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because speech is an effect of <s>Vyāna</s>.

children.text: yasmādvyānanirvartyā vāktasmādaprāṇannanapānanprāṇāpānavyāpārāvakurvanvācamabhivyāharatyuccārayati lokaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: Since speech is produced by <s>Vyāna</s>, therefore, without breathing out and without breathing in — [that is,] without performing the functions of <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s> — the world utters, produces speech. (1.3.3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.3.3:] 'Now indeed' — the meditation on the <s>Udgītha</s> is stated by another method: one should meditate upon <s>Vyāna</s> — whose characteristic will be described — [which is] a particular mode of <s>Prāṇa</s> itself — as the <s>Udgītha</s>. Now its true nature is determined: what the person breathes out (<s>prāṇiti</s>) — [that is,] expels air outward through the mouth and nostrils — that particular mode of air called <s>Prāṇa</s>; what he breathes in (<s>apāniti</s>) — [that is,] draws air inward through those very [openings] — that [particular] mode called <s>Apāna</s>. Then what? It is said: 'Now, that which is the junction of <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s> as described' — the particular mode [of breath] between those two — that is <s>Vyāna</s>. [This is] the one well-known in the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and other treatises. The specific determination [here is] through <s>Śruti</s> — the intended meaning is that that [described here] is not the [same] <s>Vyāna</s> [as in those treatises].

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.3.4]

children.text:
yā vāk sark |
tasmād aprāṇann anapānann ṛcam abhivyāharati |
yark tat sāma |
tasmād aprāṇann anapānan sāma gāyati |
yat sāma sa udgīthaḥ |
tasmād aprānann anapānann udgāyati || ChUp_1,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: That which is speech, that is <s>Ṛc</s> (verse). Therefore, without breathing out and without breathing in, one utters the <s>Ṛc</s>. That which is <s>Ṛc</s>, that is <s>Sāman</s> (chant). Therefore, without breathing out and without breathing in, one sings the <s>Sāman</s>. That which is <s>Sāman</s>, that is the <s>Udgītha</s>. Therefore, without breathing out and without breathing in, one chants the <s>Udgītha</s>. (ChUp 1.3.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,3.4 tathā vāgviśeṣāmṛcamṛksaṃsthaṃ ca sāma sāmāvayavaṃ codgīthamaprāṇannanapānanvyānenaiva nirvartayatītyabhiprāyaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 1.3.4:] Similarly, the particular [forms of] speech — the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse), the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) based on the <s>Ṛc</s>, and the <s>Udgītha</s> as a component of the <s>Sāman</s> — one produces all of these without breathing out and without breathing in, through <s>Vyāna</s> alone. This is the intended meaning. (1.3.4)

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 1.3.5]

children.text:
ato yāny anyāni vīryavanti karmāṇi yathāgner manthanam ājeḥ saraṇaṃ dṛḍhasya dhanuṣa āyamanam aprāṇann anapānaṃs tāni karoti |
etasya hetor vyānam evodgītham upāsīta || ChUp_1,3.5 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever other powerful actions there are — such as the churning of fire, the running of a race, the drawing of a strong bow — one performs them without breathing out and without breathing in. For this reason, one should meditate upon <s>Vyāna</s> indeed as the <s>Udgītha</s>. (ChUp 1.3.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,3.5 na kevalaṃ vāgādyabhivyāharaṇamevāto 'smādanyānyapi yāni vīryavanti karmāṇi prayatnādhikyanirvartyāni yathāgnermanthanamājermaryādāyāḥ saraṇaṃ dhāvanaṃ dṛḍhasya dhanuṣa āyamanamākarṣaṇamaprāṇannanapānaṃstāni karoti /
atoviśiṣṭo vyānaḥ prāṇādivṛttibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>vyāna</s> is superior to the other functions such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest.

children.text: viśiṣṭasyopāsanaṃ jyāyaḥ phalavattvādrājopāsanavat /
children.translated_text: The meditation on that which is superior is greater, because it yields greater fruit, just as meditation on a king.

children.text: etasya hetoretasmātkāraṇādvyānamevodgīthamupāsīta nānyadvṛttyantaram /
children.translated_text: For this reason, for this cause, one should meditate on <s>vyāna</s> alone as the <s>udgītha</s>, and not on any other vital function.

children.text: karmavīryavattaratvaṃ phalam //5 //
children.translated_text: The fruit is the superiority in the power of action. //5//

Not only the utterance of speech and other faculties, but also other powerful actions requiring great effort are accomplished by it — such as the churning of fire, running to the boundary line, the stretching and drawing of a strong bow — these he performs without breathing in or breathing out.

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.6
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,3.6

children.text:
atha khalūdgīthākṣarāṇy upāsīta ud-gī-tha iti |
prāṇa evot |
prāṇena hy uttiṣṭhati |
vag gīḥ |
vāco ha gira ity ācakṣate |
annaṃ tham |
anne hīdaṃ sarvaṃ sthitam || ChUp_1,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Now, one should meditate on the syllables of the <s>udgītha</s> — <s>ut</s>, <s>gī</s>, <s>tha</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) indeed is <s>ut</s>, for by <s>prāṇa</s> one rises up. Speech is <s>gī</s>, for speeches are called <s>giraḥ</s> (songs). Food is <s>tha</s>, for upon food all this is established.

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,3.6 athādhunā khalūdgīthākṣarāṇyupāsīta bhaktyakṣarāṇi mā bhūvannityato viśinaṣṭi-udgītha iti /
udgīthanāmākṣarāṇītyartho nāmākṣaropāsane 'pi nāmavata evopāsanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavedamukamiśrā iti yadvat /
prāṇa evot, udityasminnakṣare prāṇadṛṣṭiḥ /
kathaṃ prāṇasyottvamityāha-prāṇena hyuttiṣṭhati sarvo 'prāṇasyāvasādadarśanādato 'styudaḥ prāṇasya ca sāmānyam /
children.translated_text: How is the quality of 'rising' (<s>uttva</s>) attributed to <s>prāṇa</s>? He says — for by <s>prāṇa</s> one rises up; since one who lacks <s>prāṇa</s> is seen to sink down, there is a commonality between <s>ut</s> (rising) and <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: vāggīḥ /
children.translated_text: Speech is <s>gī</s>.

children.text: vāco ha gira ityācakṣate śiṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: The learned call speeches <s>giraḥ</s>.

children.text: tathānnaṃ thamanne hīdaṃ sarvaṃ sthitamato 'styannasya thākṣarasya ca sāmānyam //6 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, food is <s>tha</s> — for upon food all this is established; thus there is a commonality between food and the syllable <s>tha</s>. //6//

Now one should meditate on the syllables of the <s>udgītha</s> — lest the syllables be taken in a fragmented way, he specifies — <s>ut</s>, <s>gī</s>, <s>tha</s>. The meaning is: the syllables that constitute the name '<s>udgītha</s>.' Even in meditating on the syllables of the name, the meditation is indeed of the one bearing the name, just as when one says 'so-and-so of mixed descent.' <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is <s>ut</s> — in the syllable <s>ut</s>, the vision of <s>prāṇa</s> is to be superimposed.

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.7
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,3.7

children.text:
dyaur evot |
antarikṣaṃ gīḥ |
pṛthivī tham |
āditya evot |
vāyur gīḥ |
agnis tham |
sāmaveda evot |
yajurvedo gīḥ |
ṛgvedas tham |
dugdhe 'smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ |
annavān annādo bhavati |
ya etāny evaṃ vidvān udgīthākṣarāṇy upāsta ud-gī-tha iti || ChUp_1,3.7 ||
children.translated_text: Heaven indeed is <s>ut</s>. The mid-region is <s>gī</s>. The earth is <s>tha</s>. The sun indeed is <s>ut</s>. The wind is <s>gī</s>. Fire is <s>tha</s>.
