The <s>Sāmaveda</s> indeed is <s>ut</s>. The <s>Yajurveda</s> is <s>gī</s>. The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is <s>tha</s>. Speech yields its milk for him — that milk which is the milk of speech. He becomes possessed of food, an eater of food — he who, knowing thus, meditates on the syllables of the <s>udgītha</s> — <s>ut</s>, <s>gī</s>, <s>tha</s>.

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,3.7 trayāṇāṃ śrutyuktāni sāmānyāni tāni tenānurūpeṇa śeṣeṣvapi draṣṭavyāni /
dyaurevoduccaiḥ sthānāt /
antarikṣaṃ gārgiraṇāllokānām /
pṛthivī thaṃ prāṇisthānāt /
āditya evodūrdhvatvāt /
vāyurgīragnyādīnāṃ giraṇāt /
agnisthaṃ yajñīyakarmāvasthānāt /
sāmaveda evotsvargasaṃstutatvāt /
yajurvedo gīryajuṣā prattasya haviṣo devatānāṃ giraṇāt /
ṛgvedasthamṛcyadhyūḍhatvātsāmnaḥ /
udgīthākṣaropāsanaphalamadhunocyate-dugdhe dogdhyasmai sādhakāsya /
kā sā vāk, kaṃ doham /
ko 'sau doha ityāha-yo vāco dohaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is that milk? He says — that which is the milk of speech.

children.text: ṛgvedādiśabdasādhyaṃ phalamityabhiprāyastadvāco dohastaṃ svayameva vāgdogdhyātmānameva dogdhi /
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is that the fruit attainable through the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and other scriptures is the milk of speech; speech itself milks that, yields itself.

children.text: kiñcānnavānprabhūtānno 'nnādaśca dīptāgnirbhavati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, he becomes possessed of food, having abundant food, and an eater of food, one with blazing digestive fire.

children.text: ya etāni yathoktānyevaṃ yathoktaguṇānyudgīthākṣarāṇi vidvānsannupāsta udgītha iti //7 //
children.translated_text: He who, knowing, meditates on the syllables of the <s>udgītha</s> as described, with the qualities as stated — <s>ut</s>, <s>gī</s>, <s>tha</s>. //7//

The commonalities stated by scripture for the three are to be seen in the remaining cases as well, by analogy. Heaven indeed is <s>ut</s>, because of its high position. The mid-region is <s>gī</s>, because it swallows (<s>giraṇa</s>) the worlds. The earth is <s>tha</s>, because it is the abode of living beings. The sun indeed is <s>ut</s>, because of its being above. The wind is <s>gī</s>, because it swallows fire and other elements. Fire is <s>tha</s>, because it is the basis of sacrificial rites. The <s>Sāmaveda</s> indeed is <s>ut</s>, because it is praised in connection with heaven. The <s>Yajurveda</s> is <s>gī</s>, because the deities swallow (<s>giraṇa</s>) the oblations offered through the <s>Yajus</s>. The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is <s>tha</s>, because the <s>Sāman</s> is established upon the <s>Ṛc</s>. Now the fruit of the meditation on the syllables of the <s>udgītha</s> is stated — speech milks, yields for him, for the practitioner. What is that speech? What is the milk?

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.8
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,3.8

children.text:
atha khalv āśīḥ samṛddhiḥ |
upasaraṇānīty upāsīta |
yena sāmnā stoṣyan syāt tat sāmopadhāvet || ChUp_1,3.8 ||
children.translated_text: Now then, the fulfillment of wishes. One should meditate on them as approaches. Whatever <s>Sāman</s> one is about to chant, one should approach that <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,3.8 atha khalvidānīmāśīḥsamṛddhirāśiṣaḥ kāmasya samṛddhiryathā bhavettaducyata iti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now then, the fulfillment of wishes — the fulfillment, the successful accomplishment of desires — how it may come about, that is being stated; this is the completion of the sentence.

children.text: upasaraṇānyupasartavyānyupagantavyāni dhyeyānītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Approaches (<s>upasaraṇāni</s>) means things to be approached, to be resorted to, to be contemplated — this is the meaning.

children.text: katham, ityupāsīta, evamupāsīta /
children.translated_text: How? — 'thus one should meditate' — in this manner one should meditate.

children.text: tadyathā-yena sāmnā yena sāmaviśeṣeṇa stoṣyanstutiṃ kariṣyansyādbhavedudgātā tatsāmopadhāvedupasareccintayedutpattyādibhiḥ //8 //
children.translated_text: Namely — whatever <s>Sāman</s>, whatever particular <s>Sāman</s> the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priest is about to chant, is going to perform the praise with, he should approach that <s>Sāman</s>, contemplate it with respect to its origin and other aspects. //8//

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.9
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,3.9

children.text: yasyām ṛci tām ṛcaṃ, yad ārṣeyaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ, yāṃ devatām abhiṣṭoṣyan syāt tāṃ devatām upadhāvet || ChUp_1,3.9 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛc</s> in which that <s>Sāman</s> is based — one should approach that <s>Ṛc</s>; the <s>Ṛṣi</s> to whom it belongs — one should approach that <s>Ṛṣi</s>; the deity which one is about to praise — one should approach that deity.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,3.9 yasyāmṛci tatsāma tāṃ carcamupadhāveddevatādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛc</s> in which that <s>Sāman</s> is based — one should approach that <s>Ṛc</s> through contemplation of its deity and other aspects.

children.text: yadārṣeyaṃ sāma taṃ carṣim /
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛṣi</s> to whom the <s>Sāman</s> belongs — one should approach that <s>Ṛṣi</s>.

children.text: yāṃ devatāmabhiṣṭoṣyansyāttāṃ devatāmupadhāvet //9 //
children.translated_text: The deity which one is about to praise — one should approach that deity. //9//

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.10
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,3.10

children.text:
yena cchandasā stoṣyan syāt tac chanda upadhāvet |
yena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāt taṃ stomam upadhāvet || ChUp_1,3.10 ||
children.translated_text: The meter in which one is about to chant — one should approach that meter. The <s>Stoma</s> (hymn-form) with which one is about to chant — one should approach that <s>Stoma</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,3.10 yena cchandasā gāyatryādinā stoṣyansyāttacchanda upadhāvet /
children.translated_text: The meter, such as <s>Gāyatrī</s> and others, in which one is about to chant — one should approach that meter.

children.text: yena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: The <s>Stoma</s> with which one is about to chant —

children.text: stomāṅgaphalasya kartṛgāmitvādātmanepadaṃ stoṣyamāṇa iti /
children.translated_text: Because the fruit of the constituent parts of the <s>Stoma</s> accrues to the agent himself, the <s>Ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) form <s>stoṣyamāṇa</s> is used.

children.text: taṃ stomamupadhāvet //10 //
children.translated_text: One should approach that <s>Stoma</s>. //10//

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.11
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,3.11

children.text: yāṃ diśam abhiṣṭoṣyan syāt tāṃ diśam upadhāvet || ChUp_1,3.11 ||
children.translated_text: The direction toward which one is about to chant praise — one should approach that direction.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,3.11 yāṃ diśamabhiṣṭoṣyansyāttāṃ diśamupadhāvedadhiṣṭhātrādibhiḥ //11 //
children.translated_text: The direction toward which one is about to chant praise — one should approach that direction through contemplation of its presiding deity and other aspects. //11//

children.text: START ChUp 1,3.12
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,3.12

children.text:
ātmānam antata upasṛtya stuvīta kāmaṃ dhyāyann apramattaḥ |
abhyāśo ha yad asmai sa kāmaḥ smṛdhyeta yatkāmaḥ stuvīteti yatkāmaḥ stuvīteti || ChUp_1,3.12 ||
children.translated_text: Finally, having approached one's own self, one should chant the praise, meditating on one's desire, without negligence. It is likely that the desire will be fulfilled for him — whatever desire he may have when he chants, whatever desire he may have when he chants.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,3.12 ātmānamudgātā svaṃ rūpaṃ gotranāmādibhiḥ sāmādīnkrameṇa svaṃ cā'tmānamantato 'nta upasṛtya stuvīta /
children.translated_text: The <s>Udgātṛ</s> priest, having approached his own self — his own form — through lineage, name, and other aspects, and having approached the <s>Sāman</s> and other elements in sequence, and finally his own self at the end, should chant the praise.

children.text: kāmaṃ dhyāyannapramattaḥ svaroṣmavyañjanādibhyaḥ pramādamakurvaṃstato 'bhyāśaḥ kṣiprameva ha yadyatrāsmā evaṃvide sa kāmaḥ samṛdhyeta samṛddhiṃ gacchet /
children.translated_text: Meditating on his desire, without negligence — being careful about the <s>svara</s> (accents), <s>ūṣman</s> (sibilants), <s>vyañjana</s> (consonants), and other aspects — then quickly indeed will that desire be fulfilled, will reach accomplishment, for one who knows thus.

children.text: ko 'sau, yatkāmo yaḥ kāmo 'sya so 'yaṃ yatkāmaḥ sanstuvīteti /
children.translated_text: What is that desire? It is whatever desire he has — he who, having that desire, chants the praise.

children.text: dviruktikādarārthā //12//
children.translated_text: The repetition is for the sake of emphasis. //12//

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section of the first chapter in <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
om ity etad akṣaram udgītham upāsīta |
om iti hy udgāyati |
tasyopavyākhyānam || ChUp_1,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Om</s> — one should meditate on this syllable as the <s>udgītha</s>, for one chants the <s>udgītha</s> beginning with <s>Om</s>. The explanation of this follows.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,4.1 omityetadityādiprakṛtasyākṣarasya punarupādānamudgīthākṣarādyupāsanāntaritatvādanyatra prasaṅgo mā bhūdityevamartham /
children.translated_text: The repetition of the previously introduced syllable with 'Om, this' is for this purpose — lest, due to the intervening meditations on the syllables of the <s>udgītha</s> and other topics, the subject be extended elsewhere.

children.text: prakṛtasyaivākṣarasyāmṛtābhayaguṇaviśiṣṭasyopāsanaṃ vidhātavyamityārambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The commencement is for prescribing the meditation on the very same syllable that was previously introduced, qualified by the attributes of immortality and fearlessness.

children.text: omityādi vyākhyātam //1 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Om</s>' and so forth has already been explained. //1//

children.text: START ChUp 1,4.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,4.2

children.text:
devā vai mṛtyor bibhyatas trayīṃ vidyāṃ prāviśan |
te chandobhir acchādayan |
yad ebhir acchādayaṃs tac chandasāṃ chandastvam || ChUp_1,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Devas</s>, being afraid of death, entered the threefold knowledge. They covered themselves with the meters. Because they covered themselves with these, that is the meter-nature (<s>chandastva</s>) of the meters.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,4.2 devā vai mṛtyormārakādvibhyataḥ kiṃ kṛtavanta ityucyate /
trayīṃ vidyāṃ trayīvihitaṃ karma prāviśanpraviṣṭavanto vaidikaṃ karma prārabdhavanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: They entered the threefold knowledge — that is, they entered into, they undertook the rituals prescribed by the three <s>Vedas</s>; the meaning is that they commenced Vedic rituals.

children.text: tanmṛtyosrāṇaṃ manyamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thinking that this would be a refuge from death.

children.text: kiñca te karmaṇyaviniyuktaiśchandobhirmantrairjapahomādi kurvanta ātmānaṃ karmāntareṣvacchādayaṃśchāditavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, using the meters — the <s>mantras</s> not employed in other rituals — they performed <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>homa</s> (oblation), and other rites, and thereby covered, concealed themselves within the rituals.

children.text: yadyasmādebhirmantrairacchādayaṃstattasmācchandasāṃ mantrāṇāṃ chādanācchandastvaṃ prasiddhameva //2 //
children.translated_text: Because they covered themselves with these <s>mantras</s>, therefore the well-known designation 'meters' (<s>chandas</s>) for the <s>mantras</s> is derived from covering (<s>chādana</s>). //2//
The <s>Devas</s> indeed, being afraid of death, of <s>Māraka</s> (the destroyer) — what did they do? This is being stated.

children.text: START ChUp 1,4.3
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,4.3

children.text:
tān u tatra mṛtyur yathā matsyam udake paripaśyed evaṃ paryapaśyad ṛci sāmni yajuṣi |
te nu vittvordhvā ṛcaḥ sāmno yajuṣaḥ svaram eva prāviśan || ChUp_1,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: But death saw them there, just as one might see a fish in water — he saw them in the <s>Ṛc</s>, in the <s>Sāman</s>, in the <s>Yajus</s>. They, having known this, rose above the <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>Sāman</s>, and the <s>Yajus</s>, and entered into the <s>Svara</s> (the syllable <s>Om</s>) alone.

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,4.3 tāṃstatra devānkarmaparānmṛtyuryathā loke matsyaghātako matsyamudake nātigambhīre paripaśyedbaḍiśodakasrāvopāyasādhyaṃ manyamāna evaṃ paryapaśyaddṛṣṭavānmṛtyuḥ karmakṣayopāyena sādhyāndevānmena ityarthaḥ /
kvāsau devāndadarśetyucyate-ṛci sāmni yajuṣi /
ṛgyajuḥsāmasambandhikarmaṇītyarthaḥ /
te nu devā vaidikena karmaṇā saṃskṛtāḥ śuddhātmānaḥ santo mṛtyościkīrṣitaṃ viditavantaḥ /
viditvā ca ta ūrdhvā vyāvṛttāḥ karmabhya ṛcaḥ sāmno yajuṣa ṛgyajuḥsāmasambaddhātkarmaṇo 'bhyutthāyetyarthaḥ /
tena karmaṇā mṛtyubhayāpagamaṃ prati nirāśāstadapāsyāmṛtābhayaguṇamakṣaraṃ svaraṃ svaraśabditaṃ prāviśanneva praviṣṭavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having become hopeless of escaping the fear of death through that ritual action, abandoning it, they entered indeed into the syllable <s>Svara</s> — designated by the word <s>svara</s> — which is endowed with the qualities of immortality and fearlessness.

children.text: oṅkāropāsanaparāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ /
children.translated_text: They became devoted to the meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

children.text: evaśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ sansamuccayapratiṣedhārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'eva' (alone) serves the purpose of restriction, precluding combination with anything else.

children.text: tadupāsanaparāḥ saṃvṛttā ityarthaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: they became devoted solely to that meditation. //3//

Death saw those <s>Devas</s> who were devoted to ritual action there — just as in the world a fish-killer might see a fish in water that is not too deep, considering it attainable by means of hook and draining of water — so death saw, perceived, the <s>Devas</s> as conquerable through the means of exhaustion of their merits; this is the meaning. Where did he see the <s>Devas</s>? This is stated — in the <s>Ṛc</s>, in the <s>Sāman</s>, in the <s>Yajus</s>; the meaning is: in the rituals connected with the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajur</s>, and <s>Sāma Vedas</s>. Those <s>Devas</s>, having been purified by Vedic ritual, having become pure in self, came to know death's intention. Having known it, they rose up, turned away from ritual action — from the <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>Yajus</s> — that is, having risen above the rituals connected with the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajur</s>, and <s>Sāma Vedas</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,4.4
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,4.4

children.text:
yadā vā ṛcam āpnoty om ity evātisvarati evaṃ sāmaivaṃ yajuḥ |
eṣa u svaro yad etad akṣaram etad amṛtam abhayam |
tat praviśya devā amṛtā abhavan || ChUp_1,4.4 ||
children.translated_text: When one takes up the <s>Ṛc</s>, one chants '<s>Om</s>' aloud — likewise with the <s>Sāman</s>, likewise with the <s>Yajus</s>. This is the <s>Svara</s> — that which is this syllable. This is immortal, this is fearless. Having entered this, the <s>Devas</s> became immortal.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,4.4 kathaṃ punaḥ svaraśabdavācyatvamakṣarasyetyucyate-yadā vā ṛcamāpnotyomityevātisvaratyevaṃ sāmaivaṃ yajuḥ /
children.translated_text: How is it that the syllable is denoted by the word <s>Svara</s>? This is explained — when one takes up the <s>Ṛc</s>, one chants aloud with '<s>Om</s>' — likewise with the <s>Sāman</s>, likewise with the <s>Yajus</s>.

children.text: eṣa u svaraḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Svara</s>.

children.text: ko 'sau yadetadakṣarametadamṛtamabhayaṃ tatpraviśya yathāguṇamevāmṛtā abhayāścābhavandevāḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: What is it? It is this syllable. This is immortal, this is fearless. Having entered it, the <s>Devas</s> became, according to the respective qualities, immortal and fearless. //4//

children.text: START ChUp 1,4.5
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,4.5

children.text:
sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaraṃ praṇauty etad evākṣaraṃ svaram amṛtam abhayaṃ praviśati |
tat praviśya yad amṛtā devās tad amṛto bhavati || ChUp_1,4.5 ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, chants this syllable — he enters this very syllable, the <s>Svara</s>, the immortal, the fearless. Having entered it, he becomes immortal, even as the <s>Devas</s> became immortal.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,4.5 sa yo 'nyo 'pi devavadevaitadakṣaramevamamṛtamabhayaguṇaṃ vidvānpraṇauti stauti /
children.translated_text: He who, even though not a god, knowing this syllable thus as endowed with the qualities of immortality and fearlessness, chants it, praises it.

children.text: upāsanamevātra stutirabhipretā /
children.translated_text: Here, by 'praise' (<s>stuti</s>), meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) is intended.

children.text: sa tathaivaitadevākṣaraṃ svaramamṛtamabhayaṃ praviśati /
children.translated_text: He likewise enters this very syllable, the <s>Svara</s>, the immortal, the fearless.

children.text: tatpraviśya ca rājakulaṃ praviṣṭānāmiva rājño 'ntaraṅgabahiraṅgatāvanna viśiṣṭastadamṛto bhavati na nyūnatā nāpyadhikatāmṛtatva ityarthaḥ //5//
children.translated_text: And having entered it — just as for those who have entered a royal court, there is no distinction between inner and outer circles of the king — in the same way he becomes immortal; there is no inferiority nor superiority in immortality. This is the meaning. //5//

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth section of the first chapter in <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,5.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,5.1

children.text:
atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa udgītha iti |
asau vā āditya udgītha eṣa praṇavaḥ |
om iti hy eṣa svarann eti || ChUp_1,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, that which is the <s>udgītha</s> is the <s>Praṇava</s>, and that which is the <s>Praṇava</s> is the <s>udgītha</s>. Yonder sun indeed is the <s>udgītha</s>, and it is the <s>Praṇava</s>, for it moves along sounding '<s>Om</s>.'

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,5.1 prāṇādityadṛṣṭiviśiṣṭasyodgīthasyopāsanamuktamevānūdya praṇavodgīthayorekatvaṃ kṛtvā tasminprāṇaraśmibhedaguṇaviśiṣṭadṛṣṭyākṣarasyopāsanamanekaputraphalamidānīṃ vaktavyamityārabhyate-atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo bahvṛcānāṃ yaśca praṇavasteṣāṃ sa eva cchāndogya udgīthaśabdavācyaḥ /
asau vā āditya udgītha eṣa praṇavaśabdavācyo 'pi sa eva bahvṛcānāṃ nānyaḥ /
udgītha ādityaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: How is the sun the <s>udgītha</s>?

children.text: udgīthākhyamakṣaramomityetadeṣa hi yasmātsvarannuccārayannanekārthatvāddhātūnām /
children.translated_text: Because the syllable <s>Om</s>, which is called <s>udgītha</s>, is what this sun utters, sounding forth — since verbal roots have multiple meanings.

children.text: athavā svarangacchannaiti /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, moving along with sound, it goes.

children.text: ato 'sāvudgīthaḥ savitā //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore yonder sun is the <s>udgītha</s>. //1//

Having restated the previously taught meditation on the <s>udgītha</s> qualified by the visions of <s>prāṇa</s> and the sun, and having established the identity of <s>Praṇava</s> and <s>udgītha</s>, the meditation on the syllable qualified by the vision of the distinction between <s>prāṇa</s> and the rays of the sun, yielding the fruit of many sons, is now to be stated — thus begins: 'Now, that which is the <s>udgītha</s> is the <s>Praṇava</s>' of the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (followers of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>), and their <s>Praṇava</s> is that very same thing called <s>udgītha</s> by the <s>Chāndogyas</s> (followers of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>). Yonder sun indeed is the <s>udgītha</s>; and this same sun, though denoted by the word <s>Praṇava</s> among the <s>Bahvṛcas</s>, is none other.

children.text: START ChUp 1,5.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,5.2

children.text:
etam u evāham abhyagāsiṣaṃ tasmān mama tvam eko 'sīti ha kauṣītakiḥ putram uvāca |
raśmīṃs tvaṃ paryāvartayāt |
bahavo vai te bhaviṣyanti |
ity adhidaivatam || ChUp_1,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: "I have sung the praise of this one; therefore you are my only son" — thus said <s>Kauṣītaki</s> to his son. "Reflect upon the rays, and many shall be born to you." This is with reference to the deities.

children.text: ChUpBh_1,5.2 tametamu evāhamabhyagāsiṣamābhimukhyena gītavānasmyādityaraśmyabhedaṃ kṛtvā dhyānaṃ kṛtavānasmītyarthaḥ /
tena tasmātkāraṇānmama tvameko 'si putra iti ha kauṣītakiḥ kuṣītakasyāpatyaṃ kauṣītakiḥ putramuvācoktavān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for that reason, "you are my only son" — thus said <s>Kauṣītaki</s>, the descendant of <s>Kuṣītaka</s>, to his son, spoke to him.

children.text: ato raśmīnādityaṃ ca bhedena tvaṃ paryāvartayātparyāvartayetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should repeatedly contemplate the rays and the sun as distinct — 'contemplate repeatedly' is the meaning.

children.text: tvaṃyogāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with 'you.'

children.text: evaṃ bahavo vai te tava putrā bhaviṣyantītyadhi daivatam //2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, 'many indeed will be your sons' — [this is] with reference to the deity. (2)
"I have sung the praise of this one" — I have sung facing him, that is, having made the rays of the sun non-different from him, I have performed meditation — this is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 1,5.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.5.3]

children.text:
athādhyātmam |
ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇas tam udgītham upāsita |
om iti hy eṣa svarann eti || ChUp_1,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: Now, with reference to the self: 'One should meditate on the chief <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) as the <s>udgītha</s> (chanting). For this [<s>prāṇa</s>] moves along making the sound <s>Om</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.5.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,5.3 athānantaramadhyātmamucyate /
ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇastamudgīthamupāsītetyādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: 'One should meditate on the chief <s>prāṇa</s> as the <s>udgītha</s>' — and so forth, as before.

children.text: tathomiti hyeṣa prāṇo 'pi svarannetyomiti hyanujñāṃ kurvanniva vāgādipravṛttyarthametotyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'For this [<s>prāṇa</s>] too, making the sound <s>Om</s>, moves along' — meaning that, as if giving permission, it goes forth for the purpose of the activity of speech and the like — this is the meaning.

children.text: na hi maraṇakāle mumūrṣoḥ samīpasthāḥ prāṇasyoṅkāraṇaṃ śṛṇvantīti /
children.translated_text: For at the time of death, those standing near the dying person do not hear the <s>prāṇa</s> making the sound <s>Om</s>.

children.text: etatsāmānyādāditye 'pyoṅkaraṇamanujñāmātraṃ draṣṭavyam //3 //
children.translated_text: From this similarity [between <s>prāṇa</s> and the sun], the making of the <s>Om</s> sound in the sun too should be seen as merely a [metaphorical] permission. (3)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.5.3:] Now, next, with reference to the self is stated.

children.text: START ChUp 1,5.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.5.4]

children.text:
etam u evāham abhyagāsiṣaṃ tasmān mama tvam eko 'sīti ha kauṣītakiḥ putram uvāca |
prāṇāṃs tvaṃ bhūmānam abhigāyatād bahavo vai me bhaviṣyantīti || ChUp_1,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'I have sung to this [<s>prāṇa</s>]. Therefore you are my only one,' thus <s>Kauṣītaki</s> said to his son. 'You should chant to the <s>prāṇas</s> as the manifold. Many [sons] will be mine.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.5.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,5.4 etamu evāhamabhyagāsiṣityādi pūrvavadeva /
ato vāgādīnmukhyaṃ ca prāṇaṃ bhedaguṇaviśiṣṭagudgīthaṃ paśyanbhūmānaṃ manasābhigāyatāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, seeing speech and the like, and the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, as the <s>udgītha</s> qualified by the distinctive quality of difference, one should chant to the manifold with the mind.

children.text: pūrvavadāvartayetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Contemplate repeatedly' is the meaning, as before.

children.text: bahavo vai me mama putrā bhaviṣyantītyevamabhiprāyaḥ sannityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Many indeed will be my sons' — the meaning is: with this intention. Because seeing the <s>udgītha</s> through the unity of <s>prāṇa</s> and the sun results in the defect of having [only] one son, the seeing through the distinction of rays and <s>prāṇa</s> is enjoined in this section for the purpose of the fruit of having many sons. (4)

children.text: prāṇādityaikatvodgīthadṛṣṭerekaputratvaphaladoṣeṇāpoditatvādraśmiprāṇabhedadṛṣṭeḥ kartavyatā codyate 'sminkāṇḍe bahuputraphalatvārtham //4 //

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.5.4:] 'I have sung to this' — and so forth, just as before.

children.text: START ChUp 1,5.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.5.5]

children.text:
atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa udgītha iti |
hotṛṣadanād dha evāpi durudgītham anusamāharatīty anusamāharatīti || ChUp_1,5.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that which is the <s>udgītha</s> is the <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Om</s>); that which is the <s>praṇava</s> is the <s>udgītha</s>. Even from the seat of the <s>hotṛ</s> priest, one rectifies a poorly performed <s>udgītha</s> — rectifies indeed.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.5.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,5.5 atha khalu ya udgītha ityādipraṇavodgīthaikatvadarśanamapaktaṃ tasyaitatphalamāhartuṃ śakyam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.5.5:] 'Now, that which is the <s>udgītha</s>' — and so forth. The vision of the identity of <s>praṇava</s> and <s>udgītha</s> has been taught; this fruit of it can be obtained.

children.text: kiṃ taddhaivāpi durudgītaṃ duṣṭamudgītamudgānaṃ kṛtamudgātrā svakarmaṇi kṣataṃ kṛtamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is that? 'Even a poorly performed' — a defective <s>udgītha</s>, a chanting (<s>udgāna</s>) performed [with errors] — meaning that a flaw has been made by the <s>udgātṛ</s> priest in his own ritual action.

children.text: tadanusamāharatyanusandhatta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That 'he rectifies' — meaning he sets right.

children.text: cikitsayeva dhātuvaiṣamyasamīkaraṇamiti //5//
children.translated_text: Just as a physician equalizes the imbalance of the bodily humors. (5)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth section of the first chapter of <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,6.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.6.1]

children.text:
iyam evark |
agniḥ sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
iyam eva sā |
agnir amaḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'This [earth] is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>. Fire is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. This [earth] is indeed <s>Sā</s>. Fire is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,6.1 athedānīṃ sarvaphalasampattyarthamudgīthasyopāsanāntaraṃ vidhitsyate-iyameva pṛthivyṛk /
ṛci pṛthivīdṛṣṭiḥ kāryā /
tathāgniḥ sāma /
sāmnyagnidṛṣṭiḥ /
kathaṃ pṛthivyagnyor ṛksāmatvamiti /
ucyate /
tadetattadetadagnyākhyaṃ sāmaitasyāṃ pṛthivyāmṛcyadhyūḍhamadhigatamuparibhāvena sthitamityarthaḥ /
ṛcīva sāma /
tasmādata eva kāraṇādṛcyadhyūḍhameva sāma gīyata idānīmapi sāmagaiḥ /
yathā ca ṛksāmanī nātyantaṃ bhinne anyonyaṃ tathaitau pṛthivyagnidvayaṃ sāmaikaśabdābhidheyatvamāpannaṃ sāma /
children.translated_text: And just as the <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> are not utterly different from each other, so too this pair of earth and fire has come to be denoted by the single word <s>Sāma</s>.

children.text: tasmānnānyonyaṃ bhinnaṃ pṛthivyagnidvayaṃ nityasaṃśliṣṭamṛksāmanī iva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the pair of earth and fire is not different from each other — being eternally conjoined, just like the <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: tasmācca pṛthivyagnyor ṛksāmatvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, earth and fire have the nature of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: sāmākṣarayoḥ pṛthivyagnidṛṣṭividhānārthamiyameva sāgnirama iti kecit //1 //
children.translated_text: Some [say that] 'this [earth] is <s>Sā</s>, fire is <s>Ama</s>' is for the purpose of enjoining the visualization of earth and fire in the syllables of <s>Sāman</s>. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.6.1:] Now, for the purpose of obtaining the fullness of all fruits, another meditation on the <s>udgītha</s> is intended to be enjoined. 'This earth indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>' — the visualization of the earth as the <s>Ṛc</s> is to be practiced. Likewise, 'Fire is the <s>Sāman</s>' — the visualization of fire as the <s>Sāman</s>. How [is it possible that] earth and fire have the nature of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>? It is explained: 'This — this <s>Sāman</s> called fire is superimposed on (<s>adhyūḍham</s>) this earth, which is the <s>Ṛc</s>' — meaning it is placed above, stationed in a higher position. The <s>Sāman</s> is as if on the <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore, for this very reason, the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>, even now by the <s>Sāman</s> chanters.

children.text: START ChUp 1,6.2-3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.6.2-3]

children.text:
antarikṣam evark |
vāyuḥ sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
antarikṣam eva sā |
vāyur amaḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'The sky (<s>antarikṣa</s>) is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>. Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>) is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. The sky is indeed <s>Sā</s>. Wind is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.2)

children.text:
dyaur evark |
ādityaḥ sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
dyaur eva sā |
ādityo 'maḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Heaven (<s>Dyaus</s>) is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>. The sun (<s>Āditya</s>) is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. Heaven is indeed <s>Sā</s>. The sun is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,6.2,3 antarikṣamevargvāyuḥ sāmetyādi pūrvavat //2-3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.6.2-3:] 'The sky is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>, wind is the <s>Sāman</s>' — and so forth, as before. (2-3)

children.text: START ChUp 1,6.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.6.4]

children.text:
nakṣatrāny evark |
candramāḥ sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
nakṣatrāṇy eva sā |
candramā amaḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,6.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'The stars (<s>nakṣatras</s>) are indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>. The moon (<s>Candramā</s>) is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. The stars are indeed <s>Sā</s>. The moon is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,6.4 nakṣatrāṇāmadhipatiścandramā ataḥ sa sāma //4 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.6.4:] The moon is the lord of the stars; therefore it is the <s>Sāman</s>. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 1,6.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.6.5]

children.text:
atha yad etad ādityasya śuklaṃ bhāḥ saivark |
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tat sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmad ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate || ChUp_1,6.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that which is the white radiance of the sun — that is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>. And that which is dark, exceedingly black — that is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,6.5 atha yadetadādityasya śuklaṃ bhāḥ śuklā dīptiḥ saivarka /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.6.5:] Now, that which is the white radiance (<s>bhāḥ</s>) — the white brightness — of the sun, that is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>.

children.text: atha yadāditye nīlaṃ paraḥ kṛṣṇaṃ paro 'tiśayena kārṣṇyaṃ tatsāma /
children.translated_text: And that which in the sun is dark, exceedingly black — meaning supremely black in its darkness — that is the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: taddhyekāntasamāhitadṛṣṭerdṛśyate //5 //
children.translated_text: For that [darkness] is seen by one whose vision is entirely concentrated in meditation. (5)

children.text: START ChUp 1,6.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.6.6]

children.text:
atha yad evaitad ādityasya śuklaṃ bhāḥ saiva sā |
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tad amaḥ |
tat sāma |
atha ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate hiraṇyaśmaśrur hiraṇyakeśa ā praṇakhāt sarva eva suvarnaḥ || ChUp_1,6.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that very white radiance of the sun — that is <s>Sā</s>. And that which is dark, exceedingly black — that is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>. Now, this golden person (<s>puruṣa</s>) who is seen within the sun, with golden beard, golden hair, golden altogether to the very tips of his nails.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,6.6 te evaite bhāḥ śuklakṛṣṇatve sā cāmaśca sāma /
atha ya eṣo 'ntarāditye ādityasyāntarmadhye hiraṇmayo hiraṇmaya iva hiraṇmayaḥ /
na hi suvarṇavikāratvaṃ devasya sambhavati /
ṛksāmageṣṇatvāpahatapāpmatvāsambhavāt /
na hi sauvarṇe 'cetane pāpmādiprāptirasti yena pratiṣidhyeta /
cākṣuṣe cāgrahaṇāt /
ato luptopama eva hiraṇmayaśabdo jyotirmaya ityarthaḥ /
uttareṣavapi samānā yojanā /
puruṣaḥ puri śayanātpūrayati vā svenā'tmanā jagaditi /
dṛśyate nivṛttacakṣurbhiḥ samāhitacetobhirbrahmacaryādisādhanāpekṣam /
children.translated_text: 'He is seen' — by those whose eyes are withdrawn [from external objects], whose minds are concentrated — [but this seeing] depends on means such as celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) and the like.

children.text: tejasvino 'pi śmaśrukeśādayaḥ kṛṣṇāḥ syurityato viśinaṣṭi-hiraṇyaśmaśrurhiraṇyakeśa iti /
children.translated_text: Even radiant [beings] may have dark beards, hair, and the like — therefore he specifies: 'with golden beard, golden hair.'

children.text: jyotirmayānyevāsya śmaśrūṇi keśāścetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Meaning that his beards and hair are indeed made of light.

children.text: āpraṇakhātpraṇakho nakhāgraṃ nakhāgreṇa saha sarvaḥ suvarṇa iva bhārūpa ityarthaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: 'To the very tips of his nails' — <s>praṇakha</s> means the tip of the nail — meaning that together with the tip of his nails, he is entirely golden, as if made of radiance. (6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.6.6:] Those very radiances — the white and dark properties — are <s>Sā</s> and <s>Ama</s>, [hence] <s>Sāma</s>. Now, this person who is within the sun — in the interior of the sun — golden, as if made of gold. For it is not possible that the deity is actually a modification of gold, because of the impossibility of being the weaver of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, being free from evil, and so forth. For in something made of gold and insentient, there is no arising of evil and the like that would need to be negated. And because it is not apprehended by the eye [as literal gold]. Therefore the word 'golden' (<s>hiraṇmaya</s>) is an elliptical simile, meaning 'light-formed' (<s>jyotirmaya</s>). The same construction applies in the later [passages] as well. '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — because he sleeps in the city (<s>puri</s>), or because he fills the world with his own self.

children.text: START ChUp 1,6.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.6.7]

children.text:
tasya yathā kapyāsaṃ puṇḍarīkam evam akṣiṇī |
tasyod iti nāma |
sa eṣa sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhya uditaḥ |
udeti ha vai sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhyo ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_1,6.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'His eyes are like a red lotus blooming on a monkey's seat. His name is <s>Ut</s> (the risen one). He has risen above all evils. Indeed, he who knows thus rises above all evils.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.7)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,6.7 tasyaivaṃ sarvataḥ suvarṇavarṇasyāpyakṣṇorvaśeṣaḥ /
kathaṃ?tasya yathā kapermarkaṭasyā'saḥ kapyāsaḥ /
āserupaveśanārthasya karaṇe ghañ /
kapipṛṣṭhānto yenopaviśati /
kapyāsa iva puṇḍarīkamatyantatejasvyevamasya devasyākṣiṇī /
upamitopamānatvānna hīnopamā /
tasyaivaṅguṇaviśiṣṭasya gauṇamidaṃ nāmoditi /
kathaṃ gauṇatvam /
sa eṣa devaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhyaḥ pāpmanā saha tatkāryebhya ityarthaḥ /
ya ātmāpahatapāpmetyādi vakṣyati /
udita ud ita udgata ityarthaḥ /
ato 'sāvunnāmā /
children.translated_text: Therefore he is named '<s>Ut</s>' (the risen one).

children.text: tamevaṅguṇasampannamunnāmānaṃ yathoktena prakāreṇa yo veda so 'pyevamevodetyudgacchati sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who knows this deity, endowed with such qualities, named '<s>Ut</s>,' in the manner described — he too likewise rises, ascends from all evils.

children.text: ha vā ityavadhāraṇārthau nipātau /
children.translated_text: The particles <s>ha</s> and <s>vā</s> are for the purpose of emphasis.

children.text: udetyevetyarthaḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: 'He rises indeed' — this is the meaning. (7)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.6.7:] Of this [person] who is of golden color throughout, there is a distinguishing feature regarding the eyes. How? 'Of a monkey (<s>kapi</s>) — its seat (<s>āsa</s>)' is <s>kapyāsa</s>. <s>Āsa</s> [from the root <s>ās</s>] meaning 'to sit,' takes the <s>ghañ</s> suffix in the instrumental sense. The posterior of a monkey — that by which it sits — is the <s>kapyāsa</s>. A lotus [blooming] like a <s>kapyāsa</s>, exceedingly luminous — such are the eyes of this deity. Because the compared [eyes] are compared to the standard of comparison [lotus], the simile is not a degrading one. Of this [deity] thus qualified, this is the secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) name '<s>Ut</s>.' How is [the name] secondary? 'This deity has risen (<s>udita</s>) from all evils' — meaning from evil and its effects — as will be stated: 'the self free from evil' and so forth. <s>Udita</s> means '<s>ut-ita</s>' — gone upward, meaning risen.

children.text: START ChUp 1,6.8
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.6.8]

children.text:
tasyark ca sāma ca geṣṇau |
tasmād udgīthaḥ |
tasmāt tv eva udgātā |
etasya hi gātā |
sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmāt parāñco lokās teṣāṃ ceṣṭa devakāmānāṃ ca |
ity adhidaivatam || ChUp_1,6.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Ṛc</s> and the <s>Sāman</s> are his two songs. Therefore he is the <s>Udgītha</s>. Therefore indeed he is the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter). For he is the singer of this. He is the lord of the worlds that are beyond that [sun] and of the desires of the gods.' — [This is] with reference to the deity. (<s>ChUp</s> 1.6.8)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,6.8 tasyodgīthatvaṃ devasyā'dityādīnāmiva vivakṣitatvādāha-tasyarkca sāma ca geṣṇau pṛthivyādyuktalakṣaṇe parvaṇī /
sarvātmā hi devaḥ /
parāparalokakāmeśitṛtvādupapadyate pṛthivyagnyṛksāmageṣṇatvam /
sarvayonitvācca /
yata evamunnāmācāsāvṛksāmageṣṇaśca tasmādṛksāmageṣṇatvaprāptamudgīthatvamucyate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyatvāddevasya tasmādudgītha iti /
tasmāttaveva hetorudaṃ gāyatītyudgātā /
yasmāddhyetasya yathoktasyonnāmno gātāsāvato yuktodgāteti nāmaprasiddhirudgātuḥ /
children.translated_text: Since this singer is indeed the singer of the one named '<s>Ut</s>' as described, therefore the well-known naming of the <s>Udgātṛ</s> as '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' is justified.

children.text: sa eṣa deva unnāmā ye cāmuṣmādādityātparāñcaḥ parāgañcanādūrdhvā lokāsteṣāṃ lokānāṃ ceṣṭe na kevalamīśitṛtvameva caśabdāddhārayati ca /
children.translated_text: This deity named '<s>Ut</s>' is the lord of the worlds that are beyond this sun — the worlds that go upward from the sun — and not merely the lord [of those worlds]; the word 'and' [indicates that] he also supports [them].

children.text: "sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyāmutemām"ityādimantravarṇāt /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the mantra text: 'He upheld the earth and this heaven.'

children.text: kiñca devakāmānāmīṣṭa ityetadadhidaivataṃ devatāviṣayaṃ devasyodgīthasya svarūpamuktam //8//
children.translated_text: Moreover, he is the lord of the desires of the gods — this is the form of the deity's <s>udgītha</s> with reference to the deity, as stated. (8)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.6.8:] Because the <s>udgītha</s>-hood of the deity is intended [to be stated], just as [that] of the sun and the like, he says: 'The <s>Ṛc</s> and the <s>Sāman</s> are his two songs (<s>geṣṇau</s>)' — the two wings characterized as earth and the like as previously stated. For the deity is the self of all. Because of being the lord of the worlds near and far, the nature of being the weaver of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> of earth and fire is appropriate. And because of being the source of all. Because he is thus the risen one and the weaver of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>udgītha</s>-hood that follows from being the weaver of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> is expressed indirectly — because the deity is fond of the indirect — therefore [he is called] <s>Udgītha</s>. For this very reason, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> [is so called because] he chants this [<s>Ud</s>].

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhyāyasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth section of the first chapter of <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.7.1]

children.text:
athādhyātmam |
vāg evark |
prāṇaḥ sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
vāg eva sā |
prāṇo 'maḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, with reference to the self: Speech indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. Speech is indeed <s>Sā</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.7.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,7.1 athādhunādhyātmamucyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.7.1:] Now, with reference to the self is stated.

children.text: vāgevarkprāṇaḥ sāma /
children.translated_text: Speech indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: adharoparisthānatvasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the commonality of being situated below and above [respectively].

children.text: prāṇo ghrāṇamucyate saha vāyunā, vāgeva sā prāṇo 'ma ityādi pūrvavat //1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> here refers to the sense of smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>) together with the wind. 'Speech is indeed <s>Sā</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> is <s>Ama</s>' — and so forth, as before. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.7.2]

children.text:
cakṣur evark |
ātmā sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
cakṣur eva sā |
ātmāmaḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'The eye indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>. The self (<s>ātman</s>) is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. The eye is indeed <s>Sā</s>. The self is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.7.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,7.2 cakṣurevargātmā sāma /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.7.2:] The eye indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>; the self (<s>ātman</s>) is the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: ātmeti cchāyātmā tatsthatvātsāma //2 //
children.translated_text: 'The self' means the shadow-self; because of being situated in it, [it is] the <s>Sāman</s>. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.7.3]

children.text:
śrotram evark |
manaḥ sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
śrotram eva sā |
mano 'maḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,7.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'The ear indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>. The mind (<s>manas</s>) is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. The ear is indeed <s>Sā</s>. The mind is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.7.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,7.3 śrotramevarṅmanaḥ sāma, śrotrasyādhiṣṭhātṛtvānmanasaḥ sāmatvam //3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.7.3:] The ear indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>; the mind is the <s>Sāman</s>. Because the mind presides over the ear, the <s>Sāman</s>-hood of the mind [is established]. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.7.4]

children.text:
atha yad etad akṣnaḥ śuklaṃ bhāḥ saivark |
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tat sāma |
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma |
tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate |
atha yad evaitad akṣṇaḥ śuklaṃ bhāḥ saiva sā |
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tad amaḥ |
tat sāma || ChUp_1,7.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that which is the white radiance of the eye — that is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>. And that which is dark, exceedingly black — that is the <s>Sāman</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on this <s>Ṛc</s>. Therefore the <s>Sāman</s> is sung as superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>. Now, that very white radiance of the eye — that is <s>Sā</s>. And that which is dark, exceedingly black — that is <s>Ama</s>. That is <s>Sāma</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.7.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,7.4 atha yadetadakṣṇaḥ śuklaṃ bhāḥ saivarka /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.7.4:] Now, that which is the white radiance of the eye — that is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>.

children.text: atha yannīlaṃ paraḥ kṛṣṇamāditya iva dṛkśaktyadhiṣṭhānaṃ tatsāma //4 //
children.translated_text: And that which is dark, exceedingly black — the seat of the visual power, like the sun — that is the <s>Sāman</s>. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.7.5]

children.text:
atha ya eṣo 'ntar akṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate saivark |
tat sāma |
tad uktham |
tad yajuḥ |
tad brahma |
tasya etasya tad eva rūpaṃ yad amuṣya rūpam |
yāv amuṣya geṣṇau tau tau goṣṇau |
yan nāma tan nāma || ChUp_1,7.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, this person (<s>puruṣa</s>) who is seen within the eye — he is indeed the <s>Ṛc</s>. He is the <s>Sāman</s>. He is the <s>Uktha</s>. He is the <s>Yajus</s>. He is <s>Brahman</s>. The form of this one is the same as the form of that one [in the sun]. The songs of that one are the songs of this one. The name of that one is the name of this one.' (<s>ChUp</s> 1.7.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,7.5 atha ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate /
pūrvavat /
saivargadhyātmaṃ vāgādyā pṛthivyādyā cādhidaivatam /
prasiddhā ca ṛkpādabaddhākṣarātmikā /
tathā sāma /
ukthasāhacaryādvā stotraṃ sāmokthaṃ śastram /
ukthādanyat tathā yajuḥ svāhāsvadhāvaṣaḍādi sarvameva vāgyajustatsa eva /
sarvātmakatvātsarvayonitvācceti hyavocāma /
ṛgādiprakaraṇāttadbrahmeti trayo vedāḥ /
tasyaitasya cākṣuṣasya puruṣasya tadeva rūpamatidiśyate /
kiṃ tadyadamuṣyā'dityapuruṣasya /
hiraṇmaya ityādi yadadhidaivatamuktam /
yāvamuṣya geṣṇau parvaṇī tāvevāsyāpi cākṣuṣasya geṣṇau /
yaccāmuṣya nāmodityudgītha iti ca tadevāsya nāma /
sthānabhedādrūpagiṇanāmātideśādīśitṛtvaviṣayabhedavyapadeśāccā'dityacākṣuṣayorbheda iti cet /
na /
amunānenaivetyekasyobhayātmaprāptyanupapatteḥ /
dvidhābhāvenopapadyata iti cet /
vakṣyati hi sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavatītyādi /
na /
cetanasyaikasya niravayavatvāddvidhābhāvānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because it is impossible for a single conscious being, being without parts, to become twofold.

children.text: tasmādadhyātmādhidaivatayorekatvameva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is indeed oneness of the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) and the cosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) [aspects].

children.text: yattu rūpādyatideśo bhedakāraṇamavoco na tadbhedāvagamāya /
children.translated_text: As for the superimposition of form and the like that we mentioned as a cause of difference — that is not for the purpose of establishing difference.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi sthānabhedādbhedāśaṅkā mā bhūdityevamartham //5 //
children.translated_text: Rather, it is for this purpose: 'Let there not be a suspicion of difference due to the difference of locus.' [End of section 5.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad-bhāṣya</s> 1.7.5] Now, the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) who is seen within the eye — as before [the same explanation applies]. The same <s>Ṛc</s> [consists of] the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) aspects such as speech and the cosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) aspects such as earth, which are well-known. And the <s>Ṛc</s>, consisting of syllables bound in metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>), is well-known. Likewise the <s>Sāman</s>. Or, because of its association with the <s>Uktha</s>, the hymn of praise (<s>stotra</s>) is the <s>Sāman</s>, and the <s>Uktha</s> is the recitation (<s>śastra</s>). Other than the <s>Uktha</s>, whatever [is recited with] <s>svāhā</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, <s>vaṣaṭ</s>, and so forth — all of that is speech, and is <s>Yajus</s> — that is he himself. Because he is the self of all and the source of all — thus indeed we have said. From the context of the <s>Ṛc</s> and the rest, that is <s>Brahman</s> — [namely] the three <s>Veda</s>s. Of this person in the eye, that very form is superimposed (<s>atidiśyate</s>). What is it? That which belongs to that person in the sun — 'golden' and so forth — what was stated regarding the cosmic [aspect]. The two joints at his cheeks are just like those [of the solar person]. And what was stated as the name of that [solar person] — '<s>Udgītha</s>' — that very same is the name of this [person in the eye]. [Objection:] Because of the difference of locus, the enumeration of forms, the superimposition, and the designation of different domains of rulership, there is a difference between the solar and the ocular [persons]. [Reply:] No. Because it is impossible for one [entity] to attain both natures through [the phrases] 'by that one' and 'by this one.' [Objection:] If [you say] it is possible through a twofold division — for it will be said: 'He becomes one, he becomes threefold,' and so forth — [Reply:] No.

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.6
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.7.6]

children.text:
sa eṣa ye caitasmād arvāñco lokās teṣāṃ ceṣṭe manuṣyakāmānāṃ ceti |
tad ya ime vīṇāyāṃ gāyanty etaṃ te gāyanti |
tasmāt te dhanasanayaḥ || ChUp_1,7.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who is this [person in the eye] — he rules over the worlds that are below him, and over the desires of men. Therefore, those who sing to the <s>vīṇā</s> sing of him; therefore they are winners of wealth.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.7.6]

children.text: ChUpBh_1,7.6 sa eṣa cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣo ye caitasmādādhyātmikādātmanor'vāñcor'vāggatā lokāsteṣāṃ ceṣṭe manuṣyasambandhināṃ ca kāmānām /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.7.6] He who is this person in the eye — the worlds that have gone below, that are below, from this individual self (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) — he rules over them and over the desires connected with human beings.

children.text: tatsmādya ime vīṇāyāṃ gāyanti gāyakasta etameva gāyanti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who sing to the <s>vīṇā</s> — those singers sing of him alone.

children.text: yasmādīśvaraṃ gāyanti tasmātte dhanasanayo dhanalābhayuktā dhanavanta utyarthaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: Since they sing of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), therefore they are 'winners of wealth' — that is, endowed with the acquisition of wealth, meaning they become wealthy. [End of section 6.]

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.7
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.7.7]

children.text:
atha ya etad evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyaty ubhau sa gāyati |
so 'munaiva sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmāt parāñco lokās tāṃś cāpnoti devakāmāṃś ca || ChUp_1,7.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, one who, knowing this thus, sings the <s>Sāman</s> — he sings of both [the solar and the ocular persons]. Through that one [the solar person], he who is this [person in the eye] — he obtains the worlds that are beyond that one, and the desires of the gods.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.7.7]

children.text: ChUpBh_1,7.7 atha ya etadevaṃ vidvānyathoktaṃ devamudgīthaṃ vidvānsāma gāyatyubhau sa gāyati cākṣuṣamādityaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.7.7] Now, one who, knowing this as described — knowing the divine <s>Udgītha</s> — sings the <s>Sāman</s>, he sings of both — the one in the eye and the one in the sun.

children.text: tasyaivaṃvidaḥ phalamucyateso 'munaivā'dityena sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmātparāñco lokāstāṃścā'pnoti ādityāntargatadevo bhūtvetyartho devakāmāṃśca //7 //
children.translated_text: The fruit of such a knower is stated: through that one, the solar [person] — he who is this [person in the eye] — he obtains the worlds that are beyond that [solar person] — meaning he becomes a deity dwelling within the sun — and the desires of the gods. [End of section 7.]

children.text: START ChUp 1,7.8-9
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.7.8-9]

children.text:
athānenaiva ye caitasmād arvāñco lokās tāṃś cāpnoti manuṣyakāmāṃś ca |
tasmād u haivaṃvid udgātā brūyāt || ChUp_1,7.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'And through this one [the person in the eye] — he obtains the worlds that are below this one, and the desires of men. Therefore, indeed, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows this should say —' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.7.8]

children.text:
kaṃ te kāmam āgāyānīti |
eṣa hy eva kāmāgānasyeṣṭe ya evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyati sāma gāyati || ChUp_1,7.9 ||
children.translated_text: '"What desire shall I sing for you?" For he indeed is the master of singing desires — one who, knowing this, sings the <s>Sāman</s>, sings the <s>Sāman</s>.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.7.9]

children.text: ChUpBh_1,7.8 athānenaiva cākṣuṣeṇaiva ye caitasmādarvāñco lokāstāṃścā'pnoti manuṣyakāmāṃśca cākṣuṣo bhūtvetyarthaḥ /
tasmādu haivaṃvidudgātā brūyādyajamānaṃ kamiṣṭaṃ te tava kāmamāgāyānīti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, indeed, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows this should say to the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>): 'What desired thing shall I sing for you?'

children.text: eṣa hi yasmādudgātā kāmāgānasyodgānena kāmaṃ sampādayitumīṣṭe samartha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For this is the reason: the <s>Udgātṛ</s> is the master of singing desires — meaning he is capable of accomplishing the desire through his chanting (<s>udgāna</s>).

children.text: ko 'sau?ya evaṃ vidvānsāma gāyati sāma gāyati /
children.translated_text: Who is that? One who, knowing this, sings the <s>Sāman</s>, sings the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: dviruktirupāsanasamāptyarthā //8-9 //
children.translated_text: The repetition [of 'sings the <s>Sāman</s>'] is for the purpose of concluding the meditation (<s>upāsana</s>). [End of sections 8-9.]
[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.7.8] And through this one — the person in the eye alone — he obtains the worlds that are below this one, and the desires of men — meaning he becomes the one in the eye.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the first chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> with <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s commentary.

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.1]

children.text:
trayo hodgīthe kuśalā babhūvuḥ śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyano dālbhyaḥ pravāhaṇo jaivalir iti |
te hocur udgīthe vai kuśalāḥ smo hantodgīthe kathāṃ vadāma iti || ChUp_1,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Three [persons] were skilled in the <s>Udgītha</s>: <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s>, <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>, and <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s>. They said: "We are skilled in the <s>Udgītha</s>. Come, let us have a discussion about the <s>Udgītha</s>."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.1]

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,8.1 anekadhopāsyatvādakṣarasya prakārāntareṇa parovarīyastvaguṇaphalamupāsanāntaramānināya /
itihāsastu sukhāvabodhanārthaḥ /
trayastrisaṃkhyākāḥ /
ha, ityaitihyārthaḥ /
udgītha udgīthajñānaṃ prati kuśalā nipuṇā babhūvuḥ /
kasmiṃściddeśe kāle ca nimitte vā sametānāmityabhiprāyaḥ /
na hi sarvasmiñjagati trayāṇāmeva kauśalamudgīthādivijñāne /
śrūyante hyuṣastijānaśrutikaikeyaprabhṛtayaḥ sarvajñakalpāḥ /
ke te traya ityāha-śilako nāmataḥ śalāvato 'patyaṃ śālāvatyaḥ /
cikitāyanasyāpatyaṃ caikitāyanaḥ /
dalbhagotro dālbhyo dvyāmuṣyāyaṇo vā /
pravāhaṇo nāmato jīvalasyāpatyaṃ jaivalirityete trayaste hocuranyonyamudgīthe vai kuśalā nipuṇā iti prasiddhāḥ smaḥ /
ato hanta yadyanumatirbhavatāmudgītha udgīthajñānanimittāṃ kathāṃ vicāraṇāṃ pakṣapratipakṣopanyāsena vadāmo vādaṃ kurma ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'Come! — if it meets with your approval — let us have a discussion (<s>kathā</s>), that is, a deliberation occasioned by the knowledge of the <s>Udgītha</s>, by presenting thesis and counter-thesis (<s>pakṣa-pratipakṣa</s>) — meaning, let us hold a debate.'

children.text: tathā ca tadvidyasaṃvāde viparītagrahaṇanāśo 'pūrvavijñānopajanaḥ saṃśayanivṛttiśceti /
children.translated_text: And thus, in the discourse of those who know the same subject, the removal of wrong apprehension, the arising of new knowledge, and the resolution of doubt [take place].

children.text: atastadvidyasaṃyogaḥ kartavya iti cetihāsaprayojanam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, association with those who know the same subject ought to be pursued — this is the purpose of the narrative (<s>itihāsa</s>).

children.text: dṛśyate hi śilakādīnām //1 //
children.translated_text: For this is seen [in the case of] <s>Śilaka</s> and the others. [End of section 1.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.8.1] Because the syllable [<s>Om</s>] can be meditated upon in many ways, [the text] introduces another meditation with the quality of increasing excellence as its fruit. The narrative (<s>itihāsa</s>) is for the purpose of easy comprehension. 'Three' means three in number. 'Ha' indicates traditional report (<s>aitihya</s>). [They were] skilled, that is, proficient regarding the knowledge of the <s>Udgītha</s>. The meaning is that [they] came together at some place, time, or occasion. For it is not the case that in the entire world only three were skilled in the knowledge of the <s>Udgītha</s> and such [matters]. For <s>Uṣasti</s>, <s>Jānaśruti</s>, <s>Kaikeya</s>, and others who were practically omniscient are heard of [in scripture]. Who are these three? He says: <s>Śilaka</s> by name, the offspring of <s>Śalāvat</s>, hence <s>Śālāvatya</s>. The offspring of <s>Cikitāyana</s>, hence <s>Caikitāyana</s>. Of the <s>Dalbha</s> lineage, hence <s>Dālbhya</s> — or he may have a double patronymic. <s>Pravāhaṇa</s> by name, the offspring of <s>Jīvala</s>, hence <s>Jaivali</s>. These three — they said to one another: 'We are indeed well-known as skilled, that is, proficient in the <s>Udgītha</s>.'

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.2]

children.text:
tatheti ha samupaviviśuḥ |
sa ha prāvahaṇo jaivalir uvāca |
bhagavantāv agre vadatām |
bhrāmaṇayor vadator vācaṃ śroṣyāmīti || ChUp_1,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: '"So be it," they said, and sat down together. Then <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said: "Let the two venerable ones speak first. I shall listen to the words of two <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s speaking."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.2]

children.text: ChUpBh_1,8.2 tathetyuktvā te samupaviviśurhepaviṣṭavantaḥ kila /
tatra rājñaḥ prāgalbhyopapatteḥ sa ha pravāhaṇo jaivaliruvācetarau"bhagavantau pūjāvantāvagre pūrvaṃ vadatām" /
children.translated_text: There, since boldness befits a king — <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said to the other two: 'Let the two venerable ones — the honorable ones — speak first.'

children.text: brāhmaṇayoriti liṅgādrājāsau /
children.translated_text: From the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>s' [used to describe the other two], it is indicated that he [<s>Pravāhaṇa</s>] was a king.

children.text: yuvayorbrāhmaṇayorvadatorvācaṃ śroṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: 'I shall listen to the words of you two <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s as you speak.'

children.text: artharahitāmityapare vācamiti viśeṣaṇāt //2 //
children.translated_text: Others [say the word] '<s>vācam</s>' (speech) [here means] 'devoid of substance' — [this is inferred] from the qualifying word. [End of section 2.]
[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.8.2] Having said 'so be it,' they sat down together — they seated themselves, indeed.

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.3]

children.text:
sa ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvāca hanta tvā pṛcchānīti |
pṛccheti hovāca || ChUp_1,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s> said to <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>: "Come, let me question you." "Question," he said.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_1,8.3 uktayoḥ sa ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaścaikitāyanaṃ dālbhyamuvāca-"hanta yadyanumaṃsyase tvā tvāṃ pṛcchānī"tyukta itaraḥ"pṛcche"ti hovāca //3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.8.3] When [both were] thus addressed, <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s> said to <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>: 'Come, if you will agree — let me question you.' Thus addressed, the other said: 'Question.' [End of section 3.]

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.4
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.4]

children.text:
kā sāmno gatir iti |
svara iti hovāca |
svarasya kā gatir iti |
prāṇa iti hovāca |
annasya kā gatir iti |
annam iti hovāca |
annasya kā gatir iti |
āpa iti hovāca || ChUp_1,8.4 ||
children.translated_text: '"What is the support (<s>gati</s>) of the <s>Sāman</s>?" "Tone (<s>svara</s>)," he said. "What is the support of tone?" "<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath)," he said. "What is the support of <s>Prāṇa</s>?" "Food (<s>anna</s>)," he said. "What is the support of food?" "Water (<s>āpas</s>)," he said.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.4]

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,8.4 labdhānumatirāha-kā sāmnaḥ, prakṛtatvādudgīthasya /
udgītho hyatropāsyatvena prakṛtaḥ /
"parovarīyāṃsamudgītham"iti ca vakṣyati /
gatirāśrayaḥ parāyaṇamityetat /
evaṃ pṛṣṭo dālbhya uvāca-svara iti /
svarātmakatvātsāmnaḥ /
yo yadātmakaḥ sa tadgatistadāśrayaśca bhavatīti yuktaṃ mṛdāśraya iva ghaṭādiḥ /
svarasya kā gatiriti, prāṇa iti hovāca /
prāṇaniṣpādyo hi svarastasmātsavarasya prāṇo gatiḥ /
prāṇasya kā gatirityannamiti hovāca /
annāvaṣṭambho hi prāṇaḥ /
"śuṣyati vai prāṇa ṛte 'nnāt"iti hi śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: For there is the <s>śruti</s> (scripture): '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed dries up without food.'

children.text: "annaṃ dāma"iti ca /
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>]: 'Food is the bond (<s>dāman</s>).'

children.text: annasya kā gatirityāpa iti hovāca /
children.translated_text: 'What is the support of food?' 'Water (<s>āpas</s>),' he said.

children.text: apsambhavatvādannasya //4 //
children.translated_text: Because food originates from water. [End of section 4.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.8.4] Having obtained permission, he asks: 'What is [the support] of the <s>Sāman</s>?' — because the <s>Udgītha</s> is the subject under discussion. For the <s>Udgītha</s> is here presented as the object of meditation. And it will be said: 'The most excellent <s>Udgītha</s>.' '<s>Gati</s>' means support, refuge — that is the meaning. Thus questioned, <s>Dālbhya</s> said: 'Tone (<s>svara</s>).' Because the <s>Sāman</s> has tone as its essence. That which has something as its essence, has that as its support and refuge — this is reasonable, just as a pot and the like have clay as their support. 'What is the support of tone?' '<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath),' he said. For tone is produced by breath; therefore breath is the support of tone. 'What is the support of <s>Prāṇa</s>?' 'Food (<s>anna</s>),' he said. For <s>Prāṇa</s> is sustained by food.

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.5
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.5]

children.text:
apāṃ kā gatir iti |
asau loka iti hovāca |
amuṣya lokasya kā gatir iti |
na svargaṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca |
svargaṃ vayaṃ lokaṃ sāmābhisaṃsthāpayāmaḥ |
svargasaṃstāvaṃ hi sāmeti || ChUp_1,8.5 ||
children.translated_text: '"What is the support of water?" "That world [the heavenly world]," he said. "What is the support of that world?" "One should not lead the <s>Sāman</s> beyond the heavenly world," he said. "We establish the <s>Sāman</s> in the heavenly world. For the <s>Sāman</s> is praised as heaven."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.5]

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,8.5 apāṃ kā gatirityasau loka iti /
amuṣmāllokādvṛṣṭiḥ sambhavati /
amuṣya lokasya kā gatiriti pṛṣṭo dālbhya uvāca-svargamamuṃ lokamatītyāśrayāntaraṃ sāma na nayetkaściditi hovācā'ha /
children.translated_text: 'What is the support of that world?' — thus questioned, <s>Dālbhya</s> said: 'No one should lead the <s>Sāman</s> beyond that world, the heavenly world, to another support.'

children.text: ato vayamapi svargaṃ lokaṃ sāmābhisaṃsthāpayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, we too establish the <s>Sāman</s> in the heavenly world.

children.text: svargalokapratiṣṭhaṃ sāma jānīma ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: We know the <s>Sāman</s> as having the heavenly world as its foundation — that is the meaning.

children.text: svargasaṃstāvaṃ svargatvena saṃstavanaṃ saṃstāvo yasya tatsāma svargasaṃstāvaṃ hi yasmāt"svargo vai lokaḥ sāmaveda"iti śrutiḥ //5 //
children.translated_text: 'Praised as heaven' (<s>svarga-saṃstāva</s>) — that whose praise (<s>saṃstava</s>) is as heaven — that is the <s>Sāman</s> which is 'praised as heaven.' For the <s>śruti</s> says: 'The heavenly world indeed is the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.' [End of section 5.]
[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.8.5] 'What is the support of water?' 'That world [the heavenly world].' For rain originates from that [heavenly] world.

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.6
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.6]

children.text:
taṃ ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvācāpratiṣṭhitaṃ vai kila te dālbhya sāma |
yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti || ChUp_1,8.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s> said to <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>: "Your <s>Sāman</s>, O <s>Dālbhya</s>, is indeed without a firm foundation. If anyone were to say now, 'Your head shall fall off,' your head would indeed fall off."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.6]

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,8.6 tamitaraḥ śilakaḥ śālāvatyaścaikitāyanaṃ dālbhyamuvāca-apratiṣṭhitamasaṃsthitaṃ parovarīyastvenāsamāptagati sāmetyarthaḥ /
vā ityāgamaṃ smārayati kileti ca, dālbhya te tava sāma /
yastvasahiṣṇuḥ sāmavidetarhyetasminkāle brūyātkaścidviparītavijñānamapratiṣṭhitaṃ sāma pratiṣṭhitamityevaṃvādāparādhinaṃ mūrdhā śiraste vipatiṣyati vispaṣṭaṃ patiṣyatīti /
evamuktasyāparādhinastathaiva tadvipatenna saṃśayo na tvāhaṃ bravīmītyabhiprāyaḥ /
nanu mūrdhapātār'haṃ cedaparādhaṃ kṛtavānataḥ pareṇānuktasyāpi patenmūrdhā;na cedaparādhyuktasyāpi naiva patati /
anyathākṛtābhyāgamaḥ kṛtanāśaśca syātām /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be [the faults of] the occurrence of what was not done and the destruction of what was done.

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ śubhāśubhasya phalaprāpterdeśakālanimittāpekṣatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the fruition of actions — whether good or bad — depends on [the proper conjunction of] place, time, and occasion.

children.text: tatraivaṃ sati mūrdhapātanimittasyāpyajñānasya parābhivyāhāranimittāpekṣatvamiti //6 //
children.translated_text: This being so, the ignorance that is the occasion for the head falling also depends on the occasion of being declared by another. [End of section 6.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.8.6] Then the other, <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s>, said to <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>: 'Your <s>Sāman</s> is without a firm foundation — meaning its progression toward the most excellent [support] is incomplete.' 'Vai' recalls the scripture, and 'kila' [is a particle of emphasis]. 'O <s>Dālbhya</s>, your <s>Sāman</s>.' 'If anyone who cannot endure [criticism], [holding] the wrong notion that the <s>Sāman</s> without foundation is [actually] well-founded — if someone at this present time were to say, on account of holding such a wrong view: "Your head shall fall off — shall clearly fall" — then it would indeed fall off, for one who has committed such an error. There is no doubt about that — but I am not the one saying it.' That is the purport. [Objection:] If he deserves to have his head fall off because he committed an error, then even without being told by another, his head should fall. And if he has not committed an error, it should not fall even when told.

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.7
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.7]

children.text:
hantāham etad bhagavatto vedānīti |
viddhīti hovāca |
amuṣya lokasya kā gatir iti |
ayaṃ loka iti hovāca |
asya lokasya kā gatir iti |
na pratiṣṭhāṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca |
pratiṣṭhāṃ vayaṃ lokaṃ sāmābhisaṃsthāpayāmaḥ |
pratiṣṭhāsaṃstāvaṃ hi sāmeti || ChUp_1,8.7 ||
children.translated_text: '"Come, let me learn this from the venerable one." "Learn," he said. "What is the support of that world?" "This world," he said. "What is the support of this world?" "One should not lead the <s>Sāman</s> beyond the world that is its foundation," he said. "We establish the <s>Sāman</s> in the world that is its foundation. For the <s>Sāman</s> is praised as the foundation."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.7]

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,8.7 evamukto dālbhya āha-hantāhametadbhagavatto vedāni yatpratiṣṭhaṃ sāmetyuktaḥ pratyuvāca śālāvatyo viddhīti hovāca /
amuṣya lokasya kā gatiriti pṛṣṭo dālbhyena śālāvatyo 'yaṃ loka iti hovāca /
ayaṃ hi loko yāgadānahomādibhiramuṃ lokaṃ puṣyatīti /
"itaḥ pradānaṃ devā upajīvanti"iti hi śrutayaḥ /
pratyakṣaṃ hi sarvabhūtānāṃ dharaṇī pratiṣṭheti /
ataḥ sāmno 'pyayaṃ lokaḥ pratiṣṭhaiveti yuktam /
asya lokasya kā gatirityukta āha śālāvatyaḥ /
na pratiṣṭhāmimaṃ lokamatītya nayetsāma kaścit /
children.translated_text: 'No one should lead the <s>Sāman</s> beyond this world, which is its foundation.'

children.text: ato vayaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ lokaṃ sāmābhisaṃsthāpayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, we establish the <s>Sāman</s> in the world that is its foundation.

children.text: yasmātpratiṣṭhāsaṃstāvaṃ hi pratiṣṭhātvena saṃstutaṃ sāmetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the <s>Sāman</s> is 'praised as the foundation' — meaning it is praised as having its foundation [in this world] — that is the meaning.

children.text: "iyaṃ vai rathantaram"iti ca śrutiḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'This [earth] indeed is the <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>].' [End of section 7.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 1.8.7] Thus addressed, <s>Dālbhya</s> said: 'Come, let me learn this from the venerable one — namely, that the <s>Sāman</s> has a [firm] foundation.' Thus addressed, <s>Śālāvatya</s> replied: 'Learn.' 'What is the support of that world?' — questioned by <s>Dālbhya</s>, <s>Śālāvatya</s> said: 'This world.' For this world nourishes that [heavenly] world through sacrifices, gifts, oblations, and the like. For there are <s>śruti</s>s [such as]: 'The gods subsist on offerings from here.' And it is directly evident to all beings that the earth is the foundation. Therefore, it is reasonable that this world is indeed the foundation of the <s>Sāman</s> as well. 'What is the support of this world?' — thus asked, <s>Śālāvatya</s> said:

children.text: START ChUp 1,8.8
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 1.8.8]

children.text:
taṃ ha pravāhaṇo jaivalir uvāca |
antavad vai kila te śālāvatya sāma |
yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti |
hantāham etad bhagavatto vedānīti |
viddhīti hovāca || ChUp_1,8.8 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said to him: "Your <s>sāman</s> is indeed finite, O <s>Śālāvatya</s>. If someone were to say now, 'Your head will fall off,' your head would indeed fall off." "Let me learn this from the venerable sir," he said. "Learn it," the other replied. || ChUp 1.8.8 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,8.8 tamevamuktavantaṃ ha pravāhaṇo jaivaliruvācāntavadvai kila te śālāvatya sāmetyādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: To him who had spoken thus, <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said, "Your <s>sāman</s> is indeed finite, O <s>Śālāvatya</s>," and so on, as before.

children.text: tataḥ śālāvatya āha-hantāhametadbhagavatto vedānīti viddhīti hovācetaro 'nujñāta āha //8//
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śālāvatya</s> said, "Let me learn this from the venerable sir." The other, having given permission, said, "Learn it." || 8 ||

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth section of the first chapter of <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,9.1

asya lokasya kā gatir iti |
ākāśa iti hovāca |
sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny ākāśād eva samutpadyante |
ākāśaṃ praty astaṃ yanti |
ākāśo hy evaibhyo jyāyān |
ākāśaḥ parāyaṇam || ChUp_1,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: "What is the goal of this world?" "<s>Ākāśa</s> (space)," he replied. For all these beings arise from <s>ākāśa</s> alone, and they return into <s>ākāśa</s>. For <s>ākāśa</s> is indeed greater than all of them. <s>Ākāśa</s> is the ultimate refuge (<s>parāyaṇa</s>). || ChUp 1.9.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,9.1 asya lokasya kā gatiriti /
ākāśa iti hovāca pravāhaṇaḥ /
ākāśa iti ca para ātmā"ākāśo vai nāme"ti śruteḥ /
tasya hi karma sarvabhūtotpādakatvam /
tasminneva hi bhūtapralayaḥ /
tattejo 'sṛjata /
children.translated_text: "It created <s>tejas</s> (fire/light),"

children.text: tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāmiti hi vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: "<s>Tejas</s> belongs to the supreme deity" — thus it will be stated later.

children.text: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamānyākāśādeva samutpadyante tejobannādikrameṇa, sāmarthyāt /
children.translated_text: All these beings, both stationary and moving, arise from <s>ākāśa</s> alone, through the sequence of <s>tejas</s> (fire), <s>ap</s> (water), <s>anna</s> (food), and so on — this is established by reasoning.

children.text: ākāśaṃ pratyastaṃ yanti pralayakāle tenaiva viparītakrameṇa hi yasmādākāśa evaibhyaḥ sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo jyāyānmahattaro 'taḥ sa sarveṣāṃ bhṛtānāṃ paramayanaṃ parāyaṇaṃ pratiṣṭhā triṣvapi kāleṣvityarthaḥ //1//
children.translated_text: They return into <s>ākāśa</s> at the time of dissolution, in the reverse order. Because <s>ākāśa</s> is indeed greater, more vast than all these beings, therefore it is the supreme abode (<s>paramāyana</s>), the ultimate refuge (<s>parāyaṇa</s>), the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) of all beings in all three times — this is the meaning. || 1 ||

"What is the goal of this world?" <s>Pravāhaṇa</s> replied, "<s>Ākāśa</s>." And by <s>ākāśa</s> is meant the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>), because of the scriptural text "<s>Ākāśa</s> is indeed the name" (of <s>Brahman</s>). For the activity of producing all beings belongs to it. And the dissolution of beings takes place in it alone.

children.text: START ChUp 1,9.2

sa eṣa parovarīyān udgīthaḥ |
sa eṣo 'nantaḥ |
parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān parovarīyāṃsam udgītham upāste || ChUp_1,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: This is the supreme, the most excellent <s>udgītha</s>. This is infinite. He who, knowing thus, meditates on the most excellent <s>udgītha</s> — the most excellent becomes his, and he wins the most excellent worlds. || ChUp 1.9.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,9.2 yasmātparaṃ paraṃ varīyo varīyaso 'pyeṣa varaḥ paraśca varīyāśca rapovarīyānudgīthaḥ paramātmā sampanna ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because this <s>udgītha</s>, which is the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>), is the most excellent beyond the excellent — <s>parovarīyas</s> means that which is superior and more excellent than even the excellent — the meaning is that it is fully realized as <s>paramātman</s>.

children.text: ata eva sa eṣo 'nanto 'vidyāmānāntastametaṃ parovarīyāṃsaṃ paramātmabhūtamanantamevaṃ vidvānparovarīyāṃsamudgīthamupāste /
children.translated_text: Therefore this one is infinite (<s>ananta</s>), having no end. He who, knowing thus that this most excellent <s>udgītha</s> is identical with <s>paramātman</s> and is infinite, meditates upon it —

children.text: tasyaitatphalamāha-parovarīyaḥ paraṃ paraṃ varīyo viśiṣṭataraṃ jīvanaṃ hāsya viduṣo bhavati dṛṣṭaṃ phalamadṛṣṭaṃ ca parovarīyasa uttarottaraviśiṣṭatarāneva brahmākāśāntāṃllokāñjayati ya etadevaṃ vidvānudgīthamupāste //2 //
children.translated_text: The fruit of such meditation is stated: the most excellent, ever more distinguished life becomes his — this is the visible fruit for the knower. And as the invisible fruit, he wins the ever more excellent worlds up to and including <s>Brahman</s> and <s>ākāśa</s> — he who, knowing thus, meditates on the <s>udgītha</s>. || 2 ||

children.text: START ChUp 1,9.3

taṃ haitam atidhanvā śaunaka udaraśāṇḍilyāyoktvovāca |
yāvat ta enaṃ prajāyām udgīthaṃ vediṣyante parovarīyo haibhyas tāvad asmiṃl loke jīvanaṃ bhaviṣyati || ChUp_1,9.3 ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Atidhanvan Śaunaka</s> taught this <s>udgītha</s> to <s>Udaraśāṇḍilya</s>, he said: "As long as your descendants will know this <s>udgītha</s>, so long will their life in this world be the most excellent beyond all others." || ChUp 1.9.3 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,9.3 kiṃ ca tametamudgīthaṃ vidvānatidhanvā nāmataḥ śunakasyāpatyaṃ śaunaka udaraśāḍilyāya śiṣyāyaitamudgīthadarśanamuktvovāca /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the knower of this <s>udgītha</s>, <s>Atidhanvan</s> by name — the descendant of <s>Śunaka</s>, hence <s>Śaunaka</s> — having taught this vision of the <s>udgītha</s> to his pupil <s>Udaraśāṇḍilya</s>, said:

children.text: yāvatte tava prajāyāṃ prajāsantatāvityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "As long as in your progeny" — meaning in the continuous line of your descendants —

children.text: enamudgīthaṃ tvatsantatijā vediṣyante jñāsyanti tāvantaṃ kālaṃ parovarīyo haibhyaḥ prasiddhebhyo laukikajīvanebhya uttarottaraviśiṣṭataraṃ jīvanaṃ tebhyo bhaviṣyati //3 //
children.translated_text: "They will know this <s>udgītha</s>, the descendants born in your lineage will know it" — for that long a period, a life that is the most excellent, ever more distinguished than the well-known worldly lives, will be theirs. || 3 ||

children.text: START ChUp 1,9.4

tathāmuṣmiṃl loke loka iti |
sa ya etam eva vidvān upāste parovarīya eva hāsyāmuṣmiṃl loke jīvanaṃ bhavati tathāmuṣmiṃl loke loka iti loke loka iti || ChUp_1,9.4 ||
