children.translated_text: "And likewise in the other world" — thus he said. He who, knowing this, meditates upon it — his life in the other world also becomes the most excellent. "And likewise in the other world" — thus he repeated. || ChUp 1.9.4 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,9.4 tathādṛṣṭe 'pi paraloke 'muṣminparovarīyāṃlloko bhaviṣyatītyuktavāñśāṇḍilyāyātidhanvā śaunakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Likewise in the unseen other world also, the most excellent world will be his" — thus <s>Atidhanvan Śaunaka</s> said to <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.

children.text: syādetatphalaṃ pūrveṣāṃ mahābhāgyānāṃ naidaṃyugīnānāmityāśaṅkānivṛttaya āha-sa yaḥ kaścidetadevaṃ vidvānudgīthametarhyupāste tasyāpyevameva parovarīya eva hāsyāsmiṃlloke jīvanaṃ bhavati tathāmuṣmiṃlloke loke loka iti //4//
children.translated_text: Lest one think that this fruit belongs only to the great ones of former times and not to people of the present age — to remove such a doubt, it is said: whoever, even now, knowing thus, meditates on this <s>udgītha</s>, for him too the most excellent life becomes his in this world, and likewise in the other world. || 4 ||

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth section of the first chapter of <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.1
maṭacīhateṣu kuruṣv āṭikyā saha jāyayoṣastir ha cākrāyaṇa ibhyagrāme pradrāṇaka uvāsa || ChUp_1,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: When the crops in the <s>Kuru</s> land were destroyed by hailstorms, <s>Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa</s> lived in dire distress in the village of <s>Ibhyagrāma</s>, together with his wife <s>Āṭikī</s>. || ChUp 1.10.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,10.1 udgīyopāsanaprasaṅgena prastāvapratihāraviṣayamapyupāsanaṃ vaktavyamitīdamārabhyate /
ākhyāyikā ta sukhāvabodhārthā /
maṭacīhateṣu maṭacyo 'śanayastābhirhateṣu nāśiteṣu kuruṣu kurusasyeṣvityarthaḥ /
tato durbhikṣe jāta āṭikyānupajātapayodharādistrīvyañjanayā saha jāyayoṣastirha nāmataścakrasyāpatyaṃ cākrāyaṇaḥ /
ibho hastī tamarhatītībhya īśvaro hastyāroho vā tasya grāma ibhyagrāmastasminpradrāṇako 'nnālābhāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Ibhya</s> means an elephant; one who is worthy of it is <s>ibhya</s>, meaning a wealthy person or an elephant-keeper; his village is <s>Ibhyagrāma</s>. In that village, he was <s>pradrāṇaka</s>, meaning in dire distress due to inability to obtain food.

children.text: drā kutsāyāṃ gatau /
children.translated_text: The root <s>drā</s> means to go in a degraded manner.

children.text: kṛtsitāṃ gatiṃ gato 'ntyāvasthāṃ prāpta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He had gone to a degraded state, meaning he had reached the lowest condition — this is the meaning.

children.text: uvāsoṣitavānkasyacidgṛhamāśritya //1 //
children.translated_text: He lived there, having taken refuge in someone's house. || 1 ||

In connection with the meditation on the <s>udgītha</s>, the meditation concerning the <s>prastāva</s> and <s>pratihāra</s> portions must also be taught — for this purpose, this section is begun. The narrative is for the sake of easy comprehension. "Destroyed by hailstorms" — <s>maṭacī</s> means hailstorms; "destroyed by them" means the <s>Kuru</s> crops were ruined — this is the meaning. Then, when famine arose, together with <s>Āṭikī</s>, a woman whose feminine features such as breasts had not yet developed, as his wife, <s>Uṣasti</s> by name — the descendant of <s>Cakra</s>, hence <s>Cākrāyaṇa</s> —

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.2

sa hebhyaṃ kulmāṣān khādantaṃ bibhikṣe |
taṃ hovāca |
neto 'nye vidyante yac ca ye ma ima upanihitā iti || ChUp_1,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: He begged from an elephant-keeper who was eating <s>kulmāṣa</s> (coarse grain). The keeper said to him: "I have no others than these, and even these are set aside for me." || ChUp 1.10.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,10.2 so 'nnārthamaṭannibhyaṃ kulmāṣānkutsitānmāṣānkhādantaṃ bhakṣayantaṃ yadṛcchayopalabhya bibhikṣe yācitavān /
children.translated_text: He, wandering in search of food, happened to come upon an elephant-keeper who was eating, chewing <s>kulmāṣa</s> — meaning inferior beans — and begged from him, requesting food.

children.text: tamuṣastiṃ hovācebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The elephant-keeper said to him, to <s>Uṣasti</s>:

children.text: neto 'smānmayā bhakṣyamāṇāducchiṣṭarāśeḥ kulmāṣā anye na vidyante /
children.translated_text: "Apart from these <s>kulmāṣas</s> that I am eating, from the pile of leftover food, no other <s>kulmāṣas</s> exist."

children.text: yacca ye rāśau me mamopanihitāḥ prakṣiptā ime bhājate kiṃ karomītyuktaḥ pratyuvācoṣastiḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: "But whatever ones are set aside for me in this pile, these are my share — what can I do?" Thus addressed, <s>Uṣasti</s> replied: || 2 ||

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.3

eteṣāṃ me dehīti hovāca |
tān asmai pradadau |
hantānupānam iti |
ucchiṣṭaṃ vai me pītaṃ syād iti hovāca || ChUp_1,10.3 ||
children.translated_text: "Give me some of these," he said. The keeper gave them to him. "Here, have some water too," he said. "That would be drinking your leftovers," <s>Uṣasti</s> replied. || ChUp 1.10.3 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,10.3 eteṣāmetānityarthaḥ /
me mahyaṃ dehīti hovāca /
children.translated_text: "Give to me," he said.

children.text: tānsa ibhyo 'smā uṣastaye pradadau pradattavān /
children.translated_text: The elephant-keeper gave them, handed them over, to <s>Uṣasti</s>.

children.text: anupānīyaṃ samīpasthamudakaṃ hanta gṛhāṇānupānamityuktaḥ pratyuvāca /
children.translated_text: When told, "Here, take some water to drink alongside" — meaning the water nearby — he replied:

children.text: ucchiṣṭaṃ vai me mamedamudakaṃ pītaṃ syādyadi pāsyāmītyuktavantaṃ pratyuvācetaraḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: "This water of mine would be leftover (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) — if I were to drink it," he said. To this, the other replied: || 3 ||
"Of these" means "these ones" — this is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.4

na svid ete 'py ucchiṣṭā iti |
na vā ajīviṣyam imān akhādann iti hovāca |
kāmo ma udapānam iti || ChUp_1,10.4 ||
children.translated_text: "Are not these <s>kulmāṣas</s> also leftovers?" "I would not have survived without eating these," <s>Uṣasti</s> replied. "Water I can obtain at will." || ChUp 1.10.4 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,10.4 kiṃ na svidete kulmāṣā upyucchiṣṭā ityukta āhoṣastirna vā ajīviṣyaṃ na jīviṣyāmīmānkulmāṣānakhādannabhakṣayanniti hovāca /
kāma icchāto me mamodakapānaṃ labhyata ityarthaḥ /
ataścaitāmavasyāṃ prāptasya vidyādharmayaśovataḥ svātmaparopakārasamarthasyaitadapi karma kurvato nā'gaḥsparśa ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for one who has reached this dire necessity, who possesses knowledge, virtue, and fame, and who is capable of benefiting himself and others — even performing this act does not incur sin. This is the purport.

children.text: tasyāpi jāvitaṃ pratyupāyāntare 'jugupsite sati jugupsitametatkarma doṣāya /
children.translated_text: However, when there exists another means of sustaining life that is not objectionable, then even for such a person, this despicable act would be a fault.

children.text: jñānāvalepena kurvato narakapātaḥ syādevetyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one does it out of arrogance of knowledge, one would indeed fall into hell — this is the purport.

children.text: pradrāṇakaśabdaśravaṇāt //4 //
children.translated_text: This is understood from the word <s>pradrāṇaka</s> (one in dire distress). || 4 ||

"Are not these <s>kulmāṣas</s> also leftovers?" — thus addressed, <s>Uṣasti</s> said: "I would not have survived, I would not have lived, without eating these <s>kulmāṣas</s>." "Water I can obtain at will" — meaning, drinking water is available to me whenever I wish.

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.5

sa ha khāditvātiśeṣāñ jāyāyā ājahāra |
sāgra eva subhikṣā babhūva |
tān pratigṛhya nidadhau || ChUp_1,10.5 ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten, he brought the remainder to his wife. She had already become well-provisioned before that. She received them and stored them away. || ChUp 1.10.5 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,10.5 tāṃśca sa khāditvātiśeṣānatiśiṣṭāñjāyāyai kāruṇyādājahāra /
children.translated_text: Having eaten those, he brought the remainder, the leftover portion, to his wife out of compassion.

children.text: sā'ṭikyagra eva kulmāṣaprāpteḥ subhikṣā śobhanabhikṣā labdhānnetyetadbabhūva saṃvṛttā /
children.translated_text: She, <s>Āṭikī</s>, had already before the arrival of the <s>kulmāṣas</s> become well-provisioned, meaning she had obtained food — this had come about.

children.text: tathāpi strīsvābhāvyādanavajñāya tānkulmāṣānpatyurhastātpratigṛhya nidadhau nikṣiptavatī //5 //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, due to a wife's natural disposition, not disregarding them, she received those <s>kulmāṣas</s> from her husband's hand and stored them away. || 5 ||

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.6

sa ha prātaḥ saṃjihāna uvāca |
yad batānnasya labhemahi labhemahi dhanamātrām |
rājāsau yakṣyate |
sa mā sarvair ārtvijyair vṛṇīteti || ChUp_1,10.6 ||
children.translated_text: Waking up in the morning, he said: "Ah, if only we could get some food, we could earn a little wealth. That king over there is going to perform a sacrifice. He would select me for all the priestly offices." || ChUp 1.10.6 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,10.6 sa tasyāḥ karma jānanprātaruṣaḥkāle sañjihānaḥ śayanaṃ nidrāṃ vā parityajannuvāca patnyāḥ śṛṇvatyā yadyadi vateti khidyamāno 'nnasya stokaṃ labhemahi tadbhuktvānnaṃ samartho gatvā labhemahi dhanamātrāṃ dhanasyālpam /
tato 'smākaṃ jīvanaṃ bhaviṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: "Then our livelihood will be secured."

children.text: dhanalābhe ca kāraṇamāha-rājāsau nātidūre sthāne yakṣyate /
children.translated_text: He states the means of obtaining wealth: "That king, not too far from here, is going to perform a sacrifice."

children.text: yajamānatvāttasyā'tmanepadam /
children.translated_text: The reflexive form (<s>ātmanepada</s>) is used because of his being the performer of the sacrifice.

children.text: sa ca rājā mā māṃ pātramupalabhya sarvairārtvijyairṝtvikkarmabhirṝtvikkarmaprayojanāyetyartho vṛṇīteti //6 //
children.translated_text: "And that king, finding me as a worthy vessel, would select me for all the priestly offices (<s>ārtvijya</s>)" — meaning, for the purpose of performing the duties of the <s>ṛtvij</s> priests. || 6 ||

He, knowing of her provision, in the morning at dawn, waking up — abandoning sleep — said, within hearing of his wife: "If only" — speaking with distress — "we could get a little food, and having eaten it, being capable, we could go and earn a small amount of wealth."

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.7

taṃ jāyovāca |
hanta pata ima eva kulmāṣā iti |
tān khāditvāmuṃ yajñaṃ vitatam eyāya || ChUp_1,10.7 ||
children.translated_text: His wife said to him: "Here, my lord, eat these very <s>kulmāṣas</s>." Having eaten them, he went to that sacrifice which was being spread out. || ChUp 1.10.7 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,10.7 evamuktavantaṃ jāyovāca-hanta gṛhāṇa he pata ima eva ye maddhaste vinikṣiptāstvayā kulmāṣā iti /
children.translated_text: To him who had spoken thus, his wife said: "Here, take them, O lord — these very <s>kulmāṣas</s> that you deposited in my hands."

children.text: tānkhāditvāmuṃ yajñaṃ rājño vitataṃ vistāritamṛtvigbhireyāya //7 //
children.translated_text: Having eaten those, he went to that sacrifice of the king which had been spread out, arranged by the <s>ṛtvij</s> priests. || 7 ||

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.8

tatrodgātḥn āstāve stoṣyamāṇān upopaviveśa |
sa ha prastotaram uvāca || ChUp_1,10.8 ||
children.translated_text: There he sat near the <s>udgātṛ</s> priests who were about to chant in the place of chanting (<s>āstāva</s>). He said to the <s>prastotṛ</s> priest: || ChUp 1.10.8 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,10.8 tatra ca gatvodgātṝnudgātṛpuruṣānāgatya stuvantyasminnityāstāvastasminnāstāve stoṣyamāṇānupopaviveśa samīpa upaviṣṭasteṣāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone there, approaching the <s>udgātṛ</s> priests — the men belonging to the <s>udgātṛ</s> group — at the <s>āstāva</s>, the place where they chant (so called because they praise therein), he sat down near those who were about to chant — this is the meaning.

children.text: upaviśya sa ha prastotāramuvāca //8 //
children.translated_text: Having sat down, he said to the <s>prastotṛ</s> priest: || 8 ||

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.9
prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti || ChUp_1,10.9 ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>prastotṛ</s>, if you chant the <s>prastāva</s> without knowing the deity that is connected with it, your head will fall off." || ChUp 1.10.9 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,10.9 he prastotarityāmantryābhimukhīkaraṇāya /
yā devatā prastāvaṃ prastāvabhaktimanugatānvāyattā tāṃ ceddevatāṃ prastāvabhakteravidvānsanprastoṣyasi viduṣo mama samīpe /
tatparokṣe 'pi cedvipatettasya mūrdhā karmamātravidāmanadhikāra eva karmaṇi syāt /
taccāniṣṭamaviduṣāmapi karmadarśanāt /
dakṣiṇamārgaśruteśca /
anadhikāre cāviduṣāmuttara evaiko mārgaḥ śrūyeta /
na ca smārtakarmanimitta eva dakṣiṇaḥ panthāḥ /
yajñena dānenetyādiśrateḥ /
children.translated_text: because of the scriptural text "through sacrifice, through charity," and so on.

children.text: tathoktasya mayeti ca viśeṣaṇādvidvatsamakṣameva karmaṇyanadhikāro na sarvatrāgnihotrasmārtakarmādhyayanādiṣu ca /
children.translated_text: And because of the qualification "spoken by me" (in my presence), the disqualification for ritual applies only in the presence of a knower, not universally in all rituals such as <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>smārta</s> rites, Vedic study, and so on.

children.text: anujñāyāstatra tatra darśanāt karmamātravidāmapyadhikāraḥ siddhaḥ karmaṇīti /
children.translated_text: Because permission for such persons is seen in various contexts, the qualification of those who know only the ritual acts for performing rituals is established.

children.text: mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti //9 //
children.translated_text: "Your head will fall off." || 9 ||

"O <s>prastotṛ</s>" — addressing him to make him attentive. "The deity that is connected with, that follows, the <s>prastāva</s> portion — if, not knowing that deity, you chant the <s>prastāva</s> in the presence of me, a knower — " Even in his absence, if the head of one who knows only the ritual acts were to fall, it would mean that those who know only the ritual without knowing the presiding deity have no qualification for the ritual. And that is undesirable, given that even the non-knowers are seen performing rituals, and because the scripture speaks of the southern path (for ritualists). If the non-knowers had no qualification, then only one path, the northern, would be mentioned in scripture. Nor is the southern path caused solely by <s>smārta</s> (traditional) rituals,

children.text: START ChUp 1,10.10-11

evam evodgātāram uvāca |
udgātar yā devatodgītham anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān udgāsyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti || ChUp_1,10.10 ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, he said to the <s>udgātṛ</s> priest: "O <s>udgātṛ</s>, if you chant the <s>udgītha</s> without knowing the deity that is connected with it, your head will fall off." || ChUp 1.10.10 ||

children.text:
evam eva pratihartāram uvāca |
pratihartar yā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān pratihariṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti |
te ha samāratās tūṣṇīm āsāṃ cakrire || ChUp_1,10.11 ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, he said to the <s>pratihartṛ</s> priest: "O <s>pratihartṛ</s>, if you perform the <s>pratihāra</s> without knowing the deity that is connected with it, your head will fall off." They all stopped and sat in silence. || ChUp 1.10.11 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,10.10-11 evamevodgātāraṃ pratihartāramuvācetyādi samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.10.10-11:] In the same way, he addressed the <s>Udgātṛ</s> and the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> — and so forth — the rest is the same.

children.text: te prastotrādayaḥ karmabhyaḥ samāratā uparatāḥ santo mūrdhapātabhayāttūṣṇīmāsāṃcakrire 'nyaccākurvantaḥ arthitvāt //10-11 //
children.translated_text: Those <s>Prastotṛ</s> and others, having ceased from their ritual duties, remained silent out of fear of their heads splitting, and did nothing else, being desirous [of instruction]. (10-11)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhadhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth section of the first chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> with <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary.

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.1]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ yajamāna uvāca |
bhagavantaṃ vā ahaṃ vividiṣāṇīti |
uṣastir asmi cākrāyaṇa iti hovāca || ChUp_1,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then the patron of the sacrifice said to him: 'I wish to know the Blessed One.' He replied: 'I am <s>Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa</s>.' (ChUp 1.11.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,11.1 athānantaraṃ hainamuṣastiṃ yajamāno rājovāca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.1:] Then, subsequently, the patron of the sacrifice — the king — said to <s>Uṣasti</s>:

children.text: bhagavantaṃ vai pūjāvarntamahaṃ vividiṣāmi veditumicchāmītyukta uṣastirasmi cākrāyaṇastavāpi śrotrapathamāgato yadīti hovācoktavān //1 //
children.translated_text: 'I wish to know the Blessed One — the one worthy of honor — I desire to know [you].' When thus addressed, [he replied:] 'I am <s>Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa</s> — [the one whose name] has indeed reached your ears.' Thus he spoke. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.2]

children.text:
sa hovāca |
bhagavantaṃ vā aham ebhiḥ sarvair ārtvijyaiḥ paryaiṣiṣam |
bhagavato vā aham avittyānyān avṛṣi || ChUp_1,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'I sought the Blessed One for all these priestly offices. It was because I did not find the Blessed One that I chose others.' (ChUp 1.11.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,11.2 sa ha yajamāna uvāca satyamevamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ bahuguṇamaśrauṣaṃ sarvaiśca ṛcvikkarmabhirārtvijyaiḥ paryaiṣiṣaṃ paryeṣaṇaṃ kṛtavānasmi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.2:] The patron of the sacrifice said: 'Truly, I had heard of the Blessed One's many virtues, and I searched — made a search — for [you] with all the priestly offices of the <s>Ṛtvik</s> priests.'

children.text: anviṣya bhagavato vā ahamavittyālābhenānyānimānavṛṣi vṛtavānasmi //2 //
children.translated_text: 'Having searched but not finding the Blessed One, I chose — selected — these others.' (2)

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.3]

children.text:
bhagavāṃs tv eva me sarvair ārtvijyair iti |
tatheti |
atha tarhy eta eva samatisṛṣṭāḥ stuvatām |
yāvat tv ebhyo dhanaṃ dadyās tāvan mama dadyā iti |
tatheti ha yajamāna uvāca || ChUp_1,11.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'But let the Blessed One himself [officiate] for me with all priestly offices.' 'So be it.' 'Then let these very ones, being released [by you], continue to chant. But whatever wealth you would give to them, give that much to me.' The patron of the sacrifice said: 'So be it.' (ChUp 1.11.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,11.3 adyāpi bhagavāṃstveva me mama sarvairārtvijyairṛtvikkarmārthamastvityuktastathetyāhoṣast iḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.3:] 'Even now, let the Blessed One himself be for me — for my sake — with all priestly offices, for the purpose of the <s>Ṛtvik</s> duties.' When thus addressed, <s>Uṣasti</s> said 'So be it.'

children.text: kintvathaivaṃ tarhyeta eva tvayā pūrva vṛtā mayā samatisṛṣṭā mayā samyakprasannenānujñātāḥ santaḥ stuvatām /
children.translated_text: 'But then, these very ones previously chosen by you, being fully released — properly permitted — by me with full grace, let them continue to chant.'

children.text: tvayā tvetatkāryam /
children.translated_text: 'But this task is to be done by you.'

children.text: yāvattvebhyaḥ prastotrādibhyaḥ sarvebhyo dhanaṃ dadyāḥ prayacchasi tāvanmama dadyā ityuktastatheti ha yajamāna uvāca //3 //
children.translated_text: 'Whatever wealth you would give — are giving — to all these <s>Prastotṛ</s> and others, give that much to me.' When thus addressed, the patron of the sacrifice said 'So be it.' (3)

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.4]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ prastotopasasāda |
prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat |
katamā sā devateti || ChUp_1,11.4 ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Prastotṛ</s> approached him [and said]: 'O <s>Prastotṛ</s>, the Blessed One told me: "The deity that is connected with the <s>Prastāva</s> — if you chant the <s>Prastāva</s> without knowing that [deity], your head will fall off." What is that deity?' (ChUp 1.11.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,11.4 atha hainamauṣastyaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā prastotopasasādoṣastiṃ vinayenopajagāma /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.4:] Then, having heard the words of <s>Uṣasti</s>, the <s>Prastotṛ</s> approached — came near to <s>Uṣasti</s> with humility.

children.text: prastotaryā devatetyādi mā māṃ magavānavocatpūrvam /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Prastotṛ</s>, the deity...' and so forth — 'the Blessed One spoke to me earlier.'

children.text: katamā sā devatā yā prastāvabhaktimanvāyatteti //4 //
children.translated_text: 'What is that deity that is connected with — that follows — the <s>Prastāva</s> portion?' (4)

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.5]

children.text:
prāṇa iti hovāca |
sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni prāṇam evābhisaṃviśanti |
prāṇam abhyujjihate |
saiṣā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā |
tāṃ ced avidvān prāstoṣyo mūrdhā te vipatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti || ChUp_1,11.5 ||
children.translated_text: He said: '<s>Prāṇa</s> (the life-breath).' 'All these beings indeed enter into <s>Prāṇa</s> [at dissolution] and rise up from <s>Prāṇa</s> [at creation]. This is the deity connected with the <s>Prastāva</s>. Had you chanted the <s>Prastāva</s> without knowing this, your head would have fallen off, as I had told you.' (ChUp 1.11.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,11.5 pṛṣṭaḥ prāṇa iti hovāca /
yuktaṃ prastāvasya prāṇo devateti /
kathaṃ, sarvāṇi sthāvarajaṅgamāni bhūtāni prāṇamevābhisaṃviśanti pralayakāle prāṇamabhi lakṣayitvā prāṇātmanaivojjihate prāṇādevodgacchantītyarthaḥ utpattikāle /
children.translated_text: How so? All beings — movable and immovable — enter into <s>Prāṇa</s> alone at the time of dissolution, directing themselves toward <s>Prāṇa</s>, and rise up from <s>Prāṇa</s> alone — meaning they emerge from <s>Prāṇa</s> — at the time of creation.

children.text: ataḥ saiṣā devatā prastāvamanvāyattā tāṃ cedavidvāṃstvaṃ prāstoṣyaḥ prastavanaṃ prastāvabhaktiṃ kṛtavānasi yadi mūrdhā śiraste vyapatiṣyadvipatitamabhaviṣyattathoktasya mayā tatkāle mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is the deity connected with the <s>Prastāva</s>. Had you, without knowing this, performed the chanting — executed the <s>Prastāva</s> portion — your head would have split — would have fallen — as I had told you at that time: 'Your head will fall off.'

children.text: atastvayā sādhu kṛtam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you have done well.

children.text: mayā niṣiddhaḥ karmaṇo yaduparamamakārṣīrityabhiprāyaḥ //5 //
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is: [it was] good that you ceased from the ritual action when prohibited by me. (5)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.5:] When asked, he said '<s>Prāṇa</s>.' It is fitting that <s>Prāṇa</s> is the deity of the <s>Prastāva</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.6]

children.text:
atha hainam udgātopasasāda |
udgātar yā devatodgītham anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān udgāsyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat |
katamā sā devatā iti || ChUp_1,11.6 ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Udgātṛ</s> approached him [and said]: 'O <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the Blessed One told me: "The deity that is connected with the <s>Udgītha</s> — if you chant without knowing that [deity], your head will fall off." What is that deity?' (ChUp 1.11.6)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,11.6 tathodgātā papraccha katamā sodgīthabhaktimanugatānvāyattā devateti //6 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.6:] Similarly, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> asked: 'What is that deity that follows — that is connected with — the <s>Udgītha</s> portion?' (6)

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.7]

children.text:
āditya iti hovāca |
sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny ādityam uccaiḥ santaṃ gāyanti |
saiṣā devatodgītham anvāyattā |
tāṃ ced avidvān udagāsyo mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti || ChUp_1,11.7 ||
children.translated_text: He said: '<s>Āditya</s> (the sun).' 'All these beings sing to <s>Āditya</s> who is on high. This is the deity connected with the <s>Udgītha</s>. Had you chanted without knowing this, your head would have fallen off, as I had told you.' (ChUp 1.11.7)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,11.7 pṛṣṭa āditya iti hovāca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.7:] When asked, he said '<s>Āditya</s>.'

children.text: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyādityamuccairūrdhvaṃ santaṃ gāyanti śabdayanti stuvantītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: All these beings sing to — make sound toward, praise — <s>Āditya</s> who is high above — that is the intended meaning.

children.text: ucchabdasāmānyātpraśabdasāmānyādiva prāṇo 'taḥ saiṣā devatetyādi pūrvavat //7 //
children.translated_text: Due to the similarity of the word 'ucca' (high), just as <s>Prāṇa</s> [was connected] due to the similarity of the word 'pra,' therefore 'this is the deity' and so forth — as before. (7)

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.8
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.8]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ pratihartopasasāda |
pratihartar yā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān pratihariṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat |
katamā sā devateti || ChUp_1,11.8 ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> approached him [and said]: 'O <s>Pratihartṛ</s>, the Blessed One told me: "The deity that is connected with the <s>Pratihāra</s> — if you respond without knowing that [deity], your head will fall off." What is that deity?' (ChUp 1.11.8)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,11.8 evamevātha hainaṃ pratihartopasāda katamā sā devatā pratihāramanvāyatteti //8 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.8:] In the same manner, the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> approached him [and asked]: 'What is that deity connected with the <s>Pratihāra</s>?' (8)

children.text: START ChUp 1,11.9
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.11.9]

children.text:
annam iti hovāca |
sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtany annam eva pratiharamāṇāni jīvanti |
saiṣā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā |
tāṃ ced avidvān pratyahariṣyo mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti tathoktasya mayeti || ChUp_1,11.9 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'Food (<s>anna</s>).' 'All these beings live by taking in food. This is the deity connected with the <s>Pratihāra</s>. Had you responded without knowing this, your head would have fallen off, as I had told you — as I had told you.' (ChUp 1.11.9)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,11.9 pṛṣṭo 'nnamiti hovāca /
sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyannamevā'tmānaṃ prati sarvataḥ pratiharamāṇāni jīvanti /
saiṣā devatā pratiśabdasāmānyātpratihārabhaktimanugatā /
children.translated_text: This is the deity that follows — is connected with — the <s>Pratihāra</s> portion, due to the similarity of the word 'prati.'

children.text: samānamanyattathoktasya mayeti /
children.translated_text: The rest is the same — 'as I had told you.'

children.text: prastāvodgīthapratihārabhaktīḥ prāṇādityānnadṛṣṭyopāsīteti samudāyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The collective meaning is: one should meditate on the <s>Prastāva</s>, <s>Udgītha</s>, and <s>Pratihāra</s> portions with the vision of <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and <s>Anna</s> respectively.

children.text: prāṇādyāpattiḥ karmasamṛddhirvā phalamiti //9//
children.translated_text: The fruit is either attainment of <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest, or the success of the ritual. (9)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.11.9:] When asked, he said 'Food.' All these beings live by taking in food — drawing it to themselves from all sides.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh section of the first chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> with <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary.

children.text: START ChUp 1,12.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.12.1]

children.text:
athātaḥ śauva udgīthaḥ |
tad dha bako dālbhyo glāvo vā maitreyaḥ svādhyāyam udvavrāja || ChUp_1,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Udgītha</s> of the dogs. <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> — or <s>Glāva Maitreya</s> — went out for <s>svādhyāya</s> (private Vedic recitation). (ChUp 1.12.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,12.1 atīte khaṇḍe 'nnāprāptinimittā kaṣṭāvasthoktocchiṣṭaparyuṣitabhakṣaṇalakṣaṇā /
sā mā bhūdityannalābhāyāthānantaraṃ śauvaḥ śvabhirdṛṣṭa udgītha udgānaṃ sāmātaḥ prastūyate /
tattatra ha kila bako nāmato dalbhasyāpatyaṃ dālbhyo glāvo vā nāmato mitrāyāścāpatyaṃ maitreyaḥ /
vāśabdaścārthe /
dvyāmuṣyāyaṇo hyasau /
vastuviṣaye kriyāsviva vikalpānupapatteḥ /
dvināmā dvigotra ityādi hi smṛtiḥ /
dṛśyate cobhayataḥ piṇḍabhāktvam /
udgīthe baddhacittatvādṛṣāvanādarādvā /
vāśabdaḥ svādhyāyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the word 'vā' is for the purpose of [indicating] <s>svādhyāya</s>.

children.text: svādhyāyaṃ kartuṃ grāmādbahirudvavrājodgatavānviviktadeśasthodakābhyāśam /
children.translated_text: He went out — departed from the village — to perform <s>svādhyāya</s>, to a secluded place near water.

children.text: udvavrāja pratipālayāñcakāreti caikavacanālliṅgādeko 'sāvṛṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He went out' — 'he waited' — from the singular number and the grammatical sign, this was a single sage.

children.text: śvodgīthakālapratipālanādṛṣeḥ svādhyāyakaraṇamannakāmanayeti lakṣyata ityabhiprāyaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is: it is indicated that from the sage's waiting for the time of the dog-<s>Udgītha</s>, the performance of <s>svādhyāya</s> was [done] with the desire for food. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.12.1:] In the previous section, a painful condition was described — eating leftover and stale food — occasioned by not obtaining food. 'May that not happen [again]' — therefore, for the purpose of obtaining food, now the <s>Udgītha</s> seen by dogs — the chanting as <s>Sāman</s> — is introduced. There, indeed, <s>Baka</s> by name — the descendant of <s>Dalbha</s> — [was called] <s>Dālbhya</s>; or <s>Glāva</s> by name — the offspring of <s>Mitrā</s> — [was called] <s>Maitreya</s>. The word 'vā' (or) is used in the sense of 'and' (<s>ca</s>). For he was a <s>dvyāmuṣyāyaṇa</s> (one with two lineages). Because alternation is not possible regarding actual things as it is regarding actions. The <s>smṛti</s> says: 'having two names, having two lineages,' etc. And the sharing of oblations from both sides is observed. [The word 'vā' may also indicate] that being absorbed in the <s>Udgītha</s>, or due to disregard for the sage,

children.text: START ChUp 1,12.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.12.2]

children.text:
tasmai śvā śvetaḥ prādur babhūva |
tam anye śvāna upasametyocuḥ |
annaṃ no bhagavān āgāyatu |
aśanāyāma vā iti || ChUp_1,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: A white dog appeared before him. Other dogs, gathering around it, said: 'Please, Blessed One, chant for us [to obtain] food; for we are hungry.' (ChUp 1.12.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,12.2 svādhyāyena toṣitā devatarṣirvā śvarūpaṃ gṛhītvā śvā śvetaḥ saṃstasmā ṛṣaye tadanugrahārthaṃ prādurbabhūva prāduścakāra /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.12.2:] A deity or a sage, pleased by [his] <s>svādhyāya</s>, assuming the form of a dog — a white dog — appeared before that sage for the purpose of blessing him.

children.text: tamanye śuklaṃ śvānaṃ kṣullakāḥ śvāna upasametyocuruktavanto 'nnaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ bhagavānāgāyatvāgānena niṣpādayatvityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Other smaller dogs, approaching that white dog, said — spoke: 'Please, Blessed One, chant food for us — produce [it] through chanting' — that is the meaning.

children.text: mukyaprāṇaṃ vāgādayo vā prāṇamanvannabhujaḥ svādhyāyaparitoṣitāḥ santo 'nugṛhṇīyurenaṃ svarūpamādāyeti yuktamevaṃ pratipattum /
children.translated_text: It is fitting to understand it thus: the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>, or speech and the other [vital airs] — being food-eaters following <s>Prāṇa</s> — being pleased by the <s>svādhyāya</s>, would bless him by assuming their true form.

children.text: aśanāyāma vai bubhukṣitāḥ smo vā iti //2 //
children.translated_text: 'We are hungry indeed — we are famished' — [is the meaning of] 'vā iti.' (2)

children.text: START ChUp 1,12.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.12.3]

children.text:
tān hovācehaiva mā prātar upasamīyateti |
tad dha bako dālbhyo glāvo vā maitreyaḥ pratipālayāṃ cakāra || ChUp_1,12.3 ||
children.translated_text: He said to them: 'Come to me here tomorrow morning.' <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> — or <s>Glāva Maitreya</s> — kept watch. (ChUp 1.12.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,12.3 evamukte śvā śveta uvāca tānkṣullākāñśuna ihaivāsminneva deśe mā māṃ prātaḥ prātaḥkāla upasamīyāteti /
dairdhyaṃ chandasaṃ samīyāteti, pramādapāṭho vā /
children.translated_text: The lengthening [of the vowel in 'samīyāta'] is a Vedic [irregularity], or it is a variant reading due to scribal error.

children.text: prātaḥ kālakaraṇaṃ tatkāla eva kartavyājhrvyatāṭartham /
children.translated_text: The specification of morning time is for the purpose of the offering that must be performed at that very time.

children.text: annadasya vā savituraparāhne 'nābhimukhyāt /
children.translated_text: Or because in the afternoon, the food-giver sun is not facing [this way].

children.text: tattatraiva ha bako dālbhyo glāvo vā maitreya ṛṣiḥ pratipālayāñcakāra pratīkṣaṇaṃ kṛtavānityarthaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: There, in that very place, <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> — or the sage <s>Glāva Maitreya</s> — kept watch — waited — that is the meaning. (3)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.12.3:] Thus addressed, the white dog said to those smaller dogs: 'Come to me — approach me — here in this very place tomorrow morning.'

children.text: START ChUp 1,12.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.12.4]

children.text:
te ha yathaivedaṃ bahiṣpavamānena stoṣyamāṇāḥ saṃrabdhāḥ sarpantīty evam āsasṛpuḥ |
te ha samupaviśya hiñ cakruḥ || ChUp_1,12.4 ||
children.translated_text: They crept along just as [priests] creep along when about to chant the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna Stotra</s>, holding onto one another. Then they sat down together and made the sound '<s>hiṃ</s>.' (ChUp 1.12.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_1,12.4 te śvānastatraivā'gamya ṛṣeḥ samakṣaṃ yathaiveha karmaṇi bahiṣpavamānena stotreṇa stoṣyamāṇā /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.12.4:] Those dogs, having come there, in the presence of the sage — just as here in the ritual, those about to chant with the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna Stotra</s> —

children.text: udgātṛpuruṣāḥ saṃrabdhāḥ saṃlagnā anyonyameva mukhenānyonyasya pucchaṃ gṛhītvā'sasṛpurāsṛptavantaḥ paribhramaṇaṃ kṛtavanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests — holding onto one another, each one grasping another's tail with its mouth, crept — moved in a circle — that is the meaning.

children.text: ta evaṃ saṃsṛpya samupaviśyopaviṣṭāḥ santo hiṃ cakrurhiṅkāraṃ kṛtavantaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: Having thus crept around and sat down together — being seated — they performed the <s>hiṃkāra</s> — made the sound '<s>hiṃ</s>.' (4)

children.text: START ChUp 1,12.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.12.5]

children.text:
o3madā3ma |
oṃ3 pibā3ma |
oṃ3 devo varuṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ savitā2'nnam ihā2'harat |
annapate3'nnamihā2''harā2''haro3miti || ChUp_1,12.5 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Om</s>, let us eat! <s>Om</s>, let us drink! <s>Om</s>, may the god — <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s> — bring food here! O Lord of food, bring food here, bring it here, <s>Om</s>!' (ChUp 1.12.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,12.5 omadāmoṃ pibāmoṃ devo dyotanāt /
varuṇo varṣaṇājjagataḥ /
prajāpatiḥ pālanātprajānām /
savitā prasavitṛtvātsarvasyā'ditya ucyate /
etaiḥ paryāyaiḥ sa evaṃbhūta ādityo 'nnamasmabhyamihā'baradābaratviti /
ta evaṃ hiṃ kṛtvā punarapyūcuḥ-sa tvaṃ he 'nnapate /
sa hi sarvasyānnasya prasavitṛtvātpatiḥ /
na hi tatpākena vinā prabhūtamannamaṇumātramapi jāyate prāṇinām /
ato 'nnapatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore [he is] the Lord of food.

children.text: he 'nnapate 'nnamasmabhyamihā'harā'hareti /
children.translated_text: 'O Lord of food, bring food here for us, bring it' — thus.

children.text: abhyāsa ādarārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The repetition is for the sake of emphasis.

children.text: omiti //5//

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 1.12.5:] '<s>Om</s>, let us eat; <s>Om</s>, let us drink; <s>Om</s>' — the god (<s>deva</s>) [so called] because of shining; <s>Varuṇa</s> because of raining upon the world; <s>Prajāpati</s> because of protecting creatures; <s>Savitṛ</s> — <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is called [by all these names] because of being the impeller of all. By these designations, that sun of such nature brought food for us here — 'may he bring it' — thus. Having made the <s>hiṃkāra</s>, they said again: 'O you, Lord of food!' — for he is the lord of all food because of being the impeller [of its production]. Without his ripening [power], not even the smallest amount of food is produced for living beings.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the first chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> with <s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary.

children.text: START ChUp 1,13.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 1.13.1]

children.text:
ayaṃ vāva loko hāukāraḥ |
vāyur hāikāraḥ |
candramā athakāraḥ |
ātmehakāraḥ |
agnir īkāraḥ || ChUp_1,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: This world is indeed the syllable '<s>hāu</s>.' Air is the syllable '<s>hāi</s>.' The moon is the syllable '<s>atha</s>.' The self is the syllable '<s>iha</s>.' Fire is the syllable '<s>ī</s>.' (ChUp 1.13.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,13.1 bhaktiviṣayopāsanaṃ sāmāvayavasambaddhamityataḥ sāmāvayavāntarastobhākṣara viṣayāṇyupāsanāntarāṇi saṃhatānyupadiśyante 'nantaraṃ sāmāvayavasambaddhatvāviśeṣāt-ayaṃ vāvāyameva loko hāukāraḥ stobho rathantare sāmni prasiddhaḥ-"iyaṃ vai rathantaram" iti /
asmātsambandhasāmānyāddhāukārastobho 'yaṃ loka ityevamupāsīta /
vāyurhākāraḥ /
vāmadevye sāmani hāikāraḥ prasiddhaḥ /
vāyvapsambandhaśca vāmadevasya sāmno yonirityasmātsāmānyāddhāikāraṃ vāyudṛṣṭyopāsīta /
candramā athakāraḥ /
candradṛṣṭyāthakāramupāsīta /
anne hīdaṃ sthitam /
annātmā candraḥ /
thakārākārasāmānyācca /
ātmehakāraḥ /
iheti stobhaḥ pratyakṣo hyātmeti vyapadiśyate /
iheti ca stobhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And '<s>iha</s>' (here) is a <s>stobha</s> (exclamatory syllable).

children.text: tatsāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the similarity with that [direct presence].

children.text: agnirīkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Fire is the <s>ī</s>-syllable.'

children.text: īnidhanāni cā'gneyāni sarvāṇi sāmānītyatastatsāmānyāt //1 //
children.translated_text: And because all <s>Sāmans</s> whose <s>nidhana</s> (concluding part) contains the syllable '<s>ī</s>' belong to <s>Agni</s> (fire) — therefore, from that similarity. //1//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,13.1:] Since the meditation on the object of devotion is connected with the parts of the <s>Sāman</s> (chant), meditations concerning the <s>stobha</s>-syllables (exclamatory syllables) that belong to the parts of the <s>Sāman</s> are taught together, because of the absence of distinction in being connected with the parts of the <s>Sāman</s>. 'This very world is the <s>hāu</s>-syllable' — the <s>stobha</s> (exclamatory syllable) '<s>hāu</s>' is well-known in the <s>Rathantara Sāman</s> — 'This [earth] indeed is the <s>Rathantara</s>' [as stated in scripture]. Because of this general connection, one should meditate on the <s>hāu</s>-syllable as this world. 'Wind is the <s>hā</s>-syllable' — the <s>stobha</s> '<s>hāi</s>' is well-known in the <s>Vāmadevya Sāman</s>. And because of the connection between wind and water, [and because] the <s>Vāmadevya Sāman</s> has [that element] as its source — from this similarity, one should meditate on the <s>hāi</s>-syllable as wind. 'The moon is the <s>atha</s>-syllable' — one should meditate on the <s>atha</s>-syllable as the moon. [This is because] everything is established in food, and the moon is of the nature of food, and because of the similarity of the syllable '<s>tha</s>.' 'The self is the <s>iha</s>-syllable' — '<s>iha</s>' (here) is a <s>stobha</s>, and the self is spoken of as directly present.

children.text: START ChUp 1,13.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,13.2

children.text:
āditya ūkāraḥ |
nihava ekāraḥ |
viśve devā auhoyikāraḥ |
prajapatir hiṅkāraḥ |
prāṇaḥ svaraḥ |
annaṃ yā |
vāg virāṭ || ChUp_1,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: The sun is the <s>ū</s>-syllable. The <s>nihava</s> (invocation) is the <s>e</s>-syllable. The <s>Viśve Devas</s> (All-gods) are the <s>auhoyi</s>-syllable. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the <s>hiṅ</s>-syllable. <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is the <s>svara</s> (vowel). Food is '<s>yā</s>.' Speech is <s>Virāj</s>. || ChUp 1,13.2 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,13.2 āditya ūkāraḥ /
uccairūrdhvaṃ santamādityaṃ gāyantyūkāraścāyaṃ stobhaḥ /
ādityadaivatye sāmni stobha ū ityāditya ūkāraḥ /
nihava ityāhvānamekāraḥ stobhaḥ /
ehīti cā'hvayantīti tatsāmānyāt /
viśve devā auhoyikārovaiśvadevye sāmni darśanāt /
prajāpatirhiṅkāraḥ /
āniruktyāddhiṅkārasya cāvyaktatvāt /
prāṇaḥ svaraḥ /
svara iti stobhaḥ /
prāṇasya ca svarahetutvasāmānyāt /
annaṃ yā yā iti stobho 'nnam /
children.translated_text: 'Food is <s>yā</s>' — '<s>yā</s>' is a <s>stobha</s> [representing] food.

children.text: annena hīdaṃ yātītyatastatsāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Because everything moves (<s>yāti</s>) by means of food — therefore, from that similarity.

children.text: vāgiti stobho virāḍannaṃ devatāviśeṣo vā /
children.translated_text: 'Speech' is a <s>stobha</s> [representing] <s>Virāj</s>, [which is] food or a particular deity.

children.text: vairāje sāmni stobhadarśanāt //2 //
children.translated_text: Because [the stobha] is observed in the <s>Vairāja Sāman</s>. //2//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,13.2:] 'The sun is the <s>ū</s>-syllable' — they sing of the sun, [which is] high and above, with the <s>ū</s>-syllable, which is [also] a <s>stobha</s>. In the <s>Sāman</s> dedicated to the sun, the <s>stobha</s> is '<s>ū</s>' — therefore, 'the sun is the <s>ū</s>-syllable.' '<s>Nihava</s>' means invocation; the <s>e</s>-syllable is the <s>stobha</s> — and they invite saying 'come' (<s>ehi</s>) — because of that similarity. 'The <s>Viśve Devas</s> are the <s>auhoyi</s>-syllable' — because [this stobha] is observed in the <s>Sāman</s> dedicated to the <s>Viśve Devas</s>. '<s>Prajāpati</s> is the <s>hiṅ</s>-syllable' — because of <s>Prajāpati</s>'s inexpressibility, and because of the inarticulate nature of the <s>hiṅ</s>-syllable. '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>svara</s> (vowel)' — '<s>svara</s>' is a <s>stobha</s>; and because of the similarity with <s>Prāṇa</s> being the cause of sound (<s>svara</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 1,13.3
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,13.3

children.text: aniruktas trayodaśaḥ stobhaḥ saṃcaro huṅkāraḥ || ChUp_1,13.3 ||
children.translated_text: The thirteenth <s>stobha</s> (exclamatory syllable), which is indefinable, the variable one, is the <s>huṅ</s>-syllable. || ChUp 1,13.3 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_1,13.3 anirukto 'vyaktatvādidaṃ vedaṃ veti nirvaktuṃ na śakyata ityataḥ sañcaro vikalpyamānasvarūpa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,13.3:] 'Indefinable' (<s>anirukta</s>) — because of [its] inarticulate nature; 'this is such-and-such' cannot be specifically stated — therefore, [it is called] the variable one, whose form is subject to alternative interpretations — this is the meaning.

children.text: ko 'sāvityāha-trayodaśaḥ stobho huṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Who is that [indefinable stobha]? It says: the thirteenth <s>stobha</s>, the <s>huṅ</s>-syllable.

children.text: avyakto hyayamato 'niruktaviśeṣa evopāsya ityabhiprāyaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: Since this [syllable] is inarticulate, the intended meaning is that it should be meditated upon with this very indefinable characteristic. //3//

children.text: START ChUp 1,13.4
children.translated_text: START ChUp 1,13.4

children.text:
dugdhe 'smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ |
annavān annādo bhavati |
ya etām evaṃ sāmnām upaniṣadaṃ vedopaniṣadaṃ veda || ChUp_1,13.4 ||
children.translated_text: Speech yields its milk to him — the milk of speech [is speech itself]. He becomes rich in food and an eater of food — he who, knowing this, knows the <s>Upaniṣad</s> (secret teaching) of the <s>Sāmans</s>, [yes,] knows the <s>Upaniṣad</s>. || ChUp 1,13.4 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_1,13.4 dugdhe 'smai vāgdohamityādyuktārtham /
ya etāmevaṃ yathoktalakṣaṇāṃ sāmnāṃ sāmāvayavastobhākṣaraviṣayāmupaniṣadaṃ darśanaṃ veda tasyaitadyathoktaṃ phalamityarthaḥ /
dvirabhyāso 'dhyāyaparisamāptyarthaḥ /
sāmāvayavaviṣayopāsanāviśeṣaparimāptyartho veti //4 // //
children.translated_text: Or [the repetition is] for the purpose of completing [the series of] meditations concerning the parts of the <s>Sāman</s>. //4//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 1,13.4:] 'Speech yields its milk to him' — and so on — the meaning has [already] been stated. He who knows this <s>Upaniṣad</s> (secret teaching) of the <s>Sāmans</s> — [that is,] the meditation pertaining to the <s>stobha</s>-syllables of the parts of the <s>Sāman</s> — as described — for him, the fruit as stated [follows] — this is the meaning. The repetition [of 'knows the <s>Upaniṣad</s>'] is for the purpose of concluding the chapter.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣacchāṅkarabhāṣye prathamodhyāyasya trayodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the first chapter in the <s>Śāṅkara Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadbrāhmaṇe prathamodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: atha dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the second chapter.

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Om</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,1.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,1.1

children.text:
samastasya khalu sāmna upāsanaṃ sādhu |
yat khalu sādhu tat sāmety ācakṣate |
yad asādhu tad asāmeti || ChUp_2,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: The meditation on the entire <s>Sāman</s> is indeed good. Whatever is good, they call '<s>Sāman</s>'; whatever is not good, they call 'not-<s>Sāman</s>' (<s>asāman</s>). || ChUp 2,1.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,1.1
"omityetadakṣaram" ityādinā sāmāvayavaviṣayamupāsanamanekaphalamupadiṣṭam /
anantaraṃ ca stobhākṣaraviṣayamupāsanamuktam /
sarvathāpi sāmaikadeśasambaddhameva tadityathedānīṃ samaste sāmni samastasāmaviṣayāṇyupāsanāni vakṣyāmītyārabhate śrutiḥ /
yuktaṃ hyekadeśopāsanānantaramekadeśiviṣayamupāsanamucyata iti /
samastasya sarvāvayavaviśiṣṭasya pāñcabhaktikasya sāptabhaktikasya cetyarthaḥ /
khalviti vākyālaṅkārārthaḥ /
sāmna upāsanaṃ sādhu /
children.translated_text: The meditation on the <s>Sāman</s> is good.

children.text: samaste sāmni sādhudṛṣṭividhiparatvānna pūrvoktopāsananindārthatvaṃ sādhuśabdaḥ śobhanavācī /
children.translated_text: Because the purport [of the text] is the prescription of the meditation as 'good' regarding the entire <s>Sāman</s> — the word 'good' (<s>sādhu</s>) means 'beautiful,' not for the purpose of disparaging the previously stated meditations.

children.text: kathamavagamyata ityāha-yatkhalu loke sādhu śobhanamanavadyaṃ prasiddhaṃ tatsāmetyācakṣate kuśalāḥ /
children.translated_text: How is [this synonymy] understood? — It says: 'whatever is well-known in the world as good, beautiful, and blameless — that, the learned call <s>Sāman</s>.'

children.text: yadasādhu viparītaṃ tadasāmeti //1 //
children.translated_text: Whatever is not-good, [that is,] the opposite — that [they call] 'not-<s>Sāman</s>' (<s>asāman</s>). //1//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,1.1:] By 'Om, this syllable' and so forth, the meditation pertaining to the parts of the <s>Sāman</s>, yielding manifold fruits, has been taught. And next, the meditation concerning the <s>stobha</s>-syllables has been stated. In every way, that [meditation] was connected with a single part of the <s>Sāman</s> only — therefore, the <s>śruti</s> now commences: 'I shall now state meditations concerning the entire <s>Sāman</s>, pertaining to the whole <s>Sāman</s>.' For it is proper that, after the meditation on a single part, the meditation pertaining to the whole [should be taught]. 'Of the entire' — [meaning] that which is distinguished by all parts — having five sections or seven sections — this is the meaning. The word 'khalu' is for the adornment of the sentence.

children.text: START ChUp 2,1.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,1.2

children.text:
tad utāpy āhuḥ |
sāmnainam upāgād iti sādhunainam upāgād ity eva tad āhuḥ |
asāmnainam upāgād ity eva tad āhuḥ || ChUp_2,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: They also say: 'He approached him with <s>Sāman</s>' — meaning 'he approached him well.' 'He approached him without <s>Sāman</s>' — [meaning he approached him badly] — thus they say. || ChUp 2,1.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,1.2 tattatraiva sādhvasādhuvivekakaraṇa utāpyāhuḥ-sāmnainaṃ rājānaṃ sāmantaṃ copāgādupagatavān /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,1.2:] Regarding that very [distinction] between good and not-good — they also say: 'He approached this king or vassal with <s>Sāman</s>' — that is, he approached him.

children.text: ko 'sau yato 'sādhutvaprāptyāśaṅkā?sa ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who is he, regarding whom there is the suspicion of approaching with bad [intention]? That [minister] — this is the intended meaning.

children.text: śobhanābhiprāyeṇa sādhunainamupāgādityeva tattatrā'hurlaukikā bandhanādyasādhukāryamapaśyantaḥ /
children.translated_text: With the intention of [acting] well — 'he approached him well' — thus the worldly people say, not seeing any bad result such as imprisonment.

children.text: yatra punarviparyayo bandhanādyasādhukāryaṃ paśyanti tatrāsāmnainamupāgādityasādhunainamupāgādityeva tadāhuḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: But where there is the opposite — [where they] see bad results such as imprisonment — 'he approached him without <s>Sāman</s>' — meaning 'he approached him badly' — thus they say. //2//

children.text: START ChUp 2,1.3
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,1.3

children.text:
athotāpy āhuḥ |
sāma no bateti yat sādhu bhavati sādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ |
asāma no bateti yad asādhu bhavaty asādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ || ChUp_2,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: They also say: '<s>Sāma</s> indeed for us!' — [meaning] 'something good has come about for us!' — they say '<s>sādhu</s> (good) indeed!' And 'not-<s>Sāma</s> for us!' — [meaning] 'something bad has come about for us!' — they say 'not good indeed!' || ChUp 2,1.3 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,1.3 athotāpyāhuḥ svasaṃvedyaṃ sāma no 'smākaṃ batetyanukampayataḥ saṃvṛttamityāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,1.3:] They also say, regarding what is experienced by oneself: '<s>Sāma</s> for us!' — meaning, [with the compassionate exclamation] 'alas!' — '[good] has come about' — thus they say.

children.text: etattairuktaṃ bhavati yatsādhu bhavati sādhu vatetyeva tadāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: What they have said amounts to this: 'whatever is good — <s>sādhu</s> indeed!' — thus they say.

children.text: viparyaye jāte 'sāma no bateti /
children.translated_text: When the opposite has occurred — 'not-<s>Sāma</s> for us!'

children.text: yadasādhu bhavatyasādhu batetyeva tadāhuḥ tasmātsāmasādhuśabdayorekārthatvaṃ siddham //3 //
children.translated_text: Whatever is not good — 'not good indeed!' — thus they say. Therefore, the synonymy of <s>Sāma</s> and <s>sādhu</s> is established. //3//

children.text: START ChUp 2,1.4
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,1.4

children.text: sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān sādhu sāmety upāste 'bhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo dharmā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nameyuḥ || ChUp_2,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing this, meditates on '<s>Sāman</s> is good' — it is likely that good qualities (<s>dharmas</s>) would come to him and attend upon him — he who, knowing this, meditates on the entire <s>Sāman</s> [as] good. || ChUp 2,1.4 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,1.4 ataḥ sa yaḥ kaścitsādhu sāmeti sādhuguṇavatsāmetyupāste samastaṃ sāma sādhuguṇavadvidvāṃstasyaitatphalamabhyāśo ha kṣipraṃ ha;yaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇārthamenamupāsakaṃ sādhavaḥ śobhanā dharmāḥ śrutismṛtyaviruddhā ā ca gaccheyurāgaccheyuśca na kevalamāgaccheyurupa ca nameyurupanameyuśca bhogyatvenopatiṣṭheyurityarthaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,1.4:] Therefore, whoever meditates on the entire <s>Sāman</s> as 'good is <s>Sāman</s>' — [that is, meditates on] the entire <s>Sāman</s> as possessing the quality of goodness, knowing [this connection] — the fruit of this [meditation] is: 'it is likely — quickly, indeed — that' — the word 'yad' serves to qualify the action — 'good <s>dharmas</s> (virtues), not opposed to <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, would come to him, the meditator — and not only come, but also attend upon him' — that is, they would present themselves as objects of enjoyment — this is the meaning. //4//

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,2.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,2.1

children.text:
lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta |
pṛthivī hiṅkāraḥ |
agniḥ prastāvaḥ |
antarikṣam udgīthaḥ |
ādityaḥ pratihāraḥ |
dyaur nidhanam |
ity ūrdhveṣu || ChUp_2,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in the worlds. The earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Fire is the <s>prastāva</s> (prelude). The intermediate space is the <s>udgītha</s> (chant). The sun is the <s>pratihāra</s> (response). Heaven is the <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion). This is in the upward [order]. || ChUp 2,2.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,2.1 kāni punastāni sādhudṛṣṭiviśiṣṭāni samastāni sāmānyupāsyānīti /
imāni tānyucyante lokeṣu pañcavidhamityādīni /
nanu lokādidṛṣṭyā tānyupāsyāni sādhudṛṣṭyā ceti viruddham /
na /
sādhvarthasya lokādikāryeṣu kāraṇasyānugatatvāt mṛdādivadghaṭādivikāreṣu /
sādhuśabdavācyor'tho dharmo brahma vā sarvathāpi lokādikāryeṣvanugatam /
ato yathā yatra ghaṭādidṛṣṭirmṛdādidṛṣṭyanugataiva sā /
tathā sādhudṛṣṭyanugataiva lokādidṛṣṭiḥ /
dharmādikāryatvāllokādīnām /
yadyapi kāraṇatvamaviśiṣṭaṃ brahmadharmayoḥ, tathāpi dharma eva sādhuśabdavācya iti yuktaṃ"sādhukārī sādhurbhavatī"ti dharmaviṣaye sādhuśabdaprayogāt /
nanu lokādikāryeṣu kāraṇasyānugatatvādarthaprāptaiva taddṛṣṭiriti sādhu sāmetyupāsta iti na vaktavyam /
na /
śāsragamyatvāttaddṛṣṭeḥ /
sarvatra hi śāsraprāpitā eva dharmā upāsyā na vidyamānā apyaśāsrīyāḥ /
lokeṣu pṛthivyādiṣu pañcavidhaṃ pañcabhaktibhedena pañcaprakāraṃ sādhusamastaṃ sāmopāsīta /
katham /
pṛthivo hiṅkāraḥ /
lokeṣviti yā saptamī tāṃ prathamātvena vi
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,2.1:] What are those meditations on the entire <s>Sāman</s>, qualified by the vision of 'good'? — These are now stated: 'in the worlds, as fivefold,' and so forth. [Objection:] 'But they are to be meditated upon with the vision of worlds and the like, and also with the vision of good — is this not contradictory?' No. Because the good, [which is] the meaning of the word <s>sādhu</s> — [being] the cause [of all effects, namely] <s>dharma</s> (virtue) or <s>Brahman</s> — pervades [all] effects such as the worlds, just as clay [pervades] modifications such as pots. [Regardless of] whether the causality [belongs] equally to <s>Brahman</s> and <s>dharma</s>, it is proper that [only] <s>dharma</s> is denoted by the word <s>sādhu</s>, because the word <s>sādhu</s> is used in connection with <s>dharma</s> — as in 'one who performs good [deeds] becomes good.' [Objection:] 'Since the cause pervades [all] effects such as the worlds, the vision of that [cause] would follow as a matter of course — so it need not be stated that one meditates as good <s>Sāman</s>.' No. Because that vision is [only] to be obtained from scripture. For everywhere, only <s>dharmas</s> obtained through scripture are to be meditated upon — not even existing [truths], if they are non-scriptural. 'In the worlds,' [that is,] in the earth and the like — one should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold — [meaning] having five sections, five divisions, five types, [as] good [and] entire. How? 'The earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.' The locative [case] 'in the worlds' is to be construed as the nominative [for] the meditation—

children.text: START ChUp 2,2.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,2.2

children.text:
athāvṛtteṣu |
dyaur hiṅkāraḥ |
ādityaḥ prastāvaḥ |
antarikṣam udgīthaḥ |
agniḥ pratihāraḥ |
pṛthivī nidhanam || ChUp_2,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the downward [order]: heaven is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. The sun is the <s>prastāva</s>. The intermediate space is the <s>udgītha</s>. Fire is the <s>pratihāra</s>. The earth is the <s>nidhana</s>. || ChUp 2,2.2 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,2.2 athā'vṛtteṣvavāṅmukheṣu pañcavidhamucyate sāmopāsanam /
gatyāgativiśiṣṭā hi lokāḥ /
yathā te tathādṛṣṭyaiva sāmopāsanaṃ vidhīyate yato 'ta āvṛtteṣu lokeṣu /
dyaurhiṅkāraḥ prāthamyāt /
ādityaḥ prastāvaḥ /
udite hyāditye prastūyante karmāṇi prāṇinām /
antarikṣamudgīthaḥ pūrvavat /
agniḥ pratihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Fire is the <s>pratihāra</s> (response).'

children.text: prāṇibhiḥ pratiharaṇādagneḥ /
children.translated_text: Because fire is taken back (<s>pratiharaṇa</s>) by living beings.

children.text: pṛthivī nidhanam /
children.translated_text: 'The earth is the <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion).'

children.text: tata āgatānāmiha nidhanāt //2 //
children.translated_text: Because those who have come from there [heaven] find their final resting place (<s>nidhana</s>) here. //2//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,2.2:] Now, 'in the downward [order]' — [that is,] in the downward-facing [sequence] — the fivefold meditation on the <s>Sāman</s> is stated. For the worlds possess the characteristics of going and coming. Just as they are [in the upward order], so too the meditation on the <s>Sāman</s> is prescribed with that very vision [in the downward order] — since [the text says] 'in the reverse [order] of the worlds.' 'Heaven is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>' — because of [its] being first. 'The sun is the <s>prastāva</s>' — for when the sun has risen, the activities of living beings are commenced (<s>prastūyante</s>). 'The intermediate space is the <s>udgītha</s>' — as before.

children.text: START ChUp 2,2.3
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,2.3

children.text: kalpante hāsmai lokā ūrdhvāś cāvṛttaś ca ya etad evaṃ vidvāṃl lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste || ChUp_2,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: The worlds, both upward and downward, become favorable to him who, knowing this, meditates on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in the worlds. || ChUp 2,2.3 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,2.3 upāsanaphalaṃ-kalpante samarthā bhavanti hāsmai lokā ūrdhvāścā'vṛttāśca gatyāgativiśiṣṭā bhogyatvena vyavatiṣṭhanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,2.3:] The fruit of the meditation: 'the worlds become favorable' — that is, they become capable — 'for him' — the worlds, both upward and downward, distinguished by going and coming, present themselves as objects of enjoyment — this is the meaning.

children.text: ya etadevaṃ vidvāṃllokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ samastaṃ sādhu sāmetyupāsta iti sarvatra yojanā pañcavidhe saptavidhe ca //3//
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing this, meditates on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold, [as] entire [and] good, in the worlds' — this construction [applies] throughout, in both the fivefold and sevenfold [meditations]. //3//

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
vṛṣṭau pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta |
purovāto hiṅkāraḥ |
megho jāyate sa prastāvaḥ |
varṣati sa udgīthaḥ |
vidyotate stanayati sa pratihāraḥ || ChUp_2,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in rain. The wind blowing before [the rain] is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. A cloud is born — that is the <s>prastāva</s> (prelude). It rains — that is the <s>udgītha</s> (chant). It lightens and thunders — that is the <s>pratihāra</s> (response). || ChUp 2,3.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,3.1 vṛṣṭau pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta /
lokasthitervṛṣṭinimittatvādānantaryam /
purovāto hiṅkāraḥ /
purovātādyudgrahaṇāntā hi vṛṣṭiḥ /
yathā sāma hiṅkārādinidhanāntam /
ataḥ purovāto hiṅkāraḥ /
prāthamyāt /
megho jāyate sa prastāvaḥ /
prāvṛṣi meghajanane vṛṣṭeḥ prastāva iti hi prasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: For in the rainy season, the birth of a cloud is the well-known prelude to rain.

children.text: varṣati sa udgīthaḥ śraiṣṭhyāt /
children.translated_text: 'It rains — that is the <s>udgītha</s>' — because of [its] preeminence.

children.text: vidyotate stanayati sa pratihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It lightens and thunders — that is the <s>pratihāra</s> (response).'

children.text: pratihṛtatvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: Because [lightning and thunder] are held back (<s>pratihṛta</s>) [as a response]. //1//

[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,3.1:] 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in rain.' The sequence [of this topic] is due to the sustenance of the worlds being caused by rain. 'The wind blowing before [the rain] is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>' — for rain [extends] from the preceding wind up to the cessation [of rain]. Just as the <s>Sāman</s> [extends] from the <s>hiṅkāra</s> to the <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion). Therefore, the preceding wind is the <s>hiṅkāra</s> — because of [its] being first. 'A cloud is born — that is the <s>prastāva</s>' —

children.text: START ChUp 2,3.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,3.2

children.text: udgṛhṇāti tan nidhanaṃ varṣayati ha ya etad evaṃ vidvān vṛṣṭau pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste || ChUp_2,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: [The rain] ceases — that is the <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion). He brings rain — he who, knowing this, meditates on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in rain. || ChUp 2,3.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,3.2 udgṛhṇāti tannidhanam /
samāptisāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the similarity with [the Sāman's] completion.

children.text: phalamupāsanasya-varśati hāsmā icchātaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fruit of the meditation: 'it rains for him' — at [his] will.

children.text: tathā varṣayati hāsatyāmapi vṛṣṭau /
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'he causes it to rain' — even at an untimely [moment].

children.text: ya etadityādi pūrvavat //2//
children.translated_text: 'He who knows this' — and so forth — as before. //2//
[Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya on 2,3.2:] '[The rain] ceases — that is the <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion).'

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,4.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,4.1

children.text:
sarvāsv apsu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta |
megho yat saṃplavate sa hiṅkāraḥ |
yad varṣati sa prastāvaḥ |
yāḥ prācyaḥ syandante sa udgīthaḥ |
yāḥ pratīcyaḥ sa pratihāraḥ |
samudro nidhanam || ChUp_2,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in all the waters. When a cloud gathers, that is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>. When it rains, that is the <s>Prastāva</s>. [The waters] that flow eastward — that is the <s>Udgītha</s>. [The waters] that flow westward — that is the <s>Pratihāra</s>. The ocean is the <s>Nidhana</s>. (ChUp 2.4.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,4.1 sarvāsvapsu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta /
vṛṣṭipūrvakatvātsarvāsāmapāmānantaryam /
megho yatsaṃplavata ekībhāvenetaretaraṃ ghanībhavati megho yadonnatastadā saṃplavata ityucyate meghastadāpāmārambhaḥ sa hiṅkāraḥ /
yadvarṣati sa prastāvaḥ /
āpaḥ sarvato vyāptuṃ prastutāḥ /
yāḥ prācyaḥ syandante sa udgīthaḥ śraiṣṭhyāt /
children.translated_text: [The waters] that flow eastward — that is the <s>Udgītha</s>, because of [their] pre-eminence.

children.text: yāḥ pratīcyaḥ sa pratihāraḥ pratiśabdasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: [The waters] that flow westward — that is the <s>Pratihāra</s>, because of the similarity with the word 'prati' (back).

children.text: samudro nidhanam /
children.translated_text: The ocean is the <s>Nidhana</s>.

children.text: tannidhanatvādapām //1 //
children.translated_text: Because [the ocean] is the final resting-place of the waters. (2.4.1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.4.1:] One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in all the waters. Because all waters are preceded by rain, there is a [natural] sequence. When a cloud gathers (<s>saṃplavate</s>) — [that is,] when [the waters] merge into one, becoming dense — when the cloud rises, then it is said to gather; the cloud at that time is the beginning of waters — that is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>. When it rains — that is the <s>Prastāva</s>. The waters are set forth (<s>prastuta</s>) to pervade everywhere.

children.text: START ChUp 2,4.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.4.2]

children.text: na hāpsu praity apsumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān sarvāsv apsu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste || ChUp_2,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: One does not perish in water. One becomes possessed of water. [This is the fruit for] one who, knowing this, meditates upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in all the waters. (ChUp 2.4.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,4.2 na hāpsu praiti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.4.2:] One does not perish in water.

children.text: necchati cet /
children.translated_text: If one does not wish [to perish].

children.text: apsumānaṃmānbhavati phalam //2//
children.translated_text: One becomes possessed of water — this is the fruit. (2.4.2)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,5.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.5.1]

children.text:
ṛtuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta |
vasanto hiṅkāraḥ |
grīṣmaḥ prastāvaḥ |
varṣā udgīthaḥ |
śarat pratihāraḥ |
hemanto nidhanam || ChUp_2,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in the seasons. Spring is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>. Summer is the <s>Prastāva</s>. The rainy season is the <s>Udgītha</s>. Autumn is the <s>Pratihāra</s>. Winter is the <s>Nidhana</s>. (ChUp 2.5.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,5.1 ṝtuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta /
ṝtuvyavasthāyā yathoktāmbunimittatvādānantaryam /
vasanto hiṅkāraḥ /
prāthamyāt /
grīṣmaḥ prastāvaḥ /
yavādisaṃgrahaḥ prastūyate hi prāvṛḍartham /
varṣā udgīthaḥ prādhānyāt /
śaratpratihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Autumn is the <s>Pratihāra</s>.

children.text: rogiṇāṃ mṛtānāṃ ca pratiharaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the carrying away (<s>pratiharaṇa</s>) of the sick and the dead.

children.text: hemanto nidhanam /
children.translated_text: Winter is the <s>Nidhana</s>.

children.text: nivāte nidhanātprāṇinām //1 //
children.translated_text: Because of the cessation (<s>nidhana</s>) of living beings in [the season] without wind. (2.5.1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.5.1:] One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in the seasons. The sequence [follows] because the arrangement of seasons has the cause stated [in the preceding section on] waters. Spring is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>, because of [its] being first. Summer is the <s>Prastāva</s>. The gathering of barley and the like is set forth (<s>prastūyate</s>) for the purpose of the rainy season. The rainy season is the <s>Udgītha</s>, because of [its] pre-eminence.

children.text: START ChUp 2,5.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.5.2]

children.text: kalpante hāsmā ṛtava ṛtumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ṛtuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste || ChUp_2,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: The seasons arrange themselves for him. He becomes possessed of seasons — [this is the fruit for] one who, knowing this, meditates upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in the seasons. (ChUp 2.5.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,5.2 phalaṃ-kalpante ha ṛtuvyavasthānurūpaṃ bhogyatvenāsmā upāsakāyartavaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.5.2:] The fruit: the seasons arrange themselves — in accordance with the arrangement of seasons — for him, the worshipper, as objects of enjoyment.

children.text: ṛtumānārtavairbhogaiśca sampanno bhavatītyarthaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of seasons — meaning he becomes endowed with seasonal enjoyments. This is the meaning. (2.5.2)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,6.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.6.1]

children.text:
paśuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta |
ajā hiṅkāraḥ |
avayaḥ prastāvaḥ |
gāva udgīthaḥ |
aśvaḥ pratihāraḥ |
puruṣo nidhanam || ChUp_2,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in animals. Goats are the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>. Sheep are the <s>Prastāva</s>. Cows are the <s>Udgītha</s>. Horses are the <s>Pratihāra</s>. Man is the <s>Nidhana</s>. (ChUp 2.6.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,6.1 paśuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta /
samyagvṛtteṣvṛtuṣu paśavyaḥ kāla ityānantaryam /
ajā hiṅkāraḥ /
prādhānyāt prāthamyādvā /
"ajaḥ paśūnāṃ prathama"iti śruteḥ /
avayaḥ prastāvaḥ /
sāhacaryadarśanādajādīnām /
gāvaḥ udgīthaḥ /
śraiṣṭhyāt /
aśvāḥ pratihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Horses are the <s>Pratihāra</s>.

children.text: pratiharaṇātpuruśāṇām /
children.translated_text: Because of the carrying back (<s>pratiharaṇa</s>) of men [in battle].

children.text: puruṣo nidhanam /
children.translated_text: Man is the <s>Nidhana</s>.

children.text: puruṣāśrayatvātpaśūnām //1 //
children.translated_text: Because animals depend on man [as their final resting-place]. (2.6.1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.6.1:] One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in animals. When the seasons are well-regulated, the time for cattle [is favorable] — hence the sequence. Goats are the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>, because of [their] pre-eminence or primacy. [As the <s>Śruti</s> says:] 'The goat [was] the first among animals.' Sheep are the <s>Prastāva</s>, because of the observed companionship of goats and the like. Cows are the <s>Udgītha</s>, because of [their] pre-eminence.

children.text: START ChUp 2,6.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.6.2]

children.text: bhavanti hāsya paśavaḥ paśumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān paśuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste || ChUp_2,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: Animals come to belong to him. He becomes possessed of animals — [this is the fruit for] one who, knowing this, meditates upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in animals. (ChUp 2.6.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,6.2 phalaṃ-bhavanti hāsya paśavaḥ paśumānbhavati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.6.2:] The fruit: animals come to belong to him. He becomes possessed of animals.

children.text: paśuphalaiśca bhogatyāgādibhiryujyata ityarthaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Meaning he is endowed with the fruits of animals — enjoyment, sacrifice, and the like. This is the meaning. (2.6.2)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,7.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.7.1]

children.text:
prāṇeṣu pañcavidhaṃ parovarīyaḥ sāmopāsīta |
prāṇo hiṅkāraḥ |
vāk prastāvaḥ |
cakṣur udgīthaḥ |
śrotraṃ pratihāraḥ |
mano nidhanam |
parovarīyāṃsi vā etāni || ChUp_2,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s>, the 'progressively greater' (<s>parovarīyas</s>), in the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital functions). <s>Prāṇa</s> (smell) is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>. Speech (<s>Vāc</s>) is the <s>Prastāva</s>. The eye is the <s>Udgītha</s>. The ear is the <s>Pratihāra</s>. The mind is the <s>Nidhana</s>. These are indeed the 'progressively greater.' (ChUp 2.7.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,7.1 prāṇeṣu pañcavidhaṃ parovarīyaḥ sāmopāsīta /
paraṃparaṃ varīyastvaguṇavatprāṇadṛṣṭiviśiṣṭaṃ sāmopāsītetyarthaḥ /
prāṇo ghrāṇaṃ hiṅkāraḥ /
uttarottaravarīyasāṃ prāthamyāt /
vākprastāvaḥ /
vācā hi prastūyate sarvam /
vāgvarīyasī prāṇāt /
aprāptamapyucyate vācā, prāptasyaiva tu gandhasya grāhakaḥ prāṇaḥ /
cakṣurudgīthaḥ /
vāco bahutaraviṣayaṃ prakāśayati cakṣurato varīyo vācaḥ, udgīthaḥ /
śraiṣṭhyāt /
śrotraṃ pratihāraḥ /
pratihṛtatvāt /
varīyastvaṃ ca śrotrānmanasaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the ear is greater than the mind.

children.text: sarvendriyaviṣayavyāpakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because it pervades the objects of all the sense-faculties.

children.text: atīndriyaviṣayo 'pi manaso gocara eveti /
children.translated_text: Even the supersensory [realm] is indeed within the scope of the mind.

children.text: yathoktahetubhyaḥ parovarīyāṃsi prāṇādīni vā etāni //1 //
children.translated_text: For the reasons stated, the <s>prāṇas</s> beginning with [the organ of] smell are 'progressively greater.' (2.7.1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.7.1:] One should meditate upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s>, the 'progressively greater,' in the <s>prāṇas</s>. Meaning: one should meditate upon the <s>Sāman</s>, distinguished by the view of [each being] successively greater in the quality of greatness — [as applied to] <s>Prāṇa</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s>, [meaning here] the organ of smell, is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>, because of the primacy among [the senses arranged as] each successively greater. Speech is the <s>Prastāva</s>, for everything is set forth by speech. Speech is greater than <s>Prāṇa</s> (smell): even what is not [directly] reached [by smell] is expressed by speech, whereas <s>Prāṇa</s> [the organ of smell] is a grasper only of [an object's] fragrance that has been reached. The eye is the <s>Udgītha</s>. The eye illuminates a greater [range of] objects than speech, therefore it is greater than speech — [hence it is] the <s>Udgītha</s>, because of [its] pre-eminence. The ear is the <s>Pratihāra</s>, because of [its being that which] receives (<s>pratihṛta</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 2,7.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.7.2]

children.text:
parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān prāṇeṣu pañcavidhaṃ parovarīyaḥ sāmopāste |
iti tu pañcavidhasya || ChUp_2,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: The progressively greater comes to belong to him. He conquers the progressively greater worlds — [this is the fruit for] one who, knowing this, meditates upon the fivefold <s>Sāman</s>, the 'progressively greater,' in the <s>prāṇas</s>. Thus regarding the fivefold [<s>Sāman</s>]. (ChUp 2.7.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,7.2 etaddṛṣṭyā viśiṣṭaṃ yaḥ parovarīyaḥ sāmopāste parovarīyo hāsya jīvanaṃ bhavatītyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.7.2:] One who meditates upon the <s>Sāman</s>, the 'progressively greater,' distinguished by this vision — the progressively greater life comes to belong to him. This has been stated [as the meaning].

children.text: iti tu pañcavidhasya sāmna upāsanamuktamiti saptavidhe vakṣyamāṇaviṣaye buddhisamādhānārtham /
children.translated_text: 'Thus regarding the fivefold [<s>Sāman</s>]' — the meditation on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> has been stated. [This is said] for the purpose of mental composure regarding the sevenfold [<s>Sāman</s>] that will be stated [next].

children.text: nirapekṣo hi pañcavidhe, vakṣyamāṇe buddhiṃ samādhitsati //2//
children.translated_text: For [the student], having completed [the study of] the fivefold, now wishes to compose [his] mind regarding what will be stated [next]. (2.7.2)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
atha saptavidhasya |
vāci saptavidh.am sāmopāsīta |
yat kiṃca vāco hum iti sa hiṅkāraḥ |
yat preti sa prastāvaḥ |
yad eti sa ādiḥ || ChUp_2,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the sevenfold [<s>Sāman</s>]. One should meditate upon the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> in speech. Whatever of speech is '<s>hum</s>' — that is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>. Whatever is '<s>pra</s>' — that is the <s>Prastāva</s>. Whatever is '<s>ā</s>' — that is the <s>Ādi</s> (beginning). (ChUp 2.8.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,8.1 athānantaraṃ saptavidhasya samastasya sāmna upāsanaṃ sādhvidamārabhyate /
vācīti saptamī pūrvavat /
vāgdṛṣṭiviśiṣṭaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsītetyarthaḥ /
yatkiñca vācaḥ śabdasya humiti yo viśeṣaḥ sa hiṅkāro hakārasāmānyāt /
yatpreti śabdarūpaṃ sa prastāvaḥ prasāmānyāt /
yat-ā, iti sa ādiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is '<s>ā</s>' — that is the <s>Ādi</s> (beginning).

children.text: ākārasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the similarity with the syllable '<s>ā</s>.'

children.text: ādirityoṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ādi</s> [here means] <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

children.text: sarvāditvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: Because it is the beginning of all. (2.8.1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.8.1:] 'Now, next' — the meditation on the entire <s>Sāman</s> with its divisions of components — the sevenfold — is well begun here. 'In speech' — the locative is as before [indicating the basis of meditation]. Meaning: one should meditate upon the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> distinguished by the vision of speech. Whatever particular [aspect] of speech, of sound, [that corresponds to] '<s>hum</s>' — that is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>, because of the similarity with the syllable 'ha.' Whatever has the form '<s>pra</s>' — that is the <s>Prastāva</s>, because of the similarity with 'pra.'

children.text: START ChUp 2,8.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.8.2]

children.text:
yad ud iti sa udgīthaḥ |
yat pratīti sa pratihāraḥ |
