yad upeti sa upadravaḥ |
yan nīti tan nidhanam || ChUp_2,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is '<s>ud</s>' — that is the <s>Udgītha</s>. Whatever is '<s>prati</s>' — that is the <s>Pratihāra</s>. Whatever is '<s>upa</s>' — that is the <s>Upadrava</s>. Whatever is '<s>ni</s>' — that is the <s>Nidhana</s>. (ChUp 2.8.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,8.2 yaduditi sa udgīthaḥ /
phatpūrvatvādudgīthasya /
yatpratīti sa pratihāraḥ /
pratisāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: because of the similarity with [the prefix] 'prati.'

children.text: yadupeti sa upadrava upopakramatvādupadravasya /
children.translated_text: Whatever is '<s>upa</s>' — that is the <s>Upadrava</s>, because of [<s>upa</s> signifying] 'approaching,' [which is the nature] of the <s>Upadrava</s>.

children.text: yannīti tannidhanam /
children.translated_text: Whatever is '<s>ni</s>' — that is the <s>Nidhana</s>.

children.text: niśabdasāmānyāt //2 //
children.translated_text: Because of the similarity with the syllable '<s>ni</s>' [in <s>nidhana</s>]. (2.8.2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.8.2:] Whatever is '<s>ud</s>' — that is the <s>Udgītha</s>, because the <s>Udgītha</s> is preceded by [the syllable] '<s>ud</s>.' Whatever is '<s>prati</s>' — that is the <s>Pratihāra</s>,

children.text: START ChUp 2,8.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.8.3]

children.text:
dugdhe 'smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ |
annavān annādo bhavati |
ya etad evaṃ vidvān vāci saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste || ChUp_2,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: Speech yields its milk for him — the milk of speech. He becomes possessor of food and an eater of food — one who, knowing this, meditates upon the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> in speech. (ChUp 2.8.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,8.3 dugdhe 'smā ityādyuktārtham //3//
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.8.3:] 'Speech yields its milk for him' and so forth — the meaning has been stated [previously]. (2.8.3)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth section (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of the second chapter in the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
atha khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta |
sarvadā samas tena sāma |
māṃ prati māṃ pratīti sarveṇa samas tena sāma || ChUp_2,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now then, one should meditate upon the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> in that yonder sun. [The sun is] always the same (<s>sama</s>), hence [it is] <s>Sāman</s>. 'Toward me, toward me' — [the sun is] the same with respect to all, hence [it is] <s>Sāman</s>. (ChUp 2.9.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,9.1 avayavamātre sāmnyādityadṛṣṭiḥ pañcavidheṣūktā prathame cādhyāye /
athedānīṃ khalvamumādityaṃ samaste sāmnyavayavavibhāgaśo 'dhyasya saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta /
kathaṃ punaḥ sāmatvamādityasyeti /
ucyate /
udgīthatve hetuvadādityasya sāmatve hetuḥ /
ko 'sau, sarvadā samo vṛddhikṣayābhāvāttena hetunā sāmā'dityo māṃ prati māṃ pratīti tulyāṃ buddhimutpādayati /
children.translated_text: What is that? [The sun is] always the same (<s>sama</s>) — because of the absence of increase and decrease — for that reason the sun is <s>Sāman</s>. 'Toward me, toward me' — [the sun] produces equal cognition [in all],

children.text: ataḥ sarveṇa samo 'taḥ sāma samatvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore [it is] the same with all. Hence [it is] <s>Sāman</s>, because of sameness. This is the meaning.

children.text: udgīthabhaktisāmānyavacanādeva lokādiṣūktasāmānyāddhiṅkārāditvaṃ gamyata iti hiṅkārāditve kāraṇaṃ noktam /
children.translated_text: From the very general statement of the <s>Udgītha</s> portion — [and] from the generality stated regarding the worlds and the like — the [identification with] <s>Hiṅkāra</s> and so forth is understood; therefore no [separate] reason for [the identification with] <s>Hiṅkāra</s> and the rest has been stated.

children.text: sāmatve punaḥ savituranuktaṃ kāraṇaṃ na subodhamiti samatvamuktam //1 //
children.translated_text: But the reason for [the sun being] <s>Sāman</s> — which was not stated [elsewhere] for <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun) — is not easily understood; hence the sameness has been stated. (2.9.1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.9.1:] The vision of the sun as a component [of the <s>Sāman</s>] was stated in the fivefold [meditations] and also in the first chapter. Now then, one should meditate upon that yonder sun — superimposing [upon it] the division of components of the entire <s>Sāman</s> — as the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>. But how is the sun [identified as] <s>Sāman</s>? It is said: just as a reason was [given] for [the sun's being identified with] the <s>Udgītha</s>, [so too] there is a reason for [the sun's being identified with] the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,9.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.9.2]

children.text:
tasminn imāni sarvāṇi bhūtāny anvāyattānīti vidyāt |
tasya yat purodayāt sa hiṅkāraḥ |
tad asya paśavo 'nvāyattāḥ |
tasmāt te hiṅkurvanti |
hiṅkārabhājino hy etasya sāmnaḥ || ChUp_2,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: One should know that all these beings are dependent upon him [the sun]. That which [is the sun's phase] before rising — that is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>. The animals are dependent upon that. Therefore they make the sound '<s>hiṅ</s>' [at dawn]. For they partake of the <s>Hiṅkāra</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>. (ChUp 2.9.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,9.2 tasminnāditye 'vayavavibhāgaśa imāni vakṣyamāṇāni sarvāmi bhūtānyanvāyattānyanugatānyādityamupajīvyatveneti vidyāt /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.9.2:] In that sun — divided into components — all these beings that will be described are dependent, following [the sun] as living by means of [it] — one should know this.

children.text: kathaṃ, tasyā'dityasya yatpurodayāddharmarūpaṃ sa hiṅkāro bhaktistatredaṃ sāmānyaṃ yattasya hiṅkārabhaktirūpaṃ tadasyā'dityasya sāmnaḥ paśavo gavādayo 'nvāyattā anugatāstadbhaktirūpamupajīvantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: How? That which is the nature [of the sun] before rising — that is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>, a particular division. Here the generality is this: whatever constitutes the nature of the <s>Hiṅkāra</s> division of that sun's <s>Sāman</s> — upon that [division] the animals, cows and the like, are dependent, following [it] — meaning they live upon that particular division. This is the meaning.

children.text: yasmādevaṃ tasmātte hiṅkurvanti paśavaḥ prāgudayāt /
children.translated_text: Because this is so, therefore the animals make the sound '<s>hiṅ</s>' before sunrise.

children.text: tasmāddhiṅkārabhājino hyetasyā'dityākhyasya sāmnaḥ tadbhaktibhajanaśīlatvāddhi ta evaṃ vartante //2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore they partake of the <s>Hiṅkāra</s> of this <s>Sāman</s> known as the sun — because they are inclined to partake of that division, they behave thus. (2.9.2)

children.text: START ChUp 2,9.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.9.3]

children.text:
atha yat prathamodite sa prastāvaḥ |
tad asya manuṣyā anvāyattāḥ |
tasmāt te prastutikāmāḥ praśaṃsākāmāḥ |
prastāvabhājino hy etasya sāmnaḥ || ChUp_2,9.3 ||
children.translated_text: Now, that which [is the sun's phase] when first risen — that is the <s>Prastāva</s>. Humans are dependent upon that. Therefore they desire praise and commendation. For they partake of the <s>Prastāva</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>. (ChUp 2.9.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,9.3 atha yatprathamodite savitṛrūpaṃ tadasyā'dityākhyāsya sāmnaḥ sa prastāvastadasya manuṣyā anvāyattāḥ pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.9.3:] 'Now, that which [is the sun's] form when first risen' — that is the <s>Prastāva</s> of this <s>Sāman</s> known as the sun. Humans are dependent upon that — as before.

children.text: tasmātte prastutiṃ praśaṃsāṃ kāmayante /
children.translated_text: Therefore they desire praise and commendation.

children.text: yasmātprastāvabhājino hyetasya sāmnaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: Because they partake of the <s>Prastāva</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>. (2.9.3)

children.text: START ChUp 2,9.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.9.4]

children.text:
atha yat saṃgavavelāyāṃ sa ādiḥ |
tad asya vayāṃsy anvāyattāni |
tasmāt tāny antarikṣe 'nārambhaṇāny ādāyātmānaṃ paripatanti |
ādibhājīni hy etasya sāmnaḥ || ChUp_2,9.4 ||
children.translated_text: Now, that which [is the sun's phase] at the time of the gathering of cows (<s>saṅgava</s>) — that is the <s>Ādi</s>. The birds are dependent upon that. Therefore they fly about in the sky, unsupported, sustaining themselves [in flight]. For they partake of the <s>Ādi</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>. (ChUp 2.9.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,9.4 atha yatsaṅgavavelāyāṃ gavāṃ raśmīnāṃ saṅgamanaṃ saṅgamo yasyāṃ velāyāṃ, gavāṃ vā vatsaiḥ sā saṅgavavelā tasminkāle yatsāvitraṃ rūpaṃ sa ādirbhaktiviśeṣa oṅkārastadasya vayāṃsi pakṣiṇo 'nvāyattāni /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.9.4:] 'Now, that which [is the sun's phase] at the time of the gathering of cows (<s>saṅgava</s>)' — [that is,] the time at which the gathering (<s>saṅgama</s>) of the cows, [meaning] the rays, [occurs]; or [the time at which] the cows [are gathered] with [their] calves — that is the <s>saṅgava</s> time. At that time, the form of <s>Savitṛ</s> — that is the <s>Ādi</s>, the particular division [corresponding to] the <s>Oṃkāra</s>. The birds, the winged ones, are dependent upon that.

children.text: yata evaṃ tasmāttāni vayāṃstantarikṣe 'nārambaṇānyanālambanānyātmānamādāyā'tmānamevā'lambanatvena gṛhītvā paripatanti gacchantyata ākārasāmānyādādibhaktibhājīni hyetasya sāmnaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: Because this is so, therefore those birds, in the sky, unsupported — [that is,] without any support — sustaining themselves, having taken themselves as their own support, fly about, go forth. Because of the similarity with the syllable '<s>ā</s>' [in <s>Ādi</s>], they partake of the <s>Ādi</s> division of this <s>Sāman</s>. (2.9.4)

children.text: START ChUp 2,9.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.9.5]

children.text:
atha yat saṃprati madhyaṃdine sa udgīthaḥ |
tad asya devā anvāyattāḥ |
tasmāt te sattamāḥ prājāpatyānām |
udgīthabhājino hy etasya sāmnaḥ || ChUp_2,9.5 ||
children.translated_text: Now, that which [is the sun's phase] at exactly midday — that is the <s>Udgītha</s>. The gods are dependent upon that. Therefore they are the best among the offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s>. For they partake of the <s>Udgītha</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>. (ChUp 2.9.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,9.5 atha yatsamprati madhyandina ṛjumadhyandina ityarthaḥ /
sa udgīthabhaktistadasya devā anvāyattāḥ /
children.translated_text: That is the <s>Udgītha</s> division. The gods are dependent upon that.

children.text: dyotanātiśayāttatkāle /
children.translated_text: Because of the excess of brilliance at that time.

children.text: tasmātte sattamā viśiṣṭatamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore they are the best, the most distinguished.

children.text: prājāpatyānāṃ prajāpatyapatyānāmudgīthabhājino hyetasya sāmnaḥ //5 //
children.translated_text: Among the offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s>, the progeny of <s>Prajāpati</s> — because they partake of the <s>Udgītha</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>. (2.9.5)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> Bhāṣya on 2.9.5:] 'Now, that which [is the sun's phase] at exactly midday' — meaning at the exact midday.

children.text: START ChUp 2,9.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of ChUp 2.9.6]

children.text:
atha yad ūrdhvaṃ madhyaṃdināt prāg aparāhṇāt sa pratihāraḥ |
tad asya garbhā anvāyattāḥ |
tasmāt te pratihṛtā nāvapadyante |
pratihārabhājino hy etasya sāmnaḥ || ChUp_2,9.6 ||
children.translated_text: Now, that which is after midday and before afternoon, that is the <s>pratihāra</s> (response). Embryos are dependent on that. Therefore, they are held back and do not fall down, for they partake of the <s>pratihāra</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,9.6 atha yadūrdhvaṃ madhyandinātprāgaparāhnādyadrūpaṃ savituḥ sa pratihārastadasya garbhā anvāyattāḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, that form of the sun which is after midday and before afternoon, that is the <s>pratihāra</s>. Embryos are dependent on that.

children.text: ataste savituḥ pratihārabhaktirūpeṇordhvaṃ pratihṛtāḥ santo nāvapadyante nādhaḥ patanti taddvāre satyapītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, being held back in the form of partaking of the <s>pratihāra</s> of the sun, they do not fall down — they do not drop downward; the meaning is that this is by virtue of that connection.

children.text: yataḥ pratihārabhājino hyetasya sāmno garbhāḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: Because embryos partake of the <s>pratihāra</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,9.7
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.9.7

children.text:
atha yad ūrdhvam aparāhṇāt prāg astam ayāt sa upadravaḥ |
tad asyāraṇyā anvāyattāḥ |
tasmāt te puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kakṣaṃ śvabhram ity upadravanti |
upadravabhājino hy etasya sāmnaḥ || ChUp_2,9.7 ||
children.translated_text: Now, that which is after afternoon and before sunset, that is the <s>upadrava</s> (attack). Wild animals are dependent on that. Therefore, upon seeing a person, they run toward a thicket or a pit — they attack, for they partake of the <s>upadrava</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,9.7 atha yadūrdhvamaparāhnātprāgastamayātsa upadravastadasyā'raṇyāḥ paśvo 'nvāyattāḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, that which is after afternoon and before sunset, that is the <s>upadrava</s>. The wild animals of the forest are dependent on that.

children.text: tasmātte puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītāḥ kakṣamaraṇyaṃ śvabhraṃ bhayaśūnyamityupadravantyupagacchanti dṛṣṭvopadravaṇādupadravabhājino hyetasya sāmnaḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, upon seeing a person, being frightened, they run toward a thicket — the forest — or a pit — a place free from danger — they approach it. Because of running upon seeing, they partake of the <s>upadrava</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,9.8
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.9.8

children.text:
atha yat prathamāstamite tan nidhanam |
tad asya pitaro 'nvāyattāḥ |
tasmāt tān nidadhati |
nidhanabhājino hy etasya sāmnaḥ |
evaṃ khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste || ChUp_2,9.8 ||
children.translated_text: Now, the first moments after the sun has set, that is the <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion). The ancestors are dependent on that. Therefore, one lays them down. They partake of the <s>nidhana</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>. Thus indeed does one meditate on the sun as the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,9.8 atha yatprathamāstamite 'darśanaṃ jigamiṣati savitari tannidhanaṃ tadasya pitaro 'nvāyattāstasmāttānnidadhati pitṛpitāmahaprapitāmaharūpeṇa darbheṣu nikṣipanti tāṃstadarthaṃ piṇḍānvā sthāpayanti /
children.translated_text: Now, the first moments when the sun has set and is about to disappear, that is the <s>nidhana</s>. The ancestors (<s>pitaras</s>) are dependent on that. Therefore, one lays them down — one places them in the form of father, grandfather, and great-grandfather on <s>darbha</s> grass, or places the <s>piṇḍas</s> (offering balls) for that purpose.

children.text: nidhanasambandhānnidhanabhājino hyetasya sāmnaḥ pitaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the connection with the <s>nidhana</s>, the ancestors partake of the <s>nidhana</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: evamavayavaśaḥ saptadhā vibhaktaṃ khalvamumādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste yastasya tadāpattiḥ phalamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: Thus, divided sevenfold according to its parts, one meditates on the sun as the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>. The rest of the sentence means: whoever does so, the result is the attainment of that.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,10.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.10.1

children.text:
atha khalv ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta |
hiṅkāra iti tryakṣaram |
prastāva iti tryakṣaram |
tat samam || ChUp_2,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, one should meditate on the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> that is self-measured (<s>ātmasaṃmita</s>) and transcends death (<s>atimṛtyu</s>). '<s>Hiṅkāra</s>' — three syllables. '<s>Prastāva</s>' — three syllables. That is equal.

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,10.1 mṛtyurādityaḥ ahorātrādikālena jagataḥ pramāpayitṛtvāt /
tasyātitaraṇāyedaṃ sāmopāsanamupadiśyate-atha khalvanantaram /
ādityamṛtyuviṣayasāmopāsanasya, ātmasaṃmitaṃ svāvayavatulyatayā mitaṃ paramātmatulyatayā vā saṃmitamatimṛtyu mṛtyujayahetutvāt /
yathā prathame 'dhyāya udgīthabhaktināmākṣarāṇyudgītha ityupāsyatvenoktāni, tatheha sāmnaḥ saptavidhabhaktināmākṣarāṇi samāhṛtya tribhisribhiḥ samatayā sāmatvaṃ parikalpyopāsyatvenocyante /
children.translated_text: Just as in the first chapter, the syllables of the name '<s>udgītha</s>' were stated as objects of meditation through the division of <s>udgītha</s>, so here the syllables of the names of the seven divisions of the <s>Sāman</s> are collected, and by arranging equality through groups of three, the quality of being <s>Sāman</s> (sameness) is devised and declared as an object of meditation.

children.text: tadupāsanena mṛtyugocarākṣarasamakhyāsāmānyena taṃ mṛtyuṃ prāpya tadatiriktākṣareṇa tasyā'dityasya mṛtyoratikramaṇāyaiva saṃkramamaṃ kalpayati /
children.translated_text: Through that meditation, by the equality of syllable count with that which falls within death's domain, one reaches that death, and by the surplus syllable, one devises a crossing over beyond that sun, which is death.

children.text: atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta mṛtyumatikrāntamatiriktākṣarasaṃkhyayetyamṛtyu sāma /
children.translated_text: One should meditate on the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> that transcends death — the <s>Sāman</s> that has transcended death by the surplus syllable count, thus it is the immortal <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: tasya prathamabhaktināmākṣarāṇi biṅkāra ityetattryakṣaraṃ bhaktimāna prastāva iti ca bhaktestryakṣarameva māna tatpūrveṇa samam //1 //
children.translated_text: The syllables of the name of the first division are: '<s>hiṅkāra</s>' — this is three syllables, and '<s>prastāva</s>' is also three syllables as the measure of the division. That is equal to the former.

Death is the sun, because it causes the destruction of the world through time in the form of days, nights, and so on. For the purpose of transcending that, this <s>Sāman</s> meditation is taught. 'Now' means next, after the meditation on the <s>Sāman</s> concerning the sun as death. '<s>Ātmasaṃmita</s>' means measured as equal to its own parts, or measured as equal to the Supreme Self. '<s>Atimṛtyu</s>' — because it is the cause of conquering death.

children.text: START ChUp 2,10.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.10.2

children.text:
ādir iti dvyakṣaram |
pratihāra iti caturakṣaram |
tata ihaikam |
tat samam || ChUp_2,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ādi</s>' — two syllables. '<s>Pratihāra</s>' — four syllables. From the latter, one syllable is taken here. That is equal.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,10.2 ādiriti dvyakṣaraṃ, saptavidhasya sāmnaḥ saṃkhyāpūraṇa oṅkāra ādirityucyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ādi</s>' is two syllables. The <s>Oṃkāra</s>, which serves to complete the count of the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>, is called '<s>ādi</s>' (beginning).

children.text: pratihāra iti caturakṣaram /
children.translated_text: '<s>Pratihāra</s>' is four syllables.

children.text: tata ihaikamakṣaramavacchidyā'dyakṣarayoḥ prakṣipyate /
children.translated_text: From that, one syllable is separated and added to the first two syllables.

children.text: tena tatsamameva bhavati //2 //
children.translated_text: Thereby it becomes equal.

children.text: START ChUp 2,10.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.10.3

children.text:
udgītha iti tryakṣaram upadrava iti caturakṣaraṃ tribhis tribhiḥ samaṃ bhavati |
akṣaram atiśiṣyate tryakṣaram |
tat samam || ChUp_2,10.3 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Udgītha</s>' — three syllables. '<s>Upadrava</s>' — four syllables. In groups of three, it becomes equal. One syllable remains extra — three syllables. That is equal.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,10.3 udgītha iti tryakṣaramupadrava iti caturakṣaraṃ tribhisribhiḥ samaṃ bhavatyakṣaramatiśiṣ.yate 'tiricyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Udgītha</s>' is three syllables; '<s>upadrava</s>' is four syllables. In groups of three they become equal; one syllable remains, is surplus.

children.text: tena vaiṣamye prāpte sāmnaḥ samatvakaraṇāyā'ha-tadekamapi sadakṣaramiti tryakṣarameva bhavati /
children.translated_text: When inequality would thus result for the <s>Sāman</s>, in order to establish its equality, he says: that single extra syllable, being a syllable, amounts to three syllables itself.

children.text: atastatsamam //3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, that is equal.

children.text: START ChUp 2,10.4
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.10.4

children.text:
nidhanam iti tryakṣaram |
tat samam eva bhavati |
tāni ha vā etāni dvāviṃśatir akṣarāṇi || ChUp_2,10.4 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Nidhana</s>' — three syllables. That becomes equal indeed. These are twenty-two syllables.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,10.4 nidhanamiti tryakṣaraṃ tatsamameva bhavati /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nidhana</s>' is three syllables; that becomes equal indeed.

children.text: evaṃ tryakṣarasamatayā sāmatvaṃ sampādya yathāprāptānyevākṣarāṇi saṃkhyāyante - tāni ha vā etāni saptabhaktināmākṣarāṇi dvāviṃśatiḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: Having thus established the quality of <s>Sāman</s> (sameness) through the equality of three syllables, the syllables as they actually are, are counted: these syllables of the names of the seven divisions are twenty-two.

children.text: START ChUp 2,10.5
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.10.5

children.text:
ekaviṃśatyādityam āpnoti |
ekaviṃśo vā ito 'sāv ādityaḥ |
dvāviṃśena param ādityāj jayati |
tan nākam |
tad viśokam || ChUp_2,10.5 ||
children.translated_text: With twenty-one, one reaches the sun. The sun is the twenty-first from here. With the twenty-second, one conquers what is beyond the sun. That is <s>nāka</s> (heaven). That is free from sorrow.

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,10.5 tatraikaviṃśatyakṣarasaṃkhyayā'dityamāpnoti mṛtyum /
yasmādekaviṃśa ito 'smāllokādasāvādityaḥ saṃkhyayā /
"dvādaśa māsāḥ pañcartavasraya ime lokā asāvāditya ekaviṃśa"iti śruteratiśiṣṭena dvāviṃśenākṣareṇa paraṃ mṛtyorādityājjayatyāpnotītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s>: 'Twelve months, five seasons, three worlds, and that sun — twenty-one.' With the surplus twenty-second syllable, one conquers, that is, attains what is beyond death, beyond the sun.

children.text: yacca tadādityātparaṃ kiṃ tat?nākaṃ kamiti sukhaṃ tasya pratiṣedho 'kaṃ tanna bhavatīti nākaṃ kamevetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And what is that which is beyond the sun? <s>Nāka</s> — '<s>ka</s>' means happiness; its negation is '<s>a-ka</s>' — that which is not without happiness — meaning it is happiness itself, that is <s>nāka</s>.

children.text: mṛtyuviṣayatvādduḥkhasya viśokaṃ ca tadvigataśokaṃ mānasaduḥkharahitamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And because sorrow belongs to the domain of death, it is <s>viśoka</s> (free from sorrow), meaning free from mental suffering.

children.text: tadāpnotīti //5 //
children.translated_text: One attains that.
With the count of twenty-one syllables, one reaches the sun, which is death. Because the sun is the twenty-first from this world by count.

children.text: START ChUp 2,10.6
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.10.6

children.text:
āpnotīhādityasya jayam |
paro hāsyādityajayāj jayo bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste sāmopāste || ChUp_2,10.6 ||
children.translated_text: One obtains here the victory over the sun. Higher than the victory over the sun is the victory of one who, knowing thus, meditates on the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> that is self-measured (<s>ātmasaṃmita</s>) and transcends death (<s>atimṛtyu</s>). One meditates on the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,10.6 uktasyaiva piṇḍitārthamāha-ekaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā'dityasya jayamāpnoti paro hāsyaivaṃvida ādityajayānmṛtyugocarātparo jayo bhavati dvāviṃśatyakṣarasaṃkhyayetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He states the summarized meaning of what has been said: with the count of twenty-one, one obtains the victory over the sun. Higher than the victory over the sun — over that which is within death's domain — is the victory of one who knows thus, by the count of twenty-two syllables.

children.text: ya etadevaṃ dvānitikyādyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: The one who knows this, as explained beginning with 'two,' and so forth.

children.text: tasyaitadyathoktaṃ phalamiti dvirabhyāsaḥ sāptavidhyasamāptyarthaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: The result for such a person is as stated. The repetition of '<s>sāmopāste</s>' is for the purpose of completing the sevenfold meditation.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,11.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.11.1

children.text:
mano hiṅkāraḥ |
vāk prastāvaḥ |
cakṣur udgīthaḥ |
śrotraṃ pratihāraḥ |
prāṇo nidhanam |
etad gāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protam || ChUp_2,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: The mind is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Speech is the <s>prastāva</s>. The eye is the <s>udgītha</s>. The ear is the <s>pratihāra</s>. The <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Gāyatra</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths).

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,11.1 vinā nāmagrahaṇaṃ pañcavidhasya saptavidhasya ca sāmna upāsanamuktam /
athedānīṃ gāyatrādināmagrahaṇapūrvakaṃ viśiṣṭaphalāni sāmopāsanāntarāṇyucyante yathākramaṃ gāyatrādīnāṃ karmaṇi prayogastathaiva /
mano hiṅkāro manasaḥ sarvakaraṇapravṛttīnāṃ prāthamyāt /
tadānantaryādvākprastāvaścakṣurudgīthaḥ śraiṣṭhyāt /
śrotraṃ pratihāraḥ pratihṛtatvāt /
children.translated_text: The ear is the <s>pratihāra</s>, because of its being held back (restrained).

children.text: prāṇo nidhanaṃ yathoktānāṃ prāṇe nidhanātsvāpakāle /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>nidhana</s>, because the aforementioned senses find their resting place (<s>nidhana</s>) in <s>prāṇa</s> during sleep.

children.text: etadgāyatraṃ sāma prāṇeṣu protam /
children.translated_text: This <s>Gāyatra</s> <s>Sāman</s> is woven upon the <s>prāṇas</s>.

children.text: gāyatryāḥ prāṇasaṃstutatvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: Because the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is celebrated in connection with <s>prāṇa</s>.

The meditation on the fivefold and sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> without mentioning specific names has been stated. Now, meditations on other <s>Sāmans</s> with specific results, preceded by the mention of names such as <s>Gāyatra</s> and so forth, are taught, in the same order as the <s>Gāyatra</s> and other <s>Sāmans</s> are employed in ritual. The mind is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, because the mind has priority over the activity of all the senses. In sequence after that, speech is the <s>prastāva</s>, and the eye is the <s>udgītha</s>, because of its preeminence.

children.text: START ChUp 2,11.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.11.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad gāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protaṃ veda |
prāṇī bhavati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
mahāmanāḥ syāt |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this <s>Gāyatra</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon the <s>prāṇas</s> becomes endowed with <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), lives the full span of life, lives long and brightly, becomes great through progeny and cattle, becomes great in fame. One should be great-minded. That is the vow.

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,11.2 sa ya evametadgāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protaṃ veda prāṇī bhavati /
avikalakaraṇo bhavatītyetat /
sarvamāyureti /
śataṃ varṣaṇi sarvamāyuḥ puruṣasyeti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s>: 'A hundred years is the full lifespan of a person.'

children.text: jyogujjvalaṃ jīvati /
children.translated_text: One lives long and brilliantly.

children.text: mahānbhavati prajādibhirmahāṃśca kīrtyā /
children.translated_text: One becomes great through progeny and the rest, and also great in fame.

children.text: gāyatropāsakasyaitadvrataṃ bhavati yanmahāmanāstvakṣudracittaḥ syādityarthaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: The vow for the worshipper of the <s>Gāyatra</s> is that one should be great-minded — meaning one should not be small-minded.
One who knows this <s>Gāyatra</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon the <s>prāṇas</s> becomes endowed with <s>prāṇa</s> — meaning one becomes possessed of unimpaired senses. One lives the full span of life.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,12.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.12.1

children.text:
abhimanthati sa hiṅkāraḥ |
dhūmo jāyate sa prastāvaḥ |
jvalati sa udgīthaḥ |
aṅgārā bhavanti sa pratihāraḥ |
upaśāmyati tan nidhanam |
saṃśāmyati tan nidhanam |
etad rathaṃtaram agnau protam || ChUp_2,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: One churns the fire-sticks — that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Smoke is produced — that is the <s>prastāva</s>. It blazes — that is the <s>udgītha</s>. Embers are formed — that is the <s>pratihāra</s>. It subsides — that is the <s>nidhana</s>. It fully subsides — that is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon fire.

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,12.1 abhimanthati sa hiṅkāraḥ prāthamyāt /
agnerdhūmo jāyate sa prastāva ānantaryāt /
jvalati sa udgītho haviḥ sambandhācchraiṣṭhyaṃ jvalanasya /
aṅgārā bhavanti sa pratihāro 'ṅgārāṇāṃ pratihṛtatvāt /
children.translated_text: Embers are formed — that is the <s>pratihāra</s>, because embers are held back (restrained).

children.text: upaśamaḥ sāvaśeṣatvādagneḥ /
children.translated_text: Subsiding means the fire still has a remainder.

children.text: saṃśamo niḥśeṣopaśamaḥ samāptisāmānyānnidhanametadrathantara magnau protam /
children.translated_text: Complete subsiding means total extinction without remainder. Because of its similarity to completion, it is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon fire.

children.text: manthane hyagnergīyate //1 //
children.translated_text: Because the <s>Rathantara</s> is sung during the churning of fire.

One churns the fire-sticks — that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, because it comes first. Smoke is produced from the fire — that is the <s>prastāva</s>, because of sequential order. It blazes — that is the <s>udgītha</s>, because blazing has preeminence due to its connection with the oblation.

children.text: START ChUp 2,12.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.12.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad rathaṃtaram agnau protaṃ veda |
brahmavarcasy: annādo bhavati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
na pratyaṅṅ agnim ācāmen na niṣṭhīvet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this <s>Rathantara</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon fire becomes radiant with the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcas</s>), becomes an eater of food, lives the full span of life, lives long and brightly, becomes great through progeny and cattle, becomes great in fame. One should not sip water or spit facing the fire. That is the vow.

children.text: ChUpBh_2,12.2 sa ya ityādi pūrvavat /
brahmavarcasī vṛttasvādhyāyanimittaṃ tejo brahmavartasam /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmavarcasī</s> — the splendor born of proper conduct and Vedic study is called <s>brahmavarcas</s>.

children.text: tejastu kevalaṃ tviḍbhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Splendor alone, however, refers to mere radiance.

children.text: annādo dīptāgniḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Eater of food' means one whose digestive fire is strong.

children.text: na pratyaṅṅagnerabhimukho nā'cāmenna bhakṣayetkiñcinna niṣṭhīvecchleṣmanirasanaṃ ca na kuryāttadvratam //2//
children.translated_text: One should not sip water facing the fire, nor eat anything facing it, nor spit — meaning one should not expel phlegm either. That is the vow.
The passage beginning with 'One who' and so forth is as explained before.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,13.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.13.1

children.text:
upamantrayate sa hiṅkāraḥ |
jñapayate sa prastāvaḥ |
striyā saha śete sa udgīthaḥ |
prati strīṃ saha śete sa pratihāraḥ |
kālaṃ gacchati tan nidhanam |
pāraṃ gacchati tan nidhanam |
etad vāmadevyaṃ mithune protam || ChUp_2,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: He invites her — that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. He makes his desire known — that is the <s>prastāva</s>. He lies down with the woman — that is the <s>udgītha</s>. He lies upon the woman — that is the <s>pratihāra</s>. He reaches the culmination — that is the <s>nidhana</s>. He reaches the conclusion — that is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Vāmadevya</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon sexual union (<s>mithuna</s>).

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,13.1 upamantrayate saṅketaṃ karoti prāthamyātsa hiṅkāraḥ /
jñapayate toṣayati sa prastāvaḥ /
sahaśayanamekaparyaṅkagamanaṃ sa udgīthaḥ śraiṣṭhyāt /
children.translated_text: Lying together — going to the same couch — that is the <s>udgītha</s>, because of its preeminence.

children.text: prati srīṃ śayanaṃ sriyā abhimukhībhāvaḥ sa pratihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Lying upon the woman — being face to face with the woman — that is the <s>pratihāra</s>.

children.text: kālaṃ gacchati maithunena pāraṃ samāptiṃ gacchati tannidhanametadvāmadevyaṃ mithune protam /
children.translated_text: He reaches the culmination through the act of union; he reaches the conclusion, the completion — that is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Vāmadevya</s> <s>Sāman</s> woven upon sexual union (<s>mithuna</s>).

children.text: vāyvambumithunasambandhāt //1 //
children.translated_text: Because of the connection of <s>Vāmadeva</s> with wind, water, and sexual union.
He invites her — he makes a signal; because it comes first, that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. He makes his desire known — he pleases her; that is the <s>prastāva</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,13.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.13.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad vāmadevyaṃ mithune protaṃ veda |
mithunī bhavati |
mithunān mithunāt prajāyate |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
na kāṃcana pariharet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Vāmadevya</s> (Sāman) as woven into coupling, becomes one who couples. He procreates from each coupling. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not refuse any woman. That is the observance. || ChUp_2,13.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,13.2 sa ya ityādi pūrvavat /
mithunī bhavatyavidhuro bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Becomes one who couples" means he becomes one who is not deprived of a partner.

children.text: mithunānmithunātprajāyata ityamogharetastvamucyate /
children.translated_text: "He procreates from each coupling" — by this he is declared to be one whose seed never fails.

children.text: na kāñcana kāñcidapi sriyaṃ svātmatalpaprāptāṃ na pariharetsamāgamārthinīm /
children.translated_text: "He should not refuse any" — he should not refuse any woman who has come to his bed seeking union.

children.text: vāmadevyasāmopāsanāṅgatvena vidhānāt etasmādanyatra pratiṣedhasmṛtayaḥ vacanaprāmāṇyācca dharmāvagaterna pratiṣedhaśāsreṇāsya virodhaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Since this is enjoined as an auxiliary of the <s>Vāmadevya Sāman</s> meditation, the prohibitory <s>smṛti</s> texts apply elsewhere. And since <s>dharma</s> is ascertained through the authority of the scriptural word, there is no conflict with the prohibitory scriptures.
"He who" and so on — as explained before.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya tryodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
udyan hiṅkāraḥ |
uditaḥ prastāvaḥ |
madhyaṃdina udgīthaḥ |
aparāhṇaḥ pratihāraḥ |
astaṃ yan nidhanam |
etad bṛhad āditye protam || ChUp_2,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: The rising sun is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. The risen sun is the <s>prastāva</s>. Midday is the <s>udgītha</s>. Afternoon is the <s>pratihāra</s>. The setting sun is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Bṛhat</s> (Sāman) woven into the sun. || ChUp_2,14.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,14.1 udyansavitā sa hiṅkāraḥ prāthamyāddarśanasya /
uditaḥ prastāvaḥ prastavanahetutvātkarmaṇām /
madhyandina udgīthaḥ śraiṣṭhyāt /
children.translated_text: Midday is the <s>udgītha</s>, because of its preeminence.

children.text: aparāhnaḥ pratihāraḥ paśvādīnāṃ gṛhānprati haraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Afternoon is the <s>pratihāra</s>, because of the bringing back (<s>haraṇa</s>) of cattle and so forth toward (<s>prati</s>) their homes.

children.text: yadastaṃ yaṃstannidhanaṃ rātrau gṛhe nidhānātprāṇinām /
children.translated_text: When the sun sets, that is the <s>nidhana</s>, because at night living beings are deposited (<s>nidhāna</s>) in their homes.

children.text: etadbṛhadāditye protaṃ bṛhata ādityadaivatyatvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: This <s>Bṛhat</s> (Sāman) is woven into the sun, because <s>Āditya</s> is the deity of the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
The rising sun is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, because it is the first to be seen. The risen sun is the <s>prastāva</s>, because it is the cause of prompting activities.

children.text: START ChUp 2,14.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,14.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad bṛhad āditye protaṃ veda |
tejasvy: annādo bhavati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
tapantaṃ na nindet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,14.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Bṛhat</s> (Sāman) as woven into the sun, becomes radiant and a consumer of food. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not criticize that which blazes. That is the observance. || ChUp_2,14.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,14.2 sa ya ityādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: "He who" and so on — as explained before.

children.text: tapantaṃ na nindettadvratam //2//
children.translated_text: He should not criticize that which blazes — that is the observance.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya caturdaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
abhrāṇi saṃplavante sa hiṅkāraḥ |
megho jāyate sa prastāvaḥ |
varṣati sa udgīthaḥ |
vidyotate stanayati sa pratihāraḥ |
udgṛhṇāti tan nidhanam |
etad vairūpaṃ parjanye protam || ChUp_2,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: The mists gather — that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. A cloud is born — that is the <s>prastāva</s>. It rains — that is the <s>udgītha</s>. It lightens and thunders — that is the <s>pratihāra</s>. It lifts — that is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Vairūpa</s> (Sāman) woven into rain. || ChUp_2,15.1 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,15.1 abhrāṇyabbharaṇāt, megha udakasektṛtvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhra</s> (mist) is so called from its filling (<s>abbharaṇa</s>); <s>megha</s> (cloud) because it sprinkles water.

children.text: uktārthamanyat /
children.translated_text: The rest has the meaning already stated.

children.text: etadvairūpaṃ nāma sāma parjanye protam /
children.translated_text: This <s>Sāman</s> called <s>Vairūpa</s> is woven into rain (<s>Parjanya</s>).

children.text: anetarūpatvāt abhrādibhiḥ parjanyasya vairūpyam //1 //
children.translated_text: Because rain has varied forms (<s>vairūpya</s>) through mist and other manifestations, it is not of a single form.

children.text: START ChUp 2,15.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,15.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad vairūpaṃ parjanye protaṃ veda |
virūpāṃś ca surūpaṃś ca paśūn avarundhe |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
varṣantaṃ na nindet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,15.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Vairūpa</s> (Sāman) as woven into rain, obtains cattle of varied and beautiful forms. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not criticize the rain. That is the observance. || ChUp_2,15.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,15.2 virūpāṃśca surūpāṃścājāviprabhṛtīnpaśūnavarundhe prāpnotītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Cattle of varied and beautiful forms" — he obtains cattle such as goats, sheep, and others; the meaning is that he acquires them.

children.text: varṣantaṃ na nindettadvratam //2//
children.translated_text: He should not criticize the rain — that is the observance.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya pañcadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
vasanto hiṅkāraḥ |
grīṣmaḥ prastāvaḥ |
varṣā udgīthaḥ |
śarat pratihāraḥ |
hemanto nidhanam |
etad vairājam ṛtuṣu protam || ChUp_2,16.1 ||
children.translated_text: Spring is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Summer is the <s>prastāva</s>. The rains are the <s>udgītha</s>. Autumn is the <s>pratihāra</s>. Winter is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Vairāja</s> (Sāman) woven into the seasons. || ChUp_2,16.1 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,16.1 vasanto hiṃṅkāraḥ prāthamyāt /
children.translated_text: Spring is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, because it comes first.

children.text: grīṣmaḥ prastāva ityādi pūrvavat //1 //
children.translated_text: "Summer is the <s>prastāva</s>" and so on — as explained before.

children.text: START ChUp 2,16.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,16.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad vairājam ṛtuṣu protaṃ veda |
virājati prajayā |
paśubhir brahmavarcasena |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
ṛtūn na nindet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,16.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Vairāja</s> (Sāman) as woven into the seasons, shines with offspring, with cattle, and with the radiance of sacred knowledge. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not criticize the seasons. That is the observance. || ChUp_2,16.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,16.2 etadvairājamṛtuṣu protaṃ veda virājati ṛtuvadyathartava ārtavairdharmairvirājanta evaṃ prajādibhirvidvānityuktamanyat /
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Vairāja</s> woven into the seasons — he shines; just as the seasons shine with their seasonal qualities, so too the knower shines with offspring and the rest — thus it has been stated. The rest has the meaning already explained.

children.text: ṛtīnna nindettadvratam //2//
children.translated_text: He should not criticize the seasons — that is the observance.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya ṣoḍaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,17.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,17.1

children.text:
pṛthivī hiṅkāraḥ |
antarikṣaṃ prastāvaḥ |
dyaur udgīthaḥ |
diśaḥ pratihāraḥ |
samudro nidhanam |
etāḥ śakvaryo lokeṣu protāḥ || ChUp_2,17.1 ||
children.translated_text: Earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. The atmosphere is the <s>prastāva</s>. Heaven is the <s>udgītha</s>. The directions are the <s>pratihāra</s>. The ocean is the <s>nidhana</s>. These are the <s>Śakvarī</s> (Sāmans) woven into the worlds. || ChUp_2,17.1 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,17.1 pṛthivī hiṅkāra ityādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: "Earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>" and so on — as explained before.

children.text: śakvarya iti nityaṃ bahuvacanaṃ revatya iva /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakvarī</s> is always in the plural, like <s>Revatī</s>.

children.text: lokeṣu protāḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Woven into the worlds.

children.text: START ChUp 2,17.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,17.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etāḥ śakvaryo lokeṣu protā veda |
lokī bhavati sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
lokān na nindet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,17.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows these <s>Śakvarī</s> (Sāmans) as woven into the worlds, becomes a possessor of worlds. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not criticize the worlds. That is the observance. || ChUp_2,17.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,17.2 lokī bhavati lokaphalena yujyata ityartaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He becomes a possessor of worlds" means he is endowed with the fruit of the worlds.

children.text: lokānna nindettadvratam //2//
children.translated_text: He should not criticize the worlds — that is the observance.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya saptadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,18.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,18.1

children.text:
ajā hiṅkāraḥ |
avayaḥ prastāvaḥ |
gāva udgīthaḥ |
aśvāḥ pratihāraḥ |
puruṣo nidhanam |
etā revatyaḥ paśuṣu protāḥ || ChUp_2,18.1 ||
children.translated_text: Goats are the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Sheep are the <s>prastāva</s>. Cows are the <s>udgītha</s>. Horses are the <s>pratihāra</s>. Man is the <s>nidhana</s>. These are the <s>Revatī</s> (Sāmans) woven into animals. || ChUp_2,18.1 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,18.1 ajā hiṅkāra ityādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: "Goats are the <s>hiṅkāra</s>" and so on — as explained before.

children.text: paśuṣu protāḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Woven into animals.

children.text: START ChUp 2,18.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,18.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etā revatyaḥ paśuṣu protā veda |
paśumān bhavati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
paśūn na nindet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,18.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows these <s>Revatī</s> (Sāmans) as woven into animals, becomes a possessor of animals. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not criticize animals. That is the observance. || ChUp_2,18.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,18.2 paśūnna nindettadvratam //2//
children.translated_text: He should not criticize animals — that is the observance.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasyasyāṣṭādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
loma hiṅkāraḥ |
tvak prastāvaḥ |
māṃsam udgīthaḥ |
asthi pratihāraḥ |
majjā nidhanam |
etad yajñāyajñīyam aṅgeṣu protam || ChUp_2,19.1 ||
children.translated_text: Hair is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Skin is the <s>prastāva</s>. Flesh is the <s>udgītha</s>. Bone is the <s>pratihāra</s>. Marrow is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> (Sāman) woven into the bodily limbs. || ChUp_2,19.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,19.1 loma hiṅkāro dehāvayavānāṃ prāthamyāt /
tvakprastāva ānantaryāt /
māṃsamudgīthaḥ śraiṣṭhyāt /
children.translated_text: Flesh is the <s>udgītha</s>, because of its preeminence.

children.text: asthi pratihāraḥ pratihṛtatvāt /
children.translated_text: Bone is the <s>pratihāra</s>, because it is held back and enclosed.

children.text: majjā nidhanamāntyāt /
children.translated_text: Marrow is the <s>nidhana</s>, because it is last.

children.text: etadyajñāyajñīyaṃ nāma sāma dehāvayavaveṣu protam //1 //
children.translated_text: This <s>Sāman</s> called <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is woven into the bodily constituents.
Hair is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, because it is first among the bodily constituents. Skin is the <s>prastāva</s>, because it comes next in succession.

children.text: START ChUp 2,19.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,19.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad yajñāyajñīyam aṅgeṣu protaṃ veda |
aṅgī bhavati |
nāṅgena vihūrchati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
saṃvatsaraṃ majjño nāśnīyāt |
tad vratam |
majjño nāśnīyād iti vā || ChUp_2,19.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> (Sāman) as woven into the bodily limbs, becomes possessed of all limbs. He is not impaired in any limb. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not eat marrow for a year. That is the observance. Or rather, he should never eat marrow. || ChUp_2,19.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,19.2 aṅgī bhavati samagrāṅgo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
nāṅgena hastapādādinā vihūrchati na kuṭilī bhavati paṅguḥ kuṇī vetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He is not impaired in any limb" — he does not become crooked in any limb such as hand or foot; the meaning is that he does not become lame or crippled.

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsaramātraṃ majjño māṃsāni nāśnīyānna bhakṣayet /
children.translated_text: "For a year" — for a period of one year he should not eat, should not consume, marrow-meats.

children.text: bahuvacanaṃ matsyopalakṣaṇārtham /
children.translated_text: The plural form is used to indicate fish and similar creatures as well.

children.text: majjño nāśnīyātsarvadaiva nāśnīyāditi vā tadvratam //2//
children.translated_text: "Or rather, he should never eat marrow" — he should never eat it at all — that is the observance.
"He becomes possessed of all limbs" means he has all his limbs intact and complete.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasyaikonaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
agnir hiṅkāraḥ |
vāyuḥ prastāvaḥ |
āditya udgīthaḥ |
nakṣatrāṇi pratihāraḥ |
candramā nidhanam |
etad rājanaṃ devatāsu protam || ChUp_2,20.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> (Fire) is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) is the <s>prastāva</s>. <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) is the <s>udgītha</s>. The stars are the <s>pratihāra</s>. The moon is the <s>nidhana</s>. This is the <s>Rājana</s> (Sāman) woven into the deities. || ChUp_2,20.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,20.1 agnirhiṅkāraḥ prathamasthānatvāt /
vāyuḥ prastāva ānantaryasāmānyāt /
āditya udgīthaḥ śraiṣṭhyāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Āditya</s> is the <s>udgītha</s>, because of its preeminence.

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi pratihāraḥ pratihṛtatvāt /
children.translated_text: The stars are the <s>pratihāra</s>, because they are held back and enclosed.

children.text: candramā nidhanaṃ karmiṇāṃ tannidhanāt /
children.translated_text: The moon is the <s>nidhana</s>, because those who perform rituals reach their end (<s>nidhana</s>) there.

children.text: etadrājanaṃ devatāsu protaṃ devatānāṃ dīptimattvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: This <s>Rājana</s> (Sāman) is woven into the deities, because the deities are luminous.
<s>Agni</s> is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, because of its being in the first position. <s>Vāyu</s> is the <s>prastāva</s>, because of the similarity of succession.

children.text: START ChUp 2,20.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,20.2

children.text:
sa ya evam etad rājanaṃ devatāsu protaṃ veda |
etāsām eva devatānāṃ salokatāṃ sarṣṭitāṃ sāyujyaṃ gacchati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
mahān prajayā paśubhir bhavati |
mahān kīrtyā |
brāhmaṇān na nindet |
tad vratam || ChUp_2,20.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Rājana</s> (Sāman) as woven into the deities, attains co-residence, co-prosperity, and union with these very deities. He lives a full life. He lives long. He becomes great in offspring and cattle. He becomes great in fame. He should not criticize <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. That is the observance. || ChUp_2,20.2 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,20.2 vidvatphalam-etāsāmevāgnyādīnāṃ devatānāṃ salokatāṃ samānalokatāṃ sārṣṭitāṃ samānarddhitvaṃ sāyujyaṃ samugbhāvamekadehadehitvamityetat /
vāśabdo 'tra lupto draṣṭavyaḥ salokatāṃ vetyādi /
bhāvanāviśeṣataḥ phalaviśeṣopapatteḥ /
gacchati prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: "He attains" means he reaches.

children.text: samuccayānupapatteśca /
children.translated_text: And because a cumulative combination of all three is not possible.

children.text: brāhmaṇānna nindettadvratam /
children.translated_text: He should not criticize <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — that is the observance.

children.text: "ete vai devāḥ pratyakṣaṃ yadbrāhmaṇā"iti śruterbrāhmaṇanindā devatānindaiveti //2//
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s> declaration "<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are indeed the visible deities," criticizing <s>brāhmaṇas</s> is tantamount to criticizing the deities.

The fruit for the knower: he attains <s>sālokatā</s> (co-residence), that is, dwelling in the same world as these deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others; <s>sārṣṭitā</s> (co-prosperity), that is, equality of splendor; <s>sāyujya</s> (union), that is, complete merging, having the same body and soul — this is the meaning. The particle "<s>vā</s>" (or) should be understood as dropped here, reading "<s>sālokatā</s> or" and so forth. Because distinctions in the fruit follow from distinctions in meditation.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya viṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
trayī vidyā hiṅkāraḥ |
traya ime lokāḥ sa prastāvaḥ |
agnir vāyur ādityaḥ sa udgīthaḥ |
nakṣatrāṇi vayāṃsi marīcayaḥ sa pratihāraḥ |
sarpā gandharvāḥ pitaras tan nidhanam |
etat sāma sarvasmin protam || ChUp_2,21.1 ||
children.translated_text: The threefold knowledge is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. These three worlds are the <s>prastāva</s>. <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Āditya</s> are the <s>udgītha</s>. The stars, birds, and rays of light are the <s>pratihāra</s>. Serpents, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and the ancestors are the <s>nidhana</s>. This <s>Sāman</s> is woven into everything. || ChUp_2,21.1 ||

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,21.1 trayī vidyā hiṅkāraḥ /
agnyādisāmna ānantaryaṃ trayīvidyāyā agnyādikāryatvaśruteḥ /
hiṅkāraḥ prāthamyātsarvakartavyānām /
traya ime lokāstatkāryatvādanantarā iti prastāvaḥ /
agnyādīnāmudgīthatvaṃ śraiṣṭhyāt /
nakṣatrādīnāṃ pratihṛtatvātpratihāratvam /
sarpādīnāṃ dhakārasāmānyānnidhanatvametatsāma nāmaviśṣābhāvātsāmasamudāyaḥ sāmaśabdaḥ sarvasminprotam /
children.translated_text: Serpents and others are the <s>nidhana</s> because of their similarity with the syllable "dha." This <s>Sāman</s> — the word <s>Sāman</s> here refers to the totality of <s>Sāmans</s>, since there is no specific name — is woven into everything.

children.text: trayīvidyādidṛṣṭyā hiṅkārādisāmabhaktaya upāsyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the vision of the threefold knowledge and so forth, the items assigned to <s>hiṅkāra</s> and the other parts of the <s>Sāman</s> are to be meditated upon.

children.text: atīteṣvapi sāmopāsaneṣu yeṣu yeṣu protaṃ yadyatsāma taddṛṣṭyā tadupāsyamiti /
children.translated_text: In the preceding <s>Sāman</s> meditations as well, whichever <s>Sāman</s> is woven into whatever substrate, that substrate is to be meditated upon through the vision of that <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: karmāṅganāṃ dṛṣṭiviśeṣeṇājyasyeva saṃskāryatvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: Because, like clarified butter that is to be consecrated through a particular contemplation, these are auxiliaries of ritual action that are to be consecrated through a particular vision.

The threefold knowledge (<s>trayī vidyā</s>) is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. The succession from the <s>Sāman</s> of <s>Agni</s> and others follows because of the <s>śruti</s> that the threefold knowledge is the effect of <s>Agni</s> and others. It is the <s>hiṅkāra</s> because it is first among all things to be done. These three worlds, being subsequent as effects of that, are the <s>prastāva</s>. <s>Agni</s> and others are the <s>udgītha</s> because of their preeminence. The stars and others are the <s>pratihāra</s> because they are held back and enclosed.

children.text: START ChUp 2,21.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,21.2

children.text: sa ya evam etat sāma sarvasmin protaṃ veda sarvaṃ ha bhavati || ChUp_2,21.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Sāman</s> as woven into everything, becomes everything. || ChUp_2,21.2 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,21.2 sarvaviṣayasāmavidaḥ phalaṃ-sarvaṃ ha bhavati sarveśvaro bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fruit for the knower of the <s>Sāman</s> that pertains to everything: "he becomes everything" means he becomes the lord of all.

children.text: nirupacaritasarvabhāve hi diksthebhyo baliprāptyanupapattiḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: For if the word "all" is taken literally without figurative meaning, then the obtaining of tribute-offerings from those stationed in the directions would be impossible.

children.text: START ChUp 2,21.3
children.translated_text: START ChUp 2,21.3

children.text:
tad eṣa ślokaḥ |
yāni pañcadhā trīṇi trīṇi |
tebhyo na jyāyaḥ param anyad asti || ChUp_2,21.3 ||
children.translated_text: There is this verse: Those that are fivefold, each in three, beyond them there is nothing higher or other. || ChUp_2,21.3 ||

children.text: ChUpBh_2,21.3 tadetasminnartha eṣa śloko mantro 'pyasti /
children.translated_text: On this very subject, there is this verse — a <s>mantra</s> too exists.

children.text: yāni pañcadhā pañcaprakāreṇa hiṅkārādivibhāgaiḥ proktāni trīṇi trīṇi trayīvidyādīni tebhyaḥ pañcatrikebhyo jyāyo mahattaraṃ paraṃ ca vyatiriktamanyadvastvantaraṃ nāsti na vidyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which has been described in five ways — by the fivefold division of <s>hiṅkāra</s> and the like — the three groups of three beginning with the threefold knowledge (<s>trayīvidyā</s>) — nothing is greater, higher, or different from those five triads — meaning nothing else exists.

children.text: tatraiva hi sarvasyāntabhaviḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: For in those alone is the end of everything. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 2,21.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.21.4]

children.text:
yas tad veda sa veda sarvam |
sarvā diśo balim asmai haranti |
sarvam asmīty upāsita |
tad vrataṃ tad vratam || ChUp_2,21.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows that knows everything. All the directions bring offerings to him. One should meditate: "I am everything." This is the vow, this is the vow.' (<s>ChUp</s> 2.21.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,21.4 yastadyathoktaṃ sarvātmakaṃ sāma veda sa veda sarvaṃ;sa sarvajño bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.21.4:] He who knows that — the <s>Sāman</s> as described, [which is] the self of all — knows everything; meaning he becomes omniscient.

children.text: sarvā diśaḥ sarvadiksthā asmā evaṃvide baliṃ bhogaṃ haranti prāpayantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: All the directions — all beings in all directions — bring offerings, meaning enjoyments, to this knower — they convey [them] to him, is the meaning.

children.text: sarvamasmi bhavāmītyevametatsāmopāsīta tasyaitadeva vratam /
children.translated_text: 'I am everything' — 'I am [all that] exists' — one should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> in this way. This alone is his vow.

children.text: dbiruktiḥ sāmopāsanasamāptyarpthā //4//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of 'this is the vow'] is for the purpose of concluding the <s>Sāman</s> meditation. (4)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasyaikaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,22.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.22.1]

children.text:
vinardi sāmno vṛṇe paśavyam ity agner udgīthaḥ |
aniruktaḥ prajāpateḥ |
niruktaḥ somasya |
mṛdu ślakṣṇaṃ vāyoḥ |
ślakṣṇaṃ balavad indrasya |
krauñcaṃ bṛhaspateḥ |
apadhvāntaṃ varuṇasya |
tān sarvān evopaseveta |
vāruṇaṃ tv eva varjayet || ChUp_2,22.1 ||
children.translated_text: '"I choose the resounding chant of the <s>Sāman</s> that is beneficial for cattle" — that is the <s>udgītha</s> of <s>Agni</s>. The inarticulate [chant] is of <s>Prajāpati</s>. The articulate [chant] is of <s>Soma</s>. The soft and smooth [chant] is of <s>Vāyu</s>. The smooth and powerful [chant] is of <s>Indra</s>. The heron-like [chant] is of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. The muffled [chant] is of <s>Varuṇa</s>. One should practice all of these, but should avoid the one of <s>Varuṇa</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 2.22.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,22.1 sāmopāsanaprasaṅgena gānaviśeṣādisampadudgāturupadiśyate /
phalaviśeṣasambandhātṣa vinardi viśiṣṭo nardaḥ svaraviśeṣa ṛṣabhakūjitasamo 'syāstīti vinardi gānamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
tacca sāmnaḥ sambandhi paśubhyo hitaṃ paśavyamagneragnidevatyaṃ codgītha udgānam /
tadahamevaṃviśiṣṭaṃ vṛṇe prarthaya iti kaścidyajamāna udgātā vā manyate /
anirukto 'mukasama ityaviśeṣitaḥ prajāpateḥ prajāpatidevatyaḥ sa na gānaviśeṣaḥ /
āniruktyātprajāpaterniruktaḥ spaṣṭaḥ somasya, somadevatyaḥ sa udgītha ityarthaḥ /
mṛdu ślakṣaṇaṃ ca gānaṃ vāyorvāyudevatyaṃ tat /
ślakṣṇaṃ balavacca prayatnādhikyopetaṃ cendrasyaindraṃ tadgānam /
children.translated_text: The smooth and powerful [chant], endowed with greater effort, is of <s>Indra</s> — that chant is sacred to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: krauñcaṃ krauñcapakṣininādasamaṃ bṛhaspaterbārhaspatyaṃ tat /
children.translated_text: The heron-like [chant] — resembling the cry of the <s>krauñca</s> (heron) bird — is of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> — that [chant] is sacred to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: apadhvāntaṃ bhinnakāṃsyasvarasamaṃ varuṇasyaitadgānam /
children.translated_text: The muffled [chant] — resembling the sound of cracked bronze — that is the chant of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: tānsarvānevopaseveta prayuñjīta vāruṇaṃ tvevaikaṃ varjayet //1 //
children.translated_text: One should practice all of them — employ [them all]; but the one of <s>Varuṇa</s> alone should be avoided. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.22.1:] In connection with the <s>Sāman</s> meditation, the excellence of particular vocal types and the like is taught for the <s>udgātṛ</s> priest. The result is connected with specific fruits. '<s>Vinardi</s>' — a distinctive roar, a particular vocal quality resembling the lowing of a bull — [one who has] this is called <s>vinardi</s>; the word 'chant' (<s>gāna</s>) is to be supplied from the rest of the sentence. And that [chant] is connected with the <s>Sāman</s>, is beneficial for cattle (<s>paśavya</s>), and is the <s>udgītha</s> — the chanting — sacred to <s>Agni</s>. 'I choose this, I pray for this' — thus some sacrificer or <s>udgātṛ</s> priest thinks. 'Inarticulate' — resembling a mute person, meaning unspecified — is sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>; that particular type of chanting [belongs to him]. Because of the inarticulateness [belonging] to <s>Prajāpati</s>, the articulate — the clear [chant] — is of <s>Soma</s>, meaning sacred to <s>Soma</s>; that is the <s>udgītha</s>, is the meaning. The soft and smooth chant is of <s>Vāyu</s> — sacred to <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,22.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.22.2]

children.text:
amṛtatvaṃ devebhya āgāyānīty āgāyet |
svadhāṃ pitṛbhya āśāṃ manuṣyebhyas tṛṇodakaṃ paśubhyaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānāyānnam ātmana āgāyānīty etāni manasā dhyāyann apramattaḥ stuvīta || ChUp_2,22.2 ||
children.translated_text: '"May I sing immortality for the gods," thus one should chant. "May I sing <s>svadhā</s> (ancestral offering) for the fathers, hope for men, grass and water for cattle, the heavenly world for the sacrificer, food for myself" — thus one should chant. Meditating on these in the mind, one should praise attentively.' (<s>ChUp</s> 2.22.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,22.2 amṛtatvaṃ devebhya āgāyāni sādhayāni /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.22.2:] 'May I sing immortality for the gods' — may I accomplish [this for them].

children.text: svadhāṃ pitṛbhya āgāyānyāśāṃ manuṣyebhya āśāṃ prārthanāṃ prārthitamityetat /
children.translated_text: 'May I sing <s>svadhā</s> for the fathers' — 'May I sing hope (<s>āśā</s>) for men' — hope means prayer, meaning what is prayed for.

children.text: tṛṇodakaṃ paśubhyaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānāyānnamātmane mahyamāgāyānītyetāni manasā cintayandhyāyannapramattaḥ svaroṣmavyañjanādibhyaḥ stuvīta //2 //
children.translated_text: 'Grass and water for cattle, the heavenly world for the sacrificer, food for myself' — 'may I sing [all these]' — thus thinking, meditating on these in the mind, attentive — [careful] regarding vowels, sibilants, consonants, and the like — one should praise. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 2,22.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.22.3]

children.text:
sarve svarā indrasyātmānaḥ |
sarva ūṣmāṇaḥ prajāpater ātmānaḥ |
sarve sparśā mṛtyor ātmānaḥ |
taṃ yadi svareṣūpālabheta |
indraṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā prati vakṣyatīty enaṃ brūyāt || ChUp_2,22.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'All vowels are forms of <s>Indra</s>. All sibilants are forms of <s>Prajāpati</s>. All consonants are forms of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death). If someone should criticize him regarding the vowels, he should say: "I have taken refuge in <s>Indra</s>; he will answer you."' (<s>ChUp</s> 2.22.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,22.3 sarve svarā akārādaya indrasya balakarmaṇaḥ prāṇasyā'tmāno dehāvayavasthānīyāḥ sarva ūṣmāṇaḥ śaṣasahādayaḥ prajāpatervirājaḥ kaśyapasya vā'tmānaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.22.3:] All vowels beginning with <s>a</s> are the forms — like bodily parts — of <s>Indra</s>, [who is] the one whose action is strength, [i.e.,] <s>prāṇa</s>. All sibilants — <s>śa</s>, <s>ṣa</s>, <s>sa</s>, <s>ha</s>, and the like — are the forms of <s>Prajāpati</s>, [who is] <s>Virāj</s> or <s>Kaśyapa</s>.

children.text: sarve sparśāḥ kādayo vyañjanāni mṛtyorātmānastamevaṃvidamudgātāraṃ yadi kaścitsvareṣūpālabheta svarastvayā duṣṭaḥ prayukta ityevamupālabdha indraṃ prāṇamīśvaraṃ śaraṇamāśrayaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ svarān prayuñjāno 'haṃ sa indro yattava vaktavyaṃ tvā tvāṃ prati vakṣyati sa eva deva uttaraṃ dāsyatītyenaṃ brūyāt //3 //
children.translated_text: All consonants — <s>ka</s> and the like, the stop consonants — are the forms of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death). If someone should criticize this knower, the <s>udgātṛ</s>, regarding the vowels — [saying] 'the vowel was badly employed by you' — thus criticized, [the <s>udgātṛ</s> should say:] 'Having taken refuge in <s>Indra</s> — <s>prāṇa</s> — the lord — as my shelter, I have employed the vowels. He, <s>Indra</s>, will answer (<s>prati vakṣyati</s>) whatever you have to say — he, that deity, will give the reply to you.' Thus he should say [to the critic]. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 2,22.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.22.4]

children.text:
atha yady enam ūṣmāsūpālabheta |
prajāpatiṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā prati pekṣyatīty enaṃ brūyāt |
atha yady enaṃ sparśeṣūpālabheta |
mṛtyuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā prati dhakṣyatīty enaṃ brūyāt || ChUp_2,22.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'If someone should criticize him regarding the sibilants, he should say: "I have taken refuge in <s>Prajāpati</s>; he will crush you." If someone should criticize him regarding the consonants, he should say: "I have taken refuge in <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death); he will burn you."' (<s>ChUp</s> 2.22.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,22.4 atha yadyenamūṣmasu tathaivopālabheta prajāpatiṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā pratipekṣyati sañcūrṇayiṣyatītyenaṃ brūyāt /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.22.4:] If someone should likewise criticize him regarding the sibilants — [the <s>udgātṛ</s> should say:] 'I have taken refuge in <s>Prajāpati</s>. He will crush you (<s>prati pekṣyati</s>)' — meaning he will pulverize [you]. Thus he should say to him.

children.text: atha yadyenaṃ sparśeṣūpālabheta mṛtyuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā prati dhakṣyati bhasmīkariṣyatītyenaṃ brūyāt //4 //
children.translated_text: If someone should criticize him regarding the consonants — [the <s>udgātṛ</s> should say:] 'I have taken refuge in <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death). He will burn you (<s>prati dhakṣyati</s>)' — meaning he will reduce [you] to ashes. Thus he should say to him. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 2,22.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.22.5]

children.text:
sarve svarā ghoṣavanto balavanto vaktavyā indre balaṃ dadānīti |
sarva ūṣmāṇo 'grastā anirastā vivṛtā vaktavyāḥ prajāpater ātmānaṃ paridadānīti |
sarve sparśā leśenānabhinihitā vaktavyā mṛtyor ātmānaṃ pariharāṇīti || ChUp_2,22.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'All vowels should be pronounced resonant and strong — [with the thought:] "May I give strength to <s>Indra</s>." All sibilants should be pronounced neither swallowed nor ejected, but open — [with the thought:] "May I give myself to <s>Prajāpati</s>." All consonants should be pronounced with slight contact, not fully pressed — [with the thought:] "May I withdraw myself from <s>Mṛtyu</s>."' (<s>ChUp</s> 2.22.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,22.5 yata indrādyātmānaḥ svarādayo 'taḥ sarve svarā ghoṣavanto balavanto vaktavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.22.5:] Since vowels and the like are the forms of <s>Indra</s> and the others — therefore, all vowels should be pronounced resonant and strong.

children.text: tathāhamindre balaṃ dadāni balamādadhānīti /
children.translated_text: Likewise [with the thought:] 'May I give strength to <s>Indra</s>' — meaning 'may I bestow strength.'

children.text: tathā sarva ūṣmāṇo 'grastā antarapraveśitā anirastā bahiraprakṣiptā vivṛtā[vivṛttā] vivṛtaprayatnopetāḥ prajāpaterātmānaṃ paridadāni prayacchānīti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, all sibilants [should be pronounced] 'not swallowed' — not pushed inward — 'not ejected' — not thrown outward — 'open' — accompanied by open effort — [with the thought:] 'May I give myself to <s>Prajāpati</s>' — meaning 'may I offer [myself].'

children.text: sarve sparśā leśena śanakairanabhinihitā anabhinikṣiptā vaktavyā mṛtyorātmānaṃ bālāniva śanakaiḥ pariharan mṛtyorātmānaṃ pariharāṇīti //5//
children.translated_text: All consonants [should be pronounced] 'with slight [contact]' — gently — 'not fully pressed' — not forcefully struck — thus they should be uttered. [With the thought:] 'May I withdraw myself from <s>Mṛtyu</s>' — gently handling [the consonants], as one would [handle] children — 'may I remove myself from <s>Mṛtyu</s>.' (5)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya dvāviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-second section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
trayo dharmaskandhāḥ |
yajño 'dhyayanaṃ dānam iti prathamaḥ |
tapa eva dvitīyaḥ |
brahmacāryācāryakulavāsī tṛtīyo 'tyantam ātmānam ācāryakule 'vasādayan |
sarva ete puṇyalokā bhavanti |
brahmasaṃstho 'mṛtatvam eti || ChUp_2,23.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'There are three branches of <s>dharma</s> (duty). The first is sacrifice, study, and charity. The second is <s>tapas</s> (austerity) alone. The third is the celibate student (<s>brahmacārī</s>) dwelling in the teacher's household, perpetually establishing himself in the teacher's house. All of these attain worlds of merit. One who is established in <s>Brahman</s> attains immortality.' (<s>ChUp</s> 2.23.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,23.1 oṅkārasyopāsanavidhyarthaṃ trayo dharmaskandhā ityādyārabhyate /
naivaṃ manatavyaṃ sāmāvayavabhūtasyaivodgīthādilakṣaṇasyoṅkārasyopāsanātphalaṃ prāpyata iti /
kiṃ tarhi?yatsarvairapi sāmopāsanaiḥ karmabhiścāprāpyaṃ tatphalamamṛtatvaṃ kevalādoṅkāropāsanātprāpyata iti /
tatstutyarthaṃ sāmaprakaraṇe tadupanyāsaḥ /
trayasrisaṃkhyākā dharmasya skandhā dharmaskandhāḥ dharmavibāgā ityarthaḥ /
ke ta ityāha -yajño 'gnihotrādiḥ /
adhyayanaṃ saniyamasya ṛgāderabhyāsaḥ /
dānaṃ bahirvedi yathāśaktidravyasaṃvibhāgo bhikṣamāṇebhyaḥ /
ityeṣa prathamo dharmaskandhaḥ /
gṛhasthasamavetatvāttannirvartakena gṛhasthena nirdiśyate prathama eka ityartho dvitīyatṛtīyaśravaṇānnā'dyārthaḥ /
tapa eva dvitīyastapa iti kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādi tadvāṃstāpasaḥ parivrāḍvā na brahmasaṃstha āśramadharmamātrasaṃstho;brahmasaṃsthasya tvamṛtatvaśravaṇāt /
dvitīyo dharmaskandhaḥ /
brahmacāryācāryakule vastuṃ śīlamasyetyācāryakulavāsī /
atyantaṃ yāvajjīvamātmānaṃ niyamairācāryakule 'vasādayankṣapayandehaṃ tṛtīyo dharmaskandhaḥ /
atyantamityādiviśeṣaṇānnaiṣṭhika iti gamyate /
upakurvāṇasya svādhyāyagrahaṇārthatvānna puṇyalokatvaṃ brahmacaryeṇa /
sarva ete trayo 'pyāśramiṇo yathoktairdharmaiḥ puṇyalokā bhavanti /
puṇyo loko yeṣāṃ ta ime puṇyalokā āśramiṇo bhavanti /
avaśiṣṭastvanuktaḥ parivrāḍbrahmasaṃstho brahmaṇi samyaksthitaḥ so 'mṛtatvaṃ puṇyalokavilakṣaṇamamaraṇabhāvamātyantikameti nā'pekṣikaṃ devādyamṛtatvavat /
puṇyalokātpṛyagamṛtatvasya vibhāgakaraṇāt /
yadi ca pumyalokātiśayamātramamṛtatvamabhaviṣyattataḥ puṇyalokatvādvibhaktaṃ nāvakṣyat /
vibhaktepadeśāccā'tyantikamamṛtatvamiti gamyate /
atra cā'śramadharmaphalopanyāsaḥ praṇavasevāstutyarthaṃ na tatphalavidhyartham /
stutaye ca pravamasevāyā āśramadharmaphalavidhaye ceti hi bhidyeta vākyam /
tasmātsmṛtisiddhāśramaphalānuvādena praṇavasevāphalamamṛtatvaṃ bruvanpraṇavasevāṃ stauti /
yathā pūrṇavarmaṇaḥ sevā bhaktaparidhānamātraphalā rājavarmaṇastu sevā rājyatulyaphaleti tadvat /
praṇavaśca tatsatyaṃ paraṃ brahma tatpratīkatvāt /
"etaddhyevākṣaraṃ brahma etaddhyevākṣaraṃ param" ityādyāmnāyātkāṭhake yuktaṃ tatsevāto 'mṛtatvam /
caturṇāmadhikṛtatvāviśeṣāt /
brahmasaṃsthatve 'pratiṣedhācca /
svakarmacchidre ca brahmasaṃsthatāyāṃ sāmardhyopapatteḥ /
na ca yavavarāhādiśabdavadbrahmasaṃsthaśabdaḥ parivrājake rūḍhaḥ /
brahmaṇi saṃsthitinimittamupādāya pravṛttatvāt /
na hi rūḍhiśabdā nimittamupādadate /
sarveṣāṃ ca brahmaṇi sthitirupapadyate /
yatra yatra nimittamasti brahmaṇi saṃsthitistasya tasya nimittavato vācakaṃ santaṃ brahmasaṃsthaśabdaṃ parivrāḍekaviṣaye saṃkoca kāraṇābhāvānniroddhuma yuktam /
na ca pārivrājyāśramadharmamātreṇāmṛtatvam /
jñānānarthakyaprasaṅgāt /
pārivrājyadharmayuktameva jñānamamṛtatvasādhanamiti cenna /
āśramadharmatvāviśeṣāt /
dharmo vā jñānaviśiṣṭo 'mṛtatvasādhanamityedapi sarvāśramadharmāṇāmaviśiṣṭam /
na ca vacanamasti parivrājakasyaiva brahmasaṃsthasya mokṣo nānyeṣāmiti /
jñānānmokṣa iti ca sarvopaniṣadāṃ siddhāntaḥ tasmādya eva brahmasaṃsthaḥ svāśramavihitakarmavatāṃ so 'mṛtatvametīti /
kurvidaṃ mā kārṣīriti karmavidhayaḥ pravṛttāḥ /
tacca nimittaṃ na śāsrakṛtam /
sarvaprāṇiṣu darśanāt /
"sadekamevādvitīyaṃ" "ātmaivedaṃ sarvaṃ" "brahmaivedaṃ sarvam" itiśāsrajanyaḥ pratyayo vidyārūpaḥ svābhāvikaṃ kriyākārakaphalabhedapratyayaṃ karmavidhinimittamanupamṛdya na jāyate /
bhedābhedapratyayayorvirodhāt /
na hi taimirikadvicandrādibhedapratyayamanupamṛdya timirāpagame candrādyekatvapratyaya upajāyate /
vidyāvidyāpratyayayorvirodhāt /
tatraivaṃ sati yaṃ bhedapratyayamupādāya karmavidhayaḥ pravṛtāḥ sa yasyopamarditaḥ sadekamevādvitīyaṃ tatsatyaṃ vikārabhedo 'nṛtamityetadvākyapramāṇajanitenaikatvapratyayena sa sarvakarmabhyo nivṛtto nimittanivṛtte:,sa ca nivṛttakarmā brahmasaṃstha ucyate, sa ca parivrāḍevānyasyāsambhavāt /
anyo hyanivṛttabhedapratyayaḥ so 'nyatpaśyañśṛṇvanmanvāno vijānannidaṃ kṛtvedaṃ prāpnuyāmiti hi manyate /
tasyaivaṃ kurvato na brahmasaṃsthatā /
vācārambhaṇamātravikārānṛtābhisandhipratyayatvāt /
na cāsatyamityupardite bhedapratyaye satyamidamanena kartavyaṃ mayeti pramāṇaprameyabuddhirupapadyate /
ākāśa iva talamalabuddhirvivekinaḥ /
upamardite 'pi bhedapratyaye karmabhyo na nivartate cetprāgiva bhedapratyayopamardanādekatvapratyayavidhāyakaṃ vākyamapramāṇīkṛtaṃ syāt /
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇādipratiṣedhavākyānāṃ prāmāṇyavadyuktamekatvavākyasyāpi prāmāṇyam /
sarvopaniṣadāṃ tatparatvāt /
karmavidhīnāmaprāmāṇa ayaprasaṅga iti cet /
na /
anupamarditabhedapratyayavatpuruṣaviṣaye prāmāṇyopapatteḥ svapnādipratyaya iva prākprabodhāt /
vivekināmakaraṇātkarmavidhiprāmāṇyoccheda iti cet /
na /
kāmyavidhyanucchedadarśanāt /
na hi kāmātmatā na praśastetyevaṃvijñānavadbhiḥ kāmyāni karmāṇi nānuṣṭhīyanta iti kāmyakarmavidhaya ucchidyante 'nuṣṭhīyanta eva kāmibhiriti /
tathā brahmasaṃsthairbrahmavidbhirnānuṣṭhīyante karmāṇīti na tadvidhaya ucchidyante 'brahmavidbhiranuṣṭhīyanta eveti /
parivrādakānāṃ bhikṣācaraṇādivadutpannaikatvapratyayānāmapi gṛhasthādīnāmagnihotrādikarmānivṛttiriti cenna /
prāmāṇyacintāyāṃ puruṣapravṛtteradṛṣṭāntatvāt /
na hi nābhicarediti pratiṣiddhamapyabhicaramaṃ kaścitkurvandṛṣṭa iti śatrau dveṣarahitenāpi vivekinābhicaraṇaṃ kriyate /
na ca karmavidhipravṛttinimitte bhedapratyaye bādhite 'gnihotrādau pravartakaṃ nimittamasti, parivrājakasyeva bhikṣācaraṇādau bubhukṣādi pravartakam /
ihāpyakaraṇe pratyavāyabhayaṃ pravartakamiti cet /
na /
bhedapratyayavato 'dhikṛtatvāt /
bhedapratyayavānanupamarditabhedabuddhirvidyayā yaḥ sa karmaṇyadhikṛta ityavocāma /
yo hyadhikṛtaḥ karmaṇi tasya tadakarame pratyavāyo na nivṛttādhikārasya gṛhasthasyeva brahmacāriṇo viśeṣadharmānanuṣṭhāne /
evaṃ tarhi sarvaḥ svāśramastha utpannekatvapratyayaḥ parivrāḍiti cet /
na /
svasvāmitvabhedabuddhyanivṛtteḥ /
karmārthatvāccetarāśramāṇām /
"atha karma kurvīya"iti śruteḥ /
tasmātsvasvāmitvābhāvādbhikṣureka eva parivrāṭ /
na gṛhasthādiḥ /
ekatvapratyayavidhijanitena pratyayena vidhinimittabhedapratyayasyopamarditatvādyamaniyamādyanupapattiḥ parivrājakasyeti cet /
na /
bubhukṣādinaikatvapratyayātprācyāvitasyopapatternivṛttyarthatvāt /
na ca pratiṣiddhasevāprāptiḥ /
ekatvapratyayotpatteḥ prāgeva pratiṣiddhatvāt /
na hi rātrau kūpe kaṇṭake vā patita udite 'pi savitari patati tasminneva /
tasmātsiddhaṃ nivṛttakarmā bhikṣuka eva brahmasaṃstha iti /
yatpunaruktaṃ sarveṣāṃ jñānavarjitānāṃ puṇyalokateti /
satyametat /
yaccoktaṃ tapaḥśabdena parivrāḍapyukta iti /
etadasat /
kasmāt /
parivrājakasyaiva brahmasaṃsthatāsambhavāt /
sa eva hyavaśeṣita ityavocāma /
ekatvavijñānavato 'gnihotrādivattaponivṛtteśca /
bhedabuddhimata eva hi tapaḥkartavyatā syāt /
etena karmacchidre brahmasaṃsthatāsāmarthyaṃ apratiṣedhaśca pratyuktaḥ /
tathā jñānavāneva nivṛttakarmā parivrāḍiti jñānavaiyarthyaṃ pratyuktam /
yatpunaruktaṃ yavavarāhādiśabdavatparivrājake na rūḍho brahmasaṃsthaśabda iti tatparihṛtam /
tasyaiva brahmasaṃsthatāsambhavānnānyasyeti /
yatpunaruktaṃ rūḍhaśabdā nimittaṃ nopādadata iti /
tanna /
gṛhasthatakṣaparivrājakādiśabdadarśanāt /
gṛhasthitipārivrājyatakṣaṇādinimittopādānā api gṛhasthaparivrājakāśramiviśeṣe viśiṣṭajātimati ca takṣeti rūḍhā dṛśyante śabdāḥ /
na yatra yatra tāni nimittāni tatra tatra vartante /
prasiddhyabhāvāt /
tathehāpi brahmasaṃsthaśabdo nivṛttasarvakarmatatsādhanaparivrāḍekaviṣaye 'tyāśramiṇi paramahaṃsākhye vṛtta iha bhavitumarhati /
mukhyāmṛtatvaphalaśravaṇāt /
ataścedamevaikaṃ vedoktaṃ pārivrājyam /
