na yajñopavītatridaṇḍakamaṇḍalvādiparigraha iti /
"muṇḍo 'parigraho 'saṅga"iti śrutiḥ"atyākṣamibyaḥ paramaṃ pavitram" ityādi ca śvetāśvatarīye /
"niḥstutirnirnamaskāra"ityādismṛtibhyaśca /
"tasmātkarma na kurvanti yatayaḥ pāradarśinaḥ" /
"tasmādaliṅgo dharmajño 'vyaktaliṅga"ityādismṛtibhyaśca /
yattu sāṃkhyaiḥ karmatyāgo 'bhyupagamyate /
kriyākārakaphalabhedabuddheḥ satyatvābhyupagamāt tanmṛṣā /
yacca bauddhaiḥ śūnyatābhyupagamādakartṛtvamabhyupagamyate /
tadapyasat /
tadabhyupagantuḥ sattvābhyupagamāt /
yaccājñairalasatayākartṛtvābhyupagamaḥ so 'pyasan, kārakabuddheranivartatatvātpramāṇena /
tasmādvedāntapramāṇajanitaikatvapratyayavata eva karmanivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ pārivrājyaṃ brahmasaṃsthatvaṃ ceti siddham /
etena gṛhasthasyaikatvavijñāne sati pārivrājyamarthasiddham /
nanvagnyutsādanadoṣabhāksyātparivrajan /
"vīrahā vā eṣa devānāṃ yo 'gnimudvāsayate"iti śruteḥ /
na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: vedenaivotsāditatvāt utsanna eva hi sa ekatvadarśane jāte /
children.translated_text: Because it has been superseded by the <s>Vedas</s> alone — for indeed, it is annulled when the vision of oneness arises.

children.text: apāgādagneragnitvamiti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: As the <s>śruti</s> declares: 'The fire-nature has departed from fire.'

children.text: ato na doṣabhāggṛhasthaḥ parivrajanniti //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the householder is not tainted by fault [even while] renouncing. (1)

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.23.1 continued] No. Because it [the householder's state] has been superseded by the <s>Veda</s> itself; for in the vision of oneness, it is indeed superseded. [As the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'The fire-nature has departed from fire.' Therefore, the householder who renounces (<s>parivrajan</s>) is not tainted by fault. [End of section 1.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.23.2] '<s>Prajāpati</s> brooded upon the worlds. From those worlds, thus brooded upon, the threefold knowledge (<s>trayī vidyā</s>) flowed forth. He brooded upon that [threefold knowledge]. From that, thus brooded upon, these syllables flowed forth: <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.23.2] To explain that upon which [the meditator] being established attains immortality, [the text] says: <s>Prajāpati</s> — [that is,] <s>Virāṭ</s> or <s>Kaśyapa</s> — brooded upon the worlds, meaning he performed contemplation (<s>dhyāna</s>) upon them with the desire to extract their essence. From those worlds, thus brooded upon, the threefold knowledge (<s>trayī vidyā</s>), being the essence, flowed forth — meaning it appeared in <s>Prajāpati</s>'s mind. He brooded upon that — as before. From that [threefold knowledge], thus brooded upon, these syllables flowed forth: the <s>Vyāhṛti</s>s — <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>. [End of section 2.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.23.3] 'He brooded upon those [syllables]. From those, thus brooded upon, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> flowed forth. Just as all leaves are pierced through by a stalk, so all speech is pierced through by <s>Oṃ</s>. <s>Oṃ</s> indeed is all this — <s>Oṃ</s> indeed is all this.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.23.3] He brooded upon those syllables; from those, thus brooded upon, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> flowed forth — that is <s>Brahman</s>. What is it like? He says: Just as by a stalk — the central vein of a leaf — all leaves, that is, the entire class of leaf-parts, are pierced through — meaning pervaded. So too, by <s>Oṃ</s>, which is a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self — all speech, that is, the entire class of words, is pierced through. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'The letter <s>a</s> indeed is all speech.' And because [the world is] a modification of the Supreme Self and [its names are] mere designations — therefore '<s>Oṃ</s> indeed is all this.' The twofold repetition is for emphasis. The narrative of the production of worlds and so forth is for the purpose of praising <s>Oṃ</s>. [End of section 3.]

Thus ends the twenty-third section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

=======================================================================

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.1] 'The knowers of <s>Brahman</s> say: The morning pressing (<s>prātaḥ-savana</s>) belongs to the <s>Vasu</s>s; the midday pressing (<s>mādhyandina-savana</s>) to the <s>Rudra</s>s; and the third pressing to the <s>Āditya</s>s and the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.1] In connection with the meditation on the <s>Sāman</s>, having exalted <s>Oṃ</s> — which as an accessory of ritual is now set aside, and which, as a symbol of the Supreme Self, is the cause of immortality — [the text] now wishes to teach the <s>Sāman</s>, oblation, <s>mantra</s>, and rising, which are accessories of the sacrifice that is the main subject, and says: The knowers of <s>Brahman</s> say — the morning pressing belongs to the <s>Vasu</s>s. By those [<s>Vasu</s>s], who are the lords of the morning pressing, this world has been brought under control. Likewise, by the <s>Rudra</s>s, the lords of the midday pressing, the intermediate world [has been brought under control]. And by the <s>Āditya</s>s and the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s, the lords of the third pressing, the third world has been brought under control. Therefore, no other world remains for the sacrificer. [End of section 1.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.2] 'Where then is the world of the sacrificer? He who does not know that — how should he perform [the sacrifice]? But let the knower perform it.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.2] Therefore, where is the world of the sacrificer — the world for whose sake he sacrifices? The purport is: there is no world anywhere. For the <s>śruti</s> says: 'One who sacrifices, sacrifices for the sake of a world.' And in the absence of a world, he who is the sacrificer — if he does not know the means of obtaining that world, characterized as <s>Sāman</s>, oblation, <s>mantra</s>, and rising — how should the ignorant one perform the sacrifice? His agency in performing it is in no way justified — that is the meaning. Because the [passage] is intended to praise the knowledge of the <s>Sāman</s> and the rest, the agency of the unknowing person who knows only the ritual action is not being denied. For the passage is divided [into two purposes]: for praising the knowledge of the <s>Sāman</s> and the rest, and for denying the agency of the unknowing. And in the first <s>Uṣasti</s> section, we have explained the reason why even the unknowing person does have [the capacity for] ritual action. Now, let the one who knows perform [the sacrifice] with the means — the <s>Sāman</s> and the rest — that will be described. [End of section 2.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.3] 'Before the commencement of the morning recitation (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>), [the sacrificer] sits down behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, facing north, and sings the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Vasu</s>s.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.3] What is to be known? He says: Before — prior to — the commencement of the morning recitation (<s>śastra</s>), [the sacrificer] sits down behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, facing north, and sings the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Vasu</s>s — the <s>Sāman</s> whose deity is <s>Vasu</s>. [End of section 3.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.4] '[He sings:] "Open the door of the world — lo — unveil — let us see you for sovereignty — hum — jyā — yo — ā."'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.4] 'Open the door of the world' — [meaning] the door for attaining this world of earth. 'O <s>Agni</s>, open [it]! Through that door, let us see you — for sovereignty.' [End of section 4.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.5] 'Then he offers an oblation [saying]: "Homage to <s>Agni</s>, who dwells on the earth, who dwells in the world. Find a world for me, the sacrificer. This indeed is the world of the sacrificer. I shall go there."'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.5] Then, immediately after, he offers an oblation with this <s>mantra</s>: 'Homage to <s>Agni</s> — we bow to you — who dwells on the earth, who dwells in the world of earth' — that is the meaning. 'Find a world for me, the sacrificer — obtain it. This indeed is my world, the world of the sacrificer. I shall go there.' [End of section 5.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.6] '"Here, the sacrificer, after the end of life — <s>svāhā</s>." Having said "Remove the bolt," he rises. The <s>Vasu</s>s grant him the morning pressing.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.6] 'Here, in this world, I the sacrificer, after — beyond — life, that is, having died' — that is the meaning. He offers [saying] '<s>svāhā</s>.' 'Remove — take away — the bolt of the door of the world.' Having uttered this <s>mantra</s>, he rises. Thus, by these [<s>Vasu</s>s], the world connected with the morning pressing has been redeemed; and so those <s>Vasu</s>s grant the morning pressing to the sacrificer. [End of section 6.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.7-8] 'Before the commencement of the midday pressing, [the sacrificer] sits down behind the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> fire, facing north, and sings the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Rudra</s>s. "Open the door of the world — lo — unveil — let us see you for sovereignty — hum — jyā — yo — ā."'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.7-8] Likewise, [the sacrificer] sits down behind the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> — the southern fire — facing north, and sings the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Rudra</s>s — the <s>Sāman</s> whose deity is <s>Rudra</s> — the sacrificer [sings this] for sovereignty. [End of sections 7-8.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.9-10] 'Then he offers an oblation [saying]: "Homage to <s>Vāyu</s>, who dwells in the intermediate space, who dwells in the world. Find a world for me, the sacrificer. This indeed is the world of the sacrificer. I shall go there. Here, the sacrificer, after the end of life — <s>svāhā</s>." Having said "Remove the bolt," he rises. The <s>Rudra</s>s grant him the midday pressing.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.9-10] 'Who dwells in the intermediate space' and the rest — the same [explanation as before]. [End of section 9.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.11-13] 'Before the commencement of the third pressing, [the sacrificer] sits down behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, facing north, and sings the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Āditya</s>s and the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s. "Open the door of the world — lo — unveil — let us see you for supreme sovereignty — hum — jyā — yo — ā" — [this is] the <s>Āditya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]. Then the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]: "Open the door of the world — lo — unveil — let us see you for paramount sovereignty — hum — jyā — yo — ā."'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.11-13] Likewise, [the sacrificer] sits down behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, facing north, and sings in sequence the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Āditya</s>s — whose deity is <s>Āditya</s> — and the <s>Vaiśvadeva Sāman</s> — for supreme sovereignty (<s>svārājya</s>) and paramount sovereignty (<s>sāmrājya</s>), respectively. [End of sections 11-13.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.14-15] 'Then he offers an oblation [saying]: "Homage to the <s>Āditya</s>s and to the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s — those who dwell in heaven, who dwell in the world. Find a world for me, the sacrificer. This indeed is the world of the sacrificer. I shall go there. Here, the sacrificer, after the end of life — <s>svāhā</s>." Having said "Remove the bolt," he rises.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.14-15] 'Those who dwell in heaven' and the rest — the same [explanation applies]. The only difference is the plural form in 'find' (<s>vindata</s>) and 'remove' (<s>apahata</s>). But this [entire section] pertains to the sacrificer — as is indicated by [the passage]: 'I shall go there, the sacrificer' and so forth. [End of sections 14-15.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 2.24.16] 'The <s>Āditya</s>s and the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s grant him the third pressing. He indeed who knows the measure of the sacrifice — he who knows this, he who knows this.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 2.24.16] This sacrificer who knows thus — the one who knows the <s>Sāman</s> and the rest as described — knows the measure (<s>mātrā</s>) of the sacrifice, that is, the true nature of the sacrifice, as stated. The twofold repetition of 'he who knows this' is for the purpose of concluding the chapter. [End of section 16.]

Thus ends the twenty-fourth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.
Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad-brāhmaṇa</s>.
<s>Oṃ</s>
Now begins the third chapter.

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.1.1] 'That sun yonder is indeed the honey of the gods. Heaven is its crossbeam. The intermediate space is the honeycomb. The rays are the offspring.'

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.1.1] 'That sun yonder' and so forth — the connection at the beginning of this chapter [is as follows]: At the end of the immediately preceding chapter, it was said: 'He knows the measure of the sacrifice.' And the <s>Sāman</s>, oblation, <s>mantra</s>, and rising — which pertain to the sacrifice — were taught as accessories of the sacrifice for the attainment of a distinguished fruit. And the sun, which is the visible result of all sacrifices of all beings, shines with great splendor. That [sun], being the fruit of the actions of all living beings, is directly depended upon by all. Therefore, after the mention of sacrifice, the <s>śruti</s> begins [this chapter], intending: 'I shall prescribe a meditation regarding the sun — the product of that [sacrifice] — which yields the most excellent of all human goals.' [It says:] 'That sun yonder is indeed the honey of the gods' and so forth. The sun is like honey because of the enjoyment (<s>modana</s>) of the gods. And [the text] will state that [the sun] is the cause of enjoyment for the <s>Vasu</s>s and others, because the sun has the nature of the fruit of all sacrifices. How is it like honey? He says: Of that honey, heaven is like the crossbeam of a bee-hive — [that is,] [heaven is] both transverse and a beam. For heaven is perceived as extending transversely. And the intermediate space is like the honeycomb attached to the crossbeam of heaven, hanging down as it were; therefore, because of its similarity to a honeycomb, the intermediate space is the honeycomb — and because it is the support of the sun [which is the honey]. The rays (<s>marīci</s>s) — the beams of the sun — [in them abide] earthly waters drawn up by the sun. 'These waters are the self-ruling ones which are the rays' — thus it is known. Those [waters], being contained within the rays which are in the honeycomb of the intermediate space, are like bee-eggs — they are perceived as offspring, as it were. For the offspring of bees are inside the tubes of the honeycomb. [End of section 1.]

[<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.1.2] 'Its eastern rays are its eastern honey-channels. The <s>Ṛc</s>s are the honey-makers. The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the flower. Those immortal waters — those <s>Ṛc</s>s —'

children.text: START ChUp 2,23.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.23.2]

children.text:
prajāpatir lokān abhyatapat |
tebhyo 'bhitaptebhyas trayī vidyā saṃprāsravat |
tām abhyatapat |
tasyā abhitaptāyā etāny akṣarāṇi saṃprasrvanta bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti || ChUp_2,23.2 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Prajāpati</s> brooded over the worlds. From them, thus heated, the threefold knowledge flowed forth. He brooded over that. From it, thus heated, these syllables flowed forth: <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>.' (ChUp 2.23.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,23.2 yatsaṃstho 'mṛtatvameti tannirūpaṇārthamāha -prajāpatirvirāṭ kaśyapo vā lokānuddiśya teṣu sārajighṛkṣayābhyata padabhitāpaṃ kṛtavāndhyānaṃ tapaḥ kṛtavānityarthaḥ /
tebhyo 'bhitaptebhyaḥ sārabhūtā trayī vidyā samprāsravatprajāpatermanasi pratyabhādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: From those [worlds] thus heated, the threefold knowledge — being their essence — flowed forth, meaning it manifested in <s>Prajāpati's</s> mind.

children.text: tāmabhyatapat /
children.translated_text: He brooded over that [threefold knowledge].

children.text: pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: As before.

children.text: tasyā abhitaptāyā etānyakṣarāṇi samprāsravanta bhūrbhuvaḥ svaritivyāhṛtayaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: From it, thus heated, these syllables flowed forth — the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances): <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.23.2:] To explain that in which one is established and attains immortality, he says — <s>Prajāpati</s>, that is <s>Virāṭ</s> or <s>Kaśyapa</s>, directing his attention toward the worlds, with the desire to extract their essence, brooded over them — performed austerity (<s>tapas</s>), meaning he performed meditation.

children.text: START ChUp 2,23.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.23.3]

children.text:
tāny abhyatapat |
tebhyo 'bhitaptebhya oṃkāraḥ saṃprāsravat |
tad yathā śaṅkunā sarvāṇi parṇāni saṃtṛṇṇāny evam oṃkāreṇa sarvā vāk saṃtṛṇṇā |
oṃkāra evedaṃ sarvam oṃkāra eva idaṃ sarvam || ChUp_2,23.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He brooded over them. From them, thus heated, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> flowed forth. Just as all leaves are held together by a stalk, so all speech is held together by <s>Oṃ</s>. <s>Oṃ</s> is all this. <s>Oṃ</s> is indeed all this.' (ChUp 2.23.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,23.3 tānyakṣarāṇyabhyatapattebhyo 'bhitaptebhya oṅkāraḥ samprāsravattadbrahma, kīdṛśamityāha-tadyathā śaṅkunā parṇanālena sarvāṇi parṇāni patrāvayavajātāni santṛṇṇāni nividdhāni vyāptānītyarthaḥ /
evamoṅkāreṇa brahmaṇā paramātmanaḥ pratīkabhūtena sarvā vākyaśabdajātaṃ santṛṇṇā /
"akāro vai sarvā vāk"ityādiśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'The letter <s>a</s> is indeed all speech' and so forth.

children.text: paramātmavikāraśca nāmadheyamātramityata oṅkāra evedaṃ sarvamiti /
children.translated_text: And since the transformation of the Supreme Self is merely a name, therefore '<s>Oṃkāra</s> is indeed all this.'

children.text: dvirabhyāsa ādarārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The repetition [of the phrase] twice is for emphasis.

children.text: lokādiniṣpādanakathanamoṅkārastutyarthamiti //3//
children.translated_text: The narration of the production of the worlds and so forth is for the purpose of praising <s>Oṃkāra</s>. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.23.3:] He brooded over those syllables; from them, thus heated, <s>Oṃkāra</s> flowed forth — that is <s>Brahman</s>. What is it like? He says — just as by a stalk, the midrib of a leaf, all leaves — all the parts of leaves — are pierced through, penetrated, pervaded — that is the meaning. Similarly, by <s>Oṃkāra</s> — by <s>Brahman</s>, which is the symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) of the Supreme Self — all speech, the entire collection of words, is pierced through.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya trayoviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.1]

children.text:
brahmavādino vadanti |
yad vasūnāṃ prātaḥsavanam |
rudrāṇāṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam |
ādityānāṃ ca viśveṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tṛtīyasavanam || ChUp_2,24.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The knowers of <s>Brahman</s> declare: The morning pressing belongs to the <s>Vasus</s>. The midday pressing belongs to the <s>Rudras</s>. The third pressing belongs to the <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>.' (ChUp 2.24.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.1 sāmopāsanaprasaṅgena karmaguṇabhūtatvānnivartyoṅkāraṃ paramātmapratīkatvādamṛtatvahetutvena mahīkṛtya prakṛtasyaiva yajñasyāṅgabhūtāni sāmahomamantrotthānānyupadidikṣannāha-brahmavādino vadanti yatprātaḥsavanaṃ tadvasūnām /
taiśca prātaḥ savanasambaddho 'yaṃ loko vaśīkṛtaḥ savaneśānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And by these <s>Vasus</s>, who are the lords of the morning pressing, this world has been brought under control.

children.text: tathā rudrairmādhyandinasavaneśānairantarikṣalokaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, by the <s>Rudras</s>, who are the lords of the midday pressing, the intermediate world [has been brought under control].

children.text: ādityaiśca viśvairdevaiśca tṛtīyasavaneśānaistṛtīyo loko vaśīkṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And by the <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, who are the lords of the third pressing, the third world has been brought under control.

children.text: iti yajamānasya loko 'nyaḥ pariśiṣṭo na vidyate //1 //
children.translated_text: Thus, no other world remains for the sacrificer. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.1:] In connection with the meditation on <s>Sāman</s>, having exalted <s>Oṃkāra</s> — which, being an auxiliary of ritual action, is to be set aside [from ritual], but being a symbol of the Supreme Self, is a cause of immortality — wishing to teach the <s>Sāma</s>-chanting, oblation, mantra-recitation, and rising, which are subsidiary parts of the very sacrifice under discussion, he says — the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> declare: the morning pressing belongs to the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.2]

children.text:
kva tarhi yajamānasya loka iti |
sa yas taṃ na vidyāt kathaṃ kuryāt |
atha vidvān kuryāt || ChUp_2,24.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Where then is the world of the sacrificer? He who does not know this — how could he perform [the sacrifice]? But let the one who knows perform it.' (ChUp 2.24.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_2,24.2 ataḥ kva tarhi yajamānasya loko yadarthaṃ yajate /
na kvacilloko 'stītyabhiprāyaḥ /
"lokāya vai yajate yo yajate"iti śruteḥ /
lokābhāve ca sa yo yajamānastaṃ lokasvīkaraṇopāyaṃ sāmahomamantrotthānalakṣaṇaṃ na vidyānna vijānīyātso 'jñaḥ kathaṃ kuryādyajñaṃ na kathañcana tasya kartṛtvamupapadyata ityarthaḥ /
sāmādivijñānastutiparatvānnāviduṣaḥ kartṛtvaṃ karmamātravidaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: Since this is aimed at praising the knowledge of <s>Sāman</s> and the rest, the agency of the ignorant person who knows only the ritual is not [actually] denied.

children.text: stutaye ca sāmādivijñānasyāvidvatkartṛtvapratiṣedhāya ceti hi bhidyate vākyam /
children.translated_text: The sentence is divided into [two purposes]: for the praise of the knowledge of <s>Sāman</s> and the rest, and for the denial of the agency of the ignorant.

children.text: ādye cauṣastye kāṇḍe 'viduṣo 'pi karmāstīti hetumavocāma /
children.translated_text: And in the first and sixth chapters, we stated the reason that even the ignorant has ritual [eligibility].

children.text: athaitadvakṣyamāṇaṃ sāmādyupāyaṃ vidvānkuryāt //2//
children.translated_text: But let the one who knows perform [the sacrifice] with the means of <s>Sāman</s> and the rest that will now be described. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.2:] Therefore, where indeed is the world of the sacrificer — for the sake of which he sacrifices? The implication is: there is no world anywhere. Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'For a world indeed does one sacrifice who sacrifices.' And in the absence of a world, he who is the sacrificer — if he does not know that method of securing a world characterized by <s>Sāma</s>-chanting, oblation, mantra-recitation, and rising — that ignorant person, how could he perform the sacrifice? In no way can his agency be established — this is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.3]

children.text: purā prātaranuvākasyopākaraṇāj jaghanena gārhapatyasyodāṅmukha upaviśya sa vāsavaṃ sāmābhigāyati || ChUp_2,24.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Before the commencement of the morning recitation, sitting behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, facing north, he chants the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Vasus</s>.' (ChUp 2.24.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.3 kiṃ tadvedyamityāha-purā pūrvaṃ prātaranuvākasya śasrasya prārambhājjaghanena gārhapatyasya paścādudaṅmukhaḥ sannupaviśya sa vāsavaṃ vasudaivatyaṃ sāmābhigāyati //3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.3:] What is that to be known? He says — before, that is prior to, the commencement of the morning recitation (<s>śastra</s>), sitting behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, facing north, he chants the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Vasus</s> — having the <s>Vasus</s> as its deities. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.4]

children.text:
lo 3 kadvāram apāvā 3 rṇū 33 |
paśyema tvā vayaṃ rā 33333 hu 3 m ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 iti || ChUp_2,24.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'O [<s>Agni</s>], open the door of the world! Let us see you, for the sake of sovereignty!' (ChUp 2.24.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.4 lokadvāramasya pṛthivīlokasya prāptaye dvāramapāvṛṇu he 'gne tena dvāreṇa paśyema tvā tvāṃ rājyāyeti //4 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.4:] 'Door of the world' — open the door for attaining this earthly world, O <s>Agni</s>! Through that door, let us see you — for the sake of sovereignty. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.5]

children.text:
atha juhoti |
namo 'gnaye pṛthivīkṣite lokakṣite |
lokaṃ me yajamānāya vinda |
eṣa vai yajamānasya lokaḥ |
etā asmi || ChUp_2,24.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then he offers the oblation: "Salutation to <s>Agni</s>, who dwells in the earth, who dwells in the world. Find a world for me, the sacrificer. This indeed is the world of the sacrificer. I shall go there."' (ChUp 2.24.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.5 athānantaraṃ juhotyanena mantreṇa namo 'gnaye prahvībhūtāstubhyaṃ vayaṃ pṛthivīkṣite pṛthivīnivāsāya lokakṣite pṛthivīlokanivāsāyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.5:] Then, next, he offers an oblation with this mantra: 'Salutation to <s>Agni</s>' — we bow to you, O dweller in the earth (<s>pṛthivīkṣit</s>) — meaning one who resides in the earth; world-dweller (<s>lokakṣit</s>) — meaning one who resides in the earthly world.

children.text: lokaṃ me mahyaṃ yajamānāya vinda labhasva /
children.translated_text: 'Find a world for me' — obtain it for me, the sacrificer.

children.text: eṣa vai mama yajamānasya loka etā gantāsmi //5 //
children.translated_text: 'This indeed is my world, the sacrificer's world — there shall I go.' (5)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.6]

children.text:
atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā |
apajahi parigham ity uktvottiṣṭhati |
tasmai vasavaḥ prātaḥsavanaṃ saṃprayacchanti || ChUp_2,24.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Here the sacrificer [declares]: "After the end of life — <s>svāhā</s>!" Having said "Remove the bolt," he rises. To him the <s>Vasus</s> grant the morning pressing.' (ChUp 2.24.6)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.6 atrāsmiṃlloke yajamāno 'hamāyuṣaḥ parastādūrdhvaṃ mṛtaḥ sannityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.6:] 'Here' — in this world — the sacrificer, I — 'after life' — meaning after death, having died.

children.text: svāhoti juhoti /
children.translated_text: He offers with '<s>Svāhā</s>.'

children.text: apajahyapanaya parighaṃ lokadvārārgalamityevaṃ mantramuktvottiṣṭhati evametairvasubhyaḥ prātaḥ savanasambaddho loko niṣkrītaḥ syāttataste prātaḥsavanaṃ dhasavo yajamānāya samprayacchanti //6 //
children.translated_text: 'Remove the bolt' — remove the bar of the door of the world — having uttered this mantra, he rises. In this way, by these <s>Vasus</s>, the world connected with the morning pressing is redeemed; then those <s>Vasus</s> grant the morning pressing to the sacrificer. (6)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.7-8
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.7-8]

children.text: purā mādhyandinasya savanasyopākaraṇāj jaghanenāgnīdhrīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa raudraṃ sāmābhigāyati || ChUp_2,24.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'Before the commencement of the midday pressing, sitting behind the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> fire, facing north, he chants the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Rudras</s>.' (ChUp 2.24.7)

children.text:
lo 3 kadvāramapāvār 3 ṇū 33 |
paśyema tvā vayaṃ vairā 33333 hu 3 m ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 iti || ChUp_2,24.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'O [<s>Vāyu</s>], open the door of the world! Let us see you, for the sake of universal sovereignty!' (ChUp 2.24.8)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.7,8 tathā'gnīdhrīyasya dakṣiṇāgnerjaghanenodaṅmukha upaviśya sa raudraṃ sāmābhigāyati yajamāno rudradaivatyaṃvairājyāya //7-8 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.7-8:] Similarly, sitting behind the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> (the southern fire), facing north, the sacrificer chants the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Rudras</s> — having <s>Rudra</s> as its deity — for the sake of universal sovereignty (<s>vairājya</s>). (7-8)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.9-10
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.9-10]

children.text:
atha juhoti |
nāmo vāyave 'ntarikṣakṣite lokakṣite |
lokaṃ me yajamānāya vinda |
eṣa vai yajamānasya lokaḥ |
etāsmi || ChUp_2,24.9 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then he offers the oblation: "Salutation to <s>Vāyu</s>, who dwells in the atmosphere, who dwells in the world. Find a world for me, the sacrificer. This indeed is the world of the sacrificer. I shall go there."' (ChUp 2.24.9)

children.text:
atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā |
apajahi parigham ity uktvottiṣṭhati |
tasmai rudrā mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ saṃprayacchanti || ChUp_2,24.10 ||
children.translated_text: 'Here the sacrificer [declares]: "After the end of life — <s>svāhā</s>!" Having said "Remove the bolt," he rises. To him the <s>Rudras</s> grant the midday pressing.' (ChUp 2.24.10)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.9.10 antarikṣakṣita ityādi samānam //9//
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.9-10:] 'Who dwells in the atmosphere' and so forth — the rest is the same [as before]. (9)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.11-13
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.11-13]

children.text: purā tṛtīyasavanasyopākaraṇāj jaghanenāhavanīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa ādityaṃ sa vaiśvadevaṃ sāmābhigāyati || ChUp_2,24.11 ||
children.translated_text: 'Before the commencement of the third pressing, sitting behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, facing north, he chants the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Sāman</s> sacred to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>.' (ChUp 2.24.11)

children.text:
lo 3 kadvāramapāvā 3 rṇū33 |
paśyema tvā vayaṃ svārā 33333 hu3m, ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 ity ādityam || ChUp_2,24.12 ||
children.translated_text: 'O [<s>Ādityas</s>], open the door of the world! Let us see you, for the sake of supreme sovereignty!' — [this is] the <s>Āditya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]. (ChUp 2.24.12)

children.text:
atha vaiśvadevam |
lo3kadvāramapāvā3rṇū33 |
paśyema tvā vayaṃ sāmrā 33333 hu3m ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 iti || ChUp_2,24.13 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]: "O [<s>Viśvedevas</s>], open the door of the world! Let us see you, for the sake of imperial sovereignty!"' (ChUp 2.24.13)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.11-13 tathā'havanīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa ādityadaivatyamādityaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca sāmābhigāyati krameṇa svārājyāya sāmrājyāya //11-13 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.11-13:] Similarly, sitting behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, facing north, he chants the <s>Sāman</s> having the <s>Ādityas</s> as its deity, and the <s>Vaiśvadeva Sāman</s>, in order — for supreme sovereignty (<s>svārājya</s>) and for imperial sovereignty (<s>sāmrājya</s>). (11-13)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.14-15
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.14-15]

children.text:
atha juhoti |
nama ādityebhyaś ca viśvebhyaś ca devebhyo divikṣidbhyo lokakṣidbhyaḥ |
lokaṃ me yajamānāya vindata || ChUp_2,24.14 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then he offers: "Salutation to the <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, who dwell in heaven, who dwell in the world. Find a world for me, the sacrificer."' (ChUp 2.24.14)

children.text:
eṣa vai yajamānasya lokaḥ |
etāsmy atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā |
apahata parigham ity uktvottiṣṭhati || ChUp_2,24.15 ||
children.translated_text: '"This indeed is the world of the sacrificer. I shall go there. Here the sacrificer — after the end of life — <s>svāhā</s>!" Having said "Remove the bolt," he rises.' (ChUp 2.24.15)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.14-15 divikṣidbhya ityevamādi samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.14-15:] 'Who dwell in heaven' and so forth — the rest is the same.

children.text: vindatāpahateti bahivacanamātraṃ viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Find' and 'remove' — the only difference is the use of the plural form.

children.text: yājamānaṃ tvetat /
children.translated_text: But this [entire passage] pertains to the sacrificer.

children.text: etāsmyatra yajamāna ityādiliṅgāt //14-15 //
children.translated_text: This is indicated by the expression 'I shall go there, O sacrificer' and so forth. (14-15)

children.text: START ChUp 2,24.16
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.24.16]

children.text:
tasmā ādityāś ca viśve ca devās tṛtīyasavanaṃ saṃprayacchanti |
eṣa ha vai yajñasya mātrāṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_2,24.16 ||
children.translated_text: 'To him the <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Viśvedevas</s> grant the third pressing. He who knows this indeed knows the measure of the sacrifice — he who knows this.' (ChUp 2.24.16)

children.text: ChUpBh_2,24.16 eṣa ha vai yajamāna evaṃvit yathoktasya sāmādervidvānyajñasya mātrāṃ yajñayāthātmyaṃ veda yathoktam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 2.24.16:] This sacrificer, the one who knows thus — the knower of the <s>Sāman</s> and the rest as described — knows the measure of the sacrifice, the true nature of the sacrifice, as stated.

children.text: ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ vedeti dviruktiradhyāyaparisamāptyarthā //16 //
children.translated_text: 'He who knows this, he who knows this' — the repetition twice is for indicating the conclusion of the chapter. (16)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāyasya caturviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth section of the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadbrāhmaṇe dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>

children.text: atha tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now [begins] the third chapter.

children.text: START ChUp 3,1.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.1]

children.text:
asau vā ādityo devamadhu |
tasya dyaur eva tiraścīnavaṃśaḥ |
antarikṣam apūpaḥ |
marīcayaḥ putrāḥ || ChUp_3,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'That sun up there is verily the honey of the gods. Heaven is its crossbeam. The atmosphere is the honeycomb. The rays are its offspring.' (ChUp 3.1.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,1.1 asau vā āditya utyādyadhyāyārambhe sambandhaḥ /
atītānantarādhyāyānta uktaṃ yajñasya mātrāṃ vedeti yajñaviṣayāṇi ca sāmahomamantrotthānāni viśiṣṭaphalaprāptaye yajñāṅgabhūtānyupadiṣṭāni /
sarvayajñānāṃ ca kāryanirvṛttirūpaḥ savitā mahatyā śriyā dīpyate /
sa eṣa sarvaprāṇikarmaphalabhūtaḥ pratyakṣaṃ sarvairupajīvyate /
ato yajñavyapadeśānantaraṃ tatkāryabhūtasavitṛviṣayamupāsanaṃ sarvapuruṣārthebhyaḥ śreṣṭhatamaphalaṃ vidhāsyāmītyevamārabhate śrutiḥ-asau vā ādityo devamadhvityādi /
devanāṃ modanānmadhviva madhvasāvādityaḥ /
vasvādīnāṃ ca modanahetutvaṃ vakṣyati sarvayajñaphalarūpatvādādityasya /
kathaṃ madhutvamityāha-tasya madhuno dyaureva bhrāmarasyeva madhunastiraścīnaścāsau vaṃśaśceti tiraścīnavaṃśaḥ /
tiryaggateva hi dyaurlakṣyate /
children.translated_text: For heaven appears to extend horizontally.

children.text: antarikṣaṃ ca madhvapūpo dyuvaṃśe lagnaḥ sallaṃmbata ivāto madhvapūpasāmānyādantarikṣaṃ madhvapūpo madhunaḥ saviturāśrayatvācca /
children.translated_text: And the atmosphere is the honeycomb — attached to the heavenly beam, it hangs as it were; hence, because of its similarity to the honeycomb and because it is the support of the sun [which is] the honey, the atmosphere is the honeycomb.

children.text: marīcayo raśmayo raśmisthā āpo bhaumāḥ savitrākṛṣṭāḥ"etā vā āpaḥ svarājo yanmarīcaya"iti iti hi vijñāyate /
children.translated_text: The rays (<s>marīci</s>) — the beams — [and] the waters in the rays, the terrestrial waters drawn up by the sun — 'These waters are self-luminous, which are the rays' — thus it is known.

children.text: tā antarikṣamadhvapūpastharaśmyantargatatvādbhramarabījabhūtāḥ putrā iva hitā lakṣyanta iti putrā iva putrā madhvapūpanāḍyantargatā hi bhramaraputrāḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: These [waters], being within the rays situated in the atmospheric honeycomb, are like the seeds of bees — they appear as offspring, like offspring. Just as bee-larvae are within the tubes of the honeycomb, [so are these waters within the rays]. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.1.1:] 'That sun up there' and so forth — at the beginning of the chapter, the connection [is as follows]: At the end of the immediately preceding chapter it was said 'he knows the measure of the sacrifice,' and the <s>Sāma</s>-chanting, oblation, mantra-recitation, and rising were taught as auxiliaries of sacrifice for the attainment of a special result. And the product of all sacrifices — the sun (<s>Savitṛ</s>) — shines with great splendor. He, being the fruit of the actions of all beings, is directly depended upon by all. Therefore, immediately after the mention of sacrifice, the <s>śruti</s> begins this meditation on the sun — which is the effect of sacrifice — as yielding the highest fruit among all human goals, saying 'That sun up there is verily the honey of the gods' and so forth. The sun is the honey of the gods because it is the cause of their rejoicing (<s>modana</s>), like honey. And the <s>śruti</s> will state that it causes the rejoicing of the <s>Vasus</s> and others, since the sun is the embodiment of the fruits of all sacrifices. How is it like honey? He says — of that honey, heaven is like the crossbeam of a beehive — being both crosswise and a beam, it is a crossbeam (<s>tiraścīnavaṃśa</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 3,1.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.2]

children.text:
tasya ye prāñco raśmayas tā evāsya prācyo madhunāḍyaḥ |
ṛca eva madhukṛtaḥ |
ṛgveda eva puṣpam |
tā amṛtā āpaḥ |
tā vā etā ṛcaḥ || ChUp_3,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Its eastern rays are its eastern honey-channels. The <s>Ṛc</s> verses are the honey-makers. The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the flower. Those immortal waters [are the honey]. These <s>Ṛc</s> verses —' (ChUp 3.1.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,1.2 tasya saviturmadhvāśrayasya madhuno ye prāñcaḥ prācyāṃ diśi gatā raśmayastā evāsya prācyaḥ prāgañcanānmadhuno nāḍyo madhunāḍya iva madhvādhāracchidrāṇītyarthaḥ /
tatra ṛca eva madhukṛto lohitarūpaṃ savitrāśrayaṃ madhu kurvantīti madhukṛto bhramarā iva yato rasānādāya madhu kurvanti /
tatpuṣpamiva puṣpamṛgveda eva /
tatra ṛgbrāhmaṇasamudāyasya ṛgvedākhyatvācchabdamātrācca bhogyarūparasanisrāvāsambhavādṛgvedaśabdenātra ṛgvedavihitaṃ karma /
tato hi karmaphalabhūtamadhurasanisrāvasambhavāt /
children.translated_text: For from that [ritual action], the outflow of the essence that is the fruit of action — the honey — is possible.

children.text: madhukarairiva puṣpasthānīyādṛgvedavihitātkarmaṇo 'pa ādāya ṛgbhirmadhu nirvartyate /
children.translated_text: Just as by bees from the flower-counterpart — the ritual action enjoined by the <s>Ṛgveda</s> — taking the waters, honey is produced by the <s>Ṛc</s> verses.

children.text: kāstā āpa ityāha-tāḥ karmaṇi prayuktāḥ somājyapayorūpā agnau prakṣiptāstatpākābhinirvṛttā amṛtā amṛtārthatvādatyanta rasavatya āpo bhavanti /
children.translated_text: What are those waters? He says: those [waters], employed in the ritual action — in the form of <s>soma</s>, clarified butter, and milk — cast into the fire — transformed by that cooking — become immortal [waters], because of being for the purpose of immortality, and exceedingly rich in essence.

children.text: tadrasānādāya tā vā etā ṝcaḥ puṣpebhyo rasamādadānā eva bhramarāḥ ṛcaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: Taking those essences, these <s>Ṛc</s> verses are like bees extracting essence from flowers — [they are] the <s>Ṛc</s> verses [themselves]. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.1.2:] Of this sun (<s>Savitṛ</s>), the substratum of the honey — the rays that have gone eastward, to the eastern direction — those are its eastern honey-channels (<s>madhunāḍīs</s>), like the openings of a honey-reservoir, is the meaning. There, the <s>Ṛc</s> verses alone are the honey-makers (<s>madhukṛtas</s>), like bees producing the honey that has the form of reddish [color] and has the sun as its substratum — [they are] like bees that take essences and make honey. That flower is like a flower — and the flower is the <s>Ṛgveda</s> itself. There, because the collection of <s>Ṛc</s> verses and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> bears the name '<s>Ṛgveda</s>', and because from mere words no outflow of enjoyable essence is possible — [therefore] by the word '<s>Ṛgveda</s>' here is meant the ritual action enjoined by the <s>Ṛgveda</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,1.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.3]

children.text:
etam ṛgvedam abhyatapan |
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata || ChUp_3,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'They heated (<s>abhyatapan</s>) this <s>Ṛgveda</s>. From it, thus heated, was born fame (<s>yaśas</s>), splendor (<s>tejas</s>), sense-power (<s>indriya</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), and food-essence (<s>annādya</s>) — the essence (<s>rasa</s>).' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.1.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,1.3 etamṛgvedamṛgvedavihitaṃ karma puṣpasthānīyamabhyatapannabhitāpaṃ kṛtavatya ivaitā ṛcaḥ karmaṇi prayuktāḥ /
ṝgbhirhi mantraiḥ śasrādyaṅgabhāvamupagataiḥ kriyamāṇaṃ karma madhunirvartakaṃ rasaṃ muñcatītyupapadyate puṣpāṇīva bhramarairācūṣyamāṇāni /
tadetadāha-tasyargvedasyābhitaptasya /
children.translated_text: This is stated: 'of that <s>Ṛgveda</s>, thus heated.'

children.text: ko 'sau raso ya ṛṅmadhukarābhitāpaniḥsṛta ityucyate /
children.translated_text: What is that essence that flows forth from the heating by the <s>Ṛc</s> honey-makers? It is stated:

children.text: yaśo viśrutatvaṃ tejo dehagatā dīptirindriyaṃ sāmarthyopetairindriyairavaikalyaṃ vīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ balamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fame (<s>yaśas</s>) is renown; splendor (<s>tejas</s>) is the bodily radiance; sense-power (<s>indriya</s>) is the freedom from deficiency in sense organs endowed with capability; vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is capability, meaning strength.

children.text: annādyamannaṃ ca tadādyaṃ ca yenopayujyamānenāhanyahani devānāṃ sthitiḥ syāttadannādyameṣa raso 'jāyata yāgādilakṣaṇātkarmaṇaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: Food-essence (<s>annādya</s>) — food and what is eaten with it — that by the consumption of which day by day the stability of the gods would be maintained — this is the food-essence. This essence was born from the ritual action characterized by sacrifice and the like. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.1.3:] 'They heated this <s>Ṛgveda</s>' — meaning the ritual action enjoined by the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the flower-counterpart; these <s>Ṛc</s> verses, employed in the ritual action, performed a heating as it were. For through the <s>Ṛc</s> mantras, having assumed the status of accessories [of the ritual] such as the <s>śastra</s> recitation and the like, the ritual action being performed releases the essence that produces honey — this is justified — just as flowers being sucked by bees.

children.text: START ChUp 3,1.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.4]

children.text:
tad vyakṣarat |
tad ādityam abhito 'śrayat |
tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya rohitaṃ rūpam || ChUp_3,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'That flowed forth. It took shelter in the sun, on its side. That indeed is this — what is this reddish (<s>rohita</s>) form of the sun.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.1.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,1.4 yaśa ādyannādyaparyantaṃ tadvyakṣaradviśeṣeṇākṣaradagamat /
gatvā ca tadādityamabhitaḥ pārśvataḥ pūrvabhāgaṃ savituraśrayadāśritavadityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone, it took shelter in the sun on its side — meaning on the eastern face of the sun, it became established — this is the meaning.

children.text: amuṣminnāditye sañcitaṃ karmaphalākhyaṃ madhu bhokṣyāmaha ityevaṃ hi yaśa-ādilakṣaṇaphalaprāptaye karmāṇi kriyante manuṣyaiḥ kedāraniṣpādanamiva karṣakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'We shall enjoy this honey — this fruit of action — stored up in this sun' — for it is with this [intention] that ritual actions are performed by men for the attainment of the fruit characterized by fame and the like — just as cultivators prepare fields.

children.text: tatpratyakṣaṃ pradarśyate śraddhāhetostadvā etat /
children.translated_text: That [essence] is shown directly, for the sake of producing faith — 'that indeed is this.'

children.text: kiṃ tadyadetadādityasyodyato dṛśyate rohitaṃ rūpam //4//
children.translated_text: What is that? That which is the reddish form of the sun, seen at its rising. (4)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.1.4:] That [essence], from fame through food-essence, flowed forth — particularly flowed out, went.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,2.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.2.1]

children.text:
atha ye 'sya dakṣiṇā raśmayas tā evāsya dakṣiṇā madhunāḍyaḥ |
yajūṃṣy eva madhukṛtaḥ |
yajurveda eva puṣpam |
tā amṛtā āpaḥ || ChUp_3,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the rays that go to its south — those are its southern honey-channels. The <s>Yajus</s> formulas alone are the honey-makers. The <s>Yajurveda</s> is the flower. Those immortal waters [are the essence].' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.2.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,2.1 atha ye 'sya dakṣiṇā raśmaya ityādi samānam /
yajūṃ#yeva madhukṛto yajurvedavihite karmaṇi prayuktāni /
children.translated_text: The <s>Yajus</s> formulas alone are the honey-makers — employed in the ritual action enjoined by the <s>Yajurveda</s>.

children.text: pūrvavanmadhukṛta iva /
children.translated_text: Like honey-makers, as before.

children.text: yajurvedavihitaṃ karma puṣpasthānīyaṃ puṣpamityucyate /
children.translated_text: The ritual action enjoined by the <s>Yajurveda</s> is the flower-counterpart — [and so] is called the flower.

children.text: tā eva somādyā amṛtā āpaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Those same <s>soma</s> and other [liquids] are the immortal waters. (1)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.2.1:] 'Now, the rays that go to its south' — and so forth; the same [explanation applies].

children.text: START ChUp 3,2.2-3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.2.2-3]

children.text:
tāni vā etāni yajūṃṣy etaṃ yajurvedam abhyatapan |
tasya abhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata || ChUp_3,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Those <s>Yajus</s> formulas heated this <s>Yajurveda</s>. From it, thus heated, was born fame, splendor, sense-power, vigor, and food-essence — the essence.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.2.2)

children.text:
tad vyakṣarat |
tad ādityam abhito 'śrayat |
tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya śuklaṃ rūpam || ChUp_3,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That flowed forth. It took shelter in the sun, on its side. That indeed is this — what is this white (<s>śukla</s>) form of the sun.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.2.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,2.2,3 tāni vā etāni yajūṃṣyetaṃ yajurvedamabhyatapannityevamādi sarvaṃ samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.2.2-3:] 'Those <s>Yajus</s> formulas heated this <s>Yajurveda</s>' — and so forth; everything is the same.

children.text: madhvetadādityasya dṛśyate śuklaṃ rūpam //2--3 //
children.translated_text: This honey is the white form of the sun that is seen. (2-3)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,3.1-3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.3.1-3]

children.text:
atha ye 'sya pratyañco raśmāyas tā evāsya pratīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ |
sāmāny eva madhukṛtaḥ |
sāmaveda eva puṣpam |
tā amṛtā āpaḥ || ChUp_3,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the rays that go to its west — those are its western honey-channels. The <s>Sāman</s> chants alone are the honey-makers. The <s>Sāmaveda</s> is the flower. Those immortal waters [are the essence].' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.3.1)

children.text:
tāni vā etāni sāmāny etaṃ sāmavedam abhyatapan |
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata || ChUp_3,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Those <s>Sāman</s> chants heated this <s>Sāmaveda</s>. From it, thus heated, was born fame, splendor, sense-power, vigor, and food-essence — the essence.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.3.2)

children.text:
tad vyakṣarat |
tad ādityam abhito 'śrayat |
tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya kṛṣṇaṃ rūpam || ChUp_3,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That flowed forth. It took shelter in the sun, on its side. That indeed is this — what is this dark (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>) form of the sun.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.3.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3.3.1-3 atha ye 'sya pratyaśco raśmaya ityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.3.1-3:] 'Now, the rays that go to its west' — and so forth; the same [explanation applies].

children.text: tathā sāmnāṃ madhu /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the honey of the <s>Sāman</s> chants.

children.text: etadādityasya kṛṣṇaṃ rūpam //1-3 //
children.translated_text: This is the dark form of the sun. (1-3)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
atha ye 'syodañco raśmayas tā evāsyodīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ |
atharvāṅgirasa eva madhukṛtaḥ |
itihāsapurāṇaṃ puṣpam |
tā amṛtā āpaḥ || ChUp_3,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the rays that go to its north — those are its northern honey-channels. The <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> [mantras] alone are the honey-makers. The <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s> is the flower. Those immortal waters [are the essence].' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.4.1)

children.text:
te vā ete 'tharvāṅgirasa etad itihāsapūrāṇam abhyatapan |
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyāṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata || ChUp_3,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Those <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> [mantras] heated this <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s>. From it, thus heated, was born fame, splendor, sense-power, vigor, and food-essence — the essence.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.4.2)

children.text:
tad vyakṣarat |
tad ādityam abhito 'śrayat |
tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ rūpam || ChUp_3,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That flowed forth. It took shelter in the sun, on its side. That indeed is this — what is this exceedingly dark (<s>paraḥkṛṣṇa</s>) form of the sun.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.4.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,4.1-3 atha ye 'syodañco raśmaya ityādi samānam /
atharvāṅgiraso 'tharvaṇāṅgirasā ca dṛṣṭā mantrā atharvāṅgirasaḥ karmaṇi prayuktā madhukṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> [mantras] — the mantras seen by <s>Atharvan</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> — are the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>; employed in ritual action, they are the honey-makers.

children.text: itihāsapurāṇaṃ puṣpam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s> is the flower.

children.text: tayoścetihāsapurāṇayoraśvamedhe pāriplavāsu rātriṣu karmāṅgatvena viniyogaḥ siddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And of those — the <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> — their employment as accessories of the ritual is established in the <s>pāriplava</s> nights of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice).

children.text: madhvetadādityasya paraḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rūpamatiśayena kṛṣṇamityarthaḥ //1-3 //
children.translated_text: This honey is the exceedingly dark form of the sun — meaning supremely dark. (1-3)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.4.1-3:] 'Now, the rays that go to its north' — and so forth; the same [explanation applies].

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,5.1-3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.5.1-3]

children.text:
atha ye 'syordhvā raśmayas tā evāsyordhvā madhunāḍyaḥ |
guhyā evādeśā madhukṛtaḥ |
brahmaiva puṣpaṃ |
tā amṛtā āpaḥ || ChUp_3,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the rays that go upward — those are its upward honey-channels. The secret instructions (<s>guhyā ādeśāḥ</s>) alone are the honey-makers. <s>Brahman</s> alone is the flower. Those immortal waters [are the essence].' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.5.1)

children.text:
te vā ete guhyā ādeśā etad brahmābhyatapan |
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata || ChUp_3,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Those secret instructions heated this <s>Brahman</s>. From it, thus heated, was born fame, splendor, sense-power, vigor, and food-essence — the essence.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.5.2)

children.text:
tad vyakṣarat |
tad ādityam abhito 'śrayat |
tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya madhye kṣobhata iva || ChUp_3,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That flowed forth. It took shelter in the sun, on its side. That indeed is this — what seems to pulsate in the center of the sun.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.5.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,5.1,2,3 atha ye 'syordhvā raśmaya ityādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.5.1-3:] 'Now, the rays that go upward' — and so forth, as before.

children.text: guhyā gopyā rahasyā evā'deśā lokadvārīyādividhaya upāsanāni ca karmāṅgaviṣayāṇi madhukṛto brahmaiva śabdādhikārātprāṇavākhyaṃ puṣpam /
children.translated_text: The secret — [meaning] to be concealed, esoteric — instructions (<s>ādeśāḥ</s>) are the injunctions such as the 'door of the worlds' (<s>lokadvārīya</s>) and the like, as well as the meditations (<s>upāsanās</s>) that are accessories of ritual action; [they are] the honey-makers. <s>Brahman</s> alone — because of the context of the word [<s>Brahman</s>], [here meaning] that which is called <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Om</s>) — is the flower.

children.text: samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: The rest is the same.

children.text: madhvetadādityasya madhye kṣobhata iva samāhitadṛṣṭerdṛśyate sañcalatīva //1-3 //
children.translated_text: This honey is what seems to pulsate in the center of the sun — it is seen by one whose vision is concentrated, appearing to move about. (1-3)

children.text: START ChUp 3,5.4
children.translated_text: [<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.5.4]

children.text:
te vā ete rasānāṃ rasāḥ |
vedā hi rasāḥ |
teṣām ete rasāḥ |
tāni vā etāny amṛtānām amṛtāni |
vedā hy amṛtāḥ |
teṣām etāny amṛtāni || ChUp_3,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'These are indeed the essences of essences. For the <s>Vedas</s> are essences, and these are their essences. These are indeed the immortal of the immortal. For the <s>Vedas</s> are immortal, and these are their immortal [portions].' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.5.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,5.4 te vā ete yathoktā rohitādirūpaviśeṣā rasānāṃ rasāḥ /
keṣāṃ rasānāmityāha-vedā hi yasmāllokaniṣyandatvātsārā iti rasāsteṣāṃ rasānāṃ karmabhāvamāpannānāmapyete rohitādiviśeṣā rasā ityantasārabhūtā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of which essences? He says: for the <s>Vedas</s>, because of being the outpouring of the world, are the quintessence — hence they are called essences. Of those essences — even when they have assumed the form of ritual action — these specific forms such as the reddish and the like are the essences — meaning the innermost quintessence.

children.text: tathāmṛtānāmamṛtāni vedā hyamṛtā nityatvāteṣāmetāni rohitādīni rūpāṇyamṛtāni /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the immortal of the immortal — for the <s>Vedas</s> are immortal because of their eternality; these forms such as the reddish and the like are the immortal [portions] of those.

children.text: rasānāṃ rasā ityādi karmastutireṣā /
children.translated_text: 'Essences of essences' — and so forth — this is a eulogy of the ritual action.

children.text: yasyaivaṃviśiṣṭānyamṛtāni phalamiti //4//
children.translated_text: The fruit of one who has such distinguished immortal [portions] is as described. (4)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.5.4:] These, as described — the specific forms such as the reddish and the like — are the essences of essences.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,6.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.6.1]

children.text:
tad yat prathamam amṛtaṃ tad vasava upajīvanty agninā mukhena |
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti |
etad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyanti || ChUp_3,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Vasus</s> subsist on that first immortal [portion], with <s>Agni</s> as their mouth. The gods indeed do not eat, nor do they drink. They are satisfied merely by seeing this immortal [portion].' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.6.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,6.1 rūpasyeti /
na /
yaśa ādīnāṃ śrotrādigamyatvāt /
śrotragrāhyaṃ yaśaḥ /
tejorūpaṃ cākṣuṣam /
indriyaṃ viṣayagrahaṇakāryānumeyaṃ karaṇasāmarthyam /
vīryaṃ balaṃ dehagata utsāhaḥ prāṇavattā /
annādyaṃ pratyahamupajīvyamānaṃ śarīrasthitikaraṃ yadbhavati raso hyevamātmakaḥ sarvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Food-essence — that which is consumed day after day and maintains the stability of the body — for all essence is indeed of this nature.

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyanti sarve devāḥ /
children.translated_text: That which, by seeing, satisfies all the gods.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tṛpyantītyetatsarvaṃ svakaraṇairanubhūya tṛpyantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By seeing, they are satisfied' — meaning that by experiencing [everything] through their own sense faculties, they are satisfied.

children.text: ādityasaṃśrayāḥ santo vaigandhyādidehakaraṇadoṣarahitāśca //1 //
children.translated_text: Residing in the sun, they are free from defects of the body and senses such as unpleasant smell and the like. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.6.1:] [One might think it is] of [mere] form. No. Because fame and the like are apprehended by hearing and other [senses]. Fame is apprehensible by hearing. Splendor is visual, apprehensible by the eye. Sense-power is the capability of the sense organs, to be inferred from the effect of grasping objects. Vigor is strength — the bodily enthusiasm, the state of being full of <s>prāṇa</s> (life force).

children.text: START ChUp 3,6.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.6.2]

children.text:
ta etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśanti |
etasmād rūpād udyanti || ChUp_3,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'They enter into this very form. From this form they rise forth.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.6.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,6.2 kiṃ te nirudyamā amṛtamupajīvanti /
na /
kathaṃ tarhi, etadeva rūpamabhilakṣyādhunā bhogāvasaro nāsmākamiti buddhvābhisaṃviśantyudāsate /
children.translated_text: How then? Focusing on this very form, and thinking, 'This is not the time for our enjoyment now,' they enter into it — they remain quiescent.

children.text: yadā vai tasyāmṛtasya bhogāvasaro bhavettadaitasmādamṛtādamṛtabhoganimittamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the occasion for the enjoyment of that immortal [portion] arrives, then from that immortal [portion] — meaning for the purpose of the enjoyment of the immortal — this is the meaning.

children.text: etasmādrūpādudyantyutsāhavanto bhavantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: From this form they rise forth — they become full of enthusiasm, is the meaning.

children.text: na hyanutsāhavatāmananapatiṣṭhatāmalasānāṃ bhogaprāptirloke dṛṣṭā //2 //
children.translated_text: For the attainment of enjoyment is not seen in the world for those who lack enthusiasm, who do not eat, who are lazy. (2)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.6.2:] Do they subsist on the immortal [portion] without effort? No.

children.text: START ChUp 3,6.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.6.3]

children.text:
sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda vasūnām evaiko bhūtvāgninaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati |
sa etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśati |
etasmād rūpād udeti || ChUp_3,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows this immortal thus — becoming one of the <s>Vasus</s>, with <s>Agni</s> as his mouth — is satisfied by seeing this very immortal [portion]. He enters into this very form. From this form he rises forth.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.6.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,6.3 sa yaḥ kaścidetadevaṃ yathoditamṛṅmadhukaratāparasasaṃrakṣaṇamṛgvedavihitakarmapuṣpāttasya cā'dityasaṃśrayaṇaṃ rohita rūpatvaṃ cāmṛtasya prācīdiggataraśmināḍīsaṃsthatāṃ vasudevabhogyatāṃ tadvidaśca vasubhiḥ sahaikatāṃ gatvāgninā mukenopajīvanaṃ darśanamātreṇa tṛptiṃ svabhogāvasara udyamanaṃ tatkālāpāye ca saṃveśanaṃ veda so 'pi vasuvatsarvaṃ tathaivānubhavati //3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.6.3:] He who, whoever [he may be], knows this immortal as described — the honey-making and heating by the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, the essence-protection, [produced] from the flower-counterpart that is the ritual action enjoined by the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, its taking shelter in the sun, its nature as the reddish form, its being stationed in the honey-channels of the rays going east, its being the enjoyment of the <s>Vasu</s> deities, and the one who knows this becoming one with the <s>Vasus</s> — having attained oneness with the <s>Vasus</s>, subsisting through <s>Agni</s> as the mouth, being satisfied merely by seeing, rising forth at the time of one's own occasion for enjoyment, and entering in at the passing of that time — he too, like a <s>Vasu</s>, experiences everything in the same way. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 3,6.4
children.translated_text: [<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.6.4]

children.text: sa yāvad ādityaḥ purastād udetā paścād astam etā vasūnām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā || ChUp_3,6.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'As long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west — so long does he encompass the lordship and sovereignty of the <s>Vasus</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 3.6.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,6.4 kiyantaṃ kālaṃ vidvāṃstadamṛtamupajīvatītyucyate - sa vidvānyāvadādityaḥ purastātprācyāṃ diśyudetā paścātpratīcyāmastametā tāvadvasūnāṃ bhogakālastāvantameva kālaṃ vasūnāmādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryatā parito gantā bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.6.4:] For how long does the knower subsist on that immortal [portion]? It is stated: this knower — as long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west — [for] so long is the time of enjoyment of the <s>Vasus</s>; for that same duration, he encompasses — meaning goes around entirely — the lordship and sovereignty of the <s>Vasus</s>, is the meaning.

children.text: na yathā candramaṇḍalasthaḥ kevalakarmī paratantro devānāmannabhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not like one stationed in the lunar sphere — a mere performer of rituals — who is dependent [on others] and has become food for the gods.

children.text: kiṃ tarhyayamādhipatyaṃ svarāḍbhāvaṃ cādhigacchati //4//
children.translated_text: What then? He attains sovereignty and the state of being self-ruling. //4//

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,7.1-3
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,7.1-3

children.text:
atha yad dvitīyam amṛtaṃ tad rudrā upajīvantīndreṇa mukhena |
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti |
etad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyanti || ChUp_3,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, the second <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality) — the <s>Rudras</s> live upon it, with <s>Indra</s> as their mouth. Verily, the gods neither eat nor drink; they are satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s>.

children.text:
ta etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśanti |
etasmād rūpād udyanti || ChUp_3,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: They enter into this very form, and they rise from this form.

children.text:
sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda rudrāṇām evaiko bhūtvendreṇaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati |
sa etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśati |
etasmād rūpād udeti || ChUp_3,7.3 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, becoming one among the <s>Rudras</s>, is satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s> with <s>Indra</s> as his mouth. He enters into this very form, and he rises from this form.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,7.1-3 athā yaddvitīyamamṛtaṃ tadrudrā upajīvantītyādi samānam //1-2-3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: "Now, the second <s>amṛta</s> — the <s>Rudras</s> live upon it" — and so on; the explanation is the same as before. //1-2-3//

children.text: START ChUp 3,7.4
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,7.4

children.text: sa yāvad ādityaḥ purastād udetā paścād astam etā dvis tāvad dakṣiṇata udetottarato 'stam etā rudrāṇām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā || ChUp_3,7.4 ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, twice that long it rises in the south and sets in the north — for that long extends the sovereignty and self-rule of the <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,7.4 sa yāvadādityaḥ purastādudetā paścādastametā dvistāvattato dviguṇaṃ kālaṃ dakṣiṇata udetottarato 'stametā rudrāṇāṃ tāvadbhogakālaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: "For as long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, twice that duration" — meaning double that time — "it rises in the south and sets in the north" — that long is the period of enjoyment of the <s>Rudras</s>. //4//

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,8.1-4
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,8.1-4

children.text:
atha yat tṛtīyam amṛtaṃ tad ādityā upajīvanti varuṇena mukhena |
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti |
etad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyanti || ChUp_3,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, the third <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality) — the <s>Ādityas</s> live upon it, with <s>Varuṇa</s> as their mouth. Verily, the gods neither eat nor drink; they are satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s>.

children.text:
ta etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśanti |
etasmād rūpād udyanti || ChUp_3,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: They enter into this very form, and they rise from this form.

children.text:
sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ vedādityānām evaiko bhūtvā varuṇenaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati |
sa etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśati |
etasmād rūpād udeti || ChUp_3,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, becoming one among the <s>Ādityas</s>, is satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s> with <s>Varuṇa</s> as his mouth. He enters into this very form, and he rises from this form.

children.text: sa yāvad ādityo dakṣiṇata udetottarato 'stam etā dvis tāvat paścād udetā purastād astam etādityānām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā || ChUp_3,8.4 ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the sun rises in the south and sets in the north, twice that long it rises in the west and sets in the east — for that long extends the sovereignty and self-rule of the <s>Ādityas</s>.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,9.1-4
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,9.1-4

children.text:
atha yac caturtham amṛtaṃ tan maruta upajīvanti somena mukhena |
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti |
etad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyanti || ChUp_3,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, the fourth <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality) — the <s>Maruts</s> live upon it, with <s>Soma</s> as their mouth. Verily, the gods neither eat nor drink; they are satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s>.

children.text:
ta etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśanti |
etasmād rūpād udyanti || ChUp_3,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: They enter into this very form, and they rise from this form.

children.text:
sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda marutām evaiko bhūtvā somenaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati |
sa etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśati |
etasmād rūpād udeti || ChUp_3,9.3 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, becoming one among the <s>Maruts</s>, is satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s> with <s>Soma</s> as his mouth. He enters into this very form, and he rises from this form.

children.text: sa yāvad ādityaḥ paścād udetā purastād astam etā dvis tāvad uttarata udetā dakṣiṇato 'stam etā marutām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā || ChUp_3,9.4 ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the sun rises in the west and sets in the east, twice that long it rises in the north and sets in the south — for that long extends the sovereignty and self-rule of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,10.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,10.1

children.text:
atha yat pañcamam amṛtaṃ tat sādhyā upajīvanti brahmaṇā mukhena |
na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti |
etad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyanti || ChUp_3,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, the fifth <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality) — the <s>Sādhyas</s> live upon it, with <s>Brahmā</s> as their mouth. Verily, the gods neither eat nor drink; they are satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s>.

children.text:
ta etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśanti |
etasmād rūpād udyanti || ChUp_3,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: They enter into this very form, and they rise from this form.

children.text:
sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda sādhyānām evaiko bhūtvā brahmaṇaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati |
sa etad eva rūpam abhisaṃviśati |
etasmād rūpād udeti || ChUp_3,10.3 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, becoming one among the <s>Sādhyas</s>, is satisfied merely by beholding this <s>amṛta</s> with <s>Brahmā</s> as his mouth. He enters into this very form, and he rises from this form.

children.text: sa yāvad āditya uttarata udetā dakṣiṇato 'stam etā dvis tāvad ūrdhvam udetārvāg astam etā sādhyānām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā || ChUp_3,10.4 ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the sun rises in the north and sets in the south, twice that long it rises upward and sets downward — for that long extends the sovereignty and self-rule of the <s>Sādhyas</s>.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3.8.1-4, 9.1-4, 10.1-4 tathā paścāduttarata ūrdhvamudetā viparyayeṇāstametā /
pūrvasmātpūrvasmāddviguṇottarottareṇa kālenetyapaurāṇaṃ darśanam /
savituścaturdiśamindrayamavaruṇasomapurīṣūdayāstamayakālasya tulyatvaṃ hi paurāṇikairuktam /
mānasottarasya mūrdhani meroḥ pradakṣiṇāvṛttestulyatvāditi /
atroktaḥ parihāra ācāryaiḥ /
amarāvatyādīnāṃ purīṇāṃ dviguṇottarottareṇa kālenodvāsaḥ syāt /
udayaśca nāma savitustannivāsināṃ prāṇināṃ cakṣugocarāpattistadatyayaṣcastamanaṃ na paramārthata udayāstamane staḥ /
tannivāsināṃ ca prāṇināmabhāve tānprati tenaiva mārgeṇa gacchannapi naivodetā nāstameteti cakṣurgocarāpattestadatyayasya cābhāvāt /
tathāmarāvatyāḥ sakāśāddviguṇaṃ kālaṃ saṃyamanī purī vasatyatastannivāsinaḥ prāṇinaḥ prati dakṣiṇata ivodetyuttarato 'stametītyucyate 'smadbuddhiṃ cāpekṣya /
tathottarāsvapi purīṣu yojanā /
sarveṣāṃ ca meruruttarato bhavati /
yadāmarāvatyāṃ madhyāhnagataḥ savitā tadā saṃyamanyāmudyandṛśyate tatra madhyāhnagato vāruṇyāmudyandṛśyate, tathottarasyāṃ, pradakṣiṇāvṛttestulyatvāt /
ilāvṛtavāsināṃ sarvataḥ parvataprākāranivāritādityaraśmīnāṃ savitordhva ivodetāvagistametā dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: For the inhabitants of <s>Ilāvṛta</s>, whose sunlight is blocked by the surrounding mountain walls on all sides, the sun appears to rise upward and set downward,

children.text: parvatordhvacchidrapraveśātsavitṛprakāśasya /
children.translated_text: because the sunlight of the sun enters through openings above the mountains.

children.text: tathargādyamṛtopajīvināmamṛtānāṃ ca dviguṇottarottaravīryavattvamanumīyate bhogakāladvaiguṇyaliṅgena /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the successive doubling of potency among the <s>amṛtas</s> enjoyed by the <s>Ṛg</s>-group and others is inferred from the indicator of the doubling of the period of enjoyment.

children.text: udyamanasaṃveśanādi devānāṃ rudrādīnāṃ viduṣaśca samānam //1-4 //
children.translated_text: The rising, entering into form, and so on of the gods — the <s>Rudras</s> and others — and of the knower are the same as explained before. //1-4//

[<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: Likewise, it rises in the west, north, and upward, and sets in the opposite directions. The time-period doubles successively from the preceding one — this is the non-Purāṇic view. The Purāṇic authorities state that the sun's rising and setting times in the four directions — at the cities of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Soma</s> — are equal, because of the uniformity of its clockwise circuit on the summit of <s>Meru</s>, atop <s>Mānasottara</s> mountain. Here the <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) have given the following reconciliation: the successive doubling of time refers to the periods of residence at the cities <s>Amarāvatī</s> and the rest. Rising of the sun means its coming within the range of vision of the beings dwelling there, and its passing beyond that range is setting — there is no rising and setting in the ultimate sense. And in the absence of beings dwelling there, even though the sun travels along the very same path, it neither rises nor sets, because there is no coming into or passing beyond the range of vision. Thus, the city of <s>Saṃyamanī</s> is situated at twice the distance from <s>Amarāvatī</s>, and therefore for the beings dwelling there, the sun is said to rise as if from the south and set in the north — this is stated with reference to our understanding. The same explanation applies to the cities further north. <s>Meru</s> is to the north of all of them. When the sun is at midday over <s>Amarāvatī</s>, it is seen rising at <s>Saṃyamanī</s>; when at midday there, it is seen rising at <s>Vāruṇī</s>; and likewise for the northern city — because of the uniformity of the clockwise circuit.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasyāṣṭamanavamadaśamakhaṇḍāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus end the eighth, ninth, and tenth <s>khaṇḍas</s> (sections) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,11.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,11.1

children.text:
atha tata ūrdhva udetya naivodetā nāstam etaikala eva madhye sthātā |
tad eṣa ślokaḥ || ChUp_3,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, having risen above from there, it neither rises nor sets; it stands alone in the middle. On this there is this verse:

children.text: ChUpBh_3,11.1 kṛtvaivamudayāstamanena prāṇināṃ svakarmaphalabhoganimittamanugrahaṃ tatkarmaphalopabhogakṣaye tāni prāṇijātānyātmani saṃhṛtyātha tatastasmādanantaraṃ prāṇyanugrahakālādūrdhvaḥ sannātmanyudetyodgamya yānpratyudeti teṣāṃ prāṇināmabhāvātsvātmastho naivodetā nāstametaikalo 'dvitīyo 'navayavo madhye svātmanyeva sthātā /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: Having thus bestowed grace upon beings through rising and setting for the purpose of their experiencing the fruits of their actions, when the fruits of those actions are exhausted, having withdrawn those classes of beings into itself — then, after that, subsequent to the time of bestowing grace upon beings, being above, it rises into itself. Having risen, since there are no beings for whom it rises, remaining in its own self, it neither rises nor sets; alone, without a second, without parts, it stands in the middle, in its own self alone.

children.text: tatra kaścidvidvānvasvādisamānacaraṇo rohitādyamṛtabhogabhāgī yathoktakrameṇa svātmānaṃ savitāramātmatvenopetya samāhitaḥ sannetaṃ mantraṃ dṛṣṭvotthito 'nyasmai pṛṣṭavate jagāda /
children.translated_text: There, a certain knower belonging to the same lineage as <s>Vasu</s> and others, sharing in the enjoyment of the <s>amṛta</s> beginning with <s>rohita</s> (the red), having approached the sun as his own self in the manner described, being absorbed in meditation, having perceived this <s>mantra</s>, rose and declared it to another who had asked.

children.text: yatastvamāgato brahmalokātkiṃ tatrāpyahorātrābhyāṃ parivartamānaḥ savitā prāṇināmāyuḥ kṣapayati yathehāsmākamityevaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ pratyāha /
children.translated_text: "From the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of <s>Brahman</s>) whence you have come — does the sun there too, revolving with days and nights, diminish the lifespan of beings as it does for us here?" — being asked thus, he replied.

children.text: tattatra yathā pṛṣṭe yathokte cārtha eṣa śloko bhavati tanokto yogineti śrutervacanamidam //1 //
children.translated_text: The answer to what was asked, and the meaning as stated — this verse expresses it. The statement is that of the <s>yogī</s>, as indicated by the <s>śruti</s> (scripture). //1//

children.text: START ChUp 3,11.2
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,11.2

children.text:
na vai tatra na nimloca |
nodiyāya kadācana |
devās tenāhaṃ satyena |
mā virādhiṣi brahmaṇeti || ChUp_3,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: Verily, there it has never set, nor has it ever risen. O gods, by this truth, may I never be separated from <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,11.2 na vai tatra yato 'haṃ brahmalokādāgatastasminna vai tatraitadasti yatpṛcchasi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: "Verily, there" — in that <s>Brahmaloka</s> from which I have come — "there, what you ask does not exist."

children.text: na hi tatra nimloco 'stamagamatsavitā na codiyāyodgataḥ kutaścitkadācana kasmiṃścidapi kāla iti /
children.translated_text: "For there the sun has never set, nor has it risen from anywhere at any time" — this is the meaning.

children.text: udayāstamayavarjito brahmaloka ityanupapannamityuktaḥ śuthamiva pratipede /
children.translated_text: Being told that <s>Brahmaloka</s> is devoid of rising and setting — which seems impossible — he accepted it like one who has bathed (i.e., with faith, as one purified).

children.text: he devāḥ sākṣiṇo yūyaṃ śṛṇuta yathā mayoktaṃ satyaṃ vacastena steyanāhaṃ brahmaṇā brahmasvarūpeṇa mā virādhiṣi mā virudhyeyamaprāptirbrahmaṇā mama mā bhūdityarthaḥ //2 //
