children.translated_text: "O gods, you are witnesses — hear! As what I have spoken is true, by that truth, may I not be separated from <s>Brahman</s>, from the nature of <s>Brahman</s>. May the non-attainment of <s>Brahman</s> never be mine" — this is the meaning. //2//

children.text: START ChUp 3,11.3
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,11.3

children.text:
na ha vā asmā udeti na nimlocati |
sakṛd divā haivāsmai bhavati |
ya etām evaṃ brahmopaniṣadaṃ veda || ChUp_3,11.3 ||
children.translated_text: Verily, for him the sun neither rises nor sets. For him it is perpetual day. He who knows this secret teaching of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahmopaniṣad</s>) thus —

children.text: ChUpBh_3,11.3 satyaṃ tenoktamityāha śrutiḥ-na ha vā asmai yathoktabrahmavide nodeti na nimlocati nāstameti kiṃ tu brahmavide 'smai sakṛddivā haiva sadaivāharbhavati svayañjyotiṣṭvādya etāṃ yathoktāṃ brahmopaniṣadaṃ vedaguhyaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: That what he said is true, the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) declares — "Verily, for him" — for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> as described — "the sun neither rises nor sets." Rather, for this knower of <s>Brahman</s>, "it is perpetual day forever," because he is self-luminous. He who knows this secret teaching of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahmopaniṣad</s>) as described.

children.text: evaṃ tantreṇa vaṃśāditrayaṃ pratyamṛtasambandhaṃ ca yaccānyadavocāmaivaṃ jānātītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, through this systematic exposition, one should understand the connection of the three lineages and others with the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), and whatever else has been stated — this is the meaning.

children.text: vidvānudayāstamayakālāparicchedyaṃ nityamajaṃ brahma bhavatītyarthaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: The knower becomes <s>Brahman</s>, which is eternal, unborn, and not delimited by the times of rising and setting — this is the meaning. //3//

children.text: START ChUp 3,11.4
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,11.4

children.text:
tad dhaitad brahmā prajāpataya uvāca |
prajāpatir manave |
manuḥ prajābhyaḥ |
tad dhaitad uddālakāyāruṇaye jyeṣṭhāya putrāya pitā brahma provāca || ChUp_3,11.4 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> taught this to <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> to <s>Manu</s>; <s>Manu</s> to his descendants. And the father taught this <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) to <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>, his eldest son.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,11.4 taddhaitanmadhujñānaṃ brahmā hiraṇyagarbho virāje prajāpataya uvāca /
so 'pi manave /
manurikṣvākvādyābhyaḥ prajābhyaḥ provāceti vidyāṃ stauti brahmādiviśiṣṭakramāgateti /
kiṃ ca taddhaitanmadhujñānamuddālakāyā'ruṇaye pitā
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: This knowledge of the honey doctrine (<s>madhu-vidyā</s>) — <s>Brahmā</s>, that is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, taught to <s>Virāj</s>, who is <s>Prajāpati</s>. He in turn taught it to <s>Manu</s>. <s>Manu</s> taught it to his descendants such as <s>Ikṣvāku</s> and others — thus the <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is glorified as having come down through an illustrious lineage beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>. Furthermore, the father taught this knowledge of the honey doctrine to <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,11.5
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,11.5

children.text: idaṃ vāva taj jyeṣṭhāya putrāya pitā brahma prabrūyāt praṇāyyāya vāntevāsine || ChUp_3,11.5 ||
children.translated_text: A father should indeed teach this <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) to his eldest son, or to a worthy disciple (<s>antevāsin</s>).

children.text: ChUpBh_3,11.5 idaṃ vāva tadyathoktamanyo 'pi jyeṣṭhāya putrāya sarvapriyārhāya brahma prabrūyāt /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: "This indeed" — as described — another also should teach this <s>Brahman</s> to his eldest son, who is worthy of all that is dear,

children.text: praṇāyyāya vā yogyāyāyantevāsine śiṣyāya //5 //
children.translated_text: or to a worthy, that is, a qualified, disciple (<s>antevāsin</s>). //5//

children.text: START ChUp 3,11.6
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,11.6

children.text:
nānyasmai kasmaicana |
yady apy asmā imām adbhiḥ parigṛhītāṃ dhanasya pūrṇāṃ dadyād etad eva tato bhūya iti || ChUp_3,11.6 ||
children.translated_text: To no one else whatsoever. Even if someone were to give him this entire earth surrounded by waters and filled with wealth — this (knowledge) is greater than that.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,11.6 nānyasmai kasmaicana prabrūyāttīrthadvayamanujñātamanekeṣāṃ prāptānāṃ tīrthānāmācāryādīnām /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya</s>]: "To no one else whatsoever" should it be taught — two channels of transmission are sanctioned out of the many possible channels such as the teacher and others.

children.text: kasmātpunastīrthasaṅkocanaṃ vidyāyā niṣkrayārthamācāryāya dhanasya pūrṇāṃ sampannāṃ bhogopararaṇairnāsāvasya niṣkrayo yasmāttato 'pi dānādetadeva yanmadhuvidyādānaṃ bhūyo bahutaraphalamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Why this restriction of the channels of transmission? For the purpose of compensating the teacher, even if one were to give the earth full and furnished with all objects of enjoyment — that would not be its adequate price, because the giving of this <s>madhu-vidyā</s> (honey doctrine) yields far greater fruit than even that — this is the meaning.

children.text: dvirabhyāsa ādarārthaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: The repetition is for the sake of emphasis. //6//

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the third <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.1
children.translated_text: START ChUp 3,12.1

children.text:
gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yad idam kiñca |
vāg vai gāyatrī |
vāg vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ gāyati ca trāyate ca || ChUp_3,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gāyatrī</s> is verily all this — whatever exists here. Speech indeed is <s>Gāyatrī</s>, for speech sings of (<s>gāyati</s>) and protects (<s>trāyate</s>) all this that exists.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,12.1 yata evamatiśayaphalaiṣā brahmavidyātaḥ sā prakārāntareṇāpi vaktavyeti gāyatrī vā ityādyārabhyate /
gāyatrīdvāreṇa cocyate /
brahmaṇaḥ sarvaviśeṣarahitasya neti netītyādiśiṣapratiṣedhagamyasya durbodhatvāt /
satsvanekeṣu cchandaḥsu gāyatryā eva brahmajñānadvāratayopādānaṃ prādhānyāt /
somāharaṇāt itaracchandokṣarāharaṇenetaracchandovyāptyā ca sarvasavanavyāpakatvācca yajñe prādhānyaṃ gāyatryāḥ /
gāyatrīsāratvācca brāhmaṇasya mātaramiva hitvā gurutarāṃ gāyatrīṃ tato 'nyadgurutaraṃ na pratipadyate yathoktaṃ brahmāpīti /
tasyāmatyantagauravasya prasiddhatvāt /
ato gāyatrīmukhenaiva brahmocyate /
gāyatrī vā ityavadhāraṇārtho vaiśabdaḥ /
idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ prāmijātaṃ yatkiñca sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ vā tatsarvaṃ gāyatryeva /
children.translated_text: 'All this that has come into being, whatever is stationary or moving — all that is indeed <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone.'

children.text: tasyāśchandomātrāyāḥ sarvabhūtatvamanupapannamiti gāyatrīkāraṇaṃ vācaṃ śabdayatyasau gaurasāvaśva iti ca trāyate ca rakṣatyamuṣmānmā bhaiṣīḥ kiṃ te bhayamutthitamityādinā sarvato bhayānnivartyamāno vācā trātaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Since the identity of all beings with [<s>Gāyatrī</s>] as a mere metre is untenable, [the identity is established through] speech, which is the cause of <s>Gāyatrī</s> — speech that gives voice (<s>gāyati</s>): 'That is a cow, that is a horse' — and protects (<s>trāyate</s>), delivering one from all fears through [words such as] 'Do not fear, what cause of fear has arisen for you?' — thus one is protected by speech.

children.text: yadvāgbhūtaṃ gāyati ca trāyate ca gāyatryeva tadgāyati ca trāyate ca vāco 'nanyatvādgāyatryāḥ /
children.translated_text: That which speech has become — it sings (<s>gāyati</s>) and protects (<s>trāyate</s>) — is indeed <s>Gāyatrī</s>; it sings and protects because <s>Gāyatrī</s> is non-different from speech.

children.text: gānāttrāṇācca gāyatryā gāyatrītvam //1 //
children.translated_text: Because of singing (<s>gāna</s>) and protecting (<s>trāṇa</s>), <s>Gāyatrī</s> has its nature as <s>Gāyatrī</s>. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.1:] Since this knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> yields such supreme fruit, it should be stated in yet another way — hence the section beginning with '<s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed' is commenced. And it is taught through the medium of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, because <s>Brahman</s>, which is devoid of all distinctions and is to be apprehended only through the negation of all teachings such as 'not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>), is difficult to comprehend. Among the many metres that exist, <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone is chosen as the gateway to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> because of its pre-eminence. Because of the extraction of <s>Soma</s>, the absorption of syllables from other metres, the pervading of other metres, and its presence in all <s>savana</s>s (pressings), <s>Gāyatrī</s> has pre-eminence in the sacrifice. And because the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has <s>Gāyatrī</s> as its essence — like abandoning one's own mother who is most venerable — having abandoned the weightier <s>Gāyatrī</s>, one does not resort to anything weightier than that, as stated in 'even <s>Brahman</s>.' Because of the well-known supreme venerability of that [<s>Gāyatrī</s>], <s>Brahman</s> is spoken of through the medium of <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone. In '<s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed' (<s>gāyatrī vā</s>), the word <s>vai</s> has the sense of emphasis.

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.2]

children.text:
yā vai sā gāyatrīyaṃ vāva sā yeyaṃ pṛthivī |
asyāṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ pratiṣṭhitam |
etām eva nātiśīyate || ChUp_3,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is <s>Gāyatrī</s> — it is indeed this earth. For upon this [earth] all beings are established. They do not go beyond this [earth].' (ChUp 3.12.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,12.2 yā vai saivaṃlakṣaṇā sarvabhūtarūpā gāyatrī, iyaṃ vāva sā yeyaṃ pṛthivī /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.2:] That which is <s>Gāyatrī</s> characterized thus, having the form of all beings — it is indeed this earth.

children.text: kathaṃ punariyaṃ pṛthivī gāyatrīti, ucyatesarvabhūtasambandhāt /
children.translated_text: How can this earth be <s>Gāyatrī</s>? It is explained — because of [its] connection with all beings.

children.text: kathaṃ sarvabhūtasambandhaḥ, asyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ hi yasmātsarvaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca bhūtaṃ pratiṣṭhitametāmeva pṛthivīṃ nātiśīyate nātivartata ityetat /
children.translated_text: How is there a connection with all beings? Because upon this earth, all beings — both stationary and moving — are established; they do not go beyond, do not surpass, this earth — that is the meaning.

children.text: yathā gānatrāṇābhyāṃ bhūtasambandho gāyatryā evaṃ bhūtapratiṣṭhānādubhūtasambaddhā pṛthivyato gāyatrī pṛthivī //2 //
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Gāyatrī</s> is connected with beings through singing and protecting, so too the earth is connected with beings through being the support of beings — therefore the earth is <s>Gāyatrī</s>. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.3]

children.text:
yā vai sā pṛthivīyaṃ vāva sā yad idam asmin puruṣe śarīram |
asmin hīme prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ |
etad eva nātiśīyante || ChUp_3,12.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this earth — it is indeed this body in this person. For in this [body] these <s>prāṇa</s>s are established. They do not go beyond this [body].' (ChUp 3.12.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,12.3 yā vai sā pṛthivī gāyatrīyaṃ vāva sedameva /
tatkiṃ, yadidamasminpuruṣe kāryakāraṇasaṅghāte jīvati śarīraṃ pārthivatvāccharīrasya /
kathaṃ śarīrasya gāyatrītvamiti /
children.translated_text: How does the body have the nature of <s>Gāyatrī</s>?

children.text: ucyate-asminhīme prāṇā bhūtaśabdavācyāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: It is explained — in this [body] indeed, these <s>prāṇa</s>s, which are denoted by the word 'beings' (<s>bhūta</s>), are established.

children.text: ataḥ pṛthivīvadbhūtaśabdavācyaprāṇapratiṣṭhānāccharīraṃ gāyatrī /
children.translated_text: Therefore, like the earth, the body is <s>Gāyatrī</s> because the <s>prāṇa</s>s denoted by the word 'beings' are established in it.

children.text: etadeva yasmāccharīraṃ nātiśīyante prāṇāḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: The <s>prāṇa</s>s do not go beyond this body. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.3:] That which is this earth, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — it is indeed this very [body]. What is that? It is the body (<s>śarīra</s>) in this person (<s>puruṣa</s>), the aggregate of cause and effect that is alive — because the body is made of earth.

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.4]

children.text:
yad vai tat puruṣe śarīram idaṃ vāva tad yad idam asminn antaḥ puruṣe hṛdayam |
asmin hīme prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ |
etad eva nātiśīyante || ChUp_3,12.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this body in a person — it is indeed this heart within the person. For in this [heart] these <s>prāṇa</s>s are established. They do not go beyond this [heart].' (ChUp 3.12.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,12.4 yadva tatpuruṣe śarīraṃ gāyatrīdaṃ vāva tat /
yadidamasminnantarmadhye puruṣe hṛdayaṃ puṇḍarīkākhyametadgāyatrī /
kathamityāha-asminhīme prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitā ataḥ śarīravadgāyatrī hṛdayam /
etadeva ca nātiśīyante prāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the <s>prāṇa</s>s do not go beyond this [heart].

children.text: "prāṇo ha pitā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the father;

children.text: prāṇo mātā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is the mother' —

children.text: "iti,"ahiṃsansarvabhūtāni"iti ca śruterbhūtaśabdavācyāḥ prāṇāḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: thus from the <s>śruti</s>, and 'not harming any being' — from this <s>śruti</s>, the <s>prāṇa</s>s are denoted by the word 'beings' (<s>bhūta</s>). (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.4:] That which is the body in the person, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — it is indeed this [heart]. That which is within, in the interior of the person — the heart called <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (lotus) — that is <s>Gāyatrī</s>. How? He says — in this [heart] indeed these <s>prāṇa</s>s are established; therefore, like the body, the heart is <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.5]

children.text:
saiṣā catuṣpadā ṣaḍvidhā gāyatrī |
tad etad ṛcābhyanūktam || ChUp_3,12.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Gāyatrī</s> has four feet and is sixfold. This is declared by the <s>ṛc</s> (Vedic verse).' (ChUp 3.12.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,12.5 saiṣā catuṣpadā ṣaḍakṣarapadā chandorūpā satī bhavati gāyatrī ṣaḍvidhā vāgbhūtapṛthivīśarīrahṛdayaprāṇarūpā satī ṣaḍvidhā bhavati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.5:] This <s>Gāyatrī</s>, having four feet with six syllables per foot, while being in the form of a metre, is [also] sixfold — being of the nature of speech, beings, earth, body, heart, and <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: vākprāṇayoranyārthanirdiṣṭayorapi gāyatrīprakāratvam /
children.translated_text: Speech and <s>prāṇa</s>, though mentioned for a different purpose, also serve as aspects of <s>Gāyatrī</s>,

children.text: anyathā ṣaḍvidhasaṃkhyāpūraṇānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: because otherwise the completion of the sixfold enumeration would be impossible.

children.text: tadetasminnartha etadgīyatryākhyaṃ brahma gāyatryanugataṃ gāyatrīmukhenoktamṛcāpi mantreṇābhyanūktaṃ prakāśitam //5 //
children.translated_text: In this regard, this <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Gāyatrī</s>, pervaded by <s>Gāyatrī</s>, taught through the medium of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, is also declared — made manifest — by a Vedic verse (<s>ṛc</s>), a <s>mantra</s>. (5)

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.6]

children.text:
tāvān asya mahimā tato jyāyāṃś ca puruṣaḥ |
pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni tripād asyāmṛtaṃ divīti || ChUp_3,12.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Such is His greatness, and greater still than that is the <s>Puruṣa</s>. One foot of His is all beings; three feet of His are the immortal in heaven.' (ChUp 3.12.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,12.6 tāvānasya gāyatryākhyasya brahmaṇaḥ samastasya mahimā vibhūtivistāraḥ /
yāvāṃścatuṣpātṣaḍvidhaśca brahmaṇo vikāraḥ pādo gāyatrīti vyākhyātaḥ /
atastasmādvikāralakṣaṇādgāyatryākhyādvācārambhaṇamātrāttato jyāyānmahattaraśca paramārthasatyarūpo 'vikāraḥ pūruṣaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvapūraṇātpuri śayanācca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, greater than that modification characterized as <s>Gāyatrī</s> — which is a mere verbal designation — is the <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is of the nature of ultimate reality, without modification — [called] <s>Puruṣa</s> because of filling all (<s>pūraṇa</s>) and lying in the city (<s>puri śayana</s>).

children.text: tasyāsya pādaḥ sarvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni tejobannādīni sasthāvarajaṅgamāni /
children.translated_text: One foot (<s>pāda</s>) of this [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is all beings — all things such as fire, water, food, and so on, including both stationary and moving [beings].

children.text: tripāttrayaḥ pādā asya so 'yaṃ tripāt /
children.translated_text: Three feet — three quarters of Him — He is this three-footed one.

children.text: tripādamṛtaṃ puruṣākhyaṃ samastasya gāyatryātmano divi dyotanavati svātmanyavasthitamityartha iti //6 //
children.translated_text: The three-footed immortal, called <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the entire <s>Gāyatrī</s>-self, abides in heaven — in that which is luminous — meaning it is established in its own Self. (6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.6:] 'Such is His greatness' — such is the greatness, the extent of glory, of this <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Gāyatrī</s> in its entirety. The modification of <s>Brahman</s> which has four feet and is sixfold has been explained as the one foot called <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.7]

children.text:
yad vai tad brahmetīdaṃ vāva tad yo 'yaṃ bahirdhā puruṣād ākāśaḥ |
yo vai sa bahirdhā puruṣād ākāśaḥ || ChUp_3,12.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is <s>Brahman</s> — it is indeed this space outside a person. That which is this space outside a person —' (ChUp 3.12.7)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,12.7 yadvai tat tripādamṛtaṃ gāyatrīmukhenoktaṃ brahmetīdaṃ vāva tadidameva /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.7:] That which is the three-footed immortal, spoken of through the medium of <s>Gāyatrī</s> as <s>Brahman</s> — it is indeed this very [space].

children.text: tadyo 'yaṃ prasiddho bahirdhā bahiḥ puruṣādākāśo bhautiko yo vai sa bahirdhā puruṣādākāśa uktaḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: That which is the well-known physical space outside the person — that which is the space outside the person has been stated. (7)

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.8

ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yam antaḥ puruṣa ākāśaḥ |
yo vai so 'ntaḥ puruṣa ākāśaḥ || ChUp_3,12.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'It is indeed this space within a person. That which is this space within a person —' (ChUp 3.12.8)
[Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.8]

children.text: ChUpBh_3,12.8 ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yamantaḥ puruṣe śarīra ākāśo yo vai so 'ntaḥ puruṣa ākāśaḥ //8 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.8:] It is indeed this space within the person, within the body — that which is the space within the person. (8)

children.text: START ChUp 3,12.9
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.9]

children.text:
ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yam antarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ |
tad etat pūrṇam apravarti |
pūrṇam apravartinīṃ śriyaṃ labhate ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,12.9 ||
children.translated_text: 'It is indeed this space within the heart. That is full (<s>pūrṇa</s>) and unchanging (<s>apravarti</s>). He who knows this obtains full, unchanging prosperity.' (ChUp 3.12.9)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,12.9 ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yamantarhṛdaye hṛdayapuṇḍarīka ākāśaḥ /
kathamekasya sata ākāśasya tridhā bheda iti /
ucyate-bāhyendriyaviṣaye jāgaritasthāne nabhasi duḥkhabāhulyaṃ dṛśyate /
tato 'ntaḥśarīre svapnasthānabhūte mandataraṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavati svapnānpaśyataḥ /
hṛdayasthe punarnabhasi na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṃ paśyati /
ataḥ sarvaduḥkhanivṛttirūpamākāśaṃ suṣuptasthānam /
ato yuktamekasyāpi tridhā bhedānvākhyānam /
bahirdhā puruṣādārabhyā'kāśasya hṛdaye saṅkocakaraṇaṃ cetaḥsamādhānasthānastutaye /
yathā"trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ kurukṣetraṃ viśiṣyate /
ardhatastu kurukṣetramardhatastu pṛthūdakam"iti tadvat /
tadetaddhārdākāśākhyaṃ brahma pūrṇaṃ sarvagataṃ na hṛdayamātraparicchinnamiti mantavyam /
children.translated_text: This <s>Brahman</s> called the space within the heart is full, all-pervading — it should not be thought of as confined to the heart alone.

children.text: yadyapi hṛdayākāśe cetaḥ samādhīyate 'pravarti na kutaścitkvacitpravartituṃ śīlamasyetyapravarti tadanucchittidharmakam /
children.translated_text: Although the mind is concentrated in the space of the heart, it is <s>apravarti</s> — that whose nature is not to proceed anywhere from anything — meaning it has the nature of being indestructible.

children.text: yathānyāni bhūtāni paricchinnānyucchittidharmakāṇi na tathā hārdaṃ nabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Unlike other elements which are limited and subject to destruction, the space within the heart is not so.

children.text: pūrṇāmapravartinīmanucchedātmikāṃ śriyaṃ vibhūtiṃ guṇaphalaṃ labhate dṛṣṭaṃ ya evaṃ yathoktaṃ pūrṇāpravartiguṇaṃ brahma veda jānātīhaiva jīvaṃstadbhāvaṃ pratipadyata ityarthaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: One obtains full, unchanging, imperishable prosperity — glory, the fruit of [these] qualities — that is manifest. He who knows <s>Brahman</s> thus, as having the qualities of fullness and unchangingness, attains that state while still living — that is the meaning. (9)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.12.9:] It is indeed this space within the heart, in the lotus of the heart. How can there be a threefold division of the one space? It is explained — in the external realm of the senses, in the waking state, in the sky, much suffering is seen. Then within the body, which corresponds to the dream state, there is lesser suffering for the one who sees dreams. But in the space situated in the heart, one desires no desire and sees no dream. Therefore, the space that is the cessation of all suffering is the state of deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>). Hence, the explanation of the threefold division of even one [space] is appropriate. The progressive contraction of space, beginning from that which is outside the person to the heart, is for the praise of the place of mental concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). Just as [it is said]: 'Of all the three worlds, <s>Kurukṣetra</s> is the most distinguished; the half of <s>Kurukṣetra</s> [is excellent], the half of that is <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>' — in the same way.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,13.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.13.1]

children.text:
tasya ha vā etasya hṛdayasya pañca devasuṣayaḥ |
sa yo 'sya prāṅ suṣiḥ sa prāṇaḥ |
tac cakṣuḥ |
sa ādityaḥ |
tad etat tejo 'nnādyam ity upāsīta |
tejasvy annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of this heart there are five divine openings (<s>devasuṣi</s>). That which is its eastern opening — that is <s>prāṇa</s>; that is the eye; that is <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). Meditate on that as radiance (<s>tejas</s>) and as the power of eating food (<s>annādya</s>). He becomes radiant and an eater of food, who knows this.' (ChUp 3.13.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,13.1 tasya ha vā ityādinā gāyatryākhyasya brahmaṇa upāsanāṅgatvena dvārapālādiguṇavidhānārthamārabhyate /
yathā loke dvārapālā rājña upāsanena vaśīkṛtā rājaprāptyarthā bhavanti tathehāpīti /
tasyeti prakṛtasya hṛdayasyetyarthaḥ /
etasyānantaranirdiṣṭasya pañca pañcasaṃkhyākā devānāṃ suṣayo devasuṣayaḥ svargalokaprāptidvāracchidrāṇi deveḥ prāṇādityādibhī rakṣyamāṇānītyato devasuṣayastasya svargalokabhavanasya hṛdayasyāsya yaḥ prāṅsuṣiḥ pūrvābhimukhasya prāggataṃ yacchidraṃ dvāraṃ sa prāṇastatsthastena dvāreṇa yaḥ sañcarati vāyuviśeṣaḥ sa prāganitīti prāṇaḥ /
tenaiva sambaddhamavyatiriktaṃ taccakṣustathaiva sa ādityaḥ"ādityo ha vai bāhyaḥ prāṇaḥ"iti śruteścakṣūrūpapratiṣṭhākrameṇa hṛdi sthitaḥ /
"sa ādityaḥ kasminpratiṣṭhita iti cakṣuṣi"ityādi hi vājasaneyake /
prāṇavāyudevataiva hyekā cakṣurādityaśca sahā'śrayeṇa /
vakṣyati ca-prāṇāya svāheti hatuṃ haviḥ sarvametattarpayatīti /
tadetprāṇākhyaṃ svargalokadvārapālatvādbrahma /
children.translated_text: This [entity] called <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, because of its being the door-keeper of the heavenly world.

children.text: svargalokaṃ pratipitsustejaścaitaccakṣurādityasvarūpeṇa, annādyatvācca savitustejo 'nnādyamityābhyāṃ guṇābhyāmupāsīta /
children.translated_text: One who wishes to attain the heavenly world should meditate on this radiance (<s>tejas</s>) in the form of the eye and <s>Āditya</s>, and as the power of eating food (<s>annādya</s>) because of the nourishing nature of the sun — with these two qualities.

children.text: tatastejasvyannādaścā'mayāvitvarahito bhavati ya evaṃ veda tasyaitadguṇaphalam /
children.translated_text: Then one becomes radiant and an eater of food, free from disease — he who knows this; this is the fruit of that [meditation].

children.text: upāsanena vaśīkṛto dvārapaḥ svargalokaprāpti heturbhavatīti mukhyaṃ ca phalam //1 //
children.translated_text: The door-keeper, won over through meditation, becomes the means for attaining the heavenly world — this is the principal fruit. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.13.1:] The section beginning with 'Of this' is commenced for the purpose of prescribing the qualities of door-keepers and such, as auxiliary to the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Just as in the world, door-keepers who have been won over through service to a king become the means for reaching the king, so too here. 'Of this' means of the heart under discussion. 'Of this' — of the one mentioned immediately before — there are five, five in number, divine openings (<s>devasuṣi</s>) — openings that are doors and apertures leading to the attainment of the heavenly world, [called] <s>devasuṣi</s> because they are guarded by the deities <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and others — hence 'divine openings' of this heart which is the abode of the heavenly world. Its eastern opening — the aperture facing east of the one facing eastward — [that is associated with] the particular form of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) that moves through that door — it moves forward (<s>prāk aniti</s>), hence <s>prāṇa</s>. Connected with it, non-different from it, is the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>); likewise, that is <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) — because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'The Sun is indeed the external <s>prāṇa</s>' — [<s>Āditya</s>] is situated in the heart through the sequence of [its] support in the form of sight. For in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension it is said]: 'Where is <s>Āditya</s> established? In the eye.' For <s>Prāṇa</s>, the deity of the wind, is one together with the eye and <s>Āditya</s> along with [their] substratum. And it will be said: 'By offering <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Prāṇa</s>, all this oblation satisfies [all].'

children.text: START ChUp 3,13.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.13.2]

children.text:
atha yo 'sya dakṣiṇaḥ suṣiḥ sa vyānaḥ |
tac chrotram |
sa candramāḥ |
tad etac chrīś ca yaśaś cety upāsīta |
śrīmān yaśasvī bhavati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that which is its southern opening — that is <s>vyāna</s>; that is the ear; that is the moon (<s>Candramā</s>). Meditate on that as prosperity (<s>śrī</s>) and fame (<s>yaśas</s>). He becomes prosperous and famous, who knows this.' (ChUp 3.13.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,13.2 atha yo 'sya dakṣiṇaḥ suṣistatstho vāyuviśeṣaḥ sa vīryavatkarma kurvanvigṛhya vā prāṇāpānau, nānā vānitīti vyānastatsambaddhameva ca tacchrotramindriyaṃ tathā sa candramāḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.13.2:] Now, that which is its southern opening — the particular form of wind (<s>vāyu</s>) stationed there, which performs powerful actions or holds together <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, or moves variously — that is <s>vyāna</s>. Connected with it is the faculty of hearing (<s>śrotra</s>); likewise, that is <s>Candramā</s> (the moon).

children.text: "śrotreṇa sṛṣṭā diśaśca candramāśce"ti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'From the ear were created the directions and the moon.'

children.text: sahāśrayau pūrvavattadetacchrīśca vibhūtiḥ śrotracandramasorjñānānnahetutvamatastābhyāṃ śrītvam /
children.translated_text: Together with their substratum, as before — that is prosperity (<s>śrī</s>), meaning abundance, because the ear and the moon are causes of knowledge and food — hence the quality of prosperity from these two.

children.text: jñānānnavataśca yaśaḥ khyātirbhavatīti yaśohetutvādyaśastvamatastābhyāṃ guṇābhyāmupāsītetyādi samānam //2 //
children.translated_text: And because of the abundance of knowledge and food, there is fame (<s>yaśas</s>) — renown — hence [these two] are causes of fame; therefore, one should meditate on them with these two qualities — the rest is the same as before. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 3,13.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.13.3]

children.text:
atha yo 'sya pratyaṅ suṣiḥ so 'pānaḥ |
sā vāk |
so 'gniḥ |
tad etad brahmavarcasam annādyam ity upāsīta |
brahmavarcasy annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,13.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that which is its western opening — that is <s>apāna</s>; that is speech (<s>vāk</s>); that is <s>Agni</s> (fire). Meditate on that as the lustre of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>) and the power of eating food (<s>annādya</s>). He becomes lustrous with sacred knowledge and an eater of food, who knows this.' (ChUp 3.13.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,13.3 atha yo 'sya pratyaṅsuṣiḥ paścimastatstho vāyuviśeṣaḥ sa mūtrapurīṣādyapanayannadho 'nitītyapānaḥ sā tathā vāk /
tatsambandhāttathāgnistadetadbrahmavarcasaṃ, vṛttasvādhyāyanimittaṃ tejo brahmavarcasam /
children.translated_text: Because of its connection with that [speech], fire (<s>Agni</s>) is likewise [its cosmic counterpart]. That is the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>) — the radiance arising from [proper] conduct and Vedic study (<s>svādhyāya</s>).

children.text: agnisambandhādvṛttasvādhyāyasya /
children.translated_text: Because of the connection of [proper] conduct and Vedic study with fire.

children.text: annaghrasanahetutvādapānasyānnādyatvam /
children.translated_text: He who knows this — he becomes possessed of the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>). And he becomes possessed of the splendor of food (<s>annavarcasa</s>).

children.text: samānamanyat //3 //
children.translated_text: Because of its being food. [End of section 3.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.13.3] Now, the western channel (<s>suṣi</s>) of this [person in the heart] — the particular vital air stationed there, which carries away urine, feces, and the like downward, is called <s>Apāna</s> ('downward breath'). That is likewise speech (<s>vāk</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 3,13.4
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.13.4]

children.text:
atha yo 'syodaṅ suṣiḥ sa samānaḥ |
tan manaḥ |
sa parjanyaḥ |
tad etat kīrtiś ca vyuṣṭiś cetyupāsīta |
kīrtimān vyuṣṭimān bhavati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,13.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the northern channel of this [person] — the particular vital air stationed there is <s>Samāna</s> (the equalizing breath). That is likewise the mind (<s>manas</s>).' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.13.4]

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,13.4 atha yo 'syodaṅsuṣirudaggataḥ suṣistatsyo vāyuviśeṣaḥ so 'śitapīte samaṃ nayatīti samānaḥ /
tatsambaddhaṃ mano 'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ sa parjanyo vṛṣṭyātmako devaḥ parjanyanimittāścā'pa iti /
"manasā sṛṣṭā āpaśca varuṇaśca"iti śruteḥ /
tadetkīrtiśca /
manaso jñānasya kīrtihetutvāt /
ātmaparokṣaṃ vuśrutatvaṃ kīrtiḥ /
yaśaḥ svakaraṇasaṃvedyaṃ viśrutatvam /
children.translated_text: Because of its connection with that [mind], <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) [is the cosmic counterpart]. That is fame and glory (<s>kīrti</s> and <s>yaśas</s>).

children.text: vyuṣṭiḥ kāntirdehagataṃ lāvaṇyam /
children.translated_text: He who knows this becomes possessed of fame and glory. [End of section 4.]

children.text: tataśca kīrtisambhavātkīrtiśceti /
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.13.5]

children.text: samānamanyat //4 //
children.translated_text: 'Now, the upward channel of this [person] — the particular vital air stationed there is <s>Udāna</s> (the upward breath). That is likewise touch (<s>sparśa</s>).' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.13.5]
[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.13.4] Now, the northern channel — the particular vital air there, which equalizes the food and drink consumed, is <s>Samāna</s>. That is likewise the mind (<s>manas</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 3,13.5
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.13.5] Now, the upward channel — the particular vital air there, which leads upward [at the time of death], is <s>Udāna</s>. That is likewise touch (<s>sparśa</s>).

children.text:
atha yo 'syordhvaḥ suṣiḥ sa udānaḥ |
sa vāyuḥ |
sa ākāśaḥ |
tad etad ojaś ca mahaś cety upāsīta |
ojasvī mahasvān bhavati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,13.5 ||
children.translated_text: Because of its connection with that [touch], the wind (<s>Vāyu</s>) [is the cosmic counterpart]. That is <s>Brahman</s>'s world — the space within the heart (<s>ākāśa</s>).

children.text: ChUpBh_3,13.5 atha yo 'syordhvaḥ suṣiḥ sa udāna ā pādalādārabhyordhvamutkramaṇādutkarṣārthaṃ ca karma kurvannanitītyudānaḥ sa vāyustadādhāraścā'kāśastadetadvāyvākāśayorojohetutvādojo balaṃ mahatvācca maha iti /
children.translated_text: He who knows this becomes possessed of what relates to <s>Brahman</s>'s world. [End of section 5.]

children.text: samānamanyat //5 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,13.6

te vā ete pañca brahmapuruṣāḥ svargasya lokasya dvārapāḥ |
sa ya etān evaṃ pañca brahmapuruṣān svargasya lokasya dvārapān vedāsya kule vīro jāyate |
pratipadyate svargaṃ lokaṃ ya etān evaṃ pañca brahmapuruṣān svargasya lokasya dvārapān veda || ChUp_3,13.6 ||
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.1]

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,13.6 te vā ete yathoktāḥ pañcasuṣisambandhātpañca brahmaṇo hārdasya puraṣā rājapuruṣā iva dvārasthāḥ svargasya hārdasya lokasya dvārapā dvārapālāḥ /
etairhi cakṣuḥśrotravāṅmanaḥprāṇairbahirmukhapravṛttairbrahmaṇo hārdasya prāptidvārāṇi niruddhani /
pratyakṣaṃ hyetadajitakaraṇatayā bāhyaviṣayāsaṅgānṛtaprarūḍhatvānna hārde brahmaṇi manastiṣṭhati /
tasmātsatyamuktamete pañca brahmapuruṣāḥ svargasya dvārapā iti /

ataḥ sa ya etānevaṃ yathoktaguṇaviśiṣṭānsvargasya lokasya dvārapānvedopāsta upāsanayā vaśīkaroti sa rājadvārapālānivopāsanena vaśīkṛtya tairanivāritaḥ pratipadyate svargaṃ lorka rājānamiva hārdaṃ brahma /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.14.1] 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' — [meaning] all this modified [universe], including names and forms, which is perceived — is indeed <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self. Because all this has <s>Brahman</s> as its origin, its dissolution, and its sustenance — therefore it is <s>Brahman</s> alone, like pots and the like [which are] clay alone. '<s>Tajjalān</s>' — that from which (<s>tad-ja</s>) [all things are born], into which they dissolve (<s>tad-la</s>), and in which they breathe (<s>tad-an</s>). Having thus understood, one should meditate (<s>upāsīta</s>) in a state of calm (<s>śānta</s>). [One should meditate upon it] as <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is truth, knowledge, and infinity.

children.text: kiñcāsya viduṣaḥ kule vīraḥ putro jāyate vīrapuruṣasevanāt /
children.translated_text: Because a person is made of conviction (<s>kratu</s>) — as is one's conviction in this world, so does one become after departing [from this body]. Therefore, let one form the conviction: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>.' [End of section 1.]

children.text: tasya carṇāpākaraṇena brahmopāsanapravṛttihetutvam /
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.2]

children.text: tataśca svargalokapratipattaye pāramparyeṇa bhavatīti svargalokapratipattirevaikaṃ phalama //6 //
children.translated_text: '[This self is] <s>manomaya</s> (made of mind), <s>prāṇa</s>-bodied, of luminous form, of true resolve, of space-like nature, the agent of all actions, the possessor of all desires, possessed of all fragrances, possessed of all tastes, encompassing all this, without speech, without concern.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.2]

'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. [One should] meditate upon it calmly as <s>tajjalān</s> — that from which [all things] are born, into which they dissolve, and in which they breathe. For a person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is made of conviction (<s>kratu</s>). As is one's conviction (<s>kratu</s>) in this world, so does one become upon departing [from this body]. Therefore, let one form [this] conviction.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.1]

children.text: START ChUp 3,13.7
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.14.2] [This is] the <s>Śāṇḍilya-vidyā</s> (the meditation taught by <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>). [The self] described here with the qualities beginning from '<s>manomaya</s>' is <s>Brahman</s> itself, to be meditated upon as possessing these [qualities].

children.text:
atha yad ataḥ paro divo jyotir dīpyate viśvataḥpṛṣṭheṣu sarvataḥpṛṣṭheṣv anuttameṣūttameṣu lokeṣv idaṃ vāva tad yad idam asminn antaḥ puruṣe jyotiḥ |
tasyaiṣā dṛṣṭir yatraitad asmiñ charīre saṃsparśenoṣṇimānaṃ vijānāti |
tasyaiṣā śrutir yatraitat karṇāv apigṛhya ninadam iva nadathur ivāgner iva jvalata upaśṛnoti |
tad etad dṛṣṭaṃ ca śrutaṃ cety upāsīta |
cakṣuṣyaḥ śruto bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,13.7 ||
children.translated_text: Of true resolve (<s>satya-saṃkalpa</s>) — whose will is infallible. Of space-like nature (<s>ākāśātman</s>) — whose self is like space, all-pervading.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,13.7 atha yadasau vidvānsvargaṃ lokaṃ vīrapuruṣasevanātpratipadyate /
yaccoktaṃ"tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divī"ti tadidaṃ liṅgena cakṣuḥśrotrendriyagocaramāpādayitavyam, yathāgnyādi dhūmādiliṅgena /
tathā hyevamevedamiti yathokte 'tha dṛḍha pratītiḥ syāt /
ananyatvena ca niścaya iti /
ata āha-yadato 'muṣmāddivo dyulokātparaḥ paramiti liṅgavyatyayena /
jyotirdīpyate /
svayaṃprabhaṃ sadāprakāśatvāddīpyate iva dīpyata ityucyate /
agnyādivājjvalanalakṣaṇāyā dīpterasambhavāt /
viśvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣvityetasya vyākhyāna sarvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣviti /
saṃsārāduparītyarthaḥ /
saṃsāra eva hi sarvaḥ /
asaṃsāriṇa ekatvānnirbhedatvācca /
anuttameṣu tatpuruṣasamāsāśaṅkānivṛttaya āhottameṣu lokeṣviti satyalokādiṣu hiraṇyagarbhādikāryasthaparasyeśvarasyā'sannatvāducyata uttameṣu lokeṣviti /
idaṃ vāvedameva tadyadidamasminpuruṣe 'ntarmadhye jyotiścakṣuḥ - śrotragrāhyeṇa liṅgenoṣṇimnā śabdena cāvagamyate /
yattvacā sparśarūpeṇa gṛhyate taccakṣuṣaiva /
dṛḍhapratītikaratvāttvacaḥ /
avinābhūtatvācca rūpasparśayoḥ /
kathaṃ punastasya jyotiṣo liṅgaṃ tvagdṛṣṭigocaratvamāpadyata iti, āha-yatra yasminkāle /
etaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇam /
asmiñśarīre hastenā'labhya saṃsparśenoṣṇimānaṃ rūpasahabhāvinamuṣṇasparśabhāvaṃ vijānāti /
sa hyūṣṇimā nāmarūpavyākaraṇāya dehamanupraviṣṭasya caitanyātmajyotiṣo liṅgamavyabhicārāt /
na hi jīvantamātmānamūṣṇimā vyabhicarati"uṣṇa eva jīviṣyañśīto mariṣyann" iti hi vijñāyate /
maraṇakāle ca tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāmiti pareṇāvibhāgatvopagamāt /
ato 'sādhāramaṃ liṅgamauṣṇyamagneriva dhūmaḥ /
atastasya parasyaiṣā dṛṣṭiḥ sākṣādiva darśanaṃ darśanopāya ityarthaḥ /
tathā tasya jyotiṣa eṣā śrutiḥ śravaṇaṃśravaṇopāyo 'pyucyamānaḥ /
yatra yadā puruṣo jyotiṣo liṅgaṃ śuśrūṣati śrotamicchati tadaitatkarṇāvapigṛhyaitacchabdaḥ kriyāviśeṣaṇam /
apigṛhyāpidhāyetyartho 'ṅgulibhyāṃ prorṇutya ninadamiva rathasyeva ghoṣo ninadastamiva śṛṇoti nadathuriva ṛṣabhakūjitamiva śabdo yathā cāgnerbahirjvalata evaṃ śabdamantaḥ śarīra upaśṛṇoti tadetajjyotirdṛṣṭaśrutaliṅgatvāddṛṣṭaṃ ca śrutaṃ cetyupāsīta /
tathopāsanāccakṣuṣyo darśanīyaḥ śruto viśrutaśca /
yatsparśaguṇopāsananimittaṃ phalaṃ tadrūpe sampādayati cakṣuṣya iti /
rūpasparśayoḥ sahabhāvitvāt /
iṣṭatvācca darśanīyatāyāḥ /
evaṃ ca vidyāyāḥ phalamupapannaṃ syānna tu mṛdutvādisparśavattve /
children.translated_text: Possessed of all fragrances (<s>sarvagandha</s>) and all tastes (<s>sarvarasa</s>) — as the cause of all, he possesses all fragrances and tastes. Encompassing all this (<s>sarvam idam abhyātta</s>) — pervading this entire [universe].

children.text: ya evaṃ yathoktau guṇau veda /
children.translated_text: Without speech (<s>avākya</s>) — not capable of being expressed by speech. Without concern (<s>anādara</s>) — free from attachment.

children.text: svargalokapratipattistūktamadṛṣṭaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.14.2 continued] How [is it to be meditated upon]? '<s>Manomaya</s>' means 'consisting chiefly of mind.' Mind (<s>manas</s>) is that by which one thinks; when it is engaged in objects through its own activity, [<s>Brahman</s>] is pervaded by that mind — appearing as if engaged [in worldly things] and as if withdrawn [from them]. It is precisely for this reason that [<s>Brahman</s> is described as] '<s>Prāṇa</s>-bodied' — <s>Prāṇa</s> being the subtle body (<s>liṅgātman</s>), which is a combination of the two powers of cognition and action. The <s>śruti</s> says: 'That which is <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Prajñā</s> (consciousness); that which is <s>Prajñā</s> is <s>Prāṇa</s>.'

children.text: dvirabhyāsa ādarārthaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: From the <s>mantra</s> text: 'Without hands and feet, swift is the grasper; he sees without eyes, he hears without ears.'
The agent of all actions (<s>sarvakarmā</s>) — being the inner controller, he is the impeller of all actions. The possessor of all desires (<s>sarvakāma</s>) — all desires are his.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya trayodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Without concern' (<s>anādara</s>) means without agitation.
For agitation would arise in [one who has] not yet attained what is to be attained — [that is,] in one whose desires are unfulfilled.

children.text: START ChUp 3,14.1
children.translated_text: But for the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), who is eternally fulfilled (<s>āptakāma</s>) and ever-satisfied (<s>nityatṛpta</s>), there is no agitation whatsoever. [End of section 2.]

children.text:
sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma tajjalān iti śānta upāsīta |
atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākratur asmiṃl loke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati |
sa kratuṃ kurvīta || ChUp_3,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.3]

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,14.1 punastasyaiva tripādamṛtasya brahmaṇo 'nantaguṇavato 'nantaśakteranekabhedopāsyasya viśiṣṭaguṇaśaktimatvenopāsanaṃ vidhitsannāha-sarvaṃ samastaṃ;khalviti vākyālaṅkārārtho nipātaḥ /
idaṃ jagannāmarūpavikṛtaṃ pratyakṣādiviṣayaṃ brahmakāraṇaṃ vṛddhatamatvādbrahma /
kathaṃ sarvasya brahmatvamityata āha-tajjalāniti /
tasmādbrahmaṇo jātaṃ tejobannādikrameṇa sarvam /
atastajjam /
tathā tenaiva jananakrameṇa pratilomatayā tasminneva brahmaṇi līyate tadātmatayā śliṣyata iti tallam /
tathā tasminneva sthitikāle 'niti prāṇiti ceṣṭata iti /
evaṃ brahmātmatayā triṣu kāleṣvaviśiṣṭaṃ tadvyatirekeṇāgrahaṇāt /
atastadevedaṃ jagat /
yathā cedaṃ tadevaikamadvitīyaṃ tathā ṣaṣṭhe vistareṇa vakṣyāmaḥ /
yasmācca sarvamidaṃ brahma, ataḥ śānto rāgadveṣādidoṣarahitaḥ saṃyataḥ sanyattatsarvaṃ brahma tadvakṣyamāṇairguṇairupāsīta /
kathamupāsīta /
kratuṃ kurvīta kraturniścayo 'dhyavasāya evameva nānyathetyavicalaḥ pratyayastaṃ kratuṃ kurvītopāsītetyanena vyavahitena sambandhaḥ /
kiṃ punaḥ kratukaraṇena kartavyaṃ prayojanam /
kathaṃ vā kratuḥ kartavyaḥ kratukaraṇaṃ cābhipretārthasiddhisādhanaṃ kathamityasyārthasya pratipādanārthamathetyādigranthaḥ /
atha khalviti hetvarthaḥ /
yasmātkratumayaḥ kratuprāyo 'dhyavasāyātmakaḥ puruṣo jīvaḥ /
yathākraturyādṛśaḥ kraturasya so 'yaṃ yathākraturyathādhyavasāyo yādṛṅniścayo 'smiṃlloke jīvanniha puruṣo bhavati tatheto 'smāddehātpretya mṛtvā bhavati /
kratvanurūpaphalātmako bhavatītyarthaḥ /
evaṃ hyetacchāsrato dṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.14.3] This [self] with the qualities described — is my self within the heart, in the interior of the lotus of the heart — smaller, that is, more minute than a grain of rice, or than a grain of barley, and so forth — [this enumeration is] for demonstrating extreme subtlety.

children.text: "yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram"ityādi /
children.translated_text: 'Smaller than a <s>śyāmāka</s> grain, smaller than the kernel of a <s>śyāmāka</s> grain' — when it has been stated that [the self] is smaller than [even] these definite measurements, one might suspect that it has the dimension of an atom. To prevent that, [the text] begins: 'This is my self within the heart, greater than the earth' and so forth.

children.text: yata evaṃ vyavasthā śāsradṛṣṭātaḥ sa evaṃ jānankatuṃ kurvīta yādṛśaṃ kratuṃ vakṣyāmastam /
children.translated_text: And by showing its greatness beyond [any] great magnitude, [the text] demonstrates its infinite magnitude. [End of section 3.]

children.text: yata evaṃ śāsraprāmāṇyādupapadyate kratvanurūpaṃ phalamataḥ sa kartavyaḥ kratuḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.4]

'This is my self within the heart, smaller than a grain of rice, smaller than a grain of barley, smaller than a mustard seed, smaller than a <s>śyāmāka</s> grain, smaller than the kernel of a <s>śyāmāka</s> grain. This is my self within the heart, greater than the earth, greater than the intermediate space, greater than heaven, greater than these worlds.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.3]

children.text: START ChUp 3,14.2
children.translated_text: '[This self is] the agent of all actions, the possessor of all desires, possessed of all fragrances, possessed of all tastes, encompassing all this, without speech, without concern. This is my self within the heart. This is <s>Brahman</s>. "On departing from here, I shall merge into this" — he who has this [conviction], for him there is assuredly no doubt.' Thus indeed spoke <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>. [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 3.14.4]

children.text: manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ satyasaṃkalpa ākāśātmā sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvam idam abhyatto 'vāky anādaraḥ || ChUp_3,14.2 ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.14.4] The Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), characterized by the qualities described from '<s>manomaya</s>' to 'greater than these worlds,' is to be meditated upon — but not merely as qualified by those specific attributes alone. Just as, when one says 'bring the king's man, <s>Citragu</s>,' one does not exert oneself to bring the qualifying attributes [themselves] — so too here. Having understood this, in order to prevent [the misunderstanding that only the qualified form is meant], the restatement 'the agent of all actions' and so forth is made. Therefore, [<s>Brahman</s>] qualified by such attributes as '<s>manomaya</s>' and the rest is to be meditated upon — but [the meditation ultimately aims at] the unqualified <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,14.2 katham /
manomayo manaḥprāyaḥ /
manute 'neneti manastatsvavṛttyā viṣayeṣu pravṛttaṃ bhavati tena manasā tanmayaḥ, tathā pravṛtta iva tatprāyo nivṛtta iva ca /
ata eva prāṇaśarīraḥ prāṇo liṅgātmā vijñānakriyāśaktidvayasaṃmīrchitaḥ /
"yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā yā vā prajñā sa prāṇaḥ"iti śruteḥ /
sa śarīraṃ yasya sa prāṇaśarīraḥ /
"manomayaḥ úāṇaśarīranetā"iti ca śrutyantarāt /
bhārūpaḥ /
bhā dīptiścaitanyalakṣaṇaṃ rūpaṃ yasya sa bhārūpaḥ /
satyasaṅkalpaḥ /
satyā avitathāḥ saṅkalpā yasya so 'yaṃ satyasaṅkalpaḥ /
na yathā saṃsāriṇa ivānaikāntikaphalaḥ saṅkalpa īśvarasyetyarthaḥ /
anṛtena mithyāphalatvahetunā pratyūḍhatvātsaṅkalpasya mithyāphalatvam /
vakṣyatyanṛtena hi pratyūḍhā iti /
ākāśātmā /
ākāśa ivā'tmā svarūpaṃ yasya sa ākāśātmā /
sarvagatatvaṃ sūkṣmatvaṃ rūpadihīnatvaṃ cā'kāśatulyateśvarasya /
sarvakarmā /
sarvaṃ viśvaṃ teneśvareṇa kriyata iti jagatsarvaṃ karmāsya sa sarvakarmā /
"sa hi sarvasya kartā"iti śruteḥ /
sarvakāmaḥ /
sarve kāmā doṣarahitā asyeti sarvakāmaḥ /
"dharmaviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo 'smi"iti smṛteḥ /
nanu kāmo 'smīti vacanādiha bahuvrīhistathā kāmo 'smītismṛtyartho vācyaḥ /
sarvagandhaḥ /
sarve gandhāḥ sukhakarā asya so 'yaṃ sarvagandhaḥ /
"puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyām"iti smṛteḥ /
tathā rasā api vijñeyāḥ. apuṇyagandharasagrahaṇasya pāpmasambandhanimittatvaśravaṇāt /
"tasmāttenobhayaṃ jighrati surabhi ca durgandhi ca /
pāpmanā hyeṣu viddhaḥ"iti śruteḥ /
na ca pāpmasaṃsarga īśvarasya, avidyādidoṣasyānupapatteḥ /
sarvamidaṃ jagadabhyātto 'bhivyāptaḥ /
atatervyāptyarthasya kartari niṣṭhā /
tathāvākyucyate 'nayeti vāgvāgeva vākaḥ /
dvā vacerghañantasya karaṇe vāk /
sa yasya vidyate sa vākī na vākyavākī /
vākpratiṣedhaścātropalakṣaṇārthaḥ /
gandharasādiśravaṇādīśvarasya prāptānighrāṇādīni karaṇāni gandhādigrahaṇāya /
ato vākpratiṣedhena pratiṣidhyante tāni /
"apāṇipādo javano grahītā paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ"ityādimantravarṇāt /
children.translated_text: From the mantra text: 'Without hands and feet, yet swift and grasping; he sees without eyes, he hears without ears.'

children.text: anādaro 'saṃbhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Anādara</s> (without concern) means absence of agitation.

children.text: aprāptaprāptau hi saṃbhramaḥ syādanāptakāmasya /
children.translated_text: For agitation would occur in one who has not attained what is to be attained — one whose desires are unfulfilled.

children.text: na tvāptakāmatvānnityatṛptasyeśvarasya saṃbhramo 'sti kvacit //2 //
children.translated_text: But for <s>Īśvara</s>, who has attained all desires and is eternally satisfied, there is no agitation anywhere. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.14.2:] How? <s>Manomaya</s> (made of mind) — predominantly mind; by that which is called mind, through its own activity, it becomes engaged in sense objects — being pervaded by that mind, it is as if engaged when engaged, and as if withdrawn when withdrawn. Hence, <s>prāṇaśarīra</s> (having <s>prāṇa</s> as body) — <s>prāṇa</s> is the subtle self (<s>liṅgātman</s>), a combination of the two powers of knowledge and action. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'That which is <s>prāṇa</s> is <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness); that which is <s>prajñā</s> is <s>prāṇa</s>.' That which is its body — hence <s>prāṇaśarīra</s>. And from another <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Manomaya</s>, having <s>prāṇa</s> as body, the leader.' <s>Bhārūpa</s> (having the form of light) — <s>bhā</s> means radiance, whose form is characterized by consciousness — that is <s>bhārūpa</s>. <s>Satyasaṅkalpa</s> (of unfailing will) — one whose resolves (<s>saṅkalpas</s>) are true, unfailing — that is <s>satyasaṅkalpa</s>. Not like worldly beings whose resolves yield uncertain results — the meaning is that <s>Īśvara's</s> resolve is not so. The falsity of resolve's fruit is due to its being obstructed by untruth, the cause of false results. He will say: 'For they are obstructed by untruth.' <s>Ākāśātman</s> (having space as self) — one whose self, whose essential nature, is like space — that is <s>ākāśātman</s>. All-pervadingness, subtlety, and freedom from form belong to <s>Īśvara</s>, like space. <s>Sarvakarmā</s> (all-acting) — everything, the entire universe, is made by that <s>Īśvara</s> — thus the entire world is his action, hence <s>sarvakarmā</s>. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'For he is the maker of all.' <s>Sarvakāma</s> (having all desires) — all desires, free from defects, are his — hence <s>sarvakāma</s>. From the <s>smṛti</s>: 'I am desire not opposed to <s>dharma</s> in beings.' Now, since [the Lord] says 'I am desire,' it should be construed as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound here too, and the meaning of the <s>smṛti</s> 'I am desire' should be stated accordingly. <s>Sarvagandha</s> (having all fragrances) — all fragrances that bring happiness are his — that is <s>sarvagandha</s>. From the <s>smṛti</s>: 'The pure fragrance in the earth.' Likewise, tastes should also be understood. For [the scripture] declares that the apprehension of impure fragrances and tastes is caused by the connection with sin. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'Therefore by it (the nose) one smells both — the fragrant and the foul-smelling; for it is pierced by sin.' And there is no connection with sin for <s>Īśvara</s>, since defects such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are impossible [for him]. He has pervaded (<s>abhyātta</s>) all this world — the word <s>abhyātta</s> is a past participle in the agent sense from the root <s>at</s> meaning 'to pervade.' Similarly, <s>avākī</s> — one who is without speech (<s>vāk</s>) — <s>vāk</s> is speech itself; <s>vāka</s> is derived with the suffix <s>ghañ</s> from the root <s>vac</s> in the instrumental sense. One who possesses it is <s>vākī</s>; one without speech is <s>avākī</s>. And the negation of speech here is intended as illustrative (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). Since fragrances, tastes, and other [qualities] are mentioned as belonging to <s>Īśvara</s>, the corresponding sense organs such as the nose are implied for apprehending fragrances and the rest. Therefore, by the negation of speech, those [organs] are [also] negated.

children.text: START ChUp 3,14.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.14.3]

children.text:
eṣa ma ātmā antarhṛdaye 'ṇīyān vrīher vā yavād vā sarṣapād vā śyāmākād vā śyāmākataṇḍulād vā |
eṣa ma ātmā antarhṛdaye jyāyān pṛthivyā jyāyān antarikṣāj jyāyān divo jyāyān ebhyo lokebhyaḥ || ChUp_3,14.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'This is my <s>ātman</s> (Self) within the heart, smaller than a grain of rice, smaller than a grain of barley, smaller than a mustard seed, smaller than a grain of <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet), smaller than the kernel of a <s>śyāmāka</s> grain. This is my <s>ātman</s> within the heart, greater than the earth, greater than the atmosphere, greater than heaven, greater than these worlds.' (ChUp 3.14.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,14.3 eṣa yathoktaguṇo me mamā'tmāntarhṛdaye hṛdayapuṇḍarīkasyāntarmadhye 'ṇīyānaṇutaro vrīhervā yavādvetyādyatyantasūkṣmatvapradarśanārtham /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.14.3:] This, possessing the qualities described above, is my <s>ātman</s> within the heart — in the interior, in the middle of the heart-lotus — smaller, more minute than a grain of rice, or than a grain of barley, and so on — this is to demonstrate extreme subtlety.

children.text: śyāmākādvā śyāmākataṇḍulādveti paricchinnaparimāṇādaṇīyānityukte 'ṇuparimāṇatvaṃ prāptamāśaṅkyātastatpratiṣedhāyā'rabhate - eṣa ma ātmāntarhṛdaye jyāyānpṛthivyā ityādinā /
children.translated_text: When it is said to be smaller than a <s>śyāmāka</s> grain or smaller than a <s>śyāmāka</s> kernel — since it is said to be smaller than something of finite measure, the notion that it has atomic dimensions might arise. To negate that, he begins: 'This is my <s>ātman</s> within the heart, greater than the earth' and so on.

children.text: jyāyaḥparimāṇācca jyāyastvaṃ darśayannanantaparimāṇatvaṃ darśayati //3 //
children.translated_text: By showing greatness surpassing all measures of greatness, he demonstrates its infinite measure. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 3,14.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.14.4]

children.text:
sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvam idam abhyatto 'vākyanādaraḥ |
eṣa ma ātmā antarhṛdaye |
etad brahma |
etam itaḥ pretyābhisaṃbhavitā asmīti yasya syād addhā na vicikitsā asti |
iti ha smāha śāṇḍilyaḥ śāṇḍilyaḥ || ChUp_3,14.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'All-acting, all-desiring, having all fragrances, having all tastes, pervading all this [universe], without speech, without concern — this is my <s>ātman</s> within the heart. This is <s>Brahman</s>. Upon departing from here, I shall merge into it — thus whoever has this [conviction], for him indeed there is no doubt.' Thus spoke <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>. (ChUp 3.14.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,14.4 manomaya ityādinā jyāyānebhyo lokebhya ityantena yathoktaguṇalakṣaṇa īśvaro dhyeyo na tu tadguṇaviśiṣṭa eva yathā rājapuruṣamānaya citraguṃ vetyukte na viśeṣaṇaśyāpyānayane vyāpriyate tadvadihāpīti prāptamatastannivṛttyartha sarvakarmetyādi punarvacanam /
tasmānmanomayatvādiguṇaviśiṣṭa eveśvaro dhyeyaḥ /
ata eva ṣaṣṭhasaptamayoriva tattvamasyātmaivedaṃ sarvamiti neha svārājye 'bhiṣiñcati /
eṣa ma ātmaitadbrahmaitamitaḥ pratyābhisambhavitāsmīti liṅgānna tvātmaśabdena pratyagātmaivocyate /
mameti ṣaṣṭhyāḥ sambandhārthapratyāyakatvādetamabhisambhavitāsmīti ca karmakartṛtvanirdeśāt /
nanu ṣaṣṭhe 'pyatha sampatsya iti satsampatteḥ kālāntaritatvaṃ darśayati /
na, ārabdhasaṃskāraśeṣasthityarthaparatvāt na kālāntaritārthatā /
anyathā tattvamasītyetasyārthasya bādhaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be the undesirable consequence of contradicting the meaning of 'You are That.'

children.text: yadyapyātmaśabdasya pratyagarthatvaṃ sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahmeti ca prakṛtameṣa ma ātmāntarhṛdaya etadbrahmetyucyate tathāpyantardhānamīṣadaparityajyaivaitamātmānamito 'smāccharīrātpretyābhisambhavitāsmītyuktam /
children.translated_text: Although the word <s>ātman</s> has the meaning of the inner Self, and although 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' is the subject matter, and it is said 'This is my <s>ātman</s> within the heart, this is <s>Brahman</s>' — nevertheless, without entirely abandoning the concealment, it is said 'Upon departing from this body, I shall merge into this <s>ātman</s>.'

children.text: yathākraturūpasyā'tmanaḥ pratipattāsmīti yasyaivaṃvidaḥ syādbhavedaddhā satyamevaṃ syāmahaṃ pretya evaṃ na syāmiti na ca vicikitsāstītyetasminnarthe kratuphalasambandhe sa tathaiveśvarabhāvaṃ pratipadyate vidvānityetadāha smoktavānkila śāṇḍalyo nāmarṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose nature is according to one's resolve — 'I am the one who attains' — whoever of such knowledge has this [conviction]: 'Truly, so shall I become after departing; I shall not fail to become so' — and there is no doubt regarding this matter, regarding the connection between resolve and its fruit — he indeed attains the state of <s>Īśvara</s>. This is what the sage named <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> has said.

children.text: dvirabhyāsa ādarārthaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: The twofold repetition [of <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>] is for emphasis. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.14.4:] <s>Īśvara</s>, characterized by the qualities described from '<s>manomaya</s>' up to 'greater than these worlds,' is to be meditated upon — but not merely as qualified by those attributes alone. Just as when told 'Bring the king's servant, <s>Citragu</s>,' one does not exert effort to bring the qualifications as well — similarly here too, [one might think that the qualifications alone are to be meditated upon]. To negate that, the repetition '<s>sarvakarmā</s>' and so on is stated. Therefore, <s>Īśvara</s> qualified by the attributes of being <s>manomaya</s> and the rest is indeed to be meditated upon. For this very reason, unlike in the sixth and seventh [chapters], where 'You are That' and 'All this is indeed the Self' — here [the text] does not consecrate [the meditator] into self-sovereignty. From the indicative marks: 'This is my <s>ātman</s>; this is <s>Brahman</s>; upon departing from here, I shall merge into it' — it is not the inner Self that is being spoken of by the word <s>ātman</s>. Because the sixth case ending (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>) 'my' (<s>mama</s>) indicates a relation, and because of the statement 'I shall merge into it' which indicates different roles for agent and object. But in the sixth [chapter] too, 'then it will merge' shows that the merging with <s>Sat</s> (Being) is at a future time. No — because that [passage] is meant for the remaining duration of the effects of commenced actions (<s>ārabdha-saṃskāra</s>), and not for a different future time.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya caturdaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,15.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.15.1]

children.text:
antarikṣodaraḥ kośo bhūmibudhno na jīryati |
diśo hy asya sraktayo dyaur asyottaraṃ bilam |
sa eṣa kośo vasudhānas tasmin viśvam idaṃ śritam || ChUp_3,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The chest (<s>kośa</s>) whose belly is the atmosphere, whose bottom is the earth — it does not decay. The directions are its corners; heaven is its upper opening. This chest is the container of wealth; in it all this [universe] rests.' (ChUp 3.15.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,15.1 asya kule vīro jāyata ityuktam /
na vīrajanmamātraṃ pitustrāṇāya /
"tasmātputramanuśṣṭaṃ lokyamāhuḥ"iti śrutyantarāt /
atastaddīrghāyuṣṭvaṃ kathaṃ syādityevamarthaṃ kośavijñānārambhaḥ /
abhyarhitavijñānavyāsaṅgādanantarameva noktaṃ tadidānīmevā'rabhyate-antarikṣamudaramantaḥsuṣiraṃ yasya so 'yamantarikṣodaraḥ kośaḥ kośa ivānekadharmasādṛśyātkośaḥ /
sa ca bhūmibudhno bhūmirbudhno mūlaṃ yasya sa bhūmibudhno na jīryati na vinaśyati trailokyātmakatvāt /
sahasrayugakālāvasthāyī hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: For it endures for the duration of a thousand <s>yugas</s>.

children.text: diśo hyasya sarvāḥ sraktayaḥ koṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: All the directions are its corners (<s>sraktayas</s>).

children.text: dyaurasya kośasyottaramūrdhvaṃ bilaṃ sa eṣa yathoktaguṇaḥ kośo vasudhāno vasu dhīyate 'sminprāṇināṃ karmaphalākhyamato vasudhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Heaven is this chest's upper opening (<s>bila</s>). This chest, described with the above qualities, is a container of wealth (<s>vasudhāna</s>) — wealth (<s>vasu</s>) in the form of the fruits of the actions of living beings is placed in it, hence <s>vasudhāna</s>.

children.text: yasminnantarviśvaṃ samastaṃ prāṇikarmaphalaṃ saha tatsādhanairidaṃ yadgṛhyate pratyakṣādipramāṇaiḥ śritamāśritaṃ sthitamityarthaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Within which the entire universe — all the fruits of living beings' actions together with their means — whatever is apprehended by the senses and other means of knowledge — rests, abides — this is the meaning. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.15.1:] It was said: 'A hero is born in his family.' Merely the birth of a son is not for the protection of the father. From another <s>śruti</s>: 'Therefore they say a son who is well-instructed is fit for the world.' Hence, how may his long life be [ensured]? — with this purpose, the meditation on the chest (<s>kośa</s>) is begun. Due to the connection with the preceding meditation that was being honored, it was not stated immediately; now it is begun. The atmosphere is the belly, the interior hollow — that whose belly is the atmosphere is <s>antarikṣodara</s>; it is a chest (<s>kośa</s>) — like a chest, due to similarity in many properties. And it has the earth as its bottom — <s>bhūmibudhna</s>, the earth is the bottom, the base — it does not decay, does not perish, because it consists of the three worlds.

children.text: START ChUp 3,15.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.15.2]

children.text:
tasya prācī dig juhūr nāma |
sahamānā nāma dakṣiṇā |
rājñī nāma pratīcī |
subhūtā nāmodīcī |
tāsāṃ vāyur vatsaḥ |
sa ya etam evaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda na putrarodaṃ roditi |
so 'ham etam evaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda |
mā putrarodaṃ rudam || ChUp_3,15.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Its eastern quarter is named <s>Juhū</s>. Its southern [quarter] is named <s>Sahamānā</s>. Its western [quarter] is named <s>Rājñī</s>. Its northern [quarter] is named <s>Subhūtā</s>. Their calf is the wind (<s>Vāyu</s>). He who knows this wind as the calf of the directions does not weep with weeping for a son. I know this wind as the calf of the directions. May I not weep with weeping for a son.' (ChUp 3.15.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,15.2 tasyāsya prācī digprāggato bhāgo juhūrnāma juhvatyasyāṃ diśi karmiṇaḥ prāṅmukhāḥ santa iti juhūnami /
sahamānā māna sahante 'syāṃ pāpakarmaphalāni yamapuryāṃ prāṇina iti sahamānā nāma dakṣiṇādik /
tathā rājñī nāma pratīcī paścimā digrājñī rājñā varuṇenādhiṣṭhitā sandhyārāgayogādvā /
subhūtā nāma bhūtimadbhirīśvarakuberādibhiradhiṣṭhitatvātsubhūtā nāmodīcī /
tāsāṃ diśāṃ vāyurvatso digjatvādvāyoḥ /
"purovāta"ityādidarśanāt /
sa yaḥ kaścitputradīrghajīvitarthyevaṃ yathoktaguṇaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsamamṛtaṃ veda sa na putrarodaṃ putranimittaṃ rodanaṃ na roditi putro na mriyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever, desiring long life for his son, knows in this manner the wind as the calf of the directions, as immortal — he does not weep with weeping for a son, meaning his son does not die.

children.text: yata evaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ kośadigvatsaviṣayaṃ vijñānamataḥ so 'haṃ putrajīvitārthyevametaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda jāne /
children.translated_text: Since such distinguished knowledge concerning the chest, directions, and calf [exists], therefore I, desiring the life of my son, know this wind as the calf of the directions.

children.text: ato mā putrarodaṃ rudaṃ mā rudaṃ putramaraṇanimittam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, may I not weep — may I not weep on account of a son's death.

children.text: putrorodo mama mā bhūdityarthaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: may the death-lamentation for a son not befall me. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.15.2:] Its — this [chest's] — eastern direction, the portion facing east, is named <s>Juhū</s> — because in this direction, ritualists offer oblations (<s>juhvati</s>) facing east, hence the name <s>Juhū</s>. <s>Sahamānā</s> — living beings in <s>Yama's</s> city endure the fruits of sinful actions in this direction, hence the southern direction is named <s>Sahamānā</s>. Likewise, <s>Rājñī</s> is the name of the western direction — the western direction presided over by the king <s>Varuṇa</s>, or because of the association with the red glow of twilight. <s>Subhūtā</s> — because it is presided over by prosperous beings such as <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Kubera</s>, the northern direction is named <s>Subhūtā</s>. The calf of these directions is the wind (<s>Vāyu</s>), because <s>Vāyu</s> is born from the directions. From the observation: '<s>purovāta</s>' (east wind) and so forth.

children.text: START ChUp 3,15.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.15.3]

children.text:
ariṣṭaṃ kośaṃ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā |
prāṇaṃ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā |
bhūḥ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā |
bhuvaḥ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā |
svaḥ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā || ChUp_3,15.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'I take refuge in the imperishable chest, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so. I take refuge in <s>prāṇa</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so. I take refuge in <s>bhūḥ</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so. I take refuge in <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so. I take refuge in <s>svaḥ</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so.' (ChUp 3.15.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,15.3 ariṣṭamavināśinaṃ kośaṃ yathoktaṃ prapadye prapanno 'smi putrāyuṣe /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.15.3:] I take refuge in — I have taken refuge in — the imperishable, indestructible chest described above, for the sake of my son's long life.

children.text: amunāmunāmuneti trirnāma gṛhṇāti putrasya /
children.translated_text: 'By so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so' — he utters the name of the son three times.

children.text: tathā prāṇaṃ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā, bhūḥ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā bhuvaḥ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā svaḥ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā, sarvatra prapadya iti trinami gṛhṇāti punaḥ punaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'I take refuge in <s>prāṇa</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so; I take refuge in <s>bhūḥ</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so; I take refuge in <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so; I take refuge in <s>svaḥ</s>, by so-and-so, by so-and-so, by so-and-so' — everywhere with 'I take refuge,' he utters the name three times again and again. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 3,15.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.15.4]

children.text:
sa yad avocaṃ prāṇaṃ prapadya iti |
prāno vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca |
tam eva tat prāpatsi || ChUp_3,15.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'When I said "I take refuge in <s>prāṇa</s>" — <s>prāṇa</s> indeed is all this that exists, whatever there is. In that alone I have taken refuge.' (ChUp 3.15.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,15.4 sa yadavocaṃ prāṇaṃ prapadya iti vyākhyānārthamupanyāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.15.4:] 'When I said "I take refuge in <s>prāṇa</s>"' — this is an introductory statement for the purpose of explanation.

children.text: prāṇo vā idaṃsarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yadidaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is all this that exists — whatever this world is.

children.text: "yathā vārānābhāv" iti vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: As will be stated: 'Just as the spokes [are fixed in the hub].'

children.text: atastameva sarvaṃ tattena prāṇaprapadanena prāpatsi prapanno 'bhavam //4//
children.translated_text: Therefore, by that very taking refuge in <s>prāṇa</s>, I have taken refuge in that totality — I have become one who has taken refuge. (4)

children.text: atha yadavīcaṃ bhūḥ prapadya iti pṛthivīṃ prapadye 'ntarikṣaṃ prapadye divaṃ prapadya ityeva tadavocam //5//
children.translated_text: 'And when I said "I take refuge in <s>bhūḥ</s>" — I take refuge in the earth, I take refuge in the atmosphere, I take refuge in heaven — that is what I said.' (5)
[<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.15.5]

children.text: ChUpBh_3,15.5
tathā bhūḥ prapadya iti trīṃllokānbhūrādīnprapadya iti tadavocam //5 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'I take refuge in <s>bhūḥ</s>' — by this I said: I take refuge in the three worlds beginning with <s>bhūḥ</s>. (5)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.15.5:]

children.text: START ChUp 3,15.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.15.6]

children.text: atha yad avocaṃ bhuvaḥ prapadya ity agniṃ prapadye vāyuṃ prapadya ādityaṃ prapadya ity eva tad avocam || ChUp_3,15.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'And when I said "I take refuge in <s>bhuvaḥ</s>" — I take refuge in <s>Agni</s> (fire), I take refuge in <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), I take refuge in <s>Āditya</s> (sun) — that is what I said.' (ChUp 3.15.6)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,15.6 atha yadavocaṃ bhuvaḥ prapadya ityagnyādīnprapadya iti tadavocam //6 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.15.6:] And when I said 'I take refuge in <s>bhuvaḥ</s>' — I said: I take refuge in <s>Agni</s> and the rest. (6)

children.text: START ChUp 3,15.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.15.7]

children.text: atha yad avocaṃ svaḥ prapadya ity ṛgvedaṃ prapadye yajurvedaṃ prapadye sāmavedaṃ prapadya ity eva tad avocam || ChUp_3,15.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'And when I said "I take refuge in <s>svaḥ</s>" — I take refuge in the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, I take refuge in the <s>Yajurveda</s>, I take refuge in the <s>Sāmaveda</s> — that is what I said.' (ChUp 3.15.7)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,15.7 atha yadavocaṃ svaḥ prapadya ityṛgvedādīnprapadya ityeva tadavocamiti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.15.7:] And when I said 'I take refuge in <s>svaḥ</s>' — I said: I take refuge in the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the rest.

children.text: upariṣṭānmantrāñjapettataḥ pūrvoktamajaraṃ kośaṃ sadigvatsaṃ yathāvaddhyātvā dvirvacanamādarārtham //7//
children.translated_text: After reciting the mantras given above, one should meditate properly on the imperishable chest described earlier, together with the directions and their calf. The twofold repetition is for emphasis. (7)

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya pañcadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,16.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.16.1]

children.text:
puruṣo vāva yajñaḥ |
tasya yāni caturviṃśativarṣāṇi tat prātaḥsavanam |
caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī |
gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanam |
tad asya vasavo 'nvāyattāḥ |
prāṇā vāva vasavaḥ |
ete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vāsayanti || ChUp_3,16.1 ||
children.translated_text: A person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is verily the sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>). His first twenty-four years are the morning pressing (<s>prātaḥsavana</s>). The <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter has twenty-four syllables. The morning pressing is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. The <s>Vasus</s> are connected with this [pressing] of his. The <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) are verily the <s>Vasus</s>, for they cause all this to dwell (<s>vāsayanti</s>).

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,16.1 putrāyuṣa upāsanamuktaṃ japaśca /
athedānīmātmano dīrghajīvanāyedamupāsanaṃ japaṃ ca vidadhadāha /
jīvanhi svayaṃ putrādiphalena yujyate nānyathā ityata ātmānaṃ yajñaṃ sampādayati-puraṣaḥ puruṣo jīvanaviśiṣṭaḥ kāryakaraṇasaṅghāto yathāprasiddha eva /
vāvaśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ /
puraṣa eva yajña ityarthaḥ /
tathā hi sāmānyaiḥ sampādayati yajñatvam /
katham /
tasya puruṣasya yāni caturviṃśativarṣāṇyāyuṣastatprātaḥsavanaṃ yajñasya /
kena sāmānyenetyāha-caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatro chando gāyatraṃ gāyatrīchandaskaṃ hi vidhiyajñasya prātaḥsavanam /
ataḥ prātaḥsavanasampannena caturviṃśativarṣāyuṣā yuktaḥ puruṣaḥ /
ato vidhiyajñasādṛśyādyajñaḥ /
tathottarayorapyāyuṣoḥ savanadvayasampattisriṣṭubjagatyakṣarasaṃkhyāsāmānyato vācyā /
kiñca tadasya puruṣayajñasya prātaḥsavanaṃ vidhiyajñasyeva vasavo devā anvāyattā anugatāḥ /
savanadevatātvena svāmina ityarthaḥ /
puruṣayajñe 'pi vidhiyajña ivāgnyādayo vasavo devāḥ prāptā ityato viśinaṣṭi-prāṇā vāva vasavo vāgādayo vāyavaśca /
children.translated_text: Since in the <s>puruṣa</s>-sacrifice too, the <s>Vasus</s> — deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others — are obtained just as in the ritual sacrifice, he specifies: the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) are verily the <s>Vasus</s> — namely speech and the other [senses], and the vital airs.

children.text: tehi yasmādidaṃ puruṣādiprāṇijātamete vāsayanti /
children.translated_text: For they cause this entire class of beings, beginning with the person, to dwell.

children.text: prāṇeṣu hi dehe vatsatu sarvamida vasati nānyathā /
children.translated_text: For when the <s>prāṇas</s> dwell in the body, all this dwells; not otherwise.

children.text: ityato vasanādvāsanācca vasavaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from causing to dwell (<s>vasana</s>) and from making to dwell (<s>vāsana</s>), they are called <s>Vasus</s>.

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.16.1] The meditation for the son's longevity has been stated, along with the <s>japa</s> (recitation). Now, for the purpose of one's own long life, he teaches this meditation and <s>japa</s>, saying — for only while living does one enjoy the fruits such as sons, not otherwise; therefore he identifies the self with the sacrifice. '<s>Puruṣa</s>' means a person distinguished by being alive, the well-known aggregate of body and organs. The word '<s>vāva</s>' is for emphasis — the meaning is that the person alone is the sacrifice. And so he establishes the sacrificial nature through common features. How? The first twenty-four years of that person's life constitute the morning pressing of the sacrifice. By what common feature? He says — the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter has twenty-four syllables; the morning pressing of the ritual sacrifice (<s>vidhiyajña</s>) is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. Therefore the person is connected with the morning pressing through the twenty-four years of life. Hence he is a sacrifice by virtue of resemblance to the ritual sacrifice. Similarly, for the remaining two portions of life, the correspondence with the two other pressings should be stated through the common number of syllables in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s> meters. Furthermore, the <s>Vasus</s>, the deities, are connected with the morning pressing of this <s>puruṣa</s>-sacrifice (<s>puruṣayajña</s>), just as in the ritual sacrifice — as lords by virtue of being the deities of the pressing, that is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 3,16.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.16.2]

children.text:
taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt |
prāṇā vasava idaṃ me prātaḥsavanaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ vasūnāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti |
ud dhaiva tata ety agado ha bhavati || ChUp_3,16.2 ||
children.translated_text: If anything should afflict him during this period of life, he should say: 'O <s>Prāṇas</s>, O <s>Vasus</s>, let this morning pressing of mine be extended to the midday pressing. May I, the sacrifice, not be cut off in the midst of the <s>Prāṇas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>.' He rises up from that [affliction] and becomes free from illness.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,16.2 taṃ cedyajñasampāditametasminprātaḥ savanasampanne vayasi kiñcidvyādhyādi maraṇaśaṅkāraṇamupatapedduḥkhamutpādayetsa tadā yajñasampādī puruṣa ātmānaṃ yajñaṃ manyamāno brūyājjapedityarthaḥ imaṃ mantraṃ he prāṇā vasava adaṃ me prātaḥ savanaṃ mama yajñasya vartate tanmādhyandinaṃ savanamanusantanuteti mādhyandinena savanenā'yuṣā sahitamekībhūtaṃ santataṃ kurutetyarthaḥ /
māhaṃ yajño yuṣmākaṃ prāṇānāṃ vasūnāṃ prātaḥsavaneśānāṃ madhye vilopsīya vilupyeya vicchidyeyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May I, the sacrifice, not be cut off (<s>vilopsīya</s>) — not be destroyed, not be interrupted — in the midst of you, the <s>Prāṇas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the lords of the morning pressing' — that is the meaning.

children.text: itiśabdo mantraparisamāptyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>iti</s>' serves to indicate the conclusion of the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: sa tena japena dhyānena ca tatastasmādupatāpādudetyudgacchati /
children.translated_text: Through that <s>japa</s> (recitation) and meditation, he rises up, emerges from that affliction.

children.text: udgamya vimuktaḥ sannagado hānupatāpo bhavatyeva //2 //
children.translated_text: Having risen up and become free, he becomes indeed without disease and without affliction.

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.16.2] If anything — some disease or other cause giving rise to the fear of death — should afflict him, that is, produce suffering, during this period of life corresponding to the morning pressing, which has been identified as the sacrifice, then the person who has identified himself as the sacrifice, regarding himself as the sacrifice, should recite (<s>japet</s>) — that is the meaning — this <s>mantra</s>: 'O <s>Prāṇas</s>, O <s>Vasus</s>, this morning pressing of my sacrifice is taking place; let it be extended to the midday pressing' — meaning, let it be made continuous, unified with the life-span of the midday pressing.

children.text: START ChUp 3,16.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.16.3]

children.text:
atha yāni catuścatvāriṃśad varṣāṇi tan mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam |
catuścatvāriṃśadakṣarā triṣṭup |
traiṣṭubhaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam |
tad asya rudrā anvāyattāḥ |
