prāṇā vāva rudrāḥ |
ete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ rodayanti || ChUp_3,16.3 ||
children.translated_text: Then the forty-four years [from twenty-four to sixty-eight] constitute the midday pressing. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter has forty-four syllables. The midday pressing is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. The <s>Rudras</s> are connected with this [pressing] of his. The <s>prāṇas</s> are verily the <s>Rudras</s>, for they make all this weep (<s>rodayanti</s>).

children.text: ChUpBh_3,16.3 atha yāni catuścatvāriṃśadvarṣāṇītyādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.16.3] 'Then the forty-four years' and so on — the rest is the same [as before].

children.text: rudanti rodayantīti prāṇā rudrāḥ /
children.translated_text: They weep (<s>rudanti</s>) and make others weep (<s>rodayanti</s>) — therefore the <s>prāṇas</s> are called <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: krūrā hi te madhyamevayasyato rudrāḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: For they are fierce in the middle period of life — hence they are <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,16.4-6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.16.4–6]

children.text:
taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt |
prāṇā rudrā idaṃ me mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ tṛtīyasavanam anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti |
ud dhaiva tata ety agado ha bhavati || ChUp_3,16.4 ||
children.translated_text: If anything should afflict him during this period of life, he should say: 'O <s>Prāṇas</s>, O <s>Rudras</s>, let this midday pressing of mine be extended to the third pressing. May I, the sacrifice, not be cut off in the midst of the <s>Prāṇas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>.' He rises up from that and becomes free from illness.

children.text:
atha yāny aṣṭācatvāriṃśad varṣāṇi tat tṛtīyasavanam |
aṣṭācatvāriṃśadakṣarā jagatī |
jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanam |
tad asyādityā anvāyattāḥ |
prāṇā vāvādityāḥ |
ete hīdaṃ sarvam ādadate || ChUp_3,16.5 ||
children.translated_text: Then the forty-eight years [from sixty-eight to one hundred and sixteen] constitute the third pressing. The <s>Jagatī</s> meter has forty-eight syllables. The third pressing is in the <s>Jagatī</s> meter. The <s>Ādityas</s> are connected with this [pressing] of his. The <s>prāṇas</s> are verily the <s>Ādityas</s>, for they take up (<s>ādadate</s>) all this.

children.text:
taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt |
prāṇā ādityā idaṃ me tṛtīyasavanam āyur anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānām ādityānāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti |
ud dhaiva tata ety agado haiva bhavati || ChUp_3,16.6 ||
children.translated_text: If anything should afflict him during this period of life, he should say: 'O <s>Prāṇas</s>, O <s>Ādityas</s>, let this third pressing of mine extend my lifespan. May I, the sacrifice, not be cut off in the midst of the <s>Prāṇas</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>.' He rises up from that and becomes indeed free from illness.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,16.4-6 tathā'dityāḥ prāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.16.4–6] Similarly, the <s>Ādityas</s> are the <s>prāṇas</s>.

children.text: te hīdaṃ śabdādijātamādadate 'ta ādityāstṛtīyasavanamāyuḥ ṣoḍaśottaravarṣaśataṃ samāpayatānusantanuta yajñaṃ samāpayatetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For they take up (<s>ādadate</s>) this entire class of sound and other [sense objects] — hence they are <s>Ādityas</s>. The third pressing: 'Let the lifespan — one hundred and sixteen years — be completed; extend [it], complete the sacrifice' — that is the meaning.

children.text: samānamanyat //4-6 //
children.translated_text: The rest is the same [as before].

children.text: START ChUp 3,16.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.16.7]

children.text:
etad dha sma vai tad vidvān āha mahidāsa aitareyaḥ |
sa kiṃ ma etad upatapasi yo 'ham anena na preṣyām iti |
sa ha ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśatam ajīvat |
pra ha ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśataṃ jīvati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,16.7 ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, <s>Mahidāsa Aitareya</s> indeed said: 'Why do you afflict me, I who shall not die by this?' He lived one hundred and sixteen years. He who knows thus lives one hundred and sixteen years.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,16.7 niścitā hi vidyā phalāyetyetaddarśayannudāharati-etadyajñadarśanaṃ ha sma vai kila tadvidvānāha mahidāso nāmataḥ /
itarāyā apatyamaitareyaḥ /
kiṃ kasmānme mamaitadupatapanamupatapasi sa tvaṃ he roga yo 'haṃ yajño 'nena tvatkṛtenopatāpena na preṣyāmi na mariṣyāmyato vṛthā tava śrama ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Why — for what reason — do you afflict me with this affliction? O you disease, I who am the sacrifice shall not die (<s>na preṣyāmi</s>) by this affliction caused by you; therefore your effort is in vain' — that is the meaning.

children.text: ityevamāha smeti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke — this connects with the preceding [statement].

children.text: sa evaṃniścayaḥ sanṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśatamajīvat /
children.translated_text: He, having such firm conviction, lived one hundred and sixteen years.

children.text: anyo 'pyevaṃniścaḥ ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśataṃ prajīvati ya evaṃ yathoktaṃ yajñasampādanaṃ veda jānāti sa ityarthaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: Anyone else too, having such firm conviction, lives one hundred and sixteen years — he who knows thus, who knows the identification with the sacrifice as described — that is the meaning.

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.16.7] To show that knowledge, when firmly grasped, produces its result, he cites an illustration: knowing this vision of sacrifice, <s>Mahidāsa</s> by name — the son of <s>Itarā</s>, hence <s>Aitareya</s> — indeed said [the following].

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya ṣoḍaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: sa yad aśiśiṣati yat pipāsati yan na ramate tā asya dīkṣāḥ || ChUp_3,17.1 ||
children.translated_text: When he hungers, when he thirsts, when he does not enjoy pleasure — these are his <s>dīkṣās</s> (initiatory rites).

children.text: ChUpBh_3,17.1 sa yadaśiśiṣatotyādiyajñasāmānyanirdeśaḥ puruṣasya pūrveṇaiva sambadhyate /
yadaśiśiṣatyaśitumicchati /
children.translated_text: 'When he hungers' (<s>aśiśiṣati</s>) means when he desires to eat.

children.text: tathā pipāsati pātumicchati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'when he thirsts' (<s>pipāsati</s>) means when he desires to drink.

children.text: yanna ramata iṣṭādyaprāptinimittaṃ yadaivañjātīyakaṃ duḥkhamanubhavati tā asya dīkṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When he does not enjoy pleasure' — when he experiences such suffering caused by the non-attainment of desired objects and the like — these are his <s>dīkṣās</s> (initiatory rites),

children.text: duḥkhasāmānyādvidhiyajñasyeva //1 //
children.translated_text: because of the common feature of suffering, just as in the ritual sacrifice.
[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.17.1] 'When he hungers' and so on — this indication of common features with the sacrifice connects the person with the preceding [section].

children.text: START ChUp 3,17.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.17.2]

children.text: atha yad aśnāti yat pibati yad ramate tad upasadair eti || ChUp_3,17.2 ||
children.translated_text: Then when he eats, when he drinks, when he enjoys pleasure — these correspond to the <s>Upasad</s> ceremonies.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,17.2 atha yadaśnāti yatpibati yadramate ratiṃ cānubhavatīṣṭādisaṃyogāttadupasadaiḥ samānatāmeti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.17.2] Then when he eats, when he drinks, when he enjoys pleasure — that is, when he experiences delight through contact with desired objects — these attain similarity with the <s>Upasad</s> ceremonies.

children.text: upasadāṃ ca payovratatvanimittaṃ sukhamasti /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Upasad</s> ceremonies too, there is pleasure arising from the milk-vow.

children.text: alpabhojanīyāni cāhānyāśvāsannānīti praśvāso 'to 'śanādīnāmupasadāṃ ca sāmānyam //2 //
children.translated_text: And they are days of sparse eating, providing comfort and relief — therefore there is a common feature between eating and the like and the <s>Upasad</s> ceremonies.

children.text: START ChUp 3,17.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.17.3]

children.text: atha yad dhasati yaj jakṣati yan maithunaṃ carati stutaśastrair eva tad eti || ChUp_3,17.3 ||
children.translated_text: Then when he laughs, when he feasts, when he engages in sexual union — these correspond to the <s>Stuta</s> and <s>Śastra</s> chants.

children.text: ChUpBh_3,17.3 atha yaddhasati yajjakṣati bhakṣayati yanmaithunaṃ carati stutaśasraireva tatsamānatāmeti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.17.3] Then when he laughs, when he eats (<s>jakṣati</s>, meaning partakes of food), when he engages in sexual union — these attain similarity with the <s>Stuta</s> and <s>Śastra</s> chants,

children.text: śabdavattvasāmānyāt //3 //
children.translated_text: because of the common feature of being accompanied by sound.

children.text: START ChUp 3,17.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.17.4]

children.text: atha yat tapo dānam ārjavam ahiṃsā satyavacanam iti tā asya dakṣiṇāḥ || ChUp_3,17.4 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>dāna</s> (charity), <s>ārjava</s> (uprightness), <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), and <s>satyavacana</s> (truthfulness) — these are his <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees).

children.text: ChUpBh_3,17.4 atha yattapo dānamārjavamahiṃsā satyavacanamiti tā asya dakṣiṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.17.4] Then <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>dāna</s> (charity), <s>ārjava</s> (uprightness), <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), and <s>satyavacana</s> (truthfulness) — these are his <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees),

children.text: dharmapuṣṭikaratvasāmānyāt //4 //
children.translated_text: because of the common feature of nourishing <s>dharma</s> (righteousness).

children.text: START ChUp 3,17.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.17.5]

children.text:
tasmād āhuḥ soṣyaty asoṣṭeti |
punar utpādanam evāsya tat |
maraṇam evāvabhṛthaḥ || ChUp_3,17.5 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say 'he will press' (<s>soṣyati</s>) and 'he has pressed' (<s>asoṣṭa</s>). The re-birth [of a person] is that [pressing]. Death itself is the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath).

children.text: ChUpBh_3,17.5 yasmācca yajñaḥ puraṣastasmāttaṃ janayiṣyati mātā yadā tadā'huranye soṣyatīti tasya mātaraṃ yadā ca prasūtā bhavati tadāsoṣṭa pūrṇiketi vidhiyajña iva soṣyati somaṃ devadatto 'soṣṭa somaṃ yajñadatta iti, ataḥ śabdasāmānyādvā puruṣo yajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.17.5] And since the person is a sacrifice, therefore when his mother is about to give birth to him, others say 'she will press' (<s>soṣyati</s>), and when she has given birth, 'she has pressed' (<s>asoṣṭa</s>) — just as in the ritual sacrifice [they say] '<s>Devadatta</s> will press the <s>Soma</s>' and '<s>Yajñadatta</s> has pressed the <s>Soma</s>.' Therefore, on account of the similarity of expression, the person is a sacrifice.

children.text: punarutpādanamevāsya tatpuruṣākhyasya yajñasya yatsoṣyatyasoṣṭeti śabdasambandhitvaṃ vidhiyajñasyeva /
children.translated_text: The re-birth is indeed that — of this sacrifice called the person — namely the connection with the expressions 'he will press' and 'he has pressed,' just as in the ritual sacrifice.

children.text: kiñca tanmaraṇamevāsya puruṣayajñasyāvabhṛthaḥ samāptisāmānyāt //5 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, death itself is the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) of this <s>puruṣa</s>-sacrifice, because of the common feature of being the conclusion.

children.text: START ChUp 3,17.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.17.6]

children.text:
tad dhaitad ghora āṅgirasaḥ kṛṣṇāya devakīputrāyoktvovāca |
apipāsa eva sa babhūva |
so 'ntavelāyām etat trayaṃ pratipadyetākṣitam asy acyutam asi prāṇasaṃśitam asīti |
tatraite dve ṛcau bhavataḥ || ChUp_3,17.6 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ghora Āṅgirasa</s> taught this to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Devakī</s>, and having taught it, said: At the final hour, one should take refuge in these three [utterances]: 'You are the imperishable (<s>akṣita</s>), you are the unshakable (<s>acyuta</s>), you are sharpened by <s>prāṇa</s> (<s>prāṇasaṃśita</s>).' Regarding this, there are two <s>Ṛc</s> verses.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,17.6 taddhaitadyajñadarśanaṃ ghoro nāmata āṅgiraso gotrataḥ kṛṣṇāya devakīputrāya śiṣyāyokatvovāca tadetattrayamityādivyavahitena sambandhaḥ /
sa caitaddarśanaṃ śrutvāpipāsa evāmyābhyo vidyābhyo babhūva /
itthaṃ ca viśiṣṭeyaṃ vidyā yatkṛṣṇasya devakīputrasyānyāṃ vidyāṃ prati tṛḍvicchedakarīti puruṣayajñavidyāṃ stauti /
ghora āṅgirasaḥ kṛṣṇāyoktvemāṃ vidyāṃ kimuvāceti tadāha-sa evaṃ yathoktayajñavidantavelāyāṃ maraṇakāla etanmantratrayaṃ pratipadyeta japedityarthaḥ /
kiṃ tadakṣitamakṣīṇamakṣataṃ vāsītyekaṃ yajuḥ sāmarthyādādityasthaṃ prāṇaṃ caikīkṛtyā'ha /
tathā tamevā'hācyutaṃ svarūpādapracyutamasīti dvitīyaṃ yajuḥ /
prāṇasaṃśitaṃ prāṇaśca sa saṃśitaṃ samyaktanūkṛtaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ tattvamasīti tṛtīyaṃ yajuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Sharpened by <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>prāṇasaṃśita</s>) — it is <s>prāṇa</s>, and it is sharpened (<s>saṃśita</s>), well refined and subtle — 'that you are' — this is the third <s>Yajus</s>.

children.text: tatraitasminnarthe vidyāstutipare dve ṛcau mantrau bhavato na japārthe /
children.translated_text: In this context, for the purpose of praising this knowledge, there are two <s>Ṛc</s> verses (mantras), not for the purpose of recitation.

children.text: trayaṃ pratipadyeteti tritvasaṃkhyābādhanāt /
children.translated_text: Because the statement 'one should take refuge in these three' limits the number to three,

children.text: pañcasaṃkhyā hi tadā syāt //6 //
children.translated_text: for otherwise the number would become five.

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 3.17.6] This vision of sacrifice — <s>Ghora</s> by name, <s>Āṅgirasa</s> by lineage — taught to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Devakī</s>, who was his disciple, and having taught it said 'these three' and so on — this connects with what follows after an interval. And he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), having heard this teaching, became free from thirst (<s>apipāsa</s>) — [that is, free from desire] for any other knowledge. This knowledge is thus distinguished in that it quenched the thirst of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Devakī</s>, for any other knowledge — thus the <s>puruṣa</s>-sacrifice knowledge is praised. What did <s>Ghora Āṅgirasa</s> say to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> after teaching this knowledge? To this he replies: One who knows the sacrifice as described above, at the final hour — at the time of death — should take refuge in, should recite, these three <s>Yajus</s> formulas. What are they? 'You are the imperishable (<s>akṣita</s>) — the undiminished, the uninjured' — this is one <s>Yajus</s>, which by implication addresses <s>Prāṇa</s> as established in <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), unifying them. Similarly, he says to that same [<s>Prāṇa</s>]: 'You are the unshakable (<s>acyuta</s>) — unfallen from your own nature' — this is the second <s>Yajus</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,17.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.17.7]

children.text:
ādit pratnasya retasaḥ |
ud vayaṃ tamasaspari |
jyotiḥ paśyanta uttaram |
svaḥ paśyanta uttaram |
devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotir uttamam iti jyotir uttamam iti || ChUp_3,17.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'From the ancient seed, beyond the darkness, we perceive the higher light; perceiving the higher heaven, we have reached <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), the god among the gods, the supreme light' — the supreme light.

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,17.7 ādidityatrā'kārasyānubandhastakāro 'narthaka icchabdaśca /
pratnasya cirantanasya purāṇasyetyarthaḥ /
retasaḥ kāraṇasya bījabhūtasya jagataḥ sadākhyasya jyotiḥ prakāśaṃ paśyanti /
āśabda utsṛṣṭānubandhaḥ paśyantītyanena sambadhyate /
kiṃ tajjayotiḥ paśyanti /
vāsaramaharahariva tatsarvato vyāptaṃ brahmaṇo jyotiḥ /
nivṛttacakṣuṣo brahmavido brahmacaryādinivṛttisādhanaiḥ śuddhāntaḥkaraṇā ā samantato jyotiḥ paśyantītyarthaḥ /
paraḥ paramiti liṅgavyatyayena, jyotiṣparatvāt /
yadidhyate dīpyate divi dyotanavati pasminbrahmaṇi vartamānam /
yena jyotiṣeddhaḥ savitā tapati candramā bhāti vidyudvidyotate grahatārāgaṇā vibhāsante /
kiñcānyo mantradṛgāha yathoktaṃ jyotiḥ paśyan /
udvayaṃ tamaso 'jñānalakṣaṇātpari parastāditi śeṣaḥ /
tamaso vāpanetṛ yajjayotiruttaramādityasthaṃ paripaśyanto vayamudaganmeti vyavahitena sambandhaḥ /
tajjyotiḥ svaḥ svamātmīyamasmaddhṛdi sthitam /
ādityasthaṃ ca tadekaṃ jyotiḥ /
yaduttaramutkṛṣṭataramūrdhvataraṃ vāparaṃ jyotirapekṣya paśyanta udaganma vayam /
kamudaganmetyāha /
children.translated_text: Who has ascended? — he says:

children.text: devaṃ dyotanavantaṃ devatrā deveṣu sarveṣu sūryaṃ rasānāṃ raśmīnāṃ prāṇānāṃ ca jagata īraṇātsūryastamudaganma gatavanto jyotiruttamaṃ sarvajyotirbhya utkṛṣṭatamamaho prāptā vayamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The god' — the luminous one — [who is] 'among the gods' (devatrā), among all the gods — the sun (<s>Sūrya</s>), [so called] because of his propulsion (īraṇa) of juices (rasa), rays (raśmi), and vital forces (prāṇa) of the world — him we have ascended to, having reached the supreme light, the most excellent among all lights. 'We have attained' — this is the meaning.

children.text: idaṃ tajjyotiryadṛgbhyāṃ stutaṃ yadyajustrayeṇa prakāśitam /
children.translated_text: This is that light which was praised through the <s>Ṛc</s> verses and illuminated by the <s>Yajus</s> triad.

children.text: dvirabhyāso yajñakalpanāparisamāptyarthaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: The twofold repetition [of 'ya evaṃ veda'] is for the purpose of completing the conception of the [life as] sacrifice. (7)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 3.17.7:] In the beginning [of the verse], the 'ā' is a mere appendage to the 'a'-vowel, [and] the 'ta'-syllable is meaningless, as is the 'i'-particle. 'Pratna' means ancient, of long standing — this is the meaning. They see the light — the radiance — of the seed-nature, the causal, primordial world called 'Sat' (Being). The 'ā' prefix, freed from its augment, connects with 'paśyanti' (they see). What light do they see? That which pervades everything like daytime — that is the light of <s>Brahman</s>. Those who have withdrawn their [outer] senses, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, whose inner organs have been purified through the means of cessation such as <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and the like — they see the light from all sides, completely — this is the meaning. 'Paraḥ param' — [there is] a transposition of gender, because the light is supreme. That which is meditated upon, which shines in the luminous heaven — existing in that <s>Brahman</s>. By that light, the sun (<s>Savitṛ</s>) blazes, the moon shines, lightning flashes, and the multitudes of planets and stars gleam. Moreover, another seer of mantras says, seeing the light as described: 'Upward, beyond the darkness' — characterized by ignorance — 'beyond' is to be supplied. [Or alternatively,] 'the remover of darkness' — 'seeing the supreme light stationed in the sun, we have ascended' — this is the connection with the separated [phrases]. That light is one's own (svaḥ), belonging to oneself, situated in our heart. And the light stationed in the sun is that very same one light. Seeing that which is higher — more excellent, or more elevated — compared to the other, lower light, 'we have ascended.'

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasya saptadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,18.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.18.1]

children.text:
mano brahmety upāsīta |
ity adhyātmam |
athādhidaivatam |
ākāśo brahma |
ity ubhayam ādiṣṭaṃ bhavaty adhyātmaṃ cādhidaivataṃ ca || ChUp_3,18.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'One should meditate on the mind as <s>Brahman</s>' — this is with reference to the individual self (adhyātma). Now with reference to the divinities (adhidaivata): '<s>Ākāśa</s> (space) is <s>Brahman</s>.' Thus both are instructed — with reference to the individual self and with reference to the divinities. (ChUp 3.18.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,18.1 manomaya īśvara ukta ākāśātmeti ca brahmaṇo guṇaikadeśatvena /
athedānīṃ mana ākāśayoḥ samastabrahmadṛṣṭividhānārtha ārambho mano brahmetyādi /
mano manute 'nenetyantaḥkaraṇaṃ tadbrahma paramityupāsīteti etadātmaviṣayaṃ darśanamadhyātmam /
athādhidaivataṃ devatāviṣayamidaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ /
ākāśo brahmetyupāsīta /
evamabhuyamadhyātmamadhidaivataṃ cobhayaṃ brahmadṛṣṭiviṣayamādiṣṭamupadiṣṭaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus both — the adhyātma and the adhidaivata — both being objects of the vision of <s>Brahman</s>, have been instructed, taught.

children.text: ākāśamanasoḥ sūkṣmatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the subtlety of space and mind.

children.text: manasopalabhyatvācca brahmaṇo yogyaṃ mano brahmadṛṣṭeḥ /
children.translated_text: And because <s>Brahman</s> is apprehended by the mind, the mind is fit for the vision of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ākāśaśca sarvagatatvātsūkṣmatvādupādhihīnatvācca //1 //
children.translated_text: And space, because of its all-pervasiveness, subtlety, and freedom from limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>). (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.18.1:] The manomaya (mind-made) Lord has been mentioned, and <s>Brahman</s> [has been described] as having space as its self — but only as a partial attribute of <s>Brahman</s>. Now, for the purpose of prescribing the complete vision of <s>Brahman</s> through mind and space, this [section] beginning with 'One should meditate on the mind as <s>Brahman</s>' commences. The mind — the inner organ by which one thinks — that is <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme — one should meditate thus. This vision pertaining to the self is the adhyātma (individual) aspect. Now we shall state the adhidaivata (divine) aspect, pertaining to the divinities: 'One should meditate on <s>ākāśa</s> (space) as <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: START ChUp 3,18.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.18.2]

children.text:
tad etac catuṣpād brahma |
vāk pādaḥ prāṇaḥ pādaś cakṣuḥ pādaḥ śrotraṃ pādaḥ |
ity adhyātmam |
athādhidaivatam |
agniḥ pādo vāyuḥ pāda ādityaḥ pādo diśaḥ pādaḥ |
ity ubhayam evādiṣṭaṃ bhavaty adhyātmaṃ cādhidaivataṃ ca || ChUp_3,18.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Brahman</s> has four feet. Speech is one foot, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is one foot, the eye is one foot, the ear is one foot — this is with reference to the individual self (adhyātma). Now with reference to the divinities (adhidaivata): <s>Agni</s> (fire) is one foot, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is one foot, <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is one foot, the directions are one foot. Thus both are instructed — with reference to the individual self and with reference to the divinities.' (ChUp 3.18.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,18.2 tadetanmana ākhyaṃ catuṣpādbrahma, catvāraḥ pādā asyeti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.18.2:] This <s>Brahman</s> called 'mind' has four feet — meaning it has four quarters.

children.text: kathaṃ catuṣpāttvaṃ manaso brahmaṇa ityāha-vākprāṇaścakṣuḥ śrotramityete pādā ityadhyātmam /
children.translated_text: How is the mind as <s>Brahman</s> four-footed? — He says: speech, <s>prāṇa</s>, eye, and ear — these are its feet. This is the adhyātma aspect.

children.text: athādhidaivatamākāśasya brahmaṇo 'gnirvāyurādityo diśa ityete /
children.translated_text: Now the adhidaivata aspect: of <s>Brahman</s> as space — <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and the directions — these [are its feet].

children.text: evamubhayameva catuṣpādbrahmā'diṣṭaṃ bhavatyadhyātmaṃ caivādhidaivataṃ ca //2 //
children.translated_text: Thus both — the four-footed <s>Brahman</s> — have been instructed, both the adhyātma and the adhidaivata. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 3,18.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.18.3]

children.text:
vāg eva brahmaṇaś caturthaḥ pādaḥ |
so 'gninā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca |
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,18.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Speech alone is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>. It shines and blazes with the light of <s>Agni</s>. He who knows thus shines and blazes with fame, renown, and the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcas</s>).' (ChUp 3.18.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,18.3 tatra vāgeva manaso brahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pāda itarapādatrayāpekṣayā /
vācā hi pādeneva gavādi vaktavyaviṣayaṃ prati pratiṣṭhati /
ato manasaḥ pāda iva vāk /
tathā prāṇo ghrāṇaḥ pādaḥ /
tenāpi gandhaviṣayaṃ prati caṅkramati /
tathā cakṣuḥ pādaḥ śrotraṃ pāda ityevamadhyātmaṃ catuṣpāttavaṃ manaso brahmaṇaḥ /
athādhidaivatamagnivāyvādityadiśa ākāśasya brahmaṇa udāra iva goḥ pādā vilagnā upalabhyante /
tena tasyā'kāśasyāgnyādayaḥ pādā ucyante /
evamubhayamadhyātmaṃ caivādhidaivataṃ catuṣpādādiṣṭaṃ bhavati /
tatra vāgeva manaso brahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, speech alone is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s> as mind.

children.text: so 'gninādhidaivatena jyotiṣā bhāti ca dīpyate tapati ca santāpaṃ cauṣṇyaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: It shines — is luminous — and blazes — produces heat and warmth — with <s>Agni</s>, the corresponding divinity, as its light.

children.text: athavā tailaghṛtādyāgneyāśaneneddhā vāgbhāti ca tapati ca vadanāyotsāhavatī syādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, speech, kindled by <s>Agni</s>-natured nourishment such as oil, ghee, and the like, shines and blazes — meaning it becomes enthusiastic for speaking, this is the sense.

children.text: vidvatphalaṃ bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ yathoktaṃ vedaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: The fruit for the knower: he shines and blazes with fame, renown, and the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcas</s>) — he who knows thus, as described. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.18.3:] In this context, speech alone is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s> as mind — 'fourth' in relation to the other three feet. For just as [a cow] stands firm with respect to cows and other objects to be spoken about by means of speech as a foot, so speech is like a foot of the mind. Likewise, <s>prāṇa</s> — the sense of smell — is a foot; by it too, one moves toward the domain of scent. Similarly, the eye is a foot and the ear is a foot — thus is the four-footedness of the mind as <s>Brahman</s> in the adhyātma aspect. Now the adhidaivata aspect: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and the directions — like the udder of a cow — are observed as feet attached to space as <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, <s>Agni</s> and the others are called the feet of that space. Thus both — the adhyātma and the adhidaivata — the four-footed [<s>Brahman</s>] has been instructed.

children.text: START ChUp 3,18.4-6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.18.4-6]

children.text:
prāṇa eva brahmaṇaś caturthaḥ pādaḥ |
sa vāyunā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca |
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,18.4 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) alone is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>. It shines and blazes with the light of <s>Vāyu</s>. He who knows thus shines and blazes with fame, renown, and the splendor of sacred knowledge.' (ChUp 3.18.4)

children.text:
cakṣur eva brahmaṇaś caturthaḥ pādaḥ |
sa ādityena jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca |
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,18.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'The eye alone is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>. It shines and blazes with the light of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). He who knows thus shines and blazes with fame, renown, and the splendor of sacred knowledge.' (ChUp 3.18.5)

children.text:
śrotram eva brahmaṇaś caturthaḥ pādaḥ |
sa digbhir jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca |
bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_3,18.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'The ear alone is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>. It shines and blazes with the light of the directions. He who knows thus shines and blazes with fame, renown, and the splendor of sacred knowledge — he who knows thus.' (ChUp 3.18.6)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,18.4,5,6 tathā prāṇa eva brahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ /
sa vāyunā gandhāya bhāti ca tapati ca /
children.translated_text: It shines and blazes with <s>Vāyu</s> — for the apprehension of scent.

children.text: tatā cakṣurādityena rūpagrahaṇāya śrotraṃ digbhiḥ śabdagrahaṇāya /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the eye [shines and blazes] with <s>Āditya</s> for the apprehension of form; the ear with the directions for the apprehension of sound.

children.text: vidyāphalaṃ samānaṃ sarvatra brahmasampattiradṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ ya evaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: The fruit of this knowledge is the same everywhere — attainment of the state of <s>Brahman</s> is the unseen fruit for him who knows thus.

children.text: dviruktirdarśanasamāptyarthā //4-6 //
children.translated_text: The twofold repetition [of 'ya evaṃ veda'] is for the purpose of completing the meditation. (4-6)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.18.4-6:] Likewise, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) alone is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasyāṣṭādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 3,19.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.19.1]

children.text:
ādityo brahmety ādeśaḥ |
tasyopavyākhyānam |
asad evedam agra āsīt |
tat sad āsīt |
tat samabhavat |
tad āṇḍaṃ niravartata |
tat saṃvatsarasya mātrām aśayata |
tan nirabhidyata |
te āṇḍakapāle rajataṃ ca suvarṇaṃ cābhavatām || ChUp_3,19.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is <s>Brahman</s>' — this is the teaching. Its elaboration [is as follows]: In the beginning, this [universe] was indeed non-existent (asat). That became existent (sat). That came into being. That turned into an egg (āṇḍa). It lay for the measure of a year. It split open. The two halves of the eggshell became silver and gold. (ChUp 3.19.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,19.1 ādityo brahmaṇaḥ pāda ukta iti tasminsakalabrahmadṛṣṭyarthamidamārabhyate-ādityo brahmetyādeśa upadeśastasyopavyākhyānaṃ kriyate stutyartham /
asadavyakṛtanāmarūpamidaṃ jagadaśeṣamagre prāgavasthāyāmutpatterāsīnna tvasadeva /
kathamasataḥ sajjāyetetyasatkāryatvasya pratiṣedhāt /
nanvihāsadeveti vidhānādvikalpaḥ syāt /
na, kriyāsviva vastuni vikalpānupapatteḥ /
kathaṃ tarhīdamasadeveti /
nanvavocāmāvyākṛtanāmarūpatvādasadivāsaditi /
nanvevaśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ /
satyamevaṃ, na tu sattvābhāvamavadhārayati /
kiṃ tarhi?vyākṛtanāmarūpābhāvamavadhārayati nāmarūpavyākṛtaviṣaye sacchabdaprayogo dṛṣṭaḥ /
tacca nāmarūpavyākaraṇamādityāyattaṃ prāyaśo jagataḥ tadabhāve hyandhaṃ tama idaṃ na prajñāyeta kiñcanetyatastatstutipare vākye sadapīdaṃ rājñaḥ kulaṃ sarvaguṇasampanne pūrṇavarmaṇi rājanyasatīti tadvat /
na ca sattvamasattvaṃ veha jagataḥ pratipipādayiṣitamādityo brahmetyādeśaparatvāt /
upasaṃhariṣyatyanta ādityaṃ brahmetyupāsta iti /
tatsadāsīttadasacchabdavācyaṃ prāgutpatteḥ stimitamanispandamasadiva satkāryābhimukhamīṣadupajātapravṛtti sadāsīttato labdhaparispandaṃ tatsamabhavadalpataranāmarūpavyākaraṇenāṅkurībhūtami va bījam /
tato 'pi krameṇa sthūlībhavattadadbhya āṇḍaṃ samavartata saṃvṛttam /
āṇḍamiti dairdhyaṃ chāndasam /
children.translated_text: The [lengthened form] 'āṇḍa' [for 'aṇḍa'] is a Vedic irregularity in vowel length.

children.text: tadaṇḍaṃ saṃvatsarasya kālasya prasiddhasya mātrāṃ parimāṇamabhinnasvarūpamevāśayata sthitaṃ babhūva /
children.translated_text: That egg lay for the measure — the extent — of a well-known year, remaining with its nature undivided.

children.text: tattataḥ saṃvatsaraparimāṇātkālādūrdhvaṃ nirabhidyata nirbhinnaṃ vayasāmivāṇḍam /
children.translated_text: Then, after the period measuring a year, it split open — was broken, like the egg of a bird.

children.text: tasya nirbhinnasyāṇḍasya kapāle dve rajataṃ ca suvarṇaṃ cābhavatāṃ saṃvṛtte //1 //
children.translated_text: Of that broken egg, the two shell-halves became silver and gold. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.19.1:] Since <s>Āditya</s> has been mentioned as a foot of <s>Brahman</s>, for the purpose of prescribing the vision of the complete <s>Brahman</s> in him, this [section] commences: '<s>Āditya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — this is the teaching (ādeśa), the instruction. Its elaboration is made for the purpose of praise. 'This entire universe, with its names and forms unmanifest (avyākṛta), was non-existent (asat) in the beginning — in its prior state, before creation — it was not [absolutely] non-existent, however.' Why? Because of the refutation of the doctrine that the effect is non-existent [before its production] — 'How can the existent be born from the non-existent?' [One might object:] 'But here [the text says] asat eva with the particle eva indicating restriction.' [Reply:] No, because restriction does not apply to a thing [an ontological reality] as it does to [ritual] actions. 'Then how [should we understand] this was asat eva?' We have already said: because of its names and forms being unmanifest, [it was] as if non-existent — hence [called] non-existent. [Objection:] 'But the particle eva has a restrictive sense.' True, but it does not restrict [away] the existence [of the thing]. What then? It restricts [away] the manifestation of names and forms — [for] the usage of the word sat (existent) is seen [only] with respect to what has manifest names and forms. And that manifestation of names and forms is mostly dependent on <s>Āditya</s>; for in its absence, 'blind darkness [would prevail], nothing would be discerned' — therefore, in a statement whose purpose is the praise of [<s>Āditya</s>], even an existent [entity is called non-existent], like [saying] 'this family too is [as if] non-existent without the excellent king <s>Pūrṇavarman</s>' — similarly. And here neither the existence nor non-existence of the world is intended to be established, because the [text's] purpose is the teaching '<s>Āditya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' [The text] will conclude: 'One should meditate on <s>Āditya</s> as <s>Brahman</s>.' That which was denoted by the word asat — before creation, quiescent, motionless, as if non-existent — being oriented toward [producing] the effect (satkāryābhimukham), with activity slightly commenced — 'was sat' (became existent). Then, having attained momentum, it came into being (samabhavat) — like a seed beginning to sprout, with a slight manifestation of names and forms. Then, progressively becoming grosser, from that [emerged] the egg — it came about, was formed.

children.text: START ChUp 3,19.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.19.2]

children.text:
tad yad rajataṃ seyaṃ pṛthivī |
yat suvarṇaṃ sā dyauḥ |
yaj jarāyu te parvatāḥ |
yad ulbaṃ (sa) samegho nīhāraḥ |
yā dhamanayas tā nadyaḥ |
yad vāsteyam udakaṃ sa samudraḥ || ChUp_3,19.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which was silver — that is this earth. That which was gold — that is heaven. The outer membrane (jarāyu) — those are the mountains. The inner membrane (ulba) — that is cloud and mist. The veins (dhamanī) — those are the rivers. The fluid within (vāsteya udaka) — that is the ocean.' (ChUp 3.19.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,19.2 tattayoḥ kapālayoryadrajataṃ kapālamāsītseyaṃ pṛthivī pṛthivyupalakṣitamadho 'ṇḍakapālamityarthaḥ /
yatsuvarṇaṃ kapālaṃ sā dyaurdyulokopalakṣitamūrdhvaṃ kapālamityarthaḥ /
yajjarāyu garbhapariveṣṭanaṃ sthūlamaṇḍasya dviśakalībhāvakāla āsītte parvatā babhūvuḥ /
children.translated_text: The outer membrane (jarāyu) — the thick covering around the embryo — [which was present] at the time of the egg splitting into two halves — those became the mountains.

children.text: yadulvaṃ sūkṣmaṃ garbhapariveṣṭanaṃ tatsaha medyaiḥ samegho nīhāro 'vaśyāyo babhūvetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The inner membrane (ulba) — the thin covering around the embryo — that, together with fat, became cloud and mist (nīhāra, hoarfrost), is the meaning.

children.text: yā garbhasya jātasya dehe dhamanayaḥ śirāstā nadyo babhūvuḥ /
children.translated_text: The veins (dhamanī) — the channels in the body of the embryo once born — those became the rivers.

children.text: yattasya bastau bhavaṃ vāsteyamudakaṃ sa samudraḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: The fluid contained in its bladder — the vāsteya water — that [became] the ocean. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.19.2:] Of those two shell-halves, that which was the silver half — that is this earth; meaning the lower eggshell, indicated by the earth, is the sense. That which was the gold half — that is heaven; meaning the upper eggshell, indicated by the celestial world, is the sense.

children.text: START ChUp 3,19.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.19.3]

children.text:
atha yat tad ajāyata so 'sāv ādityaḥ |
taṃ jāyamānaṃ ghoṣā ulūlavo 'nūdatiṣṭhant sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ |
tasmāt tasyodayaṃ prati pratyāyanaṃ prati ghoṣā ulūlavo 'nūttiṣṭhanti sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ || ChUp_3,19.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that which was born [from the egg] — that is this sun (<s>Āditya</s>). When it was being born, shouts and cries of joy arose, as did all beings and all desires. Therefore, at its rising and at its return, shouts and cries of joy arise, as do all beings and all desires.' (ChUp 3.19.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_3,19.3 atha yattadajāyata garbharūpaṃ tasminnaṇḍe so 'sāvādityastamādityaṃ jāyamānaṃ ghoṣāḥ śabdā ulūlava urūravo vistīrṇaravā udatiṣṭhannutthitavanta īśvarasyeveha prathamaputrajanmani sarvāṇi ca sthāvarajaṅgamāni bhūtāni sarve ca teṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ kāmāḥ kāmyanta iti viṣayāḥ strīvasrānnādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.19.3:] Now, that which was born in that egg in embryonic form — that is this sun (<s>Āditya</s>). When that <s>Āditya</s> was being born, shouts — sounds — and cries of joy (ulūlava) — widespread roars, extended cries — arose, like [the celebration] here in this world at the birth of the first son of a lord; and all beings, movable and immovable, and all the desires (kāma) of those beings — meaning the objects of desire: women, garments, food, and the like.

children.text: yasmādādityajanmanimittā bhūtakāmotpattistasmādadyatve 'pi tasyā'dityasyodayaṃ prati pratyāyanaṃ pratyastagamanaṃ ca pratyathavā punaḥ punaḥ pratyāgamanaṃ pratyāyanaṃ tatprati tannimittīkṛtyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the arising of beings and desires was occasioned by the birth of <s>Āditya</s>, therefore even now, at the rising of that <s>Āditya</s>, and at its return — its setting — or alternatively, 'pratyāyana' means its coming again and again — with respect to that, meaning occasioned by that, is the sense.

children.text: sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmā ghoṣā ulūlavaścānūttiṣṭhanti /
children.translated_text: All beings and all desires, together with shouts and cries of joy, arise.

children.text: prasiddhaṃ hyetadudayādau savituḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: For this is well known — [happening] at the time of the rising of the sun. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 3,19.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.19.4]

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān ādityaṃ brahmety upāste |
abhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo ghoṣā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nimreḍeran nimreḍeran || ChUp_3,19.4 ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, meditates on the sun as <s>Brahman</s> — it is likely that auspicious sounds will come to him and delight him, delight him. (<s>ChUp</s> 3.19.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_3,19.4 sa yaḥ kaścidetamevaṃ yathoktamahimānaṃ vidvānsannādityaṃ brahmetyupāste sa tadbhāvaṃ pratipadyata ityarthaḥ /
kiñca dṛṣṭaṃ phalamabhyāśaḥ kṣipraṃ tadvido yaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇamenamevaṃvidaṃ sādhavaḥ /
śobhanā ghoṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: good sounds —

children.text: sādhutvaṃ ghoṣādīnāṃ yadupabhoge pāpānubandhābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: the goodness of sounds and such [means] the absence of sinful consequences in their enjoyment —

children.text: ā ca gaccheyurāgaccheyuścopa ca nimreḍerannupanimreḍeraṃśca na kevalamāgamanamātraṃ ghoṣāṇāmupasukhayeyuścopasukhaṃ ca kuryarityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'will come to him' means they will approach him, and 'will delight him' means they will not merely come but will bring him pleasure — they will make him happy — this is the meaning.

children.text: dvirabhyāso 'dhyāyaparisamāptyarthaḥ ādarārthaśca //4 //
children.translated_text: The repetition [of the word] is for the purpose of concluding the chapter and for emphasis. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 3.19.4:] He who — whoever — knowing thus, having understood its greatness as described, meditates on the sun as <s>Brahman</s>, attains identity with that — this is the meaning. Moreover, the visible fruit [is]: 'likely' means quickly; [this is] a modifier of the action, [meaning] that to this knower, auspicious [people] —

children.text: iti chāndogyopaniṣadi tṛtīyādhyāyasyaikonaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth section of the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadbrāhmaṇe tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: IN REE NICHT ZULÄSSIGE ZEICHEN:
children.translated_text: CONTAINS INVALID CHARACTERS:

children.text: atha caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the fourth chapter.

children.text: START ChUp 4,1.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.1

children.text:
jānaśrutir ha pautrāyaṇaḥ śraddhādeyo bahudāyī bahupākya āsa |
sa ha sarvata āvasathān māpayāṃ cakre sarvata eva me 'nnam atsyantīti || ChUp_4,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> was a man of faith, a generous giver, one who had much food cooked [for others]. He had rest-houses built everywhere, [thinking] 'Everywhere people shall eat my food.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,1.1 vāyuprāṇayorbrahmaṇaḥ pādadṛṣṭyadhyāsaḥ purastādvarṇitaḥ /
athedānīṃ tayoḥ sākṣādbrahmatvenopāsyatvāyottaramārabhyate /
sukhāvabodhārthā'khyāyikā, vidyādānagrahaṇavidhipradarśanārthā ca śraddhānnadānānuddhatatvādīnāṃ ca vidyāprāpti sādhanatvaṃ pradarśyata ākhyāyikayā /
jānaśrutirjanaśrutasyāpatyam /
haḥ aitihyārthaḥ /
putrasya pautraḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ sa eva śraddhādeyaḥ śraddhāpuraḥsarameva brāhmaṇādibhyo deyamasyeti śraddhādeyaḥ /
bahudāyī prabhūtaṃ dātuṃ śīlamasyeti bahudāyī /
bahupākyo bahu paktavyamahanyahani gṛhe yasyāsaubahupākyaḥ /
bhojanārthibhyo bahvasya gṛhe 'nnaṃ pacyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [This means] much food is cooked in his house for those who come seeking meals — this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṅguṇasampanno 'sau jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇo viśiṣṭe deśe kāle ca kasmiṃścidāsa babhūva /
children.translated_text: This <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s>, endowed with such qualities, was — existed — at a particular place and time.

children.text: sa ha sarvataḥ sarvāsu dikṣu grāmeṣu nagareṣu cā'vasathānetya vasanti yeṣvityāvasathāstānmāpayāñcakre kāritavānityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He had rest-houses built everywhere' — in all directions, in villages and cities, he had rest-houses — [places] where people come and stay — constructed, meaning he had them built.

children.text: sarvata eva me mamānnaṃ teṣvāvasatheṣu vasanto 'tsyanti bhokṣyanta ityevamabhiprāyaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: 'Everywhere people shall eat my food' — [meaning] those staying in those rest-houses will eat, will partake of [my food] — this was his intention. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.1.1:] The superimposition of the vision of a quarter of <s>Brahman</s> upon <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Prāṇa</s> has been described earlier. Now, for the purpose of [teaching] their meditation upon as <s>Brahman</s> directly, the subsequent [section] is begun. The narrative (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>) is for ease of understanding, and for demonstrating the injunction regarding the giving and receiving of knowledge, and that faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), food-giving (<s>annadāna</s>), humility, and such qualities are means for attaining knowledge — [all this] is shown through the narrative. <s>Jānaśruti</s> is the descendant of <s>Janaśruta</s>. The particle 'ha' indicates tradition. The grandson of a son [of <s>Janaśruta</s>] is <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>. He is 'of faith in giving' (<s>śraddhādeya</s>) — one whose giving to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others is always preceded by faith. 'A generous giver' (<s>bahudāyī</s>) — one whose habit is to give abundantly. 'One who has much cooked' (<s>bahupākya</s>) — one in whose house much is to be cooked every day.

children.text: START ChUp 4,1.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.2

children.text:
atha ha haṃsā niśāyām atipetuḥ |
tad dhaivaṃ haṃso haṃsam abhyuvāda |
ho ho 'yi bhallākṣa bhallākṣa jānaśruteḥ pautrāyaṇasya samaṃ divā jyotir ātataṃ tan mā prasāṅkṣīs tat tvāṃ mā pradhākṣīr iti || ChUp_4,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: Then, at night, <s>haṃsas</s> (geese) flew overhead. One <s>haṃsa</s> addressed another <s>haṃsa</s> thus: 'Ho ho! O <s>Bhallākṣa</s>, <s>Bhallākṣa</s>! The radiance of <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> has spread equal to the sky. Do not touch it, lest it burn you!' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,1.2 tatraivaṃ sati rājani tasmindharmakāle harmyatalasthe 'tha ha haṃsā niśāyāṃ rātrāvatipetuḥ /
ṛṣayo devatā vā rājño 'nnadānaguṇaistoṣitāḥ santo haṃsārūpā bhūtvā rājño darśanagocare 'tipetuḥ /
tattasminkāle teṣāṃ patatāṃ haṃsānāmekaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ patannagrataḥ patantaṃ haṃsamabhyuvādābhyuktavānho ho 'yīti bho bho iti sambodhya bhallākṣa bhallākṣetyādaraṃ darśayan yathā paśya paśyā'ścaryamiti tadvat /
bhallākṣeti mandadṛṣṭitvaṃ sūcayannāha /
athavā samyagbrahmadarśanābhimānavattvāttasyāsakṛdupālabdhastena pīḍyamāno 'marṣitayā tatsūcayati bhallākṣeti /
jānaśruteḥ pautrāyaṇasya samaṃ tulyaṃ divā dyulokena jyotiḥ prabhāsvaramannadānādijanitaprabhāvajamātataṃ vyāptaṃ dyulokaspṛgityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The radiance of <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s>' — equal to, the same as, heaven; 'radiance' means brilliance born of the power generated by food-giving and such [meritorious acts]; 'spread' means pervading, reaching to the heavenly realm — this is the meaning.

children.text: divāhnā vā samaṃ jyotirityetat /
children.translated_text: Or, the radiance [is] equal to the daytime — this is what is meant.

children.text: tanmā prasāṅkṣīḥ sañjanaṃ saktiṃ tena jyotiṣā sambandhaṃ mā kārṣīrityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do not touch it' — do not make contact, do not become connected with that radiance — this is the meaning.

children.text: tatprasañjanena tajjyotistvā tvāṃ mā pradhākṣīrmā dahatvityarthaḥ puruṣavyatyanena mā pradhākṣīditi //2 //
children.translated_text: 'Lest it burn you' — lest that radiance, through [your] contact [with it], burn you — this is the meaning; with an exchange of grammatical person, [it says] 'lest it burn.' (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.1.2:] In that situation, when the king was on the terrace of his palace at that auspicious time, then at night <s>haṃsas</s> flew overhead. They were sages or deities who, being pleased with the king's qualities of food-giving, assumed the form of <s>haṃsas</s> and flew within the king's field of vision. At that time, while they were flying, one <s>haṃsa</s>, flying behind, addressed the one flying ahead: 'Ho ho!' — [meaning] 'O sir!' — addressing him thus, [and saying] '<s>Bhallākṣa</s>, <s>Bhallākṣa</s>!' — showing eagerness, as if saying 'Look, look at this wonder!' By [saying] '<s>Bhallākṣa</s>' (dim-sighted one), he indicates that the other has defective vision. Alternatively, because [the other] had the conceit of perfect vision of <s>Brahman</s>, having been repeatedly reproached by him, being afflicted and angered, [the speaker] indicates this by [calling him] '<s>Bhallākṣa</s>'.

children.text: START ChUp 4,1.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.3

children.text:
tam u ha paraḥ pratyuvāca kam v ara enam etat santaṃ sayugvānam iva raikvam āttha iti |
yo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva iti || ChUp_4,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: The other replied to him: 'Who indeed is this one that you speak of as if he were <s>Raikva</s> with the cart (<s>sayugvān</s>)?' 'How then is <s>Raikva</s> [called] the one with the cart (<s>sayugvān</s>)?' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,1.3 tamevamuktavantaṃ para itaro 'gragāmī pratyuvācāre nikṛṣṭo 'yaṃ rājā varākastaṃ kamu enaṃ santaṃ kena māhātmyena yuktaṃ santamiti kutsayatyenamevaṃ sabahumānametadvacanamāttha raikvamiva, sayugvānaṃ saha yugvanā gantryā vartata iti sayugvā raikvaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.1.3:] The other — the one who flew ahead — replied to the one who had spoken thus: 'This king is lowly, a wretch — who is this one, with what greatness is he endowed?' — thus disparaging him, [saying] 'you speak of him with such respect as if [he were] <s>Raikva</s>' — <s>sayugvān</s> means one who lives with a cart (<s>yugvanā</s>, a small vehicle), such is <s>Raikva</s>.

children.text: tamivā'tthainam /
children.translated_text: 'You speak of him as if [he were] that [<s>Raikva</s>].'

children.text: ananurūpamasminnayuktamīdṛśaṃ vaktuṃ raikva ivetyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The purport is: it is inappropriate and unfitting to speak thus about this [king] as if [he were] <s>Raikva</s>.

children.text: itaraścā'ha-yo nu kathaṃ tvayocyate sayugvā raikva ityuktavantaṃ bhallākṣa āha śṛṇu yathā sa raikvaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: And the other said: 'How is it that you call [him] <s>Raikva</s> with the cart (<s>sayugvān</s>)?' — [to which] the one addressed as <s>Bhallākṣa</s> said: 'Listen, [I shall tell you] how that <s>Raikva</s> [is so called].' (3)

children.text: START ChUp 4,1.4
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.4

children.text:
yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃca prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti |
yas tad veda yat sa veda sa mayaitad ukta iti || ChUp_4,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: Just as the lower throws in a game of dice all go to the winner who has thrown the highest (<s>kṛta</s>), so everything that creatures do that is good goes to him. Whoever knows what he knows — of him this has been said [by me]. (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,1.4 yathā loke kṛtāyaḥ kṛto nāmāyo dyūtasamaye prasiddhaścaturaṅkaḥ sa yadā jayati dyūte pravṛttānāṃ tasmai vijitāya tadarthamitare tridvyekāṅkā adhare 'yāstretādvāparakalināmānaḥ saṃyanti saṃgacchante 'ntarbhavanti /
caturaṅke kṛtāye tridvyekāṅkānāṃ vidyamānatvāttadantarbhavantītyarthaḥ /
yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭānta evamenaṃ raikvaṃ kṛtāyasthānīyaṃ tretādyāyasthānīyaṃ sarvaṃ tadabhisametyantarbhavati raikve /
kiṃ tadyatkiñca loke sarvāḥ prajāḥ sādhu śobhanaṃ dharmajātaṃ kurvanti tatsarvaṃ raikvasya dharme 'ntarbhavati /
tasya ca phale sarvaprāṇidharmaphalamantarbhavatītyarthaḥ /
tathānyo 'pi kaścidyastadvedyaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: Likewise, anyone else who knows what is to be known —

children.text: kiṃ tadyadvedyaṃ sa raikvo veda /
children.translated_text: what is that which is to be known? [It is] what <s>Raikva</s> knows.

children.text: tadvedyamanyo 'pi yo veda tamapi sarvaprāṇidharmajātaṃ tatphalaṃ ca raikvamivābhisametītyanuvartate /
children.translated_text: Whoever else also knows that which is to be known, to him too all the merit of all beings and its fruit converge, just as to <s>Raikva</s> — this continues [from above].

children.text: sa evaṃbhūto mayā vidvānetadikta evamukto raikvavatsa eva kṛtāyasthānīyo bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: 'Such a one has been spoken of by me as a knower' — [meaning] the one thus spoken of, like <s>Raikva</s>, holds the position of the <s>kṛta</s> throw. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.1.4:] Just as in the world, the <s>kṛta</s> — the well-known four-count [throw] in a dice game — when it wins, the other [throws] — the three, two, and one-count [throws] named <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s> — which are the lower throws, go to, converge upon, become absorbed in that winning [throw]. Because in the four-count <s>kṛta</s> throw, the three, two, and one-count [throws] are already contained — this is the meaning. Just as this illustration [shows], so to this <s>Raikva</s>, who holds the position of the <s>kṛta</s> throw, all that [merit] which holds the position of the <s>Tretā</s> and other throws converges upon, becomes absorbed in <s>Raikva</s>. What is that? Whatever all creatures in the world do that is good — all virtuous acts — all of that becomes absorbed in <s>Raikva's</s> merit. And the fruit of the merit of all beings becomes absorbed in his fruit — this is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 4,1.5-6
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.5-6

children.text:
tad u ha jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇa upaśuśrāva |
sa ha saṃjihāna eva kṣattāram uvācāṅgāre ha sayugvānam iva raikvam āttheti |
yo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva iti || ChUp_4,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> overheard this. Rising up [from his bed], he said to his attendant (<s>kṣattā</s>): 'My dear, you speak of [him] as if [he were] <s>Raikva</s> with the cart (<s>sayugvān</s>)!' 'How then is <s>Raikva</s> [called] the one with the cart (<s>sayugvān</s>)?' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.5)

children.text:
yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃca prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti |
yas tad veda yat sa veda sa mayaitad ukta iti || ChUp_4,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: Just as the lower throws in a game of dice all go to the winner who has thrown the highest (<s>kṛta</s>), so everything that creatures do that is good goes to him. Whoever knows what he knows — of him this has been said [by me]. (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,1.5,6 tadu ha tadetadīdṛśaṃ haṃsavākyamātmanaḥ kutsārūpamanyasya viduṣo raikvādeḥ praśaṃsārūpamupaśuśrāva śrutavānharmyatalastho rājā jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ /
tacca haṃsavākyaṃ smaranneva paunaḥ punyena rātriśeṣamativāhayāmāsa /
tataḥ sa bandibhī rājā stutiyuktābhirvāgbhiḥ pratibodhyamāna uvāca kṣattāraṃ saṃjihāna eva śayanaṃ nidrāṃ vā parityajanneva he 'ṅga vatsāre sa sayugvānamiva raikvamāttha kiṃ mām /
sa eva stutyarhe nāhamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The purport is: 'He alone [<s>Raikva</s>] is worthy of praise, not I.'

children.text: athavā sayugvānaṃ raikvamāttha gatvā mama taddidṛkṣā;tadevaśabdo 'vadhāraṇārtho 'narthako vā vācyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, 'You speak of <s>Raikva</s> with the cart' [means]: 'Go and [bring him, for] I wish to see him.' In this case, the particle 'eva' is either emphatic or semantically redundant.

children.text: sa ca kṣattā pratyuvāca raikvānayanakāmo rājño 'bhiprāyajño yo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva iti, rājñaivaṃ cokta ānetuṃ taccihnaṃ jñatumicchanyo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva ityavocat /
children.translated_text: And the attendant (<s>kṣattā</s>), desiring to bring <s>Raikva</s> and knowing the king's intention, replied: 'How then is <s>Raikva</s> [called] the one with the cart?' — the king having thus spoken, [the attendant,] wishing to find out the identifying mark in order to fetch him, said: 'How then is <s>Raikva</s> the one with the cart?'

children.text: sa ca bhallākṣavacanamevāvocat //5-6 //
children.translated_text: And [the king] repeated the very words of <s>Bhallākṣa</s>. (5-6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.1.5-6:] This speech of the <s>haṃsas</s> — which was in the form of disparagement of himself and praise of another knower, <s>Raikva</s> and others — <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s>, the king, heard while on the terrace of his palace. And remembering that speech of the <s>haṃsas</s>, he spent the rest of the night in repeated contemplation. Then, being awakened by the bards (<s>bandins</s>) with eulogy-laden words, he said to his attendant (<s>kṣattā</s>), even as he was rising — abandoning his bed or sleep — 'O my dear boy! You speak of <s>Raikva</s> with the cart — but what about me?'

children.text: START ChUp 4,1.7
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.7

children.text:
sa ha kṣattānviṣya nāvidam iti pratyeyāya |
taṃ hovāca yatrāre brāhmaṇasyānveṣaṇā tad enam arccheti || ChUp_4,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: The attendant (<s>kṣattā</s>), having searched, returned saying 'I could not find him.' [The king] said to him: 'Where a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> would be sought, go and look for him there.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.7)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,1.7 tasya smaransa ha kṣattā nagaraṃ grāmaṃ vā gatvānviṣya raikvaṃ nāvidaṃ na vyajñāsiṣamiti pratyeyāya pratyāgatavān /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.1.7:] Remembering [the king's words], the attendant, having gone to the city or village and searched for <s>Raikva</s>, returned saying 'I could not find him — I could not identify him.'

children.text: taṃ hovāca kṣattaramare yatra brāhmaṇasya brahmavida ekānte 'raṇye nadīpulinādau vivikte deśe 'nveṣaṇānumārgaṇaṃ bhavati tattatrainaṃ raikvamarcha ṛccha gaccha tatra mārgaṇaṃ kurvityarthaḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: The king said to the attendant: 'My dear, where a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — a knower of <s>Brahman</s> — is to be sought, in a solitary place, a forest, a riverbank, or a secluded spot — search for him there. Go there, seek him out, and look for him there — this is the meaning.' (7)

children.text: START ChUp 4,1.8
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.8

children.text:
so 'dhastāc chakaṭasya pāmānaṃ kaṣamāṇam upopaviveśa |
taṃ hābhyuvāda tvaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sayugvā raikva iti |
ahaṃ hy arā 3 iti ha pratijajñe |
sa ha kṣattāvidam iti pratyeyāya || ChUp_4,1.8 ||
children.translated_text: He [the attendant] approached [<s>Raikva</s>] sitting under a cart, scratching an itch. He addressed him: 'Are you, revered sir, <s>Raikva</s> with the cart (<s>sayugvān</s>)?' 'Yes, I am indeed,' he acknowledged. The attendant returned saying 'I have found him.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.1.8)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,1.8 ityuktaḥ kṣattānviṣya taṃ vijane deśe 'dhastācchakaṭasya gantryāḥ pāmānaṃ kharjūṃ kaṣamāṇaṃ kaṇḍūyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvāyaṃ nūnaṃ sayugvā raikva ityupa samīpa upaviveśa vinayenopaviṣṭavān /
taṃ ca raikvaṃ hābhyuvādoktavān /
children.translated_text: And he addressed <s>Raikva</s>, spoke to him —

children.text: tvamasi he bhagavo bhagavansayugvā raikva iti /
children.translated_text: 'Are you, O revered sir (<s>bhagavan</s>), <s>Raikva</s> with the cart (<s>sayugvān</s>)?'

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭo 'hamasmi hyarā 3 ara iti hānādara eva pratijajñe 'bhyupagatavān /
children.translated_text: Being thus asked, 'Yes, I am indeed' — with a tone of indifference, he acknowledged, he assented.

children.text: sa taṃ vijñāyāvidaṃ vijñātavānasmīti pratyeyāya pratyāgata ityarthaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: He, having identified him, returned [to the king] — meaning he came back [saying] 'I have identified [him].' (8)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.1.8:] Thus instructed, the attendant, having searched and found him in a secluded place, sitting under a cart — a small vehicle (<s>gantrī</s>) — scratching, rubbing an itch (<s>kharjū</s>), seeing him [and thinking] 'This must be <s>Raikva</s> with the cart,' approached him respectfully, sat down near him with humility.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,2.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.2.1

children.text:
tad u ha jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ ṣaṭ śatāni gavāṃ niṣkam aśvatarīrathaṃ tad ādāya praticakrame |
taṃ hābhyuvāda || ChUp_4,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s>, taking six hundred cows, a gold necklace (<s>niṣka</s>), and a chariot drawn by she-mules, went forth [to <s>Raikva</s>]. He addressed him: (<s>ChUp</s> 4.2.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,2.1 tattatra ṛṣergārhasthyaṃ pratyabhiprayaṃ buddhvā dhanārthitāṃ co ha, eva jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ ṣaṭśatāni gavāṃ niṣkaṃ kaṇṭhahāramaśvatarīrathamaśvatarībhyāṃ yuktaṃ rathaṃ tadādāya dhanaṃ gṛhītvā praticakrame raikvaṃ prati gatavān /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.2.1:] There, having understood the sage's inclination toward the householder's life and [his] desire for wealth, <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> [took] six hundred cows, a <s>niṣka</s> (a gold neck-ornament), and a chariot yoked with she-mules — having taken that wealth, he went forth, proceeded toward <s>Raikva</s>.

children.text: taṃ ca gatvābhyuvāda hābhyuktavān //1 //
children.translated_text: And having gone [there], he addressed him, spoke to him. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 4,2.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.2.2

children.text:
raikvemāni ṣaṭ śatāni gavām ayaṃ niṣko 'yam aśvatarīrathaḥ |
anu ma etāṃ bhagavo devatāṃ śādhi yāṃ devatām upāssa iti || ChUp_4,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Raikva</s>, here are six hundred cows, this gold necklace (<s>niṣka</s>), and this chariot drawn by she-mules. Please teach me, revered sir, about that deity whom you worship.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.2.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,2.2 he raikva gavāṃ ṣaṭśatānīmāni tubhyaṃ mayā'nītānyayaṃ niṣko 'śvatarīrathaścāyametaddhanamādatsva bhagavo 'nuśādhi ca me māmetāṃ yāṃ ca devatāṃ tvamupāḥse taddevatopadeśena māmanuśādhītyarthaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.2.2:] 'O <s>Raikva</s>, these six hundred cows have been brought by me for you, and this <s>niṣka</s> and this chariot drawn by she-mules — accept this wealth. O revered sir, teach me — instruct me — about that deity which you worship; through the teaching of that deity, instruct me' — this is the meaning. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 4,2.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.2.3

children.text:
tam u ha paraḥ pratyuvācāha hāretvā śūdra tavaiva saha gobhir astv iti |
tad u ha punar eva jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ sahasraṃ gavāṃ niṣkam aśvatarīrathaṃ duhitaraṃ tad ādāya praticakrame || ChUp_4,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: The other [<s>Raikva</s>] replied to him: 'Aha! Take them away, O <s>Śūdra</s>! Let [these gifts] remain yours along with the cows.' Then <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s>, again taking a thousand cows, a gold necklace (<s>niṣka</s>), a chariot drawn by she-mules, and [this time also] his daughter, went forth [again]. (<s>ChUp</s> 4.2.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,2.3 tamevamuktavantaṃ rājānaṃ pratyuvāca paro raikvaḥ /
ahetyayaṃ nipāto vinigrahārthīyo 'nyatreha tvanarthakaḥ /
evaśabdasya pṛthakprayogāt /
hāretvā hāreṇa yuktetvā gantrī seyaṃ hāretvā gobhiḥ saha tavaivāstu tiṣṭhatu na mamāparyāptena karmārthamanena prayojanamityabhiprāyo he śūdreti /
nanu rājāsau kṣattṛsambandhātsa ha kṣattāramuvācetyuktam /
vidyāgrahaṇāya ca brāhmaṇasamīpopagamācchūdrasya cānadhikārātkathamidamananurūpaṃ raikveṇocyate he śūdreti /
tatrā'hurācāryāḥ-haṃsavacanaśravaṇācchugenamāviveśa /
tenāsau śucā śrutvā raikvasya mahimānaṃ vā ādravatīti ṛṣirātmanaḥ parokṣajñatāṃ darśayañśūdretyāheti /
śūdravadvā dhanenaivainaṃ vidyāgrahaṇāyopajagāma na ca śuśrūṣayā /
na tu jātyaiva śūdra iti /
children.translated_text: But he is not a <s>Śūdra</s> by birth.

children.text: apare punarāhuralpaṃ dhanamāhṛtamiti ruṣaivainamuktavāñchūdreti /
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that he called him '<s>Śūdra</s>' out of anger because he had brought too little wealth.

children.text: liṅgaṃ ca bahvāharaṇa upādānaṃ dhanasyeti /
children.translated_text: And the evidence [for this] is the bringing of additional wealth on the second occasion.

children.text: taduharṣermataṃ jñātvā punareva jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇo gavāṃ sahasramadhikaṃ jāyāṃ carṣerabhimatāṃ duhitaramātmanastadādāya praticakrame krāntavān //3 //
children.translated_text: Then, having understood the opinion of the <s>ṛṣi</s>, <s>Jānaśruti</s> <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> returned, taking [with him] a thousand cows in addition, his own daughter as a wife favored by the <s>ṛṣi</s> — he went forth having taken [all this]. (4.2.3)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.2.3:] <s>Raikva</s>, the superior one, replied to the king who had spoken thus. 'Aha' — this particle expresses reproach; elsewhere it is meaningless, since the word 'eva' is used separately. 'Hāretvā' means 'may this necklace together with the cows remain with you alone; let it stay — I have no use for this insufficient [offering] meant for ritual purposes' — such is the purport. 'O <s>Śūdra</s>' — but was he not a king? It was stated 'he spoke to the attendant (<s>kṣattṛ</s>),' indicating a <s>kṣattṛ</s> connection. And since one approaches a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> to receive knowledge, and since a <s>Śūdra</s> has no qualification [for Vedic knowledge], how does <s>Raikva</s> inappropriately say 'O <s>Śūdra</s>'? On this, the teachers say: having heard the words of the swan, grief (<s>śuc</s>) entered him; therefore, having heard with that grief about <s>Raikva</s>'s greatness, he 'ran toward' [him] — the <s>ṛṣi</s>, showing his knowledge of what is hidden in the other's mind, said 'O <s>Śūdra</s>.' Or, like a <s>Śūdra</s>, he approached him for acquiring knowledge with wealth alone and not with service.

children.text: START ChUp 4,2.4-5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.2.4-5]

children.text:
taṃ hābhyuvāda |
raikvedaṃ sahasraṃ gavām ayaṃ niṣko 'yam aśvatarīratha iyaṃ jāyāyaṃ grāmo yasminn āsse 'nv eva mā bhagavaḥ śādhīti || ChUp_4,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'He addressed him: "O <s>Raikva</s>, here are a thousand cows, this gold necklace, this chariot with mules, this wife, and this village in which you dwell — please teach me, O Venerable one."' (ChUp 4.2.4)

children.text:
tasyā ha mukham upodgṛhṇann uvācājahāremāḥ śūdrānenaiva mukhenālāpayiṣyathā iti |
te haite raikvaparṇā nāma mahāvṛṣeṣu yatrāsmā uvāsa |
tasmai hovāca || ChUp_4,2.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Lifting up her face, he said: "You have brought these, O <s>Śūdra</s>; but by this face alone you would have made me speak." Those [villages] are indeed known as <s>Raikvaparṇa</s> in the <s>Mahāvṛṣa</s> [region], where he dwelt. To him he then taught.' (ChUp 4.2.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,2.4,5 raikvedaṃ gavāṃ sahasramayaṃ niṣko 'yamaśvatarīratha iyaṃ jāyārthaṃ mama duhitā'nītāyaṃ ca grāmo yasminnāḥse tiṣṭhasi sa ca tvadarthe mayā kalpitaḥ tadetatsarvamādāyānuśādhyeva mā māṃ he bhagava ityuktastasyā jāyārthamānītāyā rājño duhiturhaiva mukhaṃ dvāraṃ vidyāyā dāne tīrthamupodgṛhṇañjānannityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.2.4-5:] 'O <s>Raikva</s>, here are a thousand cows, this gold necklace, this chariot with mules, this wife — my daughter brought for this purpose — and this village in which you dwell, which has been arranged by me for your sake. Taking all this, please do teach me, O Venerable one' — thus addressed, lifting up the face, that is, the door or gateway for the giving of knowledge, of the wife — the king's daughter — brought for this purpose, understanding [her as a worthy offering] — this is the meaning.

children.text: brahmacārī dhanadāyī medhāvī śrotriyaḥ priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A celibate student, a giver of wealth, one of intelligence, one learned in scripture, one who is dear —

children.text: vidyayā vā vidyā prāha tāni tīrthāni ṣaṇmama //
children.translated_text: by knowledge, or knowledge is imparted — these are the six gateways for me.'

children.text:
iti vidyāyā vacanaṃ vijñāyate hi /
evaṃ jānannupodgṛhṇannuvācoktavān /
ājahārā'hṛtavānbhavānyadimā gā yaccānyaddhanaṃ tatsādhviti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
śūdreti pūrvoktānukṛtimātraṃ na tu kāraṇāntarāpekṣayā pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Śūdra</s>' — this is merely a repetition of what was said before, not said with reference to any other reason as previously.

children.text: anenaiva mukhena vidyāgrahaṇatīrthenā'lāpayiṣyathā ālāpayasīti māṃ bhāṣayasītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By this face alone' — that is, by this very gateway of receiving knowledge — 'you would have made me speak' means 'you are making me speak' — this is the meaning.

children.text: te haite grāmā raikvaparṇā nāma vikhyātā mahāvṛṣeṣu deśeṣu yatra yeṣu grāmeṣūvāsoṣitavān raikvastānasau grāmānadādasmai raikvāya rājā /
children.translated_text: Those villages are indeed famous as <s>Raikvaparṇa</s> by name, in the <s>Mahāvṛṣa</s> regions, where — in which villages — <s>Raikva</s> dwelt and resided; the king gave those villages to that <s>Raikva</s>.

children.text: tasmai rājñe dhanaṃ dattavate ha kilovāca vidyāṃ sa raikvaḥ //4-5 //
children.translated_text: To that king who had given wealth, <s>Raikva</s> indeed taught the knowledge. (4.2.4-5)

Thus a statement regarding [the gateways of] knowledge is well known. Knowing thus, lifting up [her face], he said — he spoke. 'You have brought' — 'you have brought these cows and whatever other wealth; that is good' — this is the completion of the sentence.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>khaṇḍa</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.1]

children.text:
vāyur vāva saṃvargaḥ |
yadā vā agnir udvāyati vāyum evāpyeti |
yadā sūryo 'stam eti vāyum evāpyeti |
yadā candro 'stam eti vāyum evāpyeti || ChUp_4,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is indeed <s>saṃvarga</s> (the absorber). For when fire goes out, it enters <s>Vāyu</s> alone. When the sun sets, it enters <s>Vāyu</s> alone. When the moon sets, it enters <s>Vāyu</s> alone.' (ChUp 4.3.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,3.1 vāyurvāva saṃvargo vāyurbāhyo vāvetyavadhāraṇārthaḥ /
saṃvargaḥ saṃvarjanātsaṃgrahaṇātsaṃgrasanādvā saṃvargaḥ /
vakṣyamāṇā agnyādyā devatā ātmabhāvamāpādayatītyataḥ saṃvargaḥ /
savarjavākhyo guṇo dhyeyo vāyuvat /
kṛtāyāntabharvadṛṣṭāntāt /
kathaṃ saṃvargattvaṃ vāyorityāha /
yadā yasminkāle vā agnirudvāyatyudvāsanaṃ prāpnotyupaśāmyati tadāsāvagnirvāyumevāpyeti vāyusvābhāvyamapigacchati /
tathā yadā sūryo 'stameti vāyumevāpyeti /
yadā candro 'stameti vāyumevāpyeti /
nanu kathaṃ sūryācandramasoḥ svarūpāvasthitayorvāyāvapigamanam /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect.

children.text: astamane 'darśanaprāptervāyunimittatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because at the time of setting, their invisibility is caused by <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: vāyunā hyastaṃ nīyate sūryaḥ calanasya vāyukāryatvāt /
children.translated_text: For the sun is carried to setting by <s>Vāyu</s>, since motion is an effect of <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: athavā pralaye sūryācandramasoḥ svarūpabhraṃśe tejorūpayorvāyāvevāpigamanaṃ syāt //1 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, at the time of cosmic dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), when the sun and moon lose their essential forms, being of the nature of light, they would indeed enter into <s>Vāyu</s>. (4.3.1)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.1:] '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed <s>saṃvarga</s>' — <s>Vāyu</s>, the external [element]; 'vāva' is used in the sense of emphatic assertion. <s>Saṃvarga</s> — because of absorbing (<s>saṃvarjana</s>), gathering together (<s>saṃgrahaṇa</s>), or swallowing up (<s>saṃgrasana</s>), he is <s>saṃvarga</s>. Because he causes the deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others, which will be mentioned, to enter into his own nature — therefore he is <s>saṃvarga</s>. The quality called <s>saṃvarga</s> (absorption) is to be meditated upon, like <s>Vāyu</s>, from the illustration of the dice game in which the winner absorbs [all stakes]. How is <s>Vāyu</s> the absorber? — to this he says: When — at whatever time — fire goes out, that is, reaches extinction, becomes extinguished, then that fire enters <s>Vāyu</s> alone — it attains the nature of <s>Vāyu</s>. Likewise, when the sun sets, it enters <s>Vāyu</s> alone. When the moon sets, it enters <s>Vāyu</s> alone. But how can the sun and moon, which remain in their own forms, enter into <s>Vāyu</s>?

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.2]

children.text:
yadāpa ucchuṣyanti vāyum evāpiyanti |
vāyur hy evaitān sarvān saṃvṛṅkte |
ity adhidaivatam || ChUp_4,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'When the waters dry up, they enter <s>Vāyu</s> alone. For <s>Vāyu</s> indeed absorbs all these. Thus with reference to the deities (<s>adhidaivatam</s>).' (ChUp 4.3.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,3.2 tathā yadā'pa ucchuṣyantyucchoṣamāpnuvanti tadā vāyumevāpiyanti /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.2:] Likewise, when the waters dry up — reach desiccation — then they enter <s>Vāyu</s> alone.

children.text: vāyurhi yasmādevaitānagnyādyānmahābalānsaṃvṛṅkte /
children.translated_text: For <s>Vāyu</s> indeed absorbs all these — <s>Agni</s> and the others — who are of great power.

children.text: ato vāyuḥ saṃvargaguṇa upāsya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Vāyu</s>, possessing the quality of <s>saṃvarga</s> (absorption), is to be meditated upon — this is the meaning.

children.text: ityadhidaivataṃ devatāsu saṃvargadarśanamuktam //2 //
children.translated_text: Thus — 'with reference to the deities (<s>adhidaivatam</s>)' — the perception of <s>saṃvarga</s> among the deities has been stated. (4.3.2)

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.3]

children.text:
athādhyātmam |
prāṇo vāva samvargaḥ |
sa yadā svapiti prāṇam eva vāg apy eti |
prāṇaṃ cakṣuḥ |
prāṇaṃ śrotram |
prāṇaṃ manaḥ |
prāṇo hy evaitān sarvān saṃvṛṅkta iti || ChUp_4,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now with reference to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>). <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath) is indeed <s>saṃvarga</s>. When one sleeps, speech enters <s>Prāṇa</s> alone; sight [enters] <s>Prāṇa</s>; hearing [enters] <s>Prāṇa</s>; mind [enters] <s>Prāṇa</s>. For <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed absorbs all these.' (ChUp 4.3.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,3.3 athānantaramadhyātmamātmani saṃvargadarśanamidamucyate /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.3:] Now, next, with reference to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>) — the perception of <s>saṃvarga</s> in the self is being stated.

children.text: prāṇo mukhyovāva saṃvargaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, the chief [vital breath], is indeed <s>saṃvarga</s>.

children.text: sa puruṣo yadā yasminkāle svapiti prāṇameva vāgapyeti vāyumivāgniḥ prāṇaṃ cakṣuḥ prāṇaṃ śrotraṃ prāṇaṃ manaḥ prāṇo hi yasmādevaitānvāgādīnsarvānsaṃvṛṅkta iti //3 //
children.translated_text: When a person sleeps — at whatever time — speech enters <s>Prāṇa</s> alone, just as fire [enters] <s>Vāyu</s>; sight [enters] <s>Prāṇa</s>; hearing [enters] <s>Prāṇa</s>; mind [enters] <s>Prāṇa</s>. For <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed absorbs all these — speech and the rest. (4.3.3)

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.4]

children.text:
tau vā etau dvau samvargau |
vāyur eva deveṣu prāṇaḥ prāṇeṣu || ChUp_4,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'These two are indeed the two absorbers (<s>saṃvarga</s>): <s>Vāyu</s> among the deities and <s>Prāṇa</s> among the vital functions.' (ChUp 4.3.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,3.4 tau vā etau dvau saṃvargau saṃvarjanaguṇo vāyureva deveṣu saṃvargaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇeṣu vāgādiṣu mukhyaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.4:] These two are indeed the two <s>saṃvargas</s> — possessing the quality of absorption: <s>Vāyu</s> alone is the <s>saṃvarga</s> among the deities, and <s>Prāṇa</s>, the chief [vital breath], among the vital functions such as speech and the rest. (4.3.4)

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.5]

children.text:
atha ha śaunakaṃ ca kāpeyam abhipratāriṇaṃ ca kākṣaseniṃ pariviṣyamāṇau brahmacārī bibhikṣe |
tasmā u ha na dadatuḥ || ChUp_4,3.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, while <s>Śaunaka</s> <s>Kāpeya</s> and <s>Abhipratārin</s> <s>Kākṣaseni</s> were being served [food], a <s>brahmacārin</s> begged for alms. They did not give to him.' (ChUp 4.3.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,3.5 athaitayoḥ stutyarthamiyamākhyāyikā'rabhyate /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.5:] Now, for the purpose of glorifying these two [<s>saṃvargas</s>], this narrative is begun.

children.text: hetyaitihyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ha' is used in the sense of tradition (<s>aitihya</s>).

children.text: śaunakaṃ ca śunakasyāpatyaṃ śonakaṃ kāpeyaṃ kapigotramabhipratāriṇaṃ ca nāmataḥ kakṣasenasyāpatyaṃ kākṣaseniṃ bhojanāyopaviṣṭau pariviṣyamāṇau sūpakārairbrahmacārī brahmavicchaṇḍo bibhikṣe bhikṣitavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Śaunaka</s> — the descendant of <s>Śunaka</s> — <s>Kāpeya</s>, of the <s>Kapi</s> lineage; and <s>Abhipratārin</s> by name, the son of <s>Kakṣasena</s>, <s>Kākṣaseni</s> — these two, seated for their meal, being served by cooks, a <s>brahmacārin</s> — a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, bold — begged for alms.

children.text: brahmacāriṇo brahmavinmānitāṃ buddhvā taṃ jijñāsamānau tasmā u bhikṣāṃ na jajaturna dattavantau ha kimayaṃ bakṣyatīti //5 //
children.translated_text: Recognizing the <s>brahmacārin</s> as an honored knower of <s>Brahman</s>, and wishing to test him, they did not give him alms — they did not offer [food] — [thinking] 'what will he say?' (4.3.5)

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.6]

children.text:
sa hovāca |
mahātmanaś caturo deva ekaḥ kaḥ sa jagāra bhuvanasya gopāḥ |
taṃ kāpeya nābhipaśyanti martyā abhipratārin bahudhā vasantam |
yasmai vā etad annaṃ tasmā etan na dattam iti || ChUp_4,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'He said: "The one God who is the guardian of the world has swallowed the four great beings. O <s>Kāpeya</s>, mortals do not perceive Him, O <s>Abhipratārin</s>, though He dwells in manifold forms. To whom this food [belongs], to him it has not been given."' (ChUp 4.3.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,3.6 sa hovāca brahmacārī mahātmanaścatura iti dvitīyābahuvacanam /
deva eko 'gnyādīnvāyurvāgādīnprāṇaḥ /
kaḥ sa prajāpatirjagāra grasitavān /
kaḥ sa jagāreti praśnameke /
children.translated_text: Some [interpret] 'Who is it that has swallowed?' as a question.

children.text: bhuvanasya bhavantyasminbhūtānīti bhuvanaṃ bhūrādiḥ sarvo lokastasya gopā gopāyitā rakṣitā goptetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhuvana</s>' — that in which beings exist is <s>bhuvana</s>, [meaning] the entire world beginning with the earth; its guardian (<s>gopā</s>) means protector, keeper — this is the meaning.

children.text: taṃ kaṃ prajāpatiṃ he kāpeya nābhipaśyanti na jānanti martyā maraṇadharmāṇo 'vivekino vā he 'bhipratārinbahudhādhyātmādhidaivatādhibhūtaprakārairvasantam /
