children.translated_text: Him — <s>Prajāpati</s> — O <s>Kāpeya</s>, mortals — those subject to death, or those lacking discrimination — do not perceive, do not know, O <s>Abhipratārin</s>, though He dwells in manifold ways — through the modes of <s>adhyātma</s> (the individual self), <s>adhidaivata</s> (the deities), and <s>adhibhūta</s> (the elements).

children.text: yasmai vā etadahanyahanyannamadanāyā'hriyate saṃskriyate ca tasmai prajāpataya etadannaṃ na dattamiti //6 //
children.translated_text: To whom this food is brought and prepared day after day for consumption — to that <s>Prajāpati</s>, this food has not been given. (4.3.6)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.6:] The <s>brahmacārin</s> said: 'The four great beings' — this is the accusative plural. The one God — <s>Vāyu</s> [who absorbs] <s>Agni</s> and the rest, [and] <s>Prāṇa</s> [who absorbs] speech and the rest. 'Kaḥ' means <s>Prajāpati</s> — He has swallowed.

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.7]

children.text:
tad u ha śaunakaḥ kāpeyaḥ pratimanvānaḥ pratyeyāya |
ātmā devānāṃ janitā prajānāṃ hiraṅyadaṃṣṭro babhaso 'nasūriḥ |
mahāntam asya mahimānam āhur anadyamāno yad anannam atti |
iti vai vayam brahmacārin nedam upāsmahe dattāsmai bhikṣām iti || ChUp_4,3.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then <s>Śaunaka</s> <s>Kāpeya</s>, reflecting upon this, approached [him and said]: "He is the Self of the gods, the progenitor of creatures, He of golden fangs, the devourer, the truly wise. They speak of His great majesty — that, though uneaten, He eats the uneaten. Thus indeed, O <s>brahmacārin</s>, do we meditate upon this. Give him alms."' (ChUp 4.3.7)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,3.7 tadu ha brahmacāriṇo vacanaṃ śaunakaḥ kāpeyaḥ pratimanvāno manasā'locayanbrahmacāriṇaṃ pratyeyāyā'jagāma /
gatvā cā'ha-yaṃ tvamavoco na paśyanti martyā iti taṃ vayaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
katham?ātmā sarvasya sthāvarajaṅgamasya /
kiñca devānāmagnyādīnāmātmani saṃhṛtya grasitvā punarjanitotpādayitā vāyurūpeṇādhidaivatamagnyādīnām /
adhyātmaṃ ca prāṇarūpeṇa vāgādīnāṃ prajānāṃ ca danitā /
atha vā'tmā devānāmagnivāgādīnāṃ janitā prajānāṃ sthāvarajaṅgamānām /
hiraṇyadaṃṣṭro 'bhagnadaṃṣṭra iti yāvat /
babhaso bhakṣaṇaśīlaḥ /
anasūriḥ sūrirmedhāvī na sūrirasūristatpratiṣedho 'nasūriḥ sūrirevetyarthaḥ /
mahāntamatipramāṇamaprameyamasya prajāpatermahimānaṃ vibhūtimāhurbrahmavidaḥ /
yasmātsvayamanyairanadyamāno 'bhakṣyamāṇo yadanannamagnivāgādidevatārūpamatti bhakṣayatīti /
vā iti nirarthakaḥ /
vayaṃ he brahmacārin, ā, idamevaṃ yathoktalakṣaṇaṃ brahma vayamā upāsmahe /
vayamiti vyavahitena sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'We' — the connection is with the separated [word].

children.text: anye na vayamidamupāsmahe /
children.translated_text: Others [say]: 'It is not this that we meditate upon.'

children.text: kiṃ tarhi parameva brahmopāsmaha iti varṇayanti /
children.translated_text: 'Rather, we meditate upon the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone' — thus they explain.

children.text: dattāsmai bhikṣāmityavocadbhṛtyān //7 //
children.translated_text: 'Give him alms' — he said to the servants. (4.3.7)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.7:] Then, reflecting upon the words of the <s>brahmacārin</s>, <s>Śaunaka</s> <s>Kāpeya</s>, contemplating in his mind, approached the <s>brahmacārin</s>. Having gone, he said: 'This [being] you spoke of as one whom mortals do not perceive — we perceive Him. How? He is the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) of all — movable and immovable. Furthermore, among the deities — having absorbed <s>Agni</s> and the others into Himself, and having swallowed them — He is the progenitor who again generates them in the form of <s>Vāyu</s>, with reference to the deities; and with reference to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), in the form of <s>Prāṇa</s>, [He is the progenitor] of speech and the other faculties and of all creatures. Or alternatively: He is the Self of the gods — <s>Agni</s>, speech, and the rest — and the progenitor of creatures, both movable and immovable. 'Of golden fangs' means one whose fangs are unbroken. '<s>Babhasa</s>' means one given to devouring. '<s>Anasūri</s>' — <s>sūri</s> means a wise person; 'not a <s>sūri</s>' is <s>asūri</s>; the negation of that — <s>anasūri</s> — means 'one who is indeed a <s>sūri</s>' (truly wise) — this is the meaning. They speak of the great — immeasurable, incomprehensible — majesty, the glory of this <s>Prajāpati</s>, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> [say]: because, though Himself uneaten — not consumed by others — He eats, He devours that which is 'uneaten' (<s>ananna</s>), namely the deities in the form of <s>Agni</s>, speech, and the rest. 'Vā' is meaningless [here]. 'We, O <s>brahmacārin</s>, indeed — this, of such characteristics as described — <s>Brahman</s>, we do meditate upon.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,3.8
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.3.8]

children.text:
tasmai u ha daduḥ |
te vā ete pañcānye pañcānye daśa santas tat kṛtam |
tasmāt sarvāsu dikṣv annam eva daśa kṛtam |
saiṣā virāḍ annādī |
tayedaṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭam |
sarvam asya idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavaty annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_4,3.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'They gave to him. These five and [another] five, being ten, that is <s>kṛta</s> (the winning throw). Therefore in all directions, food alone is ten, [which is] <s>kṛta</s>. This is <s>Virāṭ</s>, the eater of food. By her all this is seen. All this becomes seen for him, and he becomes an eater of food — he who knows thus, he who knows thus.' (ChUp 4.3.8)

children.text:
tasmā u ha daduste hi bhikṣām /
te vai ye grasyante 'gnyādayo yaśca teṣāṃ grasitā vāyuḥ pañcānye vāgādibhyaḥ, tathānye tebhyaḥ pañcādhyātmaṃ vāgādayaḥ prāṇaśca, te sarve daśa santastatkṛtaṃ bhavati, te caturaṅka ekāya evaṃ catvāraḥ tryaṅkāyaḥ evaṃ trayo 'pare dvyaṅkāyaḥ evaṃ dvāvanyāvekāṅkāya evameko 'nya, ityevaṃ deśa santastatkṛtaṃ bhavati /
yata evaṃ tasmātsarvāsu dikṣu daśasvapyagnyādyā vāgādyāśca daśasaṃkhyāsāmānyādannameva"daśākṣarā virāḍ virāḍannam" iti hi śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 4.3.8:] They gave him the alms. Those that are swallowed — <s>Agni</s> and the rest — and he who is their swallower, <s>Vāyu</s> — five other than speech and the rest; likewise, the other five with reference to the self — speech and the rest, along with <s>Prāṇa</s> — all these being ten, that becomes <s>kṛta</s> (the winning throw). Those four [counted] for the one [absorber] — thus four; three for the next — thus three more; two for the next — thus two more; one for the last — thus one more — in this way, being ten, it becomes <s>kṛta</s>. Since this is so, therefore in all ten directions, <s>Agni</s> and the rest, and speech and the rest, by the commonality of the number ten, are indeed food — for the <s>śruti</s> says: 'The ten-syllabled <s>Virāṭ</s>; <s>Virāṭ</s> is food.'

children.text:
ato 'nnameva daśasaṃkhyatvāt /
tata eva daśa kṛtaṃ kṛte 'ntarbhāvāccaturāyatvenetyavocāma /
saiṣā virāḍdaśasaṃkhyā satyannaṃ cānnādyannādinī ca kṛtatvena daśasaṃkhyayānnaṃ kṛtasaṃkhyayānnādī tayā annānnādinyā idaṃ sarvaṃ jagaddaśadiksaṃsthaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kṛtasaṃkhyābhūtayopalabdham /
children.translated_text: This <s>Virāṭ</s>, having the number ten, being food and also the eater of food — through being <s>kṛta</s> (the winning throw), by the number ten [she is] food, and by the <s>kṛta</s> number [she is] the eater of food — by her, who is both food and eater of food, all this universe, situated in the ten directions, is seen, that is, perceived as having become the <s>kṛta</s> number.

children.text: evaṃvido 'sya sarvaṃ kṛtasaṃkhyābhūtasya daśadiksaṃbaddhaṃ dṛṣṭamupalabdhaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: For one who knows thus, all this — connected with the ten directions and having become the <s>kṛta</s> number — becomes seen, becomes perceived.

children.text: kiñcānnādaśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda yathoktadarśī /
children.translated_text: Moreover, one who knows thus, as described, becomes a consumer of food (<s>annāda</s>).

children.text: dvirabhyāsa upāsanamāptyarthaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of the phrase] twice is for the purpose of concluding the meditation (<s>upāsana</s>). (8)

Therefore, food alone [is identified with <s>Virāṭ</s>] because of [sharing] the number ten. And from that very [reasoning], ten is <s>kṛta</s> — because <s>kṛta</s> is included [in the count] as fourfold — thus we have stated.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,4.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.1

children.text:
satyakāmo ha jābālo jabālāṃ mātaram āmantrayāṃ cakre |
brahmacaryaṃ bhavati vivatsyāmi kiṃgotro nv aham asmīti || ChUp_4,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Satyakāma</s>, the son of <s>Jabālā</s>, addressed his mother <s>Jabālā</s> [saying]: "I wish to live the life of a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student). Of what lineage (<s>gotra</s>) am I?"' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.4.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,4.1 sarvaṃ vāgādyagnyādi cānnānnādatvasaṃstutaṃ jagadekīkṛtya ṣoḍaśadhā pravibhajya tasminbrahmadṛṣṭirvidhātavyetyārabhyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.1:] Having unified the entire world — beginning with speech (<s>vāc</s>) and the rest, and fire (<s>agni</s>) and the rest — all glorified as food and consumer of food, and having divided it sixteenfold, the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> in that [is now] to be enjoined — thus [this section] begins.

children.text: śraddhātapasorbrahmopāsanāṅgatvapradarśanāyā'khyāyikā /
children.translated_text: This narrative (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>) is for the purpose of demonstrating that faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and austerity (<s>tapas</s>) are auxiliaries of the meditation on <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: satyakāmo ha nāmato haśabda aitihyārtho jabālāyā apatyaṃ jābālo jabalāṃ svāṃ mātaramāmantrayāñcakra āmantritavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Satyakāma</s> — by name; the particle 'ha' indicates tradition — the offspring of <s>Jabālā</s>, hence <s>Jābāla</s>, addressed his own mother <s>Jabālā</s> — that is, he spoke to her.

children.text: brahmacaryaṃ svādhyāyagrahaṇāya he bhavati vivatsyāmyācāryakule, kiṅgotro 'haṃ kimasya mama gotraṃ so 'haṃ nvahamasmīti //1 //
children.translated_text: 'O revered one (<s>bhavati</s>), I wish to dwell in the teacher's household for the purpose of studying the sacred texts as a <s>brahmacārin</s>. Of what lineage (<s>gotra</s>) am I — what is my <s>gotra</s>? Who am I?' (1)

children.text: START ChUp 4,4.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.2

children.text:
sā hainam uvāca |
nāham etad veda tāta yadgotras tvam asi |
bahv aham carantī paricāriṇī yauvane tvām alabhe |
sāham etan na veda yadgotras tvam asi |
jabālā tu nāmāham asmi |
satyakāmo nāma tvam asi |
sa satyakāma eva jābālo bruvīthā iti || ChUp_4,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'She said to him: "I do not know this, dear child — of what lineage you are. I was much occupied as a serving woman in my youth when I obtained you. I do not know this — of what lineage you are. But my name is <s>Jabālā</s>, and your name is <s>Satyakāma</s>. You may call yourself <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>."' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.4.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,4.2 evaṃ pṛṣṭā jabālā sā hainaṃ putramuvāca-nāhametattava gotraṃ veda he tāta yadgotrastvamasi /
kasmānna vetsītyuktā'ha-bahu bhartṛgṛhe paricaryājātamatithyabhyāgatādi carantyahaṃ paricāriṇī paricarantīti paricaraṇaśīlaivāhaṃ paricaraṇacittatayā gotrādismaraṇe mama mano nābhūt /
yauvane ca tatkāle tvāmalabhe labdhavatyasmi /
children.translated_text: 'And in my youth, at that time, I obtained you — I gave birth to you.'

children.text: tadaiva te pitoparataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'At that very time, your father passed away.'

children.text: ato 'nāthāhaṃ sāhametanna veda yadgotrastvamasi /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, I was without a protector. Thus I do not know of what lineage you are.'

children.text: jabālā tu nāmāhamasmi satyakāmo nāma tvamasi sa tvaṃ satyakāma evāhaṃ jābālo 'smītyācāryāya bruvīthāḥ yadyācāryeṇa pṛṣṭa ityabhiprāyaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: 'But my name is <s>Jabālā</s>; your name is <s>Satyakāma</s>. You should tell the teacher: "I am <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>" — if asked by the teacher, is the intended meaning.' (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.2:] Being asked thus, <s>Jabālā</s> — she said to him, her son: 'I do not know this — your lineage, dear child — of what lineage you are.' When asked 'Why do you not know?', she said: 'I was much occupied — performing service in the husband's household — attending to guests and visitors and other duties — I was a serving woman (<s>paricāriṇī</s>), one devoted to service. Due to my mind being absorbed in service, my mind did not turn to remembering lineage and such things.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,4.3-4
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.3-4

children.text:
sa ha hāridrumataṃ gautamam etyovāca |
brahmacaryaṃ bhagavati vatsyāmi |
upeyāṃ bhagavantam iti || ChUp_4,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He went to <s>Hāridrumata Gautama</s> and said: "I wish to live as a <s>brahmacārin</s> with you, revered sir. May I approach you, revered sir [as a student]."' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.4.3)

children.text:
taṃ hovāca kiṃgotro nu somyāsīti |
sa hovāca |
nāham etad veda bho yadgotro 'ham asmi |
apṛcchaṃ mātaram |
sā mā pratyabravīd bahv aham carantī paricariṇī yauvane tvām alabhe |
sāham etan na veda yadgotras tvam asi |
jabālā tu nāmāham asmi |
satyakāmo nāma tvam asīti |
so 'haṃ satyakāmo jābālo 'smi bho iti || ChUp_4,4.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'He [<s>Gautama</s>] said to him: "Of what lineage are you, dear boy?" He [<s>Satyakāma</s>] replied: "I do not know this, sir — of what lineage I am. I asked my mother. She told me: 'I was much occupied as a serving woman in my youth when I obtained you. I do not know of what lineage you are. But my name is <s>Jabālā</s> and your name is <s>Satyakāma</s>.' So I am <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>, sir."' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.4.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,4.4 sa ha satyakāmo hāridrumataṃ haridrumato 'patyaṃ hāridrumataṃ gautamaṃ gotrata etya gatvovāca brahmacaryaṃ bhagavati pūjāvati tvayi vatsyāmyata upeyāmupagaccheyaṃ śiṣyatayā bhagavantamityuktavantaṃ taṃ hovāca gautamaḥ /
kiṅgotro nu somyāsīti vijñātakulagotraḥ śiṣya upanetavya iti pṛṣṭaḥ pratyāha satyakāmaḥ /
sa hovāca nāhametadveda bho yadgotro 'hamasmi /
kiṃ tvapṛcchaṃ pṛṣṭavānasmi mātaram /
children.translated_text: 'However, I asked — I questioned — my mother.'

children.text: sā mayā pṛṣṭā māṃ pratyabravīnmātā /
children.translated_text: 'She, being asked by me, told me — my mother [replied to me].'

children.text: bahvahaṃ carantītyādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: 'I was much occupied' — and so on, as before.

children.text: tasyā ahaṃ vacaḥ smarāmi so 'haṃ satyakāmo jābālo 'smi bho iti //3-4 //
children.translated_text: 'I remember her words. So I am <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>, sir.' (3-4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.4:] That <s>Satyakāma</s> went to <s>Hāridrumata</s> — the son of <s>Haridrumat</s>, hence <s>Hāridrumata</s> — [who was] <s>Gautama</s> by lineage — having approached him, he said: 'I wish to dwell as a <s>brahmacārin</s> with you, the revered one (<s>bhagavat</s>). May I approach you, the revered sir, as a student.' To him who had spoken thus, <s>Gautama</s> said: 'Of what lineage are you, dear boy?' — since a student whose family and lineage are known should be initiated (<s>upanīta</s>) — being thus asked, <s>Satyakāma</s> replied. He said: 'I do not know this, sir, of what lineage I am.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,4.5
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.5

children.text:
taṃ hovāca |
naitad abrahmaṇo vivaktum arhati |
samidhaṃ somyāhara |
upa tvā neṣye na satyād agā iti |
tam upanīya kṛśānām abalānāṃ catuḥśatā gā nirākṛtya uvācemāḥ somyānusaṃvrajeti |
tā abhiprasthāpayann uvāca |
nāsahasreṇāvarteyeti |
sa ha varṣagaṇaṃ provāsa |
tā yadā sahasraṃ sampeduḥ || ChUp_4,4.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'He [<s>Gautama</s>] said to him: "A non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> would not be able to speak thus. Bring fuel, dear boy. I shall initiate you. You have not departed from truth." Having initiated him, he separated out four hundred lean and weak cows and said: "Follow these, dear boy." As he drove them forth, he said: "I shall not return without a thousand." He dwelt away for a number of years. When they reached a thousand —' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.4.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,4.5 taṃ hovāca gautamo naitadvaco 'brāhmaṇo viśeṣeṇa vaktumarhatyārjavārthasaṃyuktam /
ṛjavo hi brahmaṇā netare svabhāvataḥ /
yasmānna satyādbrāhmaṇajātidharmādagā nāpetavānasi /
ato brāhmaṇaṃ tvāmupaneṣye 'taḥ saṃskārārthaṃ homāya samidhaṃ somyā'haretyuktvā tamupanīya kṛśānāmabalānāṃ goyūthānnirākṛtyāpakṛṣya catuḥśatā catvāri śatāni gavāmuvācemā gāḥ somyānusaṃvrajānugaccha /
children.translated_text: 'therefore I shall initiate you as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' Having said 'Bring fuel, dear boy, for the purpose of the consecration ritual (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and oblation,' and having initiated him, he separated out — set apart — from the herds of cattle four hundred, four hundred cows that were lean and weak, and said: 'Follow these cows, dear boy.'

children.text: ityuktastā araṇyaṃ pratyabhiprasthāpayannuvāca-nāsahasreṇāpūrṇena sahasreṇa nā'varteya na pratyāgaccheyam /
children.translated_text: Being told thus, as he was driving them forth toward the forest, he said: 'I shall not return without a full thousand — I shall not come back.'

children.text: sa evamuktvā gā araṇyaṃ tṛṇodakabahulaṃ dvandvaṃrahitaṃ praveśya sa ha varṣagaṇaṃ dīrghaṃ provāsa proṣitavān /
children.translated_text: Having said this, he took the cows into a forest abundant in grass and water and free from extremes [of climate], and he dwelt away (<s>provāsa</s>) for a long number of years.

children.text: tāḥ samyaggāvo rakṣitā yadā yasminkāle sahasraṃ saṃpeduḥ saṃpannā babhūvuḥ //5//
children.translated_text: Those cows, well-tended, when — at which time — they reached a thousand — they became complete [in number]. (5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.5:] <s>Gautama</s> said to him: 'This speech, endowed with the quality of straightforwardness, a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> would not be able to speak in this particular way. For <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are naturally straightforward, not others, by their very nature. Since you have not departed from — not deviated from — truth, [which is] the natural quality of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> caste,'

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,5.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.1

children.text:
atha hainam ṛṣabho 'bhyuvāda satyakāma 3 iti |
bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva |
prāptāḥ somya sahasraṃ smaḥ |
prāpaya na ācāryakulam || ChUp_4,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then a bull addressed him: "<s>Satyakāma</s>!" "Revered sir," he responded.' 'We have reached a thousand, dear boy. Lead us to the teacher's house.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.5.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,5.1 tametaṃ śraddhātapobhyāṃ siddhaṃ vāyudevatā diksaṃbandhinī tuṣṭā satyṛṣabhamanupraviśyarṣabhāpannānugrahāyātha hainamṛṣabho 'bhyuvādābhyuktavānsatyakāma 3 iti saṃbodhya, tamasau satyakāmo bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva prativacanaṃ dadau /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.1:] The deity of wind (<s>Vāyu</s>), associated with the directions, being pleased with him who had accomplished [spiritual readiness] through faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and austerity (<s>tapas</s>), entered into a bull in order to bestow grace — then this bull addressed him, spoke to him [saying] '<s>Satyakāma</s>!' — calling him thus. That <s>Satyakāma</s> responded with 'Revered sir (<s>bhagavaḥ</s>)' — he gave a reply.

children.text: praptāḥ somya sahasraṃ smaḥ pūrṇā tava pratijñātaḥ prāpaya no 'smānācāryakulam //1 //
children.translated_text: 'We have reached a thousand, dear boy — we are complete, as you had resolved. Lead us — take us — to the teacher's house.' (1)

children.text: START ChUp 4,5.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.2

children.text:
brahmaṇaś ca te pādaṃ bravāṇi iti |
bravītu me bhagavān iti |
tasmai hovāca |
prācī dik kalā |
praticī dik kalā |
dakṣiṇā dik kalā |
udīcī dik kalā |
eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān nāma || ChUp_4,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: '"I shall tell you a quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>." "Please tell me, revered sir." He said to him: "The eastern direction is a part (<s>kalā</s>). The western direction is a part. The southern direction is a part. The northern direction is a part. This indeed, dear boy, is the four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Prakāśavān</s> (the Luminous)."' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.5.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,5.2 kiñcāhaṃ braṅmaṇaḥ parasya te tubhyaṃ pādaṃ bravāṇi kathayāni /
ityuktaḥ pratyuvāca-bravītu kathayatu me mahyaṃ bhagavān /
ityukta ṛṣabhastasmai satyakāmāya hovāca /
children.translated_text: Being thus requested, the bull said to that <s>Satyakāma</s>:

children.text: prācī dikkalā brahmaṇaḥ pādasya caturtho bhāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The eastern direction is a part (<s>kalā</s>) — a fourth portion — of the quarter of <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: tathā pratīcī dikkalā dakṣiṇā dikkalodīcī dikkalaiṣa vai saimya brahmaṇaḥ pādaścatuśaṣkalaścatasraḥ kalā avayavā yasya so 'yaṃ catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavānnāma prakāśavānityavaṃ nāmābhidhānaṃ yasya /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, the western direction is a part, the southern direction is a part, the northern direction is a part. This indeed, dear boy, is a quarter of <s>Brahman</s> that is four-parted — having four parts (<s>kalās</s>) as its components — and its name is <s>Prakāśavān</s> (the Luminous) — meaning that is the designation by which it is known.'

children.text: tathottare 'pi pādāstrayaścatuṣkalā brahmaṇaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: 'Similarly, the remaining three quarters of <s>Brahman</s> are also four-parted.' (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.2:] 'Moreover, I shall tell you — declare to you — a quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.' Being told thus, he replied: 'Please tell — please declare — to me, revered sir.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,5.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.3

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān ity upāste prakāśavān asmiṃl loke bhavati |
prakāśavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān ity upāste || ChUp_4,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>Prakāśavān</s> (the Luminous) — becomes luminous in this world. He conquers luminous worlds — he who, knowing thus, meditates on this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>Prakāśavān</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.5.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,5.3 sa yaḥ kaścidevaṃ yathoktametaṃ brahmaṇaścatuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ vidvānprakāśavānityanena guṇena viśiṣṭamupāste tasyedaṃ phalaṃ prakāśavānasmin loke bhavati prakhyāto bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.3:] He who — whoever — knowing thus as described, meditates on this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> with the particular quality [named] <s>Prakāśavān</s> — for him this is the fruit: he becomes luminous (<s>prakāśavān</s>) in this world — meaning he becomes renowned.

children.text: tathādṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prakāśavato ha lokāndevādisaṃbandhino mṛtaḥ sañjayati prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the unseen fruit [is]: he conquers luminous worlds — worlds connected with the gods and such — [meaning] after death he attains [them].

children.text: ya etameva vidvāṃścatuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavānityupāste //3//
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, meditates on this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>Prakāśavān</s>. (3)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,6.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.6.1

children.text:
agniṣṭe pādaṃ vakteti |
sa ha śvo bhūte gā abhiprasthāpayāṃ cakāra |
tā yatrābhisāyaṃ babhūvus tatrāgnim upasamādhāya gā uparudhya samidham ādhāya paścād agneḥ prāṅ upopaviveśa || ChUp_4,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: '"<s>Agni</s> (Fire) will tell you a quarter." The next day, he drove the cows onward. Where they happened to be at evening, there he built a fire, penned in the cows, laid on fuel, and sat down behind the fire facing east.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.6.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,6.1 so 'gniste pādaṃ vaktetyupararāmarṣabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.6.1:] The bull, having said '<s>Agni</s> will tell you a quarter,' ceased speaking.

children.text: sa satyākāmo ha śvobhūte paredyurnaityakaṃ nityaṃ karma kṛtvā gā abhiprasthāpayāñcakārā'cāryakulaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: That <s>Satyakāma</s>, the next day (<s>śvobhūte</s>) — the following day — having performed his daily obligatory rites (<s>naityaka karma</s>), drove the cows onward toward the teacher's house.

children.text: tāḥ śanaiścarantya ācāryakulābhimukhyaḥ prasthitā yatra yasminkāle deśe 'bhi sāyaṃ niśāyāmabhisaṃbabhūvurekatrābhimukhyaḥ saṃbhūtāḥ, tatrāgnimupasamādhāya gā uparudhya samidhamādhāya paścādagneḥ praṅupopaviveśa ṛṣabhavaco dhyāyan //1 //
children.translated_text: Those [cows], walking slowly, heading toward the teacher's house — where, at what time and place, they came together at evening — [there] he built a fire (<s>agni</s>), penned in the cows, laid on fuel, and sat down behind the fire facing east, contemplating the words of the bull. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 4,6.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.6.2

children.text:
tam agnir abhyuvāda satyakāma 3 iti |
bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva || ChUp_4,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Agni</s> addressed him: "<s>Satyakāma</s>!" "Revered sir," he responded.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.6.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,6.2 tamagnirabhyuvāda satyakāma 3 iti saṃbodhya, tamasau satyakāmo bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva prativacanaṃ dadau //2 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.6.2:] <s>Agni</s> addressed him — spoke to him — calling '<s>Satyakāma</s>!' That <s>Satyakāma</s> responded with 'Revered sir (<s>bhagavaḥ</s>)' — he gave a reply. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 4,6.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.6.3

children.text:
brahmaṇaḥ somya te pādaṃ bravāṇīti |
bravītu me bhagavān iti |
tasmai ha uvāca |
pṛthivī kalā |
antarikṣaṃ kalā |
dyauḥ kalā |
samudraḥ kalā |
eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇo 'nantavān nāma || ChUp_4,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: '"I shall tell you, dear boy, a quarter of <s>Brahman</s>." "Please tell me, revered sir." He said to him: "The earth is a part. The atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>) is a part. Heaven (<s>dyaus</s>) is a part. The ocean is a part. This indeed, dear boy, is the four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Anantavān</s> (the Infinite)."' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.6.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,6.3 brahmaṇaḥ somya te pādaṃ bravāṇīti bravītu me bhagavānīti tasmai hovāca pṛthivī kalāntarikṣaṃ kalā dyauḥ kalā samudraḥ kaletyātmagocarameva darśanamagnirabravīt /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.6.3:] 'I shall tell you, dear boy, a quarter of <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Please tell me, revered sir.' He said to him: 'The earth is a part, the atmosphere is a part, heaven is a part, the ocean is a part' — <s>Agni</s> spoke about what pertains to his own domain of perception.

children.text: eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇo 'nantavānnāma //3 //
children.translated_text: 'This indeed, dear boy, is the four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Anantavān</s> (the Infinite).' (3)

children.text: START ChUp 4,6.4
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.6.4

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo 'nantavān ity upāste 'nantavān asmiṃl loke bhavati |
anantavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo 'nantavān ity upāste || ChUp_4,6.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>Anantavān</s> (the Infinite) — becomes infinite in this world. He conquers infinite worlds — he who, knowing thus, meditates on this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>Anantavān</s>.' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.6.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,6.4 sa yaḥ kaścidyathoktaṃ pādamanantavattvena guṇenopāste sa tathaiva tadguṇo bhavatyasmiṃlloke /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.6.4:] He who — whoever — meditates on the quarter as described, with the quality of being infinite (<s>anantavattva</s>) — he likewise becomes endowed with that quality in this world.

children.text: mṛtaścānantavato ha lokānsa jayati ya etamevamityādi pūrvavat //4//
children.translated_text: And after death, he conquers infinite worlds. 'He who [knows] this thus' — and so forth, as before. (4)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭha khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.
[<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.7.1-2]

children.text: haṃsaste pādaṃ vakteti sa ha śvobhūte gā abhiprasthāpayāñcakāra tā yatrābhisāyaṃ babhūvustatrāgnimupasamādhāyā gā uparudhya samidhamādhāya paścādagneḥ prāṅupopaviveśa //1 //
children.translated_text: '"A <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) will tell you a quarter." The next day, he drove the cows onward. Where they happened to be at evening, there he built a fire, penned in the cows, laid on fuel, and sat down behind the fire facing east.' (1)

children.text: taṃ haṃsa upanipatyābhyuvāda satyakāma 3 iti bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva //2//
children.translated_text: 'A <s>haṃsa</s>, flying down, addressed him: "<s>Satyakāma</s>!" "Revered sir," he responded.' (2)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,7.1,2 so 'gnirhaṃsaste pādaṃ vaktetyuktavopararāma /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.7.1-2:] That <s>Agni</s>, having said 'A <s>haṃsa</s> will tell you a quarter,' ceased speaking.

children.text: haṃsa ādityaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>haṃsa</s> is <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun).

children.text: śauklyātpatanasāmānyācca /
children.translated_text: [It is called <s>haṃsa</s>] because of [its] whiteness and the similarity of [its] movement [through the sky].

children.text: sa ha śvobhūta ityādi samānam //1-2 //
children.translated_text: 'The next day' — and so forth — is the same [as before]. (1-2)

children.text: START ChUp 4,7.3-4
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.7.3-4

children.text:
brahmaṇaḥ somya te pādaṃ bravāṇīti |
bravītu me bhagavān iti |
tasmai hovāca |
agniḥ kalā |
sūryaḥ kalā |
candraḥ kalā |
vidyut kalā |
eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇo jyotiṣmān nāma || ChUp_4,7.3 ||
children.translated_text: '"I shall tell you, dear boy, a quarter of <s>Brahman</s>." "Please tell me, revered sir." He said to him: "Fire (<s>Agni</s>) is a part. The sun (<s>Sūrya</s>) is a part. The moon (<s>Candra</s>) is a part. Lightning (<s>Vidyut</s>) is a part. This indeed, dear boy, is the four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Jyotiṣmān</s> (the Radiant)."' (<s>ChUp</s> 4.7.3)

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo jyotiṣmān ity upāste jyotiṣmān asmiṃl loke bhavati |
jyotiṣmato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo jyotiṣmān ity upāste || ChUp_4,7.4 ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, meditates upon this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>jyotiṣmān</s> (possessed of light), becomes luminous in this world. He conquers the luminous worlds, who, knowing thus, meditates upon this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>jyotiṣmān</s> (possessed of light). [ChUp 4.7.4]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,7.3,4 agniḥkalā sūryaḥ kalā candraḥ kalā vidyutkalaiṣa vai somyeti jyotirviṣayameva ca darśanaṃ provācāto haṃsasyā'dityatvaṃ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.7.3-4] <s>Agni</s> (fire) is one part, <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun) is one part, <s>Candra</s> (the moon) is one part, lightning is one part — 'this indeed, dear one' — he taught a vision pertaining only to luminous objects. From this, the identity of the <s>haṃsa</s> with <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is understood.

children.text: vidvatphalaṃ-jyotiṣmāndīptiyukto 'smiṃlloke bhavati /
children.translated_text: The fruit for the knower is that he becomes <s>jyotiṣmān</s> — endowed with radiance — in this world.

children.text: candrādityādīnāṃ jyotiṣmata eva ca mṛtvā lokāñjayati /
children.translated_text: And after death he conquers the luminous worlds of the moon, sun, and others.

children.text: samānamuttaram //3-4 //
children.translated_text: The rest is the same as before. [3-4]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh <s>khaṇḍa</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,8.1
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.8.1]

children.text:
madguṣṭe pādaṃ vakteti |
sa ha śvo bhūte gā abhiprasthāpayāṃ cakāra |
tā yatrābhisāyaṃ babhūvus tatrāgnim upasamādhāya gā uparudhya samidham ādhāya paścād agneḥ prāṅ upopaviveśa || ChUp_4,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>madgu</s> (water-bird) will tell you one quarter,' he said. The next day, he drove the cows forth. Where they came together in the evening, there he built a fire, penned the cows, placed fuel on the fire, and sat down behind the fire facing east. [ChUp 4.8.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,8.1 haṃso 'pi madguṣṭe pādaṃ vaktetyupararāma /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.8.1] The <s>haṃsa</s> also ceased, saying 'the <s>madgu</s> will tell you one quarter.'

children.text: madgurudakacaraḥ pakṣī sa cāpsambandhātprāṇaḥ sa ha śvobhūta ityādi pūrvavat //1 //
children.translated_text: The <s>madgu</s> is a water-dwelling bird, and because of its connection with water, it represents <s>Prāṇa</s>. 'The next day' and so on is as before. [1]

children.text: START ChUp 4,8.2-3
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.8.2-3]

children.text:
taṃ madgur upanipatyābhyuvāda satyakāma 3 iti |
bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva || ChUp_4,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>madgu</s> approached him and addressed him: '<s>Satyakāma</s>!' 'Sir,' he responded. [ChUp 4.8.2]

children.text:
brahmaṇaḥ somya te pādaṃ bravāṇīti |
bravītu me bhagavān iti |
tasmai hovāca |
prāṇaḥ kalā |
cakṣuḥ kalā |
śrotraṃ kalā |
manaḥ kalā |
eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇa āyatanavān nāma || ChUp_4,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'O dear one, I shall tell you a quarter of <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Please tell me, sir.' He then said to him: '<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is one part, the eye is one part, the ear is one part, the mind is one part. This indeed, dear one, is the four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> called <s>āyatanavān</s> (having a foundation).' [ChUp 4.8.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,8.2,3 sa ca madguḥ prāṇaḥ svaviṣayameva ca darśanamuvāca prāṇaḥ kaletyādi, āyatanavānityevaṃ nāma /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.8.2-3] That <s>madgu</s>, which is <s>Prāṇa</s>, taught a vision pertaining only to its own domain — '<s>Prāṇa</s> is one part' and so on. Its name is <s>āyatanavān</s> (having a foundation).

children.text: āyatanaṃ nāma manaḥ sarvakaraṇopahṛtānāṃ bhogānāṃ tadyasminpāde vidyata ityāyatanavānnāma pādaḥ //2-3 //
children.translated_text: The foundation (<s>āyatana</s>) is the mind, for it is the repository of all enjoyments brought together by all the sense organs. That quarter in which this is present is called the <s>āyatanavān</s> quarter. [2-3]

children.text: START ChUp 4,8.4
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.8.4]

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇa āyatanavān ity upāsta āyatanavān asmiṃl loke bhavati |
āyatanavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇa āyatanavān ity upāste || ChUp_4,8.4 ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, meditates upon this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>āyatanavān</s> (having a foundation), becomes one who has a foundation in this world. He conquers the worlds that have a foundation, who, knowing thus, meditates upon this four-parted quarter of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>āyatanavān</s>. [ChUp 4.8.4]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,8.4 taṃ pādaṃ tathaivopāste yaḥ sa āyatanavānāśrayavānasmiṃlloke bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.8.4] He who meditates upon that quarter in this way becomes <s>āyatanavān</s> — one who has a support, a refuge — in this world.

children.text: tathā'yatanavata eva sāvakāśāṃllokānmṛto jayati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, after death, he conquers the worlds that have a foundation, that is, spacious worlds.

children.text: ya etamevamityādi pūrvavat //4//
children.translated_text: 'He who thus' and so on is as before. [4]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth <s>khaṇḍa</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,9.1
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.9.1]

children.text:
prāpa hācaryakulam |
tam ācaryo 'bhyuvāda satyakāma 3 iti |
bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva || ChUp_4,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: He arrived at the teacher's house. The teacher addressed him: '<s>Satyakāma</s>!' 'Sir,' he responded. [ChUp 4.9.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,9.1 sa evaṃ brahmavitsanprāpa ha prāptavānācāryakulam /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.9.1] He, being thus a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, arrived — reached — the teacher's house.

children.text: tamācāryo 'bhyuvāda satyakāma 3 iti /
children.translated_text: The teacher addressed him: '<s>Satyakāma</s>!'

children.text: bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva //1 //
children.translated_text: 'Sir,' he responded. [1]

children.text: START ChUp 4,9.2
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.9.2]

children.text:
brahmavid iva vai somya bhāsi |
ko nu tvānuśaśāseti |
anye manuṣyebhya iti ha pratijajñe |
bhagavāṃs tv eva me kāme brūyāt || ChUp_4,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Dear one, you shine like a knower of <s>Brahman</s>. Who has taught you?' 'Beings other than men,' he acknowledged. 'But may you, sir, please teach me.' [ChUp 4.9.2]

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,9.2 brahmavidiva vai somya bhāsi /
prasannendriyaḥ prahasitavadanaśca niścintaḥ kṛtārtho brahmavidbhavati /
ata ācāryo brahmavidiva bhāsoti /
ko nviti vitarkayannuvāca kastvāmanuśaśāseti /
sa cā'ha satyakāmo 'nye manuṣyebhyaḥ /
devatā māmanuśiṣṭavatyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The deities have instructed me.'

children.text: ko 'nyo bhagavacchiṣyaṃ māṃ manuṣyaḥ sannanuśāsitumutsahetetyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The implied meaning is: 'What other human being would dare to instruct me, who am your disciple, sir?'

children.text: ato 'nye manuṣyebhya iti ha pratijajñe pratijñātavān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'beings other than men' — thus he acknowledged, that is, he declared.

children.text: bhagavāṃstveva me kāme mamecchāyāṃ brūyātkimanyairuktena nāhaṃ tadgaṇayāmītyabhiprāyaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: 'But may you, sir, teach me according to my desire' — the implied meaning is: 'What is the use of what others have said? I do not value that.' [2]

[Bhāṣya 4.9.2] 'Dear one, you shine like a knower of <s>Brahman</s>.' A knower of <s>Brahman</s> has serene senses, a smiling face, is free from anxiety, and has fulfilled his purpose. Therefore the teacher said, 'You shine like a knower of <s>Brahman</s>.' Speculating, he asked, 'Who has taught you?' <s>Satyakāma</s> replied, 'Beings other than men.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,9.3
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.9.3]

children.text:
śrutaṃ hy eva me bhagavaddṛśebhya ācāryād dhaiva vidyā viditā sādhiṣṭhaṃ prāpatīti |
tasmai ha etad eva uvāca |
atra ha na kiṃcana vīyāyeti vīyāyeti || ChUp_4,9.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'For I have heard from those like you, sir, that knowledge learned from the teacher alone leads one most excellently to the goal.' He then taught him the very same thing. In this, nothing was lost — nothing was lost at all. [ChUp 4.9.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,9.3 kiñca śrutaṃ hi yasmānmama vidyata evāsminnarthe bhagavatsamebhya ṝṣibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.9.3] Moreover, 'I have heard' — because it is well known to me on this matter from sages who are like you, sir,

children.text: ācāryāddhaiva vidyā viditā sādhiṣṭhaṃ sādhutamatvaṃ prāpaditi prāpnotītyato bhagavāneba brūyādityukta ācāryo 'bravīttasmai tāmeva daivatairuktāṃ vidyām /
children.translated_text: that knowledge learned from the teacher alone reaches the most excellent state, the highest perfection — therefore, 'may you, sir, teach me.' Thus addressed, the teacher taught him that very same knowledge that had been taught by the deities.

children.text: atra ha na kiñcana ṣoḍaśakalavidyāyāḥ kiñcidekadeśamātramapi na vīyāya na vigatamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In this' — not even a single portion, not even the slightest part, of the sixteen-parted knowledge was lost, was absent — that is the meaning.

children.text: dvirabhyāso vidyāparisamāptyarthaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: The repetition is for the purpose of completing the knowledge. [3]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth <s>khaṇḍa</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,10.1
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.10.1]

children.text:
upakosalo ha vai kāmalāyanaḥ satyakāme jābāle brahmacāryam uvāsa |
tasya ha dvādaśa vārṣāny agnīn paricacāra |
sa ha smānyān antevāsinaḥ samāvartayaṃs taṃ ha smaiva na samāvartayati || ChUp_4,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Upakosala</s>, the son of <s>Kamala</s>, <s>Kāmalāyana</s>, lived as a <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student) in the house of <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>. For twelve years he tended the sacred fires. Though the teacher performed the <s>samāvartana</s> (completion ceremony) for his other students, he did not perform it for him. [ChUp 4.10.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,10.1 punarbrahmavidyāṃ prakārāntareṇa vakṣyāmītyārabheta gatiṃ ca tadvido 'gnividyāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.10.1] 'I shall now teach <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) in another manner' — thus he begins, and also the <s>agni-vidyā</s> (knowledge of the fires) and the destiny of the one who knows it.

children.text: ākhyāyikā pūrvavacchraddhātapasorbrahmavidyāsādhanatvapradaśranārthā-upakosalo ha vai nāmataḥ kamalasyāpatyaṃ kāmalāyanaḥ satyakāme jābāle brahmacaryamuvāsa tasya, haḥ etihyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The narrative, as before, is intended to demonstrate that faith and austerity are the means to <s>brahmavidyā</s>. <s>Upakosala</s> — that is his name — the son of <s>Kamala</s>, <s>Kāmalāyana</s>, lived the life of a <s>brahmacārī</s> in the house of <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>. 'Ha' here indicates tradition.

children.text: tasyā'cāryasya dvādaśa varṣāṇyagnīnparicacārāgnīnāṃ paricaraṇaṃ kṛtavān /
children.translated_text: He tended the fires — he performed the service of the fires — for twelve years of his teacher's.

children.text: sa ha smā'cāryo 'nyānbrahmacāriṇaḥ svādhyāyaṃ grāhayitvā samāvartayaṃstamevopakosalamekaṃ na samāvartayati sma ha //1 //
children.translated_text: The teacher, having taught the other <s>brahmacārīs</s> (celibate students) the sacred texts, performed the <s>samāvartana</s> (completion ceremony) for them, but he did not perform the <s>samāvartana</s> for <s>Upakosala</s> alone. [1]

children.text: START ChUp 4,10.2
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.10.2]

children.text:
taṃ jāyovāca tapto brahmacārī kuśalam agnīn paricacārīt |
mā tvā agnayaḥ paripravocan |
prabrūhy asmā iti |
tasmai hāprocyaiva pravāsāṃ cakre || ChUp_4,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: His wife said to him: 'This <s>brahmacārī</s> has undergone great austerity and has skillfully tended the fires. Do not let the fires reproach you. Teach him.' But without having taught him, he departed on a journey. [ChUp 4.10.2]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,10.2 tamācāryajāyovāca taptobrahmacārī kuśalaṃ samyagagnīnparicacārītparicaritavān /
bhagavāṃścāgniṣu bhaktaṃ na samāvartayati /
children.translated_text: 'And yet you do not perform the completion ceremony for one who is devoted to the fires.'

children.text: ato 'smadbhaktaṃ na samāvartayatīti jñātvā tvāmagnayo mā paripravocangarhāṃ tava mā kuryuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, knowing that you are not performing the completion ceremony for one devoted to us, may the fires not reproach you — may they not find fault with you.'

children.text: ataḥ prabrūhyasmai vidyāmiṣṭāmupakosalāyeti /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, teach this desired knowledge to <s>Upakosala</s>.'

children.text: tasmā evaṃ jāyayokto 'pi hāprocyaivānuktvaiva kiñcitpravāsāṃcakre pravasitavān //2 //
children.translated_text: But even though thus told by his wife, without having told him anything at all, he departed on a journey. [2]
[Bhāṣya 4.10.2] The teacher's wife said to him: 'This <s>brahmacārī</s> has undergone great austerity and has properly, skillfully tended the fires.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,10.3
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.10.3]

children.text:
sa ha vyādhinā anaśituṃ dadhre |
tam ācāryajāyā uvāca brahmacārinn aśāna |
kiṃ nu na aśnāsi iti |
sa ha uvāca bahava ime 'smin puruṣe kāmā nānātyāyāḥ |
vyādhībhīḥ pratipūrṇo 'smi |
na as/iṣyāmi iti || ChUp_4,10.3 ||
children.translated_text: He fell ill with distress and resolved not to eat. The teacher's wife said to him: '<s>Brahmacārī</s>, please eat. Why are you not eating?' He replied: 'There are many desires in this person, leading in various directions. I am filled with afflictions. I shall not eat.' [ChUp 4.10.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,10.3 sa hopakosalo vyādhinā mānasena duḥkhenānaśitumanaśanaṃ kartuṃ dadhre dhṛtavānmanaḥ /
taṃ tūṣṇīmagnyagāre 'vasthitamācāryajāyovāca he brahmacārinnaśāna bhuṅkṣva kiṃ nu kasmānnu kāraṇānnāśnāsīti /
children.translated_text: As he sat silently in the fire-hall, the teacher's wife said: 'O <s>brahmacārī</s>, eat! Partake of food! Why, for what reason, are you not eating?'

children.text: sa hovāca bahavo 'neke 'sminpuruṣe 'kṛtārthe prākṛte kāmā icchāḥ kartavyaṃ prati nānātyayo 'tigamanaṃ yeṣāṃ vyādhīnāṃ kartavyacintānāṃ te nānātyayā vyādhayaḥ kartavyatāprāptinimittāni cittaduḥkhānītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He replied: 'There are many, numerous desires — wishes regarding what must be done — in this person who has not fulfilled his purpose, in this ordinary person. These afflictions whose passing leads in various directions — these mental sufferings arising from the failure to accomplish what must be done — are the afflictions leading in various directions. That is the meaning.

children.text: taiḥ pratipūrṇo 'smi /
children.translated_text: 'I am filled with them.'

children.text: ato nāśiṣyāmīti //3 //
children.translated_text: 'Therefore I shall not eat.' [3]
[Bhāṣya 4.10.3] <s>Upakosala</s>, afflicted by mental illness — mental suffering — resolved, made up his mind, to fast, to abstain from eating.

children.text: START ChUp 4,10.4
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.10.4]

children.text:
atha hāgnayaḥ samūdire |
tapto brahmacārī kuśalaṃ naḥ paryacārīt |
hantāsmai prabravāmeti tasmai hocuḥ |
prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahmeti || ChUp_4,10.4 ||
children.translated_text: Then the fires conferred among themselves: 'This <s>brahmacārī</s> has undergone great austerity and has served us well. Come, let us teach him.' They said to him: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>ka</s> (bliss) is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>kha</s> (space) is <s>Brahman</s>.' [ChUp 4.10.4]

children.text: ChUpBh_4,10.4 uktvā tūṣṇīṃbhūte brahmacāriṇyatha hāgnayaḥ śuśrūṣayā'varjitāḥ kāruṇyāviṣṭāḥ santasrayo 'pi samūdire saṃbhūyoktavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 4.10.4] When the <s>brahmacārī</s> had finished speaking and fallen silent, then the fires, won over by his devoted service and filled with compassion, all three conferred together — they spoke in unison.

children.text: hantedānīmasmai brahmacāriṇe 'smadbhaktāya duḥkhitāya tapasvine śraddadhānāya sarve 'nuśāsmo 'nuprabravāma brahmavidyāmiti /
children.translated_text: 'Come now, let us all instruct this <s>brahmacārī</s> who is devoted to us, who is suffering, who has undergone austerity, and who has faith — let us teach him <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>).'

children.text: evaṃ saṃpradhārya tasmai hocuruktavantaḥ prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahmeti //4 //
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, they said to him — they told him: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>ka</s> (bliss) is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>kha</s> (space) is <s>Brahman</s>.' [4]

children.text: START ChUp 4,10.5
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 4.10.5]

children.text:
sa hovāca |
vijānāmy ahaṃ yat prāṇo brahma |
kaṃ ca tu khaṃ ca na vijānāmīti |
te hocuḥ |
yad vāva kaṃ tad eva kham |
yad eva khaṃ tad eva kam iti |
prāṇaṃ ca hāsmai tad ākāśaṃ cocuḥ || ChUp_4,10.5 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'I understand that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>. But I do not understand <s>ka</s> and <s>kha</s>.' They replied: 'That which is <s>ka</s> (bliss) is indeed <s>kha</s> (space), and that which is <s>kha</s> (space) is indeed <s>ka</s> (bliss).' Thus they taught him <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Ākāśa</s> (space). [ChUp 4.10.5]

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,10.5 sa hovāca brahmacārī vijānāmyahaṃ yadbhavadbhiruktaṃ prasiddhapadārthakatvātprāṇo brahmeti /
yasminsati jīvanaṃ yadapagame ca na bhavatīti tasminvāyuviśeṣe loke rūḍho 'to yuktaṃ brahmatvaṃ tasya /
tena prasiddhapadārthakatvādvijānāmyahaṃ yatprāṇo brahmeti /
kaṃ ca tu khaṃ na vijānāmīti /
nanu kaṅkhaṃśabdayorapi sukhākāśaviṣayatvena prasiddhapadārthakatvameva, kasmādbrahmacāriṇo 'jñānam?nṛnaṃ sukhasya kaṃśabdavācyasya kṣaṇapradhvaṃsitvātkhaṃśabdavācyasya cā'kāśasyācetanasya kathaṃ brahmatvamiti manyate /
kathaṃ ca bhavatāṃ vākyamapramāṇaṃ syāditi /
ato na vijānāmītyāha /
tamevamuktantaṃ brahmacāriṇaṃ te hāgnayaḥ ūcuḥ yadvāva yadeva vayaṃ kamavocāma tadeva khamākāśamityevaṃ khena viśeṣyamāṇaṃ kaṃ viṣayendrisaṃyogajātsukhānnivartitaṃ syānnīleneva viśeṣyamāṇamutpalaṃ raktādibhyaḥ /
yadeva khamityākāśamavocāma tadeva ca kaṃ sukhamiti jānīhi /
evaṃ ca sukhena viśeṣyamāṇaṃ khaṃ bhautikādacetanātkhānnivartitaṃ syānnīlotpalavadeva /
sukhamākāśasthaṃ netarallaukikam /
ākāśaṃ ca sukhāśrayaṃ netaradbhautikamityarthaḥ /
nanvākāśaṃ cetsukhena viśeṣayitumiṣṭamastvanyataradeva viśeṣaṇaṃ yadvāva kaṃ tadeva khamityatiriktamitarat /
yadeva khaṃ tadeva kamiti pūrvaviśeṣeṇaṃ vā /
nanu sukhākāśayorubhayorapi laukikasukhākāśābhyāṃ vyāvṛttiriṣṭetyavocāma /
sukhenā'kāśe viśeṣite vyāvṛttirubhayorarthaprāptaiveti cetsatyamevaṃ kintu sukhena viśeṣitasyaivā'kāśasya dhyeyatvaṃ vihitaṃ na tvākāśaguṇasya viśeṣaṇasya sukhasya dhyeyatvaṃ vihitaṃ syāt /
viśeṣaṇopādānasya viśeṣyaniyantṛtvenaivopakṣayāt /
ataḥ khena sukhamapi viśeṣyate dhyeyatvāya /
kutaścaitanniścīyate /
kaṃśabdasyāpi brahmaśabdasambandhātkaṃ brahmeti /
yadi hi sukhaguṇaviśiṣṭasya khasya dhyeyatvaṃ vivakṣitaṃ syātkaṃ khaṃ brahmeti brūyuragnayaḥ prathamam /
na caivamuktavantaḥ /
kiṃ tarhi kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahmeti /
ato brahmacāriṇo mohāpanayanāya kaṅkhaṃśabdayoritaretaraviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatva nirdeśo yukta eva yadvāva kamityādiḥ /
tadetadagnibhiruktaṃ vākyārthamasmadbodhāya śrutirāha-prāṇaṃ ca hāsmai brahmacāriṇe /
children.translated_text: This meaning of the statement made by the fires — the <s>śruti</s> states for our understanding: '[They taught] <s>prāṇa</s> to this <s>brahmacārin</s>.'

children.text: tasyā'kāśastadākāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Its space' — that is the space [of <s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: prāṇasya sambandhyāśrayatvena hārda ākāśa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the space within the heart, as being the abode connected with <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: sukhaguṇavattvanirdeśāttaṃ cā'kāśaṃ sukhaguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ brahma tatsthaṃ ca prāṇaṃ brahmasamparkādeva brahmetyubhayaṃ prāṇaṃ cā'kāśaṃ ca samuccitya brahmaṇī ūcuragnaya iti //5//
children.translated_text: Because of the indication of possessing the quality of happiness, that space qualified by the quality of happiness is <s>Brahman</s>; and <s>prāṇa</s> abiding therein is also <s>Brahman</s> by virtue of its connection with <s>Brahman</s> — thus the fires taught both <s>prāṇa</s> and space together as <s>Brahman</s>. (5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.10.5:] He said: 'O <s>brahmacārin</s>, I understand what has been said by you, since it employs well-known terms — <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is <s>Brahman</s>. That in whose presence there is life and in whose absence there is none — in that particular form of wind (<s>vāyu</s>), the conventional usage in the world is established, hence its being <s>Brahman</s> is fitting. Therefore, since it employs well-known terms, I understand that <s>prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>. But I do not understand <s>ka</s> (happiness) and <s>kha</s> (space).' Objection: But the words <s>ka</s> and <s>kha</s> also employ well-known terms, denoting happiness and space respectively — so why does the <s>brahmacārin</s> not understand? [Reply:] He thinks: 'How can happiness, denoted by the word <s>ka</s>, which is momentarily perishable, and space, denoted by the word <s>kha</s>, which is insentient, be <s>Brahman</s>? And how can your statement be lacking in authority?' Therefore he says 'I do not understand.' To him, the <s>brahmacārin</s> who had spoken thus, those fires said: 'What indeed we called <s>ka</s> (happiness), that is the same as <s>kha</s> (space)' — meaning that <s>ka</s>, when qualified by <s>kha</s> (space), would be distinguished from happiness born of contact between sense organs and objects, just as a lotus qualified by 'blue' is distinguished from red and other [lotuses]. 'And what we called <s>kha</s> (space), know that to be the same as <s>ka</s> (happiness).' Thus, <s>kha</s> (space) when qualified by happiness would be distinguished from elemental, insentient space, just like a blue lotus. [The meaning is:] happiness that abides in space, not the other ordinary kind; and space that is the substratum of happiness, not the other elemental kind. Objection: If space is to be qualified by happiness, let the other qualifier be a separate one — 'what indeed is <s>ka</s>, that is <s>kha</s>' — this makes the other one additional. Or [alternatively]: 'what is <s>kha</s>, that is <s>ka</s>' — this would be a qualification of the former. [Reply:] We have already said that the mutual distinction of both happiness and space from ordinary happiness and space is intended. If it be said that when space is qualified by happiness, the distinction of both is already implied — true, that is so; however, only space qualified by the quality of happiness would be prescribed as an object of meditation, but happiness, being merely a qualifier, would not be prescribed as an object of meditation, since the function of adopting a qualifier is exhausted in delimiting the qualificand. Therefore, happiness too is qualified by space, for the purpose of meditation. How is this determined? Because the word <s>ka</s> also has a connection with the word <s>Brahman</s> — '<s>ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' For if the fires intended to prescribe as the object of meditation the space qualified by the quality of happiness, they would have said '<s>ka</s> <s>kha</s> <s>Brahman</s>' first. But they did not say thus. Rather, they said '<s>ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' Therefore, for removing the <s>brahmacārin's</s> confusion, the indication of mutual qualifier-qualificand relationship between the words <s>ka</s> and <s>kha</s> is entirely appropriate — beginning with 'what indeed is <s>ka</s>' and so forth.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
atha hainaṃ gārhapatyo 'nuśaśāsa pṛthivy agnir annam āditya iti |
ya eṣa āditye puruṣo dṛśyate so 'ham asmi sa eva aham asmi iti || ChUp_4,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire taught him: Earth, fire, food, and the sun — these [are my forms]. The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is seen in the sun — I am he. I am indeed he.' (ChUp 4.11.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,11.1 sambhūyāgnayo brahmacāriṇe brahmoktavantaḥ /
athānantaraṃ pratyekaṃ svasvaviṣayāṃ vidyāṃ vaktumārebhire /
tatrā'dāvenaṃ brahmacāriṇaṃ gārhapatyo 'gniranuśaśāsa /
pṛthivyagnirannamāditya iti mamaitāścasrastanavaḥ /
tatra ya āditya eṣa puruṣo dṛśyate so 'hamasmi gārhapatyo 'gniryaśca gārhapatyo 'gniḥ sa evāhamādityo puruṣo 'smīti /
punaḥ parāvṛttyā sa evāhamasmīti vacanam /
children.translated_text: The repetition 'I am indeed he' is by way of reaffirmation.

children.text: pṛthivyannayoriva bhojyatvalakṣaṇayoḥ sambandho na gārhapatyādityayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The connection between earth and food is through the characteristic of being enjoyed, just as [they relate to each other]; not so between the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire and the sun [which share a different relation].

children.text: attṛtvapaktṛtvaprakāśanadharmā aviśiṣṭā ityata ekatvamevānayoratyantam /
children.translated_text: Since the properties of consuming, cooking, and illuminating are not different [between them], the identity of these two (<s>Gārhapatya</s> and the sun) is indeed absolute.

children.text: pṛthivyannayostu bhojyatvenā'bhyāṃ sambandhaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: But the connection of earth and food with these two is through the characteristic of being enjoyed. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.11.1:] Having together taught <s>Brahman</s> to the <s>brahmacārin</s>, the fires then began to teach individually, each its own respective knowledge. There, first, the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire taught this <s>brahmacārin</s>: 'Earth, fire, food, and the sun — these are my four bodies.' Among these, 'the <s>puruṣa</s> who is seen in the sun — I am he, the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire; and he who is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire — I am that very <s>puruṣa</s> in the sun.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,11.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.11.2]

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste |
apahate pāpakṛtyām |
lokī bhavati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
na asya avarapuruṣāḥ kṣīyante |
upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo 'smiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca |
ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste || ChUp_4,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on this — he destroys sinful action. He becomes possessor of a world. He lives his full lifespan. He lives long. His descendants are not diminished. We nurture him in this world and in the next — he who, knowing thus, meditates on this.' (ChUp 4.11.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,11.2 sa yaḥ kaścidevaṃ yathoktaṃ gārhapatyamagnimannānnādatvena caturdhā pravibhaktamupāste so 'pahate vināśayati pāpakṛtyāṃ pāpaṃ karma /
lokī lokavāṃścāsmadāyena lokenā'gneyena tadvānbhavati yathā vayamiha ca loke /
sarvaṃ varṣaśatamāyureti prāpnoti jyogujjavalaṃ jīvati nāprakhyāta ityetat /
na cāsyāvarāśca te puruṣāścāsya viduṣaḥ santatijā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And his descendants — 'those who are inferior' means his offspring born in succession — the meaning is that they

children.text: na kṣīyante santatyucchedo na bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: are not diminished — meaning there is no cutting off of lineage.

children.text: kiṃ ca taṃ vayamupabhuñjāmaḥ pālayāmo 'smiṃśca loke jīvantamamuṣmiṃśca paraloke /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'we nurture him' — we protect him, the living one in this world, and in the next world as well.

children.text: ya etamevaṃ vidvānupāste yathektaṃ tasyaitatphalamityarthaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on this' — this is the fruit for one who does so — this is the meaning. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.11.2:] Whoever, knowing thus as described, meditates on the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire as fourfold — as food and eater — he destroys, eliminates sinful action, evil <s>karma</s>. He becomes possessor of a world — one who possesses a world, by our grace, the world of fire — he becomes endowed with that, just as we are in this world. He attains the full lifespan of one hundred years. He lives long, brightly — meaning not in obscurity.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,12.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.12.1]

children.text:
atha ha enam anvāhāryapacano 'nuśaśāsa āpo diśo nakṣatrāṇi candramā iti |
ya eṣa candramasi puruṣo dṛṣyate so 'ham asmi sa eva aham asmi iti || ChUp_4,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern sacrificial fire) taught him: Waters, the quarters, the stars, and the moon — these [are my forms]. The <s>puruṣa</s> who is seen in the moon — I am he. I am indeed he.' (ChUp 4.12.1)

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste |
apahate pāpakṛtyām |
lokī bhavati |
sarvam āyur eti |
jyog jīvati |
na asya avarapuruṣāḥ kṣīyante |
upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo 'smiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca |
ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste || ChUp_4,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on this — he destroys sinful action. He becomes possessor of a world. He lives his full lifespan. He lives long. His descendants are not diminished. We nurture him in this world and in the next — he who, knowing thus, meditates on this.' (ChUp 4.12.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,12.1,2 atha hainamanvāhāryapacano 'nuśaśāsa dakṣiṇāgnirāpo diśo nakṣatrāṇi candramā ityetā mama catasrastanavaścaturdhāhamanvāhāryapacana ātmānaṃ pravibhajyāvasthitaḥ tatra ya eṣa candramasi puruṣo dṛśyate so 'hamasmi sa evāhamasmīti pūrvavat /
annasambandhājjyotiṣṭvasāmānyāccānvāhāryapacanacandramasorekatvandakṣiṇā(ṇa) diksambandhācca /
apāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca pūrvavadannatvenaiva sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The connection of waters and stars is, as before, through the characteristic of being food.

children.text: nakṣatrāṇāṃ candramaso bhogyatvaprasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: This is because the stars are well-known as food for the moon.

children.text: apānnotpādakatvādannatvaṃ dakṣiṇāgneḥ pṛthivīvadgārhapatyasya /
children.translated_text: The quality of being food of the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) is because it produces food from water, just as the earth [does] for the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire.

children.text: samānamanyat //1-2 //
children.translated_text: The rest is the same. (1-2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.12.1-2:] Then this <s>brahmacārin</s> was taught by the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> — the southern fire (<s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>): 'Waters, the quarters, the stars, and the moon — these are my four bodies. I, the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s>, have divided myself fourfold and remain established thus. Among these, the <s>puruṣa</s> who is seen in the moon — I am he. I am indeed he' — as before. The identity of the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> and the moon is due to the connection with food and the commonality of luminosity; and also due to the connection with the southern quarter.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,13.1

atha hainam āhavanīyo 'nuśaśāsa prāṇa ākāśo dyaur vidyud iti |
ya eṣa vidyuti puruṣo dṛśyate so 'ham asmi sa evāham asmīti || ChUp_4,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire taught him: <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), space, heaven, and lightning — these [are my forms]. The <s>puruṣa</s> who is seen in lightning — I am he. I am indeed he.' (ChUp 4.13.1)
[Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.13.1]

children.text:
sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste |
apahate pāpakṛtyām |
lokī bhavati |
sarvam ayur eti |
jyog jīvati |
nāsyāvarapuruṣāḥ kṣīyante |
upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo 'smiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca |
ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste || ChUp_4,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on this — he destroys sinful action. He becomes possessor of a world. He lives his full lifespan. He lives long. His descendants are not diminished. We nurture him in this world and in the next — he who, knowing thus, meditates on this.' (ChUp 4.13.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,13.1,2 atha hainamāhavanīyo 'nuśaśāsa prāṇa ākāśo dyaurvidyuditi mamāpyetāścatasrastanavaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.13.1-2:] Then the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire taught him: '<s>Prāṇa</s>, space, heaven, and lightning — these too are my four bodies.'

children.text: ya eva vidyuti puruṣo dṛśyate so 'hamasmītyādi pūrvavatsāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is seen in lightning — I am he' — and so on, as before, because of the commonality [of attributes].

children.text: divā(dyvā) kāśayostvāśrayatvādvidyudāhavanīyayorbhogyatvenaiva sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The connection between heaven and space is through the relation of support; the connection between lightning and the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire is through the characteristic of being enjoyed.

children.text: samānamanyat //1-2 //
children.translated_text: The rest is the same. (1-2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya trayodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,14.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.14.1]

children.text:
te hocuḥ |
upakosalaiṣā somya te 'smadvidyātmavidyā ca |
ācāryas tu te gatiṃ vakteti |
ājagāma hāsyācāryaḥ |
tam ācāryo 'bhyuvādopakosala 3 iti || ChUp_4,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'They said: "O <s>Upakosala</s>, dear one, this is our knowledge for you — the knowledge of ourselves — and the knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). But your teacher will tell you the way." His teacher arrived. The teacher addressed him: "O <s>Upakosala</s>!"' (ChUp 4.14.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,14.1 te punaḥ sambhūyocurhepakosalaiṣā somya te tavāsmadvidyāgnividyetyarthaḥ /
ātmavidyā pūrvoktā prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahmeti ca /
children.translated_text: And the knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> is what was previously stated: '<s>prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: ācāryastu te gatiṃ vaktā vidyāphalaprāptaya ityuktvoparemuragnayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But your teacher will tell you the way (<s>gati</s>) — the path for attaining the fruit of this knowledge' — having said this, the fires ceased.

children.text: ājagāma hāsyā'cāryaḥ kālena /
children.translated_text: His teacher arrived in due course of time.

children.text: taṃ ca śiṣyamācāryo 'bhyuvādopakosala3 iti //1 //
children.translated_text: And the teacher addressed this disciple: 'O <s>Upakosala</s>!' (1)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.14.1:] Then, having come together again, they said: 'O <s>Upakosala</s>, dear one, this knowledge of ours — meaning the knowledge of the fires — is for you.'

children.text: START ChUp 4,14.2-3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.14.2-3]

children.text:
bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva |
brahmavida iva somya mukhaṃ bhāti |
ko nu tvānuśaśāseti |
ko nu mānuśiśyād bho itīhāpeva nihnute |
ime nūnam īdṛśā anyādṛśā itīhāgnīn abhyūde |
kiṃ nu somya kila te 'vocann iti || ChUp_4,14.2 ||
children.translated_text: '"Blessed one!" he responded. "Your face shines like that of a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, dear one. Who has taught you?" "Who indeed could teach me, sir?" — thus he seemingly denies it. "These [fires], which now look like this, were different before" — thus he pointed to the fires. "What indeed did they tell you, dear one?"' (ChUp 4.14.2)

children.text:
idam iti ha pratijajñe |
lokān vāva kila somya te 'vocan |
ahaṃ tu te tad vakṣyāmi yathā puṣkarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyanta evam evaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyata iti |
bravītu me bhagavān iti |
tasmai hovāca || ChUp_4,14.3 ||
children.translated_text: '"This" — thus he acknowledged. "They told you about the worlds, dear one. But I shall tell you that [knowledge] whereby, just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so sinful action does not cling to one who knows thus." "Please tell me, Blessed One." Then he spoke to him.' (ChUp 4.14.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,14.2,3 bhagava iti ha pratiśuśrāva /
brahmavida iva somya te mukhaṃ prasannaṃ bhāti ko nu tvānuśaśāsetyuktaḥ pratyāha /
ko nu mānuśiṣyādanuśāsanaṃ kuryādbho bhagavaṃstvayi proṣita itīhāpeva nihnute 'panihnuta iveti vyavahitena sambandho na cāpanihnute na ca yatāvadagnibhiruktaṃ bravītītyabhiprāyaḥ /
kathamime 'gnayo mayā paricaritā uktavanto nūnaṃ yatastvāṃ dṛṣṭvā vepamānā ivedṛśā dṛśyante pūrvamanyādṛśāḥ santa itīhāgnīnabhyūde 'bhyuktavānkākvāgnīndarśayan /
children.translated_text: 'How [is it that] these fires, which were tended by me, have spoken? For now, upon seeing you, they appear trembling as if they look like this, whereas previously they were different' — thus he pointed to the fires, showing them with a gesture.

children.text: kiṃ nu somya kila te tubhyamavocannagnaya iti pṛṣṭa ityevamidamuktavanta ityevaṃ ha pratijajñe pratijñātavānpratīkamātraṃ kiñcinna sarvaṃ yathoktamagnibhiruktamavocat /
children.translated_text: 'What indeed, dear one, did the fires tell you?' Being asked thus, 'this' — thus he acknowledged, admitted — only a hint, a brief indication — he did not report everything exactly as said by the fires.

children.text: yata āhā'cāryo lokānvāva pṛthivyādīnhe somya kila te 'vocanna brahma sākalyena /
children.translated_text: Therefore the teacher said: 'They told you about the worlds — earth and the rest — O dear one, but not <s>Brahman</s> in its completeness.'

children.text: ahaṃ tu te tubhyaṃ tadbrahma yadicchasi tvaṃ śrotuṃ vakṣyāmi, śṛṇu tasya mayocyamānasya brahmaṇo jñānamāhātmyaṃ yathā puṣkarapalāśe padmapatra āpo na śilaṣyanta evaṃ yatā vakṣyāmi brahmaivaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śilaṣyate na sambadhyata ityevamuktavatyācārya āhopakosalo bravītu me bhagavāniti tasmai hovācā'cāryaḥ //2-3 //
children.translated_text: 'But I shall tell you — to you — that <s>Brahman</s>, if you wish to hear. Listen to the greatness of knowing the <s>Brahman</s> that I shall speak of: just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf (<s>puṣkara-palāśa</s>), so sinful action does not cling to — does not attach itself to — one who knows the <s>Brahman</s> that I shall teach thus.' When the teacher had spoken thus, <s>Upakosala</s> said: 'Please tell me, Blessed One.' Then the teacher spoke to him. (2-3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.14.2-3:] 'Blessed one!' — thus he responded. 'Your face shines radiantly, dear one, like that of a knower of <s>Brahman</s>. Who taught you?' Being asked thus, he replied: 'Who indeed could teach me — who could give instruction — sir, while you were away?' — thus he seemingly denies it. The word 'seemingly' (<s>iva</s>) connects with the separated [phrase] — he does not actually deny it, nor does he accurately report what the fires said — this is the intended meaning.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya caturdaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,15.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.15.1]

children.text:
ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca |
etad amṛtam abhayam etad brahmeti |
tad yady apy asmin sarpir vodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmanī eva gacchati || ChUp_4,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The person that is seen in the eye — this is the <s>Ātman</s>,' he said. 'This is the immortal, the fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>. Even if one pours ghee or water into [the eye], it goes only to the eyelids.' (ChUp 4.15.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,15.1 ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate nivṛttacakṣurbhirbrahmacaryādisādhanasampannaiḥ śāntairvivekibhirdṛṣṭerdraṣṭā"cakṣuṣaścakṣuḥ"ityādiśrutyantarāt /
nanvagnibhiruktaṃ vitathaṃ yata ācāryastu te gatiṃ vakteti gatimātrasya vaktetyavocanbhaviṣyadviṣayāparijñānaṃ cāgnīnam /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
sukhākāśasyaivākṣiṇi dṛśyata iti draṣṭuranuvādāt /
eṣa ātmā prāṇināmiti hovācaivamuktavānetadyadevā'tmatattvamavocāma /
children.translated_text: 'This is the <s>Ātman</s> of all living beings,' he said — thus he spoke [about] the very same reality of the <s>Ātman</s> that we spoke of.

children.text: etadamṛtamamaraṇadharmyavināśyata evābhayaṃ yasya hi vināśāśaṅkā tasya bhayopapattistadabhāvādabhayamata evaitadbrahma bṛhadanantamiti /
children.translated_text: This is immortal — having the nature of not dying, imperishable; and fearless — for one who has the apprehension of destruction, fear is possible; in the absence of that, [it is] fearless; therefore this is <s>Brahman</s> — great, infinite.

children.text: kiñcāsya brahmaṇo 'kṣipuruṣasya māhātmyaṃ tattatra puruṣasya sthāne 'kṣiṇi yadyapyasminyarpirvodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmanī eva gacchati pakṣmāveva gacchati na cakṣuṣā sambandhyate padmapatreṇevodakam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, [there is] this greatness of <s>Brahman</s>, the person in the eye: in the place of the person — in the eye — even if one pours ghee or water, it goes only to the eyelids — it goes only to the lashes and does not come into contact with the eye, like water on a lotus petal.

children.text: sthānasyāpyetanmāhātmyaṃ kiṃ punaḥ sthānino 'kṣipuruṣasya nirañjanatvaṃ vaktavyamityabhiprāyaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: If even the abode has such greatness, how much more need be said about the stainless nature of the indweller — the person in the eye — this is the intended meaning. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.15.1:] The person that is seen in the eye — seen by those who have withdrawn their [external] sight, who are endowed with the means such as <s>brahmacarya</s>, who are tranquil and discriminating — is the seer of seeing, 'the eye of the eye,' as known from other <s>śruti</s> passages. [Objection:] But the fires said something false, since the teacher said 'I will tell you the path' — they said only that [he] would tell the path, and the fires did not have full knowledge of the subject. [Reply:] This is no defect — because the statement 'the one seen in the eye' is merely a reiteration of the seer [already identified as] the space of bliss in the heart.

children.text: START ChUp 4,15.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.15.2]

children.text:
etaṃ saṃyadvāma ity ācakṣate |
etaṃ hi sarvāṇi vāmāny abhisaṃyanti |
sarvāṇy enaṃ vāmāny abhisaṃyanti ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_4,15.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'They call him <s>Saṃyadvāma</s> (the one to whom all desirable things come together). For all desirable things come together to him. All desirable things come together to one who knows thus.' (ChUp 4.15.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,15.2 etaṃ yathoktaṃ puruṣaṃ saṃyadvāma ityācakṣate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.15.2:] This person as described is called <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>.

children.text: kasmāt /
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: yasmādetaṃ sarvāṇi vāmāni vananīyāni saṃbhajanīyāni śobhanānyabhisaṃyantyabhisaṅgacchantītyataḥ saṃyadvāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because all <s>vāma</s>s — things that are to be desired, to be worshipped, beautiful — come together (<s>abhisaṃyanti</s>) to him — therefore [he is called] <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>.

children.text: tathaivaṃvidamenaṃ sarvāṇi vāmānyabhisaṃyanti ya evaṃ veda //2 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, all desirable things come together to one who knows thus. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 4,15.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.15.3]

children.text:
eṣa u eva vāmanīḥ |
eṣa hi sarvāṇi vāmāni nayati |
sarvāṇi vāmāni nayati ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_4,15.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He is also <s>Vāmanī</s> (the one who leads desirable things). For he leads all desirable things [to beings]. One who knows thus leads all desirable things.' (ChUp 4.15.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,15.3 eṣa u eva vāmanīryasmādeṣa hi sarvāṇi vāmāni puṇyakarmaphalāni puṇyānurūpaṃ prāṇibhyo nayati prāpayati vahati cā'tmadharmatvena /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.15.3:] He is indeed <s>Vāmanī</s>, because he leads — conveys, carries — all <s>vāma</s>s (desirable things), the fruits of meritorious actions, to living beings in accordance with their merit, as his own inherent function.

children.text: viduṣaḥ phalaṃ-sarvāṇi vāmāni nayati ya evaṃ veda //3 //
children.translated_text: The fruit for the knower: one who knows thus leads all desirable things. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 4,15.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.15.4]

children.text:
eṣa u eva bhāmanīḥ |
eṣa hi sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti |
sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_4,15.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'He is also <s>Bhāmanī</s> (the one who shines). For he shines in all worlds. One who knows thus shines in all worlds.' (ChUp 4.15.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,15.4 eṣa u eva bhāmanīreṣa hi yasmātsarveṣu lokeṣvādityacandrāgnyādirūpairbhāti dīpyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.15.4:] He is indeed <s>Bhāmanī</s>, because he shines — illumines — in all worlds in the forms of the sun, moon, fire, and so on.

children.text: "tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti"iti śruterato bhāmāni nayatīti bhāmanīḥ /
children.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s>: 'By his light all this shines' — therefore he leads lights (<s>bhāmāni</s>), hence <s>Bhāmanī</s>.

children.text: ya evaṃ vedāsāvapi sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti //4 //
children.translated_text: One who knows thus also shines in all worlds. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 4,15.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.15.5]

children.text:
atha yad u caivāsmiñ chavyaṃ kurvanti yadi ca nārciṣam evābhisaṃbhavanti |
arciṣo 'haḥ |
ahna āpūryamāṇapakṣam |
āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaḍ udaṅṅ eti māsāṃs tān |
māsebhyaḥ saṃvatsaram |
saṃvatsarād ādityam |
ādityāc candramasam |
candramaso vidyutam |
tat puruṣo 'mānavaḥ |
sa enān brahma gamayati |
eṣa devapatho brahmapathaḥ |
etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavam āvartaṃ nāvartante nāvartante || ChUp_4,15.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, whether or not they perform funeral rites for such a one, they pass into the light.
