From the light [they pass] to the day; from the day to the bright half of the month; from the bright half to the six months during which the sun moves northward; from those months to the year; from the year to the sun; from the sun to the moon; from the moon to lightning. There is a person who is non-human. He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>. This is the path of the gods, the path to <s>Brahman</s>. Those who proceed by this path do not return to this human cycle — they do not return.' (ChUp 4.15.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,15.5 athedānīṃ yathoktabrahmavido gatirucyate /
yadyadi u caivāsminnevaṃvidi śavyaṃ śavakarma mṛte kurvanti yadi ca na kurvanti ṛtvijaḥ sarvathāpyevaṃvittena śavakarmaṇākṛtenāpi pratibaddho na brahma[dmaṭaprāpnoti /
na ca kṛtena śavakarmaṇāsya kaścanābhyadhiko lokaḥ /
"na karmaṇā vardhate no kanīyān"iti śrutyantarāt /
śavakarmaṇyanādaraṃ darśayanvidyāṃ stauti na punaḥ śavakarmaivaṃvido na kartavyamiti /
akriyamāṇe hi śavakarmaṇi karmaṇā phalārambhe pratibandhaḥ kaścidanumīyate 'nyatra /
yata iha vidyāphalārambhakāle śavakarma syādvā na veti vidyāvato 'pratibandhena phalārambhaṃ darśayati /
ye sukhākāśamakṣisthaṃ saṃyadvāmo vāmanīrbhāmanīrityevaṅguṇamupāsate prāṇasahitāmagnividyāṃ ca teṣāmanyatkarma bhavatu mā vā bhūtsarvathāpi te 'rciṣamevābhisambhavantyarcirabhimāninīṃ devatāmabhisambhavanti pratipadyanta ityarthaḥ /
arciṣo 'rcirdevatāyā aharaharabhimāninīṃ devatāmahna āpūryamāṇapakṣaṃ śuklapakṣadevatāmāpūryamāṇapakṣādyānṣaṇmāsānudaṅṅuttarāṃ diśameti savitā tānmāsānuttarāyaṇadevatāṃ tebhyo māsebhyaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsaradevatāṃ tataḥ saṃvatsarādādidityamādityāccandramasaṃ candramaso vidyutaṃ tattatrasthāṃstānpuruṣaḥ kaścidbrahmalokādetyāmānavo mānavyāṃ sṛṣṭau bhavo mānavo na mānavo 'mānavaḥ sa puruṣa enānbrahma satyalokasthaṃ gamayati gantṛgantavyagamayitṛtvavyapadeśebhyaḥ /
sanmātrabrahmaprāptau tadanupapatteḥ /
brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyetīti hi tatra vaktuṃ nyāyyam /
sarvabhedanirāsena sanmātrapratipattiṃ vakṣyati /
na cādṛṣṭo mārgo 'gamanāyopatiṣṭhate /
"sa enamavidito na bhunakti"iti śrutyantarāt /
eṣa devapathaḥ devairarcirādibhiḥ gamayitṛtvenādhikṛtaiḥ upalakṣitaḥ panthā devapatha ucyate /
children.translated_text: This is the path of the gods — the path marked by the gods, namely the light and so on, who are designated as guides — is called the <s>Devapatha</s> (path of the gods).

children.text: brahma gantavyaṃ tena copalakṣita iti brahmapathaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is the destination, and [the path] is marked by that — hence <s>Brahmapatha</s> (path to <s>Brahman</s>).

children.text: etena pratipadyamānā gacchanto brahmemaṃ mānavaṃ manusambandhinaṃ manoḥ sṛṣṭilakṣaṇamāvata nā'vartanta āvartante 'smiñjananamaraṇaprabandhacakrārūḍhā ghaṭīyantravatpunaḥ punarityārvatastaṃ na pratipadyante /
children.translated_text: Those proceeding by this [path] — going to <s>Brahman</s> — do not return to this human cycle, the cycle belonging to <s>Manu</s>, characterized by <s>Manu's</s> creation. They do not return — they do not again mount the wheel of the continuous stream of birth and death, revolving like a water-wheel, again and again — they do not reach that [cycle].

children.text: nāvartante nā'vartante iti dviruktiḥ saphalāyā vidyāyāḥ parisamāptipradarśanārthā //5//
children.translated_text: The repetition 'they do not return, they do not return' is for the purpose of indicating the completion of the fruitful knowledge. (5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.15.5:] Now the path of one who knows <s>Brahman</s> as described is stated. Whether or not funeral rites are performed for such a knower when he dies — whether the <s>Ṛtvij</s> priests perform them or not — in either case, such a knower is not obstructed from attaining <s>Brahman</s> even without funeral rites being performed. Nor does performing funeral rites give him any higher world. [This is known] from another <s>śruti</s>: 'He is not increased by action nor diminished.' By showing disregard for funeral rites, [the text] praises knowledge — but it does not mean that funeral rites should not be performed for such a knower. For when funeral rites are not performed, some obstruction to the fruition of karma is inferred elsewhere. Since here, at the time of the fruition of knowledge, whether funeral rites are performed or not, [the text] shows the unobstructed fruition for the knower. Those who meditate on the space of bliss residing in the eye with the qualities <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>, <s>Vāmanī</s>, <s>Bhāmanī</s>, along with the <s>Prāṇa</s>-fire knowledge — whether they have other ritual karma or not — in all cases they attain the light, meaning they reach the deity presiding over the light. From the light to the deity presiding over the day; from the day to the deity of the bright half-month; from the bright half to the six months during which the sun moves northward — to the deity of the <s>Uttarāyaṇa</s>; from those months to the year — to the deity of the year; from that to the sun; from the sun to the moon; from the moon to lightning. There, a certain person comes from <s>Brahmaloka</s> — he is non-human (<s>amānava</s>), not born in the human creation. That person leads them to <s>Brahman</s> dwelling in <s>Satyaloka</s> — [this is known] from the references to a goer, a destination, and a guide. [This is not attainment of] pure Being as <s>Brahman</s>, for that would be contradictory. For there it would be proper to say: 'Being already <s>Brahman</s>, one attains <s>Brahman</s>.' [The text] will speak of the realization of pure Being through the negation of all distinctions. And an unseen path does not serve for non-going. From another <s>śruti</s>: 'The unknown does not enjoy him.'

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya pañcadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
eṣa ha vai yajño yo 'yaṃ pavate |
eṣa ha yann idaṃ sarvaṃ punāti |
yad eṣa yann idaṃ sarvaṃ punāti |
tasmād eṣa eva yajñaḥ |
tasya manaś ca vāk ca vartanī || ChUp_4,16.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'This indeed is the sacrifice — this [wind] that blows. It purifies all this. Because it, moving, purifies all this — therefore it alone is the sacrifice. Mind and speech are its two tracks.' (ChUp 4.16.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,16.1 rahasyaprakaraṇe prasaṅgādāraṇyakatvasāmānyācca yajñe kṣata utpanne vyāhṛtayaḥ prāyaścittārthā vidhātavyāstadabhijñasya cartvijo brahmaṇo maunamityata idamārabhyate-eṣa ha vā eṣa vāyuryo 'yaṃ pavate 'yaṃ yajñaḥ /
ha vā iti prasiddhārthāvadyotakau nipātau /
vāyupratiṣṭho hi yajñaḥ prasiddhaḥ śrutiṣu /
"svāhā vātedhāḥ /
" "ayaṃ vai yajño yo 'yaṃ pavate"ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
vāta eva hi calanātmavatvātkriyāsamavāyī /
"vāta eva yajñasyā'rambhako vātaḥ pratiṣṭhā"iti ca śravaṇāt /
eṣa ha yangacchaṃścalannidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatpunāti pāvayati śodhayati /
na hyacalataḥ śuddhirasti /
doṣanirasanaṃ calato hi dṛṣṭaṃ na sthirasya /
yadyasmācca yannaṣa idaṃ sarvaṃ punāti tasmādeṣa eva yajño yatpunātīti /
tasyāsyaivaṃ viśiṣṭasya yajñasya vākca mantroccāraṇe vyāpṛtā /
manaśca yathābhūtārthajñāne vyāpṛtam /
children.translated_text: and mind — employed in the knowledge of things as they truly are —

children.text: te ete vāṅmanase vartanī mārgau yābhyāṃ yajñastāyamānaḥ pravartate te vartanī /
children.translated_text: these two, speech and mind, are the two tracks — the two paths by which the sacrifice, being extended, proceeds — [hence] they are called tracks.

children.text: prāṇāpānaparicalanavatyā hi"vācaścittasya cottarottarakramo yadyajñaḥ"iti hi śrutyantaram /
children.translated_text: For [the sacrifice proceeds] through the movement of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, and the successive progression of speech and mind — as another <s>śruti</s> says: 'That which is the successive progression of speech and mind — that is the sacrifice.'

children.text: ato vāṅmanasābhyāṃ yajño vartata iti vāṅmanase vartanī ucyete yajñasya //1//
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the sacrifice operates through speech and mind, speech and mind are called the two tracks of the sacrifice. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.16.1:] In the context of the esoteric teaching, by connection and similarity with [texts taught] in the forest, [the following is taught:] when a fault occurs in the sacrifice, the <s>Vyāhṛti</s>s are to be prescribed as expiation — [but] the <s>Brahman</s> priest who knows this should remain silent — therefore this [section] is begun. This wind that blows — this is the sacrifice. The particles 'ha vā' illuminate a well-known meaning. For it is well-known in the <s>śruti</s>s that the sacrifice is established in the wind — from <s>śruti</s>s such as '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Vāta</s>,' 'This indeed is the sacrifice — this that blows,' and so on. Wind alone, being of the nature of movement, is inherently connected with action. And from the statement: 'Wind is the initiator of the sacrifice; wind is [its] foundation.' This [wind], moving, purifies — cleanses — all this world. For there is no purification without movement. The removal of defects is seen in what moves, not in what is stationary. Because it, moving, purifies all this — therefore it alone is the sacrifice, since it purifies. Of this sacrifice thus qualified, speech — employed in the utterance of mantras —

children.text: START ChUp 4,16.2-3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.16.2-3]

children.text:
tayor anyatarāṃ manasā saṃskaroti brahmā |
vācā hotādhvaryur udgātānyatarām |
sa yatropākṛte prātaranuvāke purā paridhānīyāyā brahmā vyavavadati || ChUp_4,16.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Brahman</s> priest prepares one of these [tracks] with the mind. The <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>Adhvaryu</s>, and <s>Udgātṛ</s> prepare the other with speech. When, after the morning recitation has begun, the <s>Brahman</s> priest speaks before the concluding hymn —' (ChUp 4.16.2)

children.text:
anyatarām eva vartanīṃ saṃskaroti |
hīyate 'nyatarā |
sa yathaikapād vrajan ratho vaikena cakreṇa vartamāno riṣyaty evam asya yajño riṣyati |
yajñaṃ riṣyantaṃ yajamāno 'nu riṣyati |
sa iṣṭvā pāpīyān bhavati || ChUp_4,16.3 ||
children.translated_text: '— he prepares only one track. The other is damaged. Just as a one-legged person walking, or a chariot moving on one wheel, is impaired — so his sacrifice is impaired. When the sacrifice is impaired, the patron of the sacrifice is impaired along with it. He who sacrifices thus becomes worse off.' (ChUp 4.16.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,16.3 tayorvartanyoranyatarāṃ vartanīṃ manasā vivekajñānavatā saṃskaroti brahmartvigvācā vartanyā hotādhvaryurudgātetyete trayo 'pyṛtvijo 'nyatarāṃ vāglakṣaṇāṃ vartanīṃ vācaiva saṃskurvanti /
tatraivaṃ sati vāṅmanase vartanī saṃskārye yajñe /
atha sa brahmā yatra yasminkāla upākṛte prārabdhe prātaranuvāke śasre purā pūrvaṃ paridhānīyāyā ṛco brahmaitasminnantare kāle vyavavadati maunaṃ parityajati yadi tadānyatarāmeva vā#agvartanīṃ saṃskaroti brahmaṇāsaṃskriyamāṇā manovartanī hīyate vinaśyati cchidrībhavatyanyatarā /
sa yajño vāgvartanyaivānyatarayā vartitumaśaknuvanriṣyati /
kathamivetyāha /
sa yathaikapātpuruṣo brajangacchannadhvānaṃ riṣyati, ratho vaikena cakreṇa vartamāno gacchanriṣyatyevamasya yajamānasya kubrahmaṇā yajño riṣyati vinaśyati /
yajñaṃ riṣyantaṃ yajamāno 'riṣyati /
children.translated_text: When the sacrifice is impaired, the patron of the sacrifice is impaired along with it.

children.text: yajñaprāṇo hi yajamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the patron's life depends on the sacrifice.

children.text: ato yukto yajñareṣe reṣastasya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is fitting that when the sacrifice is impaired, he too is impaired.

children.text: sa taṃ yajñamiṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ pāpīyānpāpataro bhavati //2-3 //
children.translated_text: Having performed such a sacrifice, he becomes worse off — more sinful. (2-3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.16.2-3:] Of the two tracks, the <s>Brahman</s> priest — endowed with discriminative knowledge — prepares one track with the mind. The <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>Adhvaryu</s>, and <s>Udgātṛ</s> — these three priests — prepare the other track characterized by speech, through speech alone. In that case, both speech and mind being the two tracks to be prepared in the sacrifice — now, when the <s>Brahman</s> priest, at the time when the morning recitation (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>) has been begun, before the concluding hymn (<s>paridhānīyā</s>), breaks his silence during that interval — then he prepares only the speech-track; the mind-track, not being prepared by the <s>Brahman</s> priest, is damaged — becomes defective. That sacrifice, unable to proceed on only one track — the speech-track alone — is impaired. How so? Just as a one-legged person walking — going on the road — is impaired, or a chariot moving on one wheel is impaired — so the sacrifice of this patron is impaired, destroyed by the incompetent <s>Brahman</s> priest.

children.text: START ChUp 4,16.4-5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.16.4-5]

children.text:
atha yatra upākṛte prātaranuvāke na purā paridhānīyāyā brahmā vyavavadaty ubhe eva vartanī saṃskurvanti |
na hīyate 'nyatarā || ChUp_4,16.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'But when, after the morning recitation has begun, the <s>Brahman</s> priest does not speak before the concluding hymn — they prepare both tracks. Neither is damaged.' (ChUp 4.16.4)

children.text:
sa yathobhayapād vrajan ratho vobhābhyāṃ cakrābhyāṃ vartamānaḥ pratitiṣṭhaty evam asya yajñaḥ pratitiṣṭhati yajñaṃ pratitiṣṭhantaṃ yajamāno 'nu pratitiṣṭhati |
sa iṣṭvā śreyān bhavati || ChUp_4,16.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as a two-legged person walking, or a chariot moving on both wheels, is firmly established — so his sacrifice is firmly established. When the sacrifice is established, the patron is established along with it. He who sacrifices thus becomes better off.' (ChUp 4.16.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,16.4,5 atha punaryatra brahmā vidvānmaunaṃ parigṛhya vāgvisargamakurvanvartate yāvatparidhānīyāyā na vyavavadati tathaiva sarvartvija ubhe eva vartanī saṃskurvanti na hīyate 'nyatarāpi /
kimivetyāha /
children.translated_text: How so? He gives [two] illustrations:

children.text: pūrvoktaviparītau dṛṣṭāntau /
children.translated_text: The illustrations are the opposite of those stated before.

children.text: evamasya yajamānasya yajñaḥ svavartanībhyāṃ vartamānaḥ pratitiṣṭhati svenā'tmanāvinaśyanvartata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the sacrifice of this patron, proceeding on both its tracks, is firmly established — meaning it continues without being destroyed, in its own nature.

children.text: yajñaṃ pratitiṣṭhantaṃ yajamāno 'nupratitiṣṭhati sa yajamāna evaṃ maunavijñānavadbrahmopetaṃ yajñamiṣṭvā śreyānbhavati śreṣṭho bhavatītyarthaḥ //4-5 //
children.translated_text: The sacrificer follows the sacrifice that is being established — the meaning is that the sacrificer, having performed a sacrifice endowed with <s>Brahman</s> possessing silence and knowledge in this manner, becomes better, becomes the most excellent. (4-5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.16.4-5:] But when the <s>Brahman</s> priest, being learned, having adopted silence and not releasing speech, continues thus until the concluding hymn without speaking — then all the priests prepare both tracks; neither one is damaged.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya ṣoḍaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 4,17.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.17.1]

children.text:
prajāpatir lokān abhyatapat |
teṣāṃ tapyamānānāṃ rasān prāvṛhat |
agniṃ pṛthivyāḥ |
vāyum antarikṣāt |
ādityaṃ divaḥ || ChUp_4,17.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Prajāpati</s> brooded over the worlds. From them, as they were being heated, he extracted their essences: fire from earth, wind from the atmosphere, and the sun from heaven.' (ChUp 4.17.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,17.1 atra brahmaṇo maunaṃ vihitaṃ tadreṣe brahmatvakarmaṇi cānyasmiṃśca hotrādikarmareṣe vyāhṛtihomaḥ prāyaścittamiti tadarthaṃ vyāhṛtayo vidhātavyā ityāha-prajāpatirlokānabhyatapallokānuddiśya tatra sārajighṛkṣayā dhyānalakṣaṇaṃ tapaścacāra /
teṣāṃ tapyamānānāṃ lokānāṃ rasānsārarūpānprāvṛhaduddhṛtavāñjagrāhetyarthaḥ /
kān /
children.translated_text: Which [essences]?

children.text: agniṃ rasaṃ pṛthivyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Fire — as the essence of earth.

children.text: vāyumantarikṣāt /
children.translated_text: Wind from the atmosphere.

children.text: ādityaṃ divaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: The sun from heaven. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.17.1:] Here, silence has been prescribed for <s>Brahman</s> (the officiating priest). When there is a defect in the <s>Brahman's</s> ritual duty or in any other duty of the <s>Hotṛ</s> and other priests, the oblation with <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) is the expiation — for that purpose the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> are to be enjoined — hence the text says: <s>Prajāpati</s> brooded over the worlds — he performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity) in the form of meditation, directing it toward the worlds with the desire to extract their essence. From those worlds, as they were being heated, he extracted — drew out, grasped — their essences, their quintessential forms — this is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 4,17.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.17.2]

children.text:
sa etās tisro devatā abhyatapat |
tāsāṃ tapyamānānāṃ rasān prāvṛhat |
agner ṛcaḥ |
vāyor yajūṃṣi |
sāmāny ādityāt || ChUp_4,17.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He brooded over these three deities. From them, as they were being heated, he extracted their essences: the <s>Ṛc</s> verses from fire, the <s>Yajus</s> formulas from wind, and the <s>Sāman</s> chants from the sun.' (ChUp 4.17.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,17.2 punarapyevamevamagnyādyāḥ sa etāstisro devatā uddiśyābhyatapat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.17.2:] Again, in the same manner, directing his attention toward fire and the other [deities], he brooded over these three deities.

children.text: tato 'pi sāraṃ rasaṃ trayīvidyāṃ jagrāha //2 //
children.translated_text: From them too he grasped the further essence — the threefold knowledge (<s>trayī vidyā</s>). (2)

children.text: START ChUp 4,17.3-4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.17.3-4]

children.text:
sa etāṃ trayīṃ vidyām abhyatapat |
tasyās tapyamānāyā rasān prāvṛhat |
bhūr ity ṛgbhyaḥ |
bhuvar iti yajurbhyaḥ |
svar iti sāmabhyaḥ || ChUp_4,17.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He brooded over this threefold knowledge. From it, as it was being heated, he extracted its essences: <s>Bhūḥ</s> from the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> from the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, and <s>Svaḥ</s> from the <s>Sāman</s> chants.' (ChUp 4.17.3)

children.text:
tad yady ṛkto riṣyed bhūḥ svāheti gārhapatye juhuyāt |
ṛcām eva tadrasenarcāṃ vīryeṇarcāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'If there is a defect arising from the <s>Ṛc</s> [portion of the sacrifice], one should offer in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire saying "<s>Bhūḥ Svāhā</s>." By the essence of the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, by the power of the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, he repairs the defect of the sacrifice [arising] from the <s>Ṛc</s> [portion].' (ChUp 4.17.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,17.3,4 sa etāṃ punarabhyatapattrayīṃ vidyām /
tasyāstapyamānāyā rasaṃ bhūriti vyāhṛtimṛgbhyo jagrāha /
bhuvariti vyāhṛtiṃ yajurbhyaḥ /
svariti vyāhṛtiṃ sāmabhyaḥ /
ata eva lokadevavedarasā mahāvyāhṛtayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hence the great <s>vyāhṛtis</s> are the essences of the worlds, the deities, and the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: atastattatra yajñe yadyṛkta ṛksambandhādṛṅnimittaṃ riṣyedyajñaḥ kṣataṃ prāpnuyādbhūḥ svāheti gārhapatye juhuyāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in that sacrifice, if there is a defect arising from the <s>Ṛc</s> — a defect connected with the <s>Ṛc</s>, caused by the <s>Ṛc</s> — if the sacrifice suffers damage, one should offer in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire saying '<s>Bhūḥ Svāhā</s>.'

children.text: sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ /
children.translated_text: That is the expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) in that case.

children.text: katham, ṝcāmeva taditi kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ, rasenarcāṃ vīryeṇaujasarcāṃ yajñasya ṛksambandhino yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ vicchinnaṃ kṣatarūpamutpannaṃ sandadhāti pratisandhatte //3-4 //
children.translated_text: How? 'By the essence of the <s>Ṛc</s> verses' — this qualifies the ritual action — by the power, by the vigour of the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, he repairs — mends, restores — the damage, the broken state that has arisen in the sacrifice connected with the <s>Ṛc</s>. (3-4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.17.3-4:] He again brooded over this threefold knowledge. From it, as it was being heated, he grasped the essence — the <s>vyāhṛti</s> <s>Bhūḥ</s> from the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, the <s>vyāhṛti</s> <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> from the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, and the <s>vyāhṛti</s> <s>Svaḥ</s> from the <s>Sāman</s> chants.

children.text: START ChUp 4,17.5-6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.17.5-6]

children.text:
atha yadi yajuṣṭo riṣyed bhuvaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnau juhuyāt |
yajuṣām eva tadrasena yajuṣāṃ vīryeṇa yajuṣāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'If there is a defect arising from the <s>Yajus</s> [portion], one should offer in the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) saying "<s>Bhuvaḥ Svāhā</s>." By the essence of the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, by the power of the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, he repairs the defect of the sacrifice [arising] from the <s>Yajus</s> [portion].' (ChUp 4.17.5)

children.text:
atha yadi sāmato riṣyet svaḥ svāhety āhavanīye juhuyāt |
sāmnām eva tadrasena sāmnāṃ vīryeṇa sāmnāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'If there is a defect arising from the <s>Sāman</s> [portion], one should offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire saying "<s>Svaḥ Svāhā</s>." By the essence of the <s>Sāman</s> chants, by the power of the <s>Sāman</s> chants, he repairs the defect of the sacrifice [arising] from the <s>Sāman</s> [portion].' (ChUp 4.17.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,17.5,6 atha yadi yajuṣṭo yajurnimittaṃ riṣyedbhuvaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnau juhuyāt /
tathā sāmanimitte reṣe svaḥ svāhetyāhavanīye juhuyāt /
tathā pūrvavadyajñaṃ sandadhāti /
brahmanimitte tu reṣe triṣvagniṣu /
tisṛbhirvyāhṛtibhirjuhuyāt /
children.translated_text: One should offer with all three <s>vyāhṛtis</s>.

children.text: trayyā hi vidyāyāḥ sa reṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: For that defect pertains to the entire threefold knowledge.

children.text: "atha kena brahmatvamityanayaiva trayyā vidyayā"iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'And by what means does one attain the role of <s>Brahman</s>? By this very threefold knowledge.'

children.text: nyāyāntaraṃ vā mṛgyaṃ brahmatvanimitte reṣe //5-6 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, another method should be sought for a defect caused by the <s>Brahman</s> priest. (5-6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.17.5-6:] If the defect arises from the <s>Yajus</s> — caused by the <s>Yajus</s> — one should offer in the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> saying '<s>Bhuvaḥ Svāhā</s>.' Likewise, when the defect is caused by the <s>Sāman</s>, one should offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> saying '<s>Svaḥ Svāhā</s>.' Similarly, as before, one repairs the sacrifice. But when the defect is caused by <s>Brahman</s> (the officiating priest), [one should offer] in all three fires.

children.text: START ChUp 4,17.7-8
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.17.7-8]

children.text:
tad yathā lavaṇena suvarṇaṃ saṃdadhyāt |
suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena trapu trapuṇā sīsaṃ sīsena lohaṃ lohena dāru dāru carmaṇā || ChUp_4,17.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as one would join gold with salt [borax], silver with gold, tin with silver, lead with tin, iron with lead, wood with iron, and wood with leather.' (ChUp 4.17.7)

children.text:
evam eṣāṃ lokānām āsāṃ devatānām asyās trayyā vidyāyā vīryeṇa yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti |
bheṣajakṛto ha vā eṣa yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati || ChUp_4,17.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'Thus, by the power of these worlds, of these deities, and of this threefold knowledge, he repairs the defect of the sacrifice. That sacrifice is truly healed where such a knower serves as <s>Brahman</s> priest.' (ChUp 4.17.8)

children.text:
ChUpBh_4,17.7,8 tadyathā lavaṇena suvarṇaṃ sandadhyāt /
kṣāreṇa ṭaṅkaṇādinā khare;mṛdutvakaraṃ hi tat /
suvarṇena rajatamaśakyasandhānaṃ sandadhyāt /
rajatena tathā trapu trapuṇā sīsaṃ sīsena loha lohena dāru dāru carmaṇā carmabandhanena /
evameṣāṃ lokānāmāsāṃ devatānāmasyāsrayyā vidyāyā vīryeṇa rasākhyenaujasā yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ sandadhāti /
bheṣajakṛto ha vā eṣa yajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: That sacrifice is truly healed.

children.text: rogārta iva pumāṃścikitsakena suśikṣitenaiṣa yajño bhavati /
children.translated_text: Like a man afflicted with disease [is healed] by a well-trained physician — so is this sacrifice.

children.text: ko 'sau /
children.translated_text: Which [sacrifice] is that?

children.text: yatra yasminyajña evaṃvidyathoktavyāhṛtihomaprāyaścittavidbrahmartvigbhavati sa yajña ityarthaḥ //7-8 //
children.translated_text: The sacrifice in which a <s>Brahman</s> priest who knows thus — who knows the <s>vyāhṛti</s> oblation expiation as described — serves as the officiating <s>Brahman</s> — that is the meaning. (7-8)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.17.7-8:] Just as one would join gold with salt — with an alkali such as borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) and the like; for that makes what is crude into something refined. With gold one would join silver — which is otherwise impossible to join. With silver, tin; with tin, lead; with lead, iron; with iron, wood; and wood with leather — by means of a leather binding. Thus, by the power — the vigour called essence — of these worlds, of these deities, and of this threefold knowledge, he repairs the defect of the sacrifice.

children.text: START ChUp 4,17.9
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.17.9]

children.text:
eṣa ha vā udakpravaṇo yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati |
evaṃvidaṃ ha vā eṣā brahmāṇam anu gāthā |
yato yata āvartate tat tad gacchati || ChUp_4,17.9 ||
children.translated_text: 'That sacrifice inclines northward where such a knower serves as <s>Brahman</s> priest. Regarding such a knowing <s>Brahman</s> priest, there is this verse: wherever it turns aside, there he goes.' (ChUp 4.17.9)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,17.9 kiñcaiṣa ha vā udakpravaṇa udaṅnimno dakṣiṇocchrāyo yajño bhavati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.17.9:] Furthermore, this sacrifice inclines northward — slopes downward toward the north and rises toward the south.

children.text: uttaramārgapratipattiheturityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is that it becomes the cause for attaining the northern path [of the gods].

children.text: yatraivaṃvidbrahmā bhavatyevaṃvidaṃ ha vai brahmāṇamṛtvijaṃ pratyeṣānugāthā brahmaṇaḥ stutiparā /
children.translated_text: Where such a knowing <s>Brahman</s> priest officiates — regarding such a knowing <s>Brahman</s> priest, this verse (<s>gāthā</s>) praises the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].

children.text: yato yata āvartate karma pradeśādṛtvijāṃ yajñaḥ kṣatībhavaṃstattadyajñasya kṣatarūpaṃ pratisandadhatprāyaścittena gacchati paripālayatītyetat //9 //
children.translated_text: 'Wherever the sacrifice turns aside' — from whatever part of the ritual the sacrifice of the priests suffers damage — 'there he goes' — meaning he goes to that damaged part of the sacrifice and, through expiation, restores and protects it. (9)

children.text: START ChUp 4,17.10
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.17.10]

children.text: mānavo brahmaivaika ṛtvikkurūnaśvābhirakṣatyevaṃviddha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ sarvāṃś
children.translated_text: 'The descendant of <s>Manu</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> priest alone, the single <s>ṛtvik</s> (officiating priest), protects the <s>Kurus</s> like a mare [protects her foal]. Indeed, such a knowing <s>Brahman</s> priest protects the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all

children.text: cartvijo 'bhirakṣati tasmādevaṃvidameva brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta nānevaṃvidaṃ nānevaṃvidam //10//
children.translated_text: the officiating priests. Therefore, one should appoint only such a knower as <s>Brahman</s> priest, and never one who does not know thus, never one who does not know thus.' (10)

children.text:
mānavaḥ |
brahmaivaika ṛtvik kurūn aśvābhirakṣati |
evaṃvid dha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ sarvāṃś cartvijo 'bhirakṣati |
tasmād evaṃvidam eva brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta nānevaṃvidaṃ nānevaṃvidam || ChUp_4,17.10 ||
children.translated_text: 'The descendant of <s>Manu</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> priest alone, the single <s>ṛtvik</s>, protects the <s>Kurus</s> like a mare. Indeed, such a knowing <s>Brahman</s> priest protects the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all the officiating priests. Therefore, one should appoint only such a knower as <s>Brahman</s> priest, never one who does not know thus, never one who does not know thus.' (ChUp 4.17.10)

children.text: ChUpBh_4,17.10 mānavo bhrahmā maunācaraṇānmananādvā jñāvanattvāttato brahmaivaikartvikkurūnkartṝn /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.17.10:] The descendant of <s>Manu</s> (<s>mānava</s>) — the <s>Brahman</s> priest, [so called] because of the practice of silence (<s>mauna</s>), or because of reflection (<s>manana</s>), or because of being endowed with knowledge — therefore the <s>Brahman</s> priest alone, the single <s>ṛtvik</s>, [protects] the <s>Kurus</s> — the performers,

children.text: yoddhṝnārūḍhānaśvā vaḍavā yathābhirakṣatyevaṃviddha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ sarvāṃścartvijo 'bhirakṣati tatkṛtadoṣāpanayanāt /
children.translated_text: the warriors mounted [on horses] — just as a mare (<s>aśvā</s>) protects [her foal] — so indeed such a knowing <s>Brahman</s> priest protects the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all the officiating priests, by removing defects caused by them.

children.text: yata evaṃviśiṣṭo brahmā vidvāṃstasmādevaṃvidameva yathoktavyāhṛtyādividaṃ brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta nānevaṃvidaṃ kadācaneti /
children.translated_text: Since such a distinguished <s>Brahman</s> priest who is learned [in this way is so important], therefore one should appoint only such a knower — one who knows the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> and the rest as described — as <s>Brahman</s> priest, and never one who does not know thus.

children.text: dvirabhyāso 'dhyāyaparisamāptyarthaḥ //10 //
children.translated_text: The double repetition is for the purpose of concluding the chapter. (10)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi caturthādhyāyasya saptadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth section of the fourth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: iti śrīmadgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaparamahaṃsapar ivrājakācāryaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau cchāndogyopaniṣadvivaraṇe caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fourth chapter in the commentary on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>, composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the supreme <s>Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya</s>, disciple of the venerable <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>.

children.text: atha pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the fifth chapter.

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.1.1]

children.text:
yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaś ca ha vai śreṣṭhaś ca bhavati |
prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca || ChUp_5,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows the eldest and the best becomes indeed the eldest and the best. <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is indeed the eldest and the best.' (ChUp 5.1.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,1.1
saguṇa brahmavidyāyā uttarā gatiruktā /
athedānīṃ pañcame 'dhyāye pañcāgnivido gṛhasthasyordhvaretasāṃ ca śraddhālūnāṃ vidyāntaraśīlināṃ tāmeva gatimanūdyānyā dakṣiṇadiksambandhinī kevalakarmiṇāṃ dhūmādilakṣaṇā punarāvṛttirūpā tṛtīyā ca tataḥ kaṣṭatarā saṃsāragatirvairāgyahetorvaktavyetyārabhyate /
prāṇaḥ śreṣṭho vāgādibhyaḥ prāṇo vāva saṃvarga ityādi ca bahuśo 'tīte granthe prāṇagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam /

sa kathaṃ śreṣṭho vāgādiṣu sarvaiḥ saṃhatyakāritvāviśeṣe?kathaṃ ca tasyopāsanamiti tasya śreṣṭhatvādiguṇavidhitsayedamanantaramārabhyate-yo ha vai kaścijjyeṣṭhaṃ ca prathamaṃ vayasā vāva jyeṣṭhaśca vayasā vāgādibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: How is it the best among speech and the rest, when all [organs] function collectively without distinction? And how should one meditate on it? With the intention of enjoining its qualities such as being the best, the following section begins immediately: 'He who indeed knows the eldest' — whoever [knows] the eldest, the first in age — indeed, <s>prāṇa</s> is the eldest in age compared to speech and the rest.

children.text: garbhasthe hi puruṣe prāṇasya vṛttirvāgādibhyaḥ pūrvaṃ labdhātmikā bhavati yayā garbho vivardhate cakṣurādisthānāvayavaniṣpattau satyāṃ paścādvāgādīnāṃ vṛttilābha iti prāṇo jyeṣṭho vayasā bhavati /
children.translated_text: For in the person dwelling in the womb, the function of <s>prāṇa</s> is obtained prior to speech and the rest — by which the embryo grows. Only after the formation of the bodily parts that are the seats of the eye and other [organs] do speech and the rest subsequently acquire their functions — thus <s>prāṇa</s> is the eldest in age.

children.text: śreṣṭhatvaṃ tu pratipādayiṣyati suhaya ityādinidarśanena /
children.translated_text: But its being the best will be demonstrated through the illustration beginning with 'su-haya' (excellent horse).

children.text: ataḥ prāṇa eva jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaścāsminkāryakaraṇasaṅghāte //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>prāṇa</s> alone is the eldest and the best in this aggregate of body and organs. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.1.1:] The higher path of the knower of <s>Brahman</s> with qualities (<s>saguṇa</s>) has been stated. Now, in the fifth chapter, the following topics are to be discussed in order to produce dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>): the very same path is restated for the householder who knows the five fires (<s>pañcāgni-vidyā</s>), for celibates (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>), for those endowed with faith, and for those who practice other forms of knowledge; another path connected with the southern direction, characterized by smoke and the rest, involving return [to rebirth], belonging to mere ritualists; and a third path, even more wretched than that, the course of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Throughout the preceding text, the mention of <s>prāṇa</s> has been made many times — '<s>prāṇa</s> is the best among speech and the rest,' '<s>prāṇa</s> is indeed the absorber (<s>saṃvarga</s>),' and so on.

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.1.2]

children.text:
yo ha vai vasiṣṭhaṃ veda vasiṣṭho ha svānāṃ bhavati |
vāg vāva vasiṣṭhaḥ || ChUp_5,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭha</s>) becomes the most excellent among his own [people]. Speech is indeed the most excellent.' (ChUp 5.1.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.2 yo ha vai vasiṣṭhaṃ vasitṛtamamācchādayitṛtamaṃ vasumattamaṃ vā yo veda sa tathaiva vasiṣṭho ha bhavati svānāṃ jñātīnām /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.1.2:] He who knows the most excellent — the most overcoming, the most covering, or the most wealthy — he becomes likewise the most excellent among his own kinsmen.

children.text: kastarhi vasiṣṭha ityāha /
children.translated_text: What then is the most excellent? The text says:

children.text: vāgvāva vasiṣṭho vāgmino hi puruṣā vasantyabhibhavantyanyānvasumattamāścāto vāgvasiṣṭhaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: Speech is indeed the most excellent — for men who are eloquent dominate others and are the most wealthy; therefore speech is the most excellent. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.1.3]

children.text:
yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhaty asmiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca |
cakṣur vāva pratiṣṭhā || ChUp_5,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) stands firm in this world and in the next. The eye is indeed the foundation.' (ChUp 5.1.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.3 yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda sa cāsmiṃlloke 'muṣmiṃśca pare pratitiṣṭhati ha /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.1.3:] He who knows the foundation stands firm in this world and in the next world.

children.text: kā tarhi pratiṣṭhetyāha-cakṣurvāva pratiṣṭhā /
children.translated_text: What then is the foundation? The text says: the eye is indeed the foundation.

children.text: cakṣuṣā hi paśyansame ca durge ca pratitiṣṭhati yasmādataḥ pratiṣṭhā cakṣuḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: For by seeing with the eye, one stands firm on both level and difficult ground — therefore the eye is the foundation. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.1.4]

children.text:
yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai kāmāḥ padyante daivāś ca mānuṣāś ca |
śrotraṃ vāva saṃpat || ChUp_5,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows prosperity (<s>saṃpad</s>) — for him both divine and human desires are fulfilled. The ear is indeed prosperity.' (ChUp 5.1.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.4 yo ha vai sampadaṃ veda tasmā asmai daivāśca mānuṣāśca kāmāḥ sampadyante ha /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.1.4:] He who knows prosperity — for him, divine and human desires are fulfilled.

children.text: kā tarhi sampadityāha-śrotraṃ vāva sampat /
children.translated_text: What then is prosperity? The text says: the ear is indeed prosperity.

children.text: yasmācchrotreṇa vedā gṛhyante tadarthavijñānaṃ ca tataḥ karmāṇi kriyante tataḥ kāmasampadityevaṃ kāmasampaddhetutvācchrotraṃ vāva saṃpat //4 //
children.translated_text: Because through the ear the <s>Vedas</s> are apprehended, from that comes the understanding of their meaning, from that rituals are performed, and from that comes the fulfilment of desires — thus, being the cause of the fulfilment of desires, the ear is indeed prosperity. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.1.5]

children.text:
yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatanaṃ ha svānāṃ bhavati |
mano ha vā āyatanam || ChUp_5,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows the abode (<s>āyatana</s>) becomes the abode of his own [people]. The mind is indeed the abode.' (ChUp 5.1.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.5 yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedā'yatanaṃ ha svānāṃ bhavatyāśrayo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.1.5:] He who knows the abode becomes the abode of his own people — meaning he becomes their refuge.

children.text: kiṃ tadāyatanamityāha-mano ha vā āyatanam /
children.translated_text: What is that abode? The text says: the mind is indeed the abode.

children.text: indriyopahṛtānāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ bhoktrarthānāṃ pratyayarūpāmāṃ mana āyatanamāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind is the abode — the support — of sense objects brought by the organs, [which are] for the enjoyer, in the form of cognitions.

children.text: ato mano ha vā āyatanamityuktam //5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore it is said: the mind is indeed the abode. (5)

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.1.6]

children.text:
atha ha prāṇā ahaṃśreyasi vyūdire |
ahaṃ śreyān asmy ahaṃ śreyān asmīti || ChUp_5,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) disputed among themselves about their own superiority: "I am the best! I am the best!"' (ChUp 5.1.6)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.6 atha ha prāṇā evaṃ yathoktaguṇāḥ santo 'haṃśreyasyahaṃ śreyānasmyahaṃ śreyānasmītyetasminprayojane vyūdire nānā viruddhaṃ codira uktavantaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.1.6:] Then the <s>prāṇas</s>, possessing the qualities described above, disputed — spoke variously, in contradiction with one another — regarding the claim 'I am the best, I am the best' — they declared [this]. (6)

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.1.7]

children.text:
te ha prāṇāḥ prajāpatiṃ pitaram etyocuḥ bhagavan ko naḥ śreṣṭha iti |
tān hovāca |
yasmin va utkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭhataram iva dṛśyeta sa vaḥ śreṣṭha iti || ChUp_5,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>s) went to <s>Prajāpati</s>, their father, and said: "O Blessed One, who is the best among us?" He said to them: "He, upon whose departure the body appears to be in its worst state — he is the best among you."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.7]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.7 te ha - tai haivaṃ vivadamānā ātmanaḥ śreṣṭhatvavijñānāya prajāpatiṃ pitaraṃ janayitāraṃ kañcidetyocuruktavanto he bhagavanko no 'smākaṃ madhye śreṣṭho 'bhyadhiko guṇairityevaṃ pṛṣṭavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.1.7] They — the vital breaths, disputing thus among themselves, in order to ascertain their own pre-eminence, went to <s>Prajāpati</s>, their father, their progenitor — someone [in that role] — and said: 'O Blessed One, who among us is the best, the most excellent in qualities?' — thus they asked.

children.text: tānpitovāca ha yasminvo yuṣmākaṃ madhye utkrānte śarīramidaṃ pāpiṣṭhamivātiśayena jīvato 'pi, samutkrāntaprāṇaṃ tato 'pi pāpiṣṭhataramivātiśayena dṛṣyate kuṇapamaspṛśyamaśuci dṛśyeta sa vo yuṣmākaṃ śreṣṭha ityavocatkākvā tadduḥkhaṃ parijihīrṣuḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: The father said to them: 'He, upon whose departure from among you, this body appears to be in its worst state — exceedingly [deteriorated] even though [the person is] still alive — and upon the departure of the vital breath, [it appears] even more exceedingly [deteriorated] — like a corpse, untouchable and impure — he is the best among you.' [He spoke thus] wishing to resolve that doubt. [End of section 7.]

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.8-11
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.8-11]

children.text:
sā ha vāg uccakrāma |
sā saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya paryetyovāca |
katham aśakatarte maj jīvitum iti |
yathā kalā avadantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti |
praviveśa ha vāk || ChUp_5,1.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then speech departed. Having been away for a year, it came back and said: "How were you able to live without me?" [They replied:] "Like mute persons, not speaking, [yet] breathing with the breath, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind — thus [we lived]." Speech re-entered.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.8]

children.text:
cakṣur hoccakrāma |
tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya paryetyovāca |
katham aśakatarte maj jīvitum iti |
yathāndhā apaśyantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti |
praviveśa ha cakṣuḥ || ChUp_5,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: 'The eye departed. Having been away for a year, it came back and said: "How were you able to live without me?" [They replied:] "Like blind persons, not seeing, [yet] breathing with the breath, speaking with speech, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind — thus [we lived]." The eye re-entered.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.9]

children.text:
śrotraṃ hoccakrāma |
tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya paryetyovāca katham aśakatarte maj jīvitum iti |
yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā dhyāyanto manasaivam iti |
praviveśa ha śrotram || ChUp_5,1.10 ||
children.translated_text: 'The ear departed. Having been away for a year, it came back and said: "How were you able to live without me?" [They replied:] "Like deaf persons, not hearing, [yet] breathing with the breath, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, thinking with the mind — thus [we lived]." The ear re-entered.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.10]

children.text:
mano hoccakrāma |
tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya paryetyovāca |
katham aśakatarte maj jīvitum iti |
yathā bālā amanasaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇaivam iti |
praviveśa ha manaḥ || ChUp_5,1.11 ||
children.translated_text: 'The mind departed. Having been away for a year, it came back and said: "How were you able to live without me?" [They replied:] "Like infants, without mind, [yet] breathing with the breath, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear — thus [we lived]." The mind re-entered.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.11]

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,1.8,9,10,11 tathokteṣu pitrā prāṇeṣu sā ha vāguccakrāmotkrāntavatī /
sā cotkramya saṃvatsaramātraṃ proṣya svavyāpārānnivṛttā satī punaḥ paryetyetarānprāṇānuvāca kathaṃ kena prakāreṇāśakata śaktavanto yūyaṃ madṛte māṃ vinā jīvituṃ dhārayitumātmānamiti te hocuryathākalā ityādi /
akalā mūkā yathā loke 'vadanto vācā jīvanti /
katham?prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaścakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivaṃ sarvakaraṇaceṣṭāṃ kurvanta ityarthaḥ /
evaṃ vayamajīviṣmetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus we lived — that is the meaning.

children.text: ātmano 'śreṣṭhatāṃ prāṇeṣu buddhvā praviveśa ha vākpunaḥ svavyāpāre pravṛttā babhūvetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having understood its own non-pre-eminence among the vital breaths, speech re-entered — meaning it resumed its own function.

children.text: samānamanyaccakṣurheccakrāma śrotraṃ hoccakrāma mano hoccakrāmetyādi /
children.translated_text: The same [explanation applies to] the rest — 'the eye departed,' 'the ear departed,' 'the mind departed,' and so forth.

children.text: yathā bālā amanaso 'prarūḍhamanasa ityarthaḥ // 8-11 //
children.translated_text: 'Like infants, without mind (<s>amanasaḥ</s>)' means those whose minds have not yet developed — that is the meaning. [End of sections 8-11.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.1.8-11] When the vital breaths were thus addressed by the father — speech departed, went out. Having departed and stayed away for the duration of one year, having ceased from its own function, it came back and said to the other vital breaths: 'How — by what means — were you able to live, to sustain yourselves, without me?' They said: 'Like mute persons (<s>akalā</s>)' — <s>akalā</s> means those who are mute, who —

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.12
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.12]

children.text:
atha ha prāṇa uccikramiṣan sa yathā suhayaḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkūn saṃkhided evam itarān prāṇān samakhidat |
taṃ hābhisametyocuḥ |
bhagavann edhi |
tvaṃ naḥ śreṣṭho 'si |
motkramīr iti || ChUp_5,1.12 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then, when the vital breath (<s>Prāṇa</s>) was about to depart — just as a fine horse would pull out the pegs of its tethering — it pulled out the other vital breaths [along with it]. They came together to it and said: "O Blessed One, be [our lord]. You are the best among us. Do not depart."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.12]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.12 evaṃ parīkṣiteṣu vāgādiṣvathānantaraṃ ha sa mukhyaḥ prāṇa uccikramiṣannutkramitumicchankimakarodityucyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.1.12] When speech and the others had thus been tested — then, next, the chief vital breath (<s>mukhya prāṇa</s>), wishing to depart — what did it do? It is said:

children.text: yathā loke suhayaḥ śobhano 'śvaḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkūnpādabandhanakīlānparīkṣaṇāyā'rūḍhena kaśyāhataḥ sansaṅkhidetsamutkhanet samutpāṭayet, evamitarānvāgādīnprāṇānsamakhidatsamuddhṛtavān /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, a fine horse (<s>suhaya</s>), a noble steed — being struck with a whip by its mounted rider — would pull out, uproot, the pegs that bind its feet, for testing [its strength] — so too [the chief vital breath] pulled out the other vital breaths — speech and the rest — it uprooted them.

children.text: te prāṇāḥ sañcālitāḥ santaḥ svasthāne sthātumanutsahamānā abhisametya mukhyaṃ prāṇaṃ tamūcurheṃ bhagavannedhi bhava naḥ svāmī yasmāttvaṃ no 'smākaṃ śreṣṭho 'si mā cāsmāddehādutkramīriti //12 //
children.translated_text: Those vital breaths, being shaken, unable to remain in their own places, came together to the chief vital breath and said: 'O Blessed One, be [our lord]; be our master, since you are the best among us. And do not depart from this body.' [End of section 12.]

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.13-14
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.13-14]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ vāg uvāca |
yad ahaṃ vasiṣṭho 'smi tvaṃ tadvasiṣṭho 'sīti |
atha hainaṃ cakṣur uvāca |
yad ahaṃ pratiṣṭhāsmi tvaṃ tatpratiṣṭhāsīti || ChUp_5,1.13 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then speech said to it: "In that I am the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭha</s>), you are thereby the most excellent." Then the eye said to it: "In that I am the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), you are thereby the foundation."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.13]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ śrotram uvāca |
yad ahaṃ saṃpad asmi tvaṃ tatsaṃpad asīti |
atha hainaṃ mana uvāca |
yad aham āyatanam asmi tvaṃ tadāyatanam asīti || ChUp_5,1.14 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the ear said to it: "In that I am prosperity (<s>sampat</s>), you are thereby prosperity." Then the mind said to it: "In that I am the abode (<s>āyatana</s>), you are thereby the abode."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.14]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,1.13,14 atha hainaṃ vāgādayaḥ prāṇasya śreṣṭhatvaṃ kāryeṇā'pādayanta āhurbalimiva haranto rājñe viśaḥ /
kathaṃ, vāk tāvaduvāca yadahaṃ vasiṣṭho 'smi /
children.translated_text: How? First, speech said: 'In that I am the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭha</s>)' —

children.text: yaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ yadvasiṣṭhatvaguṇāsmītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'yat' (in that) qualifies the action — the meaning is: 'in that I possess the quality of being the most excellent.'

children.text: tvaṃ tadvasiṣṭhastena vasiṣṭhatvaguṇo 'jñānānmameti mayābhimata ityetat /
children.translated_text: 'You are thereby the most excellent' — by that quality of being the most excellent, [which] through ignorance [was] considered mine — that is the meaning.

children.text: tathottareṣu yojyaṃ cakṣuḥśrotramanaḥsu // 13-14 //
children.translated_text: The same [explanation] should be applied to the subsequent [statements] regarding the eye, the ear, and the mind. [End of sections 13-14.]
[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.1.13-14] Then speech and the others established the pre-eminence of the vital breath through [its] effects — like subjects offering tribute to a king.

children.text: START ChUp 5,1.15
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.15]

children.text:
na vai vāco na cakṣūṃṣi na śrotrāṇi na manāṃsīty ācakṣate |
prāṇā ity evācakṣate |
prāṇo hy evaitāni sarvāṇi bhavati || ChUp_5,1.15 ||
children.translated_text: 'People do not call them "speeches" or "eyes" or "ears" or "minds"; they call them "vital breaths" (<s>prāṇa</s>s). For the vital breath alone becomes all of these.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.1.15]

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,1.15 śruteridaṃ vaco yuktamidaṃ vāgādibhirmukhyaṃ prāṇaṃ pratyabhihitaṃ yasmānna vai loke vāco na cakṣūṃṣi na śrotrāṇi na manāṃsīti vāgādīni karaṇānyācakṣate laukikā āgamajñā vā /
kiṃ tarhi?prāṇā ityevā'cakṣate kathayanti yasmātprāṇo hyevaitāni sarvāṇi vāgādīni karaṇajātāni bhavatyato mukhyaṃ prāmaṃ pratyanurūpameva vāgādibhiruktamiti prakaraṇārthamupasañjihīrṣati /
nanu kathamidaṃ yuktaṃ cetanāvanta iva puruṣā ahaṃśreṣṭhatāyai vivadanto 'nyonyaṃ spardheranniti /
na hi cakṣurādīnāṃ vācaṃ pratyākhyāya pratyekaṃ vadanaṃ sambhavati /
tathāpagamo dehātpunaḥ praveśo brahmagamanaṃ prāṇastutirvopapadyate /
tatrāgnyādicetanāvaddevatādhiṣṭhitatvādvāgādīnāṃ cetanāvattvaṃ tāvatsiddhamāgamataḥ. tārkikasamayavirodha iti ceddeha ekasminnanekacetanāvattve /
na /
īśvarasya nimittakāramatvābhyupagamāt /
ye tāvadīśvaramabhyupagacchanti tārkikāste mana ādikāryakaramānāmādhyātmikānāṃ bāhyānāṃ ca pṛthivyādīnāmīśvarādhiṣṭhitānāmeva niyamena pravṛttimicchanti rathādivat /
na cāsmābhiragnyādyāścetanāvatyo 'pi devatā adhyātmaṃ bhoktryo 'bhyupagamyante, kiṃ tarhi,kāryakaraṇavatīnāṃ hi tāsāṃ prāṇaikadevatābhedānāmadhyātmādhibhūtādhidaivabhedakoṭivikalpānāmadhyakṣatāmātreṇa niyanteśvaro 'bhyupagamyate /
sa hyakaraṇaḥ /
"hiraṇyagarbhaṃ janayāmāna pūrvam"ityādi ca śvetāśvatarīyāḥ paṭhanti /
bhoktā karmaphalasambandhī dehe tadvilakṣaṇo jīva iti vakṣyāmaḥ /
vāgādīnāṃ ceha saṃvādaḥ kalpito viduṣo 'nvayavyatirekābhyāṃ prāṇaśreṣṭhatānirdhāraṇārtham /
yathā loke puruṣā anyonyamātmanaḥ śreṣṭhatāyai vivadamānāḥ kañcidguṇaviśeṣābhijñaṃ pṛcchanti ko naḥ śreṣṭho guṇairiti /
tenoktā ekaikaśyenādaḥ kāryaṃ sādhayitumudyacchata yenādaḥ kāryaṃ sādhyate sa vaḥ śreṣṭha ityuktāstathaivodyacchanta ātmano 'nyasya vā śreṣṭhavāṃ nirdhārayanti /
children.translated_text: Therefore [the father] said: 'Each of you, one by one, should endeavor to accomplish that function; he by whom that function is accomplished — he is the best among you.' Thus addressed, they endeavored accordingly — each determining that another, not itself, is the most excellent.

children.text: tatemaṃ saṃvyavahāraṃ vāgādiṣu kalpitavatī śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>śruti</s> has devised this transaction regarding speech and the others.

children.text: kathaṃ nāma vidvānvāgādīnāmekaikasyābhāve 'pi jīvanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na tu prāṇasyeti prāṇaśreṣṭhatāṃ pratipadyateti /
children.translated_text: For how would a wise person — [seeing that] when any one of speech and the others is absent, life [still] continues, but not [when] the vital breath [is absent] — not recognize the pre-eminence of the vital breath?

children.text: tathāca śrutiḥ kauṣītakinām -"jīvati vāgapeto mūkānhi pasyāmo jīvati cakṣurapeto 'ndhānhi paśyāmo jīvati śrotrāpeto badhirānhi paśyāmo jīvati manopeto bālānhi paśyāmo jīvati bāhucchinno jīvatyūrucchinnaḥ"ityādyā //15//
children.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> of the <s>Kauṣītakin</s>s [says]: 'One lives without speech — for we see mute persons; one lives without sight — for we see blind persons; one lives without hearing — for we see deaf persons; one lives without mind — for we see infants; one lives with arms cut off; one lives with legs cut off' — and so forth. [End of section 15.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.1.15] This statement of scripture is fitting — what was said by speech and the others to the chief vital breath — because people in the world, whether ordinary or versed in scripture, do not call them 'speeches,' 'eyes,' 'ears,' or 'minds' — [that is,] they do not call the sense-faculties by these names. Rather, they call them 'vital breaths' (<s>prāṇa</s>s) — that is what they say. For the vital breath alone becomes all these — speech and the rest, the entire class of sense-faculties. Therefore, the chief —

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.2.1]

children.text:
sa hovāca kiṃ me 'nnaṃ bhaviṣyatīti |
yat kiṃcid idam ā śvabhya ā śakunibhya iti hocuḥ |
tad vā etad anasyānnam |
ano ha vai nāma pratyakṣam |
na ha vā evaṃvidi kiṃcanānannaṃ bhavatīti || ChUp_5,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'He [the vital breath] said: "What will be my food?" [They replied:] "Whatever there is here — including [that eaten by] dogs and birds." That indeed is the food of <s>Ana</s> (the vital breath). <s>Ana</s> is indeed the well-known name [of the vital breath]. For one who knows this, nothing is not food.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.2.1]

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,2.1 sa hovāca mukhyaḥ prāṇaḥ kiṃ me 'nnaṃ bhaviṣyatīti /
mukhyaṃ prāṇaṃ praṣṭāramiva kalpayitvā vāgādīnprativaktṝniva kalpayantī śrutirāha-yadidaṃ loke 'nnajātaṃ prasiddhamā śvabhiḥ sahā'śakunibhyaḥ saha śakunibhiḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ yadannaṃ tattavānnamiti hocurvāgādaya iti /
prāṇasya sarvamannaṃ prāṇo 'ttā sarvasyānnasyetyevaṃ pratipattaye kalpitākhyāyikārūpādvyāvṛtya svena śrutirūpeṇā'ha-tadvā etadyatkiñcilloke prāṇibhirannamadyate 'nasya prāṇasya tadannaṃ prāṇenaiva tadadyata ityarthaḥ /
sarvaprakāraceṣṭāvyāptiguṇapradarśanārthamana iti prāṇasya pratyakṣaṃ nāma /
prādyupasargapūrvatve hi viśeṣagatireva syāt /
tathāca sarvānnānāmatturnāmagrahaṇamitīdaṃ pratyakṣaṃ nāmāna iti sarvānnānāmattuḥ sākṣādabhidhānam /
na ha vā evaṃvidi yathoktaprāṇavidi prāṇo 'hamasmi sarvabhūtasthaḥ sarvānnānāmatteti tasminnevaṃvidi ha vai kiñcana kiñcidapi prāṇibhirādyaṃ sarvairanannamannādyaṃ na bhavati sarvamevaṃvidyannaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.2.1] He — the chief vital breath — said: 'What will be my food?' The <s>śruti</s>, treating the chief vital breath as if it were the questioner and speech and the others as if they were the respondents, says: 'Whatever food is well-known in the world — from dogs to birds, together with birds — the food of all living beings — that is your food,' said speech and the others. Because all food belongs to the vital breath —

children.text: prāṇabhūtatvādviduṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the knower has become identical with the vital breath.

children.text: "prāṇādvā eṣa udeti prāṇe 'stameti"ityupakramya-"evaṃvido ha vā udeti sūrya evaṃvidyastameti"iti śrutyantarāt //1 //
children.translated_text: From another <s>śruti</s>, which begins: 'From the vital breath indeed this [sun] rises, and in the vital breath it sets,' and [concludes]: 'For one who knows this, the sun rises; for one who knows this, it sets.' [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.2.2]

children.text:
sa hovāca kiṃ me vāso bhaviṣyatīti |
āpa iti hocuḥ |
tasmād vā etad aśiṣyantaḥ purastāc copariṣṭāc cādbhiḥ paridadhati |
lambhuko ha vāso bhavati |
anagno ha bhavati || ChUp_5,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He said: "What will be my garment?" "Water," they said. Therefore, indeed, when about to eat, people cover [the hands] with water from above and below. [The vital breath thus] becomes a receiver of garments; it does not become naked.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.2.2]

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,2.2 sa hovāca punaḥ prāṇaḥ /
pūrvavadeva kalpanā /
kiṃ me vāso bhaviṣyatītyāpa iti hocurvāgādayaḥ /
yasmātprāṇasya vāsa āpastasmādvā etadaśiṣyanto bhoktavantaśca brāhmaṇā vidvāṃsa etatkurvanti /
kim /
adbhirvāsasthānīyābhiḥ purastādbhojanātpūrvamupariṣṭācca bhojanādūrdhvaṃ ca paridadhati paridhānaṃ kurvanti mukhyasya prāṇasya lambhuko sambhanaśīlo vāso ha bhavati /
vāsaso labdhaiva bhavatītyarthaḥ /
anagno ha bhavati /
vāsaso lambhukatvenārthasiddhaivānagnatetyanagno ha bhavatītyuttarīyavānbhavatītyetat /
bhokṣyamāṇasya bhuktavataśca yadācamanaṃ śuddhyarthaṃ vijñātaṃ tasminprāṇasya vāsa iti darśanamātramiha vidhīyate /
adbhiḥ paridadhatīti nā'camanāntaram /
yathā laukikaiḥ prāmibhiradyamānamannaṃ prāṇasyeti darśanamātraṃ tadvatkiṃ me 'nnaṃ kiṃ me vāsa ityādipraśnaprativacanayostulyatvāt /
yadyācamanamapūrvaṃ tādarthyena kriyate tadā kṛmyādyannamapi prāṇasya bhakṣyatvena vihitaṃ syāt /
tulyayorvijñānārthayoḥ prasnaprativacanayoḥ prakaraṇasya vijñānārthatvādardhajaratīyo nyāyo na yuktaḥ kalpayitum /
yattu prasiddhamācamanaṃ prāyatyārthaṃ prāṇasyānagnatārthaṃ ca na bhavatītyucyate na tathā vayamācamanamubhayārthaṃ brūmaḥ /
kiṃ tarhi prāyatyārthācamanasādhanabhūtā āpaḥ prāṇasya vāsa iti darśanaṃ codyata iti brūmaḥ /
tatrā'camanasyobhayārthatvaprasaṅgadoṣacodanānupapannā /
vāsortha evā'camane taddarśanaṃ syāditi cet /
children.translated_text: Rather, we say that the perception 'water, which is the means of <s>ācamana</s> performed for expiation, is the garment of <s>Prāṇa</s>' is what is taught. Therefore, the objection of <s>ācamana</s> serving two purposes does not arise.

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: If one says that the perception [of water as garment] would apply only in the context of <s>ācamana</s> for the purpose of garment —

children.text: vāsojñānārthavākye vāsorthāpūrvācamanavidhāne tatrānagnatārthatvadṛṣṭividhāne ca vākyabhedaḥ ācamanasya tadarthatvamanyārthatvaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: No. In a sentence meant for the knowledge of garment, if a new <s>ācamana</s> were enjoined for the purpose of garment, and if a perception of non-nakedness were also enjoined therein, there would be a splitting of the sentence — [with <s>ācamana</s>] serving both that purpose and another purpose.

children.text: pramāṇābhāvāt //2 //
children.translated_text: Because there is no evidence [for such splitting]. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.2.2:] He [<s>Prāṇa</s>] said again — the same construction [applies] as before. 'What will be my garment?' — 'Water,' said <s>Vāc</s> (speech) and the others. Since water is the garment of <s>Prāṇa</s>, therefore indeed, when about to eat and after having eaten, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who know [this] do the following: what? With water — which serves in place of a garment — before eating and after eating, they envelop [him] — they perform the enveloping of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>. [Thus <s>Prāṇa</s>] becomes one who obtains a garment — meaning he obtains his garment. He becomes 'not naked' (<s>anagna</s>) — the state of not being naked is established by virtue of obtaining the garment, hence 'he becomes not naked' means he becomes one who has an upper garment. The <s>ācamana</s> (sipping of water) that is known to be performed for purification before and after eating — regarding that, only the perception 'this is the garment of <s>Prāṇa</s>' is enjoined here. 'They envelop with water' — this is not [enjoining something] different from <s>ācamana</s>. Just as the perception that food eaten by worldly beings is [food] of <s>Prāṇa</s> is merely a way of seeing — similarly, the questions and answers 'What is my food?' and 'What is my garment?' are of equal nature. If <s>ācamana</s> were newly enjoined for this purpose, then even worm-food and such would have to be enjoined as food of <s>Prāṇa</s>. Since the questions and answers are both of equal [nature] and meant for knowledge, and since the context is for the purpose of knowledge, the maxim of the 'half-old' (<s>ardhajaratīya nyāya</s>) is not appropriate to apply. As for the objection that the well-known <s>ācamana</s> [performed] for the purpose of expiation does not serve the purpose of <s>Prāṇa's</s> non-nakedness — we do not say that <s>ācamana</s> serves both purposes.

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.2.3

children.text:
tad dhaitat satyakāmo jābālo gośrutaye vaiyāghrapadyāyoktvovāca |
yady apy enac chuṣkāya sthāṇave brūyāj jāyerann evāsmiñ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti || ChUp_5,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'This indeed <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s> told <s>Gośruti Vaiyāghrapadya</s> and said: "Even if one were to tell this to a dry stump, branches would grow on it and leaves would sprout forth."' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.2.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,2.3 tadetatprāṇadarśanaṃ stūyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.2.3:] This meditation on <s>Prāṇa</s> is praised.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How?

children.text: taddhaitatprāṇadarśanaṃ satyakāmo jābālo gośrutaye nāmnā vaiyāghrapadyāya vyāghrapado 'patyaṃ vaiyāghrapadyastasmai gośrutyākhyāyoktvovācānyadapi vakṣyamāṇaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: This meditation on <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s> told <s>Gośruti</s> by name — <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, being the offspring of <s>Vyāghrapada</s>, hence <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s> — to that <s>Gośruti</s>, having told [this], he also spoke the following additional words:

children.text: kiṃ taduvācetyāha-yadyapi śuṣkāya sthāṇava etaddarśanaṃ brūyātprāṇavijjāyerannutpadyerannevāsminsthāṇau śākhāḥ praroheyuśca palāśāni patrāmi, kimu jīvate puruṣāya brūyāditi //3 //
children.translated_text: What did he say? — Even if one were to tell this meditation to a dry stump, branches would be born — would sprout — on that very stump, and leaves would grow forth. How much more [effective would it be] if told to a living person! (3)

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.4
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.2.4

children.text: atha yadi mahaj jigamiṣet, amāvāsyāyām dīkṣitvā paurṇamāsyāṃ rātrau sarvauṣadhasya mantham dadhimadhunor upamathya jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet || ChUp_5,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, if one desires greatness, having consecrated oneself on the new-moon night, on the full-moon night one should prepare a mixture (<s>mantha</s>) of all herbs in curds and honey. Having offered clarified butter into the fire with [the words] "To the eldest, to the best, <s>svāhā</s>," one should pour the residue into the mixture.' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.2.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,2.4 athānantaraṃ yadi mahanmahattvaṃ jigamiṣedgantumicchenmahattvaṃ prāptuṃ yadikāmayetetyarthaḥ /
tasyedaṃ karma vidhīyate /
mahattve hi sati śrīrupanamate /
śrīmato hyarthaprāptaṃ dhanaṃ tataḥ karmānuṣṭhānaṃ tataśca devayānaṃ pitṛyāṇaṃ vā panthānaṃ pratipatsyata ityetatprayojanamurarīkṛtya mahattvaprepsoridaṃ karma na viṣayopabhogakāmasya /
tasyāyaṃ kālādividhirucyate-amāvāsyāyāṃ dīkṣitvā dīkṣita iva bhūmiśayanādiniyamaṃ kṛtvā taporūpaṃ satyavacanaṃ brahmacaryamityādidharmavānbhūtvetyarthaḥ /
na punardaikṣameva karmajātaṃ sarvamupādatte /
children.translated_text: However, one does not undertake the entire body of rituals belonging to the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) proper,

children.text: atadvikāratvānmanthākhyasya karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: because the ritual called <s>mantha</s> is not a modification of that [<s>dīkṣā</s>].

children.text: "upasadvratī"iti śrutyantarātpayomātrabhakṣamaṃ ca śuddhikāramaṃ tapa upādatte /
children.translated_text: From another <s>śruti</s> [passage stating] 'one observing the <s>upasad</s> vow,' one undertakes the drinking of milk alone as food, as well as purificatory austerity.

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ rātrau karmā'rabhate sarvauṣadhasya grāmyāraṇyānāmoṣadhīnāṃ yāvacchaktyalpamalpamupādāya tadvituṣīkṛtyā'mameva piṣṭaṃ dadhimadhunoraudumbare kaṃsākāre camasākāre vā pātre śrutyantarātprakṣipyopamathyāgrataḥ sthāpayitvā jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya svāhetyagnāvāvasathya ājyasyā'vāpasthāne hutvā sruvasaṃlagnaṃ manthe saṃpātamavanayetsaṃsravamadhaḥ pātayet //4 //
children.translated_text: On the full-moon night, one begins the ritual: gathering a small quantity of each, as far as possible, of all herbs — both cultivated and wild — dehusking them, grinding them raw, placing them into a vessel made of <s>udumbara</s> wood shaped like a cup (<s>kaṃsa</s>) or a bowl (<s>camasa</s>), as known from another <s>śruti</s>, adding curds and honey, mixing them, placing [the mixture] in front, and having offered clarified butter into the household fire (<s>āvasathya</s>) with [the words] 'To the eldest, to the best, <s>svāhā</s>' — at the place of the offering — one should pour down the residue clinging to the ladle (<s>sruva</s>) into the mixture, letting it drip below. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.2.4:] Now, next — if one desires greatness, if one wishes to attain greatness — the meaning is: if one desires it. For him, this ritual action is enjoined. For when greatness is attained, prosperity (<s>śrī</s>) approaches [of its own accord]. For a prosperous person, wealth comes naturally; from that, the performance of ritual action [becomes possible]; and from that, one will attain the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) or the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>) — accepting this purpose, this ritual is [prescribed] for one who desires greatness, not for one who desires sense enjoyment. The regulation of time and such for this person is stated: having consecrated oneself on the new-moon day — having become as if consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>), having undertaken observances such as sleeping on the ground and the like, having become endowed with austerities in the form of truthfulness, <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and other such virtues — this is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.5
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.2.5

children.text:
vasiṣṭhāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet |
pratiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet |
saṃpade svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet |
āyatanāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet || ChUp_5,2.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Having offered clarified butter into the fire with "To <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>," one should pour the residue into the mixture. Having offered clarified butter into the fire with "To the foundation, <s>svāhā</s>," one should pour the residue into the mixture. Having offered clarified butter into the fire with "To prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>," one should pour the residue into the mixture. Having offered clarified butter into the fire with "To the abode, <s>svāhā</s>," one should pour the residue into the mixture.' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.2.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,2.5 samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.2.5:] The rest is the same.

children.text: vasiṣṭhāya pratiṣṭhāyai saṃpada āyatanāya svāheti pratyekaṃ tathaiva saṃpātamavanayeddhutvā //5 //
children.translated_text: 'To <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, to the foundation, to prosperity, to the abode — <s>svāhā</s>' — with each [of these formulas] one should similarly pour the residue, having offered [the oblation]. (5)

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.6
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.2.6

children.text:
atha pratisṛpyāñjalau mantham ādhāya japati |
amo nāmāsi |
amā hi te sarvam idam |
sa hi jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭho rājādhipatiḥ |
sa mā jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gamayatu |
aham evedaṃ sarvam asānīti || ChUp_5,2.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then, moving back [from the fire], taking the mixture in his cupped hands, he recites: "Your name is <s>Ama</s>. For all this is together with you. He is the eldest, the best, the king, the overlord. May he lead me to eldership, to supremacy, to kingship, to overlordship. May I become all this."' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.2.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,2.6 atha pratisṛpyāgnerīṣadapasṛpyāñjalau manthamādhāya japatīmaṃ mantram /
amo nāmāsyamā hi te /
ama iti prāṇasya nāma /
annena hi prāṇaḥ prāṇiti deha ityato manthadravyaṃ prāṇasyānnatvātprāṇatvena stūyate 'mo nāmāsīti /
kutaḥ /
yato 'mā saha hi yasmātte tava prāṇabhūtasya sarvaṃ samastaṃ jagadidamataḥ /
sa hi prāṇabhūto mantho jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaśca /
children.translated_text: this mixture, being <s>Prāṇa</s>, is the eldest and the best.

children.text: ata eva ca rājā dīptimānadhipatiścādhiṣṭhāya pālayitā sarvasya /
children.translated_text: And precisely for that reason, [it is] a king — one who is radiant — and an overlord — one who rules over and protects all.

children.text: samā māmapi manthaḥ prāṇo jyaiṣṭhyādiguṇapūgamātmano gamayatvahamevedaṃ sarvaṃ jagadasāni bhavani prāṇavat /
children.translated_text: May that mixture, that <s>Prāṇa</s>, lead me too to the aggregate of qualities such as eldership and the rest. May I become all this world, like <s>Prāṇa</s>.

children.text: itiśabdo mantraparisamāptyarthaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: The word '<s>iti</s>' indicates the completion of the <s>mantra</s>. (6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.2.6:] Then, having moved back — having retreated slightly from the fire — taking the mixture in his cupped hands, he recites this <s>mantra</s>: '<s>Ama</s> is your name; for all is together with you.' <s>Ama</s> is a name of <s>Prāṇa</s>. For <s>Prāṇa</s> sustains the body through food — therefore the mixture-substance, being food of <s>Prāṇa</s>, is praised as being <s>Prāṇa</s> [itself]: 'Your name is <s>Ama</s>.' Why? Because together with you — since together with you, who are <s>Prāṇa</s>, the entire world exists — therefore,

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.7
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.2.7

children.text:
atha khalv etayarcā paccha ācāmati |
tat savitur vṛṇīmaha ity ācāmati |
vayaṃ devasya bhojanam ity ācāmati |
śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadhātamam ity ācāmati |
turaṃ bhagasya dhīmahīti sarvaṃ pibati |
nirṇijya kaṃsaṃ camasaṃ vā paścād agneḥ saṃviśati |
carmaṇi vā sthaṇḍile vā vācaṃyamo 'prasāhaḥ |
sa yadi striyaṃ paśyet samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt || ChUp_5,2.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then indeed, with this <s>ṛc</s> verse, he sips foot by foot: "That of <s>Savitṛ</s> we desire" — he sips. "We, the food of the god" — he sips. "The best, the most nourishing of all" — he sips. "The swift [glory] of <s>Bhaga</s> we meditate upon" — he drinks it all. Having rinsed the cup or bowl, he lies down behind the fire on a hide or on bare ground, controlling his speech, not yielding. If he sees a woman [in his dream], he should know that the rite has succeeded.' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.2.7)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,2.7 athānantaraṃ khalvetayā vakṣyamāṇayarcā pacchaḥ pādaśa ācāmati bhakṣayati, mantrasyaikaikena pādenaikaikaṃ grāsaṃ bhakṣayati /
tadbhojanaṃ savituḥ sarvasya prasavituḥ /
prāṇamādityaṃ caikīkṛtyocyate /
ādityasya vṛṇīmahe prārthayemahi mantharūpam /
yenānnena sāvitreṇa bhojanenopabhuktena vayaṃ savitṛsvarūpāpannā bhavemetyabhiprāyaḥ /
devasya savituriti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ /
śreṣṭhaṃ praśasyatamaṃ sarvānnebhyaḥ sarvadhātamaṃ sarvasya jagato dhārayitṛtamamatiśayena vidhātṛtamamiti vā /
sarvathā bhojanaviśeṣaṇam /
turaṃ tvaraṃ tūrṇaṃ śīghramityatat /
bhagasya devasya savituḥ svarūpamiti śeṣaḥ /
dhīmahi cintayemahi viśiṣṭabhojanena saṃskṛtāḥ śuddhātmānaḥ santa ityabhiprāyaḥ /
athavā bhagasya śriyaḥ kāraṇaṃ mahattvaṃ prāptuṃ karma kṛtavanto vayaṃ taddhomahi cintayemahīti sarvaṃ ca manthalepaṃ pibati nirṇijya prakṣālya kaṃsaṃ kaṃsākāraṃ camasaṃ camasākāraṃ vaudumbaraṃ pātram /
pītvā'camya paścādagneḥ prākśirāḥ saṃviśati carmaṇi vājine sthaṇḍile kevalāyāṃ vā bhūmau /
children.translated_text: having drunk and rinsed his mouth (<s>ācamya</s>), he lies down behind the fire, head facing east, on a hide — an animal skin — or on bare ground.

children.text: vācaṃyamo vāgyataḥ sannityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Controlling his speech' (<s>vācaṃyama</s>) means having restrained his speech — this is the meaning.

children.text: aprasāho na prasahyate nābhibhūyate stryādyaniṣṭasvapnadarśanena yathā tathā saṃyatacittaḥ sannityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not yielding' (<s>aprasāha</s>) — he is not overpowered, not overcome by the vision of undesirable dreams involving women and the like — meaning he remains with a controlled mind.

children.text: sa evaṃbhūto yadi sriyaṃ paśyetsvapneṣu tadā vidyātsamṛddhaṃ mamedaṃ karmeti //7 //
children.translated_text: Such a person, if he sees a woman in his dreams, then he should know: 'This ritual of mine has succeeded.' (7)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.2.7:] Then next, with this verse that will be stated, foot by foot (<s>pacchaḥ</s>) — he sips, that is, he eats — with each foot of the <s>mantra</s> he consumes one morsel. 'That food of <s>Savitṛ</s>' — of the one who impels everything — <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) are spoken of as unified. Of <s>Āditya</s>, 'we desire' — we pray for — in the form of the mixture. The purport is: 'May we, having consumed this food of <s>Savitṛ</s>, attain the nature of <s>Savitṛ</s>.' 'Of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>' connects with the preceding [phrase]. 'The best' — the most praiseworthy among all foods; 'the most nourishing of all' — the greatest sustainer of the entire world, or the greatest bestower. In every way, it is a qualifier of the food. '<s>Turam</s>' means swift, quick. 'Of <s>Bhaga</s>' — of the god <s>Savitṛ</s> — 'the nature' is to be supplied. 'We meditate upon' — we contemplate — the purport is: having been purified by this special food, being of pure self. Alternatively: 'of <s>bhaga</s>' — of prosperity — 'the cause, [which is] greatness, we who have performed the ritual to attain [it], meditate upon — we contemplate.' And he drinks all the remaining traces of the mixture. Having rinsed — having washed — the cup-shaped or bowl-shaped vessel made of <s>udumbara</s> wood,

children.text: START ChUp 5,2.8
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.2.8

children.text:
tad eṣa ślokaḥ |
yadā karmasu kāmyeṣu striyaṃ svapneṣu paśyati |
samṛddhiṃ tatra jānīyāt tasmin svapnanidarśane tasmin svapnanidarśane || ChUp_5,2.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'On this there is this verse: "When in rites performed with desire one sees a woman in dreams, one should know success from that dream-vision, from that dream-vision."' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.2.8)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,2.8 tadetasminnartha eṣa śloko mantro 'pi bhavati /
yadā karmasu kāmyeṣu kāmārtheṣu sriyaṃ svapneṣu svapnadarśaneṣu svapnakāleṣu vā paśyati samṛddhiṃ tatra jānīyīt /
children.translated_text: When, in rites performed with desire (<s>kāmya karmas</s>) — rites performed for the fulfillment of desires — one sees a woman in dreams — in dream-visions, or at dream-times — one should know success from that.

children.text: karmaṇāṃ phalaniṣpattirbhaviṣyatīti jānīyādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should know that the fruition of the ritual actions will come about — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasminstryādipraśastasvapnadarśane satītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The purport is: when there is such an auspicious dream-vision involving a woman and the like.

children.text: dviruktiḥ karmasamāptyarthā //8//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of the phrase] is for indicating the conclusion of the ritual. (8)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.2.8:] On this subject, there is this verse (<s>śloka</s>) — a <s>mantra</s> as well.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,3.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.1

children.text:
śvetaketur hāruṇeyaḥ pañcālānāṃ samitim eyāya |
taṃ ha pravāhaṇo jaivalir uvāca |
kumārānu tvā aśiṣat piteti |
anu hi bhagava iti || ChUp_5,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Śvetaketu</s>, the son of <s>Āruṇi</s>, came to the assembly of the <s>Pañcālas</s>. <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said to him: "Boy, has your father instructed you?" "Indeed he has, revered sir."' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.3.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,3.1 brahmādistambaparyantāḥ saṃsāragatayo vaktavyā vairāgyahetormumukṣūṇāmityata ākhyāyikā'rabhyate-śvetaketunamito ha, ityaitihyārthaḥ /
aruṇasyāpatyāruṇistasyāpatyamāruṇeyaḥ pañcālānāṃ samitiṃ sabhāmeyāyā'jagāma /
tamāgatavantaṃ ha pravāhaṇo nāmato jīvalasyāpatyaṃ jaivaliruvācoktavān /
children.translated_text: To him who had arrived, <s>Pravāhaṇa</s> by name — the offspring of <s>Jīvala</s>, hence <s>Jaivali</s> — said, spoke:

children.text: he kumārānu tvā tvāmaśiṣadanvasiṣatpitā /
children.translated_text: 'O boy, has your father instructed you — has he taught you?'

children.text: kimanuśiṣṭastvaṃ pitretyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Have you been instructed by your father?' — this is the meaning.

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa āhānu hyanuśiṣṭo 'smi bhagava iti sūcayannāha //1 //
children.translated_text: Being thus addressed, he replied: 'Indeed I have been instructed, revered sir' — indicating [his confidence], he says. (1)
