[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.3.1:] The transmigrations from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass are to be described, for the purpose of generating dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) in those who seek liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) — thus a narrative begins. <s>Śvetaketu</s> by name — 'ha' indicates tradition — the son of <s>Āruṇi</s> (the son of <s>Aruṇa</s>, hence <s>Āruṇi</s>), his offspring is <s>Āruṇeya</s> — came to the assembly, the court, of the <s>Pañcālas</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,3.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.2

children.text:
vettha yad ito 'dhi prajāḥ prayantīti |
na bhagava iti |
vettha yathā punar āvartanta 3 iti |
na bhagava iti |
vettha pathor devayānasya pitṛyāṇasya ca vyāvartanā 3 iti |
na bhagava iti || ChUp_5,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: '"Do you know where creatures go from here?" "No, revered sir." "Do you know how they return?" "No, revered sir." "Do you know the parting of the two paths — the path of the gods and the path of the ancestors?" "No, revered sir."' (<s>ChUp</s> 5.3.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,3.2 taṃ hovāca yadyanuśiṣṭo 'si vettha yadito 'smāllokādadhyūrdhvaṃ yatprajāḥ prayanti yadgacchanti tatkiṃ jānīṣa ityarthaḥ /
na bhagava ityāhetaro na jāne 'haṃ tadyatpṛcchasi /
evaṃ tarhi vettha jānīṣe yathā yena prakāreṇa punarāvartanta iti /
children.translated_text: 'Then do you know — do you understand — how, by what manner, they return?' — thus [he asks].

children.text: na bhagava iti pratyāha /
children.translated_text: 'No, revered sir' — he replies.

children.text: vettha pathormārgayoḥ sahaprayāṇayordevayānasya pitṛyāṇasya ca vyāvartanamitaretaraviyogasthānaṃ saha gacchatāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do you know the parting — the place of separation from each other — of the two paths, the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) and the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>), that travel together?' — this is the meaning.

children.text: na bhagava iti //2 //
children.translated_text: 'No, revered sir.' (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.3.2:] He said to him: 'If you have been instructed, do you know where — from this world, upward — creatures go, where they proceed? Do you know that?' — this is the meaning. 'No, revered sir' — the other [<s>Śvetaketu</s>] says: 'I do not know that which you ask.'

children.text: START ChUp 5,3.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.3

children.text:
vettha yathāsau loko na saṃpūryata 3 iti |
na bhagava iti |
vettha yathā pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti |
naiva bhagava iti || ChUp_5,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Do you know how yonder world never becomes full?' 'No, Blessed One.' 'Do you know how, at the fifth oblation, the waters come to be called "person"?' 'No indeed, Blessed One.' (ChUp 5.3.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,3.3 vetthā yathāsau lokaḥ pitṛsambandhī yaṃ prāpya punarāvartante bahubhiḥ prayadbhirapi yena kāramena na sampūryata iti /
na bhagava iti pratyāha /
children.translated_text: 'No, Blessed One' — thus he replies.

children.text: vettha yathā yena krameṇa pañcamyāṃ pañcasaṃkhyākāyāmāhutau hutāyāmāhutinirvṛttā āhutisādhanāścā'paḥ puruṣavacasaḥ puruṣa ityevaṃ vaco 'bhidhānaṃ yāsāṃ hūyamānānāṃ krameṇa ṣaṣṭhāhutibhūtānāṃ tāḥ puruṣavacasaḥ puruṣaśabdavācyā bhavanti puruṣākhyāṃ labhanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do you know how' — by what process, 'at the fifth oblation' — at the oblation numbered five, when it has been offered — the waters that constitute the oblation and are the means of the oblation come to be called 'person' (<s>puruṣavacas</s>) — meaning those [waters] which, when being offered in sequence, becoming the sixth oblation, acquire the designation 'person,' obtain the name 'person' — that is the meaning.

children.text: ityukto naiva bhagava ityāha /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, he says 'No indeed, Blessed One.'

children.text: naivāhamatra kiñcana jānāmītyarthaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: I do not know anything whatsoever about this. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.3.3:] 'Do you know how yonder world' — the world connected with the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors), to which [beings] go and return — by what process it never becomes full, even though many go [there]?

children.text: START ChUp 5,3.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.4]

children.text:
athānu kim anu śiṣṭho 'vocathā yo hīmāni na vidyāt |
kathaṃ so 'nuśiṣṭo bruvīteti |
sa hāyastaḥ pitur ardham eyāya |
taṃ hovācānanuśiṣya vāva kila mā bhagavān abravīd anu tvāśiṣam iti || ChUp_5,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then why did you claim to have been instructed? For one who does not know these things — how could he say he has been instructed?' He [<s>Śvetaketu</s>] went dejected to his father's place. He said to him: 'Without having instructed me, Blessed One told me "I have instructed you."' (ChUp 5.3.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,3.4 athaivamajñaḥ sankimanu kasmāttvamanuśiṣṭo 'smītyavocathā uktavānasi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.3.4:] 'Then' — being thus ignorant, why — for what reason — did you claim 'I have been instructed'?

children.text: yo hīmāni mayā pṛṣṭānyarthajātāni na vidyānna vijānītyātkathaṃ sa vidvatsvanuśiṣṭo 'smīti bruvīta /
children.translated_text: For one who does not know these matters that I have asked — how could he say among the learned 'I have been instructed'?

children.text: ityevaṃ sa śvetaketuḥ rājñā'yasta āyāsitaḥ sanpiturardhaṃ sthānameyāyā'gatavāṃstaṃ ca pituramuvācānanuśiṣyānuśāsanamakṛtvaiva mā māṃ kila bhagavānsamāvartanakāle 'bravīduktavānanu tvāśiṣamanvaśiṣaṃ tvāmiti //4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, that <s>Śvetaketu</s>, made dejected by the king, being distressed, went to his father's place and said to his father: 'Without having instructed [me] — without performing instruction — Blessed One told me at the time of my graduation ceremony (<s>samāvartana</s>), saying "I have instructed you."' (4)

children.text: START ChUp 5,3.5-6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.5-6]

children.text:
pañca mā rājanyabandhuḥ praśnān aprākṣīt |
teṣāṃ naikaṃcanāśakaṃ vivaktum iti |
sa hovāca yathā mā tvaṃ tadaitān avado yathāham eṣāṃ naikaṃcana veda |
yady aham imān avediṣyaṃ kathaṃ te nāvakṣyam iti || ChUp_5,3.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'A member of the royal class asked me five questions. Of those, I was not able to explain even one.' He [the father] said: 'Just as you have told me these, so I too do not know even one of them. If I had known them, how would I not have told you?' (ChUp 5.3.5)

children.text:
sa ha gautamo rājño 'rdham eyāya |
tasmai ha prāptāyārhāṃ cakāra |
sa ha prātaḥ sabhāga udeyāya |
taṃ hovāca |
mānuṣasya bhagavan gautama vittasya varaṃ vṛṇīthā iti |
sa hovāca |
tavaiva rājan mānuṣaṃ vittam |
yām eva kumārasyānte vācam abhāṣathās tām eva me brūhīti |
sa ha kṛcchrī babhūva || ChUp_5,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gautama</s> went to the king's place. When he arrived, the king showed him due honor. In the morning, he went to the assembly hall. The king said to him: 'Blessed <s>Gautama</s>, choose a boon of human wealth.' He replied: 'Let human wealth remain with you alone, O King. Tell me that very speech which you spoke in the presence of the boy.' The king became distressed. (ChUp 5.3.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,3.5,6 yataḥ pañca pañcasaṃkhyākānpraśnānrājanyabandhū rājānyā bandhavo 'syeti rājanyabandhuḥ svayaṃ durvṛtta ityarthaḥ /
aprākṣītpṛṣṭavāṃsteṣāṃ praśnānāṃ naikañcanaikamapi nāśakaṃ na śaktavānahaṃ vivaktuṃ viśeṣeṇārthato nirṇetumityarthaḥ /
sa hovāca pitā yathā mā māṃ vatsa tvaṃ tadā'gatamātra evaitānpraśnānavada uktavānasi teṣāṃ naikañcanāśakaṃ vivaktumiti tathā māṃ jānīhi, tvadīyājñānena liṅgena mama tadviṣayamajñānaṃ jānīhītyarthaḥ /
kathaṃ, yathāhameṣāṃ praśnānāmekañcanaikamapi na veda na jāna iti yathā tvamevāṅgaitānpraśnānna jānīṣe tathāhamapyetānna jāna ityarthaḥ /
ato mayyanyathābhāvo na kartavyaḥ /
kuta etadevaṃ yato na jāne yadyahamimānpraśnānavediṣyaṃ viditavānasmi kathaṃ te tubhyaṃ priyāya putrāya samāvartanakāle purā nāvakṣyaṃ noktavānasmītyuktvā sa ha gotrato rājño jaivalerardhaṃ sthānameyāya gatavān /
tasmai ha gautamāya prāptāyārhāmarhūṇāṃ cakāra kṛtavān /
sa ca gautamaḥ kṛtātithya uṣitvā paredyuḥ prātaḥkāle sabhāge sabhāṃ gate rājñyudeyāya /
bhajanaṃ bhāgaḥ pūjā sevā saha bhāgena vartamāno vā sabhāgaḥ pūjyamāno 'nyaiḥ svayaṃ gautama udeyāya rājānamudgatavān /
taṃ hovāca gautamaṃ rājā mānuṣasya bhagavangautama manuṣyasambandhino vittasya grāmādervaraṃ varaṇīyaṃ kāmaṃ vṛṇīthāḥ prārthayethāḥ /
children.translated_text: The king said to <s>Gautama</s>: 'Blessed <s>Gautama</s>, choose a boon — a desirable wish — of human wealth, that is, wealth relating to human beings such as villages and the like.'

children.text: sa hovāca gautamastavaiva tiṣṭhatu rājanmānuṣaṃ vittam /
children.translated_text: <s>Gautama</s> said: 'Let human wealth remain with you alone, O King.'

children.text: yāmeva kumārasya mama putrasyānte samīpe vācaṃ pañcapraśnalakṣaṇāmabhāṣathā uktavānasi tāmeva vācaṃ me mahyaṃ brūhi kathayetyukto gautamena rājā sa ha kṛcchrī duḥkhī babhūva /
children.translated_text: 'That very speech characterized by the five questions which you spoke in the presence of my son, the boy — tell that speech to me' — thus addressed by <s>Gautama</s>, the king became distressed, troubled.

children.text: kathaṃ tvidamiti //5-6 //
children.translated_text: 'How indeed [can this be]?' (5-6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.3.5-6:] Since five — five in number — questions were asked by 'a member of the royal class' (<s>rājanyabandhu</s>) — one whose relatives are royals, hence <s>rājanyabandhu</s>, meaning he himself was of bad conduct. He asked [them], and of those questions, not even one was I able to explain — meaning I was not capable of determining [their meaning] in detail. The father said: 'Just as you, my child, told me these [questions] as soon as you came back — [that] you were unable to explain even one of them — so know me [to be in the same position]; by the sign of your ignorance, know that I too am ignorant about those matters' — that is the meaning. How? 'Just as I do not know even one of these questions' — meaning just as you yourself do not know these questions, so too I do not know them. Therefore, you should not think wrongly of me. Why is this so? Because I do not know [them] — if I had known these questions, how would I not have told you, my dear son, at the time of your graduation? — Having spoken thus, that <s>Gautama</s> by lineage went to the king <s>Jaivali's</s> place. When <s>Gautama</s> arrived, the king showed him due honor (<s>arha</s>). And <s>Gautama</s>, having been shown hospitality, staying [the night], the next day in the morning, when the king had gone to the assembly (<s>sabhā</s>), <s>Gautama</s> went to the king. '<s>Sabhāga</s>' means being honored — one who is being honored by others — or one who participates in the assembly.

children.text: START ChUp 5,3.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.7]

children.text:
taṃ ha ciraṃ vasety ājñāpayāṃ cakāra |
taṃ hovāca |
yathā mā tvaṃ gautamāvadaḥ |
yatheyaṃ na prāk tvattaḥ purā vidyā brāhmaṇān gacchati |
tasmād u sarveṣu lokeṣu kṣatrasyaiva praśāsanam abhūd iti |
tasmai hovāca || ChUp_5,3.7 ||
children.translated_text: He commanded him to stay a long time. Then he said to him: 'As you told me, O <s>Gautama</s> — [the reason is] that before you, this knowledge has never reached the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. Therefore, in all the worlds, the teaching of this belonged to the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> alone.' Then he told him. (ChUp 5.3.7)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,3.7 sa ha kṛcchrībhūto 'pratyākhyeyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ manvāno nyāyena vidyā vaktavyeti matvā taṃ ha gautamaṃ ciraṃ dīrghakālaṃ vasetyevamājñāpayāñcakārā'jñaptavān /
yatpūrvaṃ pratyākhyātavānrājā vidyāṃ yacca paścācciraṃ vasetyājñaptavān, tannimittaṃ brāhmamaṃ kṣamāpayati hetuvacanoktyā-taṃ hovāca rājā sarvavidyo brahmaṇo 'pi sanyathā yena prakāreṇa mā māṃ he gautamāvadastvaṃ tāmeva vidyālakṣaṇāṃ vācaṃ me brūhītyajñānāttena tvaṃ jānīhi /

tatrāsti vaktavyaṃ yathā yena prakāreṇeyaṃ vidyā prāktvatto brāhmaṇānna gacchati na gatavatī, na ca brāhmaṇā anayā vidyayānuśāsitavantaḥ, tathaitatprasiddhaṃ loke yatastasmādu purā pūrvaṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kṣattrasyaiva kṣattrajāterevānayā vidyayā praśāsanaṃ praśāstṛtvaṃ śiṣyāmāmabhūdbabhūva /
children.translated_text: There is something to be said about this: 'The manner in which this knowledge has not reached the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> before you — and the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> have not instructed with this knowledge — this is well-known in the world, because therefore, previously, in all the worlds, the teaching — the authority to teach through this knowledge — belonged to the <s>Kṣatriya</s> class alone.'

children.text: kṣattriyaparamparayaiveyaṃ vidyatāvantaṃ kālamāgatā /
children.translated_text: This knowledge has come down through the succession of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> alone for all this time.

children.text: tathāpyahametāṃ tubhyaṃ vakṣyāmi cvatsampradānādūrdhvaṃ brāhmaṇāngamiṣyati /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, I shall tell it to you; after your receipt [of it], it will reach the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

children.text: ato mayā yaduktaṃ tatkṣantumarhasītyuktvā tasmai hovāca vidyāṃ rājā //7//
children.translated_text: Therefore, please forgive what I said — having spoken thus, the king told him the knowledge. (7)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.3.7:] He, being distressed, considering that a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> cannot be refused, and thinking that by right the knowledge must be imparted, commanded <s>Gautama</s> to stay a long time. As for the king's initial refusal of the knowledge and his later commanding him to stay long — to apologize to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for these, he offers a reason: the king said to him — 'O <s>Gautama</s>, you who are knowledgeable in all things and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too — just as you told me "Tell me that very speech characterized by the knowledge" — [this was] out of ignorance on your part; know that [from the following reason].'

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,4.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.4.1]

children.text:
asau vāva loko gautamāgniḥ |
tasyāditya eva samit |
raśmayo dhūmaḥ |
ahar arciḥ |
candramā aṅgārāḥ |
nakṣatrāṇi visphuliṅgāḥ || ChUp_5,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'That world up there, O <s>Gautama</s>, is verily the [sacrificial] fire. Its fuel is the sun. Its smoke is the rays. Its flame is the day. Its embers are the moon. Its sparks are the stars.' (ChUp 5.4.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,4.1 pañcamyāmāhutāvāpa ityayaṃ praśnaḥ prāthamyenāpākriyate /
tadapākaraṇamanvitareṣāmapākaraṇamanukūlaṃ bhavediti /
agnihotrāhutyoḥ kāryārambho yaḥ sa ukto vājasaneyake /
taṃ prati prasnāḥ-utkrāntirāhutyorgatiḥ pratiṣṭhā tṛptiḥ punarāvṛttirlokaṃ pratyutthāyī iti /
teṣāṃ cāpākaraṇamuktaṃ tatraiva-"te vā ete āhutī hute utkrāmataste antarikṣamāviśataste antarikṣamevā'havanīyaṃ kurvāte vāyuṃ samidhaṃ marīcīreva śuklāmāhutiṃ te antarikṣaṃ tarpayataste tata utkrāmata ityādyevameva pūrvavaddivaṃ tarpayataste tata āvartete /
imāmāviśya tarpayitvā puruṣamāviśataḥ /
tataḥ sriyamāviśya lokaṃ pratyutthāyā bhavati"iti /
tatrāgnihotrāhutyoḥ kāryārambhamātramevaṃprakāraṃ bhavatītyuktāma /
iha tu taṃ kāryārambhamagni hotrāpūrvavipariṇāmalakṣaṇaṃ pañcadhā pravibhajyāgnitvenopāsanamuttaramārgapratipattisādhanaṃ vidhitsannāha-asau vāva loko gautamāgnirityādi /
iha sāyaṃprātaragnihotrāhutī hute paya ādisādhane śraddhāpuraḥsare āhavanīyāgnisamiddhūmārciraṅgāravisphuliṅgabhāvite kartrādikārakabhāvite cāntarikṣakrameṇotkramya dyulokaṃ praviśantyau sūkṣmabhūte apsamavāyitvādapśabdavācye śraddhāhetutvācca śraddhāśabdavācye tayoradhikaraṇo 'gniranyacca tatsambandhaṃ samidādītyucyate /
yā cāsāvagnyādibhāvanā'hutyoḥ sāpi tathaiva nirdiśyate /
asau vāva loko 'gnirhe gautama yathāgnihotrādhikaraṇamāhavanīya iha /
tasyāgnerghulokākhyasyā'ditya eva samittena hīddho 'sau loko dīpyate /
ataḥ samindhanātsamidādityaḥ /
raśmayo dhūmastadutthānāt, samidho hi dhūma uttiṣṭhati /
ahararciḥ prakāśasāmānyāt, ādityakāryatvācca candramā aṅgārāḥ /
children.translated_text: The day is the flame, because of the similarity of brightness, and because the moon is a product of the sun, the moon is the embers.

children.text: ahaḥpraśame 'bhivyakteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because [the moon] becomes manifest when the [light of] day subsides.

children.text: arciṣā hi praśame 'ṅgārā abhivyajyante /
children.translated_text: For when the flame subsides, the embers become visible.

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi visphuliṅgāścandramaso 'vayavā iva viprakīrṇatvasāmānyāt //1 //
children.translated_text: The stars are the sparks — being as if parts of the moon, because of the similarity of being scattered about. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.4.1:] The question 'How at the fifth oblation the waters [become person-named]' is answered first. Its resolution will make the resolution of the other [questions] easy. The origin of the effect of the <s>agnihotra</s> oblations has been stated in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>. The questions concerning that are: the departure, the path of the oblations, their resting place, their satisfaction, their return, and who rises toward the world. Their resolution is stated there itself: 'Those two oblations, having been offered, rise up; they enter the atmosphere; they make the atmosphere itself the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire], the wind as fuel, the rays as the white oblation; they satisfy the atmosphere; then they rise from there' — and so on in the same way they satisfy heaven; then they return; entering this [world] and satisfying it, they enter the person; then entering prosperity, one rises toward the world. There, it was stated that the origin of the effect of the <s>agnihotra</s> oblations is of this nature. But here, wishing to prescribe that origin of the effect — characterized by the transformation of the <s>agnihotra</s> into something unprecedented — as divided fivefold and to be meditated upon as fire, which is the means of attaining the northern path, he says 'That world up there, O <s>Gautama</s>, is verily the fire' and so forth. Here, the evening and morning <s>agnihotra</s> oblations, having milk and the like as their substance, preceded by faith, transformed into the form of fuel, smoke, flame, embers, and sparks of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, and [similarly] into the form of agent and other grammatical factors — passing through the atmosphere, entering the heavenly world, becoming subtle, called 'waters' due to their association with waters, and called 'faith' because of being the cause of faith — the fire that is the locus of these [oblations] and whatever else is connected with it such as fuel and the rest is stated. And the meditation on those oblations as fire and the rest is also described in the same way. 'That world up there is verily the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>' — just as the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the locus of the <s>agnihotra</s> here [in the ritual]. Of that fire called the heavenly world, the sun alone is the fuel — for by it that world blazes; therefore, because of its kindling, the sun is the fuel. The rays are the smoke, because they rise from it — for smoke rises from fuel.

children.text: START ChUp 5,4.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.4.2]

children.text:
tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhuteḥ somo rājā saṃbhavati || ChUp_5,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'In this fire the gods offer faith as an oblation. From that oblation, King <s>Soma</s> arises.' (ChUp 5.4.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,4.2 tasminnetasminyathoktalakṣaṇe 'gnau devā yajamānaprāṇā agnyādirūpā adhidaivatam /
śraddhāmagnihotrāhutipariṇāmāvasthārūpāḥ sūkṣmā āpaḥ śraddhābhāvitāḥ śraddhā ucyante /
"pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti"ityapāṃ homyatayā praśne śrutatvāt /
"śraddhā vā āpaḥ śraddhāmevā'rabhya praṇīya pracarati"iti ca vijñāyate /
tāṃ śraddhāmabrūpāṃ juhvāti /
tasyā āhuteḥ somo rājāpāṃ śraddhāśabdavācyānāṃ dyulokāgnau hutānāṃ pariṇāmaḥ somo rājā sambhavati /
yathargvedādipuṣparasā ṛgādimadhukaropanītāsta āditye yaśa ādikāryaṃ rohitādirūpalakṣaṇamārabhanta ityuktaṃ tathemā agnihotrāhutisamavāyinyaḥ sūkṣmāḥ śraddhāśabdavācyā āpo dyulokamanupraviśya cāndraṃ kāryamārabhante phalarūpamagnihotrāhutyoḥ /
yajamānāśca tatkartāra āhutimayā āhutibhāvanābhāvitā āhutirūpeṇa karmaṇā'kṛṣṭāḥ śraddhāpsamavāyuno dyulokamanupraviśya bhavanti /
children.translated_text: And the sacrificers, the performers of that [ritual], being made of oblations — imbued with the nature of oblations, drawn by the action in the form of oblation — entering the heavenly world along with the waters associated with faith, come to be [there].

children.text: tadarthaṃ hi tairagnihotraṃ hutam /
children.translated_text: For it was for that purpose that the <s>agnihotra</s> was offered by them.

children.text: atra tvāhutipariṇāma eva pañcāgnisambandhakrameṇa prādhānyena vivakṣita upāsanārthaṃ na yajamānānāṃ gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: But here, primarily the transformation of the oblation alone is intended to be described in the sequence of connection with the five fires, for the purpose of meditation — not the journey of the sacrificers.

children.text: tāṃ tvaviduṣāṃ dhūmādikrameṇottaratra vakṣyati viduṣāṃ cottarāṃ vidyākṛtām //2//
children.translated_text: That [journey] of the ignorant through the path of smoke and the rest, he will state later; and also the superior [path] of the knowers, produced by knowledge. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.4.2:] In this fire of the described nature, the gods — the vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>) of the sacrificer, in their cosmic aspect (<s>adhidaivatam</s>) having the form of fire and the rest — offer faith. The subtle waters that are in the state of being a transformation of the <s>agnihotra</s> oblations, imbued with faith, are called 'faith.' [This is] because in the question 'How at the fifth oblation the waters come to be called person,' the waters are heard as what is to be offered. And it is known: 'Waters are indeed faith; having first taken up faith, one proceeds.' They offer that faith, which is the waters. From that oblation — from those waters called by the word 'faith,' offered in the fire of the heavenly world — the transformation is King <s>Soma</s>, who arises. Just as the nectars of the flowers — the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and others — brought by the honey-makers of the <s>Ṛg</s> and other [<s>Vedas</s>], produce their effects such as splendor and the rest, having the forms of red and other colors in the sun — as was stated — so these subtle [waters], associated with the <s>agnihotra</s> oblations, called by the word 'faith,' entering the heavenly world, produce the lunar effect, which is the fruit of the <s>agnihotra</s> oblations.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,5.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.5.1]

children.text:
parjanyo vāva gautamāgniḥ |
tasya vāyur eva samit |
abhraṃ dhūmaḥ |
vidyud arciḥ |
aśanir aṅgārāḥ |
hrādunayo visphuliṅgāḥ || ChUp_5,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-cloud) is verily the [sacrificial] fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. Its fuel is the wind. Its smoke is the cloud. Its flame is lightning. Its embers are the thunderbolt. Its sparks are the hailstones.' (ChUp 5.5.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,5.1 dvitīyahomaparyāyārthamāha-parjanyo vāva parjanya eva gautamāgniḥ parjanyo nāma vṛṣṭyupakaraṇābhimānī devatāviśeṣaḥ /
tasya vāyureva samit /
vāyunā hi parjanyo 'gniḥ samidhyate /
purovātādiprābalye vṛṣṭidarśanāt /
abhraṃ dhūmo dhūmakāryatvāddhūmavacca lakṣyamāṇatvāt /
vidyudarciḥ /
prakāśasāmānyāt /
aśaniraṅgārāḥ /
kāṭhinyādvidyutsambandhādvā /
children.translated_text: because of the commonality of luminosity. Thunderbolts are the embers,

children.text: hrādunayo visphuliṅgāḥ /
children.translated_text: because of their hardness or because of their connection with lightning. Rumblings are the sparks,

children.text: hrādunayo garjitaśabdāḥ /
children.translated_text: rumblings being the sounds of thunder,

children.text: meghānāṃ viprakīrṇatvasamānyāt //1 //
children.translated_text: because of the commonality with the scattered nature of clouds. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.5.1:] For the purpose of the second round of oblation, he says — '<s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire.' <s>Parjanya</s> is the particular deity presiding over the means of rain. Its fuel is wind alone, for the fire that is <s>Parjanya</s> is kindled by wind — because rain is observed when the preceding winds and such are strong. Clouds are the smoke — because they serve the function of smoke and are perceived like smoke. Lightning is the flame,

children.text: START ChUp 5,5.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.5.2]

children.text:
tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhuter varṣaṃ saṃbhavati || ChUp_5,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'In this fire the gods offer <s>Soma Rājan</s> (King <s>Soma</s>). From that oblation, rain comes into being.' (ChUp 5.5.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,5.2 tasminnetasminnagnau devāḥ pūrvavatsomaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.5.2:] In this fire, the gods, as before, offer <s>Soma Rājan</s> (King <s>Soma</s>).

children.text: tasyā āhutervarṣaṃ sambhavati /
children.translated_text: From that oblation, rain comes into being.

children.text: śraddhākhyā āpaḥ somākāraṇapariṇatā dvitīye paryāye parjanyāgniṃ prāpya vṛṣṭitvena pariṇamante //2//
children.translated_text: The waters called <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), having been transformed into the form of <s>Soma</s>, reach the fire of <s>Parjanya</s> in the second round and are transformed into rain. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,6.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.6.1]

children.text:
pṛthivī vāva gautamāgniḥ |
tasyāḥ samvatsara eva samit |
ākāśo dhūmaḥ |
rātrir arciḥ |
diśo 'ṅgārāḥ |
avāntaradiśo visphuliṅgāḥ || ChUp_5,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The earth indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire. Its fuel is the year itself. Space is the smoke. Night is the flame. The directions are the embers. The intermediate directions are the sparks.' (ChUp 5.6.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,6.1 pṛthivī vāva gautamāgnirityādi pūrvavat /
tasyāḥ pṛthivyākhyasyāgneḥ saṃvatsara eva samit /
saṃvatsareṇa hi kālena samiddhā pṛthivī vrīhyādiniṣpattaye bhavati /
ākāśo dhūmaḥ, pṛthivyā ivotthita ākāśo dṛśyate /
yathāgnerdhūmaḥ /
rātrirarciḥ pṛthivyā hyaprakāśātmikāyā anurūpā rātriḥ /
tamorūpatvāt /
children.translated_text: because of being of the nature of darkness,

children.text: agnerivānurūpamarciḥ /
children.translated_text: just as flame is suited to fire.

children.text: diśo 'ṅgārā upaśāntatvasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: The directions are the embers — because of the commonality of being subdued.

children.text: evāntaradiśo visphuliṅgāḥ kṣudratvasāmānyāt //1 //
children.translated_text: The intermediate directions are the sparks — because of the commonality of being small. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.6.1:] 'The earth indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire' and so forth — as before. The fuel of this fire called earth is the year itself, for the earth, kindled by time in the form of the year, becomes [productive] for the ripening of rice and other [crops]. Space is the smoke — space appears as if rising from the earth, just as smoke [rises] from fire. Night is the flame — for night is suited to the earth, which is of the nature of darkness,

children.text: START ChUp 5,6.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.6.2]

children.text:
tasminn etasminn agnau devā varṣaṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhuter annaṃ saṃbhavati || ChUp_5,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'In this fire the gods offer rain. From that oblation, food comes into being.' (ChUp 5.6.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,6.2 tasminnityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.6.2:] 'In this' and so forth — the same [as before].

children.text: tasyā āhuterannaṃ vrīhiyavādi sambhavati //2//
children.translated_text: From that oblation, food such as rice and barley comes into being. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,7.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.7.1]

children.text:
puruṣo vāva gautamāgniḥ |
tasya vāg eva samit |
prāṇo dhūmaḥ |
jihvārciḥ |
cakṣur aṅgārāḥ |
śrotraṃ visphuliṅgāḥ || ChUp_5,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The person (<s>puruṣa</s>) indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire. His speech is the fuel. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is the smoke. The tongue is the flame. The eyes are the embers. The ears are the sparks.' (ChUp 5.7.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,7.1 puruṣo vāva gautamāgniḥ /
tasya vāgeva samit /
vācā hi mukhena samidhyate puruṣo na mūkaḥ /
prāṇo dhūmo dhūma iva mukhānnirgamanāt /
jihvārcirlohitatvāt /
children.translated_text: The tongue is the flame — because of its redness.

children.text: cakṣuraṅgārā bhāsa āśrayatvāt /
children.translated_text: The eyes are the embers — because they are the seat of light.

children.text: śrotraṃ visphuliṅgāḥ /
children.translated_text: The ears are the sparks,

children.text: viprakīrṇatvasāmyāt //1 //
children.translated_text: because of the commonality of being scattered. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.7.1:] The person indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire. His speech alone is the fuel, for a person is kindled through speech, through the mouth — a mute person is not [so kindled]. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the smoke — because it exits from the mouth like smoke.

children.text: START ChUp 5,7.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.7.2]

children.text:
tasminn etasminn agnau devā annaṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhuter retaḥ sambhavati || ChUp_5,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'In this fire the gods offer food. From that oblation, semen (<s>retas</s>) comes into being.' (ChUp 5.7.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,7.2 samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.7.2:] The rest is the same [as before].

children.text: annaṃ juhvati vrīhyādisaṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: They offer food — prepared from rice and other [grains].

children.text: tasyā āhute retaḥ sambhavati //2//
children.translated_text: From that oblation, semen comes into being. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,8.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.8.1]

children.text:
yoṣā vāva gautamāgniḥ |
tasyā upastha eva samit |
yad upamantrayate sa dhūmaḥ |
yonir arciḥ |
yad antaḥ karoti te 'ṅgārāḥ |
abhinandā visphuliṅgāḥ || ChUp_5,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Woman (<s>yoṣā</s>) indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire. Her lap is the fuel. That which invites is the smoke. The womb is the flame. What is done within — those are the embers. The pleasures are the sparks.' (ChUp 5.8.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,8.1 yoṣā vāva gautamāgniḥ /
tasyā upastha eva samit /
tena hi sā putrādyutpādanāya samidhyate /
yadupamantrayate sa dhūmaḥ /
srīsambhavādupamantraṇasya /
children.translated_text: because of the connection of courtship with modesty.

children.text: yonirarcirlohitatvāt /
children.translated_text: The womb is the flame — because of its redness.

children.text: yadantaḥ karoti te 'ṅgārā agnisambandhāt /
children.translated_text: What is done within — those are the embers — because of the connection with fire.

children.text: abhinandāḥ sukhalavā visphuliṅgāḥ kṣudratvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: The pleasures — the particles of pleasure — are the sparks, because of their smallness. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.8.1:] Woman indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire. Her lap alone is the fuel, for by that she is kindled for the production of sons and the like. That which invites — the courtship — is the smoke,

children.text: START ChUp 5,8.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.8.2]

children.text:
tasminn etasminn agnau devā reto juhvati |
tasyā āhuter garbhaḥ saṃbhavati || ChUp_5,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'In this fire the gods offer semen. From that oblation, the embryo comes into being.' (ChUp 5.8.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,8.2 tasminnetasminnagnau devā reto juhvati /
tasyā āhutergarbhaḥ sambhavatīti /
evaṃ śraddhāsomavarṣānnaretohavanaparyāyakrameṇā'pa eva garbhībhūtāstāḥ /
tatrāpāmāhutisamavāyitvātprādhānyavivakṣā'paḥ pañcamyāmāhutau puruṣavacaso bhavantīti /
na tvāpa eva kevalāḥ somādikāryamārabhante /
na cā'po 'trivṛtkṛtāḥ santīti /
trivṛtkṛtatve 'pi viśeṣasaṃjñālābho dṛṣṭaḥ pṛthivīyamimā āpo 'yamagnirityanyatamabāhulyanimittaḥ /
tasmātsamuditānyeva bhūtānyabbāhulyātkarmasamavāyīni somādikāryārambhakāṇyāpa ityucyante /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the elements in combination, because of the predominance of water — being invariably connected with <s>karma</s> and producing effects such as <s>Soma</s> — are called 'waters.'

children.text: dṛśyate ca dravabāhulyaṃ somavṛṣṭyannaretodeheṣu /
children.translated_text: And indeed, the predominance of liquid is observed in <s>Soma</s>, rain, food, semen, and the body.

children.text: bahudravaṃ ca śarīraṃ yadyapi pārthivam /
children.translated_text: Even though the body is earthy, it has abundant liquid.

children.text: tatra pañcamyāmāhutau hutāyāṃ retorūpā āpo garbhībhūtāḥ //2//
children.translated_text: There, in the fifth oblation having been offered, the waters in the form of semen become the embryo. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.8.2:] In this fire the gods offer semen. From that oblation, the embryo comes into being. Thus, through the successive rounds of oblation — <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>Soma</s>, rain, food, and semen — the waters themselves become the embryo. Here, since the waters are invariably concomitant with the oblation, speaking of them as primary — 'in the fifth oblation, the waters become person-voiced' — but it is not that water alone, by itself, produces the effects such as <s>Soma</s>. Nor are the waters un-tripartite (<s>atrivṛtkṛta</s>). Even when tripartite, the acquisition of a specific designation is seen [elsewhere]: 'This is earth, these are waters, this is fire' — determined by the predominance of one [element].

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,9.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.9.1]

children.text:
iti tu pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti |
sa ulbāvṛto garbho daśa vā nava vā māsān antaḥ śayitvā yāvad vātha jāyate || ChUp_5,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Thus, in the fifth oblation, the waters become person-voiced. The embryo, enclosed in the membrane, having lain within for ten or nine months, or however long, is then born.' (ChUp 5.9.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,9.1 iti tvevaṃ tu pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti vyākhyāta ekaḥ praśnaḥ /
yattu dyulokādimāṃ pratyāvṛttayorāhutyo pṛthivīṃ puruṣaṃ sriyaṃ krameṇā'viśya lokaṃ pratyutthāyī bhavatīti vājasaneyaka uktaṃ tatprāsaṅgikamihocyate /
iha ca prathame praśna uktaṃ vettha yadito 'dhi prajāḥ prayantīti /
tasya cāyamupakramaḥ /
sa garbho 'pāṃ pañcamaḥ pariṇāmaviśeṣa āhutikarmasamavāyinīnāṃ śraddhāśabdavācyānāmulbāvṛta ulbena jarāyuṇā'vṛto veṣṭito daśa vā nava vā māsānantarmātuḥ kukṣau śayitvā yāvadvā yāvatā kālena nyūnenātiriktena vāthānantaraṃ jāyate /
ulbāvṛta ityādi vairāgyahetoridamucyate /
children.translated_text: The words 'enclosed in the membrane' and so forth are said for the purpose of producing detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>).

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ hi mātuḥ kukṣau mūtrapurīṣavātapittaśleṣmādipūrṇe tadanuliptasya garbhasyolbāśucipaṭāvṛtasya lohitareto 'śucibījasya māturaśitapītarasānupraveśena vivardhamānasya niruddhaśaktibalavīryatejaḥprajñāceṣṭasya śayanam /
children.translated_text: For the lying of the embryo in the mother's womb is indeed painful — [the womb being] filled with urine, excrement, wind, bile, phlegm, and the like; the embryo smeared with those [substances], wrapped in the impure membrane-cloth, having impure blood and semen as its seed, growing through the entry of the juices of what is eaten and drunk by the mother, with its powers of strength, vigor, brilliance, wisdom, and movement all suppressed.

children.text: tato yonidvāreṇa pīḍyamānasya kaṣṭatarā niḥsṛtirjanmeti vairāgyaṃ grāhayati /
children.translated_text: Then, the emergence through the passage of the womb, being pressed, is even more painful — this is birth; thus [the text] makes one grasp detachment.

children.text: muhūrtamapyasahyaṃ daśa vā nava vā māsānatidīrghakālamantaḥ śayitveti ca //1 //
children.translated_text: Having lain within for ten or nine months — an exceedingly long time — which is unbearable even for a moment. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.9.1:] 'Thus indeed, in the fifth oblation, the waters become person-voiced' — thus one question has been explained. Now, regarding that which is stated in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension] — that [the soul], having returned from the heavenly world and such, enters the earth, the person, and the woman in succession through the oblations, and then rises again to the world — that is mentioned here incidentally. And in this [Upaniṣad], in the first question it was stated: 'Do you know where beings go from here?' This is its introduction. That embryo — the fifth transformation of the waters which are denoted by the word <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and are invariably connected with the act of oblation — enclosed by the membrane (<s>ulba</s>), the caul (<s>jarāyu</s>), wrapped and enveloped, having lain within the mother's womb for ten or nine months, or however long — whether shorter or longer a period — is then born.

children.text: START ChUp 5,9.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.9.2]

children.text:
sa jāto yāvadāyuṣaṃ jīvati |
taṃ pretaṃ diṣṭam ito 'gnaya eva haranti yata eveto yataḥ saṃbhūto bhavati || ChUp_5,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Having been born, he lives as long as his lifespan. When he is dead, having reached the appointed [end], the fires alone carry him from here — to the very place whence he came, whence he was born.' (ChUp 5.9.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,9.2 sa evaṃ jāto yāvadāyuṣaṃ punaḥ punarghaṭīyantravadgamanāgamanāya karma kurvankulālacakravadvā tiryagbhramaṇāya yāvatkarmaṇopāttamāyustāvajjīvati /
tamenaṃ kṣīṇāyuṣaṃ pretaṃ mṛtaṃ diṣṭaṃ karmaṇā nirdiṣṭaṃ paralokaṃ prati yadi cejjīvanvaidike karmaṇi jñāne vādhikṛtastamenaṃ mṛtamito 'smādgrāmādagnaye 'gnyarthamṛtvijo haranti putrā vāntyakarmaṇe /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.9.2:] He, thus born, performing <s>karma</s> for the sake of going and coming again like a water-wheel, or for revolving sideways like a potter's wheel, lives as long as his lifespan — as long as the lifespan acquired through <s>karma</s>. Him — whose lifespan is exhausted — dead, departed, appointed — directed by <s>karma</s> toward the other world — if he was indeed qualified during life for Vedic ritual or knowledge — him, when dead, the priests carry from here, from this village, for the sake of the fire, or the sons [carry him] for the final rites.

children.text: yata eveta āgato 'gneḥ sakāśācchraddhādyāhutikrameṇa, yataśca pañcabhyo 'gnibhyaḥ saṃbhūta utpanno bhavati tasmā evāgnaye haranti svāmeva yonimagnimāpādayantītyarthaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: From the very place whence he came — from fire, through the succession of oblations beginning with <s>śraddhā</s> — and from which five fires he was born — to that very fire they carry him; meaning they bring him back to his own source, the fire. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.10.1-2]

children.text:
tad ya itthaṃ viduḥ |
ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate |
te 'rciṣam abhisaṃbhavanti |
arciṣo 'haḥ |
ahna āpūryamāṇapakṣam |
āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaḍ udaṅṅ eti māsāṃs tān || ChUp_5,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, those who know this, and those who in the forest worship with faith and austerity — they pass into the flame; from the flame into the day; from the day into the waxing fortnight; from the waxing fortnight into the six months during which the sun moves northward.' (ChUp 5.10.1)

children.text:
māsebhyaḥ saṃvatsaram |
saṃvatsarād ādityam |
ādityāc candramasam |
candramaso vidyutam |
tat puruṣo 'mānavaḥ |
sa enān brahma gamayati |
eṣa devayānaḥ panthā iti || ChUp_5,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'From the months into the year; from the year to <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun); from <s>Āditya</s> to <s>Candramā</s> (the Moon); from <s>Candramā</s> to lightning. There, a person who is non-human [leads them]. He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>. This is the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>).' (ChUp 5.10.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,10.1,2 vettha yadito 'dhi prajāḥ prayantītyayaṃ praśnaḥ pratyupasthito 'pākartavyatayā /
tattatra lokaṃ pratyutthitānāmadhikṛtānāṃ gṛhamedhināṃ ya itthamevaṃ yathoktaṃ pañcāgnidarśanaṃ dyulokādyagnibhyo vayaṃ krameṇa jātā agnisvarūpāḥ pañcāgnyātmāna ityevaṃ vidurjānīyuḥ /
kathamavagamyata itthaṃ viduriti gṛhasthā evocyante nānya iti? gṛhasthānāṃ ye tvanitthaṃvidaḥ kevaleṣṭāpūrtadattaparāste dhūmādinā candraṃ gacchantīti vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.10.1-2:] The question 'Do you know where beings go from here?' has now presented itself for resolution. In that regard, among the qualified householders (<s>gṛhamedhin</s>s) who have risen to the [other] world — those who know this (<s>ittham</s>), that is, who know the <s>Pañcāgni Vidyā</s> (doctrine of the five fires) as described — [knowing that] 'we have been born in succession from the fires beginning with the heavenly world, we are of the nature of fire, our selves are the five fires' — they know thus. How is it understood that 'those who know thus' refers only to householders and not others? Because it will be said that those householders who do not know thus, who are devoted solely to ritual works (<s>iṣṭāpūrta</s>) and charity, go to the moon by the path of smoke and so forth.

children.text:
ye cāraṇyopalakṣitā vaikhānasāḥ parivrājakāśca śraddhātapa ityupāsate teṣāṃ cetthaṃvidbhiḥ sahārcirādinā gamanaṃ vakṣyati pāriśeṣyādagnihotrāhutisambandhācca gṛhasthā eva gṛhyanta itthaṃ viduriti /
nanu brahmacāriṇo 'pyagṛhītā grāmaśrutyāraṇyaśrutyā vidyante kathaṃ pāriśeṣyasiddhiḥ?naiṣa doṣaḥ /
purāṇasmṛtiprāmāṇyādūrdhvaretasāṃ naiṣṭhikabrahmacāriṇāmuttareṇārthā iti na viśeṣanirdeśārhāḥ /
nanūrdhvaretastvaṃ ceduttaramārgapratipattikāraṇaṃ purāṇasmṛtiprāmāṇyādiṣyata itthaṃvittvamanarthakaṃ prāptam /
na /
gṛhasthānpratyarthavattvāt /
ye gṛhasthā anitthaṃvidasteṣāṃ svabhāvato dakṣiṇo dhūmādiḥ panthāḥ prasiddhasteṣāṃ yaṃ itthaṃ viduḥ saguṇaṃ vānyadbrahma viduḥ /
"atha yadu caivāsmiñśavyaṃ kurvanti yadi nārciṣameva"iti liṅgāduttareṇa te gacchanti /
nanūrdhvaretasāṃ gṛhasthānāṃ ca samāna āśramitva ūrdhvaretasāmevottareṇa pathā gamanaṃ na gṛhasthānāmiti na yuktamagnihotrādivaidikakarmabāhulye ca sati /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
apūtā hi te /
śatrumitrasaṃyoganimittaṃ hi teṣāṃ rāgadveṣau /
tathā dharmādharmau hiṃsānugrahanimittau /
hiṃsānṛtamāyābrahmacaryādi ca bahvaśuddhikāraṇamaparihāryaṃ teṣām /
ato 'pūtāḥ /
apūtatvānnottareṇa pathā gamanam /
hiṃsānṛtamāyābrahmacaryādiparihārācca śuddhātmāno hītare śatrumitrarāgadveṣādiparihārācca virajasasteṣāṃ yukta uttaraḥ panthāḥ /
tathāca paurāṇikāḥ - "ye prajāmīṣire 'dhīrāste śmaśānāni bhejire /
ye prajāṃ neṣire dhīrāste 'mṛtatvaṃ hi bhejire" /
ityāhuḥ /
itthaṃvidāṃ gṛhasthānāmaraṇyavāsināṃ ca samānamārgatve 'mṛtatvaphale ca satyaraṇyavāsināṃ vidyānarthakyaṃ prāptam /
tathāca śrutivirodhaḥ /
"na tatra dakṣiṇā yanti nāvidvāṃsastapasvinaḥ"iti /
"sa enamavidito na bhunakti"iti ca viruddham /
na /
ābhūtasaṃplavasthānasyāmṛtatvena vivakṣitatvāt /
tatraivoktaṃ paurāṇikaiḥ-ābhūtasaṃptavaṃ sthānamamṛtatvaṃ hi bhāṣyate iti /
yaccā'tyantikamamṛtatvaṃ tadapekṣayā"na tatra dakṣiṇā yanti" "sa enamavidito na bhunaktī"-tyādyāḥ śrutaya ityato na virodhaḥ /
"na ca punarāvartanta"iti"maṃ mānavamāvartaṃ nā'vartanta"ityādiśrutivirodha iti cet /
na /
imaṃ mānavamiti viśeṣaṇātteṣāmiha na punarāvṛttirastīti ca /
yadi hyekāntenaiva nā'varterannimaṃ mānavamiheti ca viśeṣaṇamanarthakaṃ syāt /
imamihetyākṛtimātramucyata iti cet /
na /
anāvṛttiśabdenaiva nityānāvṛttyarthasya pratītatvādākṛtikalpanānarthikā /
ata imamiheti ca viśeṣaṇārthavattvāyānyatrā'vṛttiḥ kalpanīyā /
na ca sadekamevādvitīyamityevaṃpratyayavatāṃ mūrdhanyayā nāḍyārcirādimārgeṇa gamanam /
"brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyati" /
"tasmāttatsarvamabhavat" /
"na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti /
atraiva samavanīyante"ityādiśrutiśatebhyaḥ /
nanu tasmājjīvāduccikramiṣoḥ prāṇā notkrāmanti sahaiva gacchantītyayamarthaḥ kalpyata iti cet /
na /
atraiva samavanīyanta iti viśeṣaṇānarthakyāt /
sarve prāṇā anūtkrāmantīti ca prāṇairgamanasya prāptatvāt /
tasmādutkrāmantītyanāśaṅkaivaiṣā /
yadāpi mokṣasya saṃsāragativailakṣaṇyātprāṇānāṃ jīvena sahāgamāśṅkya tasmānnotkrāmantītyucyate tadāpyatraiva samavanīyanta iti viśeṣaṇamanarthakaṃ syāt /
na ca prāṇairviyuktasya gatirupapadyate jīvatvaṃ vā /
sarvagatatvātsadātmano niravayavatvātprāṇasambandhamātrameva hyagnivisphuliṅgavajjīvatvabhedakāraṇamityatastadviyoge jīvatvaṃ gatirvā na śakyā parikalpayituṃ śrutayaścetpramāṇam /
na sato 'ṇuravayavaḥ sphuṭito jīvākhyaḥ sadrūpaṃ chidrīkurvangacchatīti śakyaṃ kalpayitum /
tasmāt"tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti"iti saguṇabrahmopākasya prāṇaiḥ saha nāḍyā gamanaṃ sāpekṣameva cāmṛtatvaṃ na sākṣānmokṣa iti gamyate /
"tadaparājitā pūstadairaṃ madīyaṃ saraḥ"ityādyuktvā"teṣāmevaiṣa brahmalokaḥ"iti viśeṣamāt /
ataḥ pañcāgnivido gṛhasthā ye ceme 'raṇye vānaprasthāḥ parivrājakāśca saha naiṣṭhikabrahmacāribhiḥ śraddhā tapa ityevamādyupāsate śraddadhānāstapasvinaścetyarthaḥ /
upāsanaśabdastātparyārthaḥ /
iṣṭāpūrte dattamityupāsata iti yadvat /
śrutyantarādye ca satyaṃ brahma hiraṇyagarbhākhyamupāsate te sarve 'rciṣamarcirabhimāninīṃ devatāmabhisambhavanti pratipadyante /
children.translated_text: And from another <s>śruti</s>, those who worship <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> as the true [<s>Brahman</s>] — all of them reach the light (<s>arcis</s>), the deity presiding over the light.

children.text: samānamanyaccaturthagativyākhyānena /
children.translated_text: The rest is the same as the explanation of the fourth course [of the soul].

children.text: eṣa devayānaḥ panthā vyākhyātaḥ satyalokāvasāno nāṇḍādbahiḥ /
children.translated_text: This <s>devayāna</s> path (path of the gods) has been explained — it ends at the world of <s>Satya</s> (truth), not outside the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>).

children.text: "yadantarā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca"iti mantravarṇāt //1-2 //
children.translated_text: From the mantra text: 'That which is between the father and the mother.' (1–2)

And those who are characterized as forest-dwellers — <s>Vaikhānasas</s> (hermits) and <s>parivrājakas</s> (wandering ascetics) — who worship through faith and austerity, [the text] will state that their journey together with those possessing this knowledge is through the path of light (<s>arcirādi</s>). By the method of elimination and because of the connection with the <s>agnihotra</s> oblation, it is householders alone who are meant by 'those who know thus.' Now, [one might object:] celibate students (<s>brahmacārins</s>) too are not included in either the term 'village' or 'forest' — how then is the conclusion by elimination established? This is not a fault. Because by the authority of <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Smṛtis</s>, for the <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> (celibate) <s>naiṣṭhika brahmacārins</s>, the result is through the northern path — hence they need not be separately mentioned. Now, if celibacy is the cause of attaining the northern path on the authority of <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Smṛtis</s>, then 'knowing thus' would become purposeless. No — because it is meaningful with respect to householders. Those householders who do not 'know thus' — for them, the southern path of smoke and the rest is naturally well-known. But those among them who 'know thus' — who know <s>Brahman</s> with attributes (<s>saguṇa</s>) or another <s>Brahman</s> — from the indicative mark: 'Whether they perform the funeral rites or not, [they go] to the path of light' — they go by the northern path. Now, [if one objects:] since both the celibates and the householders belong to the same category of <s>āśramins</s> (stages of life), it is not proper that only celibates go by the northern path and not householders — especially when householders abound in Vedic rituals such as <s>agnihotra</s>. This is not a fault. For they [householders] are impure. Their attachment and aversion are caused by contact with enemies and friends. Likewise, their merit and demerit are caused by injury and benevolence. Violence, untruth, deceit, incontinence, and the like are abundant causes of impurity that are unavoidable for them. Therefore they are impure. Because of impurity, they do not go by the northern path. But the others [renunciants], by avoiding violence, untruth, deceit, incontinence, and the like, have purified selves; and by avoiding enemies, friends, attachment, aversion, and the like, they are free from passion — for them the northern path is appropriate. And thus the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (authors of <s>Purāṇas</s>) say: 'Those unwise ones who desired progeny entered the cremation grounds; those wise ones who did not desire progeny attained immortality.' If the path and the fruit of immortality were the same for householders possessing this knowledge and forest-dwellers, then the knowledge of the forest-dwellers would become purposeless. And there would be a contradiction with <s>śruti</s>: 'The southern ones do not go there, nor do the ignorant ascetics.' And it would contradict: 'Without knowing it, it does not nourish him.' No — because what is meant by 'immortality' is a station lasting until the dissolution of the world (<s>ābhūtasaṃplava</s>). The <s>Paurāṇikas</s> themselves have said there: 'The station lasting until the dissolution of the worlds is called immortality.' And the <s>śruti</s> passages 'the southern ones do not go there' and 'without knowing it, it does not nourish him' are with reference to absolute immortality — therefore there is no contradiction. If [one objects:] there is a contradiction with <s>śruti</s> passages like 'they do not return again' and 'they do not return to this human cycle' — no, because of the qualifier 'this human [cycle],' their non-return is only to this [world]. For if they absolutely never returned, the qualifier 'this human [cycle]' and 'here' would be purposeless. If [one says:] 'this' and 'here' are merely conventional expressions — no, because since the word 'non-return' itself conveys the meaning of permanent non-return, the supposition of a conventional expression is purposeless. Therefore, the qualifiers 'this' and 'here' serve a purpose [only if] return elsewhere is to be inferred. And for those who have the realization 'Being (<s>Sat</s>) is one alone, without a second,' there is no journey through the <s>nāḍī</s> at the crown of the head via the path of light. [As the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'Being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges into <s>Brahman</s>'; 'Therefore he became everything'; 'His vital breaths do not depart; right here they are gathered together' — from hundreds of such <s>śruti</s> passages. Now, if [one suggests:] the meaning should be construed that the vital breaths do not depart from the <s>jīva</s> who is about to depart, but rather they go together with him — no, because then the qualifier 'right here they are gathered together' would be purposeless. And since 'all vital breaths follow in departing' [shows that] the departure with vital breaths is already established, [the passage 'they do not depart'] cannot be a mere doubt. Even if it is said 'they do not depart' by suspecting that the vital breaths might not accompany the <s>jīva</s> since liberation is distinct from the course of transmigration — even then, the qualifier 'right here they are gathered together' would be purposeless. And for one separated from the vital breaths, neither journey nor the state of being a <s>jīva</s> is possible. Because the <s>ātman</s>, being <s>Sat</s> (Being), is all-pervading and partless — the mere connection with the vital breaths, like the sparks from fire, is the cause of the differentiation into <s>jīva</s>-hood — therefore, upon separation from them, neither <s>jīva</s>-hood nor journey can be conceived, if the <s>śruti</s> passages are [taken as] authoritative. Nor can one conceive that a minute, partless portion of <s>Sat</s>, called <s>jīva</s>, splits off and goes, piercing through the form of <s>Sat</s>. Therefore, from 'Rising upward by it, one attains immortality' — it is understood that the journey through the <s>nāḍī</s> together with the vital breaths is for the worshipper of <s>Brahman</s> with attributes (<s>saguṇa</s>), and the immortality is relative, not direct liberation. From the specification: 'That is the unconquered city, the golden lake that is mine' and then 'This <s>Brahmaloka</s> belongs to those [alone].' Therefore, householders who know the five fires (<s>pañcāgnividya</s>), and those who are forest-dwelling <s>vānaprasthas</s> and <s>parivrājakas</s> together with lifelong celibate <s>brahmacārins</s> — [all those who] worship through faith and austerity and the like — meaning those who are faithful and practice austerity — the word 'worship' (<s>upāsana</s>) conveys the essential purport, just as in '<s>iṣṭāpūrte</s> and gifts — thus they worship.'

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.10.3]

children.text:
atha ya ime grāma iṣṭāpūrte dattam ity upāsate |
te dhūmam abhisaṃbhavanti |
dhūmād rātrim |
rātrer aparapakṣam |
aparapakṣād yān ṣaḍ dakṣiṇaiti māsāṃs tān |
naite saṃvatsaram abhiprāpnuvanti || ChUp_5,10.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'But those who in the village worship through sacrificial rites (<s>iṣṭāpūrta</s>) and charitable gifts — they go to smoke; from smoke to the night; from the night to the dark fortnight; from the dark fortnight to the six months during which the sun moves southward. They do not reach the year.' (ChUp 5.10.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,10.3 athetyarthāntaraprastāvanārtho ya ime gṛhasthā grāme /
grāma iti gṛhasthānāmasādhāraṇaṃ viśeṣaṇamaraṇyavāsibhyo vyāvṛttyartham /
yathā vānaprasthaparivrājakānāmaraṇyaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ gṛhasthebhyo vyāvṛttyarthaṃ tadvat /
iṣṭāpūrte iṣṭamagnihotrādi vaidikaṃ karma pūrtaṃ vāpīkūpataḍāgārāmādikaraṇam /
dattaṃ bahirvedi yathāśaktyarhebhyo dravyasaṃvibhāgo dattam /
ityevaṃvidhaṃ paricaraṇaparitrāṇādyupāsate /
itiśabdasya prakāradarśanārthatvāt /
te darśanavarjitatvāddhūmaṃ dhūmābhimāninīṃ devatāmabhisambhavanti pratipadyante /
tayātivāhitā dhūmādrātriṃ rātridevatāṃ rātredevatāṃ rātreraparapakṣadevatāmeva kṛṣṇapakṣābhimāninīmaparapakṣādyānṣaṇmāsāndakṣiṇā dakṣiṇāṃ daśameti savitā /
children.translated_text: Conveyed by that [deity], from smoke to the night — to the deity of the night; from the deity of the night to the deity of the dark fortnight — the deity presiding over the waning fortnight; from the dark fortnight to the six months during which the sun moves southward.

children.text: tānmāsāndakṣiṇāyanaṣaṇmāsābhimāninīrdevatāḥ pratipadyanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: They reach the deities presiding over the six months of the southern course (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>) — this is the meaning.

children.text: saṅghacāriṇyo hi ṣaṇmāsadevatā iti māsāniti bahuvacanaprayogastāsu naite karmiṇaḥ prakṛtāḥ saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsarasya hyekasyāvayavabhūte dakṣiṇottarāyaṇe tatrārcirādimārgapravṛttānāmudagayanamāsebhyo 'vayavinaḥ saṃvatsarasya prāptiruktā /
children.translated_text: For the deities of the six months travel as a group — hence the plural usage 'months' for them. These ritualists who are the subject [of discussion] do not reach the year — for the two half-years, the southern and the northern, are parts of the one year. There, for those who proceed on the path of light, arrival at the year [as a whole] through the months of the northern course has been stated.

children.text: ata ihāpi tadavayavabhūtānāṃ dakṣiṇāyanamāsānāṃ praptiṃ śrutvā tadavayavinaḥ saṃvatsarasyāpi pūrvavatpraptirāpannetyatastatprāptiḥ pratiṣidhyate naite saṃvatsaramabhiprāpnuvantīti //3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore here too, having heard of the arrival at the months of the southern course which are parts [of the year], one might infer arrival at the year [as a whole] of which they are parts, as before — hence that arrival [at the year] is negated: 'They do not reach the year.' (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.10.3:] 'But' (<s>atha</s>) introduces a different topic. Those who are householders in the village — 'in the village' is a distinguishing qualifier exclusive to householders, meant to differentiate them from forest-dwellers, just as 'forest' is the distinguishing qualifier for <s>vānaprasthas</s> and <s>parivrājakas</s>, meant to differentiate them from householders. <s>Iṣṭāpūrta</s> — <s>iṣṭa</s> is Vedic ritual action such as <s>agnihotra</s>; <s>pūrta</s> is the construction of wells, tanks, ponds, gardens, and the like. <s>Datta</s> (gifts) — giving, distributing wealth according to one's ability to the deserving, outside the sacrificial enclosure. They worship — that is, they serve and protect — in this manner. The word <s>iti</s> indicates the general character [of such activities]. They, being devoid of [higher] knowledge, go to smoke — to the deity presiding over smoke.

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.10.4]

children.text:
māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokam |
pitṛlokād ākāśam |
ākāsāc candramasam |
eṣa somo rājā |
tad devānām annam |
taṃ devā bhakṣayanti || ChUp_5,10.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'From the months to the world of the fathers; from the world of the fathers to space; from space to the moon. This is King <s>Soma</s>. That is the food of the gods. The gods consume it.' (ChUp 5.10.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,10.4 māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokaṃ pitṛlokādākāśamākāśāccandramasam /
ko 'sau yastaiḥ prāpyate candramā ya eṣa dṛśyate 'ntarikṣe somo rājā brāhmaṇānāṃ, tadannaṃ devānāṃ taṃ candramasamannaṃ devā indrādayo bhakṣayanti /
ataste dhūmādinā gatvā candrabhūtāḥ karmiṇo devairbhakṣyante /
nanvanarthāyeṣṭādikaraṇaṃ yadyannabhūtā devairbhakṣyeran /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
annamityupakaraṇamātrasya vivakṣitatvāt /
na hi te kavalotkṣepeṇa devairbhakṣyante /
kiṃ tarhyupakaraṇamātraṃ devānāṃ bhavanti te strīpaśubhṛtyādivat /
dṛṣṭaścānnaśabda upakaraṇeṣu"striyo 'nnaṃ paśavo 'nnaṃ viśāṃ viśo 'nnaṃ rājñām" ityādi /
na ca teṣāṃ stryādīnāṃ puruṣopabhogyatve 'pyupabhogo nāsti /
tasmātkarmiṇo devānāmupabhogyā api santaḥ sukhino devaiḥ krīḍanti /
śarīraṃ ca teṣāṃ sukhopabhogayogyaṃ candramaṇḍala āpyamārabhyate /
taduktaṃ purastācchraddhāśabdā āpo dyulokāgnau hutāḥ somo rājā sambhavatīti /
children.translated_text: It was stated earlier: the waters called <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), offered in the fire of the heavenly world, give rise to King <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: tā āpaḥ karmasamavāyinya itaraiśca bhūtairanugatā dyulokaṃ prāpya candratvamāpannāḥ śarīrādyārambhikā iṣṭādyupāsakānāṃ bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Those waters, conjoined with <s>karma</s> and accompanied by the other elements, having reached the heavenly world and attained the state of the moon, become the material cause of the body and the rest for the worshippers of sacrifices and the like.

children.text: antyāyāṃ ca śarīrāhutāvagnau hutāyāmagninā dahyamāne śarīre tadutthā āpo dhūmena sahordhvaṃ yajamānamāveṣṭya candramaṇḍalaṃ prāpya kuśamṛttikāsthānīyā bāhyaśarīrārambhikā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: And when the final oblation — the body — is offered in the fire, when the body is being burnt by fire, the waters arising from it, enveloping the sacrificer together with the smoke and rising upward, reach the sphere of the moon and become the material cause of the outer body, serving the function of grass and earth [in the sacrifice].

children.text: tadārabdhena ca śarīreṇeṣṭādiphalamupabhuñjānā āsate //4 //
children.translated_text: And with the body thus formed, they sit enjoying the fruits of sacrifices and the like. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.10.4:] From the months to the world of the fathers; from the world of the fathers to space; from space to the moon. Who is this moon that is reached by them? It is this <s>Soma</s> the king, visible in the sky, [the king] of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. That is the food of the gods. The gods — <s>Indra</s> and the others — consume that moon as food. Therefore, having gone by the path of smoke and the rest, the ritualists become the moon and are consumed by the gods. Now, [one might object:] if they become food and are consumed by the gods, the performance of sacrifices and the like would be to no purpose. This is not a fault — because what is meant by 'food' is merely being a means of enjoyment (<s>upakaraṇa</s>). For they are not consumed by the gods through being swallowed as morsels. Rather, they become merely instruments of enjoyment for the gods, like wives, cattle, servants, and the like. And the word 'food' is seen used for instruments: 'Women are food, cattle are food, subjects are food for the king,' and so on. And although those wives and the like are objects of enjoyment for men, it is not the case that they themselves have no enjoyment. Therefore, the ritualists, even while being objects of enjoyment for the gods, are happy and sport with the gods. And their body suitable for the enjoyment of happiness begins to be formed in the sphere of the moon from water (<s>āpya</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.10.5]

children.text:
tasmin yavātsaṃpātam uṣitvāthaitam evādhvānaṃ punar nivartante |
ākāśam |
ākāśād vāyum |
vāyur bhūtvā dhūmo bhavati |
dhūmo bhūtvābhraṃ bhavati || ChUp_5,10.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Having dwelt there as long as there is a residue [of merit], they return again by the same path — to space; from space to wind. Having become wind, one becomes smoke. Having become smoke, one becomes mist.' (ChUp 5.10.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,10.5 yāvattadupabhoganimittasya karmaṇaḥ kṣayaḥ sampatanti yeneti sampātaḥ karmaṇaḥ kṣayo yāvatsampātaṃ yāvatkarmaṇaḥ kṣaya ityarthaḥ /
tāvattasmiṃścandramaṇḍala uṣitvāthānantarametameva vakṣyamāṇamadhvānaṃ mārgaṃ punarnivartnate /
punarnivartanta iti prayogātpūrvamapyasakṛccandramaṇḍalaṃ gatā nivṛttāścā'sanniti gamyate /
tasmādiha loka iṣṭādikarmopacitya candraṃ gacchanti /
tatkṣaye cā'vartante /
kṣaṇamātramapi tatra sthātuṃ na labhyate /
sthitinimittakarmakṣayāt /
snehakṣayādiva pradīpasya /
tatra kiṃ yena karmaṇā candramaṇḍalamārūḍhastasya sarvasya kṣaye tasmādavarohaṇaṃ kiṃ vā sāvaśeṣa iti /
kiṃ tataḥ /
yadi sarvasyaiva kṣayaḥ karmaṇaścandramaṇḍalasthasyaiva mokṣaḥ prāpnoti /
tiṣṭhatu tāvattatraiva mokṣaḥ syānna veti /
tata āgatasyeha śarīropabhogādi na sambhavati /
"tataḥ śeṣeṇe"tyādismṛtivirodhaśca syāt /
nanviṣṭāpūrtadattavyatirekeṇāpi manuṣyaloke śarīropabhoganimittāni karmāṇyanekāni sambhavanti /
na ca teṣāṃ candramaṇḍala upabhogaḥ /
ato 'kṣīṇāni tāni /
yannimitaṃ candramaṇḍalamārūḍhastānyeva kṣīṇānītyavirodhaḥ /
śeṣaśabdaśca sarveṣāṃ karmatvasāmānyādaviruddhaḥ /
ata eva ca tatraiva mokṣaḥ syāditi doṣābhāvaḥ /
viruddhānekayonyupabhogaphalānāṃ ca karmaṇāmekaikasya jantorārambhakatvasambhavāt /
na caikasmiñjanmani sarvakarmaṇāṃ kṣaya upapadyate /
brahmahatyādeścaikaikasya karmaṇo 'nekajanmārambhakatvasmaraṇāt /
sthāvarādiprāptānāṃ cātyantamūḍhānāmutkarmaṣahetoḥ karmaṇa ārambhakatvāsambhavāt /
garbhabhūtānāṃ ca sraṃsamānānāṃ karmāsambhave saṃsārānupapattiḥ /
tasmānnaikasmiñjanmani sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāmupabhogaḥ /
yattu kaiściducyate sarvakarmaśriyopamardena prāyaṇe karmaṇāṃ janmārambhakatvam /
tatra kānicitkarmāṇyanārambhakatvenaiva tiṣṭhanti kānicijjanmā'rabhanta iti nopapadyate /
maraṇasya sarvakarmābhivyañjakatvātsvagocarābhivyañjakapradīpavaditi /
tadasat /
sarvasya sarvātmakatvābhyupagamāt /
na hi sarvasya sarvātmakatve deśakālanimittāvaruddhatvātsarvātmanopamardaḥ kasyacitkvacidabhivyaktirvā sarvātmanopapadyate /
tathā karmaṇāmapi sāśrayāṇāṃ bhavet /
yathā ca pūrvānubhūtamanuṣyamayūramarkaṭādijanmābhisaṃskṛtā viruddhānekavāsanā markaṭatvaprāpakena karmaṇā markaṭajanmā'rabhamāṇena nopamṛdyante tathā karmāṇyapyanyajanmaprāptinimittāni nopamṛdyanta iti yuktam /
yadi hi sarvāḥ pūrvajanmānubhavavāsanā upamṛdyeranmarkaṭajanmanimittena karmaṇā markaṭajanmanyārabdhe markaṭasya jātamātrasya mātuḥ śākhāyāḥ śākhāntaragamane māturudarasaṃlagnatvādikauśalaṃ na prāpnoti /
iha janmanyanabhyastatvāt /
na cātītānantarajanmani markaṭatvamevā'sīttasyeti śakyaṃ vaktum /
"taṃ vidyākarmaṇī samanvārabhete pūrvaprajñā ca"iti śruteḥ /
tasmādvāsanāvannāśeṣakarmopamarda iti śeṣakarmasambhavaḥ /
yata evaṃ tasmāccheṣeṇopabhuktātkarmaṇaḥ saṃsāra upapadyata iti na kaścidvirodhaḥ /
ko 'sāvadhvā yaṃ prati nivartanta ityucyate /
yathetaṃ yathāgataṃ nivartante /
nanu māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokaṃ pitṛlokādākāśamākāśāccandramasamiti gamanakrama ukto na tathā nivṛttiḥ /
kiṃ tarhyakāśādvāyumityādi, kathaṃ yathetamityucyate /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
ākāśaprāptestulyatvātpṛthivīprāpteśca na cātra yathetameveti niyamo 'nevaṃvidhamapi nivartante punarnivartante iti tu niyamaḥ /
ata upalakṣaṇārthametadyathetamiti /
ato bhautikamākāśaṃ tāvatpratipadyante /
yāsteṣāṃ candramaṇḍale śarīrārambhikā āpa āsaṃstāsteṣāṃ tatropabhoganimittānāṃ karmaṇāṃ kṣaye vilīyante /
ghṛtasaṃsthānamivāgnisaṃyoge /
tā vilīnā antarikṣasthā ākāśabhūtā iva sūkṣmā bhavanti tā antarikṣādvāyurbhavanti /
children.translated_text: Those dissolved [waters], existing in the atmosphere, become subtle like space. From the atmosphere they become wind.

children.text: vāyupratiṣṭhā vāyubhūtā itaścāmutaścohyamānāstābhiḥ saha kṣīṇakarmā vāyubhūto bhavati /
children.translated_text: Established in wind — having become wind-like — being carried here and there by it, [the soul] along with those [waters] becomes wind-like, its <s>karma</s> [for that state] having been exhausted.

children.text: vāyurbhūtvā tābhiḥ sahaiva dhūmo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Having become wind, along with those [waters] it becomes smoke.

children.text: dhūmo bhūtvābhramabbharaṇamātrarūpo bhavati //5 //
children.translated_text: Having become smoke, it becomes cloud — having merely the form of moisture-bearing [vapor]. (5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.10.5:] <s>Sampāta</s> means the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> — that by which [one falls] is the fall, [meaning] the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>; 'until the fall' means until the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>. Having dwelt that long in the lunar sphere, thereafter he returns by the very path that will be described. From the usage 'they return again,' it is understood that even before, they had gone to the lunar sphere and returned, not just once. Therefore, in this world they accumulate <s>karma</s> through <s>iṣṭa</s> (ritual offerings) and the like, go to the moon, and when that [karma] is exhausted, they return. Not even for a moment can one remain there [once karma is exhausted], because the <s>karma</s> that caused the stay is exhausted — like a lamp when oil is consumed. The question arises: is it upon the exhaustion of all the <s>karma</s> by which one ascended to the lunar sphere that one descends from it, or is there a remainder? What follows from this? If all <s>karma</s> is exhausted, then liberation should result while still in the lunar sphere. Let that be — first [consider] whether liberation would occur there or not. [If it did,] then for one who has come [back] from there, bodily experience and the like in this world would be impossible. And there would be a contradiction with the <s>smṛti</s>: 'With the remainder [of karma]...' and so on. [Objection:] But apart from <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (ritual and charitable works), there are many <s>karmas</s> that cause bodily experience in the human world. And these are not experienced in the lunar sphere. Therefore, they are not exhausted. Only those <s>karmas</s> by reason of which one ascended to the lunar sphere are exhausted — hence there is no contradiction. The word 'remainder' (<s>śeṣa</s>) is not contradicted because of the commonality of all being <s>karma</s>. And therefore the objection that liberation would occur there is also without fault. Because it is possible that <s>karmas</s> producing experience in mutually contradictory births are the initiators [of new births] for each individual being. And it is not possible that all <s>karmas</s> are exhausted in a single lifetime — because it is remembered that even a single <s>karma</s> such as <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brāhmaṇa) initiates many births. And for those who have reached the state of plants and other [immobile beings], being completely deluded, the possibility of <s>karma</s> initiating an upward movement is impossible. And for those in the womb who are miscarrying, if <s>karma</s> were impossible, <s>saṃsāra</s> would be impossible. Therefore, not all <s>karmas</s> are experienced in a single lifetime. As for what some say — that at the time of death, by the overwhelming force of all <s>karmas</s>, [certain] <s>karmas</s> initiate birth — [the objection is:] it would be impossible that some <s>karmas</s> remain without initiating [birth] while others initiate birth, because death manifests all <s>karmas</s>, like a lamp that illuminates everything within its range. That is incorrect — because it is accepted that everything has the nature of everything [i.e., all karmas are interconnected]. For if everything has the nature of everything, then, being confined by place, time, and cause, a complete overwhelming of all [karmas] by any one, or the manifestation of all at once, is impossible. The same would apply to <s>karmas</s> together with their substrata. Just as the diverse and contradictory <s>vāsanā</s>s (latent impressions) formed by previously experienced births as humans, peacocks, monkeys, and the like are not destroyed by the <s>karma</s> that brings about monkey-birth when it initiates a monkey birth — similarly, it is reasonable that <s>karmas</s> causing the attainment of other births are also not destroyed. For if all <s>vāsanā</s>s of previous births were destroyed by the <s>karma</s> causing monkey-birth, then when a monkey birth is initiated, the newborn monkey would not have the skill of moving from branch to branch or clinging to the mother's belly — since it was not practiced in this birth. Nor can it be said that in the immediately preceding birth it was also a monkey. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'Knowledge and <s>karma</s> follow him, along with previous understanding.' Therefore, since <s>vāsanā</s>s persist, there is no destruction of all remaining <s>karma</s>, and so the existence of residual <s>karma</s> is established. Since this is so, <s>saṃsāra</s> is possible through the remainder [of karma] after the experienced <s>karma</s> — hence there is no contradiction. What is this path to which they return? They return as they came. [Objection:] But the order of going was stated as: from the months to <s>Pitṛloka</s>, from <s>Pitṛloka</s> to space, from space to the moon — the return is not in that [same] order. Rather, it is: from space to wind, and so on. How then is it said 'as they came'? This is no defect — because the arrival at space is the same [in both directions], and the arrival at earth [is the same]. And there is no strict rule here that [the return must be] exactly as they came — rather the rule is only that they do return. Therefore this [phrase] 'as they came' is merely indicative. So they first reach physical space. The waters that served as the body-seed in the lunar sphere — upon the exhaustion of the <s>karmas</s> that caused their experience there, these dissolve, like ghee when brought into contact with fire.

children.text:
abhraṃ bhūtvā megho bhavati |
megho bhūtvā pravarṣati |
ta iha vrīhiyavā oṣadhivanaspatayas tilamāsā iti jāyante 'to vai khalu durniṣprapataram |
yo yo hy annam atti yo retaḥ siñcati tad bhūya eva bhavati || ChUp_5,10.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Having become cloud, it becomes a rain-cloud. Having become a rain-cloud, it rains down. They are born here as rice, barley, herbs, trees, sesame, and beans. From this state, escape is indeed most difficult. For whoever eats the food and deposits the seed, it becomes like that again.' (ChUp 5.10.6)

children.translated_text: Nor can it be inferred that Vedic rituals have a twofold result [both good and bad] because they involve <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence),

children.text: hiṃsāyāḥ śāstracoditatvāt /
children.translated_text: because the <s>hiṃsā</s> [in ritual] is enjoined by scripture.

children.text: "ahiṃsansarvabhūtānyanyatra tīrthebhyaḥ"iti śruteḥ śāstracoditāyā hiṃsāyā nādharmahetutvamabhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: From the Śruti "not harming any beings except at sacred rites (<s>tīrtha</s>)," it is accepted that violence enjoined by scripture does not cause <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).

children.text: abhyupagate 'pyadharmahetutve mantrairviṣādivattadapanayopapatterna duḥkhakāryārambhakatvopapattirvaidikānāṃ karmaṇāṃ mantreṇeva viṣabhakṣaṇasyeti //6 //
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 5.10.6] Even if it were accepted as causing <s>adharma</s>, its removal through <s>mantras</s> — like the neutralization of poison — is logically established. Therefore, it is not logical that Vedic rituals produce painful results, just as eating poison accompanied by a <s>mantra</s> [does not produce harm]. //6//

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.10.6:] Having become cloud, then it becomes a rain-cloud capable of pouring; having become a rain-cloud, it rains upon elevated places. The meaning is: in the form of rain-streams, the one with residual <s>karma</s> falls down. They are born here as rice, barley, herbs, trees, sesame, beans, and such forms. The plural is used because there are many whose <s>karma</s> is exhausted [to different degrees]. The singular was used earlier for clouds and such because they were of one form. Because there are thousands of locations — mountain slopes, ravines, rivers, oceans, forests, deserts — upon which [they] fall with the rain-streams, therefore indeed escape is most difficult — [meaning] it is very hard to get out, very hard to emerge. Because those carried by water-currents from mountain slopes reach rivers, thence the ocean, where they are eaten by crocodiles and such; those in turn by others. And having dissolved along with the crocodile in the ocean, drawn up by rain-clouds from the ocean waters, they again fall with rain-streams upon deserts or inaccessible rocky surfaces. Sometimes they are drunk by serpents and wild animals, or eaten by others; those in turn by others — such are the transformations [they undergo]. Sometimes born as inedible plants, they would dry up right there. Even for those born as edible plants, the connection with semen and a body is extremely rare because of the great number of plants — hence the difficulty of escape. Alternatively, from this state of being rice, barley, and so on, escape is most difficult. In '<s>durniṣprapataram</s>,' one 'ta' should be understood as elided. The state of rice and barley is <s>durniṣprapata</s> (hard to escape from); even harder to escape from than that is the connection with semen, body, and a woman — that is the meaning. Because they are eaten by <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> (celibates), children, those lacking virility, or the elderly, and perish in between — because food-eaters are many. Only occasionally, by a chance coincidence, are they eaten by semen-producers; when that happens, those who have attained the state of semen obtain the fruition of their <s>karma</s>. How? Whoever eats food conjoined with the latent-impression-bearers (<s>anuśayins</s>) and deposits semen in a woman during the fertile period — it becomes like that again, meaning it assumes that very form. The predominance of form of those parts — this predominance is called 'becoming that again' — having entered the womb of a woman in the form of semen, the latent-impression-bearer. Because semen takes the form of the semen-producer. From another <s>śruti</s>: 'The vital energy gathers from all the limbs.' Therefore it assumes the very form of the semen-producer — that is the meaning. Thus, from a man a man is born, having the very form of a cow from a cow — not the form of another species. Therefore it is fitting that 'it becomes like that again.' But those others who, being of sinful <s>karma</s>, without ascending to the lunar sphere and without being latent-impression-bearers, right here attain the state of rice, barley, and such, and then the state of humans and so on — for them, escape is not as difficult as for the latent-impression-bearers. Why? Because through <s>karma</s> they have assumed the body of rice and the like; upon exhaustion of the <s>karma</s> causing that experience, at the destruction of the rice-stalk body, they transition to ever-new bodies according to their earned <s>karma</s>, like a leech — being possessed of consciousness. From another <s>śruti</s>: 'He becomes possessed of consciousness; with consciousness he passes on.' Even though they go to another body with withdrawn sense-organs, still, like in a dream, they go to another body possessed of consciousness through the knowledge produced by the <s>vāsanā</s>s generated by the <s>karma</s> that causes the attainment of another body. This is established by the authority of <s>śruti</s>. Similarly, the journey via the light and via smoke is with awakened consciousness, like a dreamer. Because the journey is caused by <s>karma</s> that has obtained fruition. But for the latent-impression-bearers born as rice and the like, the conscious connection with semen, woman, and body is not possible in the same way. For there is no continuity of consciousness for those in the states of rice, salt-grinding, pounding, and such. [Objection:] But even for those descending from the lunar sphere, since the transition to another body is the same, consciousness like a leech would be fitting. If so, then terrible hellish experience would follow for performers of <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> from the lunar sphere all the way to <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> birth and the like.
