And thus, the practice of <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> and meditation prescribed [by scripture] would be for the purpose of harm alone. And the <s>śruti</s> would become unauthoritative, since Vedic rituals would be connected with harm. [Reply:] No — because a distinction is possible, like climbing a tree and falling from it. For one who wishes to transition from body to body, when the <s>karma</s> obtains fruition, consciousness through the knowledge generated by that <s>karma</s> is appropriate — like one who climbs to the top of a tree wishing to grasp a fruit. Similarly, those traveling via the light would have consciousness, and those wishing to ascend to the lunar sphere via smoke [would have consciousness]. But not so for those wishing to descend from the lunar sphere — like those falling from the top of a tree, they lack consciousness. Just as those struck by a mace and the like, with their sense-organs obstructed due to the stupefaction caused by the blow, are seen to be devoid of consciousness while being carried from place to place in their own body — similarly, for those wishing to descend from the lunar sphere to a human or other body, their bodies being crushed by the exhaustion of the <s>karma</s> that produced heavenly enjoyment, their sense-organs being obstructed — therefore, they, stupefied with the waters that are the seeds of [future] bodies, not having abandoned [those waters], descend through the sequence of space and the rest, and become connected with plant bodies and other stationary forms according to their <s>karma</s> — their consciousness not having arisen due to the obstruction of their sense-organs. Similarly, during the processes of salting, grinding, pounding, cooking, eating, transformation into essences, and the time of semen-deposit, [they remain] as if stupefied — because the <s>karma</s> that initiates another body has not yet obtained fruition. Since they exist in all states without abandoning the connection with the waters that are the seeds of bodies, the consciousness like a leech is not contradicted. But the unconsciousness in the interval is like that of a stupefied person — hence there is no fault.

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.7
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.10.7]

children.text:
tad ya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te ramaṇīyāṃ yonim āpadyeran brāhmaṇayoniṃ vā kṣatriyayoniṃ vā vaiśyayoniṃ vā |
atha ya iha kapūyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te kapūyāṃ yonim āpadyerañ śvayonim vā sūkarayoniṃ vā caṇḍālayoniṃ vā || ChUp_5,10.7 ||
children.translated_text: Now, those here whose conduct is pleasant — it is likely that they would attain a pleasant birth: the birth of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or the birth of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, or the birth of a <s>vaiśya</s>. But those here whose conduct is evil — it is likely that they would attain an evil birth: the birth of a dog, or the birth of a pig, or the birth of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>.

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,10.7 tattatra teṣvanuśayināṃ ya iha loke ramaṇīyaṃ śobhanaṃ caraṇaṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ ramaṇīyacaraṇenopalakṣitaḥ śobhano 'nuśayaḥ puṇyaṃ karma yeṣāṃ te ramaṇīyacaraṇā ucyante /
krauryānṛtamāyāvarjitānāṃ hi śakya upalakṣayituṃ śubhānuśayasadbhāvaḥ /
tenānuśayena puṇyena karmaṇā candramaṇḍale bhuktaśeṣeṇābhyāśo ha kṣiprameva /
yaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ te ramaṇīyāṃ krauryādivarjitāṃ yonimāpadyeranprāpnuyurbrāhmaṇayoniṃ vā kṣattriyayoniṃ vā vaiśyayoniṃ vā svakarmānurūpeṇa /
children.translated_text: the word 'yat' qualifies the action — they would attain, that is, reach a pleasant birth free from cruelty and the like: the birth of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or the birth of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, or the birth of a <s>vaiśya</s>, in accordance with their own <s>karma</s>.

children.text: atha punarye tadviparītāḥ kapūyacaraṇopalakṣitakarmāṇo 'śubhānuśayā abhyāśo ha yatte kapūyāṃ yathākarma yonimāpadyerankapūyāmeva dharmasambandhavarjitāṃ jugupsitāṃ yonimāpadyeran śvayoniṃ vā sūkarayoniṃ vā svakarmānurūpeṇaiva /
children.translated_text: But those who are the opposite — whose <s>karma</s> is characterized by evil conduct, who have inauspicious residual impressions — quickly indeed they would attain an evil birth. According to their <s>karma</s>, they attain an evil birth devoid of any connection with <s>dharma</s>, a despicable birth: the birth of a dog, or the birth of a pig — in accordance with their own <s>karma</s> alone.

children.text: ye tu ramaṇīyacaraṇā dvijātayaste svakarmasthāścediṣṭādikāriṇaste dhūmādigatyā gacchantyāgacchanti ca punaḥ punarghaṭīyantravat /
children.translated_text: Those of pleasant conduct who are twice-born (<s>dvijāti</s>), if they are established in their own duties and perform <s>iṣṭa</s> (sacrificial rites) and such, they go by the path of smoke and return again and again, like a water-wheel.

children.text: vidyāṃ cetprāpnuyustadārcirādinā gacchanti //7 //
children.translated_text: If they attain knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), then they go by the path of light (<s>arcis</s>) and so forth. //7//

[Bhāṣya 5.10.7] There, among those who have residual impressions (<s>anuśaya</s>), those in this world whose conduct (<s>caraṇa</s>) is pleasant (<s>ramaṇīya</s>), that is, whose character (<s>śīla</s>) is good — they are called those of pleasant conduct. Those characterized by pleasant conduct are said to have auspicious residual impressions, that is, meritorious <s>karma</s>. For those free from cruelty, falsehood, and deceit, the existence of auspicious residual impressions can be inferred. By that residual merit — the remainder of <s>karma</s> enjoyed in the lunar sphere — quickly indeed,

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.8
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.10.8]

children.text:
athaitayoḥ pathor na katareṇacana tānīmāni kṣudrāṇy asakṛdāvartīni bhūtāni bhavanti jāyasva mriyasveti |
etat tṛtīyaṃ sthānam |
tenāsau loko na saṃpūryate |
tasmāj jugupseta |
tad eṣa ślokaḥ || ChUp_5,10.8 ||
children.translated_text: But those who follow neither of these two paths — these are the tiny creatures that are born again and again in endless cycles: 'Be born and die' — this is the third state. Therefore that world is not filled up. Therefore one should feel revulsion. On this there is this verse:

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,10.8 yadā tu na vidyāsevino nāpīṣṭādikarma sevante tadāthaitayoḥ pathoryathoktayorarcirdhūmādilakṣaṇayorna katareṇānyatareṇacanāpi yanti tānīmāni bhūtāni kṣūdrāṇi daṃśamasakakīṭādīnyasakṛdāvartīni bhavanti /
ata ubhayamārgaparibhraṣṭā hyasakṛjjāyante mriyante cetyarthaḥ /
teṣāṃ jananamaraṇasantateranukaraṇamidamucyate /
jāyasva mriyasvetīśvaranimittaceṣṭocyate /
jananamaraṇalakṣaṇenaiva kālayāpanā bhavati /
na tu kriyāsu bhogeṣu vā kālo 'stītyarthaḥ /
etatkṣudrajantulakṣaṇaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pūrvoktau panthānāvapekṣya sthānaṃ saṃsaratām /
yenaivaṃ dakṣiṇamārgagā api punarāgacchantyanadhikṛtānāṃ jñānakarmaṇoragamanameva dakṣiṇena patheti /
tenāsau loko na saṃpūryate /
pañcamastu praśnaḥ pañcāgnividyayā vyākhyātaḥ /
prathamo dakṣiṇottaramārgābhyāmapākṛto dakṣiṇottarayoḥ pathorvyāvartanāpi mṛtānāmagnau prakṣepaḥ samānastato vyāvartanānye 'rcirādinā yantyanye dhūmādinā /
punaruttaradakṣiṇāyane ṣaṇmāsānprapnuvantaḥ saṃyujya punarvyāvartante /
anye saṃvatsaramanye māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokamiti vyākhyātā /
punarāvṛttirapi kṣīṇānuśayānāṃ candramaṇḍalādākāśādikrameṇoktā /
amuṣya lokasyāpūraṇaṃ svaśabdenaivoktam-tenāsau loko na saṃpūryata iti /
children.translated_text: The non-filling of that world has been stated in its own words: 'Therefore that world is not filled up.'

children.text: yasmādevaṃ kaṣṭā saṃsāragatistasmājjugupseta /
children.translated_text: Since the course of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is thus so painful, therefore one should feel revulsion.

children.text: yasmācca janmamaraṇajanitavedanānubhavakṛtakṣaṇāḥ kṣudrajantavo dhvānte ca ghore dustare praveśitāḥ sāgara ivāgādhe 'plave nirāśāścottaraṇaṃ prati tasmāccaivaṃvidhāṃ saṃsāragatiṃ jugupseta bībhatseta ghṛṇī bhavenmā bhūdevaṃvidhe saṃsāramahodadhau ghore pāta iti /
children.translated_text: And since tiny creatures, whose moments are constituted by the experience of suffering born of birth and death, are cast into a terrible, impassable darkness like a fathomless, vessel-less ocean, without any hope of crossing over — therefore one should feel revulsion, one should feel disgust, one should feel aversion toward such a course of <s>saṃsāra</s>: 'May there not be a fall into such a terrible great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>!'

children.text: tadetasminnartha eṣa ślokaḥ pañcāgnividyāstutataye //8 //
children.translated_text: On this subject, this verse is for the praise of the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s> (five-fire doctrine). //8//

[Bhāṣya 5.10.8] But when they neither pursue knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) nor perform sacrificial rites (<s>iṣṭa</s>) and the like, then — of these two paths as described, characterized by light (<s>arcis</s>) and smoke (<s>dhūma</s>) — by neither one do they go. These are the tiny creatures — gnats, mosquitoes, insects, and the like — that are born again and again in endless cycles. Therefore, those who have fallen off both paths are born and die repeatedly — that is the meaning. This describes the pattern of their continuous cycle of birth and death. 'Be born and die' is said to be the activity caused by the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). Their time is spent only in the cycle of birth and death, not in rituals or enjoyments — that is the meaning. This, characterized by tiny creatures, is the third state with reference to the two previously mentioned paths — the state of those in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Since even those who go by the southern path return again, for those who are not qualified, there is no going at all by the southern path — to knowledge or to <s>karma</s>. Therefore that world is not filled up. The fifth question has been explained through the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s> (five-fire doctrine). The first question was resolved by the southern and northern paths. Even after the divergence on the southern and northern paths, the casting of the dead into fire is the same; from there some diverge by the path of light and others by the path of smoke. Again, those reaching the northern and southern solstices for six months unite and diverge again. Some [stay] for a year, others go from months to the world of the fathers — thus it has been explained. The return of those whose residual impressions are exhausted from the lunar sphere has been described through the sequence beginning with space (<s>ākāśa</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.9
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.10.9]

children.text:
steno hiraṇyasya surāṃ pibaṃś ca |
guros talpam āvasan brahmahā ca |
ete patanti catvāraḥ pañcamaś cācaraṃs tair iti || ChUp_5,10.9 ||
children.translated_text: The thief of gold, the drinker of wine, the violator of the teacher's bed, and the slayer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — these four fall, and the fifth is one who associates with them.

children.text: ChUpBh_5,10.9 steno hiraṇyasya brāhmaṇasuvarṇasya hartā /
surāṃ pibanbrāhmaṇaḥ san /
children.translated_text: The drinker of wine — being a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: gurośca talpaṃ dārānāvasan /
children.translated_text: And one who occupies the teacher's bed — that is, his wife.

children.text: brahmahā brāhmaṇasya hantā cetyete patanti catvāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The slayer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — the killer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. These four fall.

children.text: pañcamaśca taiḥ sahā'caranniti //9 //
children.translated_text: And the fifth is one who associates with them. //9//
[Bhāṣya 5.10.9] The thief of gold — one who steals the gold of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,10.10
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.10.10]

children.text:
atha ha ya etān evaṃ pañcāgnīn veda na saha tair apy ācaran pāpmanā lipyate |
śuddhaḥ pūtaḥ puṇyaloko bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_5,10.10 ||
children.translated_text: But he who thus knows these five fires is not tainted by sin even though associating with them. He becomes pure, cleansed, and one of meritorious worlds — he who thus knows, he who thus knows.

children.text: ChUpBh_5,10.10 atha ha punaryo yathoktānpañcāgnīnveda sa tairapyācaranmahāpātakibhiḥ saha na pāpmanā lipyate śuddha eva /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 5.10.10] But he who knows the five fires as described — even associating with those great sinners (<s>mahāpātakin</s>), he is not tainted by sin; he remains pure indeed.

children.text: tena pañcāgnidarśanena pāvito yasmātpūtaḥ puṇyo lokaḥ prājāpatyādiryasya so 'yaṃ puṇyaloko bhavati ya evaṃ veda yathoktaṃ samastaṃ pañcabhiḥ praśnaiḥ pṛṣṭamarthajātaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: By that vision of the five fires he is purified; therefore he is cleansed, and the meritorious world — that of <s>Prajāpati</s> and others — becomes his. He is one of meritorious worlds who thus knows — who knows the entire subject matter asked about through the five questions as described.

children.text: dviruktiḥ samastapraśnanirṇayapradarśanārthā //10//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of 'he who thus knows'] is for the purpose of showing the resolution of all the questions taken together. //10//

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,11.1
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.11.1]

children.text:
prācīnaśāla aupamanyavaḥ satyayajñaḥ pauluṣir indradyumno bhāllaveyo janaḥ śārkarākṣyo buḍila āśvatarāśvis te haite mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ sametya mīmāṃsāṃ cakruḥ |
ko na ātmā kiṃ brahmeti || ChUp_5,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prācīnaśāla Aupamanyava</s>, <s>Satyayajña Pauluṣi</s>, <s>Indradyumna Bhāllavya</s>, <s>Jana Śārkarākṣya</s>, and <s>Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi</s> — these great householders (<s>mahāśāla</s>) and great Vedic scholars (<s>mahāśrotriya</s>), having assembled, conducted a deliberation: 'Who is our self (<s>ātman</s>)? What is <s>Brahman</s>?'

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,11.1 dakṣiṇena pathā gacchatāmannabhāva utkastaddevānāmannaṃ taṃ devā bhakṣayantīti /
kṣudrajantulakṣaṇā ca kaṣṭā saṃsāragatiruktā /
tadubhayadoṣaparijirhīrṣayā vaiśvānarāttṛbhāvapratipattyarthamuttaro grantha ārabhyate /
atsyannaṃ paśyasi priyamityādiliṅgāt /
ākhyāyikā tu sukhāvabodhārthā vidyāsampradānanyāyāpradarśanārthā ca-prācīnaśāla iti nāmata upamanyorapatyamaupamanyavaḥ /
satyayajño nāmataḥ puluṣasyāpatyaṃ pauluṣiḥ /
tathendradyumno nāmato bhallaverapatyaṃ bhāllavistasyāpatyaṃ bhāllaveyaḥ /
jana iti nāmataḥ śarkarākṣasyāpatyaṃ śārkarākṣyaḥ /
buḍilo nāmato 'śvatarāśvasyāpatyamāśvatarāśviḥ /
pañcāpi te haite mahāśālā mahāgṛhasthā vistīrṇābhiḥ śālābhiryuktāḥ sampannā ityarthaḥ /
mahāśrotriyāḥ śrutādhyayanavṛttasampannā ityarthaḥ /
ta evaṃbhūtāḥ santaḥ sametya saṃbhūya kvacinmīmāṃsā vicāraṇāṃ cakruḥ kṛtavanta ityarthaḥ /
katham /
ko no 'smākamātmā kiṃ brahmetyātmabrahmaśabdayoritaretaraviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatvam /
children.translated_text: 'Who is our <s>ātman</s>? What is <s>Brahman</s>?' — Here the words <s>ātman</s> and <s>Brahman</s> mutually qualify each other as qualifier and qualified.

children.text: brahmetyadhyātmaparicchinnamātmānaṃ nivartayatyātmeti cā'tmavyatiriktasyā'dityādibrahmaṇa upāsyatvaṃ nivartayati /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>Brahman</s>' removes the notion of <s>ātman</s> as limited to the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>), and the word '<s>ātman</s>' removes the notion that something other than the self — such as <s>Āditya</s> — is the <s>Brahman</s> to be meditated upon.

children.text: abhedenā'tmaiva brahma brahmaivā'tmetyevaṃ sarvātmā vaiśvānaro brahma sa ātmetyetatsiddhaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Through non-difference, <s>ātman</s> itself is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> itself is <s>ātman</s> — thus it is established that <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the self of all, is <s>Brahman</s>, and that is the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyadandho 'bhaviṣyadityādiliṅgāt //1 //
children.translated_text: This is indicated by signs such as 'your head would have fallen off' and 'you would have become blind.' //1//

[Bhāṣya 5.11.1] It has been stated that those who go by the southern path lack food, and that the gods consume that which is their food. And the painful course of <s>saṃsāra</s> characterized by tiny creatures has been described. With the desire to avoid both these defects and to attain the nature of the eater through <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the subsequent text is begun — as indicated by the sign 'he eats food and sees what is dear.' The narrative is for the purpose of easy understanding and for showing the proper tradition of transmitting knowledge. <s>Prācīnaśāla</s> by name, the descendant of <s>Upamanyu</s>, is <s>Aupamanyava</s>. <s>Satyayajña</s> by name, the son of <s>Puluṣa</s>, is <s>Pauluṣi</s>. Similarly <s>Indradyumna</s> by name, the descendant of <s>Bhallava</s>'s son, is <s>Bhāllavya</s>; his descendant is <s>Bhāllavya</s>. <s>Jana</s> by name, the son of <s>Śarkarākṣa</s>, is <s>Śārkarākṣya</s>. <s>Buḍila</s> by name, the son of <s>Aśvatarāśva</s>, is <s>Āśvatarāśvi</s>. These five were great householders (<s>mahāśāla</s>) — possessing spacious halls, meaning they were prosperous. Great Vedic scholars (<s>mahāśrotriya</s>) — endowed with learning, study, and good conduct, that is the meaning. Being such, having assembled, that is, having come together somewhere, they conducted a deliberation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>), an investigation — that is the meaning. How?

children.text: START ChUp 5,11.2
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.11.2]

children.text:
te ha saṃpādayāṃ cakruḥ |
uddālako vai bhagavanto 'yam āruṇiḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti |
taṃ hantābhyāgacchāmeti |
taṃ hābhyājagmuḥ || ChUp_5,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: They deliberated among themselves: 'This venerable <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> presently knows this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> self. Let us go to him.' They went to him.

children.text: ChUpBh_5,11.2 te ha mīmāṃsanto 'pi niścayamalabhamānāḥ sampādayāñcakruḥ sampāditavantaḥ ātmana upadeṣṭāram /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 5.11.2] They, though deliberating, were unable to reach a conclusion. They arranged, that is, found a teacher of the self.

children.text: uddālako vai prasiddho nāmato bhagavantaḥ pūjāvanto 'yamāruṇiraruṇasyāpatyaṃ samprati samyagimamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaramasmadabhipretamadhyeti /
children.translated_text: 'The well-known, venerable <s>Uddālaka</s> by name, the son of <s>Aruṇa</s>, that is <s>Āruṇi</s>, presently knows well this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> self that we seek.'

children.text: taṃ hantedānīmabhyāgacchāmetyevaṃ niścityaṃ taṃ hābhyājagmurgatavantastamāruṇim //2 //
children.translated_text: 'Let us now go to him.' Having thus resolved, they went to that <s>Āruṇi</s>. //2//

children.text: START ChUp 5,11.3
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.11.3]

children.text:
sa ha saṃpādayāṃ cakāra |
prakṣyanti mām ime mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ |
tebhyo na sarvam iva pratipatsye |
hantāham anyam abhyanuśāsānīti || ChUp_5,11.3 ||
children.translated_text: He deliberated within himself: 'These great householders and great Vedic scholars will question me. I may not be able to answer everything to them. Let me direct them to another teacher.'

children.text: ChUpBh_5,11.3 sa ha tāndṛṣṭvaiva teṣāmāgamanaprayojanaṃ buddhvā sampādayāñcakāra /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 5.11.3] He, upon seeing them, understanding the purpose of their visit, deliberated within himself.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How?

children.text: prakṣyanti māṃ vaiśvānaramime mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāstebhyo 'haṃ na sarvamiva pṛṣṭaṃ pratipatsye vaktuṃ notsahe /
children.translated_text: 'These great householders and great Vedic scholars will ask me about <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. I may not be able to answer everything they ask; I am not confident enough to speak.'

children.text: ato hantāhamidānīmanyameṣāmabhyanuśāsāni vakṣyāmyupadeṣṭāramiti //3 //
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let me now direct them to another — I shall tell them of a teacher.' //3//

children.text: START ChUp 5,11.4
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.11.4]

children.text:
tān hovāca |
aśvapatir vai bhagavanto 'yaṃ kaikeyaḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti |
taṃ hantābhyāgacchāmeti |
taṃ hābhyājagmuḥ || ChUp_5,11.4 ||
children.translated_text: He said to them: 'This venerable <s>Aśvapati Kaikeya</s> presently knows this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> self. Let us go to him.' They went to him.

children.text: ChUpBh_5,11.4 evaṃ sampādya tānhovāca /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 5.11.4] Having thus deliberated, he said to them:

children.text: aśvapatirvai nāmato bhagavanto 'yaṃ kekayasyāpatyaṃ kaikeyaḥ samprati samyagimamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaramadhyetītyādi samānam //4 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Aśvapati</s> by name, the venerable one, the descendant of <s>Kekaya</s>, that is <s>Kaikeya</s>, presently knows well this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> self' — and so on, the rest is the same [as before]. //4//

children.text: START ChUp 5,11.5-7

tebhyo ha prāptebhyaḥ pṛthag arhāṇi kārayāṃ cakāra |
sa ha prātaḥ saṃjihāna uvāca |
na me steno janapade na kadaryo na madyapaḥ |
nānāhitāgnir nāvidvān na svairī svairiṇī kutaḥ |
yakṣyamāṇo vai bhagavanto 'ham asmi |
yāvad ekaikasmā ṛtvije dhanaṃ dāsyāmi tāvad bhagavadbhyo dāsyāmi |
vasantu bhagavanta iti || ChUp_5,11.5 ||
children.translated_text: When they arrived, he had separate honors prepared for each of them. Rising in the morning, he said: 'In my kingdom there is no thief, no miser, no drunkard, no one without a sacred fire, no ignorant person, no adulterer — how then could there be an adulteress? I am about to perform a sacrifice, venerable sirs. I shall give to each of you as much wealth as I give to each <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest). Please stay, venerable sirs.'
[Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 5.11.5-7]

children.text:
te hocuḥ |
yena haivārthena puruṣaś caret taṃ haiva vadet |
ātmānam evemaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ saṃpraty adhyeṣi |
tam eva no brūhīti || ChUp_5,11.6 ||
children.translated_text: They said: 'The purpose for which a person comes, that alone he should speak about. You presently know this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> self. Please tell us about that.'

children.text:
tān hovāca |
prātar vaḥ prativaktāsmīti |
te ha samitpāṇayaḥ pūrvāhṇe praticakramire |
tān hānupanīyaivaitad uvāca || ChUp_5,11.7 ||
children.translated_text: He said to them: 'I shall answer you in the morning.' They approached him in the forenoon with sacrificial fuel (<s>samit</s>) in hand. He, without formally initiating them as students, spoke to them thus.

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,11.5,6,7 tebhyo ha rājā prāptebhyaḥ pṛthakpṛthagarhāṇyarhaṇāni purohitairbhṛtyaiśca kārayāñcakāra kāritavān /
sa hānyedyū rājā prātaḥ sañjihāna uvāca vinayenopagamyaitaddhanaṃ matta upādaddhvamiti /
taiḥ pratyākhyāto mayi doṣaṃ paśyanti nūnaṃ yato na pratigṛhṇanti matto dhanamiti manvāna ātmanaḥ sadvṛttatāṃ pratipipādayiṣannāha /
na me mama janapade stenaḥ parasvahartā vidyate /
na kadaryo 'dātā sati vibhave /
na madyapo dvijottamaḥ san /
nānāhitāgniḥ śataguḥ /
nāvidvānadhikārānurūpam /
na svairī paradāreṣu gantā /
ata eva svairiṇī kuto duṣṭacāriṇī na sambhavatītyarthaḥ /
taiśca na vayaṃ dhanenārdhina ityukta āha-alpaṃ matvaite dhanaṃ na gṛhṇantīti /
yakṣyamāṇo vai katibhirahobhirahaṃ he bhagavanto 'smi /
tadarthaṃ kḷptaṃ dhanaṃ mayā yāvadekaikasmai yathoktamṛtvije dhanaṃ dāsyāmi tāvatpratyekaṃ bhagavadbhyo 'pi dāsyāmi /
vasantu bhagavantaḥ paśyantu ca mama yāgamityuktāste hocuḥ /
yena haivārthena prayojanena yaṃ prati caredgacchetpuruṣastaṃ haivārthaṃ vadet /
idameva prayojanamāgamanasyetyayaṃ nyāyaḥ satām /
vayaṃ vaiśvānarajñānārthinaḥ /
ātmānamevemaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ saṃpratyadhyeṣi samyagjānāsi /
atastameva no 'smabhyaṃ brūhītyuktastānhovāca /
prātarvo yuṣmabhyaṃ prativaktāsmi prativākyaṃ dātāsmītyuktāste ha rājño 'bhiprāyajñāḥ samitpāṇayaḥ samidbhārahastā aparedyuḥ pūrvāhne rājānaṃ praticakramire gatavantaḥ /
yata evaṃ mahāśālā mahāśrotriyā brāhmaṇāḥ santo mahāśālatvādyabhimānaṃ hitvā samidbhārahastā jātito hīnaṃ rājānaṃ vidyārthino vinayenopajagmuḥ /
tathānyairvidyopāditsubhirbhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: Others seeking knowledge should likewise [approach with humility].

children.text: tebhyaścādādvidyāmanupanīyaivopanayanamakṛtvaiva tān /
children.translated_text: And he gave them knowledge without formally initiating them (<s>upanayana</s>) —

children.text: yathā yogyebhyo vidyāmadāttathānyenāpi vidyā dātavyetyākhyāyikārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as he gave knowledge to those who were worthy, so too should knowledge be given by anyone [who possesses it] — this is the meaning of the narrative.

children.text: etadvaiśvānaravijñānamuvāceti vakṣyamāṇena sambandhaḥ //5-7 //
children.translated_text: 'He taught [them] this knowledge of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — the connection is with what will be stated [next]. [End of sections 5-7.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.11.5-7] To them, upon their arrival, the king had various honors (<s>arhāṇi</s>) arranged individually through his priests and servants. The next morning, the king, waking early, said with humility: 'Accept this wealth from me.' When refused by them, thinking 'they surely see a fault in me, since they do not accept wealth from me,' and wishing to demonstrate his own good conduct, he said: 'In my kingdom there is no thief, no stealer of others' property. There is no miser, no non-giver when there is wealth. There is no drunkard among the foremost of the twice-born. There is no one who has not established the sacred fires. No one is unlearned in accordance with his station. There is no adulterer, no one who goes to another's wife. Hence there is certainly no adulteress — meaning no woman of corrupt conduct.' When they said: 'We are not [to be satisfied] with wealth,' he said, thinking 'they consider this wealth too little': 'I am indeed about to perform a sacrifice — [tell me] in how many days, O venerable ones. The wealth has been prepared for that purpose. As much as I will give to each priest as prescribed, that much I will give individually to each of you as well. Please stay, venerable ones, and witness my sacrifice.' They said: 'A man should declare the very purpose for which he travels. This is the principle of the virtuous — the very purpose of our coming. We are seekers of the knowledge of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. You now properly know this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self. Therefore, teach it to us.' Thus addressed, he said: 'I shall answer you in the morning — I shall give you a response.' The next morning, knowing the king's intention, they went to the king with fuel-sticks in hand. Since these great householders and great scholars, being <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, abandoned their pride of wealth and learning and approached the king — who was of lower birth — with humility, carrying fuel-sticks, seeking knowledge —

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,12.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.12.1]

children.text:
aupamanyava kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti |
divam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca |
eṣa vai sutejā ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse |
tasmāt tava sutaṃ prasutam āsutaṃ kule dṛśyate || ChUp_5,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: '"O <s>Aupamanyava</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self?" "Heaven itself, O venerable king," he said. "This is indeed the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [called] <s>Sutejā</s> (of beautiful radiance), whom you meditate upon as the Self. Therefore, in your family are seen the extracted [<s>Soma</s>], the fully pressed, and the well-pressed."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.12.1]

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,12.1 sa kathamuvācetyāha-aupamanyava he kamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ tvamupāḥsa iti papraccha /
nanvayamapanyāyaḥ ācāryaḥ sañśiṣyaṃ pṛcchatīti /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
"yadvettha tena mopasīda tatasta ūrdhvaṃ vakṣyāmī"ti nyāyadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: For we see the principle [stated elsewhere]: 'Whatever you know, approach me with that; beyond that, I shall teach.'

children.text: anyatrāpyācāryasya apratibhānavati śiṣye pratibhotpādanārthaḥ praśno dṛṣṭo 'jātaśatroḥ"kvaiṣa tadābhūtkuta etadāgād" iti /
children.translated_text: Elsewhere too, the teacher's question to a student who lacks insight is seen as being for the purpose of generating insight — as in [the case of] <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'Where was this [self]? From where did it come?'

children.text: divameva dyulokameva vaiśvānaramupāse bhagavo rājanniti hovāca /
children.translated_text: 'Heaven itself — the celestial world — I meditate upon as <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, O venerable king,' he said.

children.text: eṣa vai sutejāḥ śobhanaṃ tejo yasya so 'yaṃ sutejā iti prasiddho vaiśvānara ātmā'tmano 'vayavabhūtatvādyaṃ tvamātmānamātmaikadeśamupāḥse tasmātsutejaso vaiśevānarasyopāsanāttava sutamabhiṣutaṃ somarūpaṃ karmaṇi prasutaṃ prakarṣeṇa ca sutamāsutaṃ cāhargaṇādiṣu tava kule dṛśyate 'tīva karmiṇastvatkulīnā ityarthaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: This indeed is '<s>Sutejā</s>' — he who has beautiful radiance — this well-known <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self. Because [heaven] is a part of the Self, whom you meditate upon as a part of the Self — therefore, from the meditation on <s>Sutejā Vaiśvānara</s>, in your family are seen the extracted <s>Soma</s>, the fully pressed in rituals, the well-pressed in day-long ceremonies — meaning the members of your family are exceedingly devoted to ritual action. [End of section 1.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.12.1] How did he speak? He says: 'O <s>Aupamanyava</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self, as <s>Vaiśvānara</s>?' — thus he asked. [Objection:] Is it not improper that the teacher asks the student? [Reply:] This is not a fault.

children.text: START ChUp 5,12.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.12.2]

children.text:
atsy annaṃ paśyasi priyam |
atty annaṃ paśyati priyam bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ye etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste |
mūdhā tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca |
mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti || ChUp_5,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'You eat food [and] see what is dear. He who meditates upon this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> thus — he eats food, sees what is dear, and there is the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>) in his family. But this is [only] the head of the Self,' he said. 'Your head would have fallen off, had you not come to me.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.12.2]

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,12.2 atsyannaṃ dīptāgniḥ sanpaśyasi ca putrapautrādi priyamiṣṭam /
anyo 'pyattyannaṃ paśyati ca priyaṃ bhavatyasya sutaṃ prasutamāsutamityādikarmitvaṃ;brahmavarcasaṃ kule yaḥ kaścidetaṃ yathoktamevaṃ vaiśvānaramupāste /
mūrdhā tvātmano vaiśvānarasyaiṣa na samasto vaiśvānaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But this is [only] the head of the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — not the complete <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: ataḥ samastabuddhyā vaiśvānarasyopāsanānmūrdhā śiraste viparītagrāhimo vyapatiṣyadvipatitamabhaviṣyat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of meditating upon <s>Vaiśvānara</s> with the mistaken notion [that a part is the whole], your head would have fallen off —

children.text: yadyadi māṃ nā'gamiṣyo nā'gato 'bhaviṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Had you not come to me — had you not arrived.

children.text: sādhvakārṣīryanmāmāgato 'sītyabhiprāyaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: The purport is: 'You did well in coming to me.' [End of section 2.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.12.2] 'You eat food' — being one whose digestive fire is blazing — 'and see what is dear' — sons, grandsons, and so forth. Another [person] too eats food and sees what is dear — and he attains the status of a performer of rituals such as 'the extracted, the fully pressed, and the well-pressed'; [there is also] the splendor of sacred knowledge in the family — [for] whoever meditates upon this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as described.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,13.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.13.1]

children.text:
atha hovāca satyayajñaṃ pauluṣim |
prācīnayogya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti |
ādityam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca |
eṣa vai viśvarūpa ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāste |
tasmāt tava bahu viśvarūpaṃ kule dṛśyate || ChUp_5,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then he said to <s>Satyayajña Pauluṣi</s>: "O <s>Prācīnayogya</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self?" "The sun itself, O venerable king," he said. "This is indeed the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [called] <s>Viśvarūpa</s> (of universal form), whom you meditate upon as the Self. Therefore, in your family are seen many things of universal form."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.13.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,13.1 atha hovāca satyayajñaṃ pauluṣiṃ he prācīnayogya kaṃ tvamātmānamupāsta ityādityameva bhagavo rājanniti hovāca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.13.1] Then he said to <s>Satyayajña Pauluṣi</s>: 'O <s>Prācīnayogya</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self?' and so forth. 'The sun itself, O venerable king,' he said.

children.text: śuklanīlādirūpatvādviśvarūpatvamādityasya sarvarūpatvādvā /
children.translated_text: The 'universal form' (<s>viśvarūpa</s>) of the sun [is so called] because it has forms [such as] white, blue, and so forth — or because it possesses all forms.

children.text: sarvāṇi rūpāṇi hi tvāṣṭrāṇi yato 'to vā viśvarūpa ādityastadupāsanāttava bahu viśvarūpamihāmutrārthamupakaraṇaṃ dṛśyate kule //1 //
children.translated_text: For all forms are [produced by] <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>; therefore the sun is 'of universal form.' From the meditation on [the sun as] 'of universal form,' in your family are seen many things of universal form — provisions useful both here and hereafter. [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 5,13.2

pravṛtto 'śvatarīratho dāsī niṣkaḥ |
atsy annaṃ paśyasi priyam |
atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste |
cakṣuṣ ṭv etad ātmana iti hovāca |
andho 'bhaviṣyo yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti || ChUp_5,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'A chariot drawn by mules goes [before you], a maidservant [wearing] a gold necklace. You eat food [and] see what is dear. He who meditates upon this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> thus — he eats food, sees what is dear, and there is the splendor of sacred knowledge in his family. But this is [only] the eye of the Self,' he said. 'You would have become blind, had you not come to me.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.13.2]
[Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.13.2]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,13.2 kiñca tvāmanu pravṛtto 'śvatarībhyāṃ yukto ratho 'śvatarīratho dāsīniṣko dāsībhiryukto niṣko hāro dāsīniṣkaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.13.2] Furthermore, following you there is a chariot yoked with mules — a mule-chariot — and a maidservant with a gold necklace (<s>niṣka</s>) — meaning maidservants wearing necklaces.

children.text: atsyannamityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: 'You eat food' and so forth — the same [as before].

children.text: cakṣurvaiśvānarasya tu savitā /
children.translated_text: The eye of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is indeed the sun (<s>Savitṛ</s>).

children.text: tasya samastabuddhyopāsanādandho 'bhaviṣyaścakṣurhīno 'bhavi ṣyo yanmāṃ nā'gamiṣya iti pūrvavat //2//
children.translated_text: Because of meditating upon that [part alone] with the mistaken notion [that it is the whole], you would have become blind — deprived of sight — had you not come to me — as before. [End of section 2.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya trayodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,14.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.14.1]

children.text:
atha hovācendradyumnaṃ bhāllaveyam |
vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti |
vāyum eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca |
eṣa vai pṛthagvartmātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse |
tasmāt tvāṃ pṛthag balaya āyanti pṛthag rathaśreṇayo 'nuyanti || ChUp_5,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then he said to <s>Indradyumna Bhāllavya</s>: "O <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self?" "The wind itself, O venerable king," he said. "This is indeed the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [called] <s>Pṛthagvartman</s> (of diverse paths), whom you meditate upon as the Self. Therefore, offerings come to you from diverse [directions], and rows of chariots follow you from diverse [directions]."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.14.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,14.1 atha hovācendradyumnaṃ bhāllaveyaṃ vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvamātmānamupāḥsa ityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.14.1] Then he said to <s>Indradyumna Bhāllavya</s>: 'O <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self?' and so forth — the same [explanation as before].

children.text: pṛthagvartmā nānā vartmāni yasya vāyorāvahodvahādibhirbhedairvartamānasya so 'yaṃ pṛthagvartmā vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of diverse paths' (<s>Pṛthagvartman</s>) — the wind, which operates through diverse paths such as inhalation, exhalation, and the like — is [called] '<s>Pṛthagvartman</s>.'

children.text: tasmātpṛthagvartmātmano vaiśvānarasyopāsanātpṛthaṅnānādikkāstvāṃ balayo vasrānnādilakṣaṇā balaya āyantyāgacchanti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the meditation on [the wind as] 'of diverse paths' — a part of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>'s Self — offerings characterized as garments, food, and the like come to you from diverse directions.

children.text: pṛthagrathaśreṇayo rathapaṅktayo 'pi tvāmanuyanti //1 //
children.translated_text: And rows of chariots also follow you from diverse [directions]. [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 5,14.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.14.2]

children.text:
atsy annaṃ paśyasi priyam |
atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste |
prāṇas tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca |
prāṇas ta udakramiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti || ChUp_5,14.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'You eat food [and] see what is dear. He who meditates upon this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> thus — he eats food, sees what is dear, and there is the splendor of sacred knowledge in his family. But this is [only] the <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) of the Self,' he said. 'Your <s>Prāṇa</s> would have departed, had you not come to me.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.14.2]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,14.2 atsyannamityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.14.2] 'You eat food' and so forth — the same [as before].

children.text: praṇastveṣa ātmana iti hovāca prāṇaste tavodakramiṣyadutkrānto 'bhaviṣyadyanmāṃ nā'gamiṣya iti //2//
children.translated_text: 'But this is [only] the <s>Prāṇa</s> of the Self,' he said. 'Your <s>Prāṇa</s> would have departed — would have left — had you not come to me' — as before. [End of section 2.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya caturdaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,15.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.15.1]

children.text:
atha hovāca janaṃ śārkarākṣyam |
śārkarākṣya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti |
ākāśam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca |
eṣa vai bahula ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upasse |
tasmāt tvaṃ bahulo 'si prajayā ca dhanena ca || ChUp_5,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then he said to <s>Jana Śārkarākṣya</s>: "O <s>Śārkarākṣya</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self?" "Space (<s>Ākāśa</s>) itself, O venerable king," he said. "This is indeed the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [called] <s>Bahula</s> (the abundant), whom you meditate upon as the Self. Therefore, you are abundant in offspring and wealth."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.15.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,15.1 atha hovāca janamityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.15.1] Then he said to <s>Jana</s> — and so forth — the same [as before].

children.text: eṣa vai bahula ātmā vaiśvānaraḥ /
children.translated_text: This indeed is '<s>Bahula</s>' — the abundant Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: bahulatvamākāśasya sarvagatatvāt /
children.translated_text: The 'abundance' of space is due to its all-pervading nature.

children.text: bahulaguṇopāsanācca tvaṃ bahulo 'si prajayā ca putrapautrādilakṣaṇayā dhanena ca hiraṇyādinā //1 //
children.translated_text: And from the meditation on [<s>Vaiśvānara</s> as having] the quality of abundance — you are abundant in offspring — characterized as sons, grandsons, and the like — and in wealth — characterized as gold and the like. [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 5,15.2

atsy annaṃ paśyasi priyam |
atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste |
saṃdehas tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca |
saṃdehas te vyaśīryad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti || ChUp_5,15.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'You eat food [and] see what is dear. He who meditates upon this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> thus — he eats food, sees what is dear, and there is the splendor of sacred knowledge in his family. But this is [only] the trunk (<s>saṃdeha</s>) of the Self,' he said. 'Your trunk would have burst apart, had you not come to me.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.15.2]
[Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.15.2]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,15.2 sandehastveṣa sandeho madhyamaṃ śarīraṃ vaiśvānarasya /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.15.2] 'But this is [only] the trunk (<s>saṃdeha</s>)' — the trunk, the middle part of the body, of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: diherupacayārthatvānmāṃsarudhirāsthyādibhiśca bahulaṃ śarīraṃ tatsandehaste tava śarīraṃ vyaśīryacchīrṇamabhaviṣyadyanmāṃ nā'gamiṣya iti //2//
children.translated_text: Because 'deha' (body) has the sense of accumulation — and because the body is thick with flesh, blood, bones, and the like — that trunk, your body, would have burst apart — would have been shattered — had you not come to me. [End of section 2.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya pañcadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,16.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.16.1]

children.text:
atha hovāca buḍilam āśvatarāśvim |
vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti |
apa eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca |
eṣa vai rayir ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse |
tasmāt tvaṃ rayimān puṣṭimān asi || ChUp_5,16.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then he said to <s>Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi</s>: "O <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, whom do you meditate upon as the Self?" "Water itself, O venerable king," he said. "This is indeed the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [called] <s>Rayi</s> (wealth), whom you meditate upon as the Self. Therefore, you are wealthy and prosperous."' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.16.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,16.1 atha hovāca buḍilamāśvatarāśvimityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.16.1] Then he said to <s>Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi</s> — and so forth — the same [as before].

children.text: eṣa vai rayirātmā vaiśvānaro dhanarūpaḥ /
children.translated_text: This indeed is '<s>Rayi</s>' — the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in the form of wealth.

children.text: adbhyo 'nnaṃ tato dhanamiti /
children.translated_text: From water [comes] food, and from that, wealth.

children.text: tasmādrayimāndhanavāṃstvaṃ puṣṭimāṃśca śarīreṇa;puṣṭeścānnanimittatvāt //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, you are wealthy — possessing wealth — and prosperous in body; and prosperity too is caused by food. [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 5,16.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.16.2]

children.text:
atsy annaṃ paśyasi priyam |
atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste |
bastis tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca |
bastis te vyabhetsyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti || ChUp_5,16.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'You eat food [and] see what is dear. He who meditates upon this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> thus — he eats food, sees what is dear, and there is the splendor of sacred knowledge in his family. But this is [only] the bladder (<s>basti</s>) of the Self,' he said. 'Your bladder would have burst, had you not come to me.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.16.2]

children.text: ChUpBh_5,16.2 bastistveṣa ātmano vaiśvānarasya bastirmūtrasaṃgrahasthānaṃ bastirmūtrasaṃgrahasthānaṃ bastiste vyabhetsyadbhinno 'bhaviṣyadyanmāṃ nā'gamiṣya iti //2//
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 5.16.2] 'But this is [only] the bladder (<s>basti</s>)' — the bladder, the receptacle for urine, of the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. 'Your bladder would have burst — would have been split — had you not come to me.' [End of section 2.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya ṣoḍaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,17.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.17.1-2]

children.text:
atha hovācoddālakam āruṇim |
gautama kaṃ tvam ātmānam upassa iti |
pṛthivīm eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca |
eṣa vai pratiṣṭhātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse |
tasmāt tvaṃ pratiṣṭhito 'si prajayā ca paśubhiś ca || ChUp_5,17.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then he said to <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>: '<s>Gautama</s>, what do you meditate on as the Self?' 'The earth alone, Blessed King,' he replied. 'This is indeed the Self called <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) that you meditate upon. Therefore you are well-established with offspring and cattle.' (ChUp 5.17.1)

children.text:
atsy annaṃ paśyasi priyam |
atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste |
pādau tv etāv ātmana iti hovāca |
pādau te vyamlāsyetāṃ yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti || ChUp_5,17.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'You eat food and see what is dear. He who thus meditates on this Self as <s>Vaiśvānara</s> eats food, sees what is dear, and there is <s>brahmavarcas</s> (the splendor of sacred knowledge) in his family. But these are merely the feet of the Self,' he said. 'Your feet would have withered if you had not come to me.' (ChUp 5.17.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,17.1,2 atha hovācoddālakamityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.17.1-2:] 'Then he said to <s>Uddālaka</s>' and so forth — the same [pattern as before].

children.text: pṛthivīmeva bhagavo rājanniti hovāca /
children.translated_text: 'The earth alone, Blessed King,' he replied.

children.text: eṣa vai pratiṣṭhā pādau vaiśvānarasya /
children.translated_text: This is indeed the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) — the feet of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: pādau te vyamlāsyetāṃ vimlānāvabhaviṣyatāṃ ślathībhūtau yanmāṃ nā'gamiṣya iti //1-2 //
children.translated_text: 'Your feet would have withered' — would have become withered, weakened — 'if you had not come to me.' (1-2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya saptadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
tān hovāca |
ete vai khalu yūyaṃ pṛthag ivemam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vidvāṃso 'nnam attha |
yas tv etam evaṃ prādeśamātram abhivimānam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste |
sa sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmasv annam atti || ChUp_5,18.1 ||
children.translated_text: He said to them: 'You indeed eat food knowing this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as if separately. But he who meditates on this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as a span in measure and as the object of the notion "I" — he eats food in all worlds, in all beings, in all selves.' (ChUp 5.18.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,18.1 tānyathoktavaiśvānaradarśanavato hovāca /
ete yūyaṃ vai khalvityanarthakau /
yūyaṃ pṛthagivāpṛthaksantamimamekaṃ vaiśvānaramātmānaṃ vidvāṃso 'nnamattha paricchinnātmabuddhyetyetaddhastidarśana iva jātyandhāḥ /
yastvetamevaṃ yathoktāvayavairdyumūrdhādibhiḥ pṛthivīpādāntairviśiṣṭamekaṃ prādeśamātraṃ prādeśairdyumūrdhādibhiḥ pṛthivīpādāntairadhyātmaṃ mīyate jñāyata iti prādeśamātrām /
mukhādiṣu vā karaṇeṣvattṛtvena mīyata iti prādeśamātraḥ /
dyulokādipṛthivyantapradeśaparimāṇo vā prādeśamātraḥ /
prakarṣeṇa śāsreṇā'diśyanta iti prādeśā dyulokādaya etāvatparimāṇaḥ /
śākhāntare tu mūrdhādiḥ cibukapratiṣṭha iti prādeśamātraṃ kalpayanti /
iha tu na tathābhipretaḥ /
tasya ha vā etasyā'tmana ityādyupasaṃhārāt /
children.translated_text: because of the concluding statement 'Of this Self indeed' and so forth.

children.text: pratyagātmatayābhivimīyate 'hamiti jñāyata ityabhivimānastametamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ viśvānnarānnayati puṇyapāpānurūpāṃ gatiṃ sarvātmaiṣa īśvaro vaiśvānaro viśvo nara eva vā sarvātmatvāt /
children.translated_text: He is called <s>abhivimāna</s> (the object of the notion 'I') because he is identified as the inner Self — 'I' — this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> who leads all beings (<s>viśvān narān nayati</s>) to their respective destinations according to their merit and demerit, being the Self of all, this Lord is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; or he is indeed all beings (<s>viśvo nara</s>) because of being the Self of all.

children.text: viśvairvā naraiḥ pratyagātmatayā pravibhajya nīyata iti vaiśvānarastamevamupāste yaḥ so 'dannannādī sarveṣu lokeṣu dyulokādiṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu carācareṣu sarveṣvātmasu śarīrendriyamanobuddhiṣu teṣu hyātmakalpanāvyapadeśaḥ prāṇināmannamatti vaiśvānaravitsarvātmā sannannamatti /
children.translated_text: Or, he is called <s>Vaiśvānara</s> because he is apportioned by all beings as their inner Self — he who meditates on him thus, being one who eats food in all worlds such as heaven and the rest, in all beings both moving and stationary, in all selves — namely in body, senses, mind, and intellect, for the designation of 'self' is applied to these by living beings — eats food; the knower of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, being the Self of all, eats food.

children.text: na yathājñaḥ piṇḍamātrābhimānaḥ sannityarthaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Not as the ignorant person does, who identifies with a mere lump [of body] — that is the meaning. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.18.1:] He said to those who had the vision of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as described. 'You indeed' — <s>vai</s> and <s>khalu</s> are meaningless particles. 'You, knowing this one, undivided Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as if separately, eat food' — with the notion of a limited self — like those blind from birth [perceiving] an elephant. But he who [meditates on] this one — qualified by the parts described, from heaven as the head to earth as the feet — as 'a span in measure' (<s>prādeśamātra</s>) — measured by the spans (<s>prādeśa</s>) from heaven-as-head to earth-as-feet in the individual self. Or, measured as the eater in the sense organs such as the mouth and the rest, hence 'a span in measure.' Or, 'a span in measure' means having the extent of the region from heaven to earth. Or, those [regions] from heaven onward are called <s>prādeśas</s> because they are designated (<s>ādiśyante</s>) par excellence by scripture — [and <s>Vaiśvānara</s>] has that extent. In another recension, they construe 'a span in measure' as [the distance] from the head to the chin. But that is not the intended meaning here,

children.text: START ChUp 5,18.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.18.2]

children.text: tasya ha vā etasyātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāś cakṣur viśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmātmā saṃdeho bahulo bastir eva rayiḥ pṛthivy eva pādāv ura eva vedir lomāṇi barhir hṛdayaṃ gārhapatyo mano 'nvāhāryapacana āsyam āhavanīyaḥ || ChUp_5,18.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the head alone is <s>Sutejās</s> (the brilliant one), the eye is <s>Viśvarūpa</s> (the universal form), the breath is <s>Pṛthagvartman</s> (the one of diverse paths), the trunk is <s>Bahula</s> (the full one), the bladder is <s>Rayi</s> (wealth), the earth alone is the feet, the chest is the altar, the hairs are the sacred grass, the heart is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, the mind is the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire, the mouth is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.' (ChUp 5.18.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_5,18.2 kasmādevam /
yasmāttasya ha vai prakṛtasyaivaitasyā'tmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāścakṣurviśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmā'tmā sandeho bahulo bastireva rayiḥ pṛthivyeva pādau /
athavā vidhyarthametadvacanamevamupāsya iti /
athedānīṃ vaiśvānaravido bhojane 'gnihotraṃ saṃpipādayiṣannāha-etasya vaiśvānarasya bhokturura eva vedirākārasāmāvanyāt /
children.translated_text: Now, wishing to establish the <s>agnihotra</s> in connection with the eating of the knower of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, he says — of this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> who is the eater, the chest is like the altar, because of similarity in shape.

children.text: lomāni barhirvedyāmivorasi lomānyāstīrṇāni (na) dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: The hairs are the sacred grass — just as on the altar, so on the chest the hairs appear to be spread out.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ gārhapatyo hṛdayāddhi manaḥ praṇītamivānantarī bhavatyato 'nvāhāryapacano 'gnirmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The heart is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire; from the heart indeed the mind is produced, as if brought forth — being immediately next, therefore the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire is the mind.

children.text: āsyaṃ mukhamāhavanīya ivā'havanīyo hūyate 'sminnannamiti //2//
children.translated_text: The mouth is like the <s>Āhavanīya</s> — [just as] in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [oblations] are offered, so food is offered into this [mouth]. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.18.2:] Why so? Because of this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> under discussion — the head alone is <s>Sutejās</s>, the eye is <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, the breath is <s>Pṛthagvartman</s>, the trunk (<s>ātmā sandeha</s>) is <s>Bahula</s>, the bladder is <s>Rayi</s>, the earth alone is the feet. Or, this statement is for the purpose of injunction — 'one should meditate thus.'

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasyāṣṭādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,19.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.19.1]

children.text:
tad yad bhaktaṃ prathamam āgacchet tad dhomīyam |
sa yāṃ prathamām āhutiṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt prāṇāya svāheti |
prāṇas tṛpyati || ChUp_5,19.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The food that comes first should be offered as an oblation. The first oblation that one offers, one should offer with [the words] "To <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>." <s>Prāṇa</s> is satisfied.' (ChUp 5.19.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,19.1 tattatraivaṃ sati yadbhaktaṃ bhojanakāla āgacchedbhojanārthaṃ taddhotavyam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.19.1:] In that case — when this is so — the food that comes at mealtime should be offered as an oblation.

children.text: agnihotrasampanmātrasya vivakṣitatvānnāgnihotrāṅgetikartavyatāprāptiriha /
children.translated_text: Since only the resemblance to <s>agnihotra</s> is intended here, there is no obligation regarding the subsidiary details of the [actual] <s>agnihotra</s>.

children.text: sa bhoktā yāṃ prathamāmāhutiṃ juhuyāttāṃ kathaṃ juhutādityāha-prāṇāya svāhetyanena mantreṇā'hutiśabdādavadānapramāṇamannaṃ prakṣipedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The eater — the first oblation that he would offer, how should he offer it? He says — with the mantra 'To <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>' — the meaning is that food of the measure of a mouthful, as indicated by the word 'oblation,' should be placed [in the mouth].

children.text: tena prāṇastṛpyati //1 //
children.translated_text: By that, <s>Prāṇa</s> is satisfied. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 5,19.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.19.2]

children.text:
prāṇe tṛpyati cakṣus tṛpyati |
cakṣuṣi tṛpyaty ādityas tṛpyati |
āditye tṛpyati dyaus tṛpyati |
divi tṛpyantyāṃ yat kiṃca dyauś cādityaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati |
tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti || ChUp_5,19.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Prāṇa</s> is satisfied, the eye is satisfied. When the eye is satisfied, the sun is satisfied. When the sun is satisfied, heaven is satisfied. When heaven is satisfied, whatever heaven and the sun preside over is satisfied. Following that satisfaction, he [the sacrificer] is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food, radiance, and <s>brahmavarcas</s> (splendor of sacred knowledge).' (ChUp 5.19.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,19.2 prāṇe tṛpyati cakṣurādityo dyauścetyādi tṛpyati yaccānyaddyauścā'dityaśca svāmitvenādhitiṣṭhatastacca tṛpyati tasya tṛptimanu svayaṃ bhuñjānastṛpyatyevaṃ pratyakṣam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.19.2:] When <s>Prāṇa</s> is satisfied, the eye, the sun, and heaven — and so forth — are satisfied. And whatever else heaven and the sun preside over as lords is also satisfied. Following that satisfaction, he himself, while eating, is satisfied — this is directly experienced.

children.text: kiṃ ca prajādibhiśca /
children.translated_text: Moreover, [he is satisfied] with offspring and the rest.

children.text: tejaḥ śarīrasthā dīptirujjvalatvaṃ prāgalbhyaṃ vā, brahmavarcasaṃ vṛttasvādhyāyanimittaṃ tejaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: <s>Tejas</s> (radiance) is the brightness residing in the body, brilliance, or boldness; <s>brahmavarcas</s> is the splendor arising from good conduct and self-study. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasyaikonaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,20.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.20.1]

children.text:
atha yāṃ dvitīyāṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyād vyānāya svāheti |
vyānas tṛpyati || ChUp_5,20.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The second oblation that one offers, one should offer with [the words] "To <s>Vyāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>." <s>Vyāna</s> is satisfied.' (ChUp 5.20.1)

children.text:
vyāne tṛpyati śrotraṃ tṛpyati |
śrotre tṛpyati candramās tṛpyati |
candramasi tṛpyati diśas tṛpyanti |
dikṣu tṛpyantīṣu yat kiṃca diśaś candramāś cādhitiṣṭhanti tat tṛpyati |
tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti || ChUp_5,20.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Vyāna</s> is satisfied, the ear is satisfied. When the ear is satisfied, the moon is satisfied. When the moon is satisfied, the quarters are satisfied. When the quarters are satisfied, whatever the quarters and the moon preside over is satisfied. Following that satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food, radiance, and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.' (ChUp 5.20.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,20.1,2 atha yāṃ dvitīyāṃ caturthīṃ pañcamīmiti samānam //1-2 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.20.1-2:] 'The second,' 'the fourth,' 'the fifth' — the same [pattern applies throughout]. (1-2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya viṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,21.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.21.1-2]

children.text:
atha yāṃ tṛtīyāṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyād apānāya svāheti |
apānas tṛpyati || ChUp_5,21.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The third oblation that one offers, one should offer with [the words] "To <s>Apāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>." <s>Apāna</s> is satisfied.' (ChUp 5.21.1)

children.text:
apāne tṛpyati vāk tṛpyati |
vāci tṛpyantyām agnis tṛpyati |
agnau tṛpyati pṛthivī tṛpyati |
pṛthivyāṃ tṛpyantyāṃ yat kiṃ ca pṛthivī cāgniś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati |
tasyānutṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti || ChUp_5,21.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Apāna</s> is satisfied, speech is satisfied. When speech is satisfied, fire is satisfied. When fire is satisfied, the earth is satisfied. When the earth is satisfied, whatever the earth and fire preside over is satisfied. Following that satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food, radiance, and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.' (ChUp 5.21.2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasyaikaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,22.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.22.1-2]

children.text:
atha yāṃ caturthīṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt samānāya svāheti |
samānas tṛpyati || ChUp_5,22.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The fourth oblation that one offers, one should offer with [the words] "To <s>Samāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>." <s>Samāna</s> is satisfied.' (ChUp 5.22.1)

children.text:
samāne tṛpyati manas tṛpyati |
manasi tṛpyati parjanyas tṛpyati |
parjanye tṛpyati vidyut tṛpyati |
vidyuti tṛpyantyāṃ yat kiṃ ca vidyuc ca parjanyaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati |
tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti || ChUp_5,22.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Samāna</s> is satisfied, the mind is satisfied. When the mind is satisfied, <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) is satisfied. When <s>Parjanya</s> is satisfied, lightning is satisfied. When lightning is satisfied, whatever lightning and <s>Parjanya</s> preside over is satisfied. Following that satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food, radiance, and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.' (ChUp 5.22.2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya dvāviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-second section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,23.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.23.1-2]

children.text:
atha yām pañcamīṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt udānāya svāheti |
udānas tṛpyati || ChUp_5,23.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The fifth oblation that one offers, one should offer with [the words] "To <s>Udāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>." <s>Udāna</s> is satisfied.' (ChUp 5.23.1)

children.text:
udāne tṛpyati tvak tṛpyati tvaci tṛpyantyāṃ vāyus tṛpyati |
vāyau tṛpyaty ākāśas tṛpyati |
ākāśe tṛpyati yat kiṃca vāyuś cākāśaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati |
tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti || ChUp_5,23.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Udāna</s> is satisfied, the skin is satisfied. When the skin is satisfied, the wind is satisfied. When the wind is satisfied, space is satisfied. When space is satisfied, whatever the wind and space preside over is satisfied. Following that satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food, radiance, and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.' (ChUp 5.23.2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya trayoviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 5,24.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.24.1]

children.text: sa ya idam avidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti yathāṅgārān apohya bhasmani juhuyāt tādṛk tat syāt || ChUp_5,24.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who, not knowing this, offers the <s>agnihotra</s> — it would be as if, having pushed aside the embers, he were to offer into ashes.' (ChUp 5.24.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,24.1 sa yaḥ kaścididaṃ vaiśvānaradarśanaṃ yathoktamavidvānsannagnihotraṃ prasiddhaṃ juhoti yathāṅgārānāhutiyogyānapohyānāhutisthāne bhasmani juhuyāttādṛktattulyaṃ tasya tadagnihotrahavanaṃ syādvaiśvānaravido 'gnihotramapekṣyeti prasiddhāgnihotranindayā vaiśvānaravido 'gnihotraṃ stūyate //1 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.24.1:] He who, being anyone whosoever, not knowing this vision of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as described, offers the well-known <s>agnihotra</s> — it would be as if, having pushed aside the embers which are fit for the oblation, he were to offer into ashes which are unfit for the oblation; his offering of the <s>agnihotra</s> would be equivalent to that — in comparison to the <s>agnihotra</s> of the knower of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. Thus, through the censure of the well-known <s>agnihotra</s>, the <s>agnihotra</s> of the knower of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is praised. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 5,24.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.24.2]

children.text: atha ya etad evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmasu hutaṃ bhavati || ChUp_5,24.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'But he who, knowing this thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s> — his offering is made in all worlds, in all beings, in all selves.' (ChUp 5.24.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,24.2 ataścaitadviśiṣṭamagnihotram /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.24.2:] Therefore this <s>agnihotra</s> is superior.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How?

children.text: atha ya etadevaṃ vidvānagnihotraṃ juhoti tasya yathoktavaiśvānaravijñānavataḥ sarveṣu lokeṣvityādyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: He who, knowing this thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s> — for that knower of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as described, 'in all worlds' and so forth — the meaning has been stated.

children.text: hutamannamattītyanayorekārthatvāt //2 //
children.translated_text: 'The offering is made' and 'he eats food' — these two have the same meaning. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 5,24.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.24.3]

children.text: tad yatheṣīkātūlam agnau protaṃ pradūyetaivaṃ hāsya sarve pāpmānaḥ pradūyante ya etad evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti || ChUp_5,24.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as the soft tip of a reed, when thrown into fire, would be burnt up — so all his sins are burnt up, for him who, knowing this thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s>.' (ChUp 5.24.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,24.3 kiñca tadyatheṣīkāyāstūlamagramagnau protaṃ prakṣiptaṃ pradūyeta pradahyeta kṣipramevaṃ hāsya viduṣaḥ sarvātmabhūtasya sarvānnānāmattuḥ sarve niravaśiṣṭāḥ pāpmāno dharmādharmākhyā anekajanmasañcitā iha ca prāgjñānotpatterjñānasahabhāvinaśca pradūyante pradahyeranvartamānaśarīrārambhakapāpmavarjaṃ, lakṣyaṃ prati mukteṣuvatpravṛttaphalatvāttasya na dāhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 5.24.3:] Moreover — just as the soft tip of a reed, when thrown (<s>prota</s>) into fire, would be burnt up quickly — so too, for this knower who has become the Self of all and who eats all foods, all sins without remainder — called <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, accumulated over many births as well as those co-arising with knowledge before the rise of knowledge in this life — are burnt up; except for the sin that initiated the present body, which is like an arrow already released toward its target — that cannot be burnt, because its fruit has already commenced.

children.text: ya etadevaṃ vidvānagnihotraṃ juhoti bhuṅkte //3 //
children.translated_text: He who, knowing this thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s> — [or rather,] eats. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 5,24.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.24.4]

children.text:
tasmād u haivaṃvid yady api caṇḍālāya ucchiṣṭaṃ prayacchet |
ātmani haivāsya tad vaiśvānare hutaṃ syād iti |
tad eṣa ślokaḥ || ChUp_5,24.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, one who knows thus — even if he were to give his leftover food (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) to a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> — it would be offered into his own self, the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [fire].' Here is a verse on this: (ChUp 5.24.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,24.4 sa yadyapi caṇḍālāyocchiṣṭānarhāyocchiṣṭaṃ prayaccheducchiṣṭaṃ dadyātpratiṣiddhamucchiṣṭadānaṃ yadyapi kuryādātmani haivāsya caṇḍālahehasthe vaiśvānare taddhutaṃ syānnādharmanimittamiti vidyāmeva stauti /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 5.24.4:] He — even if he were to give his leftover food to a Caṇḍāla, who is unworthy of receiving leftover food — even if he were to do this prohibited act of giving leftover food — it would be [as if] offered into his own self, the Vaiśvānara, residing even in the Caṇḍāla — it would not be a cause of demerit. Thus [the text] praises the knowledge alone.

children.text: tadetasminstutyarthe śloko mantro 'pyeṣa bhavati //4 //
children.translated_text: On this subject of praise, there is also a mantra-verse: (4)

children.text: START ChUp 5,24.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 5.24.5]

children.text:
yatheha kṣudhitā bālā mātaraṃ paryupāsate |
evaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny agnihotram upāsata || ChUp_5,24.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as here [in this world] hungry children gather around their mother, so all beings gather around the Agnihotra [of one who knows thus].' (ChUp 5.24.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_5,24.5 yatheha loke kṣudhitā bubhukṣitā bālā mātaraṃ paryupāsate kadā no mātānnaṃ prayacchatītyevaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyannādānyevaṃvido 'gnihotraṃ bhojanamupāsate kadā tvasau bhokṣyata iti, jagatsarvaṃ vidvadbhojanena tṛptaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
dviruktiradhyāyaparisamāptyarthā //5 // //
children.translated_text: The twofold repetition [of 'ya evaṃ veda'] is for the purpose of concluding the chapter. (5)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 5.24.5:] Just as in this world, hungry — famished — children gather around their mother [thinking] 'When will our mother give us food?' — so all beings that eat food gather around the Agnihotra — the meal — of one who knows thus, [thinking] 'When will he eat?' The entire world becomes satisfied by the eating of the knower — this is the meaning.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi pañcamādhyāyasya caturviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth section of the fifth chapter of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadbrāhmaṇe pañcamodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa.

children.text: atha ṣaṣṭhodhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the sixth chapter.

children.text: START ChUp 6,1.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.1.1]

children.text:
śvetaketur hāruṇeya āsa |
taṃ ha pitovāca śvetaketo vasa brahmacaryam |
na vai somyāsmat kulīno 'nanūcya brahmabandhur iva bhavatīti || ChUp_6,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Śvetaketu</s>, the grandson of <s>Āruṇa</s>, lived [as a student]. His father said to him: "<s>Śvetaketu</s>, live the life of a <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student). For, dear boy, no one from our family remains unlearned, a mere nominal <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>brahmabandhu</s>)."' (ChUp 6.1.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,1.1
śvetaketurhā'ruṇeya āsetyādyadhyāyasambandhaḥ /
sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalānityuktaṃ kathaṃ tasmājjagadidaṃ jāyate tasminneva ca līyate 'niti ca tenaivetyetadvaktavyam /
anantaraṃ caikasminbhukte viduṣi sarvaṃ jagattṛptaṃ bhavatītyuktaṃ tadekatve satyātmanaḥ sarvabhūtasthasyopapadyate nā'tmabhede /
kathaṃ ca tadekatvamiti tadartho 'yaṃ ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāya ārabhyate /
pitāputrākhyāyikā vidyāyāḥ sāriṣṭhatvapradarśanārthā /
children.translated_text: The story of father and son is for the purpose of demonstrating the greatness of the knowledge.

children.text: śvetaketuriti nāmato hetyaitihyārthaḥ āruṇeyo 'ruṇasya pautra āsa babhūva /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śvetaketu</s>' is a [proper] name; 'ha' indicates tradition (aitihya). '<s>Āruṇeya</s>' means the grandson of <s>Āruṇa</s> — he lived, existed.

children.text: taṃ putraṃ hā'ruṇiḥ pitā yogyaṃ vidyābhājanaṃ manvānastasyopanayanakālātyayaṃ ca paśyannuvāca he śvetaketo 'nurūpaṃ guruṃ kulasya no gatvā vasa brahmacaryam /
children.translated_text: His father, <s>Āruṇi</s> — considering his son worthy and a fit vessel for knowledge, and seeing that the time for his investiture (<s>upanayana</s>) was passing — said: 'O <s>Śvetaketu</s>, go to a teacher befitting our family and live the life of a <s>brahmacārī</s>.'

children.text: na caitadyuktaṃ yadasmatkulīno he somyānanūcyānadhītya brahmabandhuriva bhavatīti brāhmaṇānbandhūnvyapadiśati na svayaṃ brāhmaṇavṛtta iti //1 //
children.translated_text: 'It is not proper that one of our family, dear boy, should remain unlearned — without having studied — and become a mere <s>brahmabandhu</s>' — [meaning] one who merely claims <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s as his relatives but does not himself follow the conduct of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (1)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.1.1:] '<s>Śvetaketu</s>, the grandson of <s>Āruṇa</s>, lived' — and so forth — this is the connection with the [new] chapter. It has been stated that 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>; <s>tajjalān</s>' — [meaning] how from That this world is born, into That it dissolves, and by That it is sustained — this needs to be explained. And next, it has been stated that when one knower eats, the entire world becomes satisfied — this is possible only when there is oneness of the Self which abides in all beings, not when the Self is many. How is that oneness [established]? For this purpose, this sixth chapter commences.

children.text: START ChUp 6,1.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.1.2]

children.text:
sa ha dvādaśavarṣa upetya caturviṃśativarṣaḥ sarvān vedān adhītya mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdha eyāya |
taṃ ha pitovāca || ChUp_6,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He went [to a teacher] at twelve years of age. Having studied all the <s>Vedas</s> until twenty-four, he returned — conceited, considering himself learned, and arrogant. His father said to him:' (ChUp 6.1.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,1.2 tasyātaḥ pravāso 'numīyate pituḥ /
yena svayaṃ guṇavānsanputraṃ nopaneṣyati /
children.translated_text: Because he, being himself a man of virtue, would not [otherwise] have failed to invest his own son.

children.text: sa pitroktaḥ śvetaketurha dvādaśavarṣaḥ sannupetyā'cāryaṃ yāvaccatuviṃśativarṣo babhūva tāvatsarvānvedāṃścaturo 'pyadhītya tadarthaṃ ca buddhvā mahāmanā mahadgambhīraṃ mano yasyāsamamātmānamanyairmanyamānaṃ mano yasya so 'yaṃ mahāmanāḥ anūcānamānyanūcānamātmānaṃ manyata ityevaṃśīlo yaḥ so 'nūcānamānī stabdho 'praṇatasvabhāva eyāya gṛham /
children.translated_text: He — <s>Śvetaketu</s>, told [to study] by his father — having approached a teacher at twelve years of age, until he became twenty-four — studied all four <s>Vedas</s> and understood their meaning — [he became] 'mahāmanā' (high-minded) — one whose mind is great, deep, and incomparable, considering himself unequalled by others — 'anūcānamānī' — one who considers himself learned — of such disposition — 'stabdha' — arrogant, of unyielding nature — he came home.

children.text: tamevaṃbhūtaṃ hā'tmano 'nanurūpaśīlaṃ stabdhaṃ māninaṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā pitovāca saddharmāvatāracikīrṣayā /
children.translated_text: Having seen his son thus — of a disposition unbefitting himself, arrogant and conceited — the father spoke, wishing to introduce the true doctrine (saddharma):

children.text: śvetaketo yannivadaṃ mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdhaścāsi kaste 'tiśayaḥ prāpta upādhyāyāt?utāpi tamādeśamādiśyata ityādeśaḥ kevalaśāsrācāryopadeśagamyamityetadyena vā paraṃ brahmā'diśyate sa ādeśastamaprākṣyaḥ pṛṣṭavānasyācāryam //2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Śvetaketu</s>, since you are conceited, consider yourself learned, and are arrogant — what special knowledge have you obtained from your teacher? Or were you also taught that instruction (ādeśa)' — the ādeśa is that which is accessible only through the teaching of a teacher according to scripture — 'by which the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is indicated — did you ask your teacher about that?' (2)
[Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.1.2:] From this, the father's [earlier] absence is to be inferred.

children.text: START ChUp 6,1.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.1.3]

children.text:
śvetaketo yan nu somyedaṃ mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdho 'si |
uta tam ādeśam aprākṣyaḥ yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavaty amataṃ matam avijñātaṃ vijñātam iti |
kathaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sa ādeśo bhavatīti || ChUp_6,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: '"<s>Śvetaketu</s>, since you are conceited, consider yourself learned, and are arrogant — did you ask for that instruction by which the unheard becomes heard, the unthought becomes thought, the unknown becomes known?" "How, Blessed One, can such an instruction be?"' (ChUp 6.1.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,1.3 tamādeśaṃ viśinaṣṭi-yenā'deśena śrutenāśrutamapyanyacchataṃ bhavatyamataṃ matamatarkitaṃ tarkitaṃ bhavatyavijñānaṃ vijñātamaniścitaṃ niścitaṃ bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.1.3:] He specifies that instruction: 'By which instruction, when heard, even the unheard becomes heard; the unthought — the unreasoned — becomes thought, reasoned; the unknown — the unascertained — becomes known, ascertained.'

children.text: sarvānapi vedānadhātya sarvaṃ cānyadvedyamadhigamyāpyakṛtārtha eva bhavati yāvadātmatattvaṃ na jānātītyākhyāyikāto 'vagamyate /
children.translated_text: From the narrative, it is understood that even after studying all the <s>Vedas</s> and mastering all other knowable things, one remains unfulfilled as long as one does not know the truth of the Self (<s>ātmatattva</s>).

children.text: tadetadadbhutaṃ śrutvā'ha-kathaṃ nvetadaprasiddhamanyavijñānenānyadvijñātaṃ bhavatītyevaṃ manvānaḥ pṛcchati kathaṃ nu kena prakāreṇa he bhagavaḥ sa ādeśo bhavatīti //3 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this astounding [proposition], he says — thinking 'How can this unprecedented thing be — that by knowing one thing, another becomes known?' — he asks: 'How, by what means, O Blessed One, can such an instruction be?' (3)

children.text: START ChUp 6,1.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.1.4]

children.text:
yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt |
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam || ChUp_6,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as, dear boy, by knowing one lump of clay, everything made of clay becomes known — a modification is merely a name, a verbal handle — clay alone is the reality.' (ChUp 6.1.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,1.4 yathā sa ādeśo bhavati tacchṛṇu he somya /
yathā loka ekena mṛtpiṇḍena ghaṭaśarāvādikāraṇabhūtena vijñātena sarvamanyadvikārajātaṃ mṛnmayaṃ mṛdvikārajātaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt /
kathaṃ mṛtpiṇḍe kāraṇe vijñāte kāryamanyadvijñātaṃ syāt /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
kāraṇenānanyatvātkāryasya /
yanmanyase 'nyasminvijñāte 'nyanna jñāyata iti /
satyamevaṃ syāt /
yadyanyatkāraṇātkāryaṃ syānna tvevamanyatkāraṇātkāryam /
kathaṃ tarhidaṃ loka idaṃ kāraṇamayasya vikāra iti /
śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: Listen:

children.text: vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vāgārambhaṇaṃ vāgālambanamityetat /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vācārambhaṇa</s>' means 'vāgārambhaṇa' — having speech as its support, that is, dependent merely on speech.

children.text: ko 'sau vikāro nāmadheyaṃ nāmaiva nāmadheyaṃ svārthe dheyapratyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is that modification? It is a mere name (<s>nāmadheya</s>) — name alone; the suffix '-dheya' is used in its own sense.

children.text: vāgālambanamātraṃ nāmaiva kevalaṃ na vikāro nāma vastvasti paramārthato mṛttiketyeva tu mṛttiketyeva tu mṛttikaiva satyaṃ vastvasti //4 //
children.translated_text: It is merely a support for speech — name alone. No modification truly exists in the ultimate sense — 'clay alone is the reality,' meaning clay alone is the real substance. (4)
