children.text: ChUpBh_6,7.3 evamuktavantaṃ pitā'ha-śṛṇu tatra kāraṇaṃ yena te tānyṛgādīni na pratibhāntīti (taṃ hovāca) yathā loke he somya mahato mahatparimāṇasyābhyāhitasyopacitasyendhanairagnereko 'ṅgāraḥ khadyotaparimāṇaḥ śāntasya pariśiṣṭo 'vaśiṣṭaḥ syādbhavettenoṅgāreṇa tato 'pi tatparimāṇādīṣadapi na bahu dahedevameva khalu somya te tavānnopacitānāṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānāmekā kalāvayavo 'tiśiṣṭāvaśiṣṭā na bahu dahedevameva khalu somya te tavānnopacitānāṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānāmekā kalāvayavo 'tiśiṣṭā syāttayā tvaṃ khadyotamātrāṅgāratulyayaitarhīdānīṃ vedānnānubhavasi na pratipadyase, śrutvā ca me mama vācamathāśeṣaṃ vijñāsyasyaśāna bhuṅkṣva tāvat //3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.7.3:] To him who spoke thus, the father said: 'Hear the reason why the <s>Ṛg</s> verses and the rest do not come to your mind.' (He said:) 'Just as in the world, dear one, of a great fire that has been built up — enlarged — with fuel, if a single ember the size of a firefly remains — is left over — of the extinguished [fire], by that ember, it would not burn even slightly more than that [amount]. In exactly the same way, dear one, of your sixteen parts nourished by food, one part — one fraction — may be left over. By that, which is like an ember the size of a firefly, you do not now apprehend the <s>Vedas</s> — you do not comprehend them. Having heard my words, you will then understand the rest. But eat first.' (3)

children.text: START ChUp 6,7.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.7.4]

children.text:
sa hāśa |
atha hainam upasasāda |
taṃ ha yat kiṃ ca papraccha sarvaṃ ha pratipede || ChUp_6,7.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'He ate. Then he approached [his father]. Whatever [his father] asked him, he understood everything.' (ChUp 6.7.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,7.4 sa ha tathaivā'śa bhuktavānathānantaraṃ hainaṃ pitaraṃ śuśrūṣurupasasāda taṃ hopagataṃ putraṃ yatkiñcargādiṣu papraccha grantharūpamarthajātaṃ vā pitā sa śvetaketuḥ sarvaṃ ha tatpratipede ṛgādyarthato granthataśca //4 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.7.4:] He then ate — he took food. Then immediately he approached his father, wishing to learn. Whatever the father asked the son who had come to him — whether the textual form of the <s>Ṛg</s> and other [<s>Vedas</s>] or their meanings — <s>Śvetaketu</s> understood all of it, both in meaning and in textual form. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 6,7.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.7.5]

children.text:
taṃ hovāca |
yathā somya mahato 'bhyāhitasyaikam aṅgāraṃ khadyotamātraṃ pariśiṣṭaṃ taṃ tṛnair upasamādhāya prājvalayet tena tato 'pi bahu dahet || ChUp_6,7.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'He said to him: "Just as, dear one, of a great fire that has been built up, if one ember the size of a firefly were left over, and one were to build it up with straw, it would blaze up, and by that it would then burn much."' (ChUp 6.7.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,7.5 taṃ hovāca punaḥ pitā yathā somya mahato 'bhyāhitāsyetyādi samānamekamaṅgāraṃ śāntasyāgneḥ khadyotamātraṃ pariśiṣṭaṃ taṃ tṛṇaiścūrṇaiścopasamādhāya prājvalayedvardhayet /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.7.5:] The father said to him again: 'Just as, dear one, of a great fire that has been built up' and so on — similarly — 'one ember of the extinguished fire, the size of a firefly, left over — if one were to build it up with straw and kindling, it would blaze — it would increase.'

children.text: teneddhenāṅgāreṇa tato 'pi pūrvaparimāṇādbahu dahet //5 //
children.translated_text: 'By that kindled ember, it would then burn much more than the previous size.' (5)

children.text: START ChUp 6,7.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.7.6]

children.text:
evaṃ somya te ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānām ekā kalātiśiṣṭābhūt |
sānnenopasamāhitā prājvālī |
tayaitarhi vedān anubhavasi |
annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ |
āpomayaḥ prāṇaḥ |
tejomayī vāg iti |
tad dhāsya vijajñāv iti vijajñāv iti || ChUp_6,7.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Thus, dear boy, of your sixteen parts, one part remained. That [part], nourished by food, blazed forth. By that [restored part], you now comprehend the <s>Vedas</s>. For the mind, dear boy, is made of food; <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is made of water; speech is made of fire.' He [Śvetaketu] understood that — he understood that. (ChUp 6.7.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,7.6 evaṃ somya te ṣoḍaśānāmannakalānāṃ sāmarthyarūpāṇāmekā kalātiśiṣṭābhūdatiśiṣṭā'sītpañcadaśāhānyabhuktavata ekaikenāhnaikaikā kalā candramasa ivāparapakṣe kṣīṇā sātiśiṣṭā kalā tavānnena bhuktenopasamāhitā vardhitopacitā prājvāli /
dairdhyaṃ chāndasaṃ prajvalitā vardhitetyarthaḥ /
prājvālīditi kalā tavānnena bhuktenopasamāhitā vardhitopacitā prājvāli /
dairdhyaṃ chāndasaṃ prajvalitā vardhitetyarthaḥ /
prājvālīditi pāṭhāntaraṃ tadā tenopasamāhitā svayaṃ prajvalitavatīryarthaḥ /
tayā vardhitayaitarhīdānīṃ vedānanubhavasyupalabhase /
evaṃ vyāvṛttyanuvṛttibhyāmannāmayatvaṃ manasaḥ siddhamityupasaṃharatyannamayaṃ hi somya mana ityādi /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the process of exclusion and inclusion, the conclusion that the mind is made of food is established — he sums up: 'For the mind, dear boy, is made of food' and so forth.

children.text: yathaitanmanaso 'nnamayatvaṃ tava siddhaṃ tathā'pomayaḥ prāṇastejomayī vāgityetadapi siddhamevetyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as this food-nature of the mind has been established for you, so too '<s>prāṇa</s> is made of water' and 'speech is made of fire' — this too is established — such is the import.

children.text: tadetaddhāsya pituruktaṃ mana ādīnāmannādimayatvaṃ vijajñau vijñātavāñśvetaketuḥ /
children.translated_text: That which the father had stated — that the mind and the rest are made of food and the like — <s>Śvetaketu</s> understood, comprehended it.

children.text: dvirabhyāsastrivṛtkaraṇaprakaraṇasamāptyarthaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: The twofold repetition [of 'vijajñau'] is for the purpose of concluding the section on <s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s> (tripartite combination). (6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.7.6:] 'Thus, dear boy, of your sixteen parts of food — which are in the form of capacities — one part remained, was left over, when you had not eaten for fifteen days; one part [being consumed] each day, like [the phases of] the moon in the dark fortnight. That remaining part of yours, nourished — augmented, built up — by the food you ate, blazed forth.' The lengthened [vowel] is a Vedic irregularity — meaning it was kindled, it grew. An alternate reading is 'prājvālīt' — then the meaning is: 'that part, nourished by the food you ate, blazed forth of its own accord.' 'By that restored [part], you now comprehend — apprehend — the <s>Vedas</s>.'

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh section of the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,8.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.1]

children.text:
uddālako hāruṇiḥ śvetaketuṃ putram uvāca svapnāntaṃ me somya vijānīhīti |
yatraitat puruṣaḥ svapiti nāma satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati |
svam apīto bhavati |
tasmād enaṃ svapitīty ācakṣate |
svaṃ hy apīto bhavati || ChUp_6,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Uddālaka</s> <s>Āruṇi</s> said to his son <s>Śvetaketu</s>: "Learn from me, dear boy, the nature of deep sleep (<s>svapnānta</s>). When a person sleeps — as it is called — then, dear boy, he has merged with Being (<s>Sat</s>). He has gone to his own (<s>svam apīta</s>). Therefore they say of him, 'he sleeps' (<s>svapiti</s>), for he has indeed gone to his own."' (ChUp 6.8.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,8.1 yasminmanasi jīvenā'tmanānupraviṣṭā parā devatā'darśa iva puruṣaḥ pratibimbena jalādiviṣviva ca sūryādayaḥ pratibimbaiḥ /
tanmano 'nnamayaṃ tejo 'ṃmayābhyāṃ vākprāṇābhyāṃ saṃgatamadhigatam /
yanmayo yatsthaśca jīvo mananadarśanaśravaṇādivyāvahārāya kalpate taduparame ca svaṃ devatārūpameva pratipadyate /
taduktaṃ śrutyantare"dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva sadhīḥ svapno bhūtvemaṃ lokamatikrāmati""sa vā āyamātmā brahma vijñānamayo manomaya"ityādi,"svapnena śārīram" ityādi,"prāṇanneva prāṇo nāma bhavatī"tyādi ca /
tasyāsya manaḥsthasya mana ākhyāṃ gatasya manaupaśamadvāreṇendriyaviṣayebhyo nivṛttasya yasyāṃ parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ svātmabhātāyāṃ yadavasthānaṃ tatputrāyā'cikhyāsuruddālako ha kilā'ruṇiḥ śvetaketuṃ putramuvācoktavān /
svapnāntaṃ svapnamadhyaṃ svapna iti darśanavṛtteḥ svapnasyā'khyā tasya madhyaṃ svapnāntaṃ suṣuptamityetat /
athavā svapnāntaṃ svapnasatattvamityarthaḥ tatrāpyarthātsuṣuptameva bhavati /
svamapīto bhavatīti vacanāt /
na hyanyatra suṣuptātsvamapītiṃ jīvasyecchanti brahmavidaḥ /
tatra hyādarśāpanayane puruṣapratibimbi ādarśagato yathā svameva puruṣamapīto bhavatyevaṃ mana ādyuparame caitanyapratibimbarūpeṇa jīvenā'tmanā manasi praviṣṭā nāmarūpavyākaraṇāya parā devatā sā svamevā'tmānaṃ pratipadyate jīvarūpatāṃ mana ākhyāṃ hitvā /
ataḥ suṣupta eva svapnāntaśabdavācya ityavagamyate /
yatra tu suptaḥ svapnānpaśyati tatsvāpnaṃ darśanaṃ sukhaduḥkhasaṃyuktamiti puṇyāpuṇyayorhi sukhaduḥkhārambhakatvaṃ prasiddham /
puṇyāpuṇyayoścāvidyākāmopaṣṭambhenaiva sukhaduḥkhataddarśanakāryārambhakatvamupapadyate nānyathetyavidyākāmakarmabhiḥ saṃsārahetubhiḥ saṃyukta eva svapna iti na svamapītā bhavati /
"ananvāgataṃ puṇyenānanvāgataṃ pāpena tīrṇo hi tadā sarvāñchokānhṛdayasya bhavati" "tadvā asyaitadaticchandā" "eṣa parama ānanda"ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
suṣupta eva svaṃ devatārūpaṃ jīvatvavinirmuktaṃ darśayiṣyāmītyāha /
svapnāntaṃ me mama nigadato he somya vijānīhi vispaṣṭamavadhārayetyarthaḥ /
kadā svapnānto bhavatītyucyate /
yatra yasminkāla etannāma bhavati puruṣasya svapsyataḥ /
prasiddhaṃ hi loke svapitīti /
gauṇaṃ cedaṃ nāmetyāha /
yadā svapitītyucyate puruṣastadā tasminkāle satā sacchabdavācyayā prakṛtayā devatayā saṃpanno bhavati saṃgata ekībhūto bhavati /
manasi praviṣṭaṃ mana ādisaṃsargakṛtaṃ jīvarūpaṃ parityajya svaṃ sadrūpaṃ yatparamārthasatyamapīto 'pigato bhavati /
atastasmātsvapitītyenamācakṣate lokikāḥ /
svamātmānaṃ hi yasmādapīto bhavati /
tataścā'yastānāṃ karaṇānāmanekavyāpāranimittaglānānāṃ svavyāpārebhya uparamo bhavati /
śruteśca"śrāmyatyeva vākśrāmyati cakṣur" ityevamādi /
tathā ca"gṛhītā vāggṛhītaṃ śrotraṃ gṛhītaṃ mana"ityevamādīni karaṇāni prāṇagrastāni /
prāṇa eko 'śrānto dehe kulāye yo jāgarti tadā jīvaḥ śramāpanuttaye svaṃ devatārūpamātmānaṃ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> alone remains unwearied in the body, which is its nest. At that time, the <s>jīva</s> returns to its own self, which is of the nature of the deity, in order to remove its fatigue.

children.text: nānyatra svarūpāvasthānācchramāpanodaḥ syāditi yuktā prasiddhirlaukikānāṃ svaṃ hyapīto bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: It is reasonable that removal of fatigue would not occur except by resting in one's own true nature — hence the well-known [usage] of ordinary people, 'he has gone to his own,' is appropriate.

children.text: dṛśyate hi loke jvarādirogagrastānāṃ tadvinirnoke svātmasthānāṃ viśramaṇaṃ tadvadihāpi syāditi yuktam /
children.translated_text: For it is observed in the world that those afflicted by fever and other diseases find rest when those [diseases] are removed and they return to their own natural state — it is reasonable that the same applies here as well.

children.text: "tadyathā śyeno vā suparṇo vā viparipatya śrānta"ityādiśruteṣca //1 //
children.translated_text: And from <s>śruti</s> texts such as: 'Just as a hawk or an eagle, having flown about and become weary...' and so forth. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.8.1:] The supreme deity, having entered the mind through the individual self (<s>jīva</s>), is [reflected] in [the mind] like a person's reflection in a mirror, or like the sun and the like [reflected] in water through their reflections. That mind is made of food; it is conjoined with speech and <s>prāṇa</s>, which are made of fire and water [respectively]. Whatever the <s>jīva</s> is made of and wherever it is stationed — [by that] it becomes fit for the activities of thinking, seeing, hearing, and the like; and upon the cessation [of those activities], it returns to its own form, which is the form of the deity. As stated in another <s>śruti</s>: 'It seems to think, seems to move about; having become a dream, it transcends this world' — and 'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>, made of consciousness, made of mind' — and 'Through sleep, the bodily [self]...' — and 'Breathing, it becomes by name breath (<s>prāṇa</s>)' — and so forth. For this [<s>jīva</s>] who abides in the mind — who has attained the designation 'mind' — who has withdrawn from sense-objects through the subsidence of the mind — [the text describes] the state in which it rests in the supreme deity, which has become its own nature. Wishing to explain this to his son, <s>Uddālaka</s> <s>Āruṇi</s> indeed said to his son <s>Śvetaketu</s>. '<s>Svapnānta</s>' — the interior of sleep, or the reality of sleep; since sleep (<s>svapna</s>) refers to the state of [inner] vision, its interior (<s>anta</s>) is deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>). Alternatively, '<s>svapnānta</s>' means 'the true nature of sleep' — and even in this [interpretation], it amounts to deep sleep, because of the statement 'he has gone to his own' (<s>svam apīta</s>). For the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> do not accept that the <s>jīva</s> has 'gone to its own' in any state other than deep sleep. For in that [deep sleep state] — just as when a mirror is removed, the person's reflection [which was] in the mirror returns to the person himself — so too, upon the cessation of the mind and the rest, the supreme deity, which had entered the mind in the form of a reflection of consciousness as the individual self, returns to its own self, abandoning the <s>jīva</s>-form and the designation 'mind.' Therefore, it is understood that deep sleep alone is meant by the word '<s>svapnānta</s>.' But the state in which a sleeping person sees dreams — that dream-vision, associated with pleasure and pain — [is produced] by merit and demerit, for it is well known that merit and demerit are the causes of pleasure and pain. And it is reasonable that merit and demerit produce pleasure, pain, and their corresponding dream-visions only when supported by ignorance and desire — not otherwise. Therefore, the dream state, which is connected with ignorance, desire, and action — the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> — is not one in which [the <s>jīva</s>] has 'gone to its own.' [This is supported] by <s>śruti</s> texts such as: 'Not followed by merit, not followed by demerit — for then he has crossed beyond all sorrows of the heart' — and 'That [state] of his is beyond desire' — and 'This is supreme bliss.' [The father says:] 'I shall show that in deep sleep alone, the <s>jīva</s> has [returned to] its own form — the form of the deity, free from <s>jīva</s>-hood.' '<s>Svapnānta</s>' — 'the [nature of] deep sleep, from my words — dear boy, understand clearly, comprehend' — this is the meaning. When does the '<s>svapnānta</s>' (deep sleep) occur? — it is stated: 'When' — at which time — 'this happens by name' — when a person is about to sleep. It is well known in the world [that people say] 'he sleeps.' This is a figurative name — he says. When a person is said to 'sleep' — at that time, he has become merged with Being (<s>Sat</s>) — with the primordial deity denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>' — he has become united, has become one with it. Having abandoned the <s>jīva</s>-form created by association with the mind and the rest — which had entered the mind — he has gone (<s>apīta</s>) to his own (<s>sva</s>) — to his own form, which is the ultimate reality called <s>Sat</s>. Therefore they say of him 'he sleeps' (<s>svapiti</s>) — the ordinary people [use this word]. Because he has gone to his own self. And therefore there is cessation of activity for these sense-organs, which have become exhausted by their manifold operations. As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'Speech becomes weary, the eye becomes weary' — and so forth. And similarly: 'Speech is seized, hearing is seized, mind is seized' — and so forth — the organs are [as if] swallowed by <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,8.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.2]

children.text:
sa yathā śakuniḥ sūtreṇa prabaddho diśaṃ diśaṃ patitvānyatrāyatanam alabdhvā bandhanam evopaśrayate |
evam eva khalu somya tan mano diśaṃ diśaṃ patitvānyatrāyatanam alabdhvā prāṇam evopaśrayate |
prāṇabandhanaṃ hi somya mana iti || ChUp_6,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as a bird, bound by a string, having flown in every direction and finding no resting place elsewhere, settles down upon its bond itself — so indeed, dear boy, that mind, having flown in every direction and finding no resting place elsewhere, settles down upon <s>prāṇa</s> alone. For the mind is bound to <s>prāṇa</s>, dear boy.' (ChUp 6.8.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,8.2 tatrāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto yathokter'the-sa yathā śakuniḥ pakṣī śakunighātakasya hastagatena sūtreṇa prabaddhaḥ pāśito diśaṃ diśaṃ bandhanamokṣārthī sanpratiśidiśaṃ patitvānyatra bandhanādāyatanamāśrayaṃ viśramaṇāyālabdhvāprāpya bandhanamevopaśrayate /
evameva yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ khalu he sobhya tanmanastatprakṛtaṃ poḍaśakalamannopacitaṃ mano nirdhāritaṃ tatepraviṣṭastatsthastadupalakṣito jīvastanmana iti nirdiśyate mañcākrośanavat /
sa mana ākhyopādhirjīvo 'vidyākāmakarmopadiṣṭāṃ diśaṃ diśaṃ sukhaduḥkhādilakṣaṇāṃ jāgratsvapnayoḥ patitvā gatvānubhūyetyarthaḥ /
anyatra sadākhyātsvātmana āyatanaṃ viśramaṇasthānamalabdhvā prāṇameva prāṇena sarvakāryakaraṇāśrayeṇopalakṣitā prāṇa ityucyate sadākhyā parā devatā /
children.translated_text: Finding no resting place — no place of rest — elsewhere, apart from its own self called <s>Sat</s> (Being) — it settles upon <s>prāṇa</s> alone. The supreme deity, denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>,' is called '<s>prāṇa</s>' because it is indicated by <s>prāṇa</s> — the support of all effects and instruments.

children.text: "prāṇasya prāṇaṃ" "prāṇaśarīro bhārūpa"ityādiśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: [This is supported by] <s>śruti</s> texts such as: 'The breath of breath' and '<s>Prāṇa</s>-bodied, light-formed' and so forth.

children.text: atastāṃ devatāṃ prāṇaṃ prāṇākhyāmevopaśrayate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it settles upon that deity — <s>prāṇa</s>, the one denoted by the name '<s>prāṇa</s>.'

children.text: prāṇo bandhanaṃ yasya manasastatprāṇabandhanaṃ hi yasmātsomya manaḥ prāṇopalakṣitadevatāśrayaṃ mana iti tadupalakṣito jīva iti //2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇabandhanam</s>' — that whose bond is <s>prāṇa</s> — for, dear boy, the mind has its support in the deity indicated by <s>prāṇa</s>, [and so] what is indicated by the mind — the <s>jīva</s> — [also has its support there]. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.8.2:] Here is an illustration for what has been stated: Just as a bird — caught in the hand of a bird-catcher — bound, fettered by a string — desiring to free itself from the bond, having flown in every direction — and finding no resting place, no refuge for rest, elsewhere apart from the bond — settles down upon the bond itself. Just so — as this illustration shows — dear boy, that mind — the one under discussion — built up by the sixteen parts of food — the established [mind] — the <s>jīva</s>, having entered it, stationed in it, characterized by it — is referred to as 'mind,' like [calling] the platform by the name of the person [sitting on it]. That <s>jīva</s>, whose limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) is called 'mind,' directed by ignorance, desire, and action, having flown in every direction — toward the various states characterized by pleasure, pain, and the like, in waking and dream — having gone, having experienced [them], is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 6,8.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.3]

children.text:
aśanāpipāse me somya vijānīhīti |
yatraitat puruṣo 'śiśiṣati nāmāpa eva tad aśitaṃ nayante |
tad yathā gonāyo 'śvanāyaḥ puruṣanāya ity evaṃ tad apa ācakṣate 'śanāyeti |
tatraitac chuṅgam utpatitaṃ somya vijānīhi |
nedam amūlaṃ bhaviṣyatīti || ChUp_6,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Learn from me, dear boy, about hunger and thirst. When a person is hungry — as it is called — it is water that leads away what has been eaten. Just as one speaks of a cow-leader, a horse-leader, a man-leader — so one calls water the "hunger-leader" (<s>aśanāya</s>). Know this sprout (<s>śuṅga</s>) that has sprouted forth, dear boy. It cannot be without a root.' (ChUp 6.8.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,8.3 evaṃ svapitināmaprasiddhidvāreṇa yajjīvasya satyasvarūpaṃ jagato mūlaṃ tatputrasya darśayitvā'hānnādikāryakāraṇaparamparayāpi jagato mūlaṃ saddidarśayiṣuḥ /
aśanāpipāse aśitumicchāśanā yālopena /
pātumicchā pipāsā te aśanāpipāse aśanāpipāsayoḥ satatvaṃ vijānīhītyetat /
yatra yasminkāla etannāma puruṣo bhavati /
kiṃ tat?aśiśiṣatyaśitumicchatīti /
tadā tasya puruṣasya kinimittaṃ nāma bhavatītyāha /
yattatpuruṣeṇāśitamannaṃ kaṭhinaṃ potā āpo nayante dravīkṛtya rasādibhāvena vipariṇamayante tadā bhuktamannaṃ jīryati /
atha ca bhavatyasya nāmāśiśiṣatīti gauṇam /
jīrṇe hyanne 'śitumicchati sarvo hi jantuḥ /
tat tatra apāmaśitanetṛtvādaśanāyā iti nāma prasiddhamityetasminnarthe /
yathā gonāyo gāṃ nayatīti gonāya ityucyate gopālaḥ /
tathāśvānnayatītyaśvanāyo 'śvapāla ityucyate /
puruṣanāyaḥ puruṣānnayatīti rājā senāpatirvā /
evaṃ tattadāpa ācakṣate laukikā aśanāyeti visarjanīyalopena /
children.translated_text: Thus, ordinary people speak of water as '<s>aśanāya</s>' (hunger-leader), with elision of the visarjanīya.

children.text: tatraivaṃ satyadbhī rasādibhāvena nītenāśitenānnena niṣpāditamidaṃ śarīraṃ vaṭakaṇikāyāmiva śuṅgo 'ṅkura utpatita udgatastamimaṃ śuṅgaṃ kāryaṃ śarīrākhyaṃ vaṭādiśuṅgavadutpatitaṃ he sobhya vijānīhi /
children.translated_text: This being so — this body, which has been produced by food that has been eaten and led by water in the form of rasa and the like — is like a sprout (<s>śuṅga</s>) that has sprouted forth from a banyan seed. Know this sprout — this effect called the body — which has sprouted forth like the sprout of a banyan tree and the like, dear boy.

children.text: kiṃ tatra vijñeyamityucyate /
children.translated_text: What is to be understood about it? — it is stated:

children.text: śuṇvidaṃ śuṅgavatkāryatvāccharīraṃ nāmūlaṃ mūlarahitaṃ bhaviṣyatītyukta āha śvetaketuḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: 'This [body], being an effect like a sprout, will not be without a root' — having heard this, <s>Śvetaketu</s> said: (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.8.3:] Having thus shown to his son, through the well-known [phenomenon] called sleep, the true nature of the <s>jīva</s> which is <s>Sat</s> — the root of the world — [the father] now wishes to show that <s>Sat</s> is also the root of the world through the causal chain of food and the rest. '<s>Aśanāpipāse</s>' — the desire to eat is '<s>aśanā</s>' (hunger), with elision of the final vowel; the desire to drink is '<s>pipāsā</s>' (thirst). Learn the true nature of hunger and thirst — this is what is meant. 'When' — at which time — 'this happens by name' — a person [is described in a certain way]. What is that? 'He is hungry' (<s>aśiśiṣati</s>) — he wishes to eat. Then, what causes this name to apply to the person? — he says: The food that was eaten by the person — the solid [food] — water leads it, meaning transforms it by liquefying it into the form of rasa (nutrient fluid) and the like. Then the food that was eaten is digested. And then the name applies to him — 'he is hungry' — but this is figurative. For when food is digested, every creature wishes to eat. Thus, in this matter, because water leads what is eaten, the name '<s>aśanāya</s>' (hunger) is well known. Just as a 'cow-leader' (<s>gonāya</s>) — one who leads cows — is called <s>gonāya</s>, a cowherd. Similarly, one who leads horses is called 'horse-leader' (<s>aśvanāya</s>), a horse-keeper. A 'man-leader' (<s>puruṣanāya</s>) — one who leads men — is a king or a general.

children.text: START ChUp 6,8.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.4]

children.text:
tasya kva mūlaṃ syād anyatrānnāt |
evam eva khalu somyānnena śuṅgenāpo mūlam anviccha |
adbhiḥ somya śuṅgena tejo mūlam anviccha |
tejasā somya śuṅgena sanmūlam anviccha |
sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sadāyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ || ChUp_6,8.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Where could its root be, other than in food? Even so, dear boy, with food as the sprout, seek water as the root. With water, dear boy, as the sprout, seek fire (<s>tejas</s>) as the root. With fire, dear boy, as the sprout, seek Being (<s>Sat</s>) as the root. All these creatures, dear boy, have <s>Sat</s> as their root, <s>Sat</s> as their abode, <s>Sat</s> as their foundation.' (ChUp 6.8.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,8.4 yadyevaṃ samūlamidaṃ śarīraṃ vaṭādiśuṅgavattasyāsya kva mūlaṃ syādbhavedityevaṃ pṛṣṭa āha pitā /
tasya kva mūlaṃ syādanyatrānnādannaṃ mūlamityabhiprāyaḥ /
katham /
aśitaṃ hyannamadbhirdravīkṛtaṃ jāṭhareṇāgninā pacyamānaṃ rasabhāvena pariṇamate /
rasocchoṇitaṃ śoṇitānmāṃsaṃ māṃsānmedo medaso 'sthīnyasthibhyo majjā majjāyāḥ śukram /
tathā yoṣidbhuktaṃ cānnaṃ rasādikrameṇaivaṃ pariṇataṃ lohitaṃ bhavati /
tābhyāṃ śukraśoṇitābhyāmannakāryābhyāṃ saṃyuktābhyāmannenaiva pratyahaṃ bhujyamānenā'pūryamāṇābhyāṃ kuḍyamiva mṛtpiṇḍaiḥ pratyuhamupacīyamāno 'nnamūlo dehaśuṅgaḥ pariniṣpanna ityarthaḥ /
yattu dehaśuṅgo 'nnamūla evameva khalu somyānnena śuhgena kāryabhūtenāpo mūlamannasya śuṅgasyānviccha pratipadyasva /
apāmapi vināśotpattimattavācchuṅgatvameveti adbhiḥ sīmya śuṅgena kāryeṇa kāraṇaṃ tejo mūlamanviccha /
tejaso 'pi vināśotpattimattavācchuṅgatvamiti tejasā somya śuṅgena sanmūlamekamevādvitīyaṃ paramārthasatyam /

yasminsarvamidaṃ vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyamanṛtaṃ rajjvāmiva sarpādivikalpajātamadhyastamavidyayā tadasya jagato mūlamataḥ sanmūlāḥ satkāraṇā he somyemāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamalakṣaṇāḥ sarvāḥ prajā na kevalaṃ sanmūlā evedānīmapi sthitikāle sadāyatanāḥ sadāśrayā eva /
children.translated_text: In which all this is merely a beginning of speech (<s>vācārambhaṇa</s>) — a modification, a mere name, unreal — like the imagined superimposition of a snake and the like upon a rope, superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — that is the root of this world. Therefore, having Being as their root, having Being as their cause — O dear boy, all these beings, characterized as stationary and moving — are not merely rooted in Being but even now, in the state of continued existence, they have Being as their abode (<s>sadāyatana</s>), Being as their support.

children.text: nahi mṛdamanāśritya ghaṭādeḥ sattvaṃ sthitirvāsti /
children.translated_text: For without depending on clay, there is no existence or persistence of a pot and the like.

children.text: ato mṛdvatsanmūtvātprajānāṃ sadāyatanaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ sadāyatanāḥ prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as with clay, since beings have Being as their root, they have Being as their abode — those beings which have that [Being as their abode], those are the beings with Being as their abode.

children.text: ante ca satpratiṣṭhāḥ sadeva pratiṣṭā layaḥ samāptipavasānaṃ pariśeṣo yāsāṃ tāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: And at the end, they have Being as their final resting place (<s>satpratiṣṭhā</s>) — Being alone is the resting place, the dissolution, the conclusion, the remainder of which — those [beings] have Being as their final resting place. (4)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.8.4:] If this body has a root like the sprout of a banyan tree and similar [plants], where would its root be? — being asked thus, the father answers. Where would its root be, other than in food? Food is the root — this is the purport. How so? For the food that is eaten, liquefied by water, being cooked by the digestive fire (<s>jāṭharāgni</s>), transforms into the form of juice (<s>rasa</s>). From juice comes blood, from blood comes flesh, from flesh comes fat, from fat come bones, from bones comes marrow, and from marrow comes semen. Similarly, food eaten by a woman, having transformed through the same sequence from juice onward, becomes menstrual blood. From these two — semen and blood, which are products of food — joined together and nourished daily by the food that is eaten, the body-sprout is fully developed, built up like a wall with lumps of clay added day by day — this is the meaning. Just as the body-sprout has food as its root, even so, dear boy, through the sprout that is the effect of food, seek water as the root of the food-sprout. Since water too, being subject to destruction and origination, is also a sprout — through water as the sprout, seek fire (<s>tejas</s>) as the root. Since fire too, being subject to destruction and origination, is also a sprout — through fire, dear boy, as the sprout, seek Being (<s>Sat</s>) as the root, the one without a second, the ultimate reality.

children.text: START ChUp 6,8.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.5]

children.text:
atha yatraitat puruṣaḥ pipāsati nāma teja eva tat pītaṃ nayate |
tad yathā gonāyo 'śvanāyaḥ puruṣanāya ity evaṃ tat teja ācaṣṭa udanyeti |
tatraitad eva śuṅgam utpatitaṃ somya vijānīhi |
nedam amūlaṃ bhaviṣyatīti || ChUp_6,8.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, when a person is said to be thirsty, it is fire (<s>tejas</s>) alone that leads away what has been drunk. Just as one speaks of a "cow-leader," a "horse-leader," or a "person-leader," so one calls that fire "water-leader" (<s>udanya</s>). Know this sprout to have sprung up from that [root], dear boy. It cannot be without a root.' (ChUp 6.8.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,8.5 athedānīmapśuṅgadvāreṇa sato mūlasyānugamaḥ kārya ityāha /
yatra yasminkāla etannāma pipāsati pātumicchatīti puruṣo bhavati /
aśiśiṣatītivadidamapi gauṇameva nāma bhavati /
dravīkṛtasyāśitasyānnasya netrya āpo 'nnaśuṅgaṃ dehaṃ kledayantyaḥ śithilī kuryurabbāhulyādyadi tejasā na śoṣyante /
nitarāṃ ca tejasā śoṣyamāṇā svapsu dehabhāvena pariṇamamānāsu pātumicchā puruṣasya jāyate tadā puruṣaḥ pipāsati nāma tadetadāha /
teja eva tattadā pītamabādi śoṣayaddehagatalohitaprāṇabhāvena nayate pariṇamayati /
children.translated_text: Fire (<s>tejas</s>) alone at that time leads — transforms — what has been drunk, drying it up, into the state of blood and vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) within the body.

children.text: tadyathā gonāya ityādi samānamevaṃ tatteja ācaṣṭe loka udanyetyudakaṃ nayatītyudanyam /
children.translated_text: 'Just as a cow-leader' and so forth — the same as before. Thus that fire is called by people '<s>udanya</s>' (water-leader) — meaning 'it leads water.'

children.text: udanyetīti cchāndasaṃ tatrāpi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: The form '<s>udanyeti</s>' is Vedic (Chāndasa usage). There too, the same as before.

children.text: apāmapyetadeva śarīrākhyaṃ śuṅgaṃ nānyadityevamādi samānamanyat //5 //
children.translated_text: Of water too, this very body-sprout is the sprout and nothing else — and so forth, the rest is the same as before. (5)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.8.5:] Now, through the sprout that is water, the tracing back to Being as the root is to be done — so he says. When (<s>yatra</s>) — at which time — a person is said to be thirsty, i.e., desires to drink — this too, like 'he is hungry,' is merely a figurative expression. The waters that are the carriers of the eaten food, which has been liquefied, moistening the body-sprout that is the food-sprout, would make it flaccid — if they were not dried up by fire. And when they are excessively dried up by fire, as the waters transform into the state of the body, the desire to drink arises in the person — then the person is said to be thirsty. This is what he explains.

children.text: START ChUp 6,8.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.6]

children.text:
tasya kva mūlaṃ syād anyatrādbhyaḥ |
adbhiḥ somya śuṅgena tejo mūlam anviccha |
tejasā somya śuṅgena sanmūlam anviccha |
sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sad āyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ |
yathā nu khalu somyemās tisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tad uktaṃ purastād eva bhavati |
asya somya puruṣasya prayato vāṅ manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām || ChUp_6,8.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Where would its root be, other than in water? Through water, dear boy, as the sprout, seek fire as the root. Through fire, dear boy, as the sprout, seek Being (<s>Sat</s>) as the root. All these beings, dear boy, have Being as their root, Being as their abode, Being as their final resting place. Now, how each of these three deities, upon reaching a person, becomes threefold — that has been stated earlier. When this person, dear boy, is departing [from life], speech merges into mind, mind into <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), <s>prāṇa</s> into fire (<s>tejas</s>), and fire into the supreme deity.' (ChUp 6.8.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,8.6 sāmarthyāttejaso 'pyetadeva śarīrākhyaṃ śuṅgam /
ato 'pśuṅgena dehenā'po mūlaṃ gamyate /
adbhiḥ śuṅgena tejo mūlaṃ gamyate /
tejasā śuṅgena sanmūlaṃ gamyate pūrvavat /
evaṃ hi tejobannamayasya dehaśuṅgasya vācārambhaṇamātrasyānnādiparamparayā paramārthasatyaṃ sanmūlamabhayasaṃtrāsaṃ nirāyāsaṃ sanmūlamanviccheti putraṃ gamayitvāśiśiṣati pipāsatīti nāmaprasiddhidvāreṇa yadanyadihāsminprakaraṇe tejobannānāṃ puruṣeṇopabhujyamānānāṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātasya dehaśuṅgasya svajātyasāṃkaryeṇopacayakaratvaṃ vaktavyaṃ prāptaṃ tadihoktameva draṣṭavyamiti pūrvoktaṃ vyapadiśati /
yathā nu khalu yena prakāreṇemāstejobannākhyāstisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛttrivṛdekaikā bhavati taduktaṃ purastādeva bhavatyannamaśitaṃ tredhā vidhīyata ityādi /
tatraivoktamannādīnāmasitānāṃ ye mavyamā dhātavaste sāptadhātukaṃ śarīramupacinvantītyuktam /
"māṃsaṃ bhavati lohitaṃ bhavati majjā bhavatyasthi bhavati ye tvaṇiṣṭhā dhātavo manaḥ prāṇaṃ vācaṃ dehasyāntaḥkaraṇasaṃghātamupacinvantī"ti coktaṃ"tanmano bhavati sa prāṇo bhavati sā vāgbhavatī"ti /
so 'yaṃ prāṇakaraṇasaṃghāto dehe viśīrṇe dehāntaraṃ jīvādhiṣṭhito yena krameṇa pūrvadehātpracyuto gacchati tadāhāsya he somya puruṣasya prayato mriyamāṇasya vāṅmanasi saṃpadyate manasyupasaṃhriyate /
atha tadā'hurjñātayo na vadatīti /
manaḥpūrvako hi vāgvyāpāraḥ /
"yadvai manasā dhyāyati tadvācā vadati"iti śruteḥ /
vācyupasaṃhṛtāyāṃ manasi mano mananavyāpāreṇa kevalena vartate /
mano 'pi yadopasaṃhriyate tadā manaḥ prāṇe saṃpannaṃ bhavati suṣuptakāla iva tadā pārśvasthā jñātayo na vijānātītyāhuḥ /
prāṇaśca tadordhvocchvāsī svātmanyupasaṃhṛtabāhyakaraṇaḥ saṃvargavidyāyāṃ darśanāddhastapādādīnvikṣipanmarmasthānāni nikṛntannana ivotsṛjan krameṇopasaṃhṛtastejasi sampadyate /
tadā'hurjñātayo na calatīti mṛto neti vā vicikitsanto dehamālabhamānā uṣṇaṃ copalabhamānā deha uṣṇo jīvatīti yadā tadapyauṣṇyaliṅgaṃ teja upasaṃhriyate tadā tattejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ praśāmyati /
children.translated_text: Then the relatives say: 'He does not move' — or, doubting whether he is dead, they touch the body and, perceiving warmth, [say] 'The body is warm, he is alive.' When that sign of warmth — fire — is also withdrawn, then that fire subsides into the supreme deity.

children.text: tadevaṅkrameṇopasaṃhṛte svamūlaṃ prāpte ca manasi tatstho jīvo 'pi suṣuptakālavannimittopasaṃhārādupasaṃhriyamāṇaḥ sansatyābhisaṃdhipūrvakaṃ cedupasaṃhriyate sadeva saṃpadyate na punardehāntarāya suṣuptādivottiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: When thus, in this sequence, everything has been withdrawn and has reached its own root, the <s>jīva</s> too, established in that [mind], — just as in deep sleep — being withdrawn due to the withdrawal of its adjuncts (<s>nimitta</s>), if it merges with Being (<s>Sat</s>) with a prior intention of true knowledge, it reaches Being itself and does not rise again for [taking] another body, as one does from deep sleep.

children.text: yathā loke sabhaye deśe vartamānaḥ kathañcidivābhayaṃ deśaṃ prāptastadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, one who has been in a dangerous place and somehow reaches a safe place [does not return to the dangerous place] — it is like that.

children.text: itarastvanātmajñastasmādeva mūlātsuṣuptādivotthāya mṛtvā punardehajālamāviśati //6 //
children.translated_text: But the other — the one without knowledge of the Self — from that very root, like rising from deep sleep, after dying, enters the web of bodies again. (6)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.8.6:] By implication, this very body-sprout is the sprout of fire too. Therefore, through the body as the water-sprout, water is reached as the root. Through water as the sprout, fire is reached as the root. Through fire as the sprout, Being is reached as the root — as before. Thus, of the body-sprout which is made of fire, water, and food, and which is merely a beginning of speech (<s>vācārambhaṇa</s>), through the succession of food and the rest, the ultimately real Being is the root — the fearless, the free from terror, the effortless — 'seek Being as the root' — thus having led his son [to this understanding] through hunger and thirst, the figurative expressions, whatever else in this context regarding fire, water, and food as they are consumed by a person, and how they serve the body-sprout — the aggregate of body, senses, and organs — by building it up without mixing with alien kinds, all that which needed to be stated — 'that should be seen as already stated here' — thus he refers to what was said before. 'How, in what manner, these three deities called fire, water, and food, upon reaching a person, each become threefold — that has been stated earlier' — [namely] 'food when eaten is divided threefold' and so forth. There it was stated that of the food and other [elements] that are eaten, the middling constituents build up the body of seven tissues. 'It becomes flesh, it becomes blood, it becomes marrow, it becomes bone; and the subtlest constituents build up the mind, <s>prāṇa</s>, and speech — the internal organ aggregate of the body' — and it was said: 'That becomes mind, that becomes <s>prāṇa</s>, that becomes speech.' This aggregate of <s>prāṇa</s> and organs, when the body disintegrates, governed by the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), moves to another body — in what sequence it departs from the previous body — this he states. 'When this person, dear boy, is departing — dying — speech merges into mind, is withdrawn into mind.' Then the relatives say: 'He does not speak.' For the activity of speech is preceded by mind. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'What one thinks with the mind, that one speaks with speech.' When speech has been withdrawn, mind continues functioning with the activity of thinking alone. When mind too is withdrawn, then mind has merged into <s>prāṇa</s>, as in the state of deep sleep; then the relatives standing nearby say: 'He does not recognize [us].' And <s>prāṇa</s> then, breathing upward, with the external organs withdrawn into itself — as seen in the <s>Saṃvarga Vidyā</s> — casting off the hands, feet, and the like, cutting through the vital points, like a king abandoning [his kingdom], gradually withdraws and merges into fire (<s>tejas</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 6,8.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7]

children.text:
sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,8.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this subtle essence — all this has That as its Self. That is the Truth. That is the Self (<s>Ātman</s>). That thou art (<s>tat tvam asi</s>), O <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One.' 'So be it, dear boy,' he said. (ChUp 6.8.7)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,8.7 yasmānmūlādutthāya dehamāviśati jīvaḥ sa yaḥ sadākhya eṣa ukto 'ṇimāṇubhāvo jagato mūlamaitadātmyametatsadātmā yasya sarvasya tadetadātma tasya bhāva aitadātmyam /
etena sadākhyenā'tmanā'tmavatsarvamidaṃ jagat /
nānyo 'styasyā'tmā saṃsārī /
"nānyadato 'ti śrotṛ"ityādiśrutyantarāt /
yena cā'tmanā'tmavatsarvamidaṃ jagattadeva sadākhyaṃ kāraṇaṃ satyaṃ paramārthasat /
ataḥ sa evā'tmā jagataḥ pratyaksvarūpaṃ satattvaṃ yāthātmyam /
ātmaśabdasya nirupapadasya pratyagātmani gavādiśabdavannirūḍhatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self), when used without qualification, is established in common usage as referring to the inner Self, just as the word 'cow' [refers to the animal] — [therefore it means the inner Self here].

children.text: atastatsattvamasīti he śvetaketo ityevaṃ pratyāyitaḥ putra āha-bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatu yadbhavaduktaṃ tatsandigdhaṃ mamāhanyahani sarvāḥ prajāḥ suṣupte satsaṃpadyanta ityetadyena tatsaṃpadya na viduḥ satsampannā vayamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore — '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art), O <s>Śvetaketu</s> — thus informed, the son says: 'Let the Blessed One instruct me further.' 'What you have said remains doubtful to me — that every day all beings merge into Being in deep sleep, and yet, having merged, they do not know "we have merged into Being."'

children.text: ato dṛṣṭontena māṃ pratyāyayatvityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, convince me through an illustration' — this is the meaning.

children.text: evamuktastathāstu somyeti hovāca pitā //7//
children.translated_text: Being told thus, the father said: 'So be it, dear boy.' (7)

[Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.8.7:] The <s>jīva</s> rises from that root and enters a body. That which is called Being (<s>Sat</s>), this subtle essence (<s>aṇimā</s>) — the root of the world — '<s>aitadātmya</s>' means: that whose Self is this Being — its quality is <s>aitadātmya</s> (having-this-as-its-Self). By this Self called Being, all this world is ensouled. There is no other Self of it — the transmigrating one. From the other <s>śruti</s>: 'There is no other seer than this' and so forth. And that Self by which all this world is ensouled — that very thing called Being, the cause, is the Truth (<s>Satya</s>), the ultimately real.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth section of the sixth chapter of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad.

children.text: START ChUp 6,9.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.9.1]

children.text: yathā somya madhu madhukṛto nistiṣṭhanti nānātyayānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ rasān samavahāram ekatāṃ rasaṃ gamayanti || ChUp_6,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as, dear boy, bees prepare honey by collecting the juices of various trees and reducing them to one essence—' (ChUp 6.9.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,9.1 yatpṛcchasyahanyahani satsaṃpadya na viduḥ satsaṃpannāḥ sma iti tatkasmādityatra śṛṇu dṛṣṭāntam /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.9.1:] As to what you ask — 'Why do they not know, having merged into Being every day, that they have merged into Being?' — hear this illustration.

children.text: yathā loke he somya madhukṛto madhu kurvantīti madhukṛto madhukaramakṣikā madhu nistiṣṭhanti madhu niṣpādayanti tatparāḥ santaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, dear boy, the honey-makers — the bees (<s>madhukara-makṣikā</s>), called honey-makers because they make honey — prepare honey, being devoted to that [task].

children.text: katham?nānātyayānāṃ nānāgatīnāṃ nānādikkānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ rasānsamavahāraṃ samāhṛtyaikatāmekabhāvaṃ madhutvena rasāngamayanti madhutvamāpādayanti //1 //
children.translated_text: How? By collecting the juices of various trees — trees of different kinds, of different directions — and reducing them to oneness, to the state of being one, as honey, they bring the juices to the state of honey. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 6,9.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.9.2]

children.text:
te yathā tatra na vivekaṃ labhante 'muṣyāhaṃ vṛkṣasya raso 'smy amuṣyāhaṃ vṛkṣasya raso 'smīti |
evam eva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sati saṃpadya na viduḥ sati saṃpadyāmaha iti || ChUp_6,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as those [juices] in that [honey] cannot distinguish themselves [saying] "I am the juice of this tree," "I am the juice of that tree" — even so, dear boy, all these beings, having merged into Being, do not know "We have merged into Being."' (ChUp 6.9.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,9.2 te rasā yathā madhutvenaikatāṃ gatāstatra madhuni vivekaṃ na labhante /
katham, amuṣyāhamāmrasya panasasya vā vṛkṣasya raso 'smīti /
children.translated_text: How so? [They do not say] 'I am the juice of this mango tree or that jackfruit tree.'

children.text: yathā hi loke bahūnāṃ cetanāvatāṃ sametānāṃ prāṇināṃ vivekalābho bhavatyamuṣyāhaṃ putro 'muṣyāhaṃ naptāsmīti /
children.translated_text: For just as in the world, many sentient living beings, when gathered together, attain distinction — [saying] 'I am the son of so-and-so, I am the grandson of so-and-so' —

children.text: te ca labdhavivekāḥ santo na saṃkīryante na tathehānekaprakāravṛkṣarasānāmapi madhurāmlatiktakaṭukādīnāṃ madhutvenaikatāṃ gatānāṃ madhurādibhāvena viveko gṛhyata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: and having attained distinction, they are not confused — but not so here: among the juices of many kinds of trees — sweet, sour, bitter, pungent, and so forth — when they have become one as honey, no distinction as sweet and so forth is perceived — this is the purport.

children.text: yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭānta ityevameva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajā ahanyahani sati saṃpadya suṣuptakāle maraṇapralayayośca na vidurna vijānīyuḥ sati saṃpadyāmaha iti saṃpannā iti vā //2 //
children.translated_text: As is this illustration, even so, dear boy, all these beings, every day merging into Being in deep sleep — and also at death and universal dissolution — do not know, do not perceive: 'We have merged into Being,' or 'We have merged.' (2)
[Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.9.2:] Those juices, having become one as honey, do not in that honey attain distinction.

children.text: START ChUp 6,9.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.9.3]

children.text: ta iha vyaghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yad yad bhavanti tad ābhavanti || ChUp_6,9.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Whatever they become here — whether tiger, lion, wolf, boar, worm, moth, gadfly, or mosquito — they become that again.' (ChUp 6.9.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,9.3 yasmāccaivamātmanaḥ sadrūpatāmajñātvaiva satsaṃpadyante /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 6.9.3:] Because this is so — without knowing their true nature as Being — they merge into Being.

children.text: atasta iha loke yatkarmanimittāṃ yāṃ yāṃ jātiṃ pratipannā āsurvyāghrādīnāṃ vyāghro 'haṃ siṃho 'hamityevaṃ te tatkarmajñānavāsanāṅkitāḥ santaḥ satpraviṣṭā api tadbhāvenaiva punarābhavanti punaḥ sata āgatya vyāghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yadyatpūrvamiha loke bhavanti vabhūvurityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, those [beings] in this world — whatever species they assumed due to their past actions, such as tiger and the like — 'I am a tiger,' 'I am a lion' — thus, being stamped with the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of their past actions and knowledge, even after entering <s>Sat</s> (Being), they come into existence again in that very form. Coming again from Being, they become a tiger, or a lion, or a wolf, or a boar, or an insect, or a moth, or a gadfly, or a mosquito — whatever they were before in this world — that is the meaning.

children.text: tadeva punarāgatya bhavanti yugasahasrakoṭyantaritāpi saṃsāriṇo jantoryā purā bhāvitā vāsanā sā na naśyatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Coming back again, they become that very [form] — the meaning is that even after billions of aeons, the impressions formerly cultivated by a transmigrating being do not perish.

children.text: "yathāprajñaṃ hi saṃbhavāḥ"iti śruttyantarāt //3 //
children.translated_text: Because of another <s>śruti</s>: 'For births are according to one's understanding.' (3)

children.text: START ChUp 6,9.4

sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,9.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this subtle essence — all this has that as its Self. That is the Truth. That is the Self. That thou art, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One.' 'So be it, dear one,' he said. (ChUp 6.9.4)
[Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.9.4]

children.text: ChUpBh_6,9.4 tāḥ prajā yasminpraviśya punarāvirbhavanti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.9.4:] Those beings, entering into which they come forth again —

children.text: ye tvito 'nye satsatyātmābhisaṃdhā yamaṇubhāvaṃ sadātmānaṃ praviśya nā'vartante sa ya eṣo 'ṇimetyādi vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: But those others who, with the resolve directed toward <s>Sat</s> (Being), the true Self, entering into that subtle state of Being as their Self, do not return — 'That which is this subtle essence' and so forth has been explained.

children.text: yathā loke svakīye gṛhe supta utthāya grāmāntaraṃ gato jānāti svagṛhādāgato 'smītyevaṃ sata āgato 'smīti ca jantūnāṃ kasmādvijñānaṃ na bhavatīti bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatvityuktastathā sobhyeti hovāca pitā //4//
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, one who has slept in one's own house, upon waking and going to another village, knows 'I have come from my own house' — why then do beings not have the knowledge 'We have come from Being'? — 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One' — thus addressed, 'So be it, dear one,' the father said. (4)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth section of the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,10.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.10.1]

children.text:
imāḥ somya nadyaḥ purastāt prācyaḥ syandante paścāt pratīcyaḥ |
tāḥ samudrāt samudram evāpiyanti |
sa samudra eva bhavati |
tā yathā tatra na vidur iyam aham asmīyam aham asmīti || ChUp_6,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'These rivers, dear one, flow — the eastern ones toward the east, the western ones toward the west. They go from ocean to ocean. They become the ocean itself. Just as there they do not know "I am this one," "I am this one" —' (ChUp 6.10.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,10.1 śṛṇu tatra dṛṣṭāntaṃ yathā somyemā nadyo gaṅgādyāḥ purastātpūrvāṃ diśaṃ prati prācyaḥ prāgañcanāḥ syandante sravanti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.10.1:] Hear the illustration for that — just as, dear one, these rivers, such as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and others, flowing toward the east, are eastern — they flow, they stream.

children.text: paścātpratīcīṃ diśaṃ prati sindhvādyāḥ pratīcīmañcanti gacchantīti pratīcyastāḥ samudrādambhonidherjaladharairākṣiptāḥ punarvṛṣṭirūpeṇa patitā gaṅgādinadīrūpiṇyaḥ punaḥ samudramambhonidhimevāpiyanti sa samudra eva bhavati tā nadyo yathā tatra samudre samudrātmanaikatāṃ gatā na vidurna jānantīyaṃ gaṅgāhamasmīyaṃ yamunāhamasmītīyaṃ mahyahamasmīti ca //1 //
children.translated_text: Toward the west, rivers such as the <s>Sindhu</s> and others, going westward, are western. Those [rivers], drawn up from the ocean by clouds and falling again as rain, taking the form of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and other rivers, again reach the ocean. They become the ocean itself. And just as there, in the ocean, having attained oneness with the ocean, they do not know — 'I am the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' 'I am the <s>Yamunā</s>,' 'I am the <s>Mahī</s>.' (1)

children.text: START ChUp 6,10.2-3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.10.2-3]

children.text:
evam eva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sata āgamya na viduḥ sata āgacchāmaha iti |
ta iha vyāghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yad yad bhavanti tad ābhavanti || ChUp_6,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'In the same way indeed, dear one, all these beings, having come from Being, do not know "We have come from Being." Whatever they become here — whether tiger, or lion, or wolf, or boar, or insect, or moth, or gadfly, or mosquito — that they become again.' (ChUp 6.10.2)

children.text:
sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,10.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this subtle essence — all this has that as its Self. That is the Truth. That is the Self. That thou art, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One.' 'So be it, dear one,' he said. (ChUp 6.10.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,10.2,3 evameva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajā yasmātsati sampadya na vidustasmātsata āgamya na viduḥ sata āgacchāmaha āgatā iti vā /
ta iha vyāghra ityādi samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever they become here — whether tiger' and so forth — the rest is the same.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ loke jale vīcītaraṅgaphenabudādaya utthitāḥ punastadbhāvaṃ gatā vinaṣṭā iti /
children.translated_text: It is observed in the world that waves, surges, foam, bubbles, and the like, having risen from water and again returning to that state, are destroyed.

children.text: jīvāstu tatkāraṇamaṇubhāvaṃ pratyahaṃ gacchanto 'pi suṣupte maraṇapralayayośca na vinaśyantītyetat bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatu dṛṣṭāntena /
children.translated_text: But the individual selves (<s>jīvas</s>), though entering daily into that subtle state of their cause — in deep sleep, death, and dissolution — do not perish. 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One, with an illustration [for this].'

children.text: tathā somyeti hovāca pitā //2-3 //
children.translated_text: 'So be it, dear one,' the father said. (2-3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.10.2-3:] In the same way indeed, dear one, all these beings — since, having merged into Being, they do not know — therefore, having come from Being, they do not know 'We have come from Being,' or 'We have come [from it].'

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth section of the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,11.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.11.1]

children.text:
asya somya mahato vṛkṣasya yo mūle 'bhyāhanyāj jīvan sraved yo madhye 'bhyāhanyāj jīvan sraved yo 'gre 'bhyāhanyāj jīvan sravet |
sa eṣa jīvenātmanānuprabhūtaḥ pepīyamāno modamānas tiṣṭhati || ChUp_6,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of this great tree, dear one, if one were to strike at the root, it would exude sap while living; if one were to strike at the middle, it would exude sap while living; if one were to strike at the top, it would exude sap while living. Pervaded by the living Self, it stands drinking in [moisture] and rejoicing.' (ChUp 6.11.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,11.1 śṛṇu dṛṣṭāntamasya - he somya mahato 'nekaśākhādiyuktasya vṛkṣasyāsyetyagrataḥ sthitaṃ vṛkṣaṃ darśayannāha /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.11.1:] Hear the illustration — 'of this,' dear one, great tree with many branches and so forth — saying 'this,' he points to a tree standing before them.

children.text: yadi yaḥ kaścidasya mūle 'bhyāhanyātparaśvādinā sakṛdghātamātreṇa na śuṣyatīti jīvanneva bhavati tadā tasya rasaḥ sravet /
children.translated_text: If someone were to strike at the root with an axe and the like — by a single blow it does not dry up, remaining alive — then its sap would flow.

children.text: tathā yo madhye 'bhyāhanyājjīvansravettathā yo 'gre 'bhyāhanyājjīvansravetsa eṣa vṛkṣa idānīṃ jīvenā'tmanānuprabhūto 'nuvyāptaḥ pepīyamāno 'tyarthaṃ pibannudakaṃ bhaumāṃśca rasānmūlairgṛhṇanmodamāno harṣaṃ prāpnuvaṃstiṣṭhati //1//
children.translated_text: Similarly, if one were to strike at the middle, it would exude sap while living; similarly, if one were to strike at the top, it would exude sap while living. This tree now, pervaded — permeated — by the living Self, drinking abundantly — absorbing water and earthly juices through its roots — and rejoicing — experiencing delight — stands. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 6,11.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.11.2]

children.text:
asya yad ekāṃ śākhāṃ jīvo jahāty atha sā śuṣyati |
dvitīyāṃ jahāty atha sā śuṣyati |
tṛtīyāṃ jahāty atha sā śuṣyati |
sarvaṃ jahāti sarvaḥ śuṣyati || ChUp_6,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'If the life [principle] leaves one of its branches, that branch dries up. If it leaves a second, that dries up. If it leaves a third, that dries up. If it leaves the whole [tree], the whole dries up.' (ChUp 6.11.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,11.2 tasyāsya yadekāṃ śākhāṃ rogagrastāmāhatāṃ vā jīvo jahātyupasaṃharati śākhāyāṃ viprasṛtamātmāṃśam /
atha sā śuṣyati /
vāṅmanaḥprāṇakaraṇagrāmānupraviṣṭo hi jīva iti tadupasaṃhāra upasaṃhriyate /
jīvena ca prāṇayuktenāśitaṃ potaṃ ca rasatāṃ gataṃ jīvaccharīraṃ vṛkṣaṃ vardhayadrasarūpeṇa jīvasya sadbhāve liṅgaṃ bhavati /
aśitapītābhyāṃ hi dehe jīvastiṣṭhati te cāśitapīte jīvakarmānusāriṇī iti /
tasyaikāṅgavaikalyanimittaṃ karma yadopasthitaṃ bhavati tadā jīva ekāṃ śākhāṃ jahāti śākhāyā ātmānamupasaṃharati /
atha tadā sā śākhā śuṣyati /
jīvasthitinimitto raso jīvakarmākṣipto jīvopasaṃhāre na tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: The sap, whose continued presence depends on the <s>jīva</s> and is drawn by the <s>jīva's</s> <s>karma</s>, does not remain when the <s>jīva</s> withdraws.

children.text: rasāpagame ca śākhā śoṣamupaiti /
children.translated_text: And when the sap departs, the branch withers.

children.text: tathā sarvaṃ vṛkṣameva yadāyaṃ jahāti tadā sarvo 'pi vṛkṣaḥ śuṣyati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, when it leaves the entire tree, the entire tree dries up.

children.text: vṛkṣasya rasasravaṇaśoṣaṇādiliṅgājjīvavattvaṃ dṛṣṭāntaśruteśca cetanāvantaḥ sthāvarā iti bauddhakāṇādamatamacetanāḥ sthāvarā ityetadasāramiti darśitaṃ bhavati //2 //
children.translated_text: From the signs of sap-flow and drying in trees, and from the <s>śruti</s> about the illustration [stating trees have life], it is shown that plants are sentient — and the view of the Buddhists and <s>Kaṇāda's</s> followers that plants are insentient is without substance. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.11.2:] Of this [tree] — if the life [principle] leaves one branch that is diseased or struck — withdraws the portion of itself extended into that branch — then that [branch] dries up. For the <s>jīva</s> (living self) is said to have entered the assemblage of organs — speech, mind, breath, and senses. When that [self] withdraws, [these] are withdrawn. And when the <s>jīva</s> endowed with breath has consumed food and drink, which have become sap, [it] nourishes the body-tree of the <s>jīva</s> in the form of sap — this is the sign of the <s>jīva's</s> presence. For the <s>jīva</s> abides in the body through food and drink, and those food and drink follow the <s>jīva's</s> <s>karma</s>. When the <s>karma</s> that causes weakness in one limb is ready [to ripen], then the <s>jīva</s> leaves one branch — withdraws itself from the branch — then that branch dries up.

children.text: START ChUp 6,11.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.11.3]

children.text:
evam eva khalu somya viddhīti ha uvāca |
jīvāpetaṃ vāva kiledaṃ mriyate na jīvo mriyata iti |
sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,11.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Know it to be even so, dear one,' he said. 'Indeed, when abandoned by the living [self], this [body] dies — but the living self does not die. That which is this subtle essence — all this has that as its Self. That is the Truth. That is the Self. That thou art, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One.' 'So be it, dear one,' he said. (ChUp 6.11.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,11.3 yathāsminvṛkṣadṛṣṭānte darśitaṃ jīvena yukto vṛkṣo 'śuṣko rasapānādiyukto jāvatītyucyate tadapetaśca mriyata ityucyate /
evameva khalu somya viddhīti hovāca-jīvāpetaṃ jīvaviyuktaṃ vāva kiledaṃ śarīraṃ mriyate na jīvo mriyata iti kāryaśeṣe ca suptotthitasya mamedaṃ kāryaśeṣamaparisamāptamiti smṛtvā samāpanadarśanāt /
jātamātrāṇāṃ ca jantūnāṃ stanyābhilāṣayādidarśanāccātītajanmāntarānubhūtastana (nya) pānaduḥkhānubhavasmṛtirgamyate /
agnihotrādīnāṃ ca vaidikānāṃ karmaṇāmarthavattvānna jīvo mriyata iti /
children.translated_text: And because Vedic rituals such as the <s>agnihotra</s> and the rest are meaningful — [therefore] the <s>jīva</s> does not die.

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimetyādi samānam /
children.translated_text: 'That which is this subtle essence' and so forth — the same [as before].

children.text: kathaṃ punaridamatyantasthīlaṃ pṛthivyādi nāmarūpavajjagadatyantasūkṣmātsadrūpānnāmarūparah itātsato jāyata ityetaddṛṣṭāntena bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatviti /
children.translated_text: But how does this entire world of names and forms — exceedingly gross, such as earth and the like — arise from Being (<s>Sat</s>), which is exceedingly subtle, devoid of name and form? 'Please instruct me further with an illustration, Blessed One.'

children.text: tathā somyeti hovāca pitā //3//
children.translated_text: 'So be it, dear one,' the father said. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.11.3:] Just as in this tree-illustration it has been shown — a tree joined with the <s>jīva</s> is said to be living, un-dried, endowed with sap-drinking and the rest; and when that [life] has departed, it is said to die. 'Know it to be even so, dear one,' he said — 'Indeed, when abandoned by the living [self] — separated from the <s>jīva</s> — this body dies; but the living self does not die.' And in the case of remaining work [to be done], when one awakened from sleep remembers 'This work of mine remains incomplete' and sees its completion — [this shows continuity]. And from the observation in newborn creatures of a desire for the breast and the like, it is inferred that there is memory of the experience of breast-feeding and suffering from past births.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh section of the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,12.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.12.1]

children.text:
nyagrodhaphalam ata āhareti |
idaṃ bhagava iti |
bhinddhīti |
bhinnaṃ bhagava iti |
kim atra paśyasīti |
aṇvya ivemā dhānā bhagava iti |
āsām aṅgaikāṃ bhinddhīti |
bhinnā bhagava iti |
kim atra paśyasīti |
na kiṃcana bhagava iti || ChUp_6,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Bring a fruit from that <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree.' 'Here it is, Blessed One.' 'Break it.' 'It is broken, Blessed One.' 'What do you see there?' 'These extremely fine seeds, Blessed One.' 'Break one of them.' 'It is broken, Blessed One.' 'What do you see there?' 'Nothing at all, Blessed One.' (ChUp 6.12.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,12.1 yadyetatpratyakṣīkartumicchasi, ato 'smānmahato nyagrodhātphalamekamāharetyuktastathā cakāra, sa idaṃ bhagava upahṛtaṃ phalamiti darśitavantaṃ pratyāha phalaṃ bhindhīti /
bhinnamityāhetaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is broken' — said the other.

children.text: tamāha pitā kimatra paśyasītyukta āhāṇvyo 'ṇutarā ivemā dhānā bījāni paśyāmi bhagava iti /
children.translated_text: The father said to him: 'What do you see there?' — thus asked, he said: 'I see these seeds, extremely fine, smaller [than small], Blessed One.'

children.text: āsāṃ dhānānāmekāṃ dhānāmaṅga he vatsa bhindhītyukta āha bhinnā bhagava iti /
children.translated_text: 'Of these seeds, break one seed, my dear child' — thus told, he said: 'It is broken, Blessed One.'

children.text: yadi bhinnā dhānā tasyāṃ bhinnāyāṃ kiṃ paśyasītyukta āha na kiñcana paśyāmi bhagava iti //1 //
children.translated_text: 'If the seed is broken, in that broken seed what do you see?' — thus asked, he said: 'I see nothing at all, Blessed One.' (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.12.1:] 'If you wish to perceive this directly, then bring one fruit from this great banyan tree' — thus told, he did so. He showed the brought fruit saying 'Here it is, Blessed One' — to which [the father] replied 'Break the fruit.'

children.text: START ChUp 6,12.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.12.2]

children.text:
taṃ hovāca yaṃ vai somyaitam aṇimānaṃ na nibhālayasa etasya vai somyaiṣo 'ṇimna evaṃ mahānyagrodhas tiṣṭhati |
śraddhatsva somyeti || ChUp_6,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: He said to him: 'That subtle essence which you do not perceive, dear one — from that very subtle essence this great <s>nyagrodha</s> tree stands. Have faith, dear one.' (ChUp 6.12.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,12.2 taṃ putraṃ hovāca vaṭadhānāyāṃ bhinnāyāṃ yaṃ vaṭabījāṇimānaṃ he saumyaitaṃ na nibhālayase na paśyasi /

tathāpyetasya vai kila somyaiṣa mahānnyagrodho bījasyāṇimnaḥ sūkṣmasyādṛśyamānasya kāryabhūtaḥ sthūlaśākhāskandhaphalapalāśavāṃstiṣṭhatyutpannaḥ sannuttiṣṭhatīti vocchabdo 'dhyāhāryo 'taḥ śraddhatsva somya sata evāṇimnaḥ sthūlaṃ nāmarūpādimatkāryaṃ jagadutpannamiti /
children.translated_text: nevertheless, from this very subtle essence of the seed — which is invisible — as its effect, this great banyan tree with its thick branches, trunk, fruits, and leaves stands, having arisen.' The word 'vai' is to be supplied [as emphasis]; therefore 'have faith, dear one' — [have faith] that indeed from the subtle essence of Being alone this gross world of names and forms has arisen.

children.text: yadyapi nyāyāgamābhyāṃ nirdhāritor'thastathaivetyavagamyate tathāpyatyantasūkṣmeṣvartheṣu bāhyaviṣayāsaktamanasaḥ svabhāvapravṛttasyāsatyāṃ gurutarāyāṃ śraddhāyāṃ duravagamatvaṃ syādityāha śraddhatsveti /
children.translated_text: Although the meaning has been ascertained through reasoning and scripture as being just so, nevertheless, for one whose mind is naturally inclined toward external objects, in the case of exceedingly subtle matters, without very strong faith, there would be difficulty in understanding — hence he says 'have faith.'

children.text: śraddhāyāṃ tu satyāṃ manasaḥ samādhānaṃ bubhutsiter'the bhavettataśca tadarthāvagatiḥ /
children.translated_text: But when there is faith, the mind becomes concentrated on the object one wishes to know, and from that comes the understanding of that object.

children.text: "anyatramanā abhūvam" ityādiśruteḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'My mind was elsewhere' and so forth. (2)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.12.2:] He said to his son — 'That subtle essence of the banyan seed which, O dear one, you do not perceive — you do not see — in the broken seed,

children.text: START ChUp 6,12.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.12.3]

children.text:
sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,12.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this subtle essence — all this has that as its Self. That is the Truth. That is the Self. That thou art, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One.' 'So be it, dear one,' he said. (ChUp 6.12.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,12.3 sa ya ityādyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.12.3:] 'That which' and so forth — the meaning has been stated.

children.text: yadi tatsajjagato mūlaṃ kasmānnopalabhyata ityetaddṛṣṭāntena mā bhagavānbhūya eva vijñāpayatviti /
children.translated_text: If that <s>Sat</s> (Being) is the root of the world, why is it not perceived? 'Please instruct me further with an illustration, Blessed One.'

children.text: tathā somyeti hovāca pitā //3//
children.translated_text: 'So be it, dear one,' the father said. (3)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,13.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.13.1]

children.text:
lavaṇam etad udake 'vadhāyātha mā prātar upasīdathā iti |
sa ha tathā cakāra |
taṃ hovāca |
yad doṣā lavaṇam udake 'vādhā aṅga tad āhareti |
tad dhāvamṛśya na viveda || ChUp_6,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Place this salt in water and come to me in the morning.' He did so. [The father] said to him: 'That salt which you placed in the water last night — please bring it here.' He felt around for it but could not find it. [Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.13.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_6,13.1 vidyamānamapi vastu nopalabhyate prakārāntareṇa tūpalabhyata iti śṛṇvatra dṛṣṭāntam yadi cemamarthaṃ pratyakṣo sa ha pitroktamarthaṃ pratyakṣīkartumicchaṃstathā cakāra /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 6.13.1] Even an existing thing is not perceived [by the senses], yet it can be perceived by another means — hear here an illustration of this. And if this matter is [to be made] directly perceptible — he [Śvetaketu], wishing to make directly perceptible the matter spoken by the father, did accordingly.

children.text: taṃ hovāca paredyuḥ prātarūpasīdathā upagacchethā iti /
children.translated_text: [The father] said to him the next day in the morning: 'Come to me, approach me.'

children.text: sa ha pitroktamarthaṃ pratyakṣīkartumicchaṃstathā cakāra /
children.translated_text: He [Śvetaketu], wishing to make directly perceptible the matter spoken by the father, did accordingly.

children.text: taṃ hovāca paredyuḥ prātaryallavaṃ doṣā rātrāvudake 'vādhā nikṣiptavānasyaṅga he vatsa tadāharetyuktastallavaṇamājihīrṣurha kilāvamṛśyodake na viveda na vijñātavānyathā tallavaṇaṃ, vidyamānameva sadapsu līnaṃ saṃśliṣṭamabhūtaṃ //1 //
children.translated_text: [The father] said to him the next day in the morning: 'That salt which you placed in the water last night — O dear child, bring it here.' When told thus, he wished to take out the salt, but feeling around in the water, he could not find it, could not perceive it — [because] that salt, though existing, had dissolved and merged into the water, [becoming] indistinguishable. [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 6,13.2
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.13.2]

children.text:
yathā vilīnam eva |
an;gāsyāntād ācāmeti |
katham iti |
lavaṇam iti |
madhyād ācāmeti |
katham iti |
lavaṇam iti |
antād ācāmeti |
katham iti |
lavaṇam iti |
abhiprāsyaitad atha mopasīdathā iti |
tad dha tathā cakāra |
tac chaśvat saṃvartate |
taṃ hovācātra vāva kila tat somya na nibhālayase 'traiva kileti || ChUp_6,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'As it has dissolved [and you cannot find it] — please sip from the top of it.' 'How is it?' 'Salty.' 'Sip from the middle.' 'How is it?' 'Salty.' 'Sip from the end.' 'How is it?' 'Salty.' 'Set it aside and then come to me.' He did so. It [the salt] persists always. [The father] said to him: 'Here indeed, dear boy, you do not perceive it, yet it is right here.' [Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.13.2]

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,13.2 yathā vilīnaṃ lavaṇaṃ na vettha tathāpi taccakṣuṣā sparśanena ca piṇḍarūpaṃ lavaṇamagṛhyamāṇaṃ vidyata evāpsūpalabhyate copāyāntareṇetyetatputraṃ pratyāyayitumicchannāha-aṅgāsyodakasyāntādupari gṛhītvā'cāmetyuktvā putraṃ tathākṛtavantamuvāca kathamitītara āha lavaṇaṃ svādutaḥ iti /
tathā madhyādudakasya gṛhītvā'cāmeti kathamiti lavaṇamiti /
tathāntādadhodeśādgṛhītvā'cāmeti kathamiti lavaṇamiti /
yadyevamabhiprāsya parityajyaitadudakamācamyātha mopasīdathā iti taddha tathā cakāra lavaṇaṃ parityajya pitṛsamīpamājagāmetyarthaḥ /
idaṃ vacanaṃ bravaṃstallavamaṃ tasminnevodake yanmayā rātrau kṣiptaṃ śāśvannityaṃ saṃvartate vidyamānameva satsamyagvartate /
ityevamuktavantaṃ taṃ hovāca pitā /
yathedaṃ lavaṇaṃ darśanasparśanābhyāṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhītaṃ punarudake vilīnaṃ tābhyāmagṛhyamāṇamapi vidyata evopāyāntareṇa jihvayopalabhyamānatvāt /
evamevātraivāsminneva tejobannādikārye śuṅgedehe /
vāva kiletyācāryopadeśasmaraṇapradarśanārthau /
children.translated_text: 'Here indeed' (<s>vāva kila</s>) — these particles are for the purpose of recalling the teacher's instruction.

children.text: sattejobannādiśuṅgakāramaṃ vaṭabījāṇimavadvidyamānamevendriyairnopalabhase na nibhālayase /
children.translated_text: Just as in the case of <s>sat</s> (Being), <s>tejas</s> (fire), <s>anna</s> (food), and the rest — the subtle [essence], like the subtlety of the banyan seed, exists but is not perceived by the senses — you do not perceive it.

children.text: yathātraivodake darśanasparśanābhyāmanupalabhyamānaṃ lavaṇaṃ vidyamānameva jihvayopalabdhavānasi /
children.translated_text: Just as here in this water, the salt — imperceptible through sight and touch — yet existing, you have perceived through the tongue,

children.text: evamevātraiva kila vidyamānaṃ sajjaganmūlamupāyāntareṇa lavaṇāṇimavadupalapsyasa iti vākyaśeṣaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: even so, here indeed, <s>Sat</s> (Being), the root of the world, existing [but imperceptible], you will perceive by another means, like the subtlety of salt — this is the completion of the sentence. [End of section 2.]

[Bhāṣya 6.13.2] 'As the dissolved salt you cannot find' — yet even so, the salt, not perceived as a lump through the eye and touch, does exist in the water and is perceived by another means. Wishing to make the son understand this, he said: 'Please take from the top of the water and sip' — and having told the son [who] did accordingly, he asked 'How is it?' The other replied: 'Salty in taste.'

children.text: START ChUp 6,13.3
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.13.3]

children.text:
sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,13.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this subtle essence — all this has that as its self. That is the truth. That is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). That thou art, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One.' 'So be it, dear boy,' he said. [Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.13.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_6,13.3 sa ya ityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 6.13.3] 'That which is' and so forth — the same [as before].

children.text: yadyevaṃ lavaṇāṇimavadindriyairanupalabhyamānamapi jaganmūlaṃ sadupāyāntareṇopalabdhuṃ śakyate yadupalambhātkṛtārthaḥ syāmanupalambhāccākṛtārthaḥ syāmahaṃ tasyaivopalabdhau ka upāya ityetadbhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatu dṛṣṭāntena tathā somyeti hovāca //3//
children.translated_text: If, like the subtlety of salt, the root of the world — <s>Sat</s> (Being) — though imperceptible to the senses, can be perceived by another means, and if by perceiving it one would be fulfilled, and by not perceiving it one would remain unfulfilled — then what is the means for perceiving that very [Being]? This is [the meaning of] 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One' — [requesting] by means of an illustration. 'So be it, dear boy,' he said. [End of section 3.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya trayodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the sixth <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,14.1

yathā somya puruṣaṃ gandhārebhyo 'bhinaddhākṣam ānīya taṃ tato 'tijane visṛjet |
sa yathā tatra prāṅ vodaṅ vā adharāṅ vā pratyaṅ vā pradhmāyītābhinaddhākṣa ānīto 'bhinaddhākṣo visṛṣṭaḥ || ChUp_6,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as, dear boy, someone might bring a person from the <s>Gandhāra</s> country blindfolded, and leave him in a desolate place far from habitation — and that person would cry out in every direction — east, north, south, or west — "I was brought here blindfolded! I was left here blindfolded!"' [Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.14.1]
[Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.14.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_6,14.1 yathā loke he somya puruṣaṃ yaṃ kañcidgandhārebhyo janapadebhyo 'bhinaddhākṣaṃ baddhacakṣuṣamānīya dravyahartā taskarastamabhinaddhākṣameva baddhahastamaraṇye tato 'pyatijane 'tigatajane 'tyantavigatajane deśe visṛjetsa tatra digbhramopeto yathā prāṅvā prāgañcanaḥ prāṅmukho, vetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 6.14.1] Just as in the world, dear boy — a certain person, from the <s>Gandhāra</s> country, [with] eyes blindfolded, bound-eyed — a robber who steals goods, bringing him blindfolded, with hands bound, to a forest — and even beyond that, in a place far from habitation, utterly devoid of people — would leave him. He there, confused about the directions, would [cry out] facing east, and so forth —

children.text: tathodaṅvādharāṅvā pratyaṅvā pradhmāyīta śabdaṃ kuryādvikrośet /
children.translated_text: likewise northward, southward, or westward — he would cry out (<s>pradhmāyīta</s>), make sounds, shout aloud.

children.text: abhinaddhākṣo 'haṃ gandhārebhyastaskareṇā'nīto 'bhinaddhākṣa eva visṛṣṭa iti //1 //
children.translated_text: 'I was brought from <s>Gandhāra</s> by a robber, blindfolded, and left here blindfolded' — [thus he would cry]. [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 6,14.2
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.14.2]

children.text:
tasya yathābhinahanaṃ pramucya prabrūyād etāṃ diśaṃ gandhārā etāṃ diśaṃ vrajeti |
sa grāmād grāmaṃ pṛcchan paṇḍito medhāvī gandhārān evopasaṃpadyeta |
evam evehācāryavān puruṣo veda |
tasya tāvad eva ciraṃ yāvan na vimokṣye 'tha saṃpatsya iti || ChUp_6,14.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then someone might remove his blindfold and tell him: "<s>Gandhāra</s> is in this direction; go in this direction." He, being intelligent and wise, would ask from village to village and arrive at <s>Gandhāra</s>. Even so in this world, a person who has a teacher knows. For him, the delay is only as long as he is not released [from the body]; then he will attain [<s>Brahman</s>].' [Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.14.2]

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,14.2 evaṃ vikrośatastasya yathābhinahanaṃ yathābandhanaṃ pramucya muktvā kāruṇikaḥ kaścidetāṃ diśamuttarato gandhārā etāṃ diśaṃ vrajeti prabrūyātsa evaṃ kāruṇikena bandhanānmokṣito grāmādgrāmāntaraṃ pṛcchanpaṇḍita upadeśavānmedhāvo paropadiṣṭagrāmapraveśamārgāvadhāraṇasamarthaḥ sangandhārānevopasampadyeta netaro mūḍhamatirdeśāntaradarśanatṛḍvā /
yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto varṇitaḥ svaviṣayebhyo gandhārebhyaḥ puruṣastaskarairabhinaddhākṣo 'viveko diṅmūḍho 'śanāyāpipāsādimānvyāghrataskarādyanekabhayānatharvrātayutamaraṇyaṃ praveśito duḥkhārto vikrośanbandhanebhyo mumukṣustiṣṭhati sa kathañcideva kāruṇikena kenacinmokṣitaḥ svadeśāngandhārānevā'panno nirvṛtaḥ sukhyabhūt /
