evameva sato jagadātmanaḥ svarūpāttejovannādimayaṃ dehāraṇyaṃ vātapittakapharudhiramedomāṃsāsthimajjāśukrakṛmimūtrapurīṣavacchītoṣṇādyanekadvandvasukhaduḥkhavaccedaṃ mohapaṭābhinaddhākṣo bhāryāputramitrapaśubandhvādidṛṣṭādṛṣṭānekaviṣayatṛṣṇāpāśitaḥ puṇyāpuṇyāditaskaraiḥ praveśito"'hamamuṣya putro mamaite bāndhavāḥ sukhyahaṃ duḥkhī mūḍhaḥ paṇḍito dhārmiko bandhumāñjāto mṛto jīrṇaḥ pāpī putro me mṛto dhanaṃ me naṣṭaṃ hā hato 'smi kathaṃ jāviṣyāmi kā me gatiḥ kiṃ me trāṇam" ityevamanekaśatasahasrānarthajālavānvikrośankathañcideva puṇyātiśayātparamakāruṇikaṃ kañcitsadbrahmātmavidaṃ vimuktabandhanaṃ brahmiṣṭhaṃ yadā'sādayati tena ca brahmavidā kāruṇyāddarśitasaṃsāraviṣayadoṣadarśanamārgo viraktaḥ saṃsāraviṣayebhyo nāsi tvaṃ saṃsāryamuṣya putratvādidharmavānkiṃ tarhi sadyattattvamasītyavidyāmohapaṭābhinahanānmokṣito gandhārapuruṣavacca svaṃ sadātmānamupasampadya sukhī nirvṛtaḥ syādityetamevārthamāhā'cāryavānpuruṣo vedeti tasyāsyaivamācāryavato muktāvidyābhinahanasya tāvadeva tāvāneva kālaściraṃ kṣepaḥ sadātmasvarūpasampatteriti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
kiyānkālaściramityucyate yāvanna vimokṣye na vimokṣyata ityetatpuruṣavyatyanena /
sāmarthyāt /
yena karmaṇā śarīramārabdhaṃ tasyopabhogena yenāthaśabda ānantaryārthaḥ syāt /
nanu yathā sadvijñānāntarameva dehapātaḥ satsampattiśca na bhavati karmaśeṣavaśāttathāpravṛttaphalāni prāgjñānotpatterjanmāntarasañcitānyapi karmāṇi santīti tatphalopabhogārthaṃ patite 'smiñśarīrāntaramārabdhavyam /
utpanne ca jñāne yāvajjīvaṃ vihitāni pratiṣiddhāni vā karmāṇi karotyeveti tatphalopabhogārthaṃ cāvaśyaṃ śarīrāntaramārabdhavyaṃ tataśca karmāṇi tataḥ śarīrāntaramiti jñānārthakyaṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavattvāt /
atha jñānavataḥ kṣīyante karmāṇi tadā jñānaprāptisamakālameva jñānasya satsampattihetutvānmokṣaḥ syāditi śarīrapātaḥ syāt /
tathācā'cāryābhāva "ityācāryavānpuruṣo vede"tyācāryavattvānupapattirjñānānmokṣābhāvaprasaṅgaśca /
deśāntaraprāptyupāyajñānavadanaikāntikaphalatvaṃ vā jñānasya /
na /
karmaṇāṃ pravṛttāpravṛttaphalavattvaviśeṣopapatteḥ /
yaduktamapravṛttaphalānāṃ karmamāṃ dhruvaphalavattvādbrahmavidaḥ śarīre patite śarīrāntaramārabdhavyamapravṛttakarmaphalopabhogātharmityetadasat /
viduṣa"stasya tāvadeva ciram" iti śruteḥ prāmāṇyāt /
nanu"puṇyo vai pumyena karmaṇābhavati"ityādiśruterapi prāmāṇyameva /
tasyamevam /
tathāpi pravṛttaphalānāmapravṛttaphalānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ viśeṣo 'sti /
katham /
yāni pravṛttaphalāni karmāṇi yairvidvaccharīramārabdhaṃ teṣāmupabhogenaiva kṣayaḥ /
yathā'rahdhavegasya lakṣyamukteṣvādervegakṣayādeva sthitirna tu lakṣyavedhasamakālameva prayojanaṃ nāstīti tadvat /
anyāni tvapravṛttaphalānīha prāgjñānotpatterūrdhvaṃ ca kṛtāni vā kriyamāṇāni vātītajanmāntarakṛtāni vāpravṛttaphalāni jñānena dahyante prāyaścitteneva /
"kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi"iti cā'tharvaṇe /
ato brahmavido jīvanādiprayojanābhāve 'pi pravṛttaphalānāṃ karmaṇāmavaśyameva phalopabhogaḥ syāditi mukteṣuvattasya tāvadeva ciramiti yuktamevoktamiti yathoktadoṣacodanānupapattiḥ jñānotpatterūrdhvaṃ ca brahmavidaḥ karmābhāvamavocāma"brahmasaṃstho 'mṛtatvametī"tyatra /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 6.14.2] For him, crying out thus — some compassionate person might remove his blindfold, free him from his bonds, and tell him: '<s>Gandhāra</s> is in this direction, to the north; go in this direction.' He, thus freed from bondage by that compassionate person, asking from village to village, being learned (<s>paṇḍita</s>) — that is, possessing instruction — and wise (<s>medhāvī</s>) — that is, capable of ascertaining the path to enter the village indicated by another — [would arrive at] <s>Gandhāra</s>.

children.text: tacca smartumarhasi //2 //
children.translated_text: And this you should remember. [End of section 2.]

children.text: START ChUp 6,14.3
children.translated_text: [Start of Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.14.3]

children.text:
sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,14.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this subtle essence — all this has that as its self. That is the truth. That is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). That thou art, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One.' 'So be it, dear boy,' he said. [Chāndogyopaniṣad 6.14.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_6,14.3 sa ya ityādyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: [Bhāṣya 6.14.3] 'That which is' and so forth — the meaning has been stated [before].

children.text: ācāryavānvidvānyena krameṇa satsampadyate taṃ kramaṃ dṛṣṭāntena bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatviti /
children.translated_text: One who has a teacher (<s>ācāryavān</s>) — one who is learned — the process by which he attains <s>Sat</s> (Being) — 'Please instruct me further, Blessed One, about that process by means of an illustration.'

children.text: tathā somyeti hovāca //3//
children.translated_text: 'So be it, dear boy,' he said. [End of section 3.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya caturdaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (section) of the sixth <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,15.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.15.1

children.text:
puruṣaṃ somyotopatāpinaṃ jñātayaḥ paryupāsate jānāsi māṃ jānāsi mām iti |
tasya yāvan na vāṅ manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ tāvaj jānāti || ChUp_6,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Dear boy, when a person is afflicted [with illness], his relatives sit around him [asking]: "Do you know me? Do you know me?" As long as his speech has not merged into the mind, the mind into <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), <s>prāṇa</s> into fire (<s>tejas</s>), and fire into the supreme deity — so long he knows.' (<s>ChUp</s> 6.15.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,15.1 puruṣaṃ he somyotopatāpinaṃ jvarādyupatāpavantaṃ jñātayo bāndhavāḥ parivāryopāsate mumūrṣuṃ jānāsi māṃ tava pitaraṃ putraṃ bhrātaraṃ veti pṛcchantastasya mumūrṣoryāvanna vāṅmanasi sampadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇastejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāmityetaduktartham //1 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.15.1:] 'Dear boy, when a person afflicted — suffering from fever and the like — his relatives, his kinsmen, sit around him as he is about to die, asking "Do you know me — your father, son, brother, and so on?" — as long as, of that dying person, his speech has not merged into the mind, the mind into <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> into fire, fire into the supreme deity' — this has the same meaning as stated before. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 6,15.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.15.2

children.text: atha yadāsya vāṅ manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām atha na jānāti || ChUp_6,15.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'But when his speech merges into the mind, the mind into <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> into fire, and fire into the supreme deity — then he does not know.' (<s>ChUp</s> 6.15.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,15.2 saṃsāriṇo yo maraṇakramaḥ sa evāyaṃ viduṣo 'pi satsampattikrama ityetadāha parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ tejasi sampanne 'tha na jānāti /
avidvāṃstu sata utthāya prāgbhāvitaṃ vyāghrādibhāvaṃ devamanuṣyādibhāvaṃ vā viśati /
vidvāṃstu śāsrācāryopadeśajanitajñānadīpaprakāśitaṃ sadbrahmātmānaṃ praviśya nā'vartata ityeṣa satsampattikramaḥ /
anye tu mūrdhanyayā nāḍyotkramyā'dityādidvāreṇa sadgacchantītyāhustadasat /
deśakālanimittaphalābhisandhānena gamanadarśanāt /
na hi sadātmaikatvadarśinaḥ satyābhisandhasya deśakālanimittaphalādyanṛtābhisandhirupapadyate /
virodhāt /
children.translated_text: because of [their] contradiction.

children.text: avidyākāmakarmaṇāṃ ca gamananimittānāṃ sadvijñānahutāśanavipluṣṭatvādgamanānupapattireva /
children.translated_text: And since <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire (<s>kāma</s>), and <s>karma</s> (action) — which are the causes of going — have been consumed by the fire of the knowledge of <s>Sat</s>, going itself is impossible.

children.text: "paryāptakāmasya kṛtātmanastivahaiva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ"ityādyātharvaṇe /
children.translated_text: 'For one whose desires are fulfilled, who has attained the Self — all desires dissolve right here' — thus in the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad).

children.text: nadīsamudradṛṣṭāntaśruteśca //2 //
children.translated_text: And because of the <s>śruti</s> illustration of rivers and the ocean. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.15.2:] The sequence of death that belongs to the transmigrating soul (<s>saṃsārin</s>) is the very same sequence of merging into <s>Sat</s> (<s>satsampatti</s>) even for the knower — this is what is stated: when fire has merged into the supreme deity, then he does not know. But the ignorant person, having risen from <s>Sat</s>, enters into a previously conditioned state — the condition of a tiger and such, or the condition of a god, human, and so on. The knower, however, having entered into <s>Sat</s>, the <s>Brahman</s>, the Self — illuminated by the light of knowledge born from the instruction of scripture and teacher — does not return. This is the sequence of merging into <s>Sat</s>. Others, however, say that [the knower] departs through the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) at the crown of the head and reaches <s>Sat</s> through the gateway of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) and such — but that is incorrect. Because [such] going is observed [only] through the intention directed toward place, time, cause, and result. For one who sees the oneness of <s>Sat</s> as the Self, who is truthful in his resolve, the untruthful intention directed toward place, time, cause, result, and the like is not possible,

children.text: START ChUp 6,15.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.15.3

children.text:
sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti |
tathā somyeti hovāca || ChUp_6,15.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is this finest essence — all this has that as its Self. That is the truth (<s>Satya</s>). That is the Self (<s>Ātman</s>). That you are, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, revered sir.' 'So be it, dear boy,' he said.' (<s>ChUp</s> 6.15.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,15.3 sa ya ityādi samānam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.15.3:] 'That which is' — and so on — is the same [as before].

children.text: yadi mariṣyato mumukṣataśca tulyā satsampattistatra vidvānsatsampanno nā'vartata āvartate tvavidvānityatra kāraṇaṃ dṛṣṭāntena bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatviti tathā somyeti hovāca //3//
children.translated_text: If the merging into <s>Sat</s> (<s>satsampatti</s>) is the same for the dying person and the one seeking liberation, then the knower, having merged into <s>Sat</s>, does not return —

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya pañcadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth section of the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 6,16.1
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.16.1

children.text:
puruṣaṃ somyota hastagṛhītam ānayanti |
apahārṣīt steyam akārṣīt paraśum asmai tapateti |
sa yadi tasya kartā bhavati tata evānṛtam ātmānaṃ kurute |
so 'nṛtābhisaṃdho 'nṛtenātmānam antardhāya paraśuṃ taptaṃ pratigṛhṇāti |
sa dahyate |
atha hanyate || ChUp_6,16.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Dear boy, they bring a person seized by the hand [as a suspect]: "He has stolen, he has committed theft — heat the axe for him."' (<s>ChUp</s> 6.16.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,16.1 śṛṇu yathā somya puruṣaṃ cauryakarmaṇi sandihyamānaṃ nigrahāya parīkṣaṇāya votāpi hastagṛhītaṃ baddhahastamānayanti rājapuruṣāḥ /
kiṃ kṛtavānayamiti pṛṣṭāścā'hurapahārśīddhanamasyāyam /
te cā'huḥ kimapaharaṇamātrema bandhanamarhati /
anyathā datte 'pi dhane bandhanaprasaṅgādityuktāḥ punarāhuḥ steyamakārṣīttauryeṇa dhanamapahārṣīditi /
teṣvevaṃ vadatsvitaro 'pahnate nāhaṃ tatkarteti /
children.translated_text: 'When they speak thus, the other denies it: "I did not do that."'

children.text: (te cā'huḥ sandihyamānaṃ steyamakārṣīstvamasya dhanasyeti) /
children.translated_text: '(And they say to the suspected one: "You have committed theft — this wealth [was stolen by you].")'

children.text: tasmiṃścāpahnavāne āhuḥ paraśumasmai tapateti śodhayatvātmānamiti /
children.translated_text: 'And when he denies it, they say: "Heat the axe for him — let him purify himself."'

children.text: sa yadi tasya stainyasya kartā bavati bahiścāpahnate sa evaṃbhūtastata evānṛtamanyathābhūtaṃ santamanyathā'mānaṃ kurute sa tathānṛtābhisandho 'nṛtenā'tmānamantardhāya vyavahitaṃ kṛtvā paraśuṃ taptaṃ mohātpratigṛhrāti sa dahyate 'tha hanyate rājapuruṣaiḥ svakṛtenānṛtābhisandhidoṣeṇa //1 //
children.translated_text: 'If he is indeed the doer of that theft and yet denies it outwardly, such a person, being false — he makes himself covered by untruth (<s>anṛta</s>) from that very [act of denial] —'
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.16.1:] 'Listen, dear boy — when a person suspected of theft is brought by others for punishment, seized by the hand —'

children.text: START ChUp 6,16.2
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.16.2

children.text:
atha yadi tasyākartā bhavati |
tata eva satyam ātmānaṃ kurute |
sa satyābhisandhaḥ satyenātmānam antardhāya paraśuṃ taptaṃ pratigṛhṇāti |
sa na dahyate |
atha mucyate || ChUp_6,16.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'But if he is not the doer of that [theft], then by that very [truthfulness] he makes himself truth. He, being truthfully resolved, grasps the heated axe — he is not burnt and is released.' (<s>ChUp</s> 6.16.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_6,16.2 atha yadi tasya karmaṇo 'kartā bhavati tata eva satyamātmānaṃ kurute sa satyena tayā stainyākartṛtayā'tmānamantardhāya paraśuṃ taptaṃ pratigṛhṇāti sa satyābhisandhaḥ sanna dahyate satyavyavadhānādatha mucyate ca mṛṣābhiyoktṛbhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.16.2:] But if he is not the doer of that action, then by that very [truthfulness] he makes himself truth — he covers himself with truth.

children.text: taptaparaśuhastatalasaṃyogasya tulyatve 'pi steyakartrakartroranṛtābhisandho dahyate na tu satyābhisandhaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: Although the contact of the palm of the hand with the heated axe is the same [in both cases], for the doer and non-doer of theft — the one who is resolved in untruth is burnt,

children.text: START ChUp 6,16.3
children.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.16.3

children.text:
sa yathā tatra nādāhyeta |
etad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam |
tat satyam |
sa ātmā |
tat tvam asi śvetaketo iti |
tad dhāsya vijajñāv iti vijajñāv iti || ChUp_6,16.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as in that case he is not burnt — all this has that as its Self. That is the truth. That is the Self. That you are, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' 'Please instruct me further, revered sir.' 'So be it, dear boy,' he said.' (<s>ChUp</s> 6.16.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_6,16.3 sa yathā satyābhisandhastaptaparaśugrahaṇakarmaṇi satyavyavahitahastatalatvānnādāhyeta na dahyetetyetadevaṃ sadbrahmasatyābhisandhītarayoḥ śarīrapātakāle ca tulyāyāṃ satsampattau vidvānsatsampadya na punarvyāghradevādidehagrahaṇāyā'vartate /
avidvāṃstu vikārānṛtābhisandhaḥ punarvyāghrādibhāvaṃ devatādibhāvaṃ vā yathākarma yathāśrutaṃ pratipadyate /
yadātmābhisandhyanabhisandhikṛte mokṣabandhane yacca mūlaṃ jagato yadāyatanā yatpratiṣṭhāśca sarvāḥ prajā yadātmakaṃ ca sarvaṃ yaccājamamṛtamabhayaṃ śivamadvitīyaṃ tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tavātastattvamasi he śvetaketo ityuktārthamasakṛdvākyam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 6.16.3:] Just as the one who is truthfully resolved, in the act of grasping the heated axe — being covered by truth, his hands [are protected] —

children.text:
kaḥ punarasau śvetaketustvaṃśabdārthaḥ /
yo 'haṃ śvetaketuruddālakasya putra iti vedā'tmānamādeśaṃ śrutvā matvā vijñāya cāśrutamamatamavijñātaṃ vijñātuṃ pitaraṃ papraccha kathaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sa ādeśo bavatīti sa eṣo 'dhikṛtaḥ śrotā mantā vijñātā tejobannamayaṃ kāryakāraṇasaṅghātaṃ praviṣṭā paraiva devatā nāmasvarūpavyākaraṇāyā'darśa iva puruṣaḥ sūryāduriva jalādau pratibodhitastattvamasītidṛṣṭāntairhetubhiśca tatpiturasya ha kiloktaṃ sadevāhamasmīti vijajñau vijñātavān /
dvirvacanamadhyāyaparisamāptyartham /
kiṃ punaratra ṣaṣṭhe vākyapramāṇena janitaṃ phalam?ātmani kartṛtvabhoktṛtvayoradhikṛtatvavijñānanivṛttistasya phalaṃ yaṃ vayamavocāma tvaṃśabdavācyamarthaṃ śrotuṃ mantuṃ cādhikṛtamavijñātavijñānaphalārtham /
prākcaitasmādvijñānādahamevaṃ kariṣyāmyagnihotrādīni karmāṇyahamatrādhikṛtaḥ /
eṣāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ phalamihāmutra ca bhokṣye kṛteṣu vā karmasu kṛtakartavyaḥ syāmityevaṃ kartṛtvabhoktṛtvayoradhikṛto 'smītyātmani yadvijñānamabhūttattasya yatsajjagato mūlamekamevādvitīyaṃ tattvamasītyanena vākyena pratibuddhasya nivartate /
virodhāt /
na hyekasminnadvitīya ātmanyayamahamasmīti vijñāte mamedamanyadanena kartavyamidaṃ kṛtvāsya phalaṃ bhokṣya iti vā bhedavijñānamupapadyate /
tasmātsatsatyādvitīyātmavijñāne vikārānṛtajīvātmavijñānaṃ nivartata iti yuktam /
nanu tattvamasītyatra tvaṃśabdavācyer'the sadbuddhirādhitsyate yathā'dityamana ādiṣu brahmādibuddhiḥ /
yathā ca loke pratimādiṣu viṣṇvādibuddhistadvannatu sadeva tvamiti, yadi sadeva śvetaketuḥ syātkathamātmānaṃ na vijānīyādyena tasmai tattvamasītyupadiśyate /
na /
ādityādivākyavailakṣaṇyāt /
ādityo brahmetyādāvitiśabdavyavadhānānna sākṣādbrahmatvaṃ gamyate /
rūpādimattvāccā'dityādīnāmākāśamanasoścetiśabdavyavadhānādevābrahmatvamiha tu sata eveha praveśaṃ darśayitvā tattvamasīti niraṅkuśaṃ sadātmabhāvamupadiśati /
nanu parākramādiguṇaḥ siṃho 'si tvamitivattattvamasīti syāt /
na /
mṛdādivatsadekamevādvitīyaṃ satyamityupadeśāt /
na copacāravijñānāttasya tāvadeva ciramiti satsampattirūpadiśyeta /
mṛṣātvādupacāravijñānasya /
tvamindro 'si yama itivat /
nāpi stutiranupāsyatvācchvetaketoḥ /
nāpi sacchvetaketutvopadeśena stūyeta /
na hi rājā dāsastvamiti stutyaḥ syāt /
nāpi sataḥ sarvātmana ekadeśanirodho yuktastattvamasīti deśādhipateriva grāmādhyakṣastvamiti /
na cānyā gatiriha sadātmatvopadeśādarthāntarabhūtā sambhavati /
nanu sadasmītibuddhimātramiha kartavyatayā codyate na tvajñātaṃ sadasīti jñāpyata iti cet /
nanvasminpakṣe 'pyaśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavatītyādyanupapannam /
na, sadasmītibuddhividheḥ stutyarthatvāt /
na, ācāryavānpuruṣo veda tasya tāvadeva ciramityupadeśāt /
yadi hi sadasmīti buddhimātraṃ kartavyatayā vidhīyate na tu tvaṃśabdavācyasya sadrūpatvameva tadā nā'cāryavānvedeti jñānopāyopadeśo vācyaḥ syāt /
yathāgnihotraṃ juhuyādityevamādiṣvarthaprāptamevā'cāryavattvamiti tadvat /
tasya tāvadeva ciramiti ca kṣepakaraṇaṃ na yuktaṃ syāt /
sadātmatattve 'vijñāte 'pi sakṛdbuddhimātrakaraṇe mokṣaprasaṅgāt /
na ca tattvamasītyukte nāhaṃ saditipramāṇavākyajanitā buddhīrnivartayituṃ śakyā notpanneti vā śakyaṃ vaktum /
sarvopaniṣadvākyānāṃ tatparatayaivopakṣayāt /
yathāgnihotrādividhijanitāgnihotrādikartavyatābuddhīnāmatathārthatvamanutpannatvaṃ vā na śakyate vaktuṃ tadvat /
yattūktaṃ sadātmā sannātmānaṃ kathaṃ na jānīyāditi /
nāsau doṣaḥ /
kāryakaraṇasaṅghātavyatirikto 'haṃ jīvaḥ kartā bhoktetyapi svabhāvataḥ prāṇināṃ vijñānādarśanātkisu tasya sadātmavijñānam /
kathamevaṃ vyatiriktavijñāne sati teṣāṃ kartṛtvādivijñānaṃ sambhavati dṛśyate ca /
tadvattasyāpi dehādiṣvātmabuddhitvānna syātsadātmavijñānam /
tasmādvikārānṛtādhikṛtajīvātmavijñānanivartakamevedaṃ vākyaṃ tattvamasīti siddhamiti //3 // //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this statement '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) is established as that which removes the false knowledge of the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) that is superimposed upon the [true] modifications [of Being]. (3)
But who is this <s>Śvetaketu</s> that is the referent of the word 'you'? [It is] the one who [thinks] 'I am <s>Śvetaketu</s>, the son of <s>Uddālaka</s>' —

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya ṣoḍaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth section of the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadbrāhmaṇe ṣaṣṭhodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: atha saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the seventh chapter.

children.text: START ChUp 7,1.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.1.1]

children.text:
adhīhi bhagava iti hopasasāda sanatkumāraṃ nāradaḥ |
taṃ hovāca yad vettha tena mopasīda |
tatas ta ūrdhvaṃ vakṣyāmīti |
sa hovāca || ChUp_7,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Teach me, Blessed One,' said <s>Nārada</s>, approaching <s>Sanatkumāra</s>. He said to him: 'Approach me with what you already know. Then I shall tell you what is beyond that.' He [<s>Nārada</s>] said: (ChUp 7.1.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,1.1
paramārthantattvopadeśapradhānaparaḥ ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ sadātmaikatvanirṇayaparatayaivopayuktaḥ /
na sator'vāgvikāralakṣaṇāni tattvāni nirdiṣṭānītyatastāni nāmādīni prāṇāntāni krameṇa nirdiśya taddvāreṇāpi bhūmākhyaṃ niratiśayaṃ tattvaṃ nirdekṣyāmīti śākhācandradarśanavaditīnaṃ saptamaṃ prapāṭhakamārabhate /
anirdiṣṭeṣu hi sator'vāktattveṣu sanmātre ca nirdiṣṭe 'nyadapyavijñātaṃ syādityāśaṅkā kasyacitsyātsā mā bhūditi vā tāni nirdidikṣati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.1.1:] The sixth chapter, whose primary purpose was the teaching of the ultimate reality, served the determination of the oneness of Being as the <s>Ātman</s>. Since the realities characterized as modifications below Being were not specified [there], [the text] now begins the seventh <s>prapāṭhaka</s> with the intention: 'I shall progressively specify those [realities] from name up to <s>prāṇa</s>, and through them also point to the unsurpassable reality called <s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite)' — like showing the moon by pointing to a branch. For if the realities below Being were not specified, and only pure Being were specified, someone might suspect that there is something else unknown — [this chapter is begun] so that such a doubt may not arise.

children.text:
athavā sopānārohaṇavatsthūlādārabhya sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣamataṃ ca buddhiviṣayaṃ jñāpayitvā tadatirikte svārājye 'bhiṣekṣyāmīti nāmādīni nirdidikṣati /
athavā nāmādyuttarottaraviśiṣṭāni tattvānyatitarāṃ ca teṣāmutkṛṣṭatamaṃ bhūmākhyaṃ tattvamiti tatstutyarthaṃ nāmādīnāṃ krameṇopanyāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, like ascending steps, beginning from the gross, [the text] intends to make known the subtle and the subtler object of intellect, and then to anoint [the student] in sovereignty over what transcends even that — therefore it intends to specify name and the rest. Or, the sequential presentation of name and the rest is for the purpose of praising the reality called <s>Bhūman</s> — since name and the rest are realities progressively distinguished, and <s>Bhūman</s> is the most exalted of them all.

children.text:
ākhyāyikā tu paravidyāstutyarthā /
katham /
nārado devarṣiḥ kṛtakartavyaḥ sarvavidyo 'pi sannanātmajñatvācchuśocaiva kimu vaktavyamanyo 'lpavijjanturakṛtapuṇyātiśayo 'kṛtārtha iti /
athavā nānyadātmajñānānniratiśayaśreyaḥ sādhanamastītyetatpradarśanārthaṃ sanatkumāranāradākhyāyikā'rabhyate /
yena sarvavijñānasādhanaśaktisampannasyāpi nāradasya devarṣeḥ śreyo na babhūva yenottamābhijanavidyāvṛttasādhanaśaktisampattinimittābhi mānaṃ hitvā prākṛtapuruṣavatsanatkumāramupasasāda śreyaḥsādhanaprāptaye 'taḥ prakhyāpitaṃ bhavati niratiśayaprāptisādhanatvamātmavidyāyā iti /
adhīhyadhīṣva bhagavā bha vinniti kilopasasāda /
children.translated_text: 'Teach me' — '<s>adhīhi</s>' means 'instruct [me],' 'Blessed One' — 'bhagavan' — thus he approached.

children.text: adhīhi bhagava iti mantraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Teach me, Blessed One' — this is the formula [of request].

children.text: sanatkumāraṃ yogīśvaraṃ brahmiṣṭhaṃ nārada upasannavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> approached <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, the lord of yogins, the foremost knower of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: taṃ nyāyata upasannaṃ hovāca yadātmaviṣaye kiñcidvettha tena tatprakhyāpanena māmupasīdedamahaṃ jāna iti tato 'haṃ bhavato vijñānātte tubyamūrdhvaṃ vakṣyāmītyuktavati sa hovāca nāradaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: To him who had properly approached, [<s>Sanatkumāra</s>] said: 'Whatever you know regarding the <s>Ātman</s> — approach me by declaring that, [saying] "I know this." After that, beyond your knowledge, I shall tell you.' When thus addressed, <s>Nārada</s> said: (1)

The narrative, however, is for the purpose of praising the higher knowledge. How? <s>Nārada</s>, the divine sage, having fulfilled all duties and possessing all [worldly] knowledge — yet not knowing the <s>Ātman</s> — grieved. What then need be said of another being of little knowledge, without exceptional merit, and unfulfilled? Alternatively, to demonstrate that there is no means to unsurpassable good other than knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>, the narrative of <s>Sanatkumāra</s> and <s>Nārada</s> is begun. Because <s>Nārada</s>, the divine sage endowed with the power of all knowledge and all means, did not attain the good — and because, abandoning the pride born of his accomplishment in the highest birth, learning, conduct, and power of means, he approached <s>Sanatkumāra</s> like an ordinary person for the attainment of the means to the good — thereby the [text] proclaims that knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> is the means to the unsurpassable attainment.

children.text: START ChUp 7,1.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.1.2]

children.text: ṛgvedaṃ bhagavo 'dhyemi yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham itihāsapurāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ vedānāṃ vedaṃ pitryaṃ rāśiṃ daivaṃ nidhiṃ vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyāṃ brahmavidyāṃ bhūtavidyāṃ kṣatravidyāṃ nakṣatravidyāṃ sarpadevajanavidyām etad bhagavo 'dhyemi || ChUp_7,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Blessed One, I have studied the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s> as the fourth, the <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s> as the fifth, the grammar (<s>Veda</s> of the <s>Vedas</s>), the rites for the ancestors, mathematics, the science of portents, the science of treasures, logic, ethics, the science of the gods (etymology), the science of <s>Brahman</s> (phonetics, ritual procedure, meter, and exposition), the science of beings (demonology), the science of governance (archery), the science of stars (astronomy), and the science of serpents and celestial beings. This, Blessed One, I have studied.' (ChUp 7.1.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,1.2 ṛgvedaṃ bhagavo 'dhyemi smarāmi yadvettheti vijñānasya pṛṣṭatvāt /
tathā yajurvedaṃ sāmavedamātharvaṇaṃ caturthaṃ vedaṃ vedaśabdasya prakṛtatvāditihāsapurāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ vedaṃ vedānāṃ bhāratapañcamānāṃ vedaṃ vyākaraṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.1.2:] 'Blessed One, I study — I remember — the <s>Ṛgveda</s>' — because he was asked about his knowledge [with 'what you know']. Similarly the <s>Yajurveda</s>, <s>Sāmaveda</s>, <s>Atharvaveda</s> as the fourth <s>Veda</s> — the word '<s>Veda</s>' being contextually implied. <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s> as the fifth <s>Veda</s>. The '<s>Veda</s> of the <s>Vedas</s>' — grammar — that is the meaning, since the five [texts] including the <s>Bhārata</s> [are called Vedas].

children.text:
vyākaraṇena hi padādivibhāgaśa ṛgvedādayo jñāyante /
pitryaṃ śrāddhakalpam /
kāśiṃ gaṇitam /
daivamutpātajñānam /
nidhiṃ mahākālādinidhiśāstram /
vākovākyaṃ tarkaśāsram /
ekāyanaṃ nītiśāsram /
devavidyāṃ niruktam /
brahmaṇa ṛgyajuḥsāmākhyasya vidyāṃ brahmavidyāṃ śikṣākalpacchandovicitayaḥ /
bhūtavidyāṃ bhūtatantram /
kṣattravidyāṃ dhanurvedam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṣatravidyā</s>' — the science of archery (<s>Dhanurveda</s>).

children.text: nakṣatravidyāṃ jyautiṣam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nakṣatravidyā</s>' — astronomy (<s>Jyotiṣa</s>).

children.text: sarpadevajanavidyāṃ sarpavidyāṃ gāruḍaṃ devajanavidyāṃ gandhayuktinṛtyagītavādyiśilpādivijñānāni /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sarpadevajanavidyā</s>' — <s>Sarpavidyā</s> is the <s>Gāruḍa</s> [science of snake-charming]; <s>Devajanavidyā</s> is the knowledge of perfumery, dance, song, instrumental music, craft, and such arts.

children.text: etatsarvaṃ he bhagavo 'dhyemi //2 //
children.translated_text: 'All this, O Blessed One, I have studied.' (2)

By grammar, the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and others are known through the division of words and so on. '<s>Pitrya</s>' — the rules for <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites). '<s>Rāśi</s>' — mathematics. '<s>Daiva</s>' — knowledge of portents. '<s>Nidhi</s>' — the science of treasures such as <s>Mahākāla</s>. '<s>Vākovākya</s>' — the science of logic. '<s>Ekāyana</s>' — the science of ethics/politics. '<s>Devavidyā</s>' — etymology (<s>Nirukta</s>). '<s>Brahmavidyā</s>' — the knowledge pertaining to <s>Brahman</s> [here meaning the Vedic texts in the form of <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>] — [namely] phonetics (<s>śikṣā</s>), ritual procedure (<s>kalpa</s>), meter (<s>chandas</s>), and exposition (<s>viciti</s>). '<s>Bhūtavidyā</s>' — the science of [supernatural] beings.

children.text: START ChUp 7,1.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.1.3]

children.text:
so 'haṃ bhagavo mantravid evāsmi nātmavit |
śrutaṃ hy eva me bhagavaddṛśebhyas tarati śokam ātmavid iti |
so 'haṃ bhagavaḥ śocāmi |
taṃ mā bhagavāñ chokasya pāraṃ tārayatv iti |
taṃ hovāca yad vai kiṃcaitad adhyagīṣṭhā nāmaivaitat || ChUp_7,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'I, Blessed One, am merely a knower of words (<s>mantravit</s>), not a knower of the <s>Ātman</s>. For I have heard from those like your venerable self that one who knows the <s>Ātman</s> crosses over sorrow. I, Blessed One, am sorrowful. May the Blessed One take me across to the other shore of sorrow.' He said to him: 'All that you have studied — that is merely name.' (ChUp 7.1.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,1.3 so 'haṃ bhagava etatsarvaṃ jānannapi mantravidevāsmi śabdārthamātravijñānavānevāsmītyarthaḥ /
sarvo hi śabdo 'bhidhānamātramabhidhānaṃ ca sarvaṃ mantreṣvantarbhavati /
mantravidevāsmi mantravitkarmavidityarthaḥ /
'mantreṣu karmāṇī'ti hi vakṣyati nā'tmavinnā'tmānaṃ vedbhi /
nanvātmāpi mantraiḥ prakāśyata eveti kathaṃ mantraviccennā'tmavit /
na /
abhidhānābhidheyabhedasya vikāratvāt /
na ca vikāra ātmeṣyate /
nanvātmāpyātmaśabdenābhidhīyate /
na"yato vāco nivartante" /
"yatra nānya paśyati"ityādiśruteḥ /
kathaṃ tarhyā'tmaivādhastāt' 'sa ātme'tyādiśabdā ātmānaṃ pratyāyayanti /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
dehavati pratyagātmani bhedaviṣaye prayujyamānaḥ śabdo dehādīnāmātmatve pratyākhyāyamāne yatpariśiṣṭaṃ sadavācyamapi pratyāyayati /
yathā sarājikāyāṃ dṛśyamānāyāṃ senāyāṃ chatradhvajapatākādivyavahite 'dṛśyamāne 'pi rājanyeṣa rājā dṛśyata iti bhavati śabdaprayogastatra ko 'sau rājeti rājaviśeṣanirūpaṇāyāṃ dṛśyamānetarapratyākhyāne 'nyasminnadṛśyamāne 'pi rājani rājapratītirbhavettadvat /
tasmātsohaṃ mantravitkarmavidevāsmi karmakāryaṃ ca sarvaṃ vikāra iti vikārajña evāsmi nā'tmavinnā'tmaprakṛtisvarūpajña ityarthaḥ /
ata evokta"mācāryavānpuruṣo vede"ti /
"yato vāco nivartante"ityādiśrutibhyaśca /
śrutamāgamajñānamastyeva hi yasmānme mama bhagavaddṛśebhyo yuṣmatsadṛśebhyastaratyatikrāmati śokaṃ manastāpamakṛtārthabuddhitāmātmavidityataḥ /

so 'hamanātmavittvāddhe bhagavaḥ śocāmyakṛtārthabuddhyā santapye sarvadā taṃ mā māṃ śokasya śokasāgarasya pāramantaṃ bhagavāṃstārayatvātmajñānoḍupena kṛtārthabuddhimāpādayatvabhayaṃ gamayatvityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore I, not knowing the <s>Ātman</s>, O Blessed One, am sorrowful — I am pained by the feeling of being unfulfilled. May the Blessed One take me — across to the other shore of the ocean of sorrow — by the boat of <s>Ātman</s>-knowledge, may he bring me to the state of feeling fulfilled, may he lead me to fearlessness — that is the meaning.

children.text: tamevamuktavantaṃ hovāca yadvai kiñcaitadadhyagīṣṭhā adhītavānasi /
children.translated_text: To him who spoke thus, [<s>Sanatkumāra</s>] said: 'All that you have studied —'

children.text: adhyayanena tadarthajñānamupalakṣyate jñātavānasītyetannāmaivaitat /
children.translated_text: 'studied' — by study [is indicated] the knowledge of its meaning — 'you have known' — this is merely name.

children.text: "vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam"iti śruteḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s>: 'Modification is merely a name, a verbal handle.' (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.1.3:] 'I, Blessed One, though knowing all this, am merely a knower of mantras — I am merely one who knows the meaning of words' — that is the meaning. For all speech is merely designation, and all designation is contained within the mantras. 'A knower of mantras' means 'a knower of [ritual] action,' for [the text] will say: 'In mantras [are contained] actions.' 'I am not a knower of the <s>Ātman</s> — I do not know the <s>Ātman</s>.' [Objection:] But the <s>Ātman</s> too is revealed by mantras — so how can a knower of mantras not know the <s>Ātman</s>? [Reply:] No — because the distinction between designation and designated is itself a modification. And modification is not accepted as the <s>Ātman</s>. [Objection:] But the <s>Ātman</s> too is designated by the word '<s>Ātman</s>.' [Reply:] No — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'From which words turn back,' and 'Where one does not see another.' [Objection:] Then how do words like 'the <s>Ātman</s> below' and 'this is the <s>Ātman</s>' convey the <s>Ātman</s>? [Reply:] This is no defect. When a word is used regarding the inner self dwelling in a body, in a context of distinction, and when the status of body and such as <s>Ātman</s> is negated — what remains, though inexpressible, is [indirectly] conveyed. Just as when an army is seen with a king, and when the umbrella, flag, banner, and such are distinguished — even though the king is not [separately] seen, the usage occurs: 'The king is seen here.' There, when one asks 'Who is that king?' and when the others who are seen are negated, knowledge of the king arises regarding the one not [directly] seen — it is like that. Therefore, I am a knower of mantras, a knower of [ritual] action; and all that is the product of action is modification — so I am a knower of modifications only, not a knower of the <s>Ātman</s>, not one who knows the essential nature of the <s>Ātman</s>, which is the source [of all] — that is the meaning. Hence it is said: 'One who has a teacher knows.' And from <s>śruti</s>s like: 'From which words turn back.' I have heard — there is indeed scriptural knowledge — from those like your venerable self that one who knows the <s>Ātman</s> crosses over — transcends — sorrow, the mental anguish of feeling unfulfilled.

children.text: START ChUp 7,1.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.1.4]

children.text:
nāma vā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmaveda ātharvaṇaś caturtha itihāsapurāṇaḥ pañcamo vedānāṃ vedaḥ pitryo rāśir daivo nidhir vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyā brahmavidyā bhūtavidyā kṣatravidyā nakṣatravidyā sarpadevajanavidyā |
nāmaivaitat |
nāmopāssveti || ChUp_7,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Name indeed is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s> as the fourth, the <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s> as the fifth, the grammar, the rites for ancestors, mathematics, the science of portents, the science of treasures, logic, ethics, etymology, the science of <s>Brahman</s>, the science of beings, the science of governance, astronomy, and the science of serpents and celestial beings — this is merely name. Meditate on name.' (ChUp 7.1.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,1.4 nāma vā ṛgvedo yajurveda ityādi nāmaivaitat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.1.4:] 'Name indeed is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>...' and so forth — 'this is merely name.'

children.text: nāmopāḥsva brahmeti brahmabuddhyā /
children.translated_text: 'Meditate on name as <s>Brahman</s>' — with the understanding that it is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yathā pratimāṃ viṣṇubuddhyopāste tadvat //4 //
children.translated_text: Just as one meditates on an image with the understanding that it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — in that manner. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 7,1.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.1.5]

children.text:
sa yo nāma brahmety upāste |
yāvan nāmno gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo nāma brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo nāmno bhūya iti |
nāmno vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on name as <s>Brahman</s> — as far as name extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on name as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than name, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than name.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.1.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,1.5 sa yastu nāma brahmetyupāste tasya yatphalaṃ bhavati tacchṛṇu yāvannāmno gataṃ nāmno gocaraṃ tatra tasminnāmaviṣaye 'sya yathākāmacāraḥ kāmacaraṇaṃ rājña iva svaviṣaye bhavati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.1.5:] He who meditates on name as <s>Brahman</s> — hear what fruit accrues to him: as far as name extends — as far as the range of name — in that domain of name, he has freedom of movement, like a king in his own domain.

children.text: yo nāma brahmetyupāsta ityupasaṃhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on name as <s>Brahman</s>' — this is the concluding summary.

children.text: kimasti bhagavo nāmno bhūyo 'dhikataraṃ yadbrahmadṛṣṭyarhamanyadityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is there, Blessed One, something greater than name — something more that is worthy of being regarded as <s>Brahman</s>?' — this is the intended meaning.

children.text: sanatkumāra āha nāmno vāva bhūyo 'styevetyukta āha yadyasti tanme bhagavānbravītviti //5//
children.translated_text: <s>Sanatkumāra</s> says: 'There is indeed something greater than name.' When thus told, [<s>Nārada</s>] says: 'If there is, may the Blessed One tell me that.' (5)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,2.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.2.1]

children.text:
vāg vāva nāmno bhūyasī |
vāg vā ṛgvedaṃ vijñāpayati yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham itihāsapurāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ vedānāṃ vedaṃ pitryaṃ rāśiṃ daivaṃ nidhiṃ vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyāṃ brahmavidyāṃ bhūtavidyāṃ kṣatravidyāṃ nakṣatravidyāṃ sarpadevajanavidyāṃ divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca vāyuṃ cākāśaṃ cāpaś ca tejaś ca devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca paśūṃś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatīñ śvāpadāny ākīṭapataṅgapipīlakaṃ dharmaṃ cādharmaṃ |
ca satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca sādhu cāsādhu ca hṛdayajñaṃ cāhṛdayajñaṃ ca |
yad vai vāṅ nābhaviṣyan na dharmo nādharmo vyajñāpayiṣyan na satyaṃ nānṛtaṃ na sādhu nāsādhu na hṛdayajño nāhṛdayajñaḥ |
vāg evaitad sarvaṃ vijñāpayati vācam upāssveti || ChUp_7,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Speech is indeed greater than name. Speech makes known the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s> as the fourth, the <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s> as the fifth, grammar, rites for ancestors, mathematics, the science of portents, the science of treasures, logic, ethics, etymology, the science of <s>Brahman</s>, the science of beings, the science of governance, astronomy, the science of serpents and celestial beings, heaven, earth, wind, space, water, fire, gods, humans, cattle, birds, grasses and trees, wild animals down to worms, moths, and ants, as well as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, truth and untruth, good and bad, what is pleasing to the heart and what is not. If speech did not exist, neither <s>dharma</s> nor <s>adharma</s> would be made known, neither truth nor untruth, neither good nor bad, neither what is pleasing nor what is not. Speech indeed makes all this known. Meditate on speech.' (ChUp 7.2.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,2.1 vāgvāva /
vāgitīndriyaṃ jihvābhūlādiṣvaṣṭasu sthāneṣu sthitaṃ varṇānāmabhivyañjakam /
varṇāśca nāmeti nāmno vāgbhūyasītyucyate /
kāryaddhi kāraṇaṃ bhūyo dṛṣṭaṃ loke yathā putrātpitā tadvat /
kathaṃ ca vāṅnāmno bhūyasītyāhavāgvā ṛgvedaṃ vijñāpayatyayamṛgveda iti /
tathā yajurvedamityādi samānam /
hṛdayajñaṃ hṛdayapriyam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Hṛdayajña</s>' means 'pleasing to the heart.'

children.text: tadviparītamahṛdayajñam /
children.translated_text: The opposite of that is '<s>ahṛdayajña</s>' (displeasing to the heart).

children.text: yadyadi vāṅnābhaviṣyaddharmādi na vyajñāpayiṣyadvāgabhāve 'dhyayanābhāve tadarthaśravaṇābhāvastacchravaṇābhāve dharmādi na vyajñāpayiṣyanna vijñātamabhaviṣyadityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: If speech did not exist, it would not have made <s>dharma</s> and the rest known — in the absence of speech, there would be no study; in the absence of study, no hearing of its meaning; in the absence of hearing that, <s>dharma</s> and the rest would not have been made known — would not have been known — that is the meaning.

children.text: tasmādvāgevaitacchabdoccāraṇena sarvaṃ vijñāpayatyato bhūyasī vāṅnāmnastasmādvācaṃ brahmetyupāḥsva //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, speech indeed makes all this known through the utterance of words — hence speech is greater than name. Therefore, meditate on speech as <s>Brahman</s>. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.2.1:] 'Speech indeed' — 'speech' here means the organ, situated in the eight places beginning with the chest, lips, and so on, which manifests phonemes. Since phonemes constitute name, speech is said to be greater than name. For in the world, the cause is seen to be greater than the effect — as a father is [greater] than a son. How is speech greater than name? [The text] says: 'Speech makes known the <s>Ṛgveda</s>' — [making it known as] 'This is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>.' Similarly with the <s>Yajurveda</s> and the rest — the same [explanation applies].

children.text: START ChUp 7,2.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.2.2]

children.text:
sa yo vācaṃ brahmety upāste |
yāvad vāco gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo vācaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo vāco bhūya iti |
vāco vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on speech as <s>Brahman</s> — as far as speech extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on speech as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than speech, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than speech.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.2.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,2.2 samānamanyat //2//
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.2.2:] The rest is the same [as before]. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,3.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.3.1]

children.text:
mano vāva vāco bhūyaḥ |
yathā vai dve vāmalake dve vā kole dvau vākṣau muṣṭir anubhavaty evaṃ vācaṃ ca nāma ca mano 'nubhavati |
sa yadā manasā manasyati mantrān adhīyīyety athādhīte |
karmāṇi kurvīyety atha kurute |
putrāṃś ca paśūṃś ceccheyety athecchate |
imaṃ ca lokam amuṃ ceccheyety athecchate |
mano hy ātmā |
mano hi lokaḥ |
mano hi brahma |
mana upāssveti || ChUp_7,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The mind is indeed greater than speech. Just as, indeed, the fist encompasses two <s>āmalaka</s> fruits, or two <s>kola</s> berries, or two <s>akṣa</s> nuts — so the mind encompasses both speech and name. When one wills with the mind: "Let me study the <s>mantra</s>s" — then one studies. "Let me perform the rituals" — then one performs. "Let me desire sons and cattle" — then one desires. "Let me desire this world and the next" — then one desires.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.3.1]

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,3.1 mano manasyanaviśiṣṭamantaḥkaraṇaṃ vāco bhūyaḥ /
taddhi manasyanavyāpāravadvācaṃ vaktavye prerayati /
tena vāṅmanasyantarbhavati /
yacca yasminnantarbhavati tattasya vyāpakatvāttato bhūyo bhavati /
yathā vai loke dve vā'malake phale dve vā kole badaraphale dvau vākṣau vibhītakaphale muṣṭiranubhavati muṣṭiste phale vyāpnoti muṣṭau hi te antarbhavataḥ /
evaṃ vācaṃ ca nāma cā'malakādivanmano 'nubhavati /
sa yadā puruṣe yasminkāle manasāntaḥkaraṇena manasyati manasyanaṃ vivakṣābuddhiḥ kathaṃ?mantrānadhīyīyoccārayeyamityevaṃ vivakṣāṃ kṛtvāthādhīte tathā karmāṇi kurvīyeti cikīrṣābuddhiṃ kṛtvātha kurute putrāṃśca paśūṃśceccheyeti prāptīcchāṃ kṛtvā tatprāptyupāyānuṣṭhānenāthecchate putrādīnprāpnotītyarthaḥ /
tathemaṃ ca lokamamuṃ copāyeneccheyeti tatpraptyupāyānuṣṭhānenāthecchace prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'Let me desire this world and the next by means [of obtaining them]' — and through the practice of the means for their attainment, one then desires, that is, attains [them].

children.text: mano hyātmā'tmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ ca sati manasi nānyatheti mano hyātmetyucyate /
children.translated_text: For the mind is the self — the agency and experiencer-ship of the self exist only when there is a mind, not otherwise. Therefore, the mind is said to be the self.

children.text: mano hi lokaḥ satyeva hi manasi loko bhavati tatprāptyupāyānuṣṭhānaṃ ceti mano hi loko yasmāttasmānmano hi brahma /
children.translated_text: 'The mind is the world' — for the world exists only when the mind exists, along with the practice of the means for attaining [it]. Therefore, 'the mind is the world' — and because of this, 'the mind is <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: yata evaṃ tasmānmana upāḥsveti //1 //
children.translated_text: Since this is so, 'meditate upon the mind.' [End of section 1.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.3.1] The mind — the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) whose [function is] thinking in general — is greater than speech. For the mind, in its function of thinking, impels speech to speak what is to be spoken. Therefore, speech is included within the mind. And that in which something is included — being its pervader — is greater than it. Just as in the world, two <s>āmalaka</s> fruits, or two <s>kola</s> (jujube) berries, or two <s>akṣa</s> (<s>vibhītaka</s>) nuts [are encompassed by] the fist —

children.text: START ChUp 7,3.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.3.2]

children.text:
sa yo mano brahmety upāste |
yāvan manaso gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo mano brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo manaso bhūya iti |
manaso vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates upon the mind as <s>Brahman</s> — as far as the mind extends, there he has freedom of movement — he who meditates upon the mind as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than the mind, venerable one?' 'There is indeed something greater than the mind.' 'Let the venerable one tell me that.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.3.2]

children.text: ChUpBh_7,3.2 sa yo ityādi samānam //2//
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.3.2] 'He who' and so forth — the same [as before]. [End of section 2.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,4.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.4.1]

children.text:
saṃkalpo vāva manaso bhūyān |
yadā vai saṃkalpayate 'tha manasyati |
atha vācam īrayati |
tām u nāmnīyūati |
nāmni mantrā ekaṃ bhavanti |
mantreṣu karmāṇi || ChUp_7,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Will (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) is indeed greater than the mind. For when one wills, then one thinks; then one utters speech; and that [speech] one utters through name. In name, the <s>mantra</s>s become one; in the <s>mantra</s>s, the rituals [become one].' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.4.1]

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,4.1 saṃkalpo vāva manaso bhūyān /
saṃkalpo 'pi manasyanavadantaḥkaraṇavṛttiḥ kartavyākartavyaviṣayavibhāgena samarthanam /
vibhāgena hi samarthite viṣaye cikīrṣābuddhirmanasyanānantaraṃ bhavati /
katham /
yadā vai saṃkalpayate kartavyādiviṣayānvibhajata idaṃ kartuṃ yuktamiti, atha manasyati mantrānadhīyīyetyādi /
athānantaraṃ vācamīrayati mantrādyuccāraṇe /
tāṃ ca vācamu nāmni nāmoccāraṇanimittaṃ vivakṣāṃ kṛtverayati nāmni nāmasāmānye mantrāḥ śabdaviśeṣāḥ santa ekaṃ bhavantyantarbhavantītyarthaḥ /
sāmānye hi viśeṣo 'ntabhavati /
mantreṣu karmāṇyekaṃ bhavanti /
mantraprakāśitāni karmāṇi kriyante nāmantrakamasti karma /
yaddhi mantraprakāśanena labdhasattākaṃ satkarma brāhmaṇenedaṃ kartavyamasmai phalāyeti vidhīyate /
yāpyutpattirbrāhmaṇeṣu karmaṇāṃ dṛśyate sāpi mantreṣu labdhasattākānāmeva karmaṇāṃ spaṣṭīkaraṇam /
na hi mantrāprakāśitaṃ karma kiñcidbrāhmaṇa utpannaṃ dṛśyate /
trayīvihitaṃ karmeti prasiddham loke /
children.translated_text: [The expression] 'rituals prescribed by the three [<s>Veda</s>s]' is well-known in the world.

children.text: trayīśabdaśca ṝgyajuḥsāmasamākhyā /
children.translated_text: And the word 'three' (<s>trayī</s>) denotes the names <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: mantreṣu karmāṇi kavayo yānyapaśyanniti cā'tharvaṇe /
children.translated_text: 'In the <s>mantra</s>s, the rituals [are united]' — and in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> [it is said]: 'The sages perceived the rituals in the <s>mantra</s>s.'

children.text: tasmādyuktaṃ mantreṣu karmāṇyekaṃ bhavantīti //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper [to say] 'in the <s>mantra</s>s, the rituals become one.' [End of section 1.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.4.1] Will (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) is indeed greater than the mind. Will is also a function of the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) — [namely,] the deliberation [that divides things] into what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. For when [a matter] has been deliberated upon through such division, the intention (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) to act arises immediately afterward in the mind. How? When one wills — that is, distinguishes the objects [into] 'this ought to be done' — [thinking] 'this is proper to do' — then one thinks;

children.text: START ChUp 7,4.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.4.2]

children.text:
tāni ha vā etāni saṃkalpaikāyanāni saṃkalpātmakāni saṃkalpe pratiṣṭhitāni |
samakḷpatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī |
samakalpetāṃ vāyuś cākāśaṃ ca |
samakalpantāpaś ca tejaś ca |
teṣāṃ saṃkḷptyai varṣaṃ saṃkalpate |
varṣasya saṃkḷptyā annaṃ saṃkalpate |
annasya saṃkḷptyai prāṇāḥ saṃkalpante |
prāṇānāṃ saṃkḷptyai mantrāḥ saṃkalpante |
mantrāṇāṃ saṃkḷptyai karmāṇi saṃkalpante |
karmaṇāṃ saṃkḷptyai lokaḥ saṃkalpate |
lokasya saṃkḷptyai sarvaṃ saṃkalpate |
sa eṣa saṃkalpaḥ |
saṃkalpam upāssveti || ChUp_7,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'All these [things] — mind and the rest — have will as their sole destination; they have will as their self; they are established in will. Heaven and earth were willed. Wind and space were willed. Water and fire were willed. Through their being willed, rain is willed. Through the willing of rain, food is willed. Through the willing of food, the vital breaths are willed. Through the willing of the vital breaths, the <s>mantra</s>s are willed...' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.4.2]

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,4.2 tāni ha vā etāni mana ādīni saṃkalpaikāyanāni saṃkalpa eko 'yanaṃ gamanaṃ pralayo yeṣāṃ tāni saṃkalpaikāyanāni saṃkalpātmakānyutpattau saṃkalpe pratiṣṭhitāni sthitau samakḷpatāṃ saṃkalpaṃ kṛtavatyāviva hi dyauśca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivyau niścale lakṣyete /
tathā samakalpetāṃ vāyuścā'kāśaṃ caitāvapi saṃkalpaṃ kṛtavantāviva tathā samakalpantāmāpaśca tejaśca svena rūpema niścalāni lakṣyante /
yatasteṣāṃ dyāvāpṛthivyādīnāṃ saṃkḷptyai saṃkalpanimittaṃ varṣaṃ saṃkalpante /
annamayā hi prāṇā annopaṣṭambhakāḥ /
"annaṃ dāma"iti hi śrutiḥ /
teṣāṃ saṃkḷptyai mantrāḥ saṃkalpante /
prāṇāvānhi mantrānadhīte nābalaḥ /
mantrāṇāṃ hi saṃkḷptyai karmāṇyagnihotrādīni saṃkalpante 'nuṣṭhīyamānāni mantraprakāśitāni samarthībhavanti phalāya /
tato lokaḥ phalaṃ saṃkalpate karmakartṛsamavāyitayā samarthībhavatītyarthaḥ /
lokasya saṃkḷptyai sarvaṃ jagatsaṃkalpate svarūpāvaikalyāya /
children.translated_text: Through the willing of the world — the entire universe is willed — for the completeness of its own nature.

children.text: etaddhīdaṃ sarvaṃ jagadyatphalāvasānaṃ tatsarvaṃ saṃkalpamūlam /
children.translated_text: For this entire universe, which culminates in its fruits — all of it is rooted in will.

children.text: ato viśiṣṭaḥ sa eṣa saṃkalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this will is pre-eminent.

children.text: ataḥ saṃkalpamupāḥsvetyuktvā phalamāha tadupāsakasya //2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'meditate upon will' — having said this, [the teacher] states the fruit for the one who thus meditates. [End of section 2.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.4.2] All these — the mind and the rest — have will as their sole destination (<s>ekāyana</s>) — will alone is the one destination, the goal, the dissolution of all these; they have will as their self — they originate from will; they are established in will — they subsist in will. 'Heaven and earth were willed' — heaven and earth appear as though they have made a resolve, appearing firm and motionless. Likewise, wind and space were willed.

children.text: START ChUp 7,4.3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.4.3]

children.text:
sa yaḥ saṃkalpaṃ brahmety upāste |
kḷptān vai sa lokān dhruvān dhruvaḥ pratiṣṭhitān pratiṣṭhito 'vyathamānān avyathamāno 'bhisidhyati |
yāvat saṃkalpasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yaḥ saṃkalpaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavaḥ saṃkalpād bhūya iti |
saṃkalpād vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates upon will (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) as <s>Brahman</s> — he, being firm, attains firm worlds that are established and unshaken — worlds that have been willed; as far as will extends, there he has freedom of movement — he who meditates upon will as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than will, venerable one?' 'There is indeed something greater than will.' 'Let the venerable one tell me that.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.4.3]

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,4.3 sa yaḥ saṃkalpaṃ brahmeti brahmabuddhyopāstekḷptānvai dhātrāsyeme lokāḥ phalamiti kḷptānsamarthitānsaṃkalpitānsa vidvāndhruvānnityānatyantādhruvāpekṣayā dhruvaśca svayam /
lokino hyadhruvatve loke dhruvakḷptivyartheti dhruvaḥ sanpratiṣṭhitānupakaraṇasaṃpannānityarthaḥ /
paśuputrādibhiḥ pratitiṣṭhatīti darśanātsvayaṃ ca pratiṣṭhita ātmīyopakaraṇasaṃpanno 'vyathamānānamitrāditrāsarah itānavyathamānaśca svayamabhisidhyatyabhiprāpnotītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is established through sons, cattle, and the like — as is observed. And he himself becomes established — meaning endowed with his own resources. [He attains worlds that are] unshaken — free from the fear of enemies and the like — and he himself becomes unshaken. He attains — meaning he obtains [them].

children.text: yāvatsaṃkalpasya gataṃ saṃkalpagocarastatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati ātmanaḥ saṃkalpasya na tu sarveṣāṃ saṃkalpasyeti /
children.translated_text: 'As far as will extends' — the domain of will — 'there he has freedom of movement' — [namely, the domain of] his own will, not [the domain of] everyone's will.

children.text: uttaraphalavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: Because [otherwise there would be] a contradiction with the subsequent [higher] fruits.

children.text: yaḥ saṃkalpaṃ brahmetyupāsta ityādi pūrvavat //3//
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates upon will as <s>Brahman</s>' and so forth — as before. [End of section 3.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.4.3] He who meditates upon will as <s>Brahman</s> — with the conviction that [will] is <s>Brahman</s> — [attains] worlds that have been willed, that is, established and determined by the Creator (<s>Dhātṛ</s>) as fruits — [such] determined, well-established worlds. [He] the knower [attains worlds that are] firm — eternal, comparatively [speaking], relative to what is non-eternal — and he himself becomes firm. For if the inhabitants [of those worlds] were non-eternal, the fixity of those worlds would be pointless. Being himself firm, [he attains worlds that are] established — meaning, endowed with resources.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,5.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.5.1]

children.text:
cittaṃ vāva saṃkalpād bhūyaḥ |
yadā vai cetayate 'tha saṃkalpayate |
atha manasyati |
atha vācam īrayati |
tām u nāmnīyūati |
nāmni mantrā ekaṃ bhavanti |
mantreṣu karmāṇi || ChUp_7,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Intelligence (<s>citta</s>) is indeed greater than will. For when one is intelligent, then one wills; then one thinks; then one utters speech; and that [speech] one utters through name. In name, the <s>mantra</s>s become one; in the <s>mantra</s>s, the rituals [become one].' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.5.1]

children.text: ChUpBh_7,5.1 cittaṃ vāva saṃkalpādbhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.5.1] Intelligence (<s>citta</s>) is indeed greater than will.

children.text: cittaṃ cetayitṛtvaṃ prāptakālānurūpabodhavattvamatītāna gataviṣayaprayojananirūpaṇasāmarthyaṃ ca tatsaṃkalpādapi bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Intelligence (<s>citta</s>) is the capacity to be aware (<s>cetayitṛtva</s>) — the possession of timely awareness appropriate to the occasion, and the capacity to discern the objects and purposes of past [events]. That is greater even than will.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How?

children.text: yadā vai prāptamiti cetayate tadā dānāya vāpohāya vātha saṃkalpayate 'tha manasyatītyādi pūrvavat //1 //
children.translated_text: 'When one becomes aware: "this has arrived" — then one wills, either for giving or for rejecting; then one thinks' — and so forth, as before. [End of section 1.]

children.text: START ChUp 7,5.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.5.2]

children.text:
tāni ha vā etāni cittaikāyanāni cittātmāni citte pratiṣṭhitāni |
tasmād yady api bahuvid acitto bhavati nāyam astīty evainam āhuḥ |
yad ayaṃ veda yad vā ayaṃ vidvān nettham acittaḥ syād iti |
atha yady alpavic cittavān bhavati tasmā evota śuśrūṣante |
cittaṃ hy evaiṣām ekāyanam |
cittam ātmā |
cittaṃ pratiṣṭhā |
cittam upāssveti || ChUp_7,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'All these [things] have intelligence as their sole destination; they have intelligence as their self; they are established in intelligence. Therefore, even if a greatly learned person lacks intelligence, people say of him: "He amounts to nothing." [They say:] "If he truly knew, he would not be thus unintelligent." But if a person of little learning possesses intelligence, people wish to listen to him. For intelligence alone is their sole destination; intelligence is [their] self; intelligence is [their] foundation. Therefore, meditate upon intelligence.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.5.2]

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,5.2 tāni saṃkalpādīni karmaphalāntāni cittaikāyanāni cittātmāni cittotpattīni citte pratiṣṭhitāni cittasthitānītyapi pūrvavat /
kiñca cittasya māhātmyam /
yasmāccittaṃ saṃkalpādimūlaṃ tasmādyadyapi bahuvidbahuśāsrādiparijñānavānsannacitto bhavati prāptādicetayitṛtvasāmarthyavirahito bhavati taṃ nipuṇā laukikānāyamasti vidyamāno 'pyasatsama evetyenamāhuḥ /
yaccāyaṃ kiñcicchāsrādi veda śrutavāṃstadapyasya vṛthaiveti kathayanti /
kasmāt /
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: yadyayaṃ vidvānsyāditthamevamacitto na syāttasmādasya śrutamapyaśrutamevetyāhurityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If this person truly were learned, he would not be thus unintelligent.' Therefore, [people say:] 'Even his learning is as good as unlearned' — that is the meaning.

children.text: athālpavidapi yadi cittavānbhavati tasmā etasmai taduktārthagrahaṇāyaivotāpi śuśrūṣante śrotumicchanti /
children.translated_text: But even if a person of little learning possesses intelligence — people wish to listen to him, for the sake of grasping the meaning stated by him.

children.text: tasmācca cittaṃ hyevaiṣāṃ saṃkalpādīnāmekāyanamityādi pūrvavat //2 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, 'intelligence alone is the sole destination of all these — will and the rest' — and so forth, as before. [End of section 2.]

[<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.5.2] All these — will and the rest, up to the fruits of action — have intelligence as their sole destination; they have intelligence as their self — they originate from intelligence; they are established in intelligence — they subsist in intelligence. This too is as before. Furthermore, [here is] the greatness of intelligence: since intelligence is the root of will and the rest, therefore, even if a greatly learned person — one who has extensive knowledge of many scriptures — lacks intelligence, that is, lacks the capacity for timely awareness,

children.text: START ChUp 7,5.3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.5.3]

children.text:
sa yaś cittaṃ brahmety upāste |
cittān vai sa lokān dhruvān dhruvaḥ pratiṣṭhitān pratiṣṭhito 'vyathamānān avyathamāno 'bhisidhyati |
yāvac cittasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yaś cittaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavaś cittād bhūya iti |
cittād vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates upon intelligence (<s>citta</s>) as <s>Brahman</s> — he, being firm, attains firm worlds that are established and unshaken — worlds that are enriched [by intelligence]; as far as intelligence extends, there he has freedom of movement — he who meditates upon intelligence as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than intelligence, venerable one?' 'There is indeed something greater than intelligence.' 'Let the venerable one tell me that.' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.5.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_7,5.3 cittānupacitānhuddhimadguṇaiḥ sa cittopāsako dhruvānityādi coktārtham //3//
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhāṣya</s> 7.5.3] [He attains] worlds enriched with qualities of intelligence — [that is,] the meditator on intelligence [attains worlds that are] firm — and so forth. The meaning has been stated. [End of section 3.]

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,6.1-2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 7.6.1-2]

children.text:
dhyānaṃ vāva cittād bhūyaḥ |
dhyāyatīva pṛthivī |
dhyāyatīvāntarikṣam |
dhyāyatīva dyauḥ |
dhyāyantīvāpaḥ |
dhyāyantīva parvatāḥ |
dhyāyantīva devamanuṣyāḥ |
tasmād ya iha manuṣyāṇāṃ mahattāṃ prāpnuvanti dhyānāpādāṃśā ivaiva te bhavanti |
atha ye 'lpāḥ kalahinaḥ piśunā upavādinas te |
atha ye prabhavo dhyānāpādāṃśā ivaiva te bhavanti |
dhyānam upāssveti || ChUp_7,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is indeed greater than thought (<s>citta</s>). The earth, as it were, meditates. The atmosphere, as it were, meditates. Heaven, as it were, meditates. The waters, as it were, meditate. The mountains, as it were, meditate. Gods and humans, as it were, meditate. Therefore, those among humans who attain greatness here seem to have obtained a share of the fruit of meditation. But those who are petty — quarrelsome, slanderous, fault-finding — they [are the opposite]. But those who are eminent seem to have obtained a share of the fruit of meditation. Meditate on meditation.' (ChUp 7.6.1)

children.text:
sa yo dhyānaṃ brahmety upāste |
yāvad dhyānasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo dhyānaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo dyānād bhūya iti |
dhyānād vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on meditation as <s>Brahman</s> — as far as the reach of meditation extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on meditation as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than meditation, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than meditation.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.6.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,6.1-2 dhyānaṃ vāva cittādbhūyaḥ /
dhyānaṃ nāma śāsroktadevatādyālambaneṣvacalo bhinnajātīyairanantaritaḥ pratyayasaṃtānaḥ /
ekāgrateti yamāhuḥ /
dṛśyate ca dhyānasya māhātmyaṃ phalataḥ /
katham /
yathā yogī dhyāyanniścalo bhavati dhyānaphalalābhe /
evaṃ dhyāyatīva niścalā dṛśyate pṛthivī /
dhyāyatīvāntarikṣamityādi samānamanyat /
devāśca manuṣyāśca devamanuṣyā manuṣyā eva vā devasamā devamanuṣyāḥ śamādiguṇasaṃpannā manuṣyā devasvarūpaṃ na jahatītyarthaḥ /
yasmādevaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ dhyānaṃ tasmādya iha loke manuṣyāṇāmeva dhanairvidyayā guṇairvā mahattāṃ mahattvaṃ prāpnuvanti dhanādimahattvahetuṃ labhanta ityarthaḥ /
dhyānāpādāṃśā iva dhyānasyā'pādanamāpādo dhyānaphalalābha ityetattasyāṃśo 'vayavaḥ kalā kāciddhyānaphalalābhakalāvanta ivaivetyarthaḥ /
te bhavanti niścalā iva lakṣyante na kṣudrā iva /
children.translated_text: They appear as if steady, not as if petty.

children.text: atha ye punaralpāḥ kṣudrāḥ kiñcidapi dhanādimahattvaikadeśamaprāptāste pūrvoktaviparītāḥ kalahinaḥ kalahaśīlāḥ piśunāḥ paradoṣodbhāsakā upavādinaḥ paradoṣaṃ sāmīpyayuktameva vadituṃ śīlaṃ yoṣāṃ ta upavādinaśca bhavanti /
children.translated_text: But those who are petty — insignificant, who have not attained even a portion of any greatness such as wealth — they, being the opposite of those described above, are quarrelsome — disposed to quarrel; slanderous — those who expose the faults of others; fault-finding — those whose habit is to speak of others' faults as if they were close at hand — they are fault-finders.

children.text: atha ye mahattvaṃ prāptā dhanādinimittaṃ te 'nyānprati prabhavantīti prabhavo vidyācāryarājeśvarādayo dhyānāpādāṃśā ivetyādyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: But those who have attained greatness on account of wealth and the like are eminent (<s>prabhavaḥ</s>) — they prevail over others, such as scholars, teachers, kings, and lords — they seem to have obtained a share of the fruit of meditation, and so on — the meaning has been stated.

children.text: ato dṛśyate dhyānasya mahattvaṃ phalato 'to bhūyaścittādatastadupāḥsvetyādyuktārtham //1-2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the greatness of meditation is seen from its fruits. Therefore it is greater than thought. Hence, meditate on meditation — and so on; the meaning has been stated. (1–2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.6.1–2:] Meditation is indeed greater than thought. Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is an unbroken stream of cognition directed toward the deities and other objects prescribed by scripture, uninterrupted by cognitions of a different kind — what they call one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>). And the greatness of meditation is seen from its fruits. How? Just as a yogin in meditation becomes motionless upon attaining the fruit of meditation, so the earth appears as if meditating — motionless. 'The atmosphere, as it were, meditates' and so on — the rest is similar. Gods and humans (<s>devamanuṣyāḥ</s>) — or, humans who are equal to gods, endowed with qualities such as tranquility (<s>śama</s>) and the rest — humans who do not abandon the divine nature, is the meaning. Because meditation is thus distinguished, therefore those among humans in this world who attain greatness — eminence — through wealth, learning, or virtues, meaning those who obtain the cause of greatness such as wealth — seem to have obtained a share of the fruit of meditation (<s>dhyānāpādāṃśāḥ</s>). <s>Āpādana</s> of meditation means the attainment of the fruit of meditation — a portion, a fraction of that — [they are] as if possessing a fraction of the attainment of the fruit of meditation, is the meaning.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,7.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.7.1]

children.text:
vijñānaṃ vāva dhyānād bhūyaḥ |
vijñānena vā ṛgvedaṃ vijānāti yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham itihāsapurāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ vedānāṃ vedaṃ pitryaṃ rāśiṃ daivaṃ nidhiṃ vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyāṃ brahmavidyāṃ bhūtavidyāṃ kṣatravidyāṃ nakṣatravidyāṃ sarpadevajanavidyāṃ divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca vāyuṃ cākāśaṃ cāpaś ca tejaś ca devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca paśūṃś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatīñ chvāpadāny ākīṭapataṅgapipīlakam |
dharmaṃ cādharmaṃ ca satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca sādhu cāsādhu ca hṛdayajñaṃ cāhṛdayajñaṃ cānnaṃ ca rasaṃ cemaṃ ca lokam amuṃ ca vijñānenaiva vijānāti |
vijñānam upāssveti || ChUp_7,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Understanding (<s>vijñāna</s>) is indeed greater than meditation. By understanding one understands the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s> as the fourth, <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s> as the fifth, the Veda of the Vedas [grammar], the rites for the ancestors, mathematics, the science of portents, the science of treasures, logic, ethics, the science of the gods, the science of <s>Brahman</s>, the science of beings, the science of governance, the science of the stars, the science of serpents and celestial beings, heaven and earth, wind and space, water and fire, gods and humans, cattle and birds, grasses and trees, wild animals down to insects, moths, and ants. <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), truth and falsehood, good and bad, what is agreeable to the heart and what is not, food and taste, this world and the next — by understanding alone one understands [all this]. Meditate on understanding.' (ChUp 7.7.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,7.1 vijñānaṃ vāva dhyānādbhūyaḥ /
vijñānaṃ śāsrārthaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ tasya dhyānakāraṇatvāddhyānādbhūyastvam /
kathaṃ ca tasya bhūyastvamityāha-vijñānena vā ṛgvedaṃ vijānātyayamṛgveda iti pramāṇatayā yasyārthajñānaṃ dhyānakāraṇam /
tathā yajurvedamityādi /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>Yajurveda</s> and so on.

children.text: kiñca paśvādīṃśca dharmādharmau śāsrasiddhau /
children.translated_text: Moreover, cattle and the rest, and <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, are established through scripture.

children.text: sādhvasādhunī lokataḥ siddhe, smārte vā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭāviṣayaṃ ca sarvaṃ vijñānenaiva vijānātītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Good and bad are established from worldly usage, or from <s>Smṛti</s> — pertaining to both the seen and the unseen — all this one understands by understanding alone, is the meaning.

children.text: tasmādyuktaṃ dhyānādijñānasya bhūyastvam ato vijñānamupāḥsveti //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is fitting that understanding is greater than meditation and the rest. Hence, meditate on understanding — and so on; the meaning has been stated. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.7.1:] Understanding is indeed greater than meditation. Understanding (<s>vijñāna</s>) is knowledge pertaining to the meaning of scripture. Because it is the cause of meditation, it is greater than meditation. And how is it greater? — he says: By understanding, one understands the <s>Ṛgveda</s> — 'this is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>' — the knowledge of whose meaning, serving as valid cognition, is the cause of meditation.

children.text: START ChUp 7,7.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.7.2]

children.text:
sa yo vijñānaṃ brahmety upāste |
vijñānavato vai sa lokāñ jñānavato 'bhisidhyati |
yāvad vijñānasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo vijñānaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo vijñānād bhūya iti |
vijñānād vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on understanding as <s>Brahman</s> — he attains worlds endowed with understanding and knowledge. As far as the reach of understanding extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on understanding as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than understanding, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than understanding.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.7.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,7.2 śṛṇūpāsanaphalaṃ vijñānavato vijñānaṃ yeṣu lokeṣu tānvijñānavato lokāñjñānavataścābhisidhyatyabhiprāpnoti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.7.2:] Hear the fruit of the meditation: he attains worlds endowed with understanding — worlds in which understanding is present — those worlds endowed with understanding; and worlds endowed with knowledge — he attains them.

children.text: vijñānaṃ śāsrārthaviṣayaṃ jñānamanyaviṣayaṃ naipuṇyaṃ tadvadbhiryuktāṃllokānnāprāpnotītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Understanding is knowledge pertaining to the meaning of scripture; knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) of another kind is skill. He attains worlds endowed with beings possessing such [qualities], is the meaning.

children.text: yāvadvijñānasyetyādi pūrvavat //2//
children.translated_text: 'As far as the reach of understanding' and so on — as before. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,8.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.8.1–2]

children.text:
balaṃ vāva vijñānād bhūyaḥ |
api ha śataṃ vijñānavatām eko balavān ākampayate |
sa yadā balī bhavaty athotthātā bhavati |
uttiṣṭhan paricaritā bhavati |
paricarann upasattā bhavati |
upasīdan draṣṭā bhavati śrotā bhavati mantā bhavati boddhā bhavati kartā bhavati vijñātā bhavati |
balena vai pṛthivī tiṣṭhati balenāntarikṣaṃ balena dyaur balena parvatā balena devamanuṣyā balena paśavaś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatayaḥ śvāpadāny ākīṭapataṅgapipīlakam |
balena lokas tiṣṭhati |
balam upāssveti || ChUp_7,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Strength (<s>bala</s>) is indeed greater than understanding. Even a hundred men of understanding are shaken by a single strong man. When one becomes strong, then one rises. Rising, one serves. Serving, one draws near. Drawing near, one becomes a seer, a hearer, a thinker, a knower, a doer, an understander. By strength the earth stands firm, by strength the atmosphere, by strength heaven, by strength the mountains, by strength gods and humans, by strength cattle and birds, grasses and trees, wild animals down to insects, moths, and ants. By strength the world stands firm. Meditate on strength.' (ChUp 7.8.1)

children.text:
sa yo balam upāste |
yāvad balasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo balaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo balād bhūya iti |
balād vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on strength as <s>Brahman</s> — as far as the reach of strength extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on strength as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than strength, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than strength.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.8.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,8.1-2 balaṃ vāva vijñānādbhūyaḥ /
balamityannopayogajanitaṃ manaso vijñeye pratibhānasāmarthyam /
anaśanādṛgādīni na vai mā pratibhānti bho iti śruteḥ /
śarīre 'pi tadevotthānādisāmarthyaṃ yasmādvijñānavatāṃ śatamapyekaḥ prāṇī balavānā kampayate yathā hastī matto manuṣyāṇāṃ śataṃ samuditamapi /
yasmādevamannādyupayoganimittaṃ balaṃ tasmātsa puruṣo yadā balī balena tadvānbhavatyathotthātotthānasya kartottiṣṭhaṃśca gurūṇāmācāryasya ca paricaritā paricaraṇasya śuśrūṣāyāḥ kartā bhavati paricarannupasattā teṣāṃ samīpago 'ntaraṅgaḥ prayo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
upasīdaṃśca samīpyaṃ gacchannekāgratayā'cāryasyānyasya copadeṣṭurgurordraṣṭā bhavati /
tatastaduktasya śrotā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Then he becomes a hearer of what has been said.

children.text: tata idamebhiruktamevamupapadyata ityupapattito mantā bhavati manvānaśca boddhā bhavatyevamevedamiti /
children.translated_text: Then, [thinking:] 'What has been said by them is thus logically consistent' — he becomes a thinker through reasoning, and while thinking, he becomes a knower — 'It is indeed so.'

children.text: tata evaṃ niścitya taduktārthasya kartānuṣṭhātā bhavati vijñātānuṣṭhānaphalasyānubhavitā bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having ascertained thus, he becomes a doer — a performer of what has been taught — and an understander — an experiencer of the fruit of the practice, is the meaning.

children.text: kiñca balasya māhātmyaṃ balena vai pṛthivī tiṣṭhatītyādyujvartham //1-2 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, the greatness of strength: 'By strength the earth stands firm' and so on — the meaning is clear. (1–2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.8.1–2:] Strength is indeed greater than understanding. Strength (<s>bala</s>) is the capacity of the mind, produced by the consumption of food, for illuminating the object of knowledge. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'They do not come to my mind, sir' — [said] due to not eating. In the body too, it is the same capacity for rising and the like. Because even a hundred beings possessing understanding — a single strong creature shakes them, just as a maddened elephant [shakes] even a hundred humans assembled together. Since strength is thus caused by the consumption of food, therefore, when a person becomes strong — endowed with strength — then he becomes one who rises, rising and serving the elders and the teacher — he becomes a performer of service, of attendance. While serving, he becomes one who draws near — one who becomes intimate, a close associate, is the meaning. And drawing near, approaching with one-pointedness, to the teacher or any other instructor — he becomes a seer.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,9.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.9.1]

children.text:
annaṃ vāva balād bhūyaḥ |
tasmād yady api daśa rātrīr nāśnīyāt |
yady u ha jīvet |
athavādraṣṭāśrotāmantāboddhākartāvijñātā bhavati |
athānnasyāye draṣṭā bhavati śrotā bhavati mantā bhavati boddhā bhavati kartā bhavati vijñātā bhavati |
annam upāssveti || ChUp_7,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Food (<s>anna</s>) is indeed greater than strength. Therefore, even if one does not eat for ten nights, even if one were to survive, one would become a non-seer, a non-hearer, a non-thinker, a non-knower, a non-doer, a non-understander. But upon the arrival of food, one becomes a seer, a hearer, a thinker, a knower, a doer, an understander. Meditate on food.' (ChUp 7.9.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,9.1 annaṃ vāva balādbhūyaḥ /
balahetutvāt /
kathamannasya balahetutvamityucyate /
yasmādbalakāraṇamannaṃ tasmādyadyapi kaściddaśa rātrīrnāśnīyātso 'nnopayogānimittasya balasya hānyā mriyate na cenmriyate yadyu ha jīvet /
dṛśyante hi māsamapyanaśnanto jīvantaḥ /
athavā sa jīvannapyadraṣṭā bhavati gurorapi tata evāśrotetyādi pūrvaviparītaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati /
atha yadā bahūnyahānyanaśito darśanādikriyāsvasamarthaḥ sannannasyā'yī /
āgamanamāyo 'nnasya prāptirityarthaḥ /
sā yasya vidyate so 'nnasyā'yī /
āya ityetadvarṇavyatyayena /
children.translated_text: <s>Āya</s> — this [word] is by metathesis of letters.

children.text: athānnasyā'yā ityapi pāṭha evamevārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Annasyāyā</s>' is also a reading — the meaning is the same.

children.text: draṣṭetyādikāryaśravaṇāt /
