children.translated_text: From hearing the effects [described as] 'a seer' and so on.

children.text: dṛśyate hyannopayoge darśanādisāmarthyaṃ na tadaprāptāvato 'nnamupāḥsveti //1 //
children.translated_text: For it is observed that upon consuming food, the capacity for seeing and the rest [is restored]; but not when food has not been obtained. Therefore, meditate on food. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.9.1:] Food is indeed greater than strength — because it is the cause of strength. How is food the cause of strength? — this is explained. Since food is the cause of strength, therefore even if someone does not eat for ten nights — he dies due to the loss of strength caused by not consuming food. If he does not die — even if he survives — for people are seen surviving even a month without eating — even then he becomes a non-seer, even of his teacher, and therefore a non-hearer — and so on, everything becomes the opposite of what was previously described. But when, after many days without eating and being incapable of the activities of seeing and the rest, food arrives — arrival means the coming of food, its obtainment, is the meaning — one who has that [arrival of food].

children.text: START ChUp 7,9.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.9.2]

children.text:
sa yo 'nnaṃ brahmety upāste |
annavato vai sa lokān pānavato 'bhisidhyati |
yāvad annasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo 'nnaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo 'nnād bhūya iti |
annād vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on food as <s>Brahman</s> — he attains worlds abounding in food and drink. As far as the reach of food extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on food as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than food, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than food.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.9.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,9.2 phalaṃ cānnavataḥ prabhūtānnānvai sa lokānpānavataḥ prabhūtodakāṃścānnapānayornityasaṃbandhāllokānabhisi dhyati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.9.2:] And the fruit: he attains worlds abounding in food — those worlds having abundant food — and abounding in drink — having abundant water, due to the constant connection between food and drink — he attains such worlds.

children.text: samānamanyat //2//
children.translated_text: The rest is the same [as before]. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,10.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.10.1]

children.text:
āpo vāvānnād bhūyasyaḥ |
tasmād yadā suvṛṣṭir na bhavati vyādhīyante prāṇā annaṃ kanīyo bhaviṣyatīti |
atha yadā suvṛṣṭir bhavaty ānandinaḥ prāṇā bhavanty annaṃ bahu bhaviṣyatīti |
āpa evemā mūrtā yeyaṃ pṛthivī yad antarikṣaṃ yad dyaur yat parvatā yad devamanuṣyā yat paśavaś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatayaḥ śvāpadāny ākīṭapataṅgapipīlakam |
āpa evemā mūrtāḥ |
apa upāssveti || ChUp_7,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Water (<s>āpas</s>) is indeed greater than food. Therefore, when there is no good rainfall, living beings become distressed, [thinking:] "Food will become scarce." But when there is good rainfall, living beings become joyful, [thinking:] "Food will be abundant." These very [things] — this earth, this atmosphere, this heaven, these mountains, these gods and humans, these cattle and birds, grasses and trees, wild animals down to insects, moths, and ants — are indeed embodied forms of water. Meditate on water.' (ChUp 7.10.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,10.1 āpo vāvānnādbhūyasyo 'nnakāraṇatvāt /
yasmādevaṃ tasmādyadā yasminkāle suvṛṣṭiḥ sasyahitā śobhanā vṛṣṭirna bhavati tadā vyādhīyante prāṇā duḥkhino bhavanti /
kiṃnimittamityāhānnamasminsaṃvatsare naḥ kanīyo 'lpataraṃ bhaviṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: For what reason? — he says: 'Food will be scarce for us in this year' — meaning it will be less.

children.text: atha punaryadā suvṛṣṭirbhavati tadā'nandinaḥ sukhino hṛṣṭāḥ prāṇāḥ prāṇino bhavantyantaṃ bahu prabhūtaṃ bhaviṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: But again, when there is good rainfall, then living beings become joyful — happy, delighted — [thinking:] 'Food will be abundant — plentiful.'

children.text: apsaṃbhavatvānmūrtasyānnasyā'pa evemā mūrtāmṛrtabhedākārapariṇatā iti mūrtā yeyaṃ pṛthivī yadantarikṣamityādi /
children.translated_text: Because the embodied form of food originates from water — 'These are indeed embodied forms of water' — transformed into the forms of embodied things — thus [they are] embodied; 'this earth, this atmosphere' and so on.

children.text: āpa evemā mūrtā ato 'pa upāḥsveti //1 //
children.translated_text: These are indeed embodied forms of water. Therefore, meditate on water. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.10.1:] Water is indeed greater than food — because it is the cause of food. Since this is so, therefore, at whatever time there is no good rainfall — rainfall beneficial to crops — then living beings become distressed, become unhappy.

children.text: START ChUp 7,10.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.10.2]

children.text:
sa yo 'po brahmety upāste |
āpnoti sarvān kāmāṃs tṛptimān bhavati |
yāvad apāṃ gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo 'po brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavo 'dbhyo bhūya iti |
adbhyo vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on water as <s>Brahman</s> — he attains all desires and becomes fulfilled. As far as the reach of water extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on water as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than water, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than water.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.10.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,10.2 phalaṃ-sa yo 'po brahmetyupāsta āpnoti sarvānkāmānkāmyānmūrtimato viṣayānityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 7.10.2:] The fruit: he who meditates on water as <s>Brahman</s> attains all desires — meaning all desirable material objects.

children.text: apsaṃbhavatvācca tṛpterambupāsanāttṛptimāṃśca bhavati /
children.translated_text: And since satisfaction (<s>tṛpti</s>) originates from water, through the meditation on water, he becomes fulfilled (<s>tṛptimān</s>).

children.text: samānamanyat //2//
children.translated_text: The rest is the same [as before]. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,11.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.11.1]

children.text:
tejo vāvādbhyo bhūyaḥ |
tad vā etad vāyum āgṛhyākāśam abhitapati tadāhur niśocati nitapati varṣiṣyati vā iti |
teja eva tatpūrvaṃ darśayitvāthāpaḥ sṛjate |
tad etad ūrdhvābhiś ca tiraścībhiś ca vidyudbhir āhrādāś caranti tasmād āhur vidyotate stanayati varṣiṣyati vā iti |
teja eva tatpūrvaṃ darśayitvāthāpaḥ sṛjate |
teja upāssveti || ChUp_7,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Fire (<s>tejas</s>) is indeed greater than water. It is fire that, having seized the wind, heats space. Then people say: "It is burning hot, it is scorching, it is going to rain." Fire first shows itself, and then produces water. With upward and sideways [flashes of] lightning, thunderclaps roll. Therefore they say: "It is flashing, it is thundering, it is going to rain." Fire first shows itself, and then produces water. Meditate on fire.' (ChUp 7.11.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,11.1 tejo vāvādbhyo bhūyaḥ /
tejaso 'pakāraṇatvāt /
kathamapkāraṇatvamityāha /
yasmādabyonistejastasmāttadvā etattejo vāyumāgṛhyāvaṣṭabhya svātmanā niścalīkṛtya vāyumākāśamabhitapatyākāśamabhivyāpnuvattapati yadā tadā'hurlaukikā niśocati saṃtapati sāmānyena jagannitapati dehānato varṣiṣyati vā iti /
prasiddhaṃ hi loke kāraṇamabhyudyataṃ dṛṣṭavataḥ kārya bhaviṣyatīti vijñānam /
teja eva tatpūrvamātmānamudbhūtaṃ darśayitvāthānantaramapaḥ sṛjate 'to 'psraṣṭṛtvādbhūnyo 'dbhyastejaḥ /
kiñcānyattadetatteja eva stanayitnurūpeṇa varṣaheturbhavati /
katham /
children.translated_text: How?

children.text: ūrdhvābhiścordhvagābhirvidyudbhistiraścībhiśca tiryaggatābhiśca sahā'hrādāḥ stananaśabdāścaranti /
children.translated_text: With upward-going lightning and sideways-going lightning, together with thunderclaps — roaring sounds — they move about.

children.text: tasmāttaddarśanādāhurlaukikā vidyotate stanayati varṣiṣyati vā ityādyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, upon seeing that, ordinary people say: 'It is flashing, it is thundering, it is going to rain' — the meaning has been stated [as before].

children.text: atasteja upāḥsveti //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, meditate on fire. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.11.1:] Fire is indeed greater than water — because fire is the cause of water. How is it the cause of water? — he says: Since fire is the source of water, therefore this fire, having seized the wind — having held it fast, rendered it motionless by its own power — heats space, pervading space. When it does so, then ordinary people say: 'It is burning hot' — it is scorching in general the world — 'it is going to rain.' For it is well known in the world that when one sees the cause arisen, the knowledge arises: 'The effect will come about.' Fire indeed first shows itself — having manifested itself as arisen — then afterward produces water. Therefore, fire is greater than water, since it is the producer of water. Furthermore, this very fire, in the form of thunder, becomes the cause of rain.

children.text: START ChUp 7,11.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.11.2]

children.text:
sa yas tejo brahmety upāste |
tejasvī vai sa tejasvato lokān bhāsvato 'pahatatamaskān abhisidhyati |
yāvat tejaso gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yas tejo brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavas tejaso bhūya iti |
tejaso vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on fire as <s>Brahman</s> — he becomes radiant (<s>tejasvī</s>) and attains radiant, luminous worlds from which darkness has been dispelled. As far as the reach of fire extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on fire as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than fire, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than fire.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.11.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,11.2 tasya tejasa upāsanaphalaṃ-tejasvī vai bhavati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.11.2:] The fruit of meditating on fire: he becomes radiant indeed.

children.text: tejasvata eva ca lokānbhāsvataḥ prakāśavato 'pahatatamaskānbāhyādhyātmikājñānādyapanītatamaskānabhisidhyati /
children.translated_text: And he attains radiant worlds — luminous, light-filled worlds — from which external and internal darkness such as ignorance has been dispelled.

children.text: ṛjvarthamanyat //2//
children.translated_text: The rest is straightforward in meaning. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,12.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.12.1]

children.text:
ākāśo vāva tejaso bhūyān |
ākāśe vai sūryācandramasāv ubhau vidyun nakṣatrāṇy agniḥ |
ākāśenāhvāyati |
ākāśena sṛṇoti |
ākāśena pratisṛṇoti |
ākāśe ramate |
ākāśe na ramate |
ākāśe jāyate |
ākāśam abhijāyate |
ākāśam upāssveti || ChUp_7,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is indeed greater than fire. In space exist both the sun and the moon, lightning, stars, and fire. Through space one calls out. Through space one hears. Through space one responds. In space one delights. In space one does not delight. In space one is born. One is born toward space. Meditate on space.' (ChUp 7.12.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,12.1 ākāśo vāva tejaso bhūyān /
vāyusahitasya tejasaḥ kāraṇatvādvyomno vāyumāgṛhyeti tejasā sahokto vāyuriti pṛthagiha noktastejasaḥ /
kāraṇaṃ hi loke kāryādbhūyo dṛṣṭam /
yathā ghaṭādibhyo mṛttathā'kāśo vāyusahitasya tejasaḥ kāraṇamiti tato bhūyān /
katham /
ākāśo vai sūryācandramasāvubhau tejorūpau vidyunnakṣatrāṇyagniśca tejorūpāṇyākāśe 'ntaḥ /
yacca yasyāntarvarti tadalpaṃ bhūya itarat /
children.translated_text: And that which is contained within something is lesser; that which contains it is greater.

children.text: kiñcā'kāśenā'hvayati cānyamanya āhūtaścetara ākāśena śṛṇotyanyoktaṃ ca śabdamanyaḥ pratiśṛṇotyākāśe ramate krīḍatyanyonyaṃ sarvastathā na ramate cā'kāśe vadhvādiviyoga ākāśe jāyate na mūrtenāvaṣṭabdhe /
children.translated_text: Moreover, through space one calls another, and another who is called hears another's speech through space, and responds through space. In space one plays — everyone delights mutually. Likewise, in space one does not delight — [as when there is] separation from wife and the like. In space one is born — not [born] from anything solid.

children.text: tathā'kāśamabhilakṣyāṅkurādi jāyate na pratilomam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, sprouts and such are born toward space — not in the reverse direction.

children.text: ata ākāśamupāḥsva //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, meditate on space. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.12.1:] Space is indeed greater than fire — because space is the cause of fire together with wind. Wind is mentioned together with fire [in the previous section] — 'having seized the wind' — hence wind is not separately mentioned here, [being subsumed under] fire. For in the world, the cause is seen to be greater than the effect. Just as clay is [greater] than pots and the like, so space is the cause of fire together with wind, and therefore is greater. How? In space indeed exist both the sun and the moon — which are forms of fire — lightning, stars, and fire — all forms of fire — within space.

children.text: START ChUp 7,12.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.12.2]

children.text:
sa ya ākāśaṃ brahmety upāste |
ākāśavato vai sa lokān prakāśavato 'saṃbādhān urugāyavato 'bhisidhyati |
yāvad ākāśasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati ya ākāśaṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagava ākāśād bhūya iti |
ākāśad vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on space as <s>Brahman</s> — he attains spacious, luminous, unconfined, broad-ranging worlds. As far as the reach of space extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on space as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than space, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than space.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.12.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,12.2 phalaṃ śṛṇvākāśavato vai vistārayuktānsa vidvāṃllokānprakāśavataḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.12.2:] Hear the fruit: spacious — endowed with extensiveness — such worlds does the knower attain; luminous [worlds].

children.text: prakāśākāśayornityasaṃbandhātprakāśavataśca lokānasaṃbādhānsaṃbādhanaṃ saṃbādhaḥ saṃbādho 'nyonyapīḍā tadrahitānasaṃbādhānurugāyavato vistīrṇagatīnvistīrṇapracārāṃllokānabhisidhyati /
children.translated_text: Because of the constant connection between light and space — [they are] luminous worlds; unconfined — <s>saṃbādhana</s> (crowding) is <s>saṃbādha</s> (confinement), meaning mutual pressing — free from that, unconfined; broad-ranging (<s>urugāyavat</s>) — having extensive movement, having wide scope — such worlds he attains.

children.text: yāvadākāśasyetyādyuktārtham //2//
children.translated_text: 'As far as the reach of space' and so forth — the meaning has been stated. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,13.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.13.1-2]

children.text:
smaro vāvākāśād bhūyaḥ |
tasmād yady api bahava āsīrann a smaranto naiva te kaṃcana śṛṇuyur na manvīran na vijānīran |
yadā vāva te smareyur atha śṛṇuyur atha manvīrann atha vijānīran |
smareṇa vai putrān vijānāti smareṇa paśūn |
smaram upāssveti || ChUp_7,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Memory (<s>smara</s>) is indeed greater than space. Therefore, even if many were to sit together but did not remember, they would hear nothing, think nothing, know nothing. But when they remember, then they hear, then they think, then they know. Through memory one recognizes one's sons. Through memory one recognizes one's cattle. Meditate on memory.' (ChUp 7.13.1)

children.text:
sa yaḥ smaraṃ brahmety upāste |
yāvat smarasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yaḥ smaraṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagavaḥ smarād bhūya iti |
smarād vāva bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on memory as <s>Brahman</s> — as far as the reach of memory extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on memory as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than memory, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than memory.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.13.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,13.1-2 smaro vāvā'kākāśādbhūyaḥ /
smaraṇaṃ smaro 'ntaḥkaraṇadharmaḥ /
sa ākāśādbhūyāniti draṣṭavyaṃ liṅgavyatyayena smartuḥ smaraṇe hi satyākāśādi sarvamarthavatsmaraṇavato bhogyatvāt /
asati tu smarame sadapyasadeva /
sattvakāryābhāvāt /
nāpi sattvaṃ smṛtyabhāve śakyamākāśādīnāmavagantumityataḥ smaraṇasyā'kāśādbhṛyastvam /
dṛśyate hi loke smaraṇasya bhūyastvaṃ yasmāttasmādyadyapi samuditā bahava ekasminnāsīrannupaviśeyuste tatrā'sīnā anyonyabhāṣitamapi na smarantaścetsyurnaiva te kañcana śabdaṃ śṛṇuyustathā na manvīranmantavyaṃ cetsmareyustadā manvīransmṛtyabhāvānna manvīraṃstathā na vijānīran /
yadā vāva te smareyurmantavyaṃ vijñātavyaṃ śrotavyaṃ cātha śṛṇuyuratha manvīrannatha vijānīran /
children.translated_text: But when they remember what is to be thought about, what is to be known, and what is to be heard — then they hear, then they think, then they know.

children.text: tathā smareṇa vai mama putrā eta iti putrānvijānāti smareṇa paśūn /
children.translated_text: Likewise, through memory [one knows]: 'These are my sons' — thus one recognizes one's sons through memory; [similarly] one's cattle through memory.

children.text: ato bhūyastvātsmaramupāḥsveti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of its greatness, meditate on memory.

children.text: uktārthamanyat //1-2 //
children.translated_text: The rest has the meaning already stated. (1-2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.13.1-2:] Memory is indeed greater than space. Memory — the act of remembering — is a property of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). It should be understood as greater than space, with a transposition of gender. For when there is remembering on the part of the one who remembers, everything — space and the rest — becomes meaningful, because it becomes enjoyable for the one who remembers. But without memory, even what exists is as if non-existent — because of the absence of the effect of [its] existence. Nor can the existence of space and the rest be apprehended in the absence of memory. Therefore, memory is greater than space. For the greatness of memory is seen in the world, because — therefore — even if many were to sit together in one place — those seated there, if they do not remember each other's speech — they would hear nothing; likewise they would not think — if they were to remember something to be thought about, then they would think; because of the absence of memory, they would not think; likewise they would not know.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya trayodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,14.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.14.1]

children.text:
āśā vāva smarād bhūyasī |
āśeddho vai smaro mantrān adhīte karmāṇi kurute putrāṃś ca paśūṃś cecchata imaṃ ca lokaṃ amuṃ cecchate |
āśām upāssveti || ChUp_7,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Hope (<s>āśā</s>) is indeed greater than memory. Kindled by hope, memory studies the mantras, performs rituals, desires sons and cattle, desires this world and the next. Meditate on hope.' (ChUp 7.14.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,14.1 āśā vāva smarādbhūyasī /
āśāprāptavastvākāṅkṣā'śā tṛṣṇā kāma iti yāmāhuḥ paryāyaiḥ sā ca smarādbhūyasī /
katham /
āśayā /
hyantaḥkaraṇasthayā smarati smartavyam /

āśāviṣayarūpaṃ smarannasau smaro bhavatyata āśeddha āśayābhivardhitaḥ smarabhūtaḥ smarannṛgādīnmantrānadhīte 'dhītya ca tadarthaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo vidhīṃśca śrutvā karmāṇi kurute tatphalāśayaiva putrāṃśca karmaphalabhūtānicchate 'bhivāñchatyāśayaiva tatsādhanānyanutiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: Remembering in the form of the object of hope, this remembering becomes memory. Therefore, kindled — augmented — by hope, having become memory, remembering the <s>Ṛg</s> and other mantras, one studies them; and having studied and heard from <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s the injunctions along with their meanings, one performs rituals. Impelled by hope alone, one desires sons — which are the fruits of rituals — and undertakes the means for them.

children.text: imaṃ ca lokamāśeddha eva smaraṃllokasaṃgrahahetubhiricchate /
children.translated_text: This world too, kindled by hope, remembering the means for maintaining the world, one desires.

children.text: amuṃ ca lokamāśeddhaḥ smaraṃstatsādhanānuṣṭhānenecchate 'ta āśāraśānāvabaddhaṃ smarākāśādināmaparyantaṃ jagaccakrībhūtaṃ pratiprāṇi /
children.translated_text: And the next world, kindled by hope, remembering, one desires through the performance of the means [for attaining it]. Therefore, the entire world, bound to the rope of hope, has become a wheel, extending endlessly — [revolving] in every living being — through memory, space, and the rest.

children.text: atra āśa āyāḥ smarādapi bhūyastvamityata āśāmupāḥsva //1 //
children.translated_text: Here, hope is greater than even memory — therefore, meditate on hope. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.14.1:] Hope is indeed greater than memory. Hope — the longing for what has not yet been attained — is what they call by synonyms: <s>āśā</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>kāma</s> (desire). And it is greater than memory. How? Because of hope — residing in the inner organ — one remembers what is to be remembered.

children.text: START ChUp 7,14.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.14.2]

children.text:
sa ya āśāṃ brahmety upāste |
āśayāsya sarve kāmāḥ samṛdhyanti |
amoghā hāsyāśiṣo bhavanti |
yāvad āśāyā gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati ya āśāṃ brahmety upāste |
asti bhagava āśāyā bhūya iti |
āśāyā bhūyo 'stīti |
tan me bhagavān bravītv iti || ChUp_7,14.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates on hope as <s>Brahman</s> — by hope, all his desires are fulfilled. His prayers become unfailing. As far as the reach of hope extends, so far does he have freedom of movement — he who meditates on hope as <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Is there something greater than hope, Blessed One?' 'There is indeed something greater than hope.' 'Please tell me that, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.14.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,14.2 yastvāśāṃ brahmetyupāste śṛṇu tasya phalam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.14.2:] He who meditates on hope as <s>Brahman</s> — hear his fruit.

children.text: āśayā sadopāsitayāsyopāsakasya sarve kāmāḥ samṛdhyanti samṛddhiṃ gacchanti /
children.translated_text: By hope, constantly meditated upon, all desires of this worshipper are fulfilled — they reach fulfilment.

children.text: amoghā hāsyā'śiṣaḥ prārthanāḥ sarvā bhavanti yatprārthitaṃ sarvaṃ tadavaśyaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: His prayers — all his petitions — become unfailing; meaning that whatever is prayed for, all of that inevitably comes to be.

children.text: yāvadāśāyā gatamityādi pūrvavat //2//
children.translated_text: 'As far as the reach of hope' and so forth — as before. (2)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya caturdaśa khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,15.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.15.1]

children.text:
prāṇo vāva āśāyā bhūyān |
yathā vā arā nābhau samarpitā evam asmin prāṇe sarvaṃ samarpitam |
prāṇaḥ prāṇena yāti |
prāṇaḥ prāṇaṃ dadāti |
prāṇāya dadāti |
prāṇo ha pitā |
prāṇo mātā |
prāṇo bhrātā |
prāṇaḥ svasā |
prāṇa ācāryaḥ |
prāṇo brāhmaṇaḥ || ChUp_7,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is indeed greater than hope. Just as all the spokes are fixed in the hub [of a wheel], so in this <s>prāṇa</s> everything is fixed. <s>Prāṇa</s> moves by <s>prāṇa</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> gives <s>prāṇa</s>. One gives to <s>prāṇa</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the father. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the mother. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the brother. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the sister. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the teacher. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' (ChUp 7.15.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,15.1 nāmopakramamāśāntaṃ kāryakāraṇatvena nimittanaimittikatvena cottarottarabhūyastayāvasthitaṃ smṛtinimittasadbhāvamāśāraśanāpāśairvipāśitaṃ sarvaṃ sarvato bisamiva tantubhiryasminprāṇe samarpitam /
yena ca sarvato vyāpināntarbahirgatena sūtre maṇigaṇā iva sūtreṇa grathitaṃ vidhṛtaṃ ca /
sa eṣa prāṇo vā āśāyā bhūyān /
kathamasya bhūyastvamityāha dṛṣṭāntena samarthayaṃstadbhūyastvam /
yathā vai loke rathacakrasyārā rathanābhau samarpitāḥ saṃprotāḥ saṃpraveśitā ityetat /
evamasmiṃlliṅgasaṃghātarūpe prāṇe prajñātmani dehike mukhye yasminparā devatā nāmarūpavyākaraṇāyā'darśādau pratibimbivajjīvenā'tmanānupratiṣṭā /
yaśca mahārājasyeva sarvādhikārīśvarasya /
"kasminnannvahamutkrānta utkrānto baviṣyāmi kasminvā pratiṣṭhite pratiṣṭhāsyāmīti sa prāṇamasṛjata"iti śruteḥ yastu cchāyevānugata īśvaram /
"tadyathā rathasyāreṣu nemirarpito nābhāvarā arpitā evamevaitā bhūtamātrāḥ prajñāmātrāsvarpitāḥ prajñāmātrāḥ prāṇe 'rpitāḥ /
" "sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmā"iti kauṣītakinām /
ata evamasminprāṇe sarvaṃ yathoktaṃ samarpitam /
ataḥ sa eṣa prāṇo 'paratantraḥ prāṇena svaśaktyaiva yāti nānyakṛtaṃ gamanādikriyāsvasya sāmarthyamityarthaḥ /
sarvaṃ kriyākārakaphalabhedajātaṃ prāṇa eva na prāṇādbahirbhūtamastīti prakaraṇārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The entire range of actions, agents, and results — all belongs to <s>prāṇa</s> alone; nothing exists outside of <s>prāṇa</s> — this is the purport of the passage.

children.text: prāṇaḥ prāṇaṃ dadāti yaddadāti tatsvītmabhūtameva /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> gives <s>prāṇa</s> — whatever it gives is its own self.

children.text: yasmai dadāti tadapi prāṇāyaiva /
children.translated_text: To whomever it gives, that too is for <s>prāṇa</s> alone.

children.text: ataḥ pitrādyākhyo 'pi prāṇa eva //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even what is called father and the rest is nothing but <s>prāṇa</s>. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.15.1:] The entire [series] beginning with name (<s>nāma</s>) and ending with hope (<s>āśā</s>), established in a succession of cause and effect, of ground and consequence — each progressively greater — [all of this], whose existence is caused by memory, unbound by the ropes of the cord of hope — all of it, like lotus fibres with their threads, is fixed in this <s>prāṇa</s>. And by that [<s>prāṇa</s>], which pervades everything, entering within and without, like gems strung on a thread, [everything] is threaded together and upheld. This <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed greater than hope. How is its greatness? — he says, supporting that greatness with an illustration. Just as in the world the spokes of a chariot wheel are fixed — inserted, interwoven — in the hub of the chariot. So too, in this <s>prāṇa</s>, which is of the nature of the aggregate of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), in the embodied conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>), the supreme deity — who for the purpose of differentiating name and form has established itself through the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) like a reflection in a mirror and the like. And who, like the chief minister of a great king, [governs all]. As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'In what [being] shall I, when departed, be departed? In what [being], when established, shall I be established? — He created <s>prāṇa</s>.' And who follows the Lord like a shadow. [As stated in] the <s>Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad</s>: 'Just as the rim is fixed in the spokes and the spokes are fixed in the hub, so these elemental essences (<s>bhūtamātrā</s>) are fixed in the cognitive essences (<s>prajñāmātrā</s>), and the cognitive essences are fixed in <s>prāṇa</s>.' 'This <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed the conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>).' Therefore, in this <s>prāṇa</s>, everything as described is fixed. Hence this <s>prāṇa</s>, being independent, moves by its own power alone — the meaning is that its capacity for activities such as movement is not produced by another.

children.text: START ChUp 7,15.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.15.2]

children.text:
sa yadi pitaraṃ vā mātaraṃ vā bhrātaraṃ vā svasāraṃ vācāryaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā kiṃcid bhṛśam iva pratyāha |
dhik tvāstv ity evainam āhuḥ |
pitṛhā vai tvam asi mātṛhā vai tvam asi bhrātṛhā vai tvam asi svasṛhā vai tvam asy ācāryahā vai tvam asi brāhmaṇahā vai tvam asīti || ChUp_7,15.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'If one speaks somewhat harshly to one's father, mother, brother, sister, teacher, or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, people say to him: "Shame on you! You are a slayer of your father! You are a slayer of your mother! You are a slayer of your brother! You are a slayer of your sister! You are a slayer of your teacher! You are a slayer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>!"' (ChUp 7.15.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,15.2 kathaṃ pitrādiśabdānāṃ prasiddhārthotsargeṇa prāṇaviṣayatvamiti /
ucyate - sati prāṇe pitrādiṣu pitrādiśabdaprayogāttadutkrāntau ca prayogābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: The answer is: because the words 'father' and the rest are used when <s>prāṇa</s> is present in [those called] father and the rest, and are not used when it has departed.

children.text: kathaṃ tadityāha /
children.translated_text: How so? The text explains:

children.text: sa yaḥ kaścitpitrādīnāmanyatamaṃ yadi taṃ bhṛśamiva tadananurūpamiva kiñcidvacanaṃ tvaṅkārādiyuktaṃ pratyāha tadainaṃ pārśvasthā āhurvivekino dhiktvāstu dhigastu tvāmityevam /
children.translated_text: If anyone speaks somewhat harshly — speaks some word accompanied by the familiar 'thou' and the like, inappropriate [in tone] — to any one of the father and the rest, then the bystanders who are discerning say to him: 'Shame on you! Shame upon you!'

children.text: pitṛhā vai tvaṃ piturhantetyādi //2 //
children.translated_text: 'You are a slayer of your father' — meaning, a killer of your father — and so on. (2)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.15.2:] How can the words 'father' and the rest, by abandoning their well-known meanings, refer to <s>prāṇa</s>?

children.text: START ChUp 7,15.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.15.3]

children.text:
atha yady apy enān utkrāntaprāṇāñ chūlena samāsaṃ vyatiṣaṃdahet |
naivainaṃ brūyuḥ pitṛhāsīti na mātṛhāsīti na bhrātṛhāsīti na svasṛhāsīti nācāryahāsīti na brāhmaṇahāsīti || ChUp_7,15.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'But if, when the <s>prāṇa</s> has departed from them, one were to pierce them together with a spike and burn them, no one would say to him: "You are a slayer of your father," or "You are a slayer of your mother," or "You are a slayer of your brother," or "You are a slayer of your sister," or "You are a slayer of your teacher," or "You are a slayer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>."' (ChUp 7.15.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,15.3 athainānevotkrāntaprāṇāṃstyaktadehānatha yadyapi śūlena samāsaṃ samasya vyatidahedvyatyasya saṃdahedevamapyatikrūraṃ karma samāsavyatyāsādiprakāreṇa dahanalakṣaṇaṃ taddehasaṃbaddhameva kurvāṇaṃ naivainaṃ brūyuḥ pitṛhetyādi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.15.3:] But these very same [persons], when the <s>prāṇa</s> has departed, when they have left the body — even if one were to pierce them together on a spike and burn them — even though performing such an extremely cruel act — burning — connected with those very bodies, in the manner of piercing together and arranging — no one would say to him 'You are a slayer of your father' and so on.

children.text: tasmādanvayavyatirekābhyāmavagamyata etatpitrādyākhyo 'pi prāṇa eveti //3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the method of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), it is understood that what is called 'father' and the rest is indeed nothing but <s>prāṇa</s>. (3)

children.text: START ChUp 7,15.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.15.4]

children.text:
prāṇo hy evaitāni sarvāṇi bhavati |
sa vā eṣa evaṃ paśyann evaṃ manvāna evaṃ vijānann ativādī bhavati |
taṃ ced brūyur ativādy asīti |
ativādy asmīti brūyāt |
nāpahnuvīta || ChUp_7,15.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'For <s>prāṇa</s> indeed becomes all these. He who sees thus, thinks thus, and knows thus becomes an <s>ativādin</s> (one who speaks transcendentally). If they should say to him: "You are an <s>ativādin</s>," he should say: "I am an <s>ativādin</s>." He should not deny it.' (ChUp 7.15.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,15.4 tasmātprāṇo hyevaitāni pitrādīni sarvāṇi bhavati calāni sthirāṇi ca /
sa vā eṣa prāṇavidevaṃ yathoktaprakāreṇa paśyanphalato 'nubhavannevaṃ manvāna upapattibhiścintayannevaṃ vijānannupapattibhiḥ saṃyojyaivameveti niścayaṃ kurvannityarthaḥ /
mananavijñānābhyāṃ hi saṃbhūtaḥ śāsrārtho niścito dṛṣṭo bhavet /
ata evaṃ paśyannativādī bhavati nāmādyāśāntamatītya vadanaśīlo bhavatītyarthaḥ /

taṃ cedbrūyustaṃ yadyevamativādinaṃ sarvadā sarvaiḥ śabdairnāmādyāśāntamatītya vartamānaṃ prāṇamevaṃ vadantamevaṃ paśyantamativadanaśīlamativādinaṃ brahmādistambaparyantasya hi jagataḥ prāṇa ātmāhamiti bruvāṇaṃ yadi brūyurativādyasīti /
children.translated_text: If they should say to him — if to such an <s>ativādin</s>, who always, with all words, transcends the [series from] name through hope, who thus speaks, thus sees, regarding <s>prāṇa</s> — who is prone to transcendent speech — who is an <s>ativādin</s> — who says 'I am the self of the entire world from <s>Brahmā</s> to a blade of grass, for <s>prāṇa</s> is the lord of all' — if they were to say 'You are an <s>ativādin</s>,'

children.text: bāḍhamativādyasmīti brūyānnāpahnuvīta /
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, I am an <s>ativādin</s>' — thus he should say; he should not deny it.

children.text: kasmāddhyasāvapahnuvīta /
children.translated_text: Why indeed should he deny it?

children.text: yatprāṇaṃ sarveśvaramayamahamasmītyātmatvenopagataḥ //4//
children.translated_text: Because he has accepted as his own self <s>prāṇa</s>, the lord of all — 'I am that.' (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.15.4:] Therefore, <s>prāṇa</s> indeed becomes all these — father and the rest — both moving and stationary. He, the knower of <s>prāṇa</s>, who sees thus — experiences the fruit in the manner described — who thinks thus — reflects through reasoning — who knows thus — combining with reasoning, arrives at certainty — this is the meaning. For through reflection and knowledge, the meaning of the scripture, being ascertained, would be truly seen. Thus seeing, he becomes an <s>ativādin</s> (one who transcends in speech) — meaning he becomes one whose nature is to speak transcending the [series from] name through hope.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya pañcadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,16.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.16.1]

children.text:
eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivadati |
so 'haṃ bhagavaḥ satyenātivadānīti |
satyaṃ tveva vijijñāsitavyam iti |
satyaṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,16.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'But he truly speaks transcendentally who speaks transcendentally with truth (<s>satya</s>).' 'I, Blessed One, would speak transcendentally with truth.' 'But truth indeed must be sought to be known.' 'I seek to know truth, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.16.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,16.1 sa eṣa nāradaḥ sarvātiśayaṃ prāṇaṃ svamātmānaṃ sarvātmānaṃ śrutvā nātaḥ paramastītyupararāma /
na pūrvavatkimasti bhagavaḥ prāṇādbhūya iti papraccha /
yatastamevaṃ vikārānṛtabrahmavijñānena parituṣṭamakṛtārthaṃ paramārthasatyātivādinamātmānaṃ manyamānaṃ yogyaṃ śiṣyaṃ mithyāgrahaviśeṣādvipracyāvayannāha bhagavānsanatkumāraḥ /
eṣa tu vā ativadati yamahaṃ vakṣyāmi na prāṇavidativādī paramārthataḥ /
nāmādyapekṣaṃ tu tasyātivāditvam /
yastu bhūmākhyaṃ sarvātikrāntaṃ tattvaṃ paramārthasatyaṃ veda so 'tivādītyata āha-eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ sateyana paramārthasatyavijñānavattayātivadati /
children.translated_text: But he who knows the reality called <s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite), which transcends everything, which is the ultimate truth — he is the [true] <s>ativādin</s>. Therefore the text says: 'But this one truly speaks transcendentally — who speaks transcendentally through truth' — through possessing the knowledge of ultimate truth.

children.text: so 'haṃ tvāṃ prapanno bhagavansatyenātivadāni tathāmāṃ niyunaktu bhagavānyathāhaṃ satyenātivadānītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I, having taken refuge in you, Blessed One, would speak transcendentally with truth — please direct me, Blessed One, so that I may speak transcendentally with truth' — this is the purport.

children.text: yadyevaṃ satyenātivaditumicchasi satyameva tu tāvadvijijñāsitavyamityukta āha nāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If you thus wish to speak transcendentally with truth, then truth indeed must first be sought to be known' — being thus told, <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: tathāstu tarhi satya bhagavo vijijñāse viśeṣeṇa jñātumiccheyaṃ tvatto 'hamiti //1//
children.translated_text: 'So be it then — I seek to know truth, Blessed One; I wish to know it specially, from you.' (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.16.1:] That <s>Nārada</s>, having heard that <s>prāṇa</s> is his own self, the self of all, surpassing everything, ceased [questioning], thinking 'There is nothing higher than this.' He did not ask, as before, 'Is there something greater than <s>prāṇa</s>, Blessed One?' Therefore, [seeing] him satisfied with the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> as a modification that is unreal — considering himself an <s>ativādin</s> of ultimate truth while being an unfulfilled, fit student — the Blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, dislodging him from this particular false conviction, said: 'But this one truly speaks transcendentally' — the one whom I shall describe, not the knower of <s>prāṇa</s> who is an <s>ativādin</s> in the ultimate sense. His being an <s>ativādin</s> is only relative to [the series from] name and the rest.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya ṣoḍaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,17.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.17.1]

children.text:
yadā vai vijānāty atha satyaṃ vadati |
nāvijānan satyaṃ vadati |
vijānann eva satyaṃ vadati |
vijñānaṃ tv eva vijijñāsitavyam iti |
vijñānaṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,17.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'When one truly understands, then one speaks truth. One who does not understand does not speak truth. Only one who understands speaks truth. But understanding (<s>vijñāna</s>) indeed must be sought to be known.' 'I seek to know understanding, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.17.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,17.1 yadā vai satyaṃ paramārthato vijānātīdaṃ paramārthaḥ satyamiti, tato 'nṛtaṃ vikārajātaṃ vācārambhaṇaṃ hitvā sarvavikārāvasthaṃ sadevaikaṃ satyamiti tadevātha vadati yadvadati /
nanu vikāro 'pi satyameva /
"nāmarūpe satyaṃ tābhya mayaṃ prāṇaśchannaḥ" /
"prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣāmeṣa satyam"iti śrutyantarāt /
satyamuktaṃ satyatvaṃ śrutyantare vikārasya na tu paramārthāpekṣamuktaṃ kiṃ tarhīndriyaviṣayatvāpekṣaṃ sacca tyacceti satyamityuktaṃ taddvāreṇa ca paramārthasatyasyopalabdhirvivakṣiteti /
prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣāmeṣa satyamiti coktam /
ihāpi tadiṣṭameva /
iha tu praṇaviṣayātparamārthasatyavijñānābhimānādvyutthāpya nāradaṃ yatsadeva satyaṃ paramārthato bhūmākhyaṃ tadvijñāpayiṣyāmītyeṣa viśeṣato vivakṣitor'thaḥ /
nāvijānansatyaṃ vadati yastvavijānanvadati so 'gnyādiśabdenāgnyadīnparamārthasadrūpānmanyamāno vadati na tu te rūpatrayavyatirekeṇa paramārthaḥ santi /
tathā tānyapi rūpāṇi sadapekṣayā naiva santītyato nāvijānansatyaṃ vadati /
vijānanneva satyaṃ vadati /
children.translated_text: Only one who understands speaks truth.

children.text: na ca tatsatyavijñānamavijijñāsitamaprārthitaṃ jñāyata ityāha-vijñānaṃ tveva vijijñāsitavyamiti /
children.translated_text: And that knowledge of truth cannot be known without seeking it, without desiring it — therefore the text says: 'Understanding indeed must be sought to be known.'

children.text: yadyevaṃ vijñānaṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti /
children.translated_text: 'If that is so, I seek to know understanding, Blessed One.'

children.text: evaṃ satyādīnāṃ cottarottarāṇāṃ karotyantānāṃ pūrvapūrvahetutvaṃ vyākhyeyam //1//
children.translated_text: Thus, the causal relation of each successive [principle] — from truth onward — each ending in action (<s>kṛti</s>) — to each preceding one, should be explained [similarly]. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.17.1:] When one truly understands — when one understands the ultimate truth: 'This is the ultimate truth' — then, having abandoned the unreal, the entire collection of modifications that is merely a verbal designation, [knowing] that <s>Sat</s> (Being) alone in all its modifications is the one truth — then whatever one says, one speaks that. Objection: But modification too is real — [as the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'Name and form are real; <s>prāṇa</s>, concealed by them, [is real].' And from another <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Prāṇas</s> are truth; their [ground] is the truth [of truth].' [Reply:] The reality attributed to modification in other <s>śruti</s> passages is not stated with reference to ultimate reality; rather, it is stated with reference to being objects of the senses — '<s>sat</s> and <s>tyat</s> make <s>satya</s> (truth)' — and through that doorway, the apprehension of ultimate truth is intended. And it was also said: '<s>Prāṇas</s> are truth; their [ground] is the truth [of truth].' Here too, that very [principle] is intended. But here, the specific intended meaning is: dislodging <s>Nārada</s> from his pride in knowing the ultimate truth regarding <s>prāṇa</s> [as a modification], 'I shall make him understand the reality called <s>Bhūman</s>, which is <s>Sat</s> alone — the ultimate truth.' One who does not understand does not speak truth — one who, without understanding, speaks, speaks of fire and the rest by the words 'fire' and so on, regarding them as being of the nature of ultimate <s>Sat</s> — but they do not ultimately exist apart from the three colours. Similarly, even those colours do not exist with reference to <s>Sat</s> — therefore, one who does not understand does not speak truth.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya saptadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,18.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.18.1]

children.text:
yadā vai manute 'tha vijānāti |
nāmatvā vijānāti |
matvaiva vijānāti |
matis tv eva vijijñāsitavyeti |
matiṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,18.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'When one reflects (<s>manute</s>), then one understands. Without reflecting, one does not understand. Only by reflecting does one understand. But reflection (<s>mati</s>) indeed must be sought to be known.' 'I seek to know reflection, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.18.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,18.1 yadā vai manuta iti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.18.1:] 'When indeed one reflects' —

children.text: matirmananaṃ tarko mantavyaviṣaya ādaraḥ //1//
children.translated_text: <s>Mati</s> (reflection) is <s>manana</s> (deliberation), reasoning — earnest attention directed toward the subject of deliberation. (1)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasyāṣṭadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,19.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.19.1]

children.text:
yadā vai śraddadhāty atha manute |
nāśraddadhan manute |
śraddadhad eva manute |
śraddhā tv eva vijijñāsitavyeti |
śraddhāṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,19.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'When one has faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), then one reflects. Without faith, one does not reflect. Only with faith does one reflect. But faith indeed must be sought to be known.' 'I seek to know faith, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.19.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,19.1 āstikyabuddhiḥ śraddhā //1//
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.19.1:] Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is the conviction of [the existence and truth of things] — the attitude of belief (<s>āstikyabuddhi</s>). (1)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasyaikonaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,20.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.20.1]

children.text:
yadā vai nistiṣṭhaty atha śraddadhāti |
nānistiṣṭhañ chraddadhāti |
nistiṣṭhann eva śraddadhāti |
niṣṭhā tv eva vijijñāsitavyeti |
niṣṭhāṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,20.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'When one is steadfast (<s>nistiṣṭhati</s>), then one has faith. Without steadfastness, one does not have faith. Only with steadfastness does one have faith. But steadfastness (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) indeed must be sought to be known.' 'I seek to know steadfastness, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.20.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,20.1 niṣṭhā guruśuśrūṣādistatparatvaṃ brahmavijñānāya //1//
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.20.1:] <s>Niṣṭhā</s> (steadfastness) is devoted service to the teacher and such [practices] — single-minded dedication to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. (1)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya viṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,21.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.21.1]

children.text:
yadā vai karoty atha nistiṣṭhati |
nākṛtvā nistiṣṭhati |
kṛtvaiva nistiṣṭhati |
kṛtis tv eva vijijñāsitavyeti |
kṛtiṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,21.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'When one acts (<s>karoti</s>), then one is steadfast. Without acting, one is not steadfast. Only by acting is one steadfast. But action (<s>kṛti</s>) indeed must be sought to be known.' 'I seek to know action, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.21.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,21.1 yadā vai karoti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.21.1:] 'When indeed one acts' —

children.text: kṛtirindriyasaṃyamaścittaikāgratākaraṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛti</s> (action) is the restraint of the senses and the practice of one-pointedness of mind.

children.text: satyāṃ hi tasyāṃ niṣṭhādīni yathoktāni bhavanti vijñānāvasānāni //1//
children.translated_text: For when that [action] exists, steadfastness and the rest as described arise, culminating in understanding (<s>vijñāna</s>). (1)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasyaikaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,22.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.22.1]

children.text:
yadā vai sukhaṃ labhate 'tha karoti |
nāsukhaṃ labdhvā karoti |
sukham eva labdhvā karoti |
sukhaṃ tv eva vijijñāsitavyam iti |
sukhaṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,22.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'When one obtains happiness (<s>sukha</s>), then one acts. Without obtaining happiness, one does not act. Only upon obtaining happiness does one act. But happiness indeed must be sought to be known.' 'I seek to know happiness, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.22.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,22.1 sāpi kṛtiryadā sukhaṃ labhate sukhaṃ niratiśayaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ labdhavyaṃ mayeti manyate tadā bhavatītyarthaḥ /
yathā dṛṣṭaphalasukhā kṛtistathehāpi nāsukhaṃ labdhvā karoti /
bhaviṣyadapi phalaṃ labdhvetyucyate /
taduddiśya pravṛttyupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: because activity directed toward it is justified.

children.text: athedānīṃ kṛtyādiṣūttarottareṣu satsu satyaṃ svayameva pratibhāsata iti na tadvijñānāya pṛthagyatnaḥ kārya iti prāptaṃ tata idamucyate /
children.translated_text: Now, since when each successive [stage from Prāṇa onward] is present, truth itself shines forth spontaneously — it might be concluded that no separate effort is needed for its knowledge. Against this, the following is stated:

children.text: sukhaṃ tveva vijijñāsitavyamityādi /
children.translated_text: 'Happiness (sukha) is indeed to be inquired into' and so forth.

children.text: sukhaṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa ityabhimukhībhūtāyā'ha //1//
children.translated_text: 'I wish to know happiness, Blessed One' — thus he said, having turned [his attention] to it. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.22.1:] That action too [arises] when one obtains happiness — unsurpassable happiness, which will be described — the meaning is that when one thinks 'This [happiness] is to be obtained by me,' then [action] arises. Just as action whose fruit is seen [in this world brings] happiness, so too here — 'without obtaining happiness one does not act.' Even a future fruit is said to be 'obtained,'

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya dvāviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-second section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,23.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.23.1]

children.text:
yo vai bhūmā tat sukham |
nālpe sukham asti |
bhūmaiva sukham |
bhūmā tv eva vijijñāsitavya iti |
bhūmānaṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti || ChUp_7,23.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which is the Infinite (<s>Bhūman</s>) — that is happiness. There is no happiness in the finite. The Infinite alone is happiness. But the Infinite is to be inquired into.' 'I wish to know the Infinite, Blessed One.' (ChUp 7.23.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,23.1 yo vai bhūmā mahanniratiśayaṃ bahviti paryāyāstatsukham /
tator'vāksātiśayatvādalpam /
atastasminnalpe sukhaṃ nāsti /
alpasyādhikatṛṣṇāhetutvāt /
tṛṣṇā ca duḥkhabījaṃ /
na hi duḥkhabījaṃ sukhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ jvarādi loke /
children.translated_text: and craving is the seed of suffering. For in the world, that which is the seed of suffering — like fever and such — is never seen to be happiness.

children.text: tasmādyuktaṃ nālpe sukhamastīti /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is proper to say 'There is no happiness in the finite.'

children.text: ato bhūmaiva sukham /
children.translated_text: Hence the Infinite alone is happiness,

children.text: tṛṣṇādiduḥkhabījatvāsaṃbhavādbhūmnaḥ //1//
children.translated_text: because the Infinite cannot be the seed of suffering such as craving and the like. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.23.1:] That which is the <s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite) — great, unsurpassed, abundant — these are synonyms — that is happiness. Anything less than that, being surpassable, is finite. Therefore in that which is finite there is no happiness. Because the finite causes ever-greater craving,

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya trayoviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,24.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.24.1]

children.text:
yatra nānyat paśyati nānyac chṛṇoti nānyad vijānāti sa bhūmā |
atha yatrānyat paśyaty anyac chṛṇoty anyad vijānāti tad alpam |
yo vai bhūmā tad amṛtam |
atha yad alpaṃ tan martyam |
sa bhagavaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti |
sve mahimni yadi vā na mahimnīti || ChUp_7,24.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else — that is the Infinite. But where one sees something else, hears something else, knows something else — that is the finite. That which is the Infinite — that is immortal. But that which is finite — that is mortal.' 'On what, Blessed One, is it established?' 'In its own greatness — or perhaps not even in greatness.' (ChUp 7.24.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,24.1 kiṃlakṣaṇo 'sau bhūmetyāha-yatra yasminbhūmni tattve nānyaddraṣṭavyamanyena karaṇena draṣṭānyo vibhakto dṛśyātpaśyati /
tathā nānyacchṛṇoti /
nāmarūpayorevāntarbhāvādviṣayabhedasya tadgrāhakayoreveha darśanaśravaṇayorgrahaṇamanyeṣāṃ copalakṣaṇārthatvena /
mananaṃ cātroktaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ nānyanmanuta iti /
prāyaśo mananapūrvakatvādvijñānasya /
tathā nānyadvijānāti /
evaṃlakṣaṇo yaḥ sa bhūmā /
kimatra prasidrānyadarśanābhāvo bhūmnyucyate nānyatpaśyatītyādinā, athānyanna paśyatyātmānaṃ paśyatītyetat /
kiñcātaḥ /
yadyanyadarśanādyabhāvamātramityucyate tadā dvaitasaṃvyavahāravilakṣaṇo bhūmetyuktaṃ bhavati /
athānyadraśanaviśeṣapratiṣedhenā'tmānaṃ paśyatītyucyate tadaikasminneva kriyākārakaphalabhedo 'bhyupagato bhavet /
yadyevaṃ ko doṣaḥ syāt /
nanvayameva doṣaḥ saṃsārānivṛttiḥ /
kriyākārakaphalabhedo hi saṃsāra iti /
ātmaikatva eva kriyākārakaphalabhedaḥ saṃsāravilakṣaṇa iti cet /
na /
ātmano nirviśeṣaikatvābhyupagame darśanādikriyākārakaphalabhedābhyupagamasya śabdamātratvāt /
anyadarśanādyabhāvoktipakṣe 'pi yatretyanyanna paśyatīti ca viśeṣaṇe anarthake syātāmiti cet /
dṛśyate hi loke yatra śūnye gṛhe 'nyanna paśyatītyukte stambhādīnātmānaṃ ca na na paśyatīti gamyate /
evamihāpīti cet /
na /
tattvamasītyekatvopadeśādadhikaraṇādhikartavyabhedānupapatteḥ /
tathā sadekamevādvitīyaṃ satyamiti ṣaṣṭhe nirdhāritatvāt /
"adṛśye 'nātmye" "na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpamasya" "vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāt"ityādiśrutibhyaḥ svātmani darśanādyanupapattiḥ /
yatreti viśeṣaṇamanarthakaṃ prāptamiti cet /
na /
avidyākṛtabhedāpekṣatvāt /
yathā satyekatvādvitīyatvabuddhiṃ prakṛtāmapekṣya sadekamevādvitīyamiti saṃkhyādyanarhamapyucyate /
evaṃ bhūmnyekasminneva yatreti viśeṣaṇam /
avidyāvasthāyāmanyadarśanānuvādena ca bhūmnastadabhāvatvalakṣaṇasya vivakṣitatvānnānyatpaśyatīti viśeṣaṇam /
tasmātsaṃsāravyavahāro bhūmni nāstīti samudāyārthaḥ /
atha yatrāvidyāviṣaye 'nyo 'nyenānyatpaśyatīti tadalpamavidyākālabhāvītyarthaḥ /
yathā svapnadṛśyaṃ vastu prāk prabodhāttatkālabhāvīti tadvat /
tata eva tanmartyaṃ vināśi svapnavastuvadeva tadviparoto bhūmā yastadamṛtam /
tacchabdo 'mṛtatvaparaḥ /
sa tarhyevaṃlakṣaṇo bhūmā he bhagavankasminpratiṣṭhita ityuktavantaṃ nāradaṃ pratyāha sanatkimāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Then, O Blessed One, on what is this <s>Bhūman</s> of such characteristics established?' — thus addressed, <s>Sanatkumāra</s> replied to <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: sve mahimnīti sva ātmīye mahimni māhātmye vibhūtau pratiṣṭhito bhūmā /
children.translated_text: 'In its own greatness' — in its own glory, majesty, power — the <s>Bhūman</s> is established.

children.text: yadi pratiṣṭhāmicchasi kvacidyadi vā paramārthameva pṛcchasi na mahimnyapi pratiṣṭhita iti brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: If you desire a support [for it] somewhere — or if you are asking about the ultimate truth — we say it is not established even in greatness.

children.text: apratiṣṭhito 'nāśrito bhūmā kvacidapītyarthaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhūman</s> is unsupported — not dependent on anything whatsoever — that is the meaning. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.24.1:] What is the nature of this Infinite? He says — 'Where' — in which reality, the <s>Bhūman</s>, one does not see another — the seer, being distinct from the seen, does not see [another] by another instrument. Similarly, one does not hear another. Since all diversity of objects is included within name and form, only seeing and hearing — which grasp them — are mentioned here, with the others [implied] by way of indication. Reflection is also mentioned here as to be understood — 'he does not think another.' Because knowledge is generally preceded by reflection. Similarly, 'he does not know another.' That which has this characteristic — that is the <s>Bhūman</s>. [The question arises:] Is it the well-known absence of seeing another that is called <s>Bhūman</s> in 'he does not see another' and so forth? Or rather — he does not see another [because] he sees the Self? What follows from this? If the mere absence of seeing another and the rest is what is meant, then it is being said that the <s>Bhūman</s> is different from the empirical dealings of duality. But if it is said that by negating the seeing of something particular, he sees the Self — then the distinction of action, instrument, and result would be admitted in one and the same [entity]. If so, what is the fault? Is not this very thing the fault — the non-cessation of saṃsāra? For the distinction of action, instrument, and result is saṃsāra. [If one says:] 'In the very oneness of the Self, the distinction of action, instrument, and result is different from saṃsāra' — no; because when the undifferentiated oneness of the Self is accepted, the admission of distinction of action, instrument, and result in seeing and the like becomes merely verbal. [If one objects:] 'Even in the position that states the absence of seeing another, the qualifications "where" and "he does not see another" would be purposeless' — [we reply:] it is seen in the world that when one says 'he does not see another in an empty house,' it is understood that he does not fail to see pillars and himself. Even so here, [one might think]. No — because of the teaching of oneness in 'That thou art,' the distinction of locus and agent is untenable. Similarly, because in the sixth [chapter] it has been established that 'Being is one alone without a second, the Truth.' From śrutis such as 'invisible, bodiless,' 'its form does not stand in [the range of] sight,' 'By what would one know the knower?' and so forth, seeing and the rest are untenable with respect to one's own Self. [If one says:] 'the qualification "where" would then be purposeless' — no, because it is with reference to the distinction created by avidyā (ignorance). Just as, even though [Being] is truly one, without a second, and not subject to enumeration, it is said 'Being is one alone without a second' — with reference to the presupposed notion [of multiplicity] — similarly, the qualification 'where' [applies] to the one <s>Bhūman</s> alone. And since what is intended is to characterize the <s>Bhūman</s> as lacking [duality], through the restatement of the seeing of another [as obtaining] in the state of ignorance, the qualification 'he does not see another' [is used]. Therefore, the overall meaning is: empirical transactions of saṃsāra do not exist in the <s>Bhūman</s>. But 'where' — in the domain of ignorance — one sees another by another, that is finite — meaning it exists only during the time of ignorance. Just as dream-objects exist only until awakening, being present only during that time — so too. Therefore, that is mortal, perishable, like dream-objects. The <s>Bhūman</s>, which is the opposite of that, is immortal. The word 'that' (tat) refers to immortality.

children.text: START ChUp 7,24.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.24.2]

children.text:
go 'śvam iha mahimety ācakṣate hastihiraṇyaṃ dāsabhāryaṃ kṣetrāṇy āyatanānīti |
nāham evaṃ bravīmi |
bravīmīti hovāca |
anyo hy anyasmin pratiṣṭhita iti || ChUp_7,24.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Here in [the world] they call cows and horses "greatness," elephants, gold, servants, wives, fields, and dwellings. I do not speak thus,' he said. 'For in that case, one thing would be established in another.' (ChUp 7.24.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,24.2 yadi svamahimni pratiṣṭhito bhūmā kathaṃ tarhyapratiṣṭha ucyate /
śṛṇu /
go 'śvādīha mahimetyācakṣate /
children.translated_text: Here in [the world], cows and horses and so forth are called 'greatness.'

children.text: gāvaścāśvāśca go 'śvaṃ dvandvaikavadbhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Cows and horses' (go'śva) is a dvandva compound treated as singular.

children.text: sarvatra gavāśvādi mahimeti prasiddhaṃ tadāśritastatpratiṣṭhaścaitro bhavati, yathā nāhamevaṃ svato 'nyaṃ mahimānamāśrito bhūmā caitravaditi bravīmyatra hetutvenānyo hyanyasminpratiṣṭhita iti vyavahitena sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Everywhere, cows, horses, and the like are well-known as 'greatness'; someone dependent upon them and established in them — like <s>Caitra</s> [who is wealthy] — becomes [so]. 'I do not speak thus — [saying that] the <s>Bhūman</s> depends on some greatness other than itself, like <s>Caitra</s>' — and here, as the reason, the connection is with the distant [clause]: 'for one thing would be established in another.'

children.text: kintvevaṃ bravīmīti hovāca-sa evetyādi //2//
children.translated_text: 'But I speak thus,' he said — 'He is' and so forth. (2)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.24.2:] If the <s>Bhūman</s> is established in its own greatness, how then is it said to be unsupported? Listen.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya caturviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,25.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.25.1]

children.text:
sa evādhastāt sa upariṣṭāt sa paścāt sa purastāt sa dakṣiṇataḥ sa uttarataḥ |
sa evedaṃ sarvam iti |
athāto 'haṃkārādeśa eva |
aham evādhastād aham upariṣṭād ahaṃ paścād ahaṃ purastād ahaṃ dakṣiṇato 'ham uttarato 'ham evedaṃ sarvam iti || ChUp_7,25.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'He (<s>Bhūman</s>) alone is below. He is above. He is behind. He is in front. He is to the south. He is to the north. He alone is all this.' Now, the instruction through the sense of 'I': 'I alone am below. I am above. I am behind. I am in front. I am to the south. I am to the north. I alone am all this.' (ChUp 7.25.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,25.1 kasmātpunaḥ kvacinna pratiṣṭhita ityucyate /
yasmātsa eva bhūmādhastānna tadvyatirekeṇānyadvidyate yasminpratiṣṭhitaḥ syāt /
tathopariṣṭādityādi samānam /
sati bhūmno 'nyasminbhūmā hi pratiṣṭhitaḥ syānna tu tadasti /
sa eva tu sarvam /
children.translated_text: He alone is everything.

children.text: atastasmādasau na kvacitpratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not established anywhere.

children.text: yatra nānyatpaśyatītyadhikaraṇādhikartavyatānirdeśātsa evādhastāditi ca parokṣanirdeśāddraṣṭarjīvādanyobhūmā syādityāśaṅkā kasyacinmā bhūdityathāto 'nantaramahaṅkārādeśo 'haṅkāreṇā'diśyata ityahaṅkārādeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Lest anyone doubt — from the expressions 'where one does not see another' [using third-person/locative] and 'He alone is below' [using third person] — that the <s>Bhūman</s> is other than the seer, the <s>jīva</s>: therefore, immediately after, the instruction through the 'I'-sense (<s>ahaṅkārādeśa</s>) — that which is indicated by the ego-sense — is given.

children.text: draṣṭurananyatvadarśanārthaṃ bhūmaiva nirdiśyate 'haṅkāreṇāhamevādhastādityādinā //1 //
children.translated_text: To show the non-difference of the seer [from <s>Bhūman</s>], the <s>Bhūman</s> itself is indicated through the ego-sense: 'I alone am below' and so forth. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.25.1:] Why again is it said that [the <s>Bhūman</s>] is not established anywhere? Because that very <s>Bhūman</s> is [all that is] below — there exists nothing other than it in which it could be established. Similarly above, and so forth — the same [applies]. If there were something other than the <s>Bhūman</s>, then the <s>Bhūman</s> would be established [in that]; but that does not exist.

children.text: START ChUp 7,25.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.25.2]

children.text:
athāta ātmādeśa eva |
ātmaivādhastād ātmopariṣṭād ātmā paścād ātmā purastād ātmā dakṣiṇata ātmottarata ātmaivedaṃ sarvam iti |
sa vā eṣa evaṃ paśyann evaṃ manvāna evaṃ vijānann ātmaratir ātmakrīḍa ātmamithuna ātmānandaḥ sa svarāḍ bhavati |
tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati |
atha ye 'nyathāto vidur anyarājānas te kṣayyalokā bhavanti |
teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣv akāmacāro bhavati || ChUp_7,25.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the instruction through the Self: The Self alone is below. The Self is above. The Self is behind. The Self is in front. The Self is to the south. The Self is to the north. The Self alone is all this. He who sees thus, reflects thus, knows thus — he delights in the Self, he plays in the Self, he unites with the Self, he rejoices in the Self. He becomes self-sovereign. He has freedom of movement in all worlds. But those who know otherwise than this — they are ruled by others, theirs are perishable worlds. They have no freedom of movement in all worlds.' (ChUp 7.25.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,25.2 ahaṅkāreṇa dehādisaṃghāto 'pyādiśyate 'vivekibhirityatastadāśaṅkā mā bhūdityathānantaramātmādeśa ātmanaiva kevalena satsvarūpeṇa śuddhenā'diśyate /
ātmaiva sarvataḥ sarvamityevamekamajaṃ sarvato vyomavatpūrṇamanyaśūnyaṃ paśyansa vā eṣa vidvānmananavijñānābhyāmātmaratirātmanyeva ratī ramaṇaṃ yasya so 'yamātmaratiḥ /
tathā'tmakrīḍaḥ /
dehamātrasādhanā ratirbāhyasādhanā krīḍā /
loke srībhiḥ sakhibhiśca krīḍatīti darśanāt na tathā viduṣaḥ kiṃ tarhyātmavijñānanimittamevobhayaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
mithunaṃ dvaṃndvajanitaṃ sukhaṃ tadapi dvandvanirapekṣaṃ yasya viduṣaḥ /
tathā'tmānandaḥ śabdādinimitta ānando 'viduṣāṃ na tathāsya viduṣaḥ kiṃ tarhyātmanimittameva sarvaṃ sarvadā sarvaprakāreṇa ca dehajīvitabhogādinimittabāhyavastunirapekṣa ityarthaḥ /
sa evaṃlakṣaṇo vidvāñjīvanneva svārājye 'bhiṣiktaḥ patite 'pi dehe svarāḍeva bhavati /
yata evaṃ bhavati tata eva tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati /
prāṇādiṣu pūrvabhūmiṣu tatrāsyeti tāvanmātraparicchinnakāmacāratvamuktamanrājatvaṃ cārthaprāptaṃ sātiśayatvādyathāprāptasvārājyakāmacāratvānuvādena tatannivṛttirihocyate sa svarāḍityādinā /
atha punarye 'nyathāta uktadarśanādanyathā vaiparītyena yathoktameva vā samyaṅna viduste 'nyarājāno bhavanti anyaḥ paro rājā svāmī yeṣāṃ te 'nyarājānaste /
children.translated_text: But those who know otherwise than this — differently from the vision described, or contrarily, or who do not know properly even what has been described — they become ruled by others — 'another' is a master, a lord over them, they are <s>anyarājānas</s> (ruled by others).

children.text: kiñca kṣayyo loko yeṣāṃ te kṣayylokāḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, theirs are perishable worlds — they are <s>kṣayyalokas</s> (those with perishable worlds).

children.text: bhedadarśanasyālpaviṣayatvādalpaṃ ca tanmartyamityavocāma /
children.translated_text: Since the vision of difference pertains to the finite — and we said 'that which is finite is mortal' —

children.text: tasmādye dvaitadarśinaste kṣayyalokāḥ svadarśanānurūpyeṇaiva bhavantyata eva teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣvakāmacāro bhavati //2//
children.translated_text: therefore those who see duality have perishable worlds — in accordance with their own vision. And therefore they have no freedom of movement in all worlds. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.25.2:] Since the undiscriminating also indicate the aggregate of body and so forth by the ego-sense — lest that [misunderstanding arise] — therefore, immediately after, the instruction through the Self (<s>ātmādeśa</s>): it is indicated by the Self alone — the pure, essential nature of Being. 'The Self alone is everything everywhere' — he who sees thus — one, unborn, full everywhere like space, void of anything else — this learned person, through reflection and knowledge, delights in the Self — his pleasure and enjoyment is in the Self alone — he is <s>ātmarati</s> (one who delights in the Self). Similarly, <s>ātmakrīḍa</s> (one who plays in the Self) — in worldly life, pleasure is [accomplished] with the body alone as the means, and play with external means; for in the world, one is seen to play with women and friends — but not so for the knower; rather, both [pleasure and play] arise solely from Self-knowledge — that is the meaning. <s>Ātmamithuna</s> — the happiness born of coupling — that too, for this knower, is independent of any pair. Similarly, <s>ātmānanda</s> (one whose bliss is in the Self) — for the ignorant, bliss arises from sound and other [objects]; not so for this knower; rather, everything for him, always, in every way, is solely caused by the Self, independent of external things such as body, life, enjoyments, and the like — that is the meaning. Such a knower, even while living, is anointed in self-sovereignty — and even when the body falls, he remains self-sovereign (<s>svarāṭ</s>). Because he is thus, therefore he has freedom of movement (<s>kāmacāra</s>) in all worlds. In the earlier stages concerning <s>prāṇa</s> and so forth, the statement 'so far does he have freedom of movement' indicated limited freedom according to each [level], and limited sovereignty was naturally implied; by restating the naturally obtained sovereignty and freedom of movement, their termination [in the <s>Bhūman</s>] is indicated here by 'He is self-sovereign' and so forth.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya pañcaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fifth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 7,26.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.26.1]

children.text: tasya ha vā etasyaivaṃ paśyata evaṃ manvānasyaivaṃ vijānata ātmataḥ prāṇa ātmata āśātmataḥ smara ātmata ākāśa ātmatas teja ātmata āpa ātmata āvirbhāvatirobhāvāv ātmato 'nnam ātmato balam ātmato vijñānam ātmato dhyānam ātmataś cittam ātmataḥ saṃkalpa ātmato mana ātmato vāg ātmato nāmātmato mantrā ātmataḥ karmāṇy ātmata evedaṃ sarvam iti || ChUp_7,26.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'For one who sees thus, reflects thus, knows thus — from the Self [arises] <s>prāṇa</s>, from the Self hope, from the Self memory, from the Self space, from the Self fire, from the Self water, from the Self appearance and disappearance, from the Self food, from the Self strength, from the Self knowledge, from the Self meditation, from the Self thought, from the Self will, from the Self mind, from the Self speech, from the Self name, from the Self sacred hymns, from the Self rituals — from the Self indeed is all this.' (ChUp 7.26.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_7,26.1 tasya ha vā etasyetyādi svārājyaṃ prāptasya prakṛtasya viduṣa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.26.1:] 'For one who sees thus' and so forth — the meaning is: for the knower under discussion who has attained self-sovereignty.

children.text: prāksadātmavijñānātsvātmano 'nyasmātsataḥ prāṇādernāmāntasyotpattipralayāvabhūtāṃ sadātmāvijñāne tu satīdānīṃ svātmata eva saṃvṛttau tathā sarvo 'pyanyo vyavahāra ātmata eva viduṣaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Prior to the knowledge of <s>Sat</s> as the Self, the origin and dissolution of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest up to name had been [perceived as coming] from something other than one's own Self — Being; but now, with the ignorance of <s>Sat</s> as the Self [dispelled], they have come to be from one's own Self. Similarly, all other empirical activity too is from the Self alone, for the knower. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 7,26.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.26.2]

children.text:
tad eṣa ślokaḥ |
na paśyo mṛtyuṃ paśyati na rogaṃ nota duḥkhatām |
sarvaṃ ha paśyaḥ paśyati sarvam āpnoti sarvaśaḥ |
iti |
sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavati pañcadhā |
saptadhā navadhā caiva punaś caikādaśa smṛtaḥ |
śataṃ ca daśa caikaś ca sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatiḥ |
āhāraśuddhau sattvaśuddhiḥ |
sattvaśuddhau dhruvā smṛtiḥ |
smṛtilambhe sarvagranthīnāṃ vipramokṣaḥ |
tasmai mṛditakaṣāyāya tamasas pāraṃ darśayati bhagavān sanatkumāraḥ |
taṃ skanda ity ācakṣate || ChUp_7,26.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'On this there is this verse: The seer does not see death, nor disease, nor suffering. The seer sees everything and attains everything in every way. He becomes onefold, threefold, fivefold, sevenfold, ninefold, and again elevenfold, a hundred and ten, and twenty thousand. Through the purity of food (<s>āhāra</s>), there is purity of the inner nature (<s>sattva</s>). Through purity of the inner nature, there is firm memory (<s>smṛti</s>). Upon the attainment of memory, there is the release from all knots. To him whose impurities have been crushed, the Blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s> shows the far shore beyond darkness. Him they call <s>Skanda</s>.' (ChUp 7.26.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_7,26.2 kiñca tadetasminnartha eṣa śloko mantro 'pi bhavati /
na paśyaḥ paśyatīti paśyo yathoktadarśī vidvānityarthaḥ /
mṛtyuṃ maraṇaṃ rogaṃ jvarādi duḥkhatāṃ duḥkhabhāvaṃ cāpi na paśyati /
sarvaṃ ha sarvameva sa paśyaḥ paśyatyātmānameva sarvaṃ tataḥ sarvamāpnoti sarvaśaḥ sarvaprakārairiti /
kiñca sa vidvānprāksṛṣṭiprabhedādekadhaiva bhavatyekadhaiva ca saṃsridhādibhedairanantabhedaprakāro bhavati sṛṣṭikāle /
punaḥ saṃhārakāle mūlameva svaṃ pāramārthakamekadhābhāvaṃ pratipadyate svatantra eveti vidyāṃ phalena prarocayanstauti /
athedānīṃ yathoktāyā vidyāyāḥ samyagavabhāsakāraṇaṃ mukhāvabhāsakāraṇasyevā'darśasya viśuddhikāraṇaṃ sādhanamupadiśyate-āhāraśuddhau /
āhriyata ityāhāraḥ śabdādiviṣayavijñānaṃ bhokturbhogāyā'hriyate viśuddhikāraṇaṃ sādhanamupadiśyate-āhāraśuddhau /
āhriyata ityāharaḥ śabdādiviṣayavijñānaṃ bhokturbhogāyā'hriyate tasya viṣayopalabdhilakṣaṇasya vijñānasya śuddhirāhāraśuddhī rāgadveṣamohadoṣairasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ viṣayavijñānamityarthaḥ /
tasyāmāhārāśuddhau satyāṃ tadvato 'ntaḥkaraṇasya sattvasya śuddhirnairmalyaṃ bhavati /
sattvaśuddhau ca satyāṃ yathāvagate bhūmātmani dhruvāvicchinnā smṛtiravismaramaṃ bhavati /
tasyāṃ ca labdhāyāṃ smṛtilambhe sati sarveṣāmavidyākṛtānarthapāśarūpāṇāmanekajanmāntarānubhavabhāvanākaṭhinīkṛtānāṃ hṛdayākṣayāṇāṃ granthīnāṃ vipramokṣo viśeṣeṇa pramokṣaṇaṃ vināśo bhavatīti /
yata etaduttarottaraṃ yathoktamāhāraśuddhimūlaṃ tasmātsā kāryetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since this [chain of results], each successively higher as described, is rooted in the purity of food — therefore, that [purity] must be accomplished; that is the meaning.

children.text: sarvaṃ śāsrārthamaśeṣata uktvā'khyāyikāmupasaṃharati śrutiḥ-tasmai mṛditakaṣāyāya vārkṣādiriva kaṣāyo rāgadveṣādidoṣaḥ sattvasya rañjanārūpatvātsa jñānavairāgyābhyāsarūpakṣāreṇa kṣālito mṛdito vināśito yasya nāradasya tasmai yogyāya mṛditakaṣāyāya tamaso 'vidyālakṣaṇātpāraṃ paramārthatattvaṃ darśayati darśitavānityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having stated the entire teaching of the scripture completely, the <s>śruti</s> concludes the narrative: 'To him whose impurities have been crushed' — just as the astringent quality of bark and the like, the defects of desire, aversion, and so on are the impurities of <s>sattva</s>, because they color [it]; these, washed and crushed — destroyed — by the alkali in the form of the practice of knowledge and dispassion — to that <s>Nārada</s>, who was thus qualified, whose impurities had been crushed, the far shore beyond the darkness characterized as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — the ultimate reality — [<s>Sanatkumāra</s>] shows, meaning he showed; that is the meaning.

children.text: ko 'sau, bhagavān-"utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva bhūtānāmāgatiṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: Who is he? The Blessed One — 'He who knows the origin and dissolution of beings, their coming and going,

children.text: vetti vidyāmavidyāṃ ca sa vācyo bhagavāniti //
children.translated_text: who knows knowledge and ignorance — he is to be called the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>).'

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 7.26.2:] Moreover, on this subject there is this verse — a <s>mantra</s> as well. 'The seer does not see' — 'the seer' (<s>paśyaḥ</s>) means one who sees as described, that is, the knower. He does not see death, disease such as fever and the like, nor the state of suffering. He who is a seer sees everything — he sees everything as the <s>Ātman</s> alone; therefore he attains everything, in every way, by all means. Moreover, that knower, before the differentiation of creation, exists as onefold alone, and through the differentiations of creation and the like, becomes of infinite variety in modes — at the time of creation. Again, at the time of dissolution, he returns to his own original, ultimate onefold state, being entirely autonomous — thus [the text] praises the knowledge by extolling it through its fruit. Now, the means (<s>sādhana</s>) that causes the proper illumination of the knowledge described — like the cause of purifying a mirror which is the cause of the illumination of the face — is taught: 'Through the purity of food (<s>āhāra</s>).' <s>Āhāra</s> (food) is what is brought (<s>āhriyate</s>) — the cognition of sense-objects such as sound, which is brought for the enjoyment of the enjoyer. The purity of that cognition, characterized by the apprehension of objects, is the purity of <s>āhāra</s> — meaning cognition of objects untainted by the defects of desire, aversion, and delusion. When there is such purity of <s>āhāra</s>, there is purity of <s>sattva</s> — clarity of the inner organ of one who possesses it. When there is purity of <s>sattva</s>, there is firm — unbroken — memory (<s>smṛti</s>), a constant remembrance of the <s>Bhūman</s> (Infinite), the <s>Ātman</s> as rightly understood. Upon its attainment — upon the attainment of memory — there is the release, the special liberation, the destruction of all knots — the knots of the heart, which are in the form of bonds of misfortune created by ignorance, hardened through habitual impressions of experiences across countless births.

children.text:
" evandharmā sanatkumāraḥ /
tameva sanatkumāraṃ devaṃ skanda ityācakṣate kathayanti tadvidaḥ /
dvirvacanamadhyāyaparisamāptyartham //2 // //
children.translated_text: The repetition is for the purpose of concluding the chapter. (2)
One of such qualities is <s>Sanatkumāra</s>. That very <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, the deity, those who know him call <s>Skanda</s>.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi saptamādhyāyasya ṣaḍviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth section of the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadbrahmaṇe saptamodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> with its <s>Brahmaṇa</s>.

children.text: atha aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the eighth chapter.

children.text: oṃ
