children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,1.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.1.1]

children.text:
atha yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminn antarākāsaḥ |
tasmin yad antas tad anveṣṭavyaṃ tad vāva vijijñāsitavyam iti || ChUp_8,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmapura</s>), there is a small (<s>dahara</s>) lotus-like abode. Within it is a small inner space. That which is within it — that is to be sought, that indeed is to be inquired into.' (ChUp 8.1.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,1.1
yadyapi digdeśakālādibhedaśūnyaṃ brahma sadekamevādvitīyamātmaivedaṃ sarvamiti ṣaṣṭhasaptamayoradhigataṃ tathāpīha mandabuddhīnāṃ digdeśādibhedavadvastvityevaṃ bhāvitā buddhirna śakyate sahasā paramārthaviṣayā kartumityanadhigamya ca brahma na puruṣārthasiddhiriti tadadhigamāya hṛdayapuṇḍarīkadeśa upadeṣṭavyaḥ /
yadyapi satsamyakpratyayaikaviṣayā kartumityānadhigamya ca brahma na puruṣārthasiddhiriti tadadhigamāya hṛdayapuṇḍarīkadeśa upadeṣṭavyaḥ /
yadyapi satsamyakpratyayaikaviṣayaṃ nirguṇaṃ cā'tmatattvaṃ tathāpi mandabuddhīnāṃ guṇavattvasyeṣṭatvātsatyakāmādiguṇavattvaṃ ca vaktavyam /
tathā yadyapi brahmavidāṃ stryādiviṣayebhyaḥ svayamevoparamo bhavati tathāpyanekajanmaviṣayasevābhyāsajanitā viṣayaviṣayā tṛṣṇā na sahasā nivartayituṃ śakyata iti brahmacaryādisādhanaviśeṣo vidhātavyaḥ /
tathā yadyapyātmaikatvavidāṃ gantṛgamanagantavyābhāvādavidyāviśeṣasthitinimittakṣaye gagana iva vidyududbhūta iva vāyurdagdhendhana ivāgniḥ svātmanyeva nivṛttistathāpi gantṛgamanādivāsitabuddhīnāṃ hṛdayadeśaguṇaviśiṣṭabrahmopāsakānāṃ mūrdhanyayā nāḍyā gatirvaktavyetyaṣṭamaḥ prapāṭhaka ārabhyate /
digdeśaguṇagatiphalabhedaśūnyaṃ hi paramārthasadadvayaṃ brahmamandabuddhīnāmasadiva pratibhāti /
sanmārgasthāstāvadbhavantu tataḥ śanaiḥ paramārthasadapi grāhayiṣyāmīti manyate śrutiḥ /
athānantaraṃ yadidaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ daharamalpaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ puṇḍarīkasadṛśaṃ veśmeva veśma dvārapālādimattvāt /
asminbrahmapure brahmaṇaḥ parasya puraṃ rājño 'nekaprakṛtimadyathāpuraṃ tathedamanekendriyamanobuddhibhiḥ svāmyarthakāribhiryuktamiti brahmapuram /
pure ca veśma rājño yathā tathā tasminbrahmapure śarīre daharaṃ veśma brahmaṇa upalabdhyadhiṣṭhānamityarthaḥ /
yathā viṣṇoḥ śālagrāmaḥ /
asminhi svavikāraśiṅge dehe nāmarūpavyākaraṇāya praviṣṭaṃ sadākhyaṃ braṅma jīvenā'tmanetyuktam /
tasmādasminhṛdayapuṇḍarīke veśmanyupasaṃhṛtakaraṇairbāhyaviṣayaviraktairviśeṣato brahmacaryasatyasādhanābhyāṃ yuktervakṣyamāṇaguṇavaddhyāyamānairbrahmopalabhyata iti prakaraṇārthaḥ /
daharo 'lpataro 'smindahare veśmani veśmano 'lpatvāttadantarvartino 'lpataratvaṃ veśmanaḥ /
antarākāśa ākāśākhyaṃ brahma /
ākāśo vai nāmeti hi vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: For it will be said: 'Its name is indeed space (<s>ākāśa</s>).'

children.text: ākāśa ivāśarīratvātsūkṣmatvasarvagatatvasāmānyācca /
children.translated_text: Because of the commonality of being bodiless, subtle, and all-pervading — like space.

children.text: tasminnākāśākhye yadantarmadhye tadanveṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Within that — in the middle of that which is designated as space — that is to be sought.

children.text: tadvāva tadeva ca viśeṣeṇa jijñāsitavyaṃ gurvāśrayaśravaṇādyupāyairanviṣya ca sākṣātkaraṇīyamityarthaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: That indeed is to be especially inquired into — through the means of approaching a teacher, listening, and so on; and having sought, it is to be directly realized — that is the meaning. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.1.1:] Although <s>Brahman</s> — being one, without a second, the <s>Ātman</s> itself as all this — devoid of distinctions of direction, place, time, and so on, has been understood in the sixth and seventh [chapters], nevertheless the intellect of those of dull understanding, being habituated to [thinking of] things as differentiated by direction, place, and so on, cannot suddenly be made to have ultimate reality as its object. And without comprehending <s>Brahman</s>, there is no attainment of the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). Therefore, for its comprehension, the location of the lotus of the heart must be taught. Although the reality of the <s>Ātman</s> is the sole object of correct cognition of <s>Sat</s> and is without qualities, still, since those of dull understanding desire it to possess qualities, the possession of qualities such as 'having true desires' (<s>satyakāma</s>) and so on must be stated. Likewise, although for knowers of <s>Brahman</s> there is naturally cessation [of attachment] to objects such as women, still, the craving directed toward objects, generated by the practice of serving objects over many births, cannot be suddenly stopped — therefore, specific means such as <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and the like must be enjoined. Likewise, although for knowers of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>, since there is no traveler, traveling, or destination, upon the cessation of the particular state of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), there is absorption into one's own self — like lightning in the sky, like wind when [its cause is] burnt, like fire when fuel is consumed — still, for those whose intellect is imbued with impressions of traveler, traveling, and so on — the worshippers of <s>Brahman</s> qualified by the location of the heart and specific attributes — departure through the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) at the top of the head must be stated. Thus the eighth chapter is commenced. For the ultimate reality of <s>Brahman</s>, which is non-dual <s>Sat</s>, devoid of distinctions of direction, place, attribute, destination, and fruit, appears as if non-existent to those of dull understanding. [The <s>śruti</s> thinks:] 'Let them first be established on the right path; then, gradually, I shall make them grasp even the ultimate <s>Sat</s>.' Now, that which is next [described]: in this city of <s>Brahman</s>, there is a small (<s>dahara</s>) lotus-like abode (<s>veśma</s>), resembling a lotus, like a house because it possesses door-keepers and the like. In this city of <s>Brahman</s> — the city of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — just as a king's city is endowed with many subjects, so this [body] is endowed with many sense organs, mind, and intellect, which serve the purpose of the master — hence it is the 'city of <s>Brahman</s>.' And just as in a city there is the king's abode, so in this city of <s>Brahman</s>, in the body, the small abode is <s>Brahman</s>'s place of apprehension and presiding — that is the meaning. Like <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>Śālagrāma</s>. For it has been said that <s>Sat</s>, called <s>Brahman</s>, having entered this body — its own modification, the horn [of the body] — for the purpose of manifesting name and form, [entered] 'with this living self (<s>jīva ātman</s>).' Therefore, in this lotus of the heart, the abode, <s>Brahman</s> is apprehended by those who have withdrawn their senses, who are detached from external objects, who are especially endowed with the means of <s>brahmacarya</s> and truth, meditating upon it as possessing the qualities to be described — this is the purport of the section. The inner space (<s>antarākāśa</s>) is smaller within this small abode — because the abode is small, what is contained within it is even smaller. The inner space is <s>Brahman</s> designated as space (<s>ākāśa</s>).

children.text: START ChUp 8,1.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.1.2]

children.text:
taṃ ced brūyur yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminn antarākāśaḥ kiṃ tad atra vidyate yad anveṣṭavyaṃ yad vāva vijijñāsitavyam iti |
sa brūyāt || ChUp_8,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'If they should ask him: "In this city of <s>Brahman</s>, there is this small lotus-like abode, and within it this small inner space — what is there within it that is to be sought, that is to be inquired into?" — he should say:' (ChUp 8.1.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,1.2 taṃ cedevamuktavantamācāryaṃ yadi brūyurantevāsinaścodayeyuḥ, kathaṃ, yadidamasminbrahmapure paricchinne 'ntardaharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma tato 'pyantaralpatara evā'kāśaḥ /
puṇḍarīka eva veśmani tāvatkiṃ syāt /
kiṃ tato 'lpatare khe yadbhavedityāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: What could exist in that even smaller space, they say.

children.text: daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ kiṃ tadatra vidyate na kiñcana vidyata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The small inner space within this — what is there within it?' — the implication being 'there is nothing there.'

children.text: yadi nāma badaramātraṃ kimapi vidyate kiṃ tasyānveṣaṇena vijijñāsanena vā phalaṃ vijijñāsituḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Even if something the size of a jujube fruit exists there, what fruit would the seeker gain from seeking it or inquiring into it?

children.text: ato yatttrānveṣṭavyaṃ vijijñāsitavyaṃ vā na tena prayojanamityuktavataḥ sa ācāryo brūyāditi śrutervacanam //2 //
children.translated_text: To one who has thus said 'there is no purpose in what is to be sought or inquired into there' — the teacher should reply — this is the statement of the <s>śruti</s>. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.1.2:] If they — the students — should say to the teacher who has thus spoken, should challenge him: How [can it be]? This city of <s>Brahman</s> is limited, and within it the small lotus-like abode, and within that an even smaller space. Even in the lotus-abode itself, what could there be?

children.text: START ChUp 8,1.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.1.3]

children.text:
yāvān vā ayam ākāśas tāvān eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ |
ubhe 'smin dyāvāpṛthivī antar eva samāhite |
ubhāv agniś ca vāyuś ca sūryācandramasāv ubhau vidyun nakṣatrāṇi |
yac cāsyehāsti yac ca nāsti sarvaṃ tad asmin samāhitam iti || ChUp_8,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'As vast as this [external] space, so vast is this space within the heart. In it are contained both heaven and earth, both fire and wind, both sun and moon, lightning and stars. Whatever of his exists here [in this world] and whatever does not — all that is contained in it.' (ChUp 8.1.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,1.3 śṛṇuta /
tatra yadbrūtha puṇḍarīkāntaḥkhasyālpatvāttatsthamalpataraṃ syāditi /
tadasat /
na hi khaṃ puṇḍarīkaveśamagataṃ puṇḍarīkādalpataraṃ matvāvocaṃ daharo 'rsminnantarākāśa iti /
kiṃ tarhi puṇḍarīkamalpaṃ tadanuvidhāyi tatsthamantaḥkaraṇaṃ puṇḍarīkākāśaparicchinnaṃ tasminviśuddhe saṃhṛtakaraṇānāṃ yogināṃ svaccha ivodake pratibimbarūpamādarśa iva ca śuddhe svacchaṃ vijñānajyotiḥ svarūpāvabhāsaṃ tāvanmātraṃ brahmopalabhyata iti daharo 'sminnantarākāśa ityavocāmāntaḥkaraṇopādhinimittam /
svatastu yāvānvai prasiddhaḥ parimāṇato 'yamākāśo bhautikastāvāneṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśo yasminnanveṣṭavyaṃ vijijñāsitavyaṃ cāvocāma /
nāpyākāśatulyaparimāṇatvamabhipretya tāvānityucyate /
kiṃ tarhi brahmaṇo 'nurūpasya dṛṣṭāntāntarasyābhāvāt /
kathaṃ punarnā'kāśasamameva brahmetyavagamyate /
"yenā'vṛtaṃ khaṃ ca divaṃ mahīṃ ca" /
"tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ" "etasminnu khalvakṣare gārgyākāśaḥ"ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
kiñcobhe 'smindyāvāpṛthivī brahmākāśe buddhyupādhiviśiṣṭe 'ntareva samāhite samyagāhite sthite yathā vā arā nābhāvityuktaṃ hi /
tathobhāvagniśca vāyuścetyādi samānam /
yaccāsyā'tmana ātmīyatvena dehavato 'sti vidyata iha loke /
tatā yaccā'tmīyatvena na vidyate /
children.translated_text: and whatever does not exist as one's own —

children.text: naṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyacca nāstītyucyate /
children.translated_text: what is lost and what will be are said to 'not exist,'

children.text: na tvatyantamevāsat /
children.translated_text: but [they are] not absolutely non-existent,

children.text: tasya hṛdyākāśe samādhānānupapatteḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: because their being contained in the space of the heart would be untenable [if they were absolutely non-existent]. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.1.3:] Listen. As to what you say — that because the space within the lotus is small, what is contained in it would be even smaller — that is wrong. For I did not say 'the inner space within this is small' thinking that the space, having entered the lotus abode, is smaller than the lotus. Rather, the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) that conforms to the lotus and is situated in it, delimited by the lotus-space — when it is purified, for <s>yogin</s>s who have withdrawn their senses, [<s>Brahman</s>] is apprehended therein — like a reflection in clear water, or like a clear image in a clean mirror — the light of consciousness (<s>vijñānajyoti</s>), the self-illumination of its own nature, to that extent <s>Brahman</s> is apprehended. Thus I said 'the inner space within this is small' — on account of the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of the inner organ. But in its own nature, as vast as this well-known physical space is in extent, so vast is this space within the heart — about which we said it is to be sought and inquired into. Nor is it said 'so vast' meaning it is equal in extent to [physical] space. Rather, because there is no other analogy appropriate to <s>Brahman</s>. How is it known that <s>Brahman</s> is not merely equal to space? From <s>śruti</s>s such as: 'By which space is pervaded, and heaven and earth'; 'From this <s>Ātman</s> indeed, space came into being'; 'In this imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, space [is woven],' and so on. Moreover, both heaven and earth are contained — well-contained, established — within this <s>Brahman</s>-space qualified by the limiting adjunct of intellect; just as 'all spokes are fixed in the hub' — for that has been said. Likewise, both fire and wind, and so on — the same. And whatever of this [person's], belonging to the embodied self, exists — is present — here in this world,

children.text: START ChUp 8,1.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.1.4]

children.text: taṃ ced brūyur asmiṃś cedaṃ brahmapure sarvaṃ samāhitaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmā yad enaj jarā vāpnoti pradhvaṃsate vā kiṃ tato 'tiśiṣyata iti || ChUp_8,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'If they should ask: "If in this city of <s>Brahman</s> everything is contained, and all beings and all desires — when old age reaches it or it perishes, what then remains?"' (ChUp 8.1.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,1.4 taṃ cedevamuktavantaṃ brūyuḥ punarantevāsinaḥ asmiṃścedyathokte cedyadi brahmapuropalakṣitāntarākāśa ityarthaḥ /
idaṃ sarvaṃ samāhitaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ /
kathamācāryeṇānuktāḥ kāmā antevāsibhirucyante /
naiṣa doṣaḥ yaccāsyehāsti yacca nāstītyuktā eva hyācāryeṇa kāmāḥ /
api ca sarvaśabdena coktā eva kāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, desires have been spoken of through the word 'everything' (<s>sarva</s>).

children.text: yadā yasminkāla etaccharīraṃ brahmapurākhyaṃ jarāvalīpalitādilakṣaṇā vayohānirvā'pnoti śasrādinā vā vṛkṇaṃ pradhvaṃsate visraṃsate vinaśyati kiṃ tato 'nyadatiśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: When, at whatever time, this body called the city of Brahman — [when] the diminution of life-span characterized by old age, wrinkles, grey hair, and the like overtakes it, or [when] it is struck by weapons and the like, and falls apart, disintegrates, perishes — what then remains beyond that?

children.text: ghaṭāśritakṣīradadhisnehādivadghaṭanāśe dehanāśe 'pi dehāśrayamuttarottaraṃ pūrvapūrvanāśānnaśyatītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The purport is: just as milk, curds, oil, and the like contained in a pot [are destroyed] when the pot is destroyed — so too, even when the body is destroyed, whatever depends upon the body perishes successively, each subsequent [thing perishing] upon the destruction of its predecessor.

children.text: evaṃ prāpte nāśe kiṃ tato 'nyadyathoktādatiśiṣyate 'vatiṣṭhate na kiñcanāvatiṣṭhata ityabhīprāyaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: When such destruction has occurred — what then remains beyond what has been described? Nothing at all remains — this is the purport. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.1.4:] If to one who has spoken thus they — the students — should say again: If in this, as described, the inner space characterized by the city of <s>Brahman</s> — that is the meaning — in this, everything is contained, and all beings and all desires. How can the desires, which are not mentioned by the teacher, be mentioned by the students? There is no defect — because the teacher has indeed spoken of desires through [the phrase] 'whatever of his exists here and whatever does not.'

children.text: START ChUp 8,1.5

sa brūyāt |
nāsya jarayaitaj jīryati na vadhenāsya hanyate |
etat satyaṃ brahmapuram asmin kāmāḥ samāhitāḥ |
eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ |
yathā hy eveha prajā anvāviśanti yathānuśāsanam |
yaṃ yam antam abhikāmā bhavanti yaṃ janapadaṃ yaṃ kṣetrabhāgaṃ taṃ tam evopajīvanti || ChUp_8,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'He should reply: "This [Self] does not age with the aging of this [body]; it is not slain by the slaying of this [body]. This is the true city of <s>Brahman</s>. In it all desires are contained. This is the <s>ātman</s> (Self), free from sin, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, whose desires are true, whose resolves are true. Just as here on earth, subjects follow [the king] according to his command — whatever region they desire, whatever territory, whatever portion of land — they subsist on that alone."' (ChUp 8.1.5)
[Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.1.5]

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,1.5 evamantevāsibhiścoditaḥ sa ācāryo brūyāttanmatimapanayan /

indravirocanākhyāyikāyāmupariṣṭādvakṣyāmo yuktitaḥ /
etatsatyamavitathaṃ brahmapuraṃ brahmaiva puraṃ brahmapuraṃ śarīrākhyaṃ tu brahmapuraṃ brahmopalakṣaṇārthatvāt /
tattvanṛtameva /
"vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam"iti śruteḥ /
tadvikāre 'nṛte 'pi dehaśuṅge brahmopalabhyata iti brahmapuramityuktaṃ vyāvahārikam /
satyaṃ tu brahmapurametadeva brahma /
sarvavyavahārāspadatvāt /
ato 'sminpuṇḍarīkopalakṣite brahmapure sarve kāmā ye bahirbhavadbhiḥ prārthyante te 'sminneva svātmani samāhitāḥ /
atastatprāptyupāyamevānutiṣṭhata bāhyaviṣayatṛṣmāṃ tyajatetyabhiprāyaḥ /
eṣa ātmā bhavatāṃ svarūpam /
śṛṇuta tasya lakṣaṇam /
apahatapāpmā /

tathā vijaro vigatajaro vimṛtyuśca /
taduktaṃ pūrvameva na vadhenāsya hanyata iti /

viśoko vigataśokaḥ /
śoko nāmeṣṭādiviyoganimitto mānasaḥ saṃtāpaḥ /
vijighatso vigatāśanecchaḥ /
apipāso 'pānecchaḥ /

satyamevaṃ tathāpi dharmakāryā nandavyatirekeṇa svābhāvikānando yatheśvare vijñānamānandaṃ brahmeti śruteḥ /
tathādharmakāryajarādivyatirekeṇāpi jarādiduḥkhasvarūpaṃ svābhāvikaṃ syādityāśaṅkyeta /

na svato neti netītyuktatvāt /
yathoktalakṣaṇa evā'tmā vijñeyo gurubhyaḥ śāstrataścā'tmasaṃvedyatayā ca svārājyakāmaiḥ /
na cedvijñāyate ko doṣaḥ syāditi /
śṛṇutātra doṣaṃ dṛṣṭāntena /
yathā hyeveha loke prajā anvāviśantyanuvartante /
yathānuśāsanaṃ yatheha prajā anyaṃ svāminaṃ manyamānāḥ svasya svāmino yathā yathānuśāsanaṃ tathā tathānvāviśanti /
children.translated_text: According to his command — just as here subjects, considering another as their lord, follow their own lord's commands in the manner prescribed,

children.text: kim /
children.translated_text: What [do they do]?

children.text: yaṃ yamantaṃ pratyantaṃ janapadaṃ kṣetrabhāgaṃ cābhikāmā arthinyo bhavantyātmabuddhyanurūpaṃ taṃ tameva ca pratyantādimupajīvantīti /
children.translated_text: Whatever region, outlying territory, land, or portion of land they desire, being desirous of — according to their own understanding of self — they subsist on that very [territory] and the rest.

children.text: eṣa dṛṣṭānto 'svātantryadeṣaṃ prati puṇyaphalopabhoge //5 //
children.translated_text: This illustration points to the fault of lack of independence in the enjoyment of the fruits of merit. (5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.1.5:] Thus prompted by his students, the teacher should reply, dispelling their wrong notion. How? This — what has been described above as the <s>Brahman</s> named 'inner space,' in which everything is contained — does not age with the aging of this body, does not undergo change like the body, is the meaning. Nor is it slain by the slaying of this [body] — by striking with weapons and the like — just as space [is not destroyed]; how much less <s>Brahman</s>, which is even subtler than space, soundless, touchless — it is not affected by the defects of the body, senses, and the rest. At this point, [the objection] that arises should be addressed, but to avoid a digression from the topic at hand, it is not stated. We shall explain it with reasoning below, in the narrative of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s>. This is the true — unfailing — city of <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Brahman</s> itself is the city — the city of <s>Brahman</s>. But the city of <s>Brahman</s> in the form of the body is [called so] because it serves to indicate <s>Brahman</s>. That [body] is actually unreal — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'What is a mere modification is a mere name, a verbal designation.' Though the body-modification is unreal, <s>Brahman</s> is perceived within the body-sheath — hence 'the city of <s>Brahman</s>' is said conventionally. But the true city of <s>Brahman</s> is this <s>Brahman</s> itself — because it is the substratum of all transactions. Therefore, in this [<s>Brahman</s>], indicated by the heart-lotus, all desires — which are sought externally by those who are outward-looking — are contained right here in one's own Self. Therefore, one should practice only the means to attain that; one should abandon craving for external objects — this is the purport. This is the <s>ātman</s> — your own essential nature. Hear its characteristics. Free from sin (<s>apahatapāpmā</s>) — one whose sin, consisting of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, has been destroyed — that is <s>apahatapāpmā</s>. Likewise, free from old age (<s>vijara</s>), free from death (<s>vimṛtyu</s>) — this was already stated: 'It is not slain by the slaying of this [body].' Why is it stated again? Although it is not connected with old age and death that belong to the body, the suspicion that it might be connected with them in some other way is negated [by repetition]. Free from sorrow (<s>viśoka</s>) — sorrow is the mental anguish caused by separation from beloved objects and the like. Free from hunger (<s>vijighatsa</s>) — free from the desire for food. Free from thirst (<s>apipāsa</s>) — free from the desire for drink. Now, [one might ask:] by stating freedom from sin, old age and the rest up to sorrow are already negated — because the cause [sin] is negated. For old age and the rest are effects of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. Or, by negating old age and the rest, the effects, even though <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> exist, they would be as good as non-existent due to the absence of their effects — so the separate negation would be purposeless. True — but nevertheless, the bliss that is the effect of <s>dharma</s>, distinct from the joy [of <s>Brahman</s>], is natural — as with <s>Īśvara</s>, from the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Brahman</s> is knowledge and bliss.' Similarly, one might suspect that the inherent nature of old age, sorrow, and the like as suffering — distinct from the effects of <s>adharma</s> — might be natural. Therefore, the separate negation of old age and the rest, apart from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, is justified — to negate that [suspicion]. The mention of old age and the rest is meant to indicate all forms of suffering. But since the sufferings caused by sin are infinite, and since it is impossible to negate each one individually, the statement of freedom from sin is indeed appropriate for negating all suffering. One whose desires (<s>kāma</s>) are true — unfailing — that is <s>satyakāma</s>. For the desires of worldly beings are false. Those of <s>Īśvara</s> are the opposite. Similarly, the resolves (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), which are the causes of desires, are also true for him — hence <s>satyasaṅkalpa</s>. The resolves and desires of <s>Īśvara</s> are caused by the limiting adjunct of pure <s>sattva</s> — like <s>Citragu</s> [a painting]. They are not intrinsic — because it has been said 'not this, not this.' The <s>ātman</s> with the characteristics described above is to be known — from the teachers, from scripture, and through self-realization — by those who desire self-sovereignty. If it is not known, what fault would there be? Hear the fault, with an illustration. Just as here in this world, subjects follow — obey — [the king].

children.text: START ChUp 8,1.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.1.6]

children.text:
tad yatheha karmajito lokaḥ kṣīyata evam evāmutra puṇyajito lokaḥ kṣīyate |
tad ya ihātmānam ananuvidya vrajanty etāṃś ca satyān kāmāṃs teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣv akāmacāro bhavati |
atha ya ihātmānam anivudya vrajanty etaṃś ca satyān kāmāṃs teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati || ChUp_8,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as here the world won by action perishes, so too in the next world, the world won by merit perishes. Those who depart from here without having found the <s>ātman</s> and these true desires — for them there is no freedom of movement in any of the worlds. But those who depart from here having found the <s>ātman</s> and these true desires — for them there is freedom of movement in all the worlds.' (ChUp 8.1.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,1.6 athānyo dṛṣṭāntastatkṣayaṃ prati tadyathehetyādiḥ /
tattatra yatheha loke tāsāmeva svāmyanuśāsanānuvartinīnāṃ prajānāṃ sevādijito lokaḥ parādhīnopabhogaḥ kṣīyate 'ntavānbhavati /
athedānīṃ dārṣṭāntikamupasaṃharati-evamevāmutrāgnihotrādipuṇyaj ito lokaḥ parādhīnopabhogaḥ kṣīyata evetyukto doṣa eṣāmiti viṣayaṃ darśayati-tadya ityādinā /
children.translated_text: Now he draws out the thing illustrated: 'In the same way, in the next world, the world won by merit such as <s>agnihotra</s> — the enjoyment dependent on another — also perishes.' Having stated this fault, he shows the scope [of the teaching] with 'those who' and so on.

children.text: tattatrehāsmiṃlloke jñānakarmaṇoradhikṛtā yogyāḥ santa ātmānaṃ yathoktalakṣaṇaṃ śāstrācāryopadiṣṭamananuvidya yathopadeśamanu svasaṃvedyatāmakṛtvā vrajanti dehādasmāt prayanti ya etāṃśca yathoktān satyān satyasaṃkalpakāryāṃśca svātmasthān kāmānananuvidya vrajanti teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣvakāmacāro 'svatantratā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Those who here in this world, being qualified for and fit for knowledge and action, depart — leave this body — without having found, without having made directly knowable through self-realization, as taught by scripture and teacher, the <s>ātman</s> with the characteristics described above; and without having found these true desires — which are the effects of <s>satyasaṅkalpa</s> (true resolve), abiding in one's own Self — for them there is no freedom of movement in any of the worlds, [they have] lack of independence.

children.text: yathā rājānuśāsanānuvartinīnāṃ prajānāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just like subjects who follow the king's command — this is the meaning.

children.text: atha ye 'nya iha loka ātmānaṃ śāsrācāryoradeśamanuvidya svātmasaṃvedyatāmāpādya vrajanti yathoktāṃśca satyānkāmāṃsteṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati rājña iva sārvabhaumasyeha loke //6//
children.translated_text: But those others who here in this world, having found the <s>ātman</s> according to the teaching of scripture and teacher, having attained self-realization, and [having found] the true desires described above — they depart, and for them there is freedom of movement in all the worlds, like a sovereign emperor in this world. (6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.1.6:] Now, another illustration — regarding the perishability of that — 'Just as here' and so forth. There — just as here in this world, for those very subjects who follow the lord's command, the world won through service and the like — the enjoyment dependent on another — perishes, comes to an end.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,2.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.2.1]

children.text:
sa yadi pitṛlokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya pitaraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti |
tena pitṛlokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of the fathers — by his mere resolve, the fathers arise for him. Endowed with that world of the fathers, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,2.1 kathaṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavatīti, ucyate-ya ātmānaṃ yatoktalakṣaṇaṃ hṛdi sākṣātkṛtavānvakṣyamāṇabrahmacaryādisādhanasaṃpannaḥ saṃstatsthāṃśca satyānkāmānsa tyaktadeho yadi pitṛlokakāmaḥ pitaro janayitārasta eva sukhahetutvena bhogyatvāllokā ucyante teṣu kāmo yasya taiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṃbandhecchā yasya bhavati tasya saṃkalpamātrādeva pitaraḥ samuttiṣṭhintyātmasaṃbandhitāmāpadyante /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.2.1:] How does he have freedom of movement in all the worlds? — it is explained. He who has directly realized in the heart the <s>ātman</s> with the characteristics described above, who is endowed with the means such as <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) which will be described, and [who has realized] the true desires abiding in it — if, after leaving the body, he desires the world of the fathers — the fathers are the progenitors; they are called 'worlds' because they are objects of enjoyment, being causes of happiness — if he has the desire for association with those fathers, then by his mere resolve, the fathers arise — they come into relation with him.

children.text: viśuddhasattvatayā satyasaṃkalpatvādīśvarasyeva tena pitṛlokena bhogena saṃpannaḥ saṃpattiriṣṭaprāptistayā samṛddho mahīyate pūjyate vardhate vā mahimānamanubhavati //1 //
children.translated_text: Because his <s>sattva</s> (being) is pure, his resolves are true, like those of <s>Īśvara</s>. Endowed with that world of the fathers — endowed with that enjoyment — <s>saṃpatti</s> means the attainment of what is desired — enriched by that, he is glorified — he is honored, or he grows, or he experiences his greatness. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 8,2.2-9
children.translated_text: [<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.2.2–9]

children.text:
atha yadi mātṛlokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya mātaraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti |
tena mātṛlokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of the mothers — by his mere resolve, the mothers arise for him. Endowed with that world of the mothers, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.2)

children.text:
atha yadi bhrātṛlokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya bhrātaraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti |
tena bhrātṛlokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of the brothers — by his mere resolve, the brothers arise for him. Endowed with that world of the brothers, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.3)

children.text:
atha yadi svasṛlokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya svasāraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti |
tena svasṛlokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of the sisters — by his mere resolve, the sisters arise for him. Endowed with that world of the sisters, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.4)

children.text:
atha yadi sakhilokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya sakhāyaḥ samuttiṣṭhanti |
tena sakhilokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of the friends — by his mere resolve, the friends arise for him. Endowed with that world of the friends, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.5)

children.text:
atha yadi gandhamālyalokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya gandhamālye samuttiṣṭhataḥ |
tena gandhamālyalokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of fragrance and garlands — by his mere resolve, fragrance and garlands arise for him. Endowed with that world of fragrance and garlands, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.6)

children.text:
atha yady annapānalokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsyānnapāne samuttiṣṭhataḥ |
tenānnapānalokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of food and drink — by his mere resolve, food and drink arise for him. Endowed with that world of food and drink, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.7)

children.text:
atha yadi gītavāditalokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya gītavādite samuttiṣṭhataḥ |
tena gītavāditalokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of song and music — by his mere resolve, song and music arise for him. Endowed with that world of song and music, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.8)

children.text:
atha yadi strīlokakāmo bhavati |
saṃkalpād evāsya striyaḥ samuttiṣṭhanti |
tena strīlokena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.9 ||
children.translated_text: 'If he desires the world of women — by his mere resolve, women arise for him. Endowed with that world of women, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.9)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,2.2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.2.2–9:] The rest is the same.

children.text: mātaro janayitryo 'tītāḥ sukhahetubhūtāḥ sāmardhyāt /
children.translated_text: Mothers are the progenitresses — those of the past, who were causes of happiness — [this is said] in accordance with his capacity.

children.text: na hi duḥkhahetubhūtāsu grāmasūkarādijanmanimittāsu mātṛṣu viśuddhasattvasya yogina icchā tatsaṃbandho vā yuktaḥ //2-9 //
children.translated_text: For it is not appropriate for a yogin of pure <s>sattva</s> to have desire for, or association with, mothers in births such as those of village pigs and the like, which are causes of suffering. (2–9)

children.text: START ChUp 8,2.10
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.2.10]

children.text:
yaṃ yam antam abhikāmo bhavati |
yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate |
so 'sya saṃkalpād eva samuttiṣṭhati |
tena saṃpanno mahīyate || ChUp_8,2.10 ||
children.translated_text: 'Whatever region he desires, whatever desire he desires — that arises for him by his mere resolve. Endowed with that, he is glorified.' (ChUp 8.2.10)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,2.10 yaṃ yanamtaṃ pradeśamabhikāmo bhavati /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.2.10:] Whatever region he desires,

children.text: yaṃ ca kāmaṃ kāmayate yathoktavyatirekeṇāpi so 'syāntaḥ prāptumiṣṭaḥ kāmaśca saṃkalpādeva samuttiṣṭhatyasya /
children.translated_text: and whatever desire he desires — beyond those already mentioned — that desired region and desire arise for him by his mere resolve.

children.text: tenecchāvighātatayābhipretārthaprāptyā ca saṃpanno mahīyata ityuktārtham //10//
children.translated_text: Endowed with [the fulfillment of] that — through the non-obstruction of his will and the attainment of the desired object — he is glorified. The meaning has been stated. (10)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,3.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.3.1]

children.text:
ta ime satyāḥ kāmā anṛtāpidhānāḥ |
teṣāṃ satyānāṃ satām anṛtam apidhānam |
yo yo hy asyetaḥ praiti na tam iha darśanāya labhate || ChUp_8,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'These true desires are covered by what is untrue. Though they are true in nature, untruth is their covering. For whoever of one's own departs from here, one does not obtain him for seeing in this world.' (ChUp 8.3.1)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,3.1 yathoktātmadhyānasādhanānuṣṭhānaṃ prati sādhakānāmutsāhajananārthamanukrośantyāha-kaṣṭamidaṃ khalu vartate yatsvātmasthāḥ śakyaprāpyā api ta ime satyāḥ kāmā anṛtāpidhānāsteṣāmātmasthānāṃ svāśrayāṇāmeva satāmanṛtaṃ ba3hyaviṣayeṣu stryannabhojanācchādanādiṣu tṛṣṇā tannimittaṃ ca svecchāpracāratvaṃ mithyājñānanimittatvādanṛtamityucyate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.3.1:] In order to generate enthusiasm in seekers toward the practice of the means — the meditation on the Self as described — [the text] speaks with compassion: 'What a pity this is indeed — that these true desires, though abiding in one's own Self and attainable, are covered by untruth.' Those true desires abide in the Self — in their own support. The untruth is the craving directed toward external objects such as women, food, drink, clothing, and the like, together with the arbitrary behaviour caused by it. Because it arises from false knowledge, it is called 'untruth.'

children.text: tannimittaṃ satyānāṃ kāmānāmaprāptirityapidhānamivāpidhānam /
children.translated_text: Because of that [untruth], the non-attainment of the true desires is, as it were, a covering — like a covering.

children.text: kathamanṛtāpidhānanimittaṃ teṣāmalābha iti, ucyate-yo yo hi yasmādasya jantoḥ putro bhrātā veṣṭa ito 'smāllokātpraiti pragacchati mriyate tamiṣṭaṃ putraṃ bhrātaraṃ vā svahṛdayākāśe vidyamānamapīha punardarśanāyecchannapi na labhate //1 //
children.translated_text: How is the non-attainment caused by the covering of untruth? The text explains: Whichever beloved one — whether a son or a brother — of this creature departs from this world, dies — that beloved son or brother, even though existing in one's own heart-space, one cannot find again, even though wishing to see [that person] here again. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 8,3.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.3.2]

children.text:
atha ye cāsyeha jīvā ye ca pretā yac cānyad icchan na labhate sarvaṃ tad atra gatvā vindate |
atra hy asyaite satyāḥ kāmā anṛtāpidhānāḥ |
tad yathāpi hiraṇyanidhiṃ nihitam akṣetrajñā upary upari sañcaranto na vindeyuḥ |
evam evemāḥ sarvāḥ prajā ahar ahar gacchantya etaṃ brahmalokaṃ na vindanty anṛtena hi pratyūḍhāḥ || ChUp_8,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'And whatever living ones are here, and whatever deceased ones, and whatever else one desires but does not obtain — all that one finds by going there [to the heart-space]. For here indeed are those true desires of his, covered by untruth. Just as people who do not know the terrain would walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold without finding it, so all these creatures, going day after day to this <s>Brahma-loka</s> (world of <s>Brahman</s>), do not find it — for they are carried away by untruth.' (ChUp 8.3.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,3.2 atha punarye cāsya viduṣo jantorjīvā jīvantīha putrā bhrātrādayo vā ye ca pretā mṛtā iṣṭāḥ saṃbandhino yaccānyadiha loke vastrānnapānādi ratnādi vā vastvicchanna labhate tatsarvamatra hṛdayākāśākhye brahmaṇi gatvā yathoktena vidhinā vindate labhate /
atrāsminhārdākāśe hi yasmādasyaite yathoktāḥ satyāḥ kāmā vartante 'natāpidhānāḥ /
kathamiva tadanyāyyamityucyate-tattatra yathā hiraṇyanidhiṃ hiraṇyameva punargrahaṇāya nidhātṛbhirnidhīyata iti nidhistaṃ hiraṇyanidhiṃ nihitaṃ bhūmeradhastānnikṣiptamakṣetrajñā nidhiśāsrairnidhikṣetramajānantaste nidheruparyupari saṃcaranto 'pi nidhiṃ na vindeyuḥ śakyavedanamapi /
evamevemā avidyavatyaḥ sarvā imāḥ prajā yathoktaṃ hṛdayākāśākhyaṃ brahmalokaṃ brahmaiva loko brahmalokastamaharahaḥ pratyahaṃ gacchantyo 'pi suṣuptakāle na vidandanti na labhanta eṣo 'haṃ brahmalokabhāvamāpanno 'smyadyeti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.3.2:] Furthermore, whatever living ones — sons, brothers, or others still alive — belong to this knowing person, and whatever deceased ones — dead beloved relatives — and whatever other thing in this world, such as clothing, food, drink, or jewels, one desires but does not obtain — all that one finds, obtains, by going to <s>Brahman</s> called the heart-space, through the method described. Here, in this heart-space, indeed are those true desires of his as described, which are covered by untruth. How is it as if unjust? The text gives an analogy: just as a treasure of gold — gold itself, deposited by depositors for later retrieval, that is a treasure — that hidden treasure of gold, placed underground, [is not found by] those who do not know the terrain — who, not knowing the field of the treasure through the science of treasure-finding, walk again and again over the treasure without finding it, even though it is findable. Just so, all these creatures, endowed with ignorance, going day after day — every day — to this world of <s>Brahman</s> called the heart-space — for <s>Brahman</s> itself is the world, the <s>Brahma-loka</s> — even though entering it in deep sleep, do not find it — do not realize 'I have attained the state of <s>Brahma-loka</s> today.'

children.text: anṛtena hi yathoktena hi yasmātpratyūḍhā hṛtāḥ svarūpādavidyādidoṣairbahipakṛṣṭā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For they are carried away — taken away — by untruth — by the faults of ignorance and the like, removed from their true nature, drawn outward — this is the meaning.

children.text: ataḥ kaṣṭamidaṃ vartate jantūnāṃ yatsvāyattamapi brahma na labhyata ityabhiprāyaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, what a pity this is for creatures — that <s>Brahman</s>, though dependent on oneself, is not attained — this is the purport. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 8,3.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.3.3]

children.text:
sa vā eṣa ātmā hṛdi |
tasyaitad eva niruktaṃ hṛdy ayam iti tasmād dhṛd ayam |
ahar ahar vā evaṃvit svargaṃ lokam eti || ChUp_8,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'This Self is in the heart. This is its etymology: "He is in the heart (<s>hṛdi ayam</s>)" — therefore it is called <s>hṛdayam</s>. Day after day, the one who knows thus goes to the heavenly world.' (ChUp 8.3.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,3.3 sa vai ya ātmāpahatapāpmeti prakṛto vaiśabdena taṃ smārayatyeṣa vivakṣita ātmā hṛdi hṛdayapuṇḍarīka ākāśaśabdenābhihitaḥ /
tasyaitasya hṛdayasyaitadeva niruktaṃ nirvacanaṃ nānyata /
hṛdyayamātmā vartata iti yasmāt tasmāddhṛdayaṃ hṛdayanāmanirvacanaprasiddhyāpi svahṛdaya ātmetyavagantavyamityabhiprāyaḥ /
aharaharvai pratyahamevaṃviddhṛdyayamātmeti jānansvargaṃ lokaṃ hārdaṃ brahmaiti pratipadyate /
nanvanevaṃvidapi suṣuptakāle hārdaṃ brahma pratipadyata eva suṣuptakāle satā somya tadā saṃpanna ityuktatvāt /
bāḍhamevaṃ tathāpyasti viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: True, that is so — nevertheless, there is a distinction.

children.text: yathā jānannajānaṃśca sarvo jantuḥ sadbrahmaiva tathāpi tattvamasīti pratibodhito vidvānsadeva nānyo 'smīti jānansadeva bhavati /
children.translated_text: Just as every creature, whether knowing or not knowing, is indeed <s>Sat-Brahman</s>, yet one who has been awakened [by the teaching] 'You are That (<s>tat tvam asi</s>)' — the wise one — knowing 'I am <s>Sat</s> alone, nothing other' — becomes <s>Sat</s> itself.

children.text: evameva vidvānavidvāṃścasuṣupte yadyapi satsaṃpadyate tathāpyevaṃvideva svargaṃ lokametītyucyate /
children.translated_text: Just so, even though both the wise and the unwise merge with <s>Sat</s> in deep sleep, it is said that only the one who knows thus goes to the heavenly world.

children.text: dehapāte 'pi vidyāphalasyāvaśyaṃbhāvitvādityeṣa viśeṣaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: Because the fruit of knowledge inevitably manifests even at the fall of the body — this is the distinction. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.3.3:] He indeed — the particle 'vai' reminds [us] of the Self described earlier with the attributes 'free from evil (<s>apahatapāpmā</s>)' and so on — this is the <s>Ātman</s> intended [here], [residing] in the heart, in the lotus of the heart, designated by the word 'space.' This is its etymology — the derivation of the word 'heart' (<s>hṛdaya</s>) — there is no other. 'This <s>Ātman</s> is in the heart (<s>hṛdi ayam</s>)' — because of this, it is [called] <s>hṛdayam</s>. By the established derivation of the name 'heart,' one should understand that the Self is in one's own heart — this is the purport. Day after day, the one who knows thus — who knows 'this <s>Ātman</s> is in the heart (<s>hṛdi ayam</s>)' — goes to, attains, the heavenly world — <s>Brahman</s> in the heart. Objection: But even one who does not know thus, in the state of deep sleep, attains <s>Brahman</s> in the heart — as stated: 'When, dear one, one is merged with <s>Sat</s> (Being).'

children.text: START ChUp 8,3.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.3.4]

children.text:
atha ya eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāc charīrāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpenābhiniṣpadyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca |
etad amṛtam abhayam etad brahmeti |
tasya ha vā etasya brahmaṇo nāma satyam iti || ChUp_8,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, this serene one (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), rising up from this body and reaching the supreme light, manifests in his own form — this is the Self,' he said. 'This is the immortal, the fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>. The name of this <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Satya</s> (Truth).' (ChUp 8.3.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,3.4 suṣuptakāle svenā'manā satā saṃpannaḥ sansamyakprasīdatīti jāgratsvapnayorviṣayendriyasaṃyogajātaṃ kāluṣyaṃ jahātīti saṃprasādaśabdo yadyapi sarvajantūnāṃ sādhāraṇastathāpyevaṃvitsvargaṃ lokametīti prakṛtatvādeṣa saṃprasāda iti saṃnihitavadyatnaviśeṣātso 'thedaṃ śarīraṃ hitvāsmāccharīrātsamutthāya śarīrātmabhāvanāṃ parityajyetyarthaḥ /
na tvāsanādiva samutthāyetīha yuktam /
svena rūpeṇeti viśeṣaṇāt /
na hyanyata utthāya svarūpaṃ saṃpattavyam /
svarūpameva hi tanna bhavati pratipattavyaṃ cetsyāt /
paraṃ paramātmalakṣaṇaṃ vijñaptisvabhāvaṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svāsthyamupagamyetyetat /
svena ātmīyena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate prāgetasyāḥ svarūpasaṃpatteravidyayā dehamevāparaṃ rūpamātmatvenopagata iti tadapekṣayedamucyate svena rūpeṇeti /
aśarīratā hyātmanaḥ svarūpaṃ yatsvaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥsvarūpamāpadye saṃprasāda eṣa ātmeti hovāca /
sa brūyāditi yaḥ śrutyā niyukto 'ntevāsibhyaḥ /
kiñcaitadamṛtamavināśi bhūmā yo vai bhūmā tadamṛtamityuktam /
ata evābhayaṃ bhūmno dvitīyābhāvādata etadbrahmeti /
tasya ha vā etasya brahmaṇo nāmābhidhānam /
kiṃ tatsatyamiti /
satyaṃ hyavitathaṃ brahma /
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s> is truth — unfailing.

children.text: tatsatyaṃ sa ātmeti hyuktam /
children.translated_text: 'That truth is this Self' — thus it was said.

children.text: atha kimarthamidaṃ nāma punarucyate /
children.translated_text: Now, for what purpose is this name mentioned again?

children.text: tadupāsanavidhistutyartham //4//
children.translated_text: For the purpose of the injunction of its meditation and its praise. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.3.4:] In deep sleep, being merged with <s>Sat</s> by one's own nature, one becomes perfectly serene (<s>saṃprasīdati</s>) — one abandons the turbidity born of the contact of senses and objects in the waking and dream states — hence the word <s>saṃprasāda</s> (the serene one), though common to all creatures, is used here with special application, because the one who knows thus [goes to the heavenly world] — being in the context — with special effort [of knowledge], as if proximately [present]. Then, this [serene one], abandoning this body — rising up from this body — meaning, abandoning the identification with the body as the self. Not, however, [rising up] as from a seat — because of the qualifier 'in his own form.' For one does not attain one's own form by rising up from something else. That very form is [already] one's own — it would not need to be attained if it were [already] so. Reaching the supreme light — whose nature is the Supreme Self, whose essence is consciousness (<s>vijñapti</s>) — attaining its own natural state — this is what is meant. Manifesting in one's own form — prior to this attainment of one's own form, through ignorance, one had accepted the body, which is another, inferior form, as oneself — in relation to that, this is said: 'in one's own form.' For the true nature of the Self is bodilessness — having attained that supreme light, which is one's own form — 'this is the Self,' he said — he who is appointed by the <s>śruti</s> to [teach] the students. Furthermore, this is immortal — indestructible — the <s>Bhūman</s> (Infinite), for it was said: 'That which is the Infinite, that is the immortal.' Therefore it is also fearless, because of the absence of a second in the Infinite. Hence 'this is <s>Brahman</s>.' The name — the designation — of this <s>Brahman</s> — what is it? — <s>Satya</s> (Truth).

children.text: tāni ha vā etāni trīṇyakṣarāṇi satīyamiti tadyatsattdamṛtamatha yatti tanmartyamatha
children.translated_text: 'These are indeed three syllables: <s>sa-ti-yam</s>. That which is <s>sat</s> — that is the immortal. That which is <s>ti</s> — that is the mortal. And that which is <s>yam</s> — by it,

children.text: yadyaṃ tenobhe yacchati yadanenobhe yacchati tasmādyamaharaharvā evaṃvitsvargaṃ lokameti //5//
children.translated_text: one controls both. Because by it one controls both, therefore [it is called] <s>yam</s>. Day after day, the one who knows thus goes to the heavenly world.' (ChUp 8.3.5)
[<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.3.5]

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,3.5 tāni ha vā etāni brahmaṇo nāmākṣarāṇi trīṇyetāni satīyāmati sakārastakāro yamiti ca /
takāra īkāraḥ uccāraṇārtho 'nubandhaḥ /
hrasvenaivākṣareṇa punaḥ pratinirdeśātteṣām /
tattatra yatsatsakārastadamṛtaṃ sadbrahmāmṛtavācakatvādamṛta eva sakārastakāranto nirdiṣṭaḥ /
atha yattitakārastanmartyam /
atha yadyamakṣaraṃ tenākṣareṇāmṛtamartyākhye pūrve ubhe 'kṣare yacchati yamayati niyamayati vaśīkarotyātmana ityarthaḥ /
yadyasmādanena yamityetenobhe yacchati tasmādyām /
saṃyate iva hyetena yamā lakṣyete /
children.translated_text: For by this [syllable], the one who controls (<s>yamayati</s>) is, as it were, indicated.

children.text: braṅmanāmākṣarasyāpīdamamṛtatvādidharmavattvaṃ mahābhāgyaṃ kimuta nāmavata ityupāsyatvāya stūyate /
children.translated_text: If even the syllable of <s>Brahman's</s> name possesses such qualities as immortality and the rest — what great fortune! — how much more so the bearer of the name! Thus it is praised for the purpose of meditation.

children.text: brahmanāmanirvacanenaiva nāmavato vettaivaṃvit /
children.translated_text: The one who knows thus — through the very etymology of the name of <s>Brahman</s> — knows the bearer of the name.

children.text: aharaharvā evaṃvitsvargaṃ lokametītyuktārtham //5//
children.translated_text: 'Day after day, the one who knows thus goes to the heavenly world' — the meaning has already been stated. (5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.3.5:] These syllables of <s>Brahman's</s> name are three: <s>sa-tī-yam</s> — the <s>sa</s>-syllable, the <s>ta</s>-syllable, and <s>yam</s>. The <s>ta</s>-syllable and <s>ī</s>-syllable [together form <s>tī</s>] — the <s>ī</s> is a connecting vowel for pronunciation. Because of the reference back to them with a short vowel [later in the text]. There, the <s>sat</s> — the <s>sa</s>-syllable ending in <s>ta</s>-syllable — that is the immortal. Since <s>Sat</s> (Being) is <s>Brahman</s>, and denotes the immortal, the <s>sa</s>-syllable ending in <s>ta</s> is thus indicated. Then the <s>ti</s> — the <s>ta</s>-syllable — that is the mortal. Then the <s>yam</s> syllable — by that syllable, it controls (<s>yacchati</s>), regulates, governs, brings under its power the two previous syllables called 'immortal' and 'mortal' — meaning it controls them for itself. Because by this [syllable] — since by this <s>yam</s> it controls both — therefore [it is called] <s>yam</s>.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,4.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.4.1]

children.text:
atha ya ātmā sa setur dhṛtir eṣāṃ lokānām asaṃbhedāya |
naitaṃ setum ahorātre tarato na jarā na mṛtyur na śoko na sukṛtam |
sarve pāpmāno 'to nivartante |
apahatapāpmā hy eṣa brahmalokaḥ || ChUp_8,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, this Self is the bridge (<s>setu</s>), the support (<s>dhṛti</s>) of these worlds, so that they do not fall apart. Neither day nor night crosses this bridge, nor old age, nor death, nor sorrow, nor good deeds nor evil deeds. All evils turn back from it. For this <s>Brahma-loka</s> is free from evil.' (ChUp 8.4.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,4.1 atha ya ātmeti /
uktalakṣaṇo yaḥ saṃprasādastasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyamāṇairuktaiśca guṇaiḥ punaḥ stūyate brahmacaryasādhanasaṃbandhārtham /
ya eṣa yathoktalakṣaṇa ātmā sa seturiva setuḥ /
vidhṛtirvidharaṇaḥ /
anena hi sarvaṃ jagadvarṇāśramādikriyākārakaphalādibhedaniyamaiḥ karturanurūpaṃ vidadhatā vidhṛtam /
adhriyamāṇaṃ hīśvareṇedaṃ viśvaṃ vinaśyedyatastasmātsa seturvidhṛtiḥ /
kimarthaṃ sa seturityāha-eṣāṃ bhūrādīnāṃ kartṛkarmalāśrayāṇāmasaṃbhedāyāvidāraṇāyāvināśāyetyetat /
kiṃviśṣṭaścāsau seturityāha-naitam setumātmānamahorātre sarvasya janimataḥ paricchedake satī naitaṃ tarataḥ /
yathānye saṃsāriṇaḥ kālenāhorātrādilakṣaṇena paricchedyā na tathāyaṃ kālaparicchedya ityabhiprāyaḥ /
"yasmādarvāksaṃvatsaro 'hobhiḥ parivartata"iti śrutyantarāt /
ata evainaṃ na jarā tarati na prāpnoti /
tathā na mṛtyurna śoko na sukṛtaṃ na dṛṣkṛtaṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛte dharmādharmai /
prāptiratra taraṇaśabdenābhipretā nātikramaṇam /
kāraṇaṃ hyātmā /
na śakyaṃ hi kāraṇātikramaṇaṃ kartuṃ kāryeṇa /
ahorātrādi ca sarvaṃ sataḥ kāryam /
anyena hyanyasya prāptiratikramaṇaṃ vā kriyeta /
na tu tenaiva tasya /
na hi ghaṭena mṛtprāpyate 'tikramyate vā /
yadyapi pūrvaṃ ya ātmāpahatapāpmetyādinā pāpmādipratiṣedha ukta eva tathāpīhāyaṃ viśeṣo na taratīti prāptiviṣayatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: Although the negation of evil and the like was already stated earlier with 'the Self that is free from evil (<s>apahatapāpmā</s>)' and so forth, the distinction here is that [the negation is stated in terms of] 'does not cross' — meaning [evil] does not reach [the Self].

children.text: tatrā viśeṣeṇa jarādyabhāvamātramuktam /
children.translated_text: There, [in the earlier passage], the mere absence of old age and the rest was stated without specification.

children.text: ahorātrādyā uktā anuktāścānye sarve pāpmāna ucyante 'to 'smādātmanaḥ setornivartante 'prāpyaivetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Day, night, and the rest — both mentioned and unmentioned — all evils are said to turn back from this Self, this bridge — meaning without even reaching it.

children.text: apahatapāpmā hyeṣa brahmaiva loko brahmaloka uktaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: For this <s>Brahma-loka</s> — <s>Brahman</s> itself is the world — has been called free from evil. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.4.1:] 'Now, this Self' — the one whose characteristics have been described, the serene one (<s>saṃprasāda</s>) — his true nature is praised again with the qualities about to be stated and those already stated, for the purpose of connecting it with <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) as the means [of attaining it]. This <s>Ātman</s> of the characteristics described is like a bridge (<s>setu</s>) — a bridge indeed. It is the support (<s>vidhṛti</s>) — the upholding. For by it, the entire universe is upheld — the one who, through the regulations of <s>varṇa</s> (social class), <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), actions, agents, and fruits, arranges [everything] in accordance with the doer. For if the Lord did not uphold this universe, it would be destroyed — therefore it is the bridge, the support. For what purpose is it a bridge? The text says: for the non-disintegration — the non-tearing apart, the non-destruction — of these worlds beginning with <s>bhūḥ</s> (earth), which are the supports of agents and objects of action. What are the characteristics of this bridge? The text says: neither day nor night — which, being present, delimit everything that is born — do not cross this bridge, this Self. Just as other beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> are delimited by time in the form of day, night, and the like — not so is this one delimited by time — this is the purport. [As stated] in another <s>śruti</s>: 'From whom the year with its days revolves.' Therefore, old age too does not cross it — does not reach it. Likewise, neither death, nor sorrow, nor merit, nor demerit — <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> (merit and demerit). The word 'crossing' here means 'reaching,' not 'surpassing.' For the Self is the cause — and it is impossible for an effect to surpass its cause. Day, night, and everything else is the effect of <s>Sat</s>. For it is by something other that something else is reached or surpassed — not by itself. A pot does not reach or surpass clay.

children.text: START ChUp 8,4.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.4.2]

children.text:
tasmād vā etaṃ setuṃ tīrtvā andhaḥ sann anandho bhavati |
viddhaḥ sann aviddho bhavati |
upatāpī sann anupatāpī bhavati |
tasmād vā etaṃ setuṃ tīrtvā api naktam ahar evābhiniṣpadyate |
sakṛd vibhāto hy evaiṣa brahmalokaḥ || ChUp_8,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, having crossed this bridge, one who was blind becomes no longer blind; one who was wounded becomes no longer wounded; one who was afflicted becomes no longer afflicted. Therefore, having crossed this bridge, even night manifests as day alone. For this <s>Brahma-loka</s> is eternally luminous.' (ChUp 8.4.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,4.2 yasmācca pāpmakārya māndhyādi śarīravataḥ syānna tvaśarīrasya tasmādvā etamātmānaṃ setuṃ tīrvā prāpyānandho bhavati dehavattve pūrvamandho 'pi san /
tatā viddhaḥ sandehavattve sa dehaviyoge setuṃ tīrtvā prāpyānandho bhavati dehavattve pūrvamandho 'pi san /
tathā viddhaḥ sandehavattve sa dehaviyogo setuṃ prāpyāviddho bhavati /
tathopatāpī rogādyupatāpavānsannanupatāpī bhavati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, one who was afflicted — suffering from disease and the like — becomes free from affliction.

children.text: kiñca yasmādahorātre na staḥ setau tasmādvā etaṃ setuṃ tīrtvā prāpya naktamapi tamorūpaṃ rātrirapi sarvamaharevābhiniṣpadyate /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, since day and night do not exist in the bridge [Self] — therefore, having crossed this bridge, having attained it — even night, which is of the nature of darkness — all of it manifests as day alone.

children.text: vijñaptyātmajyotiḥ svarūpamaharivāhaḥ sadaikarūpaṃ viduṣaḥ saṃpadyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The essential nature, which is the light of consciousness, like the sun, eternally uniform — that [nature] is attained by the knower — that is the meaning.

children.text: sakṛdvibhātaḥ sadā vibhātaḥ sadaikarūpaḥ svena rūpeṇaiṣa brahmalokaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: Once illumined, [it is] always illumined — always uniform — this is <s>Brahmaloka</s>, by its own nature. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.4.2:] Since blindness and the like, being effects of evil, belong to one who has a body but not to one who is bodiless — therefore, having crossed this bridge — having attained this Self — one who was formerly blind while embodied becomes no longer blind. Likewise, one who was wounded while embodied — upon separation from the body, having crossed the bridge, having attained [the Self] — becomes no longer wounded.

children.text: START ChUp 8,4.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.4.3]

children.text:
tad ya evaitaṃ brahmalokaṃ brahmacaryeṇānuvindanti teṣām evaiṣa brahmalokaḥ |
teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati || ChUp_8,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Those who find this <s>Brahmaloka</s> through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) — for them alone is this <s>Brahmaloka</s>. They have freedom of movement in all worlds.' (ChUp 8.4.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,4.3 tattatraivaṃ satyetaṃ yathoktaṃ brahmalokaṃ brahmacaryeṇa srīviṣayatṛṣṇātyāgena śāsrācāryopadeśamanuvindanti svātmasaṃvedyatāmāpādayanti ye teṣāmeva brahmacaryasādhanavatāṃ brahmavidāmeṣa brahmalokaḥ nānyeṣāṃ srīviṣayasaṃparkajātatṛṣṇānāṃ brahmavidāmapītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.4.3:] This being so, those who find this <s>Brahmaloka</s> as described — through <s>brahmacarya</s>, by the abandonment of craving for objects of sensual pleasure, and through the instruction of scripture and teacher — [meaning] they bring it to the state of being realized by their own self — for those knowers of <s>Brahman</s> who possess <s>brahmacarya</s> as their means, this <s>Brahmaloka</s> [exists]; but not for others who, though knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, have craving born of contact with objects of sensual pleasure — that is the meaning.

children.text: teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavatītyuktārtham /
children.translated_text: 'They have freedom of movement in all worlds' — this has the meaning already stated.

children.text: tasmātparamametatsādhanaṃ brahmacaryaṃ brahmavidāmityabhiprāyaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is: therefore, <s>brahmacarya</s> is the supreme means for knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, and hence must be carefully guarded. (3)

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,5.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.5.1]

children.text:
atha yad yajña ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat |
brahmacaryeṇa hy eva yo jñātā taṃ vindate |
atha yad iṣṭam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat |
brahmacaryeṇa hy eveṣṭvātmānam anuvindate || ChUp_8,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, what they call "sacrifice" (<s>yajña</s>) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. For only through <s>brahmacarya</s> does the knower find That. And what they call "the sacrificial offering" (<s>iṣṭa</s>) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. For only through <s>brahmacarya</s>, having sought, does one find the <s>Ātman</s>.' (ChUp 8.5.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,5.1 ya ātmā setutvādiguṇaiḥ stutastatprāptaye jñānasahakārisādhanāntaraṃ brahmacaryākhyaṃ vidātavyamityāha /
yajñādibhiśca tatstauti kartavyārtham- atha yadyajña ityācakṣate loke paramapuruṣārthasādhanaṃ kathayanti śiṣṭāstadbrahmacaryameva /
yajñasyāpi yatphalaṃ tadbrahmacaryavāllaṃbhate 'to yajño 'pi brahmacaryaṃ bhavati pratipattavyam /
kathaṃ brahmacaryaṃ yajña ityāha-brahmacaryeṇaiva hi yasmādyo jñātāsa taṃ brahmalokaṃ yajñasyāpi pāramparyeṇa phalabhūtaṃ vindate labhate tato yajño 'pi brahmacaryameveti /
yo jñātetyakṣarānuvṛtteryajño brahmacaryameva /
atha yadiṣṭamityācakṣate brahmacaryameva tat /
children.translated_text: 'And what they call "the offering" (<s>iṣṭa</s>) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.'

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How so?

children.text: brahmacaryeṇaiva sādhanena tamīśvaramiṣṭvā pūjayitvāthavaiṣaṇāmātmaviṣayāṃ kṛtvā tamātmānamanuvindate /
children.translated_text: Through <s>brahmacarya</s> as the means, having worshipped — honored — that Lord, or having made the quest (<s>eṣaṇā</s>) directed toward the <s>Ātman</s>, one finds that <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: eṣaṇādiṣṭamapi brahmacaryameva //1 //
children.translated_text: The quest (<s>eṣaṇā</s>) [implied by] '<s>iṣṭa</s>' is also indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.5.1:] The <s>Ātman</s> that has been praised with qualities such as being a bridge — for its attainment, another means auxiliary to knowledge, called <s>brahmacarya</s>, is to be known — thus [the text] states. And it praises that [brahmacarya] through sacrifice and the rest, for the purpose of [motivating its] practice: 'Now, what they call "sacrifice" — what the learned declare in the world as the means to the supreme human goal — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. The very fruit of sacrifice is obtained through <s>brahmacarya</s> — therefore sacrifice too should be understood as <s>brahmacarya</s>. How is <s>brahmacarya</s> sacrifice? [The text] says: because through <s>brahmacarya</s> alone, the knower finds that <s>Brahmaloka</s> which is also the ultimate fruit of sacrifice through a chain [of causation] — therefore sacrifice is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.' The [text] 'the knower' — by the recurrence of the syllable [from 'yajña'] — [confirms that] sacrifice is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,5.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.5.2]

children.text:
atha yat sattrāyaṇam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat |
brahmacaryeṇa hy eva sata ātmanas trāṇaṃ vindate |
atha yan maunam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat |
brahmacaryeṇa hy evātmānam anuvidya manute || ChUp_8,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, what they call the "<s>sattrāyaṇa</s>" (sacrificial session) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. For through <s>brahmacarya</s> alone does one find protection (<s>trāṇa</s>) of the true (<s>sat</s>) <s>Ātman</s>. And what they call "silence" (<s>mauna</s>) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. For through <s>brahmacarya</s> alone, having found the <s>Ātman</s>, does one reflect.' (ChUp 8.5.2)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,5.2 atha yatsattrāyaṇamityācakṣate brahmacaryameva tattathā sataḥ parasmādātmana ātmanasrāṇaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ brahmacaryasādhanena vindate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.5.2:] 'What they call <s>sattrāyaṇa</s> — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.' Likewise, [the word is analyzed as:] of <s>sat</s> (the true), of the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, <s>trāṇa</s> (protection) — [one] finds protection through the means of <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: ataḥ sattrāyaṇaśabdamapi brahmacaryameva sat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what is denoted by the word <s>sattrāyaṇa</s> is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: atha yanmaunamityācakṣate brahmacaryameva tadbrahmacaryeṇaiva sādhanena yuktaḥ sannātmānaṃ śāsrācāryābhyāmanuvidya paścānmanute dhyāyati /
children.translated_text: 'What they call "silence" (<s>mauna</s>) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.' Through <s>brahmacarya</s> as the means, being properly engaged, having found the <s>Ātman</s> through scripture and teacher, one afterward <s>manute</s> (meditates, reflects).

children.text: ato maunaśabdamapi brahmacaryameva //2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, what is denoted by the word <s>mauna</s> is also indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 8,5.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.5.3]

children.text:
atha yad anāśakāyanam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat |
eṣa hy ātmā na naśyati yaṃ brahmacaryeṇānuvindate |
atha yad araṇyāyanam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat |
tat araś ca ha vai ṇyaś cārṇavau brahmaloke tṛtīyasyām ito divi |
tad airaṃmadīyaṃ saraḥ |
tad aśvatthaḥ somasavanaḥ |
tad aparājitā pūr brahmaṇaḥ prabhuvimitaṃ hiraṇmayam || ChUp_8,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'What they call "fasting" (<s>anāśakāyana</s>) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. For this <s>Ātman</s> does not perish, which one finds through <s>brahmacarya</s>. And what they call "going to the forest" (<s>araṇyāyana</s>) — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. <s>Ara</s> and <s>Ṇya</s> are indeed the two oceans in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, in the third heaven from here. There is the lake <s>Airaṃmadīya</s>. There is the fig tree <s>Somasavana</s>. There is the unconquered city of <s>Brahman</s>, the golden [hall] specially measured by the Lord.' (ChUp 8.5.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,5.3 atha yadanāśakāyanamityācakṣate brahmacaryameva tat /
yamātmānaṃ brahmacaryeṇānuvindate sa eṣa hyātmā brahmacaryasādhanavato na naśyati tasmādanāśakāyanamapi brahmacaryameva /
atha yadaraṇyāyanamityācakṣate brahmacaryameva tat /
araṇyaśabdayorarṇavayorbrahmacaryavato 'yanādaraṇyāyanaṃ brahmacaryam /
yo jñānādyajña eṣaṇādiṣṭaṃ satasrāṇātsattrāyaṇaṃ mananānmaunamanaśanādanāśakāyanamaraṇyayorgamanādaraṇyāyanamityādibhirmahadbhiḥ puruṣārthasādhanaiḥ stutatvādbrahmacaryaṃ paramaṃ jñānasya sahakārikāraṇaṃ sādhanamityato brahmavidā yatnato rakṣaṇīyamityarthaḥ /
tattatra hi brahmaloke 'raśca ha vai prasiddho ṇyaścārṇavau samudropame vā sarasī tṛtīyasyāṃ bhuvamantarikṣaṃ cāpekṣya tṛtīyā dyaustasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāmito 'smāllokādārabhya gaṇyamānāyāṃ divi /
tattatraiva cairamirānnaṃ tanmaya airo maṇḍastena pūrṇamairaṃ madīyaṃ tadupayogināṃ madakaraṃ harṣotpādakaṃ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: There too is [a lake]: <s>aira</s> [means] food; <s>maṇḍa</s> [means] what is made of that; the lake filled with that, <s>airaṃmadīya</s>, producing intoxication — producing joy — for those who partake of it.

children.text: tatraiva cāśvattho vṛkṣaḥ somasavano nāmataḥ somo 'mṛtaṃ tanniḥsravo 'mṛtasrava iti vā /
children.translated_text: There too is a fig tree (<s>aśvattha</s>) named <s>Somasavana</s> — <s>Soma</s> means nectar; it flows from that — meaning [it is] a flow of nectar.

children.text: tatraiva ca brahmaloke brahmacaryasādhanarahitairbrahmacaryasādhanavadbhyo 'nyairna jīyata ityaparājitā nāma pūḥ purī brahmaṇo hiraṇyagarbhasya /
children.translated_text: There too, in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, is the city called <s>Aparājitā</s> (unconquered) — unconquered by those lacking the means of <s>brahmacarya</s>, [meaning] not won by others apart from those possessing the means of <s>brahmacarya</s> — the city of <s>Brahman</s>, [i.e.] of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.

children.text: brahmaṇā ca prabhuṇā viśeṣeṇa mitaṃ nirmitaṃ tacca hiraṇmayaṃ sauvarṇaṃ prabhuvimitaṃ maṇḍapamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ //3 //
children.translated_text: And [it is] specially measured — specially constructed — by <s>Brahman</s>, the Lord; and it is golden (<s>hiraṇmaya</s>). 'The golden pavilion specially measured by the Lord' — this is the completion of the sentence. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.5.3:] 'What they call <s>anāśakāyana</s> — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.' The <s>Ātman</s> that one finds through <s>brahmacarya</s> — this <s>Ātman</s> does not perish for one who possesses the means of <s>brahmacarya</s>. Therefore <s>anāśakāyana</s> too is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>. 'What they call <s>araṇyāyana</s> — that is indeed <s>brahmacarya</s>.' [The word is analyzed as:] <s>ayana</s> (going) to the two [oceans denoted by] the words <s>ara</s> and <s>ṇya</s> for one who possesses <s>brahmacarya</s> — that is <s>araṇyāyana</s>, which is <s>brahmacarya</s>. Since <s>brahmacarya</s> is praised by these great means to the supreme human goal — sacrifice, offering, protection of Being, silence, fasting, and going to the forest — [the intended meaning is that] <s>brahmacarya</s> is the supreme auxiliary cause and means for knowledge, and hence must be carefully guarded by the knower of <s>Brahman</s>. There indeed, in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, are <s>ara</s> and <s>ṇya</s> — two well-known oceans, or ocean-like lakes — in the third [heaven]: counting earth and the atmosphere, the third is heaven — in that third heaven, counting from this world.

children.text: START ChUp 8,5.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.5.4]

children.text:
tad ya evaitāv araṃ ca ṇyaṃ cārṇavau brahmaloke brahmacaryeṇānuvindanti teṣām evaiṣa brahmalokaḥ |
teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati || ChUp_8,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Those who find these two oceans, <s>Ara</s> and <s>Ṇya</s>, in <s>Brahmaloka</s> through <s>brahmacarya</s> — for them alone is this <s>Brahmaloka</s>. They have freedom of movement in all worlds.' (ChUp 8.5.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,5.4 tattatra hi brahmaloka etāvarṇavau yāvaraṇyākhyāvuktau brahmacaryeṇa sādhanenānuvindanti ye teṣāmevaiṣa yo vyākhyāto brahmalokasteṣāṃ ca brahmacaryasādhavanatāṃ brahmavidāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati /
nānyeṣāmabrahmacaryaparāṇāṃ bāhyaviṣayāsaktabuddhīnāṃ kadācidapītyarthaḥ /
nanvatra tvamindrastvaṃ yamastvaṃ varuṇa ityādibhiryathā kaścitstūyate mahārha evamiṣṭādibhiḥ śabdairna stryādiviṣayatṛṣṇānivṛttimātraṃ stutyarhaṃ kiṃ tarhi jñānasya mokṣasādhanatvāttadeveṣṭādibhiḥ stūyata iti kecit /
na /
stryādibāhyaviṣayatṛṣṇāpahṛtacittānāṃ pratyagātmavivekavijñānānupapatteḥ /
"parāñci khāni vyatṛṇatsvayaṃbhūstasmātparāṅpaśyati nāntarātman"ityādiśrutismṛtiśatebhyaḥ /
jñānasahakārikāraṇaṃ stryādiviṣayatṛṣṇānivṛttisādhanaṃ vidhātavyameveti yuktaiva tatstutiḥ /
nanu ca yajñādibhiḥ stutaṃ brahmacaryamiti yajñādīnāṃ puruṣārthasādhanatvaṃ gamyate /
satyaṃ gamyate /
na tviha brahmalokaṃ prati yajñādīnāṃ sādhanatvamabhipretya yajñādibhirbrahmacaryaṃ stūyate kiṃ tarhi teṣāṃ prasiddhaṃ puruṣārthasādhanatvamapekṣya /
yathendrādibhī rājā na tu yatrendrādīnāṃ vyāpārastatraiva rājña iti tadvat /
ya imer'ṇavādayo brāhmalaukikāḥ saṃkalpajāśca pitrādayo bhogāste kiṃ pārthivā āpyāśca yatheha loke dṛśyante taddhadarṇavavṛkṣapūḥsvarṇamaṇḍapānyāhosvinmānasapratyayamātrāṇīti /
kiñcātaḥ, yadi pārthivā āpyāśca sthūlāḥ syurhṛdyākāśe samādhānānupapattiḥ /
purāṇe ca"manomayāni brahmaloke śarīrādīnī"ti vākyaṃ virudhyeta /
"aśokamahimam"ityādyāśca śrutayaḥ /
nanu"samudrāḥ saritaḥ sarāṃsi vāpyaḥ kūpā yajñā vedā mantrādayaśca mūrtimanto brahmāṇamupatiṣṭhanta"iti mānasatvai virudhyeta purāṇasmṛtiḥ /
na /
mūrtimattve prasiddharūpāṇāmeva tatra gamanānupapatteḥ /
tasmātprasiddhamūrtivyatirekeṇa sāgarādīnāṃ mūrtyantaraṃ sāgarādibhirupāttaṃ brahmalokagantṛ kalpanāyāṃ yathāprasiddhā eva mānasya ākāravatyaḥ puṃstryādyā mūrtayo yuktāḥ kalpayituṃ mānasadehānurūpyasaṃbandhopapatteḥ /
dṛṣṭā hi mānasya evā'kāravatyaḥ puṃstryādyā mūrtayaḥ svapne /
nanu tā anṛtā eva /
ta ime satyāḥ kāmā iti śrutistathā sati virudhyeta /
na /
mānasapratyayasya sattvopapatteḥ /
mānasā hi pratyayāḥ srīpuruṣādyākārāḥ svapne dṛśyante /
nanu jāgradvāsanārūpāḥ svapnadṛśyā na tu tatra stryādayaḥ svapne vidyante /
atyalpamidamucyate /
jāgradviṣayā api mānasapratyayābhinirvṛttā eva sadīkṣābhinirvṛttatejo 'bannamayatvājjāgradviṣayāṇām /
saṃkalpamūlā hi lokā iti coktam"samakḷpatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī"ityatra /
sarvaśrutiṣu ca pratyagātmana utpattiḥ pralayaśca tatraiva sthitiśca"yathā vā arā nābhau"ityādinocyate /
tasmānmānasānāṃ bāhyānāṃ ca viṣayāṇāmitaretarakāryakāraṇamiṣyata eva bījāṅkuravat /
yadyapi bāhyā eva mānasā mānasā eva ca bāhyā nānṛtatvaṃ teṣāṃ kadācidapi svātmani bhavati /
nanu svapne dṛṣṭāḥ pratibuddhasyānṛtā bhavanti viṣayāḥ /
satyameva /
jāgradbodhāpekṣaṃ tu tadanṛtatvaṃ na svataḥ /
tathā svapnabodhāpekṣaṃ ca jāgraddṛṣṭaviṣayānṛtatvaṃ na svataḥ /
viśeṣākāramātraṃ tu sarveṣāṃ mithyāpratyayanimittamiti vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyamanṛtaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇītyeva satyam /
tānyapyākāraviśeṣato 'nṛtaṃ svataḥ sanmātrarūpatayā satyam prāksadātmapratibodhātsvaviṣaye 'pi sarvaṃ styameva svapnadṛśyā iveti na kaścidvirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And even those [three forms], from the standpoint of specific form, are unreal; from the standpoint of being pure <s>Sat</s> (Being) in nature, they are real. Prior to the awakening to the truth of <s>Sat</s> as the <s>Ātman</s>, everything is real even in one's own domain — like objects seen in a dream — hence there is no contradiction.

children.text: tasmānmānasā eva brāhmalaukikā araṇyādayaḥ pitrādayaḥ kāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the oceans <s>Ara</s> and <s>Ṇya</s> belonging to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, the enjoyments of ancestors, and so on — are all mental.

children.text: bāhyaviṣayabhogavadaśuddhirahitatvācchuddhasattvasaṃkalpajanyā iti niratiśayasukhāḥ satyāśceśvarāṇāṃ bhavantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Being free from impurity — unlike the enjoyment of external objects — being born of the will of pure <s>sattva</s>, they are of unsurpassable happiness and are real for the lords [of those worlds] — that is the meaning.

children.text: satsatyātmapratibodhe 'pi rajjvāmiva kalpitāḥ sarpādayaḥ sadātmasvarūpatāmeva pratipadyanta iti sadātmanā satyā eva bhavanti //4//
children.translated_text: Even upon the awakening to the true <s>Sat-Ātman</s>, they — like imagined serpents upon a rope — attain the very nature of the <s>Sat-Ātman</s>; hence by [being one with] the <s>Sat-Ātman</s>, they are indeed real. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.5.4:] There indeed, in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, those who find through <s>brahmacarya</s> as their means these two oceans called <s>Ara</s> and <s>Ṇya</s> as described — for them alone is this <s>Brahmaloka</s> that has been explained; and for those knowers of <s>Brahman</s> who possess the means of <s>brahmacarya</s>, there is freedom of movement in all worlds — but never for others who are not devoted to <s>brahmacarya</s>, whose minds are attached to external objects — that is the meaning. [Objection:] But here, just as someone is praised with [titles like] 'You are <s>Indra</s>, you are <s>Yama</s>, you are <s>Varuṇa</s>' — so too, with words like <s>iṣṭa</s> (offering) and the rest, it is not mere cessation of craving for women and such that is praiseworthy; rather, since knowledge alone is the means to liberation, it is knowledge itself that is praised through [the terms] <s>iṣṭa</s> and the rest — so say some. [Reply:] No — because for those whose minds are stolen by craving for external objects like women, the discriminative knowledge of the inner <s>Ātman</s> is impossible. [This is known] from hundreds of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> passages such as: 'The self-born one pierced the openings outward; therefore one sees outward, not the inner <s>Ātman</s>.' The means for the cessation of craving for objects like women, being an auxiliary cause of knowledge, is indeed to be enjoined — hence praise of that is entirely proper. [Objection:] But since <s>brahmacarya</s> is praised through sacrifice and the rest, the capacity of sacrifice and the rest to be means to the supreme human goal is understood. [Reply:] True, it is understood. But here, the praise of <s>brahmacarya</s> through sacrifice and the rest is not intended in the sense that sacrifice and the rest are means specifically to <s>Brahmaloka</s>; rather, it is with regard to their well-known capacity as means to [various] human goals — just as [one praises] a king by [comparing him to] <s>Indra</s> and others, but not [implying] that where <s>Indra</s> and others function, there alone the king [functions] — in the same way. Now, these oceans and so on belonging to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, and the enjoyments of ancestors and others born of will — are they earthly and watery, as seen in this world? Those oceans, trees, cities, golden pavilions — or are they merely mental concepts? What follows from this? If they were earthly and watery — gross — their accommodation in the space of the heart would be impossible. And the statement in the <s>Purāṇa</s> — 'The bodies and so on in <s>Brahmaloka</s> are made of mind' — would be contradicted. And <s>śruti</s>s like 'free from sorrow, great' [would be contradicted]. [Objection:] But [the Purāṇa says:] 'Oceans, rivers, lakes, tanks, wells, sacrifices, <s>Vedas</s>, mantras, and others, having assumed forms, attend upon <s>Brahmā</s>' — this would contradict their being mental. [Reply:] No — because those whose forms are well-known cannot in their [well-known] form travel there. Therefore, apart from the well-known forms of oceans and the like, other forms assumed by oceans and the like that go to <s>Brahmaloka</s> — in imagining [these], it is proper to imagine forms with shapes — male, female, and so on — exactly as well-known, being mental; because the connection based on suitability to mental bodies is possible. For forms with shapes — male, female, and so on — are seen to be mental in dreams. [Objection:] But those are unreal. [Reply:] The <s>śruti</s> 'These desires are real' would then be contradicted. [Reply to that:] No — because a mental concept can have being (<s>sattva</s>). Mental concepts having the forms of women, men, and so on are seen in dreams. [Objection:] But dream-objects are of the nature of waking impressions — they do not exist as women and so on in dreams. [Reply:] Very little is said [by this objection].
