Waking objects too are produced by mental concepts alone — because waking objects, being made of fire, water, and food, are produced through the creative gaze [of the Lord]. 'Worlds have their root in will' — as is said in: 'He willed heaven and earth into being.' In all <s>śruti</s>s, the origin of the inner <s>Ātman</s>, its dissolution, and its abiding there are stated with 'Just as spokes [are fixed] in the hub' and such. Therefore, for both mental and external objects, their being cause and effect of each other is accepted, like seed and sprout. Although external [objects] are indeed mental, and mental [objects] are indeed external — their unreality never pertains to their own self. [Objection:] But objects seen in dreams become unreal for one who is awake. [Reply:] True indeed. But that unreality is relative to waking consciousness — not intrinsic. Similarly, the unreality of objects seen in waking is relative to dream consciousness — not intrinsic. The specific form alone of all [objects] is the cause of false cognition — thus 'modification is merely a name, a verbal handle, unreal; the three forms [of fire, water, food] alone are the truth' — this alone is true.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,6.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.6.1]

children.text:
atha yā etā hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāḥ piṅgalasyāṇimnas tiṣṭhanti śuklasya nīlasya pītasya lohitasyeti |
asau vādityaḥ piṅgala eṣa śukla eṣa nīla eṣa pīta eṣa lohitaḥ || ChUp_8,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) of the heart — they consist of a subtle substance that is brown, white, blue, yellow, and red. The sun yonder is brown; this [fire] is white; this [cloud] is blue; this [lightning] is yellow; this [rain] is red.' (ChUp 8.6.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,6.1 yastu hṛdayapuṇḍarīkagataṃ yathoktaguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ brahma brahmacaryādisādhanasaṃpannastyaktabāhyaviṣayānṛtatṛṣṇaḥ sannupāste tasyeyaṃ mūrdhanyayā nāḍyā gatirvaktavyeti nāḍīkhaṇḍa ārabhyate- atha yā etā vakṣyamāṇā hṛdayasya puṇḍarīkākārasya brahmopāsanasthānasya saṃbandhinyo nāḍyo hṛdayamāṃsapiṇḍātsarvato viniḥsṛtā ādityamaṇḍalādiva raśmayastāścaitāḥ piṅgalasya varṇaviśeṣaviśiṣṭasyāṇimnaḥ sūkṣmarasasya rasena pūrṇāstadākārā eva tiṣṭhanti vartanta ityarthaḥ /
tathā śuklasya nīlasya pītasya lohitasya ca rasasya pūrṇā iti sarvatrādhyāhāryam /
saureṇa tejasā pittākhyena pākābhinirvṛttena kaphenālpena saṃparkātpiṅgalaṃ bhavati sauraṃ tejaḥ pittākhyām tadeva ca vātabhūyastvānnīlaṃ bhavati /
tadeva ca kaphabhūyastvācchuklam /
kaphena samatāyāṃ pītam /
śoṇita bāhulyena lohitam /
vaidyakādvā varṇaviśeṣā anveṣṭavyāḥ kathaṃ bhavantīti /
children.translated_text: or the specific colors should be investigated from medical science — how they arise.

children.text: śrutistvāhā'dityasaṃbandhādeva tattejaso nāḍīṣvanugatasyaite varṇaviśeṣā iti /
children.translated_text: But the <s>śruti</s> says that these specific colors in the <s>nāḍī</s>s are due to the connection with the sun alone — of that radiance pervading the <s>nāḍī</s>s.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How so?

children.text: asau vā ādityaḥ piṅgalo varṇata eṣa ādityaḥ śuklo 'pyeṣa nīla eṣa pīta eṣa lohita āditya eva //1 //
children.translated_text: This sun is tawny in color; this sun is also white; it is also blue; it is yellow; it is red — it is the sun itself [in all these colors]. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.6.1:] For one who, being endowed with the means of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and the like, having renounced the craving for the unreal external objects, worships <s>Brahman</s> as situated in the lotus of the heart and qualified by the attributes described — for such a one, the departure through the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) at the top of the head is to be stated; hence the section on the <s>nāḍī</s>s is commenced. Now, these <s>nāḍī</s>s that are to be described, belonging to the heart that is in the shape of a lotus and is the place of meditation on <s>Brahman</s>, having issued forth in all directions from the lump of flesh that is the heart — like rays from the solar disc — these are filled with the essence of a subtle fluid of a tawny (<s>piṅgala</s>) color-specification, and they stand in that very form — that is the meaning. Likewise, they are filled with the essence of white, blue, yellow, and red [fluids] — this is to be supplied in every case. The solar radiance, called bile (<s>pitta</s>), produced through digestion, becomes tawny through slight contact with phlegm (<s>kapha</s>). That same solar radiance becomes blue through the predominance of wind (<s>vāta</s>),

children.text: START ChUp 8,6.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.6.2]

children.text:
tad yathā mahāpatha ātata ubhau grāmau gacchatīmaṃ cāmuṃ caivam evaitā ādityasya raśmaya ubhau lokau gacchantīmaṃ cāmuṃ ca |
amuṣmād ādityāt pratāyante tā āsu nāḍīṣu sṛptāḥ |
ābhyo nāḍībhyaḥ pratāyante te 'muṣminn āditye sṛptāḥ || ChUp_8,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just as a great highway stretches between [two villages] and reaches both villages — this one and that one — so too these rays of the sun reach both worlds — this one and that one. They extend from that sun and enter into these <s>nāḍī</s>s. They extend from these <s>nāḍī</s>s and enter into that sun.' (ChUp 8.6.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,6.2 tasyādhyātmaṃ nāḍībhiḥ kathaṃ saṃbandha ityatra dṛṣṭāntamāha-tattatra yathā loke mahānvistīrṇaḥ panthā mahāpatha ātato vyāpta ubhau gacchatīmaṃ ca saṃnihitamamuṃ ca viprakṛṣṭaṃ dūrasthamevaṃ yathā dṛṣṭānto mahāpatha ubhau grāmau praviṣṭa evamevaitā ādityasya raśmaya ubhau lokāvamuṃ cā'dityamaṇḍalamimaṃ ca puruṣaṃ gacchantyubhayatra praviṣṭāḥ /
yathā mahāpathaḥ /
katham /
amuṣmādādityamaṇḍalātpratāyante saṃtatā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: From that solar disc they extend — they are continuous.

children.text: tā adhyātmamāsu piṅgalādivarṇāsu yathoktāsu nāḍīṣu sṛptā gatāḥ praviṣṭā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: They enter into these <s>nāḍī</s>s described as tawny and other colors in the individual self — meaning they have gone, they have entered.

children.text: ābhyo nāḍībhyaḥ pratāyante pravṛttāḥ santānabhūtāḥ satyaste 'muṣmin /
children.translated_text: From these <s>nāḍī</s>s they extend, having proceeded, being continuous, into that [sun].

children.text: raśmīnāmubhayaliṅgatvātta ityucyante //2 //
children.translated_text: Because the rays have a dual characteristic [of extending both ways], they are referred to as 'they' (<s>te</s>). (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.6.2:] How is the connection of the sun with the <s>nāḍī</s>s in the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>)? An analogy is given: Just as in the world, a great, extensive road — a highway — stretched out, pervading, reaches both [places] — this one that is near and that one that is far, distant — just as in this analogy the highway has entered both villages — so too these rays of the sun reach both worlds: that one, the solar disc, and this one, the person — having entered both, like the highway. How?

children.text: START ChUp 8,6.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.6.3]

children.text:
tad yatraitat suptaḥ samastaḥ saṃprasannaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānāti |
āsu tadā nāḍīṣu sṛpto bhavati |
taṃ na kaścana pāpmā spṛśati |
tejasā hi tadā saṃpanno bhavati || ChUp_8,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'When one is thus asleep, fully collected, serene, and does not perceive any dream — then one has entered into these <s>nāḍī</s>s. No evil (<s>pāpman</s>) touches that one. For one is then pervaded by radiance (<s>tejas</s>).' (ChUp 8.6.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,6.3 tattatraivaṃ sati yatra yasminkāla etatsvapanamayaṃ jīvaḥ supto bhavati /
svāpasya dviprakāratvādviśeṣaṇaṃ samasta iti /
upasaṃhṛtasarvakaraṇavṛttirityetat /
ato bāhyaviṣayasaṃparkajanitakāluṣyābhāvātsamyak /
prasannaḥ saṃprasanno bhavati /
ata eva svapnaṃ viṣayākārābhāsaṃ mānasaṃ svapnapratyayaṃ na vijānāti nānubhavatītyarthaḥ /
yadaivaṃ supto bhavatyāsu sauratejaḥpūrṇāsu yathoktāsu nāḍīṣu tadā sṛptaḥ praviṣṭo nāḍībhirdvārabhūtābhirhṛdayākāśaṃ gato bhavatītyarthaḥ /
na hyanyatra satsaṃpatteḥ svapnādarśanamastīti sāmarthyānnāḍīṣviti saptamī tṛtīyayā pariṇamyate /
taṃ satā saṃpannaṃ na kaścana na kaścidapi dharmādharmarūpaḥ pāpmā spṛśatīti svarūpāvasthitatvāttadā'tmanaḥ /
dehendriyaviśiṣṭaṃ hi sukhaduḥkhakāryapradānena pāpmā spṛśatīti na tu satsaṃpannaṃ svarūpāvasthaṃ kaścidapi pāpmā spraṣṭumutsahate /
aviṣayatvāt /
anyo hyanyasya viṣayo bhavati na tvanyatvaṃ kenacitkutaścidapi satsaṃpannasya /
svarūpapracyavanaṃ tvātmano jāgratsvapnāvasthāṃ prati gamanaṃ bāhyaviṣayapratibodho 'vidyākāmakarmabījasya brahmavidyāhutāśādāhanimittamityavocāma ṣaṣṭha eva tadihāpi pratyetavyam /
children.translated_text: The falling away from one's own nature — the going of the <s>Ātman</s> toward the waking and dream states — the awareness of external objects — has as its cause the seed of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, and <s>karma</s>, whose destruction is caused by the fire of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> — this we stated in the sixth [chapter] itself; that is to be understood here as well.

children.text: yadaivaṃ suptaḥ saureṇa tejasā hi nāḍyantargatena sarvataḥ saṃpanno vyāpto bhavati /
children.translated_text: When one is thus asleep, one is pervaded on all sides by the solar radiance within the <s>nāḍī</s>s.

children.text: ato viśeṣeṇa cakṣurādināḍīdvārairbāhyaviṣayabhogāyāprasṛtāni karaṇānyasya tadā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, at that time, one's sense-organs are not sent forth through the doors of the <s>nāḍī</s>s of the eye and such for the enjoyment of external objects.

children.text: tasmādayaṃ karaṇānāṃ nirodhātsvātmanyevāvasthitaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānātīti yuktam //3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper that this one, due to the restraint of the sense-organs, established in one's own <s>Ātman</s> alone, does not perceive any dream. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.6.3:] Then, when this is the case — at the time when this sleeping <s>jīva</s> (individual self) becomes asleep. Since sleep is of two kinds, a specification [is given]: 'fully collected' (<s>samasta</s>) — meaning one whose activity of all sense-organs has been withdrawn. Therefore, due to the absence of agitation produced by contact with external objects, one becomes perfectly serene (<s>saṃprasanna</s>). Hence, one does not perceive any dream — the mental dream-cognition that is an appearance in the form of objects — meaning one does not experience it. When one is thus asleep, then, one has entered into these <s>nāḍī</s>s filled with solar radiance as described — meaning one has entered through the <s>nāḍī</s>s, which serve as doors, into the space of the heart. For there is no non-perception of dreams other than through union with <s>Sat</s> (Being); therefore, by implication, the locative case 'in the <s>nāḍī</s>s' is to be construed as instrumental. No evil — not any <s>pāpman</s> (evil) in the form of <s>dharma</s> (merit) or <s>adharma</s> (demerit) — touches that one who has united with <s>Sat</s>, because the <s>Ātman</s> is then established in its own nature. For evil touches [the self] only when distinguished by body and sense-organs, through the bestowal of the effects of pleasure and suffering; but no evil whatsoever is able to touch one who has united with <s>Sat</s> and is established in one's own nature — because it is not an object [for evil]. For something else is an object of something else, but for one who has united with <s>Sat</s>, there is no otherness from anything whatsoever.

children.text: START ChUp 8,6.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.6.4]

children.text:
atha yatraitad abalimānaṃ nīto bhavati |
tam abhita āsīnā āhur jānāsi māṃ jānāsi mām iti |
sa yāvad asmāc charīrād anutkrānto bhavati |
tāvaj jānāti || ChUp_8,6.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, when one is brought to a state of weakness — those sitting around say: "Do you know me? Do you know me?" As long as one has not departed from this body, so long one knows.' (ChUp 8.6.4)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,6.4 tatraivaṃ satyatha yatra yasminkāle 'balimānamabalabhāvaṃ dehasya rogādinimittaṃ jarādinimittaṃ vā kṛśībhāvametannayanaṃ nītaḥ prāpito devadatto bhavati mumūrṣaryadā bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.6.4:] When this is the case — now, at the time when one is brought to a state of weakness (<s>abalimāna</s>) — the weakening of the body due to disease or old age, emaciation — when <s>Devadatta</s> (a person) has been brought to this state, when he is about to die — that is the meaning.

children.text: tamabhitaḥ sarvato veṣṭayitvā'sīnā jñātaya āhurjānāsi māṃ tava putraṃ jānāsi māṃ pitaraṃ cetyādi /
children.translated_text: Those sitting around him on all sides, surrounding him — the relatives say: 'Do you know me, your son? Do you know me, your father?' and so on.

children.text: sa mumūrṣuryāvadasmāccharīrādanutkrānto 'nirgato bhavati tāvatputrādīñjānāti //4 //
children.translated_text: He, the one about to die, as long as he has not departed, not gone out from this body — so long he knows his sons and the rest. (4)

children.text: START ChUp 8,6.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.6.5]

children.text:
atha yatraitad asmāc charīrād utkrāmati |
athaitair eva raśmibhir ūrdhvam ākramate |
sa om iti vā hod vā mīyate |
sa yāvat kṣipyen manas tāvad ādityaṃ gacchati |
etad vai khalu lokadvāraṃ viduṣāṃ prapadanaṃ nirodho 'viduṣām || ChUp_8,6.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, when one departs from this body — then one ascends upward by these very rays. One dies [while meditating on] <s>Oṃ</s>, or indeed [otherwise]. As quickly as one can direct the mind, so quickly does one reach the sun. This indeed is the door of the world — an entrance for the wise, a barrier for the ignorant.' (ChUp 8.6.5)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,6.5 atha yatra yadaitatkriyāviśeṣaṇamityasmāccharīrādutkrāmati /
atha tadaitaireva yathoktābhī raśmibhirūrdhvamākramate yathākarmārjitaṃ lokaṃ pratyavidvān /
itarastu vidvānyathoktasādhanasaṃpannaḥ sa omityoṅkāreṇā'tmānaṃ dhyāyanyathāpūrvaṃ vā haiva, udvordhvaṃ vā vidvāṃśceditarastiryaṅvetyabhiprāyaḥ /
mīyate pramīyate gacchatītyarthaḥ /
sa vidvānutkramiṣyanyāvatkṣipyenmano yāvatā kālena manasaḥ kṣepaḥ syāttāvatā kālenā'dityaṃ gacchati prapnoti kṣipraṃ gacchatītyartho na tu tāvataiva kāleneti vivakṣitam /
kimarthamādityaṃ gacchatītyucyate-etadvai khalu prasiddhaṃ brahmalokasya dvāraṃ ya ādityastena dvārabhūtena brahmaloka gacchati vidvān /
ato viduṣāṃ prapadanaṃ prapadyate brahmalokamanena dvāreṇeti prapadanam /
children.translated_text: Hence it is the entrance (<s>prapadana</s>) for the wise — meaning they enter the world of <s>Brahman</s> through this door.

children.text: nirodhanaṃ nirodho 'smādādityādaviduṣāṃ bhavatīti nirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is a barrier (<s>nirodha</s>) for the ignorant — meaning the ignorant are blocked from this [sun].

children.text: saureṇa tejasā deha eva niruddhāḥ santo mūrdhanyayā nāḍyā notkramanta evetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Being blocked by solar radiance within the body itself, [the ignorant] do not depart through the <s>nāḍī</s> at the top of the head — that is the meaning.

children.text: viṣvaṅṅanyā iti ślokāt //5 //
children.translated_text: [This is known] from the verse 'those who go in other directions.' (5)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.6.5:] Now, when — 'this' being a specification of the action — one departs from this body. Then, by these very rays as described, one ascends upward — toward the world acquired through <s>karma</s>, if one is not a knower. But the other one — the knower, endowed with the means as described — he, meditating on the <s>Ātman</s> through <s>Oṃ</s> (<s>Oṅkāra</s>), or indeed as before — if he is a knower he goes upward, otherwise he goes sideways — that is the purport. 'Dies' (<s>mīyate</s>) means passes away, departs — that is the meaning. He, the knower about to depart — as quickly as one can cast the mind, in whatever time the casting of the mind would occur, in that [same] time he reaches, attains the sun — meaning he goes swiftly. The intended meaning is not that he reaches [the sun] in literally that much time. For what purpose does [the text] say he reaches the sun? — Because this [sun] is indeed the well-known door to the world of <s>Brahman</s>. The knower goes to the world of <s>Brahman</s> through the sun, which serves as a door.

children.text: START ChUp 8,6.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.6.6]

children.text:
tad eṣa ślokaḥ |
śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāsāṃ mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtaikā |
tayordhvam āyann amṛtatvam eti viṣvaṅṅ anyā utkramaṇe bhavanty utkramaṇe bhavanti || ChUp_8,6.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'On this there is this verse: There are a hundred and one <s>nāḍī</s>s of the heart. Of these, one has issued forth to the top of the head. Going upward through it, one attains immortality. The others, going in various directions, serve for departure — serve for departure.' (ChUp 8.6.6)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,6.6 tadetasminyathokter'tha eṣa śloko mantro bhavati /
śataṃ caikā caikottaraśataṃ nāḍyo hṛdayasya māṃsapiṇḍabhūtasya saṃbandhinyaḥ pradhānato bhavanti /
children.translated_text: A hundred and one — one more than a hundred — <s>nāḍī</s>s belonging to the heart, the lump of flesh, are the principal ones.

children.text: ānantyāddehanāḍīnām /
children.translated_text: Because the <s>nāḍī</s>s of the body are infinite.

children.text: tāsāmekā mūrdhānamabhiniḥsṛtā vinirgatā tayordhvamāyangacchannamṛtatvamamṛtabhāvameti viṣvaṅnānāgatayastiryagvisarpiṇya ūrdhvagāścānyā nāḍyo bhavanti saṃsāragamanadvārabhūtā na tvamṛtatvāya kiṃ tarhyatkamaṇa evotkrāntyarthameva bhavantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of those, one has issued forth, gone out, to the top of the head. Going upward through it, one attains immortality — the state of being immortal. The others, going in various directions, extending sideways and upward — other <s>nāḍī</s>s — serve as doors for traveling in <s>saṃsāra</s>, not for immortality; rather, they serve only for departure — they exist only for the purpose of departing [into <s>saṃsāra</s>]; that is the meaning.

children.text: dvirabhyāsaḥ prakaraṇasamāptyarthaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: The repetition is for the purpose of concluding the section. (6)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.6.6:] On this subject as stated, there is this verse, a <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,7.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.7.1]

children.text:
ya ātmā apahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ |
sa sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānātīti ha prajāpatir uvāca || ChUp_8,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Ātman</s> that is free from evil, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, whose desires are true (<s>satyakāma</s>), whose resolves are true (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>) — that is to be sought, that is to be inquired into. One who finds and knows that <s>Ātman</s> obtains all worlds and all desires' — thus spoke <s>Prajāpati</s>. (ChUp 8.7.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,7.1 "atha ya eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāccharīrātsamutthāya paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyata eṣa ātmeti hovācaitadamṛtamabhayametadbrahma"ityuktam /
tatra ko 'sau saṃprasādaḥ, kathaṃ vā tasyādhigamo yathā so 'smāccharīrātsavijijñāsitavya iti caiṣa niyamavidhireva nāpūrvavidhiḥ /
evamanveṣṭavyo vijijñāsitavya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus 'he is to be sought, to be inquired into' — that is the meaning.

children.text: dṛṣṭārthatvādanveṣaṇavijijñāsanayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Because seeking and inquiring have a visible purpose.

children.text: dṛṣṭārthatvaṃ ca darśayiṣyati nāhamātra bhogyaṃ paśyāmītyanenāsakṛt /
children.translated_text: And the visible purpose will be shown repeatedly by [the statement] 'I do not see anything enjoyable here.'

children.text: pararūpeṇa ca dehādidharbhairavaganyamānasyā'tmanaḥ svarūpādhigame viparītādhigamanivṛttirdṛṣṭaṃ phalamiti niyamārthataivāsya vidheryuktā na tvāgnihotrādīnāmibāpūrvavidhitvamiha saṃbhavati //1 //
children.translated_text: And since the <s>Ātman</s> — which is apprehended through the false form of bodily attributes and the like — upon the attainment of knowledge of its true nature, results in the cessation of false apprehension — this visible fruit [makes] it appropriate that this injunction has a restrictive sense only; the novel-injunction status [applicable to rituals] such as <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like is not possible here. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.7.1:] It was said: 'This one who is serene (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), rising from this body and reaching the highest light, manifests in his own form — this is the <s>Ātman</s>, this is the immortal, the fearless, this is <s>Brahman</s>.' In that [regard]: who is that serene one, and how is he to be comprehended — such that he [departs] from this body — this is a restrictive injunction (<s>niyamavidhi</s>), not a novel injunction (<s>apūrvavidhi</s>). [The rule states:] 'He is to be inquired into' — this is to be sought, to be inquired into; that is the meaning.

children.text: START ChUp 8,7.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.7.2]

children.text:
tad dhobhaye devāsurā anububudhire |
te hocur hanta tam ātmaānam anvecchāmo yam ātmānam anviṣya sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān iti |
indro haiva devānām abhipravavrāja virocano 'surāṇām |
tau hāsaṃvidānāv eva samitpāṇī prajāpatisakāśam ājagmatuḥ || ChUp_8,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Both the gods (<s>deva</s>s) and the demons (<s>asura</s>s) heard about this. They said: "Come, let us seek that <s>Ātman</s>, by seeking which one obtains all worlds and all desires." <s>Indra</s> indeed went forth from among the gods, and <s>Virocana</s> from among the demons. The two, without consulting each other, came to the presence of <s>Prajāpati</s>, fuel in hand.' (ChUp 8.7.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,7.2 taddhobhaya ityādyākhyāyikāprayojanamuktam /
taddha kila prajāpatervacanamubhaye devāsurā devāścāsurāśca devāsurā anu paramparāgataṃ svakarṇagocarāpannamanububudhire 'nubuddhavantaḥ /
te caitatprajāpativaco buddhvā kimakurvannityucyate-te hocuruktavanto 'nyonyaṃ devāḥ svapariṣadyasurāśca hanta yadyanumatirbhavatāṃ prajāpatinoktaṃ tamātmānamanvicchāmo 'nveṣaṇaṃ kurmo yamātmānamanviṣya sarvāṃśca lokānāpnoti sarvāśca kāmānityuktvendro haiva rājaiva svayaṃ devānāmitarāndevāṃśca bhogaparicchadaṃ ca sarvaṃ sthāpayitvā śarīramātreṇaiva prajāpatiṃ pratyabhipravavrāja pragatavāṃstathā virocano 'surāṇām /
vinayena guravo 'bhigantavyā ityetaddarśayati /
children.translated_text: This shows that teachers are to be approached with humility.

children.text: trailokyarājyācca gurutarā vidyate /
children.translated_text: And [that knowledge] is weightier than sovereignty over the three worlds,

children.text: yato devāsurarājau mahārhabhogārhai santau tathā gurumabhyupagatavantau /
children.translated_text: since the kings of the gods and demons, though worthy of great enjoyments, approached the teacher in that manner.

children.text: tau ha kilāsaṃvidānāvevānyonyaṃ saṃvidamakurvāṇau vidyāphalaṃ pratyanyonyamīrṣyāṃ darśayantau samitpāṇī samidbhārahastau prajāpatisakāśamājagmaturāgatavantau //2 //
children.translated_text: Those two, it is said, not knowing each other — not making any agreement with one another — showing jealousy toward each other regarding the fruit of knowledge — came to the presence of <s>Prajāpati</s> with fuel in hand, carrying bundles of firewood. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.7.2:] The purpose of the narrative beginning with 'Both indeed' has been stated. That statement of <s>Prajāpati</s> — both the gods and demons, the gods and the demons, heard — having received it in succession through tradition, having brought it within the range of their own ears, they comprehended it. And having understood that statement of <s>Prajāpati</s>, what did they do? It is said — they said to one another — the gods within their own assembly and the demons [within theirs]: 'Come, if it meets with your approval — let us seek that <s>Ātman</s> spoken of by <s>Prajāpati</s>, let us undertake the search, by seeking which <s>Ātman</s> one obtains all worlds and all desires.' Having thus spoken, <s>Indra</s> indeed — the king himself — went forth from among the gods, leaving behind the other gods and all the paraphernalia of enjoyment, with his body alone, toward <s>Prajāpati</s>. Likewise, <s>Virocana</s> from among the demons.

children.text: START ChUp 8,7.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.7.3]

children.text:
tau ha dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi brahmacaryam ūṣatuḥ |
tau ha prajāpatir uvāca |
kim icchantāv avāstam iti |
tau hocatur ya ātmā apahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ |
sa sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānātīti bhagavato vaco vedayante |
tam icchantāv avāstam iti || ChUp_8,7.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Those two lived as <s>brahmacārins</s> for thirty-two years. <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them: "Desiring what have you lived here?" They replied: "The Self that is free from evil, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, whose desires are true, whose resolves are true — that is to be sought, that is to be known. He who finds and knows that Self attains all worlds and all desires" — these are the words of the Blessed One that are reported. Desiring that, we have lived here.' (ChUp 8.7.3)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,7.3 tau ha gatvā dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi śuśrūṣāparau bhūtvā brahmacaryamūṣaturuṣitavantau /
abhiprāyajñaḥ prajāpatistāvuvāca kimicchantau kiṃ prayojanamabhipretyecchantāvavāstamuṣitavantau yuvāmitītyuktau tau hocatuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, knowing their intention, said to them: 'Desiring what — with what purpose in mind — have you two lived here?' Being asked thus, they replied:

children.text: ya ātmetyādi bhagavato vaco vedayante śiṣṭā atastamātmānaṃ jñātumicchantāvavāstamiti /
children.translated_text: 'The Self' and so on — 'these are the words of the Blessed One that the learned report. Therefore, desiring to know that Self, we have lived here.'

children.text: yadyapi prākprajāpateḥ samīpāgamanādanyonyamīrṣyāyuktāvabūtāṃ tathāpi vidyāprāptiprayojanagauravāttyaktarāgadveṣamoherṣyādi doṣāveva bhūtvoṣaturbrahmacaryaṃ prajāpatau /
children.translated_text: Although before coming near <s>Prajāpati</s> they had been filled with mutual jealousy, yet, due to the gravity of the purpose of attaining knowledge, they had abandoned the faults of desire, hatred, delusion, jealousy, and the like, and lived as <s>brahmacārins</s> under <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tenedaṃ prakhyāpitamātmavidyāgauravam //3 //
children.translated_text: By this, the greatness of the knowledge of the Self is proclaimed. (3)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.7.3:] Those two, having gone [to <s>Prajāpati</s>], devoted to service, lived as <s>brahmacārins</s> for thirty-two years.

children.text: START ChUp 8,7.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.7.4]

children.text:
tau ha prajāpatir uvāca ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛṣyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca |
etad amṛtam abhayam etad brahmeti |
atha yo 'yaṃ bhagavo 'psu parikhyāyate yaś cāyam ādarśe katama eṣa iti |
eṣa u evaiṣu sarveṣvannteṣu parikhyāyata iti hovāca || ChUp_8,7.4 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Prajāpati</s> said to them: "The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is seen in the eye — this is the Self," he said. "This is the immortal, the fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>." "But, Blessed One, who is this one that is perceived in water, and this one in a mirror — which one of these is it?" "This very same one is perceived in all these reflective surfaces," he said.' (ChUp 8.7.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,7.4 tāvevaṃ tapasvinau śuddhakalmaṣau yogyāvupalabhya prajāpatiruvācaha-ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo nivṛttacakṣurbhirmṛditakaṣāyairdṛśyate yogibhirdraṣṭā, eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmādiguṇo yamavocaṃ purāhaṃ yadvijñānātsarvalokakāmāvāptiretadamṛtaṃ bhamākhyamata evābhayamata eva brahma vṛddhatamamiti /
athaitatprajāpatinoktamakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata iti vacaḥ śrutvā chāyārūpaṃ puruṣaṃ jagṛhatuḥ /
gṛhītvā ca dṛḍhīkaraṇāya prajāpatiṃ pṛṣṭavantau /
atha yo 'yaṃ he bhagavo 'psu parikhyāyate parisamantājjñāyate yaścāyamādarśa ātmanaḥ pratibimbākāraḥ parikhyāyate khaḍgādau ca katama eṣa eṣāṃ bhagavadbhiruktaḥ kiṃvaika eva sarveṣviti /
evaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ prajāpatiruvāca-eṣa u eva yaścakṣuṣi draṣṭā mayokta iti /
etanmanasi kṛtvaiṣu sarveṣvanteṣu madhyeṣu parikhyāyata iti hovāca /
nanu kathaṃ yuktaṃ śiṣyorviparītagrahaṇamanujñātuṃ prajāpatervigatadoṣasyā'cāryasya sataḥ /
satyameva, nānujñātam /
katham /
ātmanyadhyāropitapāṇḍityamahattvaboddhṛtvau hīndravirocanau tathaiva ca prathitau loke /
tau yadi prajāpatinā mūḍhau yuvāṃ viparītagrāhiṇāvityuktau syātāṃ tatastastayościtte duḥkhaṃ syāttajjanitācca cittāvasādātpunaḥ praśnaśravaṇagrahaṇāvadhāraṇaṃ pratyutsāhavidhātaḥ syādato rakṣaṇīyau śiṣyāviti manyate prajāpatiḥ /
gṛhṇītāṃ tāvattadudaśarāvadṛṣṭāntenāpaneṣyāmīti ca /
nanu na yuktameṣa u evetyanṛtaṃ vaktum /
na cānṛtamuktam /
katham /
children.translated_text: How so?

children.text: ātmanokto 'kṣipuruṣo manasi saṃnihitataraḥ śiṣyagṛhītācchāyātmanaḥ sarveṣāṃ cābhyantaraḥ"sarvāntaraḥ"iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: The Self spoken of — the <s>puruṣa</s> in the eye — is more intimately present in the mind than the shadow-self grasped by the students, and is interior to all — as the <s>śruti</s> states: 'the innermost of all.'

children.text: tamevāvocadeṣa u evetyato nānṛtamuktaṃ prajāpatinā /
children.translated_text: It was that very one he referred to [saying] 'This very same one' — therefore no untruth was spoken by <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tathā ca tayorviparītagrahaṇanivṛttyarthaṃ hyāha //4//
children.translated_text: And accordingly, he will speak further for the purpose of removing their wrong understanding. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.7.4:] Having observed those two — ascetics who had purified their impurities — and deeming them fit, <s>Prajāpati</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is seen in the eye — seen by yogins who have withdrawn their eyes [from external objects] and whose afflictions have been subdued — the seer — this is the Self, possessing the attributes "free from evil" and so on, which I spoke of before — by whose knowledge one attains all worlds and desires. This is the immortal, called <s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite), and therefore fearless, therefore <s>Brahman</s> — the greatest.' Now, having heard this statement of <s>Prajāpati</s> — 'the <s>puruṣa</s> is seen in the eye' — they grasped the shadow-form, the reflection-person. And having grasped it, to confirm [their understanding], they asked <s>Prajāpati</s>: 'But, Blessed One, who is this one that is perceived — fully seen — in water, and this one that is perceived in a mirror as one's own reflection-image, and in a sword and the like — which of these is it, Blessed One? Is it the one you mentioned, or is it one and the same in all of them?' Being asked thus, <s>Prajāpati</s> said: 'This very same one — the seer in the eye, as I stated — is perceived in all these intermediate [reflective surfaces].' Having this in mind, 'it is perceived in all these intermediate [surfaces],' he said. Objection: How is it proper for <s>Prajāpati</s>, a teacher free from defects, to approve the wrong understanding of his students? True, he did not approve it. How so? <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s>, having superimposed learning and greatness and the capacity to understand upon themselves, were known as such in the world. If <s>Prajāpati</s> had told them 'You two are misunderstanding,' that would have caused pain in their minds, and from the mental dejection born of that, there would have been a loss of enthusiasm for further questioning, listening, and retention — therefore <s>Prajāpati</s> thought 'The students must be protected.' 'Let them grasp [what they will] — I shall remove [the misunderstanding] through the illustration of the water-basin.' Objection: It is not proper to speak the untruth 'This very same one.' But no untruth was spoken.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,8.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.8.1]

children.text:
udaśarāva ātmānam avekṣya yad ātmano na vijānīthas tan me prabrūtam iti |
tau hodaśarāve 'vekṣāṃ cakrāte |
tau ha prajāpatir uvāca kiṃ paśyatha iti |
tau hocatuḥ sarvam evedam āvāṃ bhagava ātmānaṃ paśyāva ā lomabhyaḥ ā nakhebhyaḥ pratirūpam iti || ChUp_8,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: '"Look at yourselves in a water-basin, and whatever you do not understand about the Self, tell me." They looked into a water-basin. <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them: "What do you see?" They said: "We see this entire self, Blessed One — a perfect likeness, down to the very hairs and fingernails."' (ChUp 8.8.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,8.1 udaśarāva udakapūrṇe śarāvādāvātmānamavekṣyānantaraṃ yattatrā'tmānaṃ paśyantau na vijānīthastanme mama prabrūtamācakṣīyāthāmityuktau tau ha tathaivodaśarāve 'vekṣāñcakrāte 'vekṣaṇaṃ cakratuḥ /
tathā kṛtavantau tau ha prajāpatiruvāca kiṃ paśyatha iti /
nanu tanme prabrūtamityuktābhyāmudaśarāve 'vekṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā prajāpataye na niveditamidamāvābhyāṃ na viditamityanivedite cājñānahetau ha prajāpatiruvāca kiṃ paśyatha iti tatra ko 'bhiprāya iti /
ucyate-naiva tayoridamāvayoraviditamityāśaṅkābhūcchāyātmanyātmapratyayo niścita evā'sīt /
yena vakṣyati tau ha śāntahṛdayau pravavrajaturiti /
na hyaniścite 'bhipretārthe praśāntahṛdayatvamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: For pacification of heart is not possible when the intended meaning is not firmly grasped.

children.text: tena nocaturidamāvābhyāmaviditamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore they did not say 'We did not understand this.'

children.text: viparītagrāhiṇau ca śiṣyāvanupekṣaṇīyāviti svayameṣa papraccha kiṃ paśyatha iti, viparītaniścayāpanayāya ca vakṣyati sādhvalakṛtāvityevamādi /
children.translated_text: And since the students were misunderstanding, and could not be neglected, he himself asked 'What do you see?' — and in order to remove their wrong conviction, he will speak further [saying] 'Well adorned' and so on.

children.text: tau hocatuḥ-sarvamevedamāvāṃ bhagava ātmānaṃ paśyāva ā lomabhya ā nakhebhyaḥ pratirūpamiti, yathaivā'vāṃ he bhagavo lomanakhādimantau sva evamevedaṃ lomanakhādisahitamāvayoḥ pratirūpamudaśarāve paśyāva iti //1 //
children.translated_text: They said: 'We see this entire self, Blessed One — we see our own self down to the hairs and fingernails, a perfect likeness.' 'Just as we ourselves, Blessed One, are endowed with hair and nails, so too this image with hair, nails, and all — we see it as our likeness in the water-basin.' (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.8.1:] 'Look at yourselves in a water-basin — in a bowl filled with water — and immediately afterward, whatever you see of the self there but do not understand, tell me — declare it to me.' Being told thus, those two looked into a water-basin — they made an observation. Having done so, <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them: 'What do you see?' But [one may ask]: having been told 'tell me,' after looking in the water-basin, they did not report to <s>Prajāpati</s> 'We did not understand this' — and even though they did not report the cause of their ignorance, <s>Prajāpati</s> said 'What do you see?' — what is the intent here? The answer is: no doubt arose in them that 'We did not understand' — their conviction in the shadow-self as the true Self was firm. This is why [the text] will say: 'Those two departed with pacified hearts.'

children.text: START ChUp 8,8.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.8.2]

children.text:
tau ha prajāpatir uvāca sādhvalaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtau bhūtvodaśarāve 'vekṣethām iti |
tau ha sādhvalaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtau bhūtvodaśarāve 'vekṣāṃ cakrāte |
tau ha prajāpatir uvāca kiṃ paśyatha iti || ChUp_8,8.2 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Prajāpati</s> said to them: "Adorn yourselves well, dress well, groom yourselves, and then look into the water-basin." They adorned themselves well, dressed well, groomed themselves, and looked into the water-basin. <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them: "What do you see?"' (ChUp 8.8.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,8.2 tau ha punaḥ prajāpatiruvāca cchāyātmaniścayāpanayāya, sādhvalaṅkṛtau yathā svagṛhe suvasanau mahārhavastraparidhānau pariṣkṛtau chinnalomanakhau ca bhūtvodaśarāve tayośchāyātmagraho 'panītaḥ syāt /
sādhvalaṅkārasuvasanādīnāmāgantukānāṃ chāyākaratvamudaśarāve yathā śarīrasaṃbaddhānāmevaṃ śarīrasyāpi cchāyākaratvaṃ pūrvaṃ babhūveti gamyate /
śarīraikadeśānāṃ ca lomanakhādīnāṃ nityatvenābhipretānāmakhaṇḍitānāṃ chāyākaratvaṃ pūrvamāsīt /

chinneṣu ca teṣu naiva lomanakhādicchāyā dṛśyate 'to lomanakhādivaccharīrasyāpyāgamāpāyitvaṃ siddhamityudaśarāvādau dṛśyamānasya tannimittasya ca dehasyānātmatvaṃ siddham udaśārāvādau chāyākaratvāddehasaṃbaddhālaṅkārādivat /
children.translated_text: and when cut, their shadows are no longer seen in the water — therefore, just as the body too, like hair and nails, is subject to coming and going, so its non-self-hood is established, since what is seen in the water-basin and the body that causes it [the reflection] — [both are non-self], because, like the ornaments connected with the body, they produce shadows in the water-basin.

children.text: na kevalametāvadetena yāvatkiñcidātmīyatvābhimataṃ sukhaduḥkharāgadveṣamohādi ca kādācitkatvānnakhalomādivadanātmeti pratyetavyam /
children.translated_text: Not only this much — whatever is considered to be one's own — happiness, sorrow, desire, hatred, delusion, and the like — because of their occasional nature, like nails, hair, and the like — should be understood as non-self.

children.text: evamaśeṣamithyāgrahāpanayanimitte sādhvalaṅkārādidṛṣṭānte prajāpatinokte śrutvā tathā kṛtavatorapi cchāyātmaviparītagraho nāpajagāma yasmāttasmātsvadoṣeṇaiva kenacitpratibaddhavivekavijñānāvindravirocanāvabhūtāmit i gamyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, even though <s>Prajāpati</s> presented the illustration of well-adorning and the like — an occasion for removing every false conception — and even though [<s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s>] heard it and acted accordingly, the wrong understanding of the shadow as the self did not depart. Therefore, it is understood that <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s> had their discriminative knowledge obstructed by some fault of their own.

children.text: tau pūrvavadeva dṛḍhaniścayau papraccha kiṃ paśyatha iti //2 //
children.translated_text: He asked them, with their conviction as firm as before: 'What do you see?' (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.8.2:] <s>Prajāpati</s> again said to them — in order to remove the conviction in the shadow-self: 'Adorn yourselves well, as at your own homes — dress in fine, costly garments — groom yourselves, trimming your hair and nails — and then look into the water-basin,' [thinking] that their grasping of the shadow-self might be removed. Just as ornaments, fine clothes, and the like, being adventitious, produce shadows in the water-basin — just as things connected with the body [produce shadows] — so too the body itself is understood to be a producer of shadow, as it was before. And just as the nails, hairs, and other parts of the body, previously considered permanent, produced shadows when uncut,

children.text: START ChUp 8,8.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.8.3]

children.text:
tau hocatur yathaivedam āvāṃ bhagavaḥ sādhvalaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtau sva evam evemau bhagavaḥ sādhvallaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtāv iti |
eṣa ātmeti hovāca |
etad amṛtam abhayam etad brahmeti |
tau ha śāntahṛdayau pravavrajatuḥ || ChUp_8,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'They said: "Just as we ourselves are, Blessed One — well adorned, well dressed, well groomed — so too are these, Blessed One — well adorned, well dressed, well groomed." "This is the Self," he said. "This is the immortal, the fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>." Those two departed with pacified hearts.' (ChUp 8.8.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,8.3 tau tathaiva pratipanno yathaivedamiti pūrvavadyathā sādhvalaṅkārādiviśiṣṭāvāvāṃ sva evamevemau chāyātmānāviti sutarāṃ viparītaniścayau babhūvatuḥ /
yasyā'tmano lakṣaṇaṃ ya ātmāpahatapāpmetyuktavā punastadviśeṣamanviṣyamāṇayorya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata iti sākṣādātmani nirdiṣṭe tadviparītagrahāpanayāyodaśarāvasādhvalaṅkāradṛṣṭānte 'pyabhihita ātmasvarūpabodhādviparītagraho nāpagataḥ /
ataḥ svadoṣeṇa kenacitpratibaddhavivekavijñānasāmarthyāviti matvā yathābhipretamevā'tmānaṃ manasi nidhāyaiṣa ātmeti hovācaitadamṛtamabhayametadbrahmeti prajāpatiḥ pūrvavat /
na tu tadabhipretamātmānam /
ya ātmetyādyātmalakṣaṇaśravaṇenākṣipuruṣaśrutyā codaśarāvādyupapattyā ca saṃskṛtau tāvat /
children.translated_text: They had been prepared so far by hearing the characteristics of the Self [beginning with] 'The Self that [is free from evil],' by the statement about the <s>puruṣa</s> in the eye, and by the reasoning through the water-basin and the like.

children.text: madvacanaṃ sarvaṃ punaḥ punaḥ smaratoḥ pratibandhakṣayācca svayamevā'tmaviṣaye viveko bhaviṣyatīti manvānaḥ punarbrahmacaryādeśe ca tayościttadukhotpattiṃ parijihīrṣankṛtārthabuddhitayā gacchantāvapyupekṣitavānprajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thinking 'As they repeatedly remember all my words, the discriminative knowledge regarding the Self will arise of its own accord through the decay of the obstruction' — and wishing to spare them the pain that would arise in their minds upon being instructed to practice <s>brahmacarya</s> again — <s>Prajāpati</s> overlooked even their departure, thinking they were satisfied, as if they had accomplished their purpose.

children.text: tau hendravirocanau śāntahṛdayau tuṣṭahṛdayau kṛtārthabuddhī ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those two — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s> — departed 'with pacified hearts' — meaning with satisfied hearts, thinking they had accomplished their purpose.

children.text: na tu śama eva, śamaścettayorjāto viparītagraho vigato 'bhaviṣyatpravavrajaturgatavantau //3 //
children.translated_text: But it was not true tranquility — for if tranquility had arisen in them, the wrong understanding would have departed. They departed — they went away. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.8.3:] Those two understood in the same way — 'just as we are,' as before — 'just as we are distinguished by good adornment and the rest, so too are these shadow-selves' — they became even more firmly entrenched in their wrong conviction. When [<s>Prajāpati</s>] had stated the characteristics of the Self — 'the Self that is free from evil' — and when they were seeking its specific nature, the Self was directly indicated as 'the <s>puruṣa</s> who is seen in the eye,' and even though the illustration of the water-basin and good adornment was given to remove the wrong understanding — the wrong understanding of the Self's true nature did not depart. Therefore, having concluded that their capacity for discriminative knowledge was obstructed by some fault of their own, keeping in mind the Self as he intended it, <s>Prajāpati</s> said as before: 'This is the Self. This is the immortal, the fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>.' But not the Self they intended.

children.text: START ChUp 8,8.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.8.4]

children.text:
tau hānvīkṣya prajāpatir uvāca |
anupalabhyātmānam ananuvidya vrajato yatara etadupaniṣado bhaviṣyanti devā vā asurā vā te parābhaviṣyantīti |
sa ha śāntahṛdaya eva virocano 'surāñ jagāma |
tebhyo haitām upaniṣadaṃ provāca ātmaiveha mahayya ātmā paricaryaḥ |
ātmānam eveha mahayann ātmānaṃ paricarann ubhau lokāv āpnotīmaṃ cāmuṃ ceti || ChUp_8,8.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Looking at them, <s>Prajāpati</s> said: "They are departing without having found the Self, without having discovered it. Whichever of them — whether gods or <s>asuras</s> — will adopt this as their teaching, they shall be defeated." <s>Virocana</s>, with his heart at peace, went to the <s>asuras</s>. He taught them this teaching: "The bodily self alone is to be glorified here, the bodily self alone is to be served. He who glorifies the bodily self here and serves the bodily self — he attains both worlds, this one and the next."' (ChUp 8.8.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,8.4 evaṃ tayorgatayorindravirocanayo rājñorbhogāsaktayoryathoktavismaraṇaṃ syādityāśaṅkyāpratyakṣaṃ pratyakṣavacanena ca cittaduḥkhaṃ parijihīrṣustau dūraṃ gacchantāvanvīkṣya ya ātmāpahatapāpmetyādivacanavadetadapyanayoḥ śravaṇagocaratvameṣyatīti matvovāca prajāpatiḥ /
anupalabhya yathoktalakṣaṇamātmānamananuvidya svātmapratyakṣaṃ cākṛtvā viparītaniścayau ca bhūtvendravirocanāvetau vrajato gaccheyātām /
ato yatare devā vāsurā vā kiṃ viśeṣitenaitadupaniṣada ābhyāṃ yā gṛhītā'tmavidyā seyamupaniṣadyeṣāṃ devānāmasurāṇāṃ vā ta etadupaniṣada evaṃvijñānā etanniścayā bhaviṣyantītyarthaḥ /
te kiṃ, parābhaviṣyanti śreyomārgātparābhūtā bahirbhūtā vinaṣṭā bhaviṣyantītyarthaḥ /
svagṛhaṃ gacchatoḥ surāsurarājayoryo 'surarājaḥ sa ha śāntahṛdaya eva sanvirocano 'surāñjagāma /
gatvā ca tebhyo 'surebhyaḥ śarīrātmabuddhiryopaniṣattāmetāmupaniṣadaṃ provācoktavān /
children.translated_text: And having gone, he taught this teaching — the doctrine that the body is the Self — to those demons.

children.text: dehamātramevā'tmā pitrokta iti /
children.translated_text: 'The body alone is the Self, as declared by the Father' — thus.

children.text: tasmādātmaiva deha iha loka mahayyaḥ pūjanīyastathā paricaryaḥ paricaraṇīyastathā'tmānameveha loke dehaṃ mahayanparicaraṃścobhau lokāvavāpnotīmaṃ cāmuṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore the Self is the body; it is to be honored in this world, to be served; and one who honors the body here in this world and serves it obtains both worlds — this world and the next.'

children.text: ihalokaparalokayoreva sarve lokāḥ kāmāścāntarbhavantīti rājño 'bhiprāyaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: The king's view was that all worlds and desires are included within this world and the next world alone. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.8.4:] Thus, suspecting that these two — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s>, kings attached to enjoyments — who had gone [away] might forget what was taught, and wishing to remove the mental suffering [caused by the apparent contradiction] between the imperceptible [Self] and the statement [about it] as if perceptible, <s>Prajāpati</s> looked after them as they went far away and said — thinking 'The statement beginning with "The Self that is free from evil" will also come within the range of their hearing' — [he spoke]. Without having found the Self of the described characteristics, without having discovered it, and without having made the Self directly perceptible, these two — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s> — having arrived at contrary conclusions, depart. Therefore, whichever of the gods or demons take up this teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) — this self-knowledge that was grasped by these two — those among the gods or demons who hold this teaching will become of that same understanding — that is the meaning. What [will happen to] them? They will be defeated — turned away from the path of the good, excluded, destroyed — that is the meaning. Of the two kings of gods and demons going to their respective homes, the demon king <s>Virocana</s>, with a tranquil heart, went to the demons.

children.text: START ChUp 8,8.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.8.5]

children.text:
tasmād apyaddyehādadānam aśraddadhānam ayajamānam āhur āsuro bateti |
asurāṇāṃ hy eṣopaniṣat |
pretasya śarīraṃ bhikṣayā vasanenālaṃkāreṇeti saṃskurvanti |
etena hy ammuṃ lokaṃ jeṣyanto manyante || ChUp_8,8.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, even today, one who does not give, who has no faith, who does not sacrifice — they call him "demonic indeed." For this is the teaching of the demons. They adorn the body of the dead with food-offerings, garments, and ornaments, for they think they will conquer the other world by this.' (ChUp 8.8.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,8.5 tasmāttatsaṃpradāyo 'dyāpyanuvartata itīha loke 'dadānaṃ dānamakurvāṇamavibhāgaśīlamaśraddadhānaṃ satkāryeṣu śraddhārahitaṃ yathāśaktyayajamānamayajanasvabhāvamāhurāsuraḥ khalvayaṃ yata evaṃsvabhāvo bateti khidyamānā āhuḥ śiṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.8.5:] Therefore, that tradition continues even today. Hence, in this world, one who does not give — who does not make gifts, who is of an undiscriminating disposition — who has no faith — devoid of faith in meritorious works — who does not sacrifice — whose nature is not to perform sacrifice to the extent of one's ability — the learned say 'This one is demonic indeed,' distressed [by such behavior].

children.text: asurāṇāṃ hi yasmādaśraddadhānatādilakṣaṇaiṣopaniṣat /
children.translated_text: Because this is the teaching of the demons, characterized by faithlessness and the like.

children.text: tayopaniṣadā saṃskṛtāḥ santaḥ pretasya śarīraṃ kuṇapaṃ bhikṣayā gandhamālyānnādilakṣaṇayā vasanena vasrādinā'cchādanādiprakāreṇālaṅkāreṇa dhvajapatākādikaraṇenetyevaṃ saṃskurvantyetena kuṇapasaṃskāreṇāmuṃ pretya pratipattavyaṃ lokaṃ jeṣyanto manyante //5//
children.translated_text: Adorned by that teaching, they decorate the body of the dead — the corpse — with food-offerings such as fragrance, garlands, and food; with garments and ornaments — thinking 'By this [external adornment] we shall conquer the next world' — because they hold the body to be the Self.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasyāṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,9.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.9.1]

children.text:
atha hendro 'prāpyaiva devān etad bhayaṃ dadarśa |
yathaiva khalv ayam asmiñ charīre sādhvalaṃkṛte sādhvalaṃkṛto bhavati suvasane suvasanaḥ pariṣkṛte pariṣkṛta evam evāyam asminn andhe 'ndho bhavati srāme srāmaḥ parivṛkṇe parivṛkṇaḥ |
asyaiva śarīrasya nāśam anv eṣa naśyati |
nāham atra bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti || ChUp_8,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'But <s>Indra</s>, even before reaching the gods, saw this danger: "Just as indeed this [reflection in the body] is well-adorned when this body is well-adorned, well-dressed when it is well-dressed — so also it is blind when it is blind, lame when it is lame, crippled when it is crippled. It perishes along with the perishing of this [body]. I see no good in this."' (ChUp 8.9.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,9.1 atha ha kilendro 'prāpyaiva devāndaivyākrauryādisaṃpadā yuktatvādgurorvacanaṃ punaḥ punaḥ smaranneva gacchannetadvakṣyamāṇaṃ bhayaṃ svātmagrahaṇanimittaṃ dadarśa dṛṣṭavān /
udaśarāvadṛṣṭāntena prajāpatinā yadartho nyāya uktastadekadeśo maghavataḥ pratyabhādbuddhau /
yena cchāyātmagrahaṇe doṣaṃ dadarśa /
katham /
yathaiva khalvayamasmiñcharīre sādhvalaṅkṛte chāyātmāpi sādhvalaṅkṛto bhavati suvasane ca suvasanaḥ pariṣkṛte pariṣkṛto yathā nakhalomādidehāvayavāpagame chāyātmāpi pariṣkṛto bhavati nakhalomādirahito bhavati /
evamevāyaṃ chāyātmāpyasmiñcharīre nakhalomādibhirdehāvayavatvasya tulyatvādandhe cakṣuṣo 'pagame 'ndho bavati srāme srāmaḥ /
srāmaḥ kilekanetrastasyāndhatvena gatatvāt /
cakṣurnāsikā vā yasya sadā sravati sa srāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Srāma</s> is one whose eyes or nose always drip.

children.text: parivṛkṇaśchinnahastaśchinnapādo vā /
children.translated_text: <s>Parivṛkṇa</s> is one with severed hands or feet.

children.text: srāme parivṛkṇe vā dehe chāyātmāpi tathā bhavati /
children.translated_text: When the body is <s>srāma</s> or <s>parivṛkṇa</s>, the reflection-self also becomes so.

children.text: tathāsya dehasya nāśamanveṣa naśyati //1 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, following the destruction of this body, that [reflection] also perishes. (1)
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.9.1:] But <s>Indra</s>, even before reaching the gods — being endowed with divine qualities such as fearlessness and the like, being a worthy recipient —

children.text: START ChUp 8,9.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.9.2]

children.text:
sa samitpāṇiḥ punar eyāya |
taṃ ha prajāpatir uvāca |
maghavan yac chāntahṛdayaḥ prāvrājīḥ sārdhaṃ virocanena kim icchan punar āgama iti |
sa hovāca yathā eva khalvayyaṃ bhagavo 'smiñ charīre sādhvalaṃkṛte sādhvalaṃkṛto bhavati suvasane suvasanaḥ pariṣkṛte pariṣkṛta evam evāyam asminn andhe 'ndho bhavati srāme srāmaḥ parivṛkṇe parivṛkṇaḥ |
asyaiva śarīrasya nāśam anv eṣa naśyati |
nāham atra bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti || ChUp_8,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'He returned again with fuel in hand. <s>Prajāpati</s> said to him: "<s>Maghavan</s>, since you went away with a tranquil heart [like <s>Virocana</s>], with what desire do you come back?"' (ChUp 8.9.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,9.2 ato nāhamatrāsmiṃśchāyātmadarśane dehātmadarśane vā bhogyaṃ phalaṃ paśyāmītyevaṃ doṣaṃ dehacchāyātmadarśane 'dhyavasya sa samitpāṇirbrahmacaryaṃ vastuṃ punareyāya /
taṃ ha prajāpatiruvāca-maghavanyacchāntahṛdayaḥ prāvrājīḥ pragatavānasi virocanena sārdhaṃ kimicchanpunarāgama iti /
vijānannapi punaḥ papracchendrābhiprayābhivyaktaye yadvettha tena mopasīdeti yadvat /
tathā ca svābhiprayāṃ prakaṭamakarodyathaiva khalvayamityadi, evameveti cānvamodata prajāpatiḥ /
nanu tulye 'kṣipuruṣaśravame dehacchāyāmindro 'grahīdātmeti dehameva va virocanastatkiṃnimittam /
tatra manyate /
yathendrasyodaśarāvādiprajāpativacanaṃ smarato devānaprāptasyaivā'cāryoktabuddhyā chāyātmagrahaṇaṃ tatra doṣadarśanaṃ cābhūt /
na tathā virocanasya kiṃ tarhi deha evā'tmadarśanaṃ nāpi tatra doṣadarśanaṃ babhūva /
tadvadeva vidyāgrahaṇasāmarthyapratibandhadoṣālpatvabahutvāpekṣamindravirocanayośchāyātmadehayorgrahaṇam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.9.2:] Therefore — 'I do not see in this' — in this doctrine of the reflection-self or the body-self — a fruit worth enjoying.

children.text: indro 'lpadoṣatvāddṛśyata itiśrutyarthameva śraddadhānatayā jagrāhetaraśchāyānimittaṃ dehaṃ hitvā śrutyarthaṃ lakṣaṇayā jagrāha prajāpatinokto 'yamiti doṣabhūyastvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, because of his lesser faults, is seen [to have been receptive] — he grasped the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> with faith, while the other [<s>Virocana</s>] grasped the reflection-doctrine [erroneously].

children.text: yathā kila nīlānīlayorādarśe dṛśyamānayorvāsasoryannīlaṃ tanmahārhamiti cchāyānimittaṃ vāsa evocyate na cchāyā tadvaditi virocanābhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as when blue and non-blue garments are seen in a mirror, one determines 'the blue one is valuable' — so too with the reflection. [The difference in understanding is due to] the qualities and faults of one's own mind.

children.text: svacittaguṇadoṣavaśādeva hi śabdārthāvadhāraṇaṃ tulye 'pi śravaṇe khyāpitaṃ dāmyata datta dayadhvamiti dakāramātraśravaṇācchutyantare /
children.translated_text: For the ascertainment of the meaning of words — even with equal hearing — depends on the qualities and faults of one's own mind, as is well-known [from the example of] <s>Dāmya</s> and others.

children.text: nimittānyapi tadanuguṇānyeva sahakārīṇi bhavanti //2 //
children.translated_text: And the auxiliary causes [for right understanding] are also in accordance with that [mental disposition]. (2)

children.text: START ChUp 8,9.3

evam evaiṣa maghavann iti hovāca |
etaṃ tv eva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi |
vasāparāṇi dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇīti |
sa hāparāṇi dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇyuvāsa |
tasmai hovāca || ChUp_8,9.3 ||
children.translated_text: '"Even so, O <s>Maghavan</s>," he said. "But I shall explain this further to you. Live [here] another thirty-two years."' (ChUp 8.9.3)
[Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.9.3]

children.text: ChUpBh_8,9.3 evamevaiṣa maghavansamyaktvayāvagataṃ na cchāyātmetyuvāca prajāpatiryo mayokta ātmā prakṛta etamevā'tmānaṃ tu te bhūyaḥ pūrvaṃ vyākhyātamapyanuvyākhyāsyāmi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.9.3:] 'Even so, O <s>Maghavan</s>' — 'You have understood correctly that it is not the reflection-self,' <s>Prajāpati</s> said.

children.text: yasmātsakṛdvyākhyātaṃ doṣarahitānāmavadhāraṇaviṣayaṃ prāptamapi nāgrahīrataḥ kenaciddoṣeṇa pratibaddhagrahaṇasāmarthastvamatastatkṣapaṇāya vasāparāṇi dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇītyuktvā tathoṣitavate kṣapitadoṣāya tasmai hovāca //3//
children.translated_text: Since what was explained once — though it had become an object of apprehension for those free from faults — was not grasped [properly], therefore, by what further means [shall I teach]?

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,10.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.10.1]

children.text:
ya eṣa svapne mahīyamānaś caraty eṣa ātmeti hovāca |
etad amṛtam abhayam etad brahmeti |
sa ha śāntahṛdayaḥ pravavrāja |
sa hāprāpyaiva devān etad bhayaṃ dadarśa |
tad yady apīdaṃ śarīram andhaṃ bhavaty anandhaḥ sa bhavati yadi srāmam asrāmaḥ |
naivaiṣo 'sya doṣeṇa duṣyati || ChUp_8,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: '"He who moves about glorified in dreams — this is the Self," he said. "This is immortal, fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>."' (ChUp 8.10.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,10.1 ya ātmāpahatapāpmādilakṣaṇo ya eṣo 'kṣiṇītyādinā vyākhyāta eṣa saḥ /
ko 'sau /
yaḥ svapne mahīyamānaḥ stryādibhiḥ pūjyamānaścaratyanekavidhānsvapnabhogānanubhavatītyarthaḥ /
eṣa ātmeti hovācetyādi samānam /
sa haivamukta indraḥ śāntahṛdayaḥ pravavrāja /
sa hāprāpyaiva devānpūrvavadasminnapyātmani bhayaṃ dadarśa /
children.translated_text: He [<s>Indra</s>], even before reaching the gods, as before, saw danger in this self [the dream-self] too.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How?

children.text: tadidaṃ śarīraṃ yadyapyandhaṃ dhavati svapnātmā yo 'nandhaḥ sa bhavati /
children.translated_text: Even if this body is blind, the dream-self that is not blind — he becomes [free of that defect].

children.text: yadi srāmamidaṃ śarīramasrāmaśca sa bhavati naivaiṣa svapnātmāsya dehasya doṣeṇa duṣyati //1 //
children.translated_text: Even if this body is <s>srāma</s> (afflicted), and he [in dream] is not <s>srāma</s> — [yet] this dream-self is not [truly free from] the faults of this body.
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.10.1:] The Self characterized as free from evil and the rest, explained as 'He who is in the eye' and so forth — this is he.

children.text: START ChUp 8,10.2-4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.10.2-4]

children.text:
na vadhenāsya hanyate |
nāsya srāmyeṇa srāmaḥ |
ghnanti tv evainam |
vicchādayantīva |
apriyavetteva bhavati |
api roditīva nāham atra bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti || ChUp_8,10.2 ||
children.translated_text: '"He is not slain by the slaying of this [body]. He does not become lame by its lameness. Yet they seem to strike him. They seem to chase him —"' (ChUp 8.10.2)

children.text:
sa samitpāṇiḥ punar eyāya |
taṃ ha prajāpatir uvāca |
maghavan yac chāntahṛdayaḥ prāvrājīḥ kim icchan punar āgama iti |
sa hovāca |
tad yady apīdaṃ bhagavaḥ śarīram andhaṃ bhavaty anandhaḥ sa bhavati yadi srāmam asrāmaḥ |
naivaiṣo 'sya doṣeṇa duṣyati || ChUp_8,10.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'He returned again with fuel in hand. <s>Prajāpati</s> said to him: "<s>Maghavan</s>, since you went away with a tranquil heart [before], with what desire do you come back?"' (ChUp 8.10.3)

children.text:
na vadhenāsya hanyate |
nāsya srāmyeṇa srāmaḥ |
ghnanti tv ivainam |
vicchādayantīva |
apriyavetteva bhavati |
api roditīva |
nāham atra bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti |
evam evaiṣa maghavann iti hovāca |
etaṃ tv eva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi |
vasāparāṇi dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇīti |
sa hāparāṇi dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇyuvāsa |
tasmai hovāca || ChUp_8,10.4 ||
children.translated_text: '"He is not slain by the slaying of this [body]. He does not become lame by its lameness. Yet they seem to strike him. They seem to chase him —"' (ChUp 8.10.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,10.2-3-4 nāpyasya vadhena sa hanyate chāyātmavanna cāsya srāmyeṇa srāmaḥ svapnātmā bhavati /
yadadhyāyādāvāgamamātreṇopanyastaṃ nāsya jarayaitajjīryatītyādi tadiha nyāyenopapādayitumupanyastam /
na tāvadayaṃ chāyātmavaddehadoṣayuktaḥ kintu dhnanti tvevainam /
evaśabda ivārthe /
ghnantīvainaṃ kecaneti draṣṭavyam /
prajāpatiṃ pramāṇīkurvato 'nṛtavāditvāpādanānupapatteḥ /
etadamṛtamityetatprajāpativacanaṃ kathaṃ mṛṣā kuryādindrastaṃ pramāṇīkurvan /
nanu cchāyāpuruṣe prajāpatinokte 'sya śarīrasya nāśamanveṣa naśyatīti doṣamabhyadhāttathehāpi syāt /
naivam /
kasmāt /
ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata iti manyate tadā kathaṃ prajāpatiṃ pramāṇīkṛtya punaḥ śravaṇāya samitpāṇirgacchet /
jagāma ca /
tasmānna cchāyātmā prajāpatinokta iti manyate /
tathā ca vyākhyātaṃ draṣṭākṣiṇi dṛśyata iti /
tathā vicchādayantīva vidrāvayantīva tathā ca putrādimaraṇanimittamapriyavetteva bhavati /
api ca svayamapi roditīva /
nanvapriyaṃ vettyeva kathaṃ vetteveti /
ucyate-na amṛtābhayatvavacanānupapatteḥ /
dhyāyatīveti ca śrutyantarāt /
nanu pratyakṣavirodha iti cet /
na /
śarīrātmatvapratyakṣavadbhrāntisaṃbhavāt /
tiṣṭhatu tāvadapriyavetteva na veti /
nāhamatra bhogyaṃ paśyāmi /
svapnātmajñāne 'pīṣṭaṃ phalaṃ nopalabha ityabhiprāyaḥ. evamevaiṣa tavābhiprāyeṇeti vākyaseṣaḥ /
ātmano 'mṛtābhayaguṇavattvasyābhipretatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the attribute of immortality and fearlessness of the Self is what is intended [by <s>Indra</s>].

children.text: dviruktamapi nyāyato mayā yathāvannāvadhārayati /
children.translated_text: Even though [<s>Prajāpati</s>] has stated it twice, [<s>Indra</s>] does not properly comprehend it according to reasoning.

children.text: tasmātpūrvavadasyādyāpi pratibandhakāraṇamastīti manvānastatkṣapaṇāya vasāparāṇi dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi brahmacaryamityādideśa prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, thinking — as before — that there is still an obstructing cause in him, <s>Prajāpati</s> prescribed, for the purpose of removing that, the dwelling of another thirty-two years of <s>brahmacarya</s> and the rest.

children.text: tathoṣitavate kṣapitakalmaṣāyā'ha //2-3-4 //
children.translated_text: To him who had so dwelt and whose impurities were removed, [<s>Prajāpati</s>] spoke. (2-3-4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.10.2-3-4:] Nor is he slain by the slaying of [the body] — like the shadow-self — nor does weariness affect him — it becomes the dream-self. What was introduced at the beginning of the chapter by mere statement [from scripture] — 'It does not decay with old age' and so on — is here presented to be established by reasoning. First, this one is not, like the shadow-self, affected by bodily defects; rather, they strike it — but the word 'eva' is used in the sense of 'iva' (as if). 'They strike as if' — this is how it should be understood. Because if one accepts <s>Prajāpati</s> as authoritative, the imputation of falsehood [to him] is impossible. How could <s>Indra</s>, accepting <s>Prajāpati</s> as authoritative, make this statement of <s>Prajāpati</s> — 'This is immortal' — false? [Objection:] But when <s>Prajāpati</s> spoke of the shadow-person, [<s>Indra</s>] pointed out the defect: 'With the destruction of this body, this one also perishes.' Would the same [objection] not apply here? [Reply:] Not so. Why? [Because <s>Indra</s>] thinks: 'The person that is seen in the eye' [is the Self]. If so, how would he go again with fuel in hand to hear more, accepting <s>Prajāpati</s> as authoritative? And he did go. Therefore, he does not think that <s>Prajāpati</s> spoke of the shadow-self. And thus it was explained: 'The seer is seen in the eye.' Similarly, they cover him as if, they drive him away as if; and due to the death of son and the like, he becomes as if a knower of the unpleasant. Moreover, he himself also weeps as if. [Objection:] But he does know the unpleasant — how can it be 'as if he knows'? [Reply:] [We say] no — because the statement of immortality and fearlessness would be impossible [otherwise]. And from another <s>śruti</s>: 'He meditates as if.' [Objection:] But this contradicts direct perception! [Reply:] No — because error is possible, just as in the perception of the body as the self. Let it stand for now whether or not he knows the unpleasant. 'I do not see any enjoyment here' — the intended meaning is: even in the knowledge of the dream-self, I do not perceive the desired fruit. 'Even so indeed, this [is]' — [and] 'in accordance with your intention' — this is the completion of the sentence.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya daśamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,11.1-2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.11.1-2]

children.text:
tad yatraitat suptaḥ samastaḥ saṃprasannaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānātyeṣa ātmeti hovāca |
etad amṛtam abhayam etad brahmeti |
sa ha śāntahṛdayaḥ pravavrāja |
sa hāprāpyaiva devān etad bhayaṃ dadarśa |
nāha khalv ayam evaṃ saṃpraty ātmānaṃ jānāty ayam aham asmīti |
no evemāni bhūtāni |
vināśam evāpīto bhavati |
nāham atra bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti || ChUp_8,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'That state where one, being asleep, completely at rest, serene, knows no dream — this is the <s>Ātman</s>,' he said. 'This is the immortal, the fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>.' He departed with a peaceful heart. But before even reaching the gods, he saw this danger: 'This Self does not know itself thus — "I am this." Nor does it know these beings. It has gone to destruction, as it were. I see no good in this.' (ChUp 8.11.1)

children.text:
sa samitpāṇiḥ punar eyāya |
taṃ ha prajāpatir uvāca - maghavan yac chāntahṛdayaḥ prāvrājīḥ kim icchan punar āgama iti |
sa hovāca nāha khalv ayaṃ bhagava evaṃ saṃpraty ātmānaṃ jānāty ayam aham asmīti |
no evemāni bhūtāni |
vināśam evāpīto bhavati |
nāham atra bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti || ChUp_8,11.2 ||
children.translated_text: He returned again with fuel in hand. <s>Prajāpati</s> said to him: '<s>Maghavan</s>, you departed with a peaceful heart — desiring what have you returned?' He said: 'This Self, Blessed One, does not know itself thus — "I am this." Nor does it know these beings. It has gone to destruction, as it were. I see no good in this.' (ChUp 8.11.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,11.1-2 pūrvavadetaṃ tveva ta ityādyuktvā tadyatraitatsupta ityadi vyākhyātaṃ vākyam /
akṣiṇi yo draṣṭā svapne ca mahīyamānaścarati sa eṣa suptaḥ samastaḥ saṃprasannaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānātyeṣa ātmeti hovācaitadamṛtamabhayametadbrahmeti svābhipretameva /
maghavāṃstatrāpi doṣaṃ dadarśa /
katham /
nāha naiva suṣuptastho 'pyātmā khalvayaṃ saṃprati samyagidānīṃ cā'tmānaṃ jānāti naivaṃ jānāti /
katham /
ayamahamasmīti no evemāni bhūtāni ceti /
yathā jāgrati svapne vā /
ato vināśameva vināśamiveti pūrvavaddraṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: How? "I am this" — nor these beings. Just as in waking or in dream.

children.text: apīto 'pigato bhavati, vinaṣṭa iva bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it has gone to destruction — 'gone to destruction as it were' — to be understood as before [with 'iva'].

children.text: jñāne hi sati jñātuḥ sadbhāvo 'vagamyate nāsati jñāne /
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is: it has gone away, it is as if destroyed.

children.text: na ca suṣuptasya jñānaṃ dṛśyate 'to vinaṣṭa ivetyabhiprāyaḥ na tu vināśamevā'tmano manyate 'mṛtābhayavacanasya prāmāṇyamicchan //1-2 //
children.translated_text: For when there is knowledge, the existence of the knower is ascertained — not when knowledge is absent. And knowledge is not seen in one who is in deep sleep — hence '[it is] as if destroyed' is the intended meaning. But [<s>Indra</s>] does not think that the Self actually undergoes destruction, since he accepts the authority of the statement about immortality and fearlessness. (1-2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.11.1-2:] As before, having said 'But this very one I shall explain to you' and so forth, [<s>Prajāpati</s> speaks] the passage that has been explained: 'That state where one, being asleep...' [etc.]. He who is the seer in the eye and who moves about glorified in dreams — this very one, being asleep, completely at rest, serene, knows no dream — 'this is the <s>Ātman</s>,' he said. 'This is the immortal, the fearless. This is <s>Brahman</s>' — exactly what was intended [by <s>Prajāpati</s>]. But <s>Maghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>) saw a defect even in that. How? 'This self in deep sleep does not at all — not properly — know itself now; it does not know thus —

children.text: START ChUp 8,11.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.11.3]

children.text:
evam evaiṣa maghavann iti hovāca |
etaṃ tv eva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi |
no evānyatraitasmāt |
vasāparāṇi pañca varṣāṇīti |
sa hāparāṇi pañca varṣāṇyuvāsa |
tāny ekaśataṃ saṃpeduḥ |
etat tad yad āhuḥ |
ekaśataṃ ha vai varṣāṇi maghavān prajāpatau brahmacaryam uvāsa |
tasmai hovāca || ChUp_8,11.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Even so indeed is this, <s>Maghavan</s>,' he said. 'But I shall explain this very [Self] to you further. [It is] nothing other than this. Dwell for another five years.' He dwelt another five years. Those [years] totaled one hundred and one. This is what they say: '<s>Maghavan</s> indeed dwelt one hundred and one years of <s>brahmacarya</s> with <s>Prajāpati</s>.' To him, he said: (ChUp 8.11.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,11.3 pūrvavadevamevetyuktvā yo mayoktasribhiḥ paryāyaistamevaitaṃ no evānyatraitasmādātmano 'nyaṃ kañcana kiṃ tarhyetameva vyākhyāsyāmi /
svalpastu doṣastavāvaśiṣṭastatkṣapaṇāya vasāparāṇyanyāni pañca varṣāṇītyuktaḥ sa tathā cakāra /
tasmai mṛditakaṣāyādidoṣāya sthānatrayadoṣasaṃbandharahitamātmanaḥsvarūpamapahatapāpmatvādilakṣaṇaṃ maghavate tasmai hovāca /
children.translated_text: To him [<s>Indra</s>], whose impurities such as passion and the rest had been crushed — [<s>Prajāpati</s>] spoke to <s>Maghavan</s> about the essential nature of the Self, free from connection with the defects of the three states [waking, dream, and deep sleep], characterized by freedom from evil and the other [attributes].

children.text: tānyekaśataṃ varṣāṇi saṃpeduḥ saṃpannāni babhūvuḥ /
children.translated_text: Those [years] totaled one hundred and one years.

children.text: yadāhurloke śiṣṭā ekaśataṃ ha vai varṣāṇi maghavānprajāpatau brahmacaryamuvāseti tadetaddvātriṃśatamityādinā darśitamityākhyāyikāto 'pasṛtya śrutyocyate /
children.translated_text: What the learned say in the world — '<s>Maghavan</s> indeed dwelt one hundred and one years of <s>brahmacarya</s> with <s>Prajāpati</s>' — this very thing has been shown by the [calculation] 'thirty-two' and so on. Thus, stepping outside the narrative, the <s>śruti</s> says:

children.text: evaṃ kilaitadindratvādapi gurutaramindreṇāpi mahatā yatnenaikottaravarṣaśatakṛtāyāsena prāptamātmajñānamato nātaḥ paraṃ puruṣārthāntaramastītyātmajñānaṃ stauti //3//
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, this knowledge of the Self was attained even by <s>Indra</s> — [a position] more weighty even than <s>Indra</s>-hood — through great effort, the exertion of one hundred and one years. Therefore, there is no supreme human goal other than this Self-knowledge — thus [the text] praises Self-knowledge. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.11.3:] As before, having said 'Even so indeed,' [<s>Prajāpati</s> continued:] 'This very one whom I spoke of in three stages — nothing other than this <s>Ātman</s>, not any other whatsoever. Rather, this very same I shall explain.' 'But the defect in you is slight and remains; for its removal, dwell another five years.' When thus told, he did so.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasyaikādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

maghavan martyaṃ vā idaṃ śarīram āttaṃ mṛtyunā |
tad asyāmṛtasyāśarīrasyātmano 'dhiṣṭhānam |

children.translated_text: '<s>Maghavan</s>, this body is mortal — seized by death. It is the abode of this immortal, bodiless Self. One who has a body is seized by pleasure and pain. There is no cessation of pleasure and pain for one who has a body. But pleasure and pain do not touch one who is bodiless.' (ChUp 8.12.1)

children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary on 8.12.1:] 'O Maghavan, this body is mortal — subject to death.' What you think — that the ātman characterized as the support of the eye and the like, described as the one in deep sleep (saṃprasāda), has gone to destruction — hear the reason for that. This body indeed is mortal, perishable. And it is seized (ātta) by death — constantly grasped by it. When it is said 'it is mortal,' meaning 'it dies at some time,' there is not as much terror as when it is said 'it is already seized, already pervaded by death' — hence, for the sake of dispassion (vairāgya), the distinction is stated: 'seized by death.' [The question is:] how indeed can one who has turned away from identification with the body be established [in the Self]? The word 'body' (śarīra) here is used together with the senses and the mind. That body belongs to this one in deep sleep (saṃprasāda), who is known through the three states [waking, dream, deep sleep], who is immortal, free from the properties of the body, senses, and mind such as death. The word 'immortal' (amṛta) already establishes bodilessness; the additional statement 'bodiless' (aśarīra) is to prevent [the misconception] that the ātman has parts and form like wind and the like. Or, the ātman, being Sat (Being), the one who willed — from it, through the sequence of fire, water, and food, the body was produced as a support. Or, having entered [the body] in the form of the jīva, it indeed presides over it — hence [the body is called] a support (adhiṣṭhāna). For one whose support is of this nature — always seized by death, produced by dharma and adharma, like the pleasant and unpleasant — being presided over by that [support], possessing it, one becomes embodied (saśarīra). For the ātman whose nature is bodiless — due to the non-discrimination 'I am this body, and the body alone is I' — the selfhood, the state of being embodied, [arises]; and therefore, being embodied, one is seized, grasped by the pleasant and the unpleasant. This is well-known. And for one who is embodied, the cessation — the destruction, the interruption of the continuous flow — of the pleasant and the unpleasant, which are caused by contact with and separation from external objects, which one considers as 'mine,' does not exist. But for one whose ignorance-born identification with the body has been turned back through the knowledge of the bodiless essential nature — [for such a one], the pleasant and the unpleasant do not touch him. The verb 'touch' (spṛś) is construed with each separately — thus two sentences arise: 'the pleasant does not touch him' and 'the unpleasant does not touch him.' Just as [in the rule]: 'One should not converse with barbarians, impure persons, and the unrighteous.' For those [pleasant and unpleasant] are effects of dharma and adharma. But bodilessness is the essential nature — hence, since dharma and adharma are impossible there, their being effects is all the more remote — therefore the pleasant and the unpleasant do not touch him. Now, if the pleasant also does not touch the bodiless one, then what Maghavan said — 'the one in deep sleep has gone to destruction' — has occurred here too [as an objection]. This is not a fault — for the pleasant and unpleasant that do not touch [the bodiless one] are those caused by dharma and adharma, produced by the contact and separation with external objects. But the bliss (ānanda) that is the essential nature of the Self, free from all distinctions of enjoyer, enjoyed, and enjoyment — which is the very nature of the Self — that always exists, because there is no cause for its destruction. And its non-apprehension in deep sleep is not due to its absence, but only due to the absence of a second thing [to know it by] — the meaning is: not due to the destruction of bliss. For when there is a second thing, there is differentiation; and it is said that differentiation is 'a little of bliss' — a minute measure of bliss. But when there is no second thing, there is no differentiation, [and hence] it is the infinite, limitless bliss that is called the Bhūman (the Infinite). Therefore, there is no fault in the teaching.
