children.translated_text: Likewise, other ritualists (<s>karmin</s>s), whose minds are captivated by external objects, though relying on the <s>Veda</s> as authority, considering the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s> — which is the ultimate truth — as if it were destruction, like <s>Indra</s> [initially did], revolve ceaselessly through the modes of ascent and descent, like a water-wheel.

children.text: kimanye kṣudrajantavo vivekahīnāḥ svabhāvata eva bahirviṣayāpahṛtacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: What to speak of other insignificant creatures, devoid of discrimination, whose minds are naturally captivated by external objects?

children.text: tasmādidaṃ tyaktasarvabāhyaiṣaṇairananyaśaraṇaiḥ paramahaṃsaparivrājakairatyāśramibhirvedāntavijñānaparaireva vedanīyaṃ pūjyatamaiḥ prājāpatyaṃ cemaṃ saṃpradāyamanusaradbhirupanibaddhaṃ prakaraṇacatuṣṭayena /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is to be known only by the most venerable <s>paramahaṃsa parivrājaka</s>s (supreme renunciants) — those beyond all stages of life (<s>āśrama</s>), who have abandoned all external desires, who have no other refuge, who are devoted to the knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>, and who follow this tradition of <s>Prajāpati</s> — [this teaching is] bound together in these four sections.

children.text: tathānuśāsatyadyāpi ta eva nānya iti //1 //
children.translated_text: Thus even now, they alone teach this — no others. (1)

Moreover, if something other than the seer in the [right] eye were being taught [as the Self], then this [objection] would be justified. But having said 'This very one is to be sought' (etaṃ tveva te), the teaching is indeed of the seer — even in dream. If [one objects:] the seer is not taught in dream — no, because of the teaching: 'as if weeping, as if experiencing the unpleasant.' And no one other than the seer moves about being magnified in dream. From the reasoning established in another śruti: 'Here this person is self-luminous.' Even though in dream one has cognitions (dhī), nevertheless the cognition does not function as an instrument for the apprehension of dream experience. Rather, like paintings on a canvas, the cognition based on waking impressions becomes merely something seen — therefore the self-luminosity of the seer is not contradicted. Likewise in deep sleep — the absence of a second thing is the cause of non-apprehension [of the Self], not the absence [of the Self]. Just as in the case of fire whose fuel is exhausted — the fire has not been destroyed, only the manifestation has ceased — similarly here. Even in everyday usage, when someone says 'I slept happily, I knew nothing' — the experience of happiness and the experience of the absence of knowledge [of objects] would not be possible if the seer did not exist [in deep sleep]. The negation 'I knew nothing' negates only the object of knowledge, not the knower. For the knower cannot be negated — because of the impossibility of the negation of the one who negates. Therefore, the Self — the seer — is indestructible (avināśī), because its nature is the nature of seeing (darśana). And seeing is the nature of seeing alone, not different from the seer. And because it is partless, there is no destruction of parts. Therefore it is eternal — because it is not produced. From the śruti: 'This great unborn Self is imperishable, undecaying, immortal, fearless — Brahman.' The word 'wind' (vāyu) in the passage is for the purpose of illustration — that just as wind, though invisible and intangible, is inferred from touch, similarly the ātman, though bodiless and imperceptible, is to be inferred from consciousness (caitanya). And this ātman, being bodiless (aśarīra), is not touched by the pleasant and the unpleasant — the fruit of dharma and adharma — which result from embodiment. And being infinite, it is Brahman. 'O Maghavan, I shall explain this further' — this is to introduce the subsequent section. (1)

children.text: START ChUp 8,12.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.2]

children.text:
aśarīro vāyuḥ |
abhraṃ vidyut stanayitnur aśarīrāṇy etāni |
tad yathaitāny amuṣmād ākāśāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyante || ChUp_8,12.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Wind is bodiless. Clouds, lightning, and thunder are bodiless. Just as these, rising from that space, reach the highest light, and manifest in their own forms —' (ChUp 8.12.2)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,12.2 tatrāśarīrasya saṃprasādasyāvidyayā śarīreṇāviśeṣatāṃ sasarīratāmeva saṃprāptasya śarīrātsamutthāya svena rūpeṇa yathābhiniṣpattistathā vaktavyeti dṛṣṭānta ucyate-aśarīro vāyuravidyamānaṃ śiraḥpāṇyādimaccharīramasyetyaśarīraḥ /
kiṃ cābhraṃ vidyutstanayitnurityetāni cāśarīrāṇi /
tattatraivaṃ sati varṣādiprayojanāvasāne yathā /
amuṣmāditi bhūmiṣṭhā śrutirdyulokasaṃbandhinamākāśadeśaṃ vyapadiśati /

etāni yathoktānyākāśasamānarūpatāmāpannāni svena vāyvādirūpeṇāgṛhyamāṇānyākāśākhyatāṃ gatāni yathā saṃprasādo 'vidyāvasthāyāṃ śarīrātmabhāvamevāpannaḥ, tāni ca tathābhūtānyamuṣmāddyulokasambandhina ākāśadeśātsamuttiṣṭhanti varṣaṇādiprayojanābhinirvṛttaye /
children.translated_text: These, as described, having assumed a form identical with space — being imperceptible in their own forms as wind and so on — having attained the designation of space; just as the <s>saṃprasāda</s> (serene self), in the state of <s>avidyā</s>, has assumed the identity of the body-self — those [elements], being in that state, rise from the region of space connected with the heavenly world for the accomplishment of the purpose of rain and so on.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How?

children.text: śiśirāpāye sāvitra paraṃ jyotiḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ graiṣmakamupasaṃpadya sāvitramabhitāpaṃ prāpyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: When winter has passed, reaching the highest, intensified light of the summer sun — meaning reaching the heat of the sun; that is the meaning.

children.text: ādityābhitāpena pṛthagbhāvamāpāditāḥ santaḥ svena svena rūpeṇa purovātādivāyurūpeṇa stimitabhāvaṃ hitvābhramapi bhūmiparvatahastyādirūpeṇa vidyudapi svena jyotirlatādicapalarūpeṇa stanayitnurapi svena garjitāśanirūpeṇetyevaṃ prāvṛḍāgame svena svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyante //2 //
children.translated_text: Having been brought into differentiation by the heat of the sun, they each manifest in their own respective forms — wind in its form as preceding winds and the like, abandoning its state of stillness; clouds too, in their form as earth, mountains, elephants, and the like; lightning too, in its own flickering form as streaks of light; thunder too, in its own form as roaring and thunderbolts — thus, at the onset of the rainy season, they each manifest in their own respective forms. (2)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.12.2:] Now, the bodiless <s>saṃprasāda</s> (serene self), which has attained identity with the body through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — namely, the state of having a body — how it rises from the body and manifests in its own form must be stated; hence an analogy is given. Wind is bodiless — it has no body possessing head, hands, and such — hence it is bodiless. Moreover, clouds, lightning, and thunder — these too are bodiless. Then, when this is the case — at the end of the purpose of rain and so on — just as [these arise]. 'From that' — the <s>śruti</s>, speaking from the standpoint of those on earth, refers to the region of space connected with the heavenly world.

children.text: START ChUp 8,12.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.3]

children.text:
evam evaiṣa saṃprasādo 'smāc charīrāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate |
sa uttamapuruṣaḥ |
sa tatra paryeti jakṣat krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ strībhir vā yānair vā jñātibhir vā nopajanaṃ smarann idaṃ śarīram |
sa yathā prayogya ācaraṇe yukta evam evāyam asmiñ charīre prāṇo yuktaḥ || ChUp_8,12.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Just so, this serene self (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), rising from this body, reaches the highest light and manifests in its own form. He is the supreme person (<s>uttamapuruṣa</s>). There he moves about, eating, playing, and delighting — with women, or with chariots, or with relatives — not remembering this appendage, the body. Just as a draft animal is yoked to a carriage, so is the <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) yoked to this body.' (ChUp 8.12.3)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,12.3 yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto vāyvādīnāmākāśādisāmyagamanavadavidyayā saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ śarīrasāmyamāpanno 'hamamuṣya putro jāto jīrṇo mariṣya ityevaṃprakāraṃ prajāpatineva maghavānyathoktena krameṇa nāsi tvaṃ dehendriyādidharmā tattvamasīti pratibodhitaḥ sansa eṣa saṃprasādo jīvo 'smāccharīrādākāśādiva vāyvādayaḥ samutthāya dehādivailakṣaṇyamātmano rūpamavagamya dehātmabhāvanāṃ hitvetyetat /
svena rūpeṇa sadātmanaivābhiniṣpadyata iti vyākhyātaṃ purastāt /
sa yena svena rūpeṇa saṃprasādo 'bhiniṣpadyate prākpratibodhāttadbhrāntinimittātsarpo bhavati yatā rajjuḥ paścātkṛtaprakāśā rajjvātmanā svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate /
evaṃ ca sa uttamapuruṣa uttamaścāsau puruṣaścetyuttamapuruṣaḥ sa evottamapuruṣo 'kṣisvapnapuruṣau vyaktāvavyaktaśca suṣuptaḥ samastaḥ saṃprasanno 'śarīraśca svena rūpeṇeti /
eṣāmeṣa svena rūpeṇāvasthitaḥ kṣarākṣarau vyākṛtāvyākṛtāvapekṣyottamapuruṣaḥ kṛtanirvacano hyayaṃ gītāsu /
sa saṃprasādaḥ svena rūpeṇa tatra svātmani svasthatayā sarvātmabhūtaḥ paryeti kvacidindrādyātmanā jakṣaddhasanbhakṣayanvā bhakṣyānuccāvacānīpsitānkvacinmanomātraiḥ saṃkalpādeva samutthitairbrāhmalaukikairvā krīḍanstryādibhī ramamāṇaśca manasaiva nopajanaṃ srīpuṃsayoranyonyopagamena jāyata ityupajanamātmabhāvena vā'tmasāmīpyena jāyata ityupajanamidaṃ śarīraṃ tanna smaran /
tatsmaraṇe hi duḥkhameva syāt /
duḥkhātmakatvāttasya /
nanvanubhūtaṃ cenna smaredasarvajñatvaṃ muktasya /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
yena mithyājñānādinā janitaṃ tacca mithyājñānādi vidyayoccheditamatastannānubhūtameveti na tadasmaraṇe sarvajñatvahāniḥ /
na hyu nmattena grahagṛhītena vā yadanubhūtaṃ tadunmādādyapadame 'pi smartavyaṃ syāttathehāpi saṃsāribhiravidyādoṣavadbhiryadanubhūyate tatsarvātmānamaśarīraṃ na spṛśati /
avidyānimittābhāvāt /
ye tūcchinnadoṣairmṛditakaṣāyairmānasāḥ satyāḥ kāmā anṛtāpidhānā anubhūyante vidyābhivyaṅgyatvātta eva muktena sarvātmabhūtena saṃbadhyanta ityātmajñānastutaye nirdiśyante 'taḥ sādhvetadviśinaṣṭi-ya ete brahmaloka iti /
yatra kvacana bhavanto 'pi brahmaṇyeva hi te loke bhavantīti sarvātmatvādbrahmaṇa ucyante /
nanu kathamekaḥ'sannānyatpaśyati nānyadvijānāti sa bhūmā'kāmāṃśca brāhmalaukikān'paśyan ramata'iti ca viruddham /
yathaiko yasminneva kṣaṇe paśyati sa tasminneva kṣaṇe na paśyati ceti /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
śrutyantare parihṛtatvāt /
draṣṭurdṛṣṭeraviparilopātpaśyanneva bhavati /
draṣṭuranyatvena kāmānāmabhāvānna paśyati ceti /
yadyapi suṣupte taduktaṃ muktasyāpi sarvaikatvātsamāno dvitīyābhāvaḥ /
kena kaṃ paśyediti coktameva /
aśarīrasvarūpo 'pahatapāpmādilakṣaṇaḥ sankathameṣa puruṣo 'kṣiṇi dṛśyata ityuktaḥ prajāpatinā /
tatra yathāsāvakṣiṇi sākṣāddṛśyate tadvaktavyamitīdamārabhyate /
tatra ko heturakṣiṇi darśana ityāha-sa dṛṣṭānto yathā prayogyaḥ prayogyaparo vā saśabdaḥ /
prayujyata iti prayogyo 'śvo balīvarde vā /

yathā loka ācaratyanenetyācaraṇo ratho 'no vā tasminnācaraṇe yuktastadākarṣaṇāya, evamasmiñcharīre rathasthānīye prāṇaḥ pañcavṛttirindriyamanobuddhisaṃyuktaḥ prajñātmā vijñānakriyāśaktidvayasaṃmūrchitātmā yuktaḥ svakarmaphalopabhoganimittaṃ niyuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, that by which one moves is the carriage (<s>ācaraṇa</s>) — a chariot or cart — [the animal being] yoked to that carriage for drawing it; so too in this body, which corresponds to the chariot, the <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) of fivefold function, conjoined with senses, mind, and intellect — the <s>prajñātman</s> (conscious self), the self imbued with the dual powers of cognition and action — is yoked, appointed for the purpose of experiencing the fruits of its own <s>karma</s>.

children.text: kasminnvahamutkrānta utkrānto bhavisaṣyāmi kasminvā pratiṣṭhite pratiṣṭhāsyāmīti /
children.translated_text: 'In what, when I depart, will I depart? And in what, when it is established, will I be established?'

children.text: īśvareṇa rājñeva sarvādhikārī darśanaśravaṇaceṣṭāvyāpāre 'dhikṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a king [appointing] an all-powerful minister, [the <s>Ātman</s>] is appointed to the functions of seeing, hearing, and acting.

children.text: tasyaiva tu mātraikadeśaścakṣurindriyaṃ rūpopalabdhidvārabhūtam //3 //
children.translated_text: But only a fraction of it — the sense-organ of the eye — serves as the door for the apprehension of form. (3)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.12.3:] Just as this analogy of wind and the like — having attained identity with space, as if in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> through <s>avidyā</s> — [the self too,] having assumed identity with the body: 'I am the son of so-and-so, I was born, I have grown old, I will die' — thinking in this manner — but being awakened by <s>Prajāpati</s> himself, like <s>Maghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>), in the manner described, [being told:] 'You are not the body, senses, and their attributes — you are That (<s>tat tvam asi</s>)' — this <s>saṃprasāda</s>, the <s>jīva</s>, rises from this body, just as wind and the like [rise] from space — meaning he comprehends the distinctness of the <s>Ātman</s>'s own form from the body and abandons the identification with the body; that is the meaning. 'He manifests in his own form' — meaning in the form of <s>Sat</s> (Being) alone — this has been explained before. That [one] in whose own form the <s>saṃprasāda</s> manifests — prior to his awakening, due to the delusion that caused [the appearance of] the snake, is like a rope: just as a rope, after being illuminated, manifests in its own form as a rope. And thus he is the supreme person (<s>uttamapuruṣa</s>) — supreme and a person, hence the supreme person. This very <s>saṃprasāda</s> is the supreme person — the same one [seen in] the eye, in dream, the manifest and the unmanifest, the one in deep sleep, fully collected, serene, bodiless, 'in his own form.' Among these [states], this one established in his own form, in relation to the perishable and the imperishable, the manifest and the unmanifest, is called the supreme person — for this term is etymologically explained in the <s>Gītā</s>. He, the <s>saṃprasāda</s>, in his own form, there — in his own self, being at ease, having become the self of all — moves about; somewhere in the form of <s>Indra</s> and others, eating, consuming, or enjoying high and low desirable objects; somewhere through mind alone, through resolves that have arisen [spontaneously], or through those pertaining to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, playing; delighting with women and the like — through mind alone. Not remembering this appendage (<s>upajana</s>) — that which is born through the union of woman and man — [this] body — he does not remember that. For if he were to remember it, there would be only suffering — because that [body] is of the nature of suffering. [Objection:] But if something experienced is not remembered, the liberated one would not be omniscient. There is no defect — because the false knowledge and such by which [those experiences] were generated has been cut off by knowledge; therefore, it was not truly experienced — hence there is no loss of omniscience in not remembering it. Just as what was experienced by a madman or one possessed by a spirit need not be remembered even after the cessation of madness and the like — so too here: whatever is experienced by beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>, possessing the defect of <s>avidyā</s>, does not touch the one who has become the self of all, who is bodiless — because the cause, namely <s>avidyā</s>, is absent. But those true desires that are mental — covered by the veil of the unreal — which are experienced by those whose defects have been cut off and whose impurities have been crushed — because they are manifested by knowledge, they are connected with the liberated one who has become the self of all; hence they are indicated for the praise of self-knowledge. Therefore [the text] properly specifies: 'those that are in the world of <s>Brahman</s>' — wherever they may be, they are indeed in the world of <s>Brahman</s> — because of the all-self-hood of <s>Brahman</s>, they are called thus. [Objection:] But how [can the same person], being one, 'not see anything else, not know anything else — this is the <s>Bhūman</s> (Infinite)' and [also] 'seeing the desires in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, without desire, he delights' — [these two statements] are contradictory. [For it implies] that in the very moment when one sees, in that same moment one does not see. There is no defect — because this is resolved in another <s>śruti</s>: 'Because the seeing of the seer is never lost,' he always sees. But because the desires do not exist as different from the seer, he 'does not see.' And although this was said regarding deep sleep, for the liberated one too, because of the oneness of all, the same absence of a second [applies]: 'With what could one see what?' — this too has been said. He who is bodiless in nature, characterized as free from evil and the like — how is this person seen in the eye? — this was stated by <s>Prajāpati</s>. In that regard, how he is directly seen in the eye — this must be stated, and hence the following is commenced. The reason for [his] being seen in the eye is stated: the analogy is — just as <s>prayogya</s> (a draft animal), or the word <s>sa</s> (he) refers to the draft animal — <s>prayogya</s> means a horse or bullock that is employed.

children.text: START ChUp 8,12.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.4]

children.text:
atha yatraitad ākāśam anuviṣaṇṇaṃ cakṣuḥ sa cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣo darśanāya cakṣuḥ |
atha yo vededaṃ jighrāṇīti sa ātmā gandhāya ghrāṇam |
atha yo vededam abhivyāharāṇīti sa ātmā abhivyāhārāya vāk |
atha yo vededaṃ śṛṇvānīti sa ātmā śravaṇāya śrotram || ChUp_8,12.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, that eye which is directed toward this space — that is the person of the eye, [used] for seeing; the eye [is the instrument]. Now, he who knows "Let me smell this" — that is the <s>Ātman</s>; the nose is for smelling. Now, he who knows "Let me speak this" — that is the <s>Ātman</s>; speech is for speaking. Now, he who knows "Let me hear this" — that is the <s>Ātman</s>; the ear is for hearing.' (ChUp 8.12.4)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,12.4 atha yatra kṛṣṇatāropalakṣitamākāśaṃ dehacchidramanuviṣaṇṇamanuṣaktamanugataṃ tatra sa prakṛto 'śarīra ātmā cākṣuṣaścakṣuṣi bhava iti cākṣuṣastasya darśanāya rūpopalabdhaye cakṣuḥ karaṇaṃ yasya taddehādibhiḥ saṃhatatvātparasya draṣṭurarthe so 'tra cakṣuṣi darśanena liṅgena dṛśyate paro 'śarīro 'saṃhataḥ /
akṣiṇi dṛśyata iti prajāpatinoktaṃ sarvendriyadvāropalakṣaṇārtham /
sarvaviṣayopalabdhā hi sa eveti /
sphuṭopalabdhihetutvāttvakṣiṇīti viśeṣavacanaṃ sarvaśrutiṣu /
"ahamadarśamiti tatsatyaṃ bhavatī"ti ca śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'I saw — that becomes true.'

children.text: athāpi yo 'smindehe veda kathamidaṃ sugandhi durgandhi vā jighrāṇītyasya gandhaṃ vijānīyāmiti sa ātmā tasya gandhāya gandhavijñānāya ghrāṇam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, he who in this body knows: 'Let me smell this — whether fragrant or foul — let me perceive its odor' — that is the <s>Ātman</s>; the nose is for the perception of odor.

children.text: atha yo vededaṃ vacanamabhivyāharāṇīti vadiṣyāmīti sa ātmābhivyavaharaṇakriyāsiddhaye karaṇaṃ vāgindriyam /
children.translated_text: Now, he who knows 'Let me utter this speech' — 'I shall speak' — that is the <s>Ātman</s>; the organ of speech is the instrument for the accomplishment of the act of speaking.

children.text: atha yo vededaṃ śṛṇavānīti sa ātmā śravaṇāya śrotram //4 //
children.translated_text: Now, he who knows 'Let me hear this' — that is the <s>Ātman</s>; the ear is for hearing. (4)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.12.4:] Now, where the space of the body's aperture, indicated by the black pupil, is directed — there, that <s>Ātman</s> under discussion, the bodiless one, is the person of the eye (<s>cākṣuṣa</s>) — 'born in the eye,' hence 'of the eye.' For seeing, for the apprehension of form — the eye is the instrument; because this [self] is conjoined with body and other [factors], [it serves] for the purpose of the supreme seer — here, in the eye, through the sign of seeing, the supreme bodiless, uncompounded [self] is seen. <s>Prajāpati</s>'s statement 'he is seen in the eye' is meant to indicate [the self's presence] through all sense-doors. For he is the apprehender of all sense-objects. But 'in the eye' is specified in all <s>śruti</s>s because it most clearly manifests the apprehension.

children.text: START ChUp 8,12.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.5]

children.text:
atha yo vededaṃ manvānīti sa ātmā |
mano 'sya daivaṃ cakṣuḥ |
sa vā eṣa etena daivena cakṣuṣā manasaitān kāmān paśyan ramate ya ete brahmaloke || ChUp_8,12.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, he who knows "Let me think this" — that is the <s>Ātman</s>. The mind is his divine eye. He, verily, with this divine eye, the mind, seeing these desires that are in the world of <s>Brahman</s>, rejoices.' (ChUp 8.12.5)

children.text: ChUpBh_8,12.5 atha yo vedadaṃ manvānīti mananavyāpāramindriyāsaṃspṛṣṭaṃ kevalaṃ manvānīti veda sa ātmā mananāya manaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.12.5:] Now, he who knows 'Let me think this' — a purely mental operation untouched by the senses — 'let me think' — he who knows [this], that is the <s>Ātman</s>; for thinking, the mind [is the instrument].

children.text:
yo veda sa ātmetyevaṃ sarvatra prayogādvedanamasya svarūpamityavagamyate /
yathā yaḥ purastātprakāśayati sa ādityo yo dakṣiṇato yaḥ paścādya uttarato ya ūrdhvaṃ prakāśayati sa āditya ityukte prakāśasvarūpaḥ sa iti gamyate /
darśanādi kriyānirvṛttyarthāni tu cakṣurādikaraṇāni /
idaṃ cāsyā'tmanaḥ sāmarthyādavagamyate /
ātmanaḥ sattāmātra eva jñānakartṛtvaṃ na tu vyāpṛtatayā /
yathā savituḥ sattāmātra eva prakāśanakartṛtvaṃ na tu vyāpṛtatayeti tadvat /
mano 'syā'tmano daivamaprākṛtamitarendriyairasādhāraṇaṃ cakṣuścaṣṭe paśyatyaneneti cakṣuḥ /
vartamānakālaviṣayāṇi cendriyāṇyato 'daivāni tāni /
children.translated_text: The [other] sense-organs have as their object only the present time — hence they are 'not divine.'

children.text: manastu trikālaviṣayopalabdhikaraṇaṃ mṛditadoṣaṃ ca sūkṣmavyavahitādisarvopalabdhikaraṇaṃ ceti daivaṃ cakṣurucyate /
children.translated_text: But the mind is the instrument for apprehending objects of all three times, and when its defects have been crushed, it is also the instrument for apprehending all subtle, concealed, and other [objects] — hence it is called the divine eye.

children.text: sa vai muktaḥ svarūpāpanno 'vidyākṛtadehendriyamanoviyuktaḥ sarvātmabhāvamāpannaḥ sanneṣa vyomavadviśuddhaḥ sarveśvaro manaupādhiḥ sannetenaiveśvareṇa manasaitānkāmānsavitṛprakāśavannityapratatena darśanena paśyan ramate /
children.translated_text: He who is liberated, having attained his own form, freed from body, senses, and mind created by <s>avidyā</s>, having attained the state of being the self of all, being pure like space, the lord of all, having the mind as his limiting adjunct — with this very lordly mind, with a vision eternally extended like the light of the sun, seeing these desires, he delights.

children.text: kānkāmāniti viśinaṣṭi-ya ete brahmaṇi loke hiraṇyanidhivadbāhyaviṣayāsaṅgānṛtenāpihitāḥ saṃkalpamātralabhyāstānityarthaḥ //5 //
children.translated_text: What desires? He specifies: those that are in the world of <s>Brahman</s> — like a treasure of gold [hidden in the earth], covered by the veil of the unreal, which is the non-attachment to external objects, attainable by mere resolve alone — those [desires]; that is the meaning. (5)

'He who knows — that is the <s>Ātman</s>' — from this usage in every case, it is understood that knowing is his essential nature. Just as when it is said: 'He who illuminates in the east is the sun; he who illuminates in the south, in the west, in the north, and above — that is the sun' — it is understood that his essential nature is illumination. The sense-organs such as the eye and so on are [merely] for the accomplishment of actions such as seeing. And this is understood from the very capacity of the <s>Ātman</s>: the agency of knowing belongs to the <s>Ātman</s> merely by its existence — not through [its] being actively engaged, just as the agency of illumination belongs to the sun merely by its existence — not through active engagement; it is the same. The mind is this <s>Ātman</s>'s divine (<s>daiva</s>) — not natural, extraordinary compared to other senses — eye, in the sense that it sees through it.

children.text: START ChUp 8,12.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.6]

children.text:
taṃ vā etaṃ devā ātmānam upāsate |
tasmāt teṣāṃ sarve ca lokā āttāḥ sarve ca kāmāḥ |
sa sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānāti |
iti ha prajāpatir uvāca prajāpatir uvāca || ChUp_8,12.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'The gods meditate on this very Self. Therefore, all worlds and all desires are won by them. He who finds and knows this Self — he obtains all worlds and all desires.' Thus said <s>Prajāpati</s>, thus said <s>Prajāpati</s>. (ChUp 8.12.6)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,12.6 yasmādeṣa indrāya prajāpatinokta ātmā tasmāttataḥ śrutvā tamātmānamadyatve 'pi devā upāsate /
tadupāsanācca teṣāṃ sarve ca lokā āttāḥ prāptāḥ sarve ca kāmāḥ /
yadarthaṃ hīndra ekaśataṃ varṣāṇi prajāpatau brahmacaryamuvāsa tatphalaṃ prāptaṃ devairityabhiprāyaḥ /
tadyuktaṃ devānāṃ mahābhāgyatvānna tvidānīṃ manuṣyāṇāmalpajīvitatvānmandataraprajñatvācca saṃbhavatīti prāpta idamucyate-sa sarvāṃśca lokānāpnoti sarvāṃśca kāmānidānīntano 'pi /
ko 'sau /
children.translated_text: Who is he?

children.text: indrādivadyastamātmānamanuvidya vijānātīti ha sāmānyena kila prajāpatiruvāca /
children.translated_text: Like <s>Indra</s> and others, whoever finds and knows this Self — thus <s>Prajāpati</s> spoke in general terms.

children.text: ataḥ sarveṣāmātmajñānaṃ tatphalaprāptiśca tulyaiva bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for all, Self-knowledge and the attainment of its fruit are equal — that is the meaning.

children.text: dvirvacanaṃ prakaraṇasamāptyartham //6//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of the phrase] is for indicating the conclusion of the section. (6)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.12.6:] Since this Self was taught by <s>Prajāpati</s> to <s>Indra</s>, therefore, having heard from him, the gods meditate on this Self even now. And because of that meditation, all worlds are won by them — attained — and all desires [are fulfilled]. For <s>Indra</s> dwelt one hundred and one years of <s>brahmacarya</s> with <s>Prajāpati</s> — the fruit of that has been obtained by the gods — this is the intended meaning. That is appropriate given the great fortune of the gods, but it might be thought that this is not possible now for human beings due to their short lifespan and lesser intelligence. Against this, the following is stated: He who obtains all worlds and all desires — even one living now —

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya dvādaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,13.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.13.1]

children.text:
śyāmāc chabalaṃ prapadye |
śabalāc chyāmaṃ prapadye |
aśva iva romāṇi vidhūya pāpaṃ candra iva rāhor mukhāt pramucya dhūtvā śarīram akṛtaṃ kṛtātmā brahmalokam abhisaṃbhavāmīty abhisaṃbhavāmīti || ChUp_8,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'From the dark (<s>śyāma</s>) I approach the variegated (<s>śabala</s>). From the variegated I approach the dark. Shaking off sin as a horse shakes off its hair, freed as the moon from the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>, having cast off the body — I, the perfected Self, attain the uncreated <s>Brahmaloka</s>. I attain [it], I attain [it].' (ChUp 8.13.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,13.1 śyāmācchabalaṃ prapadya ityādimantrāmnāya pāvano japārthaśca dhyānārtho vā /
śyāmo gambhīro varṇaḥ śyāma iva śyāmo hārdaṃ brahmātyantaduravagāhyatvāttaddhārda brahma jñātvā dhyānena tasmācchyāmācchabalaṃ śabala iva śabalo 'raṇyādyanekakāmamiśratvādbrahmalokasya śābalya taṃ brahmalokaṃ śabalaṃ prapadye manasā śarīrapātādvordhvaṃ gaccheyam /
yasmādahaṃ śabalādbrahmalokānnāmarūpavyākaraṇāya śyāmaṃ prapadye hārdabhāvaṃ prapanno 'smītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since from that variegated <s>Brahmaloka</s> I approach the <s>śyāma</s> — the state of the heart — for the purpose of evolving name and form — the meaning is: I have taken refuge in the heart-state.

children.text: atastameva prakṛtisvarūpamātmānaṃ śabalaṃ prapadya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, I approach the very same Self in its original nature, the variegated — that is the meaning.

children.text: kathaṃ śabalaṃ brahmalokaṃ prapadya ityucyate-aśva iva svāni lomāni vidhūya kampanena śramaṃ pāṃsvādi ca romato 'panīya yathā nirmalo bhavatyevaṃ hārdabrahmajñānena vidhūya pāpaṃ dharmādharmākyaṃ candra iva ca rāhugrastastasmādrahormukhātmapramucya bhāsvaro bhavati yathaivaṃ dhūtvā prahāra śarīraṃ sarvānarthāśrayamihaiva dhyānena kṛtātmā kṛtakṛtyaḥ sannakṛtaṃ nityaṃ brahmalokamabhisaṃbhavāmīti /
children.translated_text: How can it be said 'I approach the variegated <s>Brahmaloka</s>'? — Like a horse shaking off its own hairs, removing fatigue, dust, and the like from its hair by shaking, and thereby becoming clean — so too, having shaken off sin called <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> in the heart — and just as the moon, seized by <s>Rāhu</s>, being freed from the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>, becomes radiant — so too, having shaken off, discarded, the body which is the locus of all misfortune — right here through meditation, the perfected Self (<s>kṛtātmā</s>), one whose purpose is fulfilled — I attain the uncreated, eternal <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: dvirvacanaṃ mantrasamāptyartham //1//
children.translated_text: The repetition [of the phrase] is for completing the mantra. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.13.1:] 'From the dark I approach the variegated' and so forth — this is a sacred formula (<s>mantra</s>) recited for purification, for <s>japa</s> (repetition) or for meditation. <s>Śyāma</s> (dark) — a deep color; dark as it were — <s>śyāma</s> is the <s>Brahman</s> in the heart, because of its utter unfathomability. Having known that <s>Brahman</s> in the heart through meditation, from that <s>śyāma</s>, I approach the <s>śabala</s> (variegated) — variegated as it were because <s>Brahmaloka</s> is mixed with manifold desires like a forest — that <s>Brahmaloka</s>, the variegated, I approach — I would go mentally after the fall of the body.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya trayodaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,14.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.14.1]

children.text:
ākāśo vai nāma nāmarūpayor nirvahitā |
te yadantarā tad brahma tad amṛtaṃ sa ātmā |
prajāpateḥ sabhāṃ veśma prapadye yaśo 'haṃ bhavāmi brāhmaṇānāṃ yaśo rājñām yaśo viśām |
yaśo 'ham anuprāpatsi |
sa hāhaṃ yaśasāṃ yaśaḥ |
śyetam adatkam adatkaṃ śyetaṃ lindu mābhigāṃ lindu mābhigām || ChUp_8,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) indeed is the name — it is the evolver of name and form. That which is between them — that is <s>Brahman</s>, that is the immortal, that is the Self. I enter the assembly-hall, the dwelling of <s>Prajāpati</s>. I become the glory of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the glory of the kings, the glory of the <s>Vaiśyas</s>. I have attained glory. May I, the glory of glories — may that slimy, toothless [old age] not come to me, may it not come to me!' (ChUp 8.14.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,14.1 ākāśo vā ityādi brahmaṇo lakṣaṇanirdeśārthamādhyānāya /
ākāśo vai nāma śrutiṣu prasiddha ātmā /
ākāśa ivāśarīratvāsūkṣmatvācca /
sa cā'kāśo nāmarūpayoḥ svātmasthayorjagadbījabhūtayoḥ salilasyeva phenasthānīyayornirvahitā nirvoḍhā vyākartā /
te nāmarūpe yadantarā yasya brahmaṇo 'ntarā madhye vartete, tayorvā nāmarūpayorantarā madhye yannāmarūpābhyāmaspṛṣṭaṃ yadityetattadbrahma nāmarūpavilakṣaṇaṃ nāmarūpābhyāmaspṛṣṭaṃ tathāpi tayornirvoḍhutvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brahmetyarthaḥ /
idameva maitreyībrāhmaṇenoktaṃ cinmātrānugamātmasarvatra citsvarūpataiveti gamyata ekavākyatā /
kartha tadavagamyata ityāha-sa ātmā /
ātmā hi nāma sarvajantūnāṃ pratyakcetanaḥ svasaṃvedyaḥ prasiddhastenaiva svarūpeṇonnīyāśarīro vyomavatsarvagata ātmā brahmetyavagantavyam /
taccā'tmā brahmāmṛtamamaraṇadharmā /
ata ūrdhva mantraḥ /
prajāpatiścaturmukhastasya sabhāṃ veśma prabhuvimitaṃ veśma prapadye gaccheyam /
kiñca yaśo 'haṃ yaśo nāmā'tmāhaṃ bhavāmi brāhmaṇānām /
brāhmaṇā eva hi viśeṣatastamupāsate tatasteṣāṃ yaśo bhavāmi /
tathā rājñāṃ viśāṃ ca /
te 'pyadhikṛtā eveti teṣāmapyātmā bhavāmi /
tadyaśo 'hamanuprāpatsyanuprāptumicchāmi sa hāhaṃ yaśasāmātmanāṃ dehendriyamanobuddhilakṣaṇānāmātmā /
kimarthamahamevaṃ prapadya iti, ucyate-śyetaṃ varṇataḥ pakvabadarasamaṃ rohitam /
children.translated_text: For what purpose do I thus take refuge? [The answer] is stated — '<s>śyeta</s>' (reddish) — in color, equal to a ripe jujube fruit, reddish.

children.text: tathādatkaṃ dantarahitamapyadatkaṃ bhakṣayitṛ srīvyañjanaṃ tatsevināṃ tejobalavīryavijñānadharmāṇāmapahantṛ vināśayitrityetat /
children.translated_text: '<s>Adatka</s>' — toothless yet devouring (<s>adatka</s>) — a sign of old age; it is the destroyer of radiance, strength, virility, knowledge, and <s>dharma</s> in those who are subject to it.

children.text: yadevaṃlakṣaṇaṃ śyetaṃ lindu picchilaṃ tanmābhigāṃ mābhigaccheyam /
children.translated_text: 'May that which has such characteristics — the reddish, slimy (<s>lindu</s>) [old age] — not come to me, may it not approach me.'

children.text: dvirvacanamatyantānarthahetutvapradarśanārtham //1//
children.translated_text: The repetition is for showing that [old age] is the cause of extreme misfortune. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.14.1:] '<s>Ākāśa</s> indeed is the name' and so forth — this is for indicating the characteristics of <s>Brahman</s>, for meditation. <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) is indeed the name — the Self well-known in the scriptures. Like space, because of being bodiless and subtle. And that <s>ākāśa</s> is the evolver (<s>nirvahitā</s>) — the bearer, the differentiator — of name and form, which abide in its own Self, which are the seeds of the world, which stand in relation [to it] as foam does to water. 'That which is between them' — that between which (<s>antarā</s>) these name and form subsist, in the middle of <s>Brahman</s>; or, in the middle of those two — name and form — that which is untouched by name and form — that is <s>Brahman</s>, distinct from name and form, untouched by name and form; yet its being the evolver of those [name and form] is its characteristic — that is <s>Brahman</s>, this is the meaning. This very thing was stated in the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s> — from the pursuit of pure consciousness alone, one arrives at the nature of consciousness everywhere — thus unity of meaning [is established]. To make that understood, he says: 'That is the Self' — for the Self is indeed well-known to all beings as the inner consciousness, self-luminous. By that very nature, one should understand the Self — bodiless, all-pervading like space — as <s>Brahman</s>. And that Self, that <s>Brahman</s>, is immortal — having the nature of deathlessness. What follows is a mantra. '<s>Prajāpati</s>' — the four-faced one — I enter his assembly-hall, the dwelling measured by the lord. Moreover, 'I become the glory' — I, the Self named 'glory,' become [the glory] of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. For <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> especially meditate on him; therefore I become their glory. Similarly, [the glory] of kings and of <s>Vaiśyas</s>. They too are qualified [for this knowledge]; therefore I become the Self of them as well. 'I have attained that glory' — I wish to attain [it]. 'I indeed am the glory of glories' — the Self of those selves characterized as body, senses, mind, and intellect.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya caturdaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: START ChUp 8,15.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.15.1]

children.text:
tad dhaitad brahmā prajāpataya uvāca prajāpatir manave manuḥ prajābhyaḥ |
ācāryakulād vedam adhītya yathāvidhānaṃ guroḥ karmātiśeṣeṇābhisamāvṛtya kuṭumbe śucau deśe svādhyāyam adhīyāno dharmikān vidadhad ātmani sarvendriyāṇi saṃpratiṣṭhāpyāhiṃsan sarvabhūtāny anyatra tīrthebhyaḥ |
sa khalv evaṃ vartayan yāvad āyuṣaṃ brahmalokam abhisaṃpadyate |
na ca punar āvartate na ca punar āvartate || ChUp_8,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'This [teaching] <s>Brahmā</s> told to <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> to <s>Manu</s>; <s>Manu</s> to his descendants. Having studied the <s>Veda</s> from the teacher's family according to the prescribed rules, in the time remaining after performing the teacher's work; having returned [home], establishing himself in a family; in a pure place, studying the scripture; producing righteous [offspring]; having withdrawn all the senses into the Self; not injuring any being, except at the sacred places [prescribed by scripture] — he who lives thus throughout his life attains <s>Brahmaloka</s>. And he does not return again, he does not return again.' (ChUp 8.15.1)

children.text:
ChUpBh_8,15.1 taddhaitadātmajñānaṃ sopakaraṇamomityetadakṣaramityādyaiḥ sahopāsanaistadvācakena granthenāṣṭādhyāyīlakṣaṇena saha brahmā hiraṇyagarbhaḥ parameśvaro vā taddvāreṇa prajāpataye kaśyapāyovāca /
asāvapi manave svaputrāya /
manuḥ prajābhya ityevaṃ śrutyarthasaṃpradāyaparamparayā'gatamupaniṣadvijñānamadyāpi vidvatsvavagamyate /
yatheha ṣaṣṭhādyadhyāyatraye prakāśitātmavidyā saphalāvagamyate tathā karmaṇāṃ na kaścanārtha iti prāpte tadānarthakyaprāptiparijihīrṣayedaṃ karmaṇo vidvadbhiranuṣṭhīyamānasya viśiṣṭaphalavattvenārthavattvamucyate-ācāryakulādvedamadhītya sahārthato 'dhyayanaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhānaṃ yathāsmṛtyuktairniyamairyuktaḥ sannityarthaḥ /
sarvasyāpi vidheḥ smṛtyuktasyopakaparvāṇakaṃ prati kartavyatve guruśuśrūṣāyāḥ prādhānyapradarśanārthamāha-guroḥ karma yatkartavyaṃ tatkṛtvā karmaśūnyo yo 'tiśiṣṭaḥ kālastena kālena vedamadhītyetyarthaḥ /
evaṃ hi niyamavatādhīto vedaḥ karmajñānaphalaprāptaye bhavati nānyathetyabhiprāyaḥ /
abhisamāvṛtya dharmajijñāsāṃ samāpayitvā gurukulannivṛtya nyāyato dārānāhṛtya kuṭumbe sthitvā gārhatthve vihite karmaṇi tiṣṭhannityarthaḥ /
tatrāpi gārhasthyavihitānāṃ karmaṇāṃ svādhyāyasya prādhānyapradarśanārthamucyate-śucau vivikte 'medhyādirahite deśe yatāvadāsīnaḥ svādhyāyamadhīyāno naityakamadhikaṃ ca yathāśakti ṛgādyabhyāsaṃ ca kurvandhārmikānputrāñśiṣyāṃśca dharmayuktānvidadhaddhārmikatvena tānniyamayannātmani svahṛdaye hārde brahmaṇi sarvendriyāṇi saṃpratiṣṭhāpyopasaṃhṛtyendriyagrahaṇātkarmāṇi ca saṃnyasyāhiṃsahiṃnsāṃ parapīḍāmakurvansarvabhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamāni bhūtānyapīḍayannityarthaḥ /
bhikṣānimittamaṭanādināpi parapīḍā syādityata āha-anyatra tīrthebhyaḥ /
tīrthaṃ nāma śāsrānujñāviṣayastato 'nyatretyarthaḥ /
sarvāśramiṇāṃ caitatsamānam tīrthebhyo 'nyatrahiṃsaiveti /
anye varṇayanti kuṭumba evaitatsarvaṃ kurvansa khalvadhikṛto yāvadāyuṣaṃ yāvajjīvamevaṃyathoktena prakāreṇaiva vartayanbrahmalokamabhisaṃpadyatedehānte /
na ca punarāvartate śarīragrahaṇāya /
punarāvṛtteḥ prāptāyāḥ pratiṣedhāt /
arcirādinā mārgeṇa kāryabrahmalokabhisaṃpadya yāvadbrahmalokasthitistāvattatraiva tiṣṭhati prāktato nā'vartata ityarthaḥ /
dvirabhyāsa upaniṣadvidyāparisamāptyarthaḥ //1 // //
children.translated_text: The repetition is for indicating the conclusion of the Upaniṣadic knowledge. (1)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 8.15.1:] This Self-knowledge, together with its auxiliaries — the meditations beginning with 'Oṃ is this syllable' — along with the text expressing it, characterized by the eight chapters — <s>Brahmā</s>, that is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> or the Supreme Lord, told to <s>Prajāpati</s>, that is <s>Kaśyapa</s>, through that [medium]. He in turn [told it] to <s>Manu</s>, his own son. <s>Manu</s> [told it] to his descendants. Thus, this Upaniṣadic knowledge, having come down through the tradition of scriptural transmission, is understood even now by the learned. Just as the Self-knowledge revealed in the three chapters beginning with the sixth is understood to be fruitful — so too, it might be concluded that ritual actions have no purpose. To avert this implication of purposelessness [of action], the following is stated — the purposefulness of ritual action as performed by the wise, having a distinguished fruit: 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s> from the teacher's family' — meaning having thoroughly studied it with understanding of its meaning; 'according to the prescribed rules' — meaning endowed with the regulations stated in the <s>Smṛtis</s>. To show that although all scriptural rules prescribed by <s>Smṛti</s> are to be followed with regard to the [time before] graduation, service to the teacher has primacy, he says: 'the teacher's work' — having done whatever work of the teacher was to be done, in the remaining time when free from work, one studies the <s>Veda</s> — that is the meaning. For the <s>Veda</s> studied under such discipline leads to the attainment of the fruits of ritual and knowledge, and not otherwise — this is the intention. 'Having returned' — having completed the desire to know <s>dharma</s>, returning from the teacher's house, having properly married, establishing himself in a family — meaning remaining in the householder's life as prescribed. Even there, to show that among the duties prescribed for the householder, <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) has primacy, it is said: 'in a pure place' — a secluded [place] free from impurity and the like — being properly seated, studying the scripture — performing the obligatory daily [recitation] and additional [study] as much as possible, practicing the repetition of <s>Ṛg</s> and other [<s>Vedas</s>]; 'producing righteous [offspring]' — making sons and students righteous, disciplining them in righteousness; 'having withdrawn all the senses into the Self' — into the <s>Brahman</s> in the heart — having withdrawn them, [meaning] because of the mention of withdrawing the senses, renouncing actions as well; 'not injuring any being' — not causing harm, not afflicting any beings, whether stationary or moving — that is the meaning. Since even wandering for alms and the like might cause harm to others, he says: 'except at the sacred places [prescribed by scripture]' — '<s>tīrtha</s>' means the domain sanctioned by scripture — 'other than that' is the meaning. And this [non-injury except at prescribed places] is common to all <s>āśramas</s>. Others explain: doing all this while remaining in the household itself — he who is qualified, living thus throughout his life, in the manner described — attains <s>Brahmaloka</s> at the end of the body. And he does not return again — for the taking up of a body. Since the return that would naturally occur is negated — [the meaning is:] having attained <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the conditioned <s>Brahman</s>) through the path of light and the rest, he remains there for as long as that world endures; only thereafter does he not return — that is the meaning.

children.text: iti cchāndogyopaniṣadi aṣṭamādhyāyasya pañcadaśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth section of the eighth chapter of the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: iti śrīmadgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaparamahaṃsapar ivrājakācāryaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau cchāndogyopaniṣadvivaraṇe aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the eighth chapter of the commentary on the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>, composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the supreme wandering ascetic and teacher, the disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>.
